| fixed angle (18 never-seen geometries, float32) | pressure rel-L2 (42 / 43 → mean) | vs constant-gauge prior | vs similarity gauge | vs unit GeoTransolver | vs unit Transolver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ISLA, reference (relative frame, total-measure scale)** | 0.0363 / 0.0405 → **0.0384** | **+10.3%** | 0.964x | 1.42x | 1.29x |
| ISLA, relative frame, reference-length scale (discriminator arm) | 0.0389 / 0.0486 → **0.0437** | +25.7% | 1.099x | 1.62x | 1.47x |
| ISLA, similarity gauge | 0.0411 / 0.0385 → 0.0398 | +14.4% | 1 | 1.47x | 1.33x |
| ISLA, constant gauge (prior) | 0.0342 / 0.0353 → 0.0348 | 1 | 0.874x | 1.29x | 1.17x |

**Against the bars.** The reference pays 10.3%, the "known price" band,
and is 3.5% more accurate than the similarity gauge on the rung where the
gauge paid most; the prediction of 10–15% for it held. The reference-length
arm pays 26%, the "expensive" band, with a 22% seed spread (0.0389 /
0.0486) against 11% for the total-measure arm and 3% for the constant gauge.
**The scale discriminator reads the opposite way from the hypothesis.** The
preregistered trigger was the total-measure arm paying ≥ 5% *more* than the
reference-length arm; instead it pays 12% *less*. Normalizing away the
absolute size does not cost accuracy on the geometry-only rung, it helps
(or, given the seed spread, is at worst neutral), so the gauge's 14.4% here
was not its scale normalization, and the total-measure scale stands as the
reference's without a caveat on this rung.

**What the fixed angle does to the recurrence reading.** The 4-geometry
rung suggested that the plain-mean frame's mesher pattern sells only where
validation geometries recur in training (@sec-nb-relframe-ladder-geo4).
The fixed angle is a never-seen-geometry rung, and under that reading the
reference should have been cheap here; it pays 10%, so recurrence is not
the whole account. What is specific to this rung is the fixed drive
direction: with every case at 12°, the reference configuration's seed
(n̂·d̂ and the measure) varies only with the surface normal, and everything
else a token knows about its place on the wing comes through anchor-relative
positions, whereas the constant gauge's positional seeds (|r|, r̂·d̂,
r̂·n̂ about the plain mean) tell each token directly where it sits along
the chord and span, which at a fixed angle is most of what determines its
pressure. The two candidate accounts of the 10% are therefore the same two
the 35-case rung had, with the balance possibly different here: the mesher
pattern in the plain mean (0.131 body lengths on these wings), or the
positional seeds themselves. At 35 cases FRAME-FULL separated them (exact
frame plus all seeds paid *more*, @sec-nb-frame-full-verdict); at the fixed
angle that discriminator has not been run and would need the frame table
extended to the 126 fixed-angle training cases (a CPU job of a few hours)
before a two-lane pair. It is the next ladder follow-up once the 21-geometry
and 210-case rungs, which test recurrence from the other side, have read
out. A third seed on both fixed-angle arms is also warranted by the spreads.

**Consistency half** of this rung (three samplers, five counts, both arms;
job 718951, 60 lanes) is running; the constant-gauge prior collapses 10.6x
/ 14.9x at 40,000 cells there and the gauge is consistent

(@sec-part-baseline). The unit-drive reruns restore the matched input,
change nothing else, and were preregistered with one prediction: the
unit-drive baselines match or beat ISLA at every rung
(@sec-nb-udrvl-210-verdict for the bars). Five rungs had been measured;

sample id; zero skipped loads), reduced with seed means and paired per-case

ladder was therefore the input-scale artifact, as at every other rung.

510 cases; 4 and 21 geometries; the fixed angle), with GeoTransolver ahead
by 0.76x to 0.92x and Transolver by 0.86x to 0.93x, and the 1,260-case
rerun is the last. Along the case ladder the baseline-to-ISLA ratio is

The two rungs preregistered together in @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-amend read
out (lanes rf_hl_mt2_meas_geometry_scarce_seed{42,43} and
rf_hl_mt2_meas_scarce_seed{42,43}; reference configuration, unit drive, lr

725855 and 727672, no loader warnings; artifact `results/frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json`, block
hilift_val). **21 geometries** (210 training cases, 18 never-seen validation
geometries): 0.1048 / 0.1084 → **0.1066**, +5.2% against the
constant-gauge prior 0.1014 and +2.2% against the similarity gauge's
0.1043. **210 cases** (recurring geometries): 0.0706 / 0.0726 →

**Against the preregistered predictions.** The discriminating cell was the
210-case rung: ≥ 8% confirms the recurrence reading, ≤ 3% refutes it in
favor of data quantity. It reads +11.3%, **recurrence confirmed**: with the
same 210 training cases, the reference pays 11% where the validation
geometries recur in training and 5% where they do not, and the 35-case rung
(recurring) paid 11% too. The 21-geometry cell was predicted ≤ 3% by both
readings and reads +5.1%, just past the cheap band; the recurrence reading
survives with the amendment that never-seen rungs are cheap but not free
when there are many training geometries at varied angles (the 4-geometry
rung, +1.0%, had too few for the pattern to matter either way). The fixed
angle (+10.3%, never seen) remains the one rung the reading does not
cover, as @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-fixed-angle stated.

**The ladder, complete on six rungs** (float32; all rate-matched at lr
1e-3 except the DrivAerML gauge row, which is rate-matched separately):

| rung | training cases | validation geometries | constant gauge (prior) | similarity gauge | **reference** (relative frame, total measure) | reference ÷ gauge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DrivAerML, 435 cars | 435 | same family | 0.0557 | 0.0543 (-2.5%) | **0.0552 (-0.9%)** | 1.017x |
| HiLift, 4 geometries | 40 | never seen | 0.2496 | 0.2680 (+7.4%) | **0.2520 (+1.0%)** | 0.940x |
| HiLift, 21 geometries | 210 | never seen | 0.1014 | 0.1043 (+2.9%) | **0.1066 (+5.2%)** | 1.022x |
| HiLift, fixed angle | 126 | never seen | 0.0348 | 0.0398 (+14.4%) | **0.0384 (+10.3%)** | 0.965x |
| HiLift, 35 cases | 35 | recurring | 0.1377 | 0.1482 (+7.6%) | **0.1529 (+11.0%)** | 1.032x |
| HiLift, 210 cases | 210 | recurring | 0.0643 | 0.0656 (+2.0%) | **0.0716 (+11.3%)** | 1.091x |

**Reading.** Two frames sit beside the plain mean now on every rung. The
similarity gauge estimates a centroid and a scale from the sample; the
reference has no frame at all. Where validation geometries recur in
training (35 and 210 cases) the gauge is 3% and 9% more accurate than the
reference; where they are never seen (4 geometries, fixed angle) the
reference is 7% and 3.5% more accurate, and at 21 geometries and on the
cars they are within 2%. That pattern says what a frame is worth: an
estimated center and scale give every token an absolute position on *this*
wing, which is reusable information when the same wings return and a
liability that has to be unlearned when they do not. The plain mean adds
the mesher's density pattern on top, which is why it beats both on the
recurring rungs and the fixed angle and neither on the never-seen rungs.
Under @sec-principle and Peter's ruling the reference stays the reference:
the property the program is buying is generalization to geometries,
meshers and poses the training set did not contain, and on the rungs that
test new geometries the frame-free construction is the most accurate ISLA
on the ladder. The price of that choice is now stated per rung: about 11%
where validation geometries recur, 5% at 21 never-seen geometries, 10% at
the fixed angle, and nothing on the cars or at 4 geometries. **The
recurring-rung price is a pro for the frame-free construction only if the
reader's deployment is on new geometries; for a fixed fleet of shapes the
gauge's frame is worth 3–9% and the plain mean's mesher pattern more.**
Both are written into the recommendation rather than hidden.

**Follow-up launched.** The fixed angle is the unexplained rung, and it
now has the prerequisite: the full-geometry frame table for its 144 cases

(exact centroid and scale, all positional seeds kept;

Third seeds of both fixed-angle reference arms (seed 44) are launched with
it, because the pair's spreads (11% and 22%) are the widest on the ladder.

(ff_hl_mt2_frame_single_aoa_12_seed{42,43}; snapshot code_frame,

| fixed angle (18 never-seen geometries, float32) | pressure rel-L2 (seeds → mean) | vs constant-gauge prior 0.0348 | vs similarity gauge 0.0398 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FRAME-FULL, exact centroid and scale, all seeds kept** | 0.0429 / 0.0415 → **0.0422** | **+21.2%** | 1.060x |
| reference (relative frame, total-measure scale), three seeds | 0.0363 / 0.0405 / 0.0427 → **0.0398** | **+14.4%** | 1.000x |
| relative frame, reference-length scale, three seeds | 0.0389 / 0.0486 / 0.0400 → 0.0425 | +22.1% | 1.068x |
| similarity gauge (two seeds) | 0.0411 / 0.0385 → 0.0398 | +14.4% | 1 |
| constant gauge (prior, two seeds) | 0.0342 / 0.0353 → 0.0348 | 1 | 0.874x |

**Against the preregistered readings.** *Recovers* was within 3% of 0.0348;
*pays* was ≥ 7%. FRAME-FULL **pays 21%**, more than the frame-free
reference, exactly as it did at 35 cases (@sec-nb-frame-full-verdict,
14–16% against 11%). Restoring all four positional seeds on an exact,
zero-variance geometric frame does not recover the constant gauge's
fixed-angle accuracy; it costs more. The fixed-angle price is therefore not
positional information lost with the seeds. It is the plain-mean frame's
content, which on these meshes is the mesher's density pattern (0.132 body
lengths of displacement from the geometric centroid, a deterministic
function of where the mesher refined), and no consistent frame can carry it.
Both FRAME-FULL experiments now agree on the mechanism, on a recurring-
geometry rung and on a never-seen-geometry rung.

**Third seeds.** The fixed-angle rung has 18 validation cases and the widest
seed spreads on the ladder. With three seeds the reference reads
0.0398 (+14.4% against the prior), up from the two-seed 0.0384 (+10.3%),
and sits at parity with the similarity gauge (1.000x) rather than 3.5%
ahead; the reference-length arm reads 0.0425 (+22.1%), so the scale
discriminator still points the same way (the total-measure arm is
6% better than the reference-length arm; scale normalization is not a
cost here). The fixed-angle cells of the ladder are updated to the
three-seed values: reference +14.4%, reference ÷ gauge 1.000. The
reading of @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-verdict stands with that correction:
the frame-free reference is the most accurate ISLA on the 4-geometry rung,
at parity with the gauge on the fixed angle and within 2% on 21 geometries
and the cars, and 3–9% behind it where geometries recur.

**Why the fixed angle pays when other never-seen rungs do not.** What is
special about the rung is that every case shares one drive direction, so
the surface pressure varies across cases only through geometry, and the
mesher's refinement pattern, which follows the leading edges, flaps and
slats of every wing in the family, is a geometric cue that does transfer
across unseen wings of the same family at the same angle; on the
varied-angle never-seen rungs the harder part of the task is the angle,
where that cue does not help. This is stated as the reading consistent
with all six rungs and both FRAME-FULL results, not as a tested claim.
What the program will not do with it is put the mesher's pattern back into
the reference: it is the input that collapses 10–15x when the sampler
changes (@sec-nb-wave4-fixed-angle-bench) and the price of leaving it is
now stated on every rung.

## 2026-09-13 — Preregistered: RELINT, the interior query-token configuration on the reference frame (one flagship frame for surface and interior) {#sec-nb-relint-prereg}

*Setting.* ISLA's surface reference configuration is the relative frame
with the total-measure scale (@sec-nb-frame-full-verdict): no centroid
anywhere in the forward pass, positions entering only as differences against
slice anchors, the length unit taken from the total quadrature measure. The
interior configuration that leads GeoTransolver-volume on velocity (query
tokens with the signed distance, `v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed42/43`) was trained
before that decision and stands on the similarity gauge, a frame estimated
from the sample. Peter's ruling of 2026-09-13: one flagship configuration;
the interior must share the reference frame.

*What is tested.* Whether the interior query-token configuration keeps its
standing when the similarity gauge is replaced by the relative frame with the
total-measure scale and nothing else changes. Two seeds
(`v0_isla_qtsdfval_relint_seed42/43`, launcher `v0/v0_relint_aga.sbatch`),
the frozen interior protocol of the reference lanes (500 epochs, lr 1e-3,
10,000 boundary cells and 10,000 interior points, bf16, no augmentation,
SDF-gradient query normals, SDF query scalar), code snapshot `code_relint`
taken from the repository head of 2026-09-13 (which also carries the
keyword-only API and the new defaults; the frame is passed explicitly). The
contracts of the combination were checked before launch on a random cloud
in float64: translation invariance without centering, rotation covariance,
and invariance to a joint geometric rescale (points by $k$, areas by $k^2$,
query scalars by $k$) all hold to $10^{-15}$.

*Bars (float32, guarded snapshot, two-seed means, the 48 DrivAerML
validation cars at the training query count of 10,000; three-seed reference
0.0553 / 0.0804 / 0.1109 for pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity).*
Supported, and the interior flagship moves to the reference frame, if every
field is within 3% of the similarity-gauge reference; "pays" if any field
is worse by more than 3% and none by more than 10%, in which case the
interior flagship still moves (the ruling is one configuration) and the
price is stated per field; "fails" if any field is worse by more than 10%,
which reopens the question of what the interior frame should be. Secondary,
not a bar: the sample-frame density probe of the surface tokens, expected
to be consistent as for the surface reference. Readings written in
advance: the surface reference paid nothing on DrivAerML, and the interior
queries consume positions only through anchor differences and the signed
distance, so the prediction is "supported". Owner: this session.

## 2026-09-13 — RELINT first attempt void: the interior configuration's boundary measure is not Horvitz–Thompson corrected, so the total-measure length unit was 200x too small and the relative-frame model never learned {#sec-nb-relint-void}

*What happened.* The two RELINT lanes (@sec-nb-relint-prereg) trained to
completion and evaluated cleanly (job 739032, 48 cars each, zero skipped
loads), and the result was not a frame price but a non-result: relative L2
of 0.75 for pressure, 0.75 for velocity and 1.00 for eddy viscosity against
the similarity-gauge reference's 0.055, 0.080 and 0.111, the level of
predicting the field mean. The training log shows why the evaluation is
not the place to look: the training loss sat at 0.073 from the first epoch
to the last (0.079 at epoch 0, 0.073 at 250 and 499), while the reference
lanes fell from 0.065 to 0.0009 over the same schedule. The model did not
learn, from the start.

*Diagnosis.* Local fit tests on a synthetic body with interior queries rule
out the combination itself: with query tokens, the signed-distance scalar
and the relative frame with the total-measure scale, the model fits a
smooth interior field as well as the similarity-gauge model in float32
and under bfloat16 autocast, with the geometry at the origin or shifted 20
body lengths away, and with the measure weights scaled down by 10,000
(length unit 0.087, coordinates up to about 50 length units). The cause is
in the data pipeline, and it is a violation of the rule the total-measure
scale was built on. The interior configuration feeds ISLA the boundary's
raw `cell_areas` after the reader has subsampled the vehicle surface to
about 365 cells (the token count the interior lanes have always had,
@sec-interior-task). Those areas are not Horvitz–Thompson corrected: their
sum is the area of the 365 kept cells, not of the car. On a saved
evaluation case the sum is $3\times10^{-5}$ in the pipeline's
nondimensional units, so the length unit $L=(\sum_i w_i)^{1/2}$ is 0.0055,
the car spans about 100 length units and the interior queries reach 2,100,
with a median of 59. The similarity gauge, which the interior reference
uses, normalizes by an RMS radius that is a *normalized* average and does
not care about the sum, which is why it never noticed. Under bfloat16
autocast the anchor positions are formed by a half-precision contraction,
so at coordinates of order 100 to 2,000 the anchor and the point-to-anchor
differences carry rounding of order 1 to 16 length units, larger than the
geometry, and every relational invariant is noise. The surface reference
lanes never met this because the surface pipeline feeds the
importance-corrected `_target_quadrature_measure`, whose sum is the surface
area.

*Reading.* The preregistered "fails" band is not reached on its own terms:
the arm did not test the frame, it tested an uncorrected measure, and the
verdict on the interior frame is void, not negative. The lesson is the one
already written in @sec-isla-forward and now enforced: the total-measure
scale requires measure weights whose sum is the integral of the geometry,
which means Horvitz–Thompson-corrected weights on every subsampled
boundary. The interior pipeline needs that correction before the relative
frame can be trained on it; the constant-gauge and similarity-gauge
configurations were insensitive to the omission, which is itself a mark
against them as instruments.

*What changes.* The RELINT lanes are relaunched once the interior pipeline
supplies a corrected boundary measure (the full vehicle geometry is present
in the pipeline before the boundary is dropped, so the correction is the
ratio of the full area to the subsample's area, an integral of the
geometry and not a sample statistic). The two void checkpoints are kept
under their run ids as the record of the defect. The preregistration's
bars stand unchanged for the relaunch. Owner: this session.

## 2026-09-13 — RELINT preregistration amended for the relaunch: corrected boundary measure, 10,000-cell boundary, reference re-based on the 10,000-cell interior lanes {#sec-nb-relint-amend}

The relaunch (`v0_isla_qtsdfval_relint2_seed42/43`, launcher
`v0/v0_relint2_aga.sbatch`, recipe copy `recipe_relint`, snapshot
`code_relint`) changes exactly what @sec-nb-relint-void identified and
nothing else. The boundary is subsampled by cells with the reader's
Horvitz–Thompson bookkeeping (the reader settings of the 10,000-cell
interior lanes, `drivaer_ml_volume_mt10k`), and a new recipe transform,
`ComposeQuadratureMeasure`, writes the corrected cell measure
`cell_areas × _measure_weights` to `cell_data.quadrature_measure`, whose
sum is the surface area; the model reads that field as its measure weights
(`forward_kwargs.measure_weights=boundaries.vehicle.cell_data.quadrature_measure`).
Two tests pin the transform: the corrected sum recovers the full area of a
1-in-4 subsample, and an unsubsampled mesh is returned with its plain
areas. Because the boundary now carries 10,000 cells, the comparison
reference is the 10,000-cell similarity-gauge interior lanes rather than
the 365-cell ones: `v0_isla_qtsdf_surf10k_seed42/43`, float32 0.0572 /
0.0848 / 0.1187 for pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity
(`results/udrv_int_reduction_2026-09-09.json`; the 365-cell reference is
0.0553 / 0.0804 / 0.1109, and the book records that the two agree within
their seed spread on pressure and velocity, @sec-interior-task). The bars
are unchanged in form: supported within 3% of that reference on every
field; pays between 3% and 10%; fails beyond 10%. Owner: this session.

## 2026-09-13 — Kernel study: ISLA's step is 1.05x GeoTransolver's on the recipe's compiled path (0.86x without recompute), the 3.7x was a retired kernel measured eager; an exact fused geometry kernel gives parity at 40k tokens {#sec-nb-kernel-study}

**Setting.** ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention) is a soft-slice transformer for surface
fields: 10,000 surface points are routed to 256 slices by a softmax over points, slice
states are quadrature-weighted means, and each point reads the slices back weighted by
a softmax over slices. What makes it different from Transolver-style slicing is the
geometry region in every layer: for every point-slice pair it evaluates six relational
invariants of the point and the slice anchor (distance, its log, and four dot products
of unit vectors), feeds them to a 6->1 Linear that biases the routing, and pools them
back to the point with the routing weights. That is a (batch x points x slices x 6)
tensor per layer -- 15 M numbers at 10k tokens, 61 M at 40k -- and the book's cost
section says the step is 3.7x slower than GeoTransolver's (`matched_memory_isla_gt_2026-09-08.json`).

**Question.** Where does the time and memory of one training step (forward, backward,
AdamW) actually go, and which implementation options -- fusion, recompute, compile
modes, a custom kernel -- shorten it while computing exactly the same function?
Options were admitted only if they reproduce the eager reference forward to 1e-6
relative and the parameter gradients to 1e-5 in fp32 and agree in float64 (same
arithmetic, different order).

**Instruments.** One NVIDIA GB300 on AGA (driver 580.167.08, torch 2.12.0+cu130), the
GPU the recipe trains on and the book's number was measured on; the reference
configuration (`isla_surface_reference.yaml`, hidden 192, 12 layers, 256 slices,
`geo_checkpoint: true`) on synthetic inputs; step time = median of 10 cuda-synchronized
steps after 3 warm-ups; peak = `max_memory_allocated`. An analytic roofline (FLOPs and
bytes per stage against measured peaks: 1925 TFLOP/s bf16, 7135 GB/s), torch.profiler
traces with every kernel attributed to its launching operator and phase, allocation
snapshots at the peak, and a numerics gate against the eager reference in fp32 and
float64. Artifacts in `results/kernel_study_2026-09-13/` (jobs 736338, 736352, 738400);
tables in `TABLES.md`; this entry is the report. An RTX 4090 Laptop was used for the first
pass; its numbers are secondary and labeled.

**What was seen.**

1. *The 3.7x reproduces and is a kernel, not the architecture.* Eager, with the
   middle-dimension point softmax that was replaced on 2026-09-10, ISLA takes 244.7 ms
   against GeoTransolver's 67.8 ms at 10k tokens (3.61x). With the row-parallel softmax
   the same eager step is 86.7 ms (1.28x), or 67.0 ms (0.99x) without `geo_checkpoint`.
   The recipe compiles both models (`compile: true`): compiled, ISLA is 47.3 ms with
   `geo_checkpoint` (1.05x GeoTransolver's 45.2 ms) or 39.0 ms without (0.86x), at 1.30
   or 1.94 GiB peak against GeoTransolver's 2.70. At 40k tokens the original-softmax
   eager step is 1284 ms; the reference eager 135 ms; compiled 108-119 ms; GeoTransolver
   compiled 53 ms.

2. *The step is far from any roofline, for two different reasons at two sizes.* The
   analytic step at 10k tokens is 404 GFLOP and 62 GB of traffic as eager PyTorch
   executes it (8.8 ms at the GB300's bandwidth), or 15 GB if every stage were fused
   (2.1 ms). The eager reference runs 33.8 ms of kernels inside a 91 ms step -- 3,224
   kernel launches, so 63% of the wall time is host-side launch and autograd overhead
   on the Grace CPU. At 40k the kernels fill the step (130.6 of 135 ms) and the
   invariants stage alone takes 71 ms against a 21 ms roofline for its eager traffic:
   it carries 61% of all bytes, and its fused-traffic roofline is 11x smaller. Every
   stage but the point MLP is memory-bound; the MLP reaches 10.7% of the bf16 FLOP peak.

3. *`torch.compile` fuses the elementwise chain but keeps the tensor, and its default
   backward configuration is poor.* Inductor still materializes the (B,N,S,6)
   invariants twice per layer (fp32, and a bf16 copy for the GEMM); one generated
   reduction kernel for the geometry backward is 13.4 of the 20.0 ms of backward
   kernels at 10k and 56 of 82 ms at 40k. `mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"` fixes
   the configuration: 10k 39.0 -> 33.3 ms; 40k 108 -> 41 ms; 40k batch 2 177 -> 67 ms.
   `mode="reduce-overhead"` (CUDA graphs) removes the launch-bound regime: 26.0 ms at
   10k, 0.58x of default-compiled GeoTransolver, at the cost of static shapes and
   activation memory that `max_memory_allocated` cannot see (2.02 GiB reserved).

4. *A fused Triton kernel for the geometry region is exact and removes the tensor.*
   `geo_kernel="fused"` (opt-in; `physicsnemo/experimental/nn/isla/geo_kernel.py`)
   evaluates invariants, routing bias, slice softmax and pooling on register tiles of
   8 points x 256 slices and never writes a (B,N,S,.) intermediate; the backward
   recomputes the tile. Region-level, one layer at 10k tokens: eager 0.70 / 1.20 ms
   (forward / backward), Inductor 0.43 / 2.09, fused 0.23 / 0.55; at 40k: 2.87 / 3.73,
   0.73 / 11.67, 0.20 / 0.77; region memory 0.265 / 0.125 / 0.034 GiB. Whole step,
   compiled: 45.3 ms at 10k (kernel time 8.8 ms in a 41.5 ms wall, so launch-bound; no
   wall-time gain over 39.0) and 52.1 ms at 40k (vs 108), at 1.27 / 4.50 GiB (vs 1.94 /
   7.13); at 40k batch 2, 54.7 ms and 8.82 GiB against GeoTransolver's 51.6 ms and
   19.85 GiB. Numerics: output 5.4e-7 relative to the eager reference (the reference's
   own fp32-vs-fp64 floor is 6.2e-7), gradient 1.1e-7, float64 agreement 1e-15; 12 new
   tests, 99 existing ISLA tests pass; compiles with zero graph breaks.

5. *Memory map.* At the eager peak (1.35 GiB at 10k) the largest live blocks are the
   MLP activations (0.48 GiB), the transposed copies the fast point softmax makes
   (0.22), and the assign logits (0.19); with `geo_checkpoint` off under compile the
   kept (B,N,S,6) invariants and (B,N,S,3) relative vectors are 0.71 of 1.76 GiB
   (2.63 of 6.96 at 40k). `geo_checkpoint` under compile buys 0.64 GiB for +21% time at
   10k; the fused kernel makes it moot.

**Why it matters.** The cost section's premise -- that ISLA's geometry makes it
several times more expensive than GeoTransolver -- does not hold on the path the
recipe runs: at 10k tokens the two are within 5-14% of each other in step time, and
ISLA uses half the memory. The remaining cost is not arithmetic (the step is 400
GFLOP on a 2 PFLOP/s part) but memory traffic of one stage and host launch overhead,
both of which are implementation choices with exact-arithmetic remedies. At the token
counts where the traffic dominates (40k and above) the fused kernel and Inductor's
autotuned mode each halve the step; combined they should do better, and none of them
changes a single output beyond fp32 roundoff.

**What is next.** (a) Measure fused + `max-autotune` and fused + `reduce-overhead`
(the profiles predict the gains add: 8.8 ms of kernels in a 41.5 ms wall at 10k).
(b) Expose `compile_mode` in the recipe and measure GeoTransolver under the same modes
so the anchor column is like-for-like. (c) One training run with `geo_kernel="fused"`
for neutrality (its bf16 backward accumulates in fp32 where eager's rounds to bf16 --
more precise, not identical) before any default changes. (d) Correct the book's cost
section from the reconciliation table in `TABLES.md`, on the GB300 numbers (done 2026-09-14, @sec-using-cost).

*Provenance.* Study run by a delegated engineering agent in an isolated worktree on
2026-09-13 at Peter's request; merged by the coordinating session on 2026-09-14 with
the fused kernel left opt-in and the class defaults unchanged. Every number above is in
the artifact JSONs of `results/kernel_study_2026-09-13/` with GPU, driver, torch version
and load snapshot recorded.

## 2026-09-14 — Verdict, RELINT2: the interior query-token configuration on the reference frame matches the similarity gauge on pressure and velocity and is 12% better on eddy viscosity; the interior flagship moves to the reference frame at no price {#sec-nb-relint-verdict}

*Setting.* After the void first attempt (@sec-nb-relint-void), the relaunch
(@sec-nb-relint-amend) trained the interior query-token configuration with
the signed-distance scalar on the frame-free reference frame (relative frame,
total-measure scale) with a Horvitz–Thompson-corrected boundary measure on a
10,000-cell boundary subsample, two seeds
(`v0_isla_qtsdfval_relint2_seed42/43`), otherwise the frozen interior
protocol. The training loss tracked the 10,000-cell similarity-gauge
reference epoch for epoch (0.0077 against 0.0079 at epoch 10; final
validation loss 0.0010 and 0.0011 against 0.0011).

*Instruments.* Float32 evaluation under the same snapshot and dataset
variant on the 48 DrivAerML validation cars at the training query count of
10,000 (job 742273; 48 cases per seed after deduplication; zero skipped
loads), reduced as two-seed means with paired per-case comparisons against
the 10,000-cell similarity-gauge lanes (`v0_isla_qtsdf_surf10k_seed42/43`),
the 365-cell three-seed reference and unit-drive GeoTransolver-volume.
Artifact: `results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json`.

*What we saw.* **Pressure 0.0550 against the reference's 0.0550 (1.000x),
velocity 0.0782 against 0.0789 (0.990x), eddy viscosity 0.1005 against
0.1142 (0.880x), the last lower on 40 of 48 cars.** Every field is inside
the 3% bar, and eddy viscosity is 12% better. Against the 365-cell
three-seed reference the ratios are 0.995 / 0.977 / 0.909. Against
unit-drive GeoTransolver-volume the standings are pressure 0.933x
(GeoTransolver-volume lower on 43 of 48), velocity 1.369x (ISLA lower on 48
of 48) and eddy viscosity 0.874x (GeoTransolver-volume lower on 22 of 48,
so the two are at parity per case while the mean favors GeoTransolver):
the velocity lead is unchanged, the pressure deficit is unchanged at 7%,
and the eddy-viscosity deficit shrinks from 27% to 14%.

*Reading.* Supported, and the ruling of one flagship configuration is met:
the interior configuration stands on the same frame as the surface
reference, with no centroid, no sample statistic and no per-dataset length
anywhere. The eddy-viscosity gain is not separately attributed: the
relaunch changed both the frame and the boundary measure (raw subsample
areas to the corrected quadrature), and the similarity gauge is
insensitive to the measure's sum while the total-measure scale depends on
it, so the two cannot be separated without a corrected-measure gauge lane;
that lane is not scheduled, since the gauge is not a candidate for the
reference. What the result does establish is that the frame-free
construction costs nothing on the interior and that the earlier interior
numbers, produced under the similarity gauge, are the prior configuration's
record in the same sense as the constant-gauge surface numbers.

*What changes.* The interior reference configuration is the relative frame
with the total-measure scale and the corrected boundary measure; the recipe
gains a reference interior config and the corrected-measure dataset
variant; chapters 3, 8 and 12 and the index carry the new interior
standings; the RELINT node is DONE. Owner: this session.

## 2026-09-14 — Global inputs: ISLA now takes zero or more global vector inputs and zero or more global scalar inputs; "drive" retired {#sec-nb-global-inputs}

**Setting.** ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention) is the equivariant slice
transformer this book develops as a surrogate for steady boundary-value
problems. Until today its forward pass took exactly one required global
unit vector, called the *drive*, and every dataset in this book supplied
the freestream direction for it. Peter's ruling of 2026-09-14: the
architecture targets steady PDEs in general, where the problem-level
data are zero or more global vectors (a freestream, a gravity or an
applied-field direction; none in steady conduction with pinned boundary
values) and zero or more global scalars (a thermal or momentum
diffusivity, an isotropic Young's modulus, a Reynolds number). The term
"drive" is retired: it locks the reader into a single vector and is not
familiar to newcomers. The vocabulary is now *global inputs*, *global
vector input(s)* and *global scalar input(s)*.

**What changed in the code.** The constructor gained `n_global_vectors`
(default 1) and `n_global_scalars` (default 0); the forward pass takes
`global_vectors` of shape (batch, $K$, 3) and `global_scalars` of shape
(batch, $S$) as keyword arguments, and the `drive` argument is gone. Each
global vector enters as a unit direction: one seed term
$\hat n_i\cdot\hat g_k$ per token and per vector (the relative-frame seed is
exactly these $K$ terms; with $K = 0$ and no other seed channel every
token starts from one learned embedding and all separation comes from the
relational anchors), one direction cosine $\hat\rho_{is}\cdot\hat g_k$ per
point-anchor pair (the relational invariants are $5 + K$ wide, plus $1 + K$
in the centered variant), and the vector head's basis is
$\{\hat g_1,\dots,\hat g_K, \hat n, \hat u\}$ with the spherical complements
of $(\hat u,\hat n)$ and of each $(\hat u,\hat g_k)$, $4 + 3K$ vectors. Global
scalars are appended to every token's seed features, boundary, support,
interacting-query and passive-query tokens alike, so they condition every
token embedding; as invariants they change no covariance contract. The
old degree-one rule, output proportional to the vector's magnitude, is
removed: a magnitude with physical content is a scalar input.

**Compatibility, verified.** With $K = 1$ and $S = 0$ the feature orderings
reproduce the former model's exactly, so every saved checkpoint keeps its
parameter layout. The pre-change file was loaded alongside the new one
with identical weights on fourteen configurations (reference; centered;
centered with local features; raw seeds; the true5 and true7 bases;
second-moment channel; sparse routing; passive decode; interacting query
tokens with the neighbor and density channels; odd head; parity fix;
similarity gauge; support tokens) and the outputs are **bitwise identical**
for unit vectors (script `equiv_check.py` in the session's job directory;
with a non-unit vector the two differ by the retired magnitude factor
only). One implementation detail mattered: the new dot products are
broadcast multiply-and-sum, not `einsum`, because autocast runs `einsum`
in bfloat16 and the geometry must stay in the input precision. The fused
Triton kernel, `odd_head`, `parity_fix`, `latent_volume_tokens` and
`wake_tokens` are written for one vector and refuse other counts at
construction.

**Tests.** The three degree-one tests became magnitude-invariance tests.
A new file, `test_isla_global_inputs.py`, adds fifteen tests: SE(3)
covariance for $K = 0$ and $K = 2$ in both frames, on the passive and
interacting query paths too; measure-scale invariance where the length
unit is constant; magnitude invariance of every vector; scalar inputs that
change the output, reach the query side and preserve every contract; the
one-vector parameter layout (seed 1/5, geometry 6/8, basis 7/5/7); the
legacy (3,), (B, 3) and (B, 1, 3) layouts; and the one-vector-only options
refusing $K \ne 1$. ISLA suites: 136 passed, 8 skipped (GPU-only kernel
tests run and pass on this machine's GPU); recipe suite: 260 passed. The
recipe's five ISLA configurations now map `global_vectors` to the unit
freestream direction.

**What is not done.** No non-aerodynamic problem has been trained; a
Laplace or conduction case with $K = 0$ and one scalar parameter is the
open acceptance item for the generalization (@sec-future). The book's
terminology was overhauled in the same pass (@sec-isla, @sec-problem):
"unit-direction baselines" replaces the old protocol label, the symbol for
the global vector inputs is $\hat g_k$, and the relational invariants are
now written $\xi_{is}$ to avoid the clash.

## 2026-09-14 — Preregistration, GLOBIN-ACCEPT: ISLA on a screened-Poisson family with no global direction and one scalar parameter {#sec-nb-globin-accept-prereg}

**Setting.** ISLA now accepts zero or more global vector inputs and zero or
more global scalar inputs (@sec-nb-global-inputs), but every problem it
has been trained on is external aerodynamics with one global vector and no
scalar. The generalization is untested on the problems it was made for.
Writing this test also exposed a gap: the per-cell boundary-data channel
(`boundary_scalars`, the Dirichlet trace) was refused on all three interior
paths, so a boundary-value problem with prescribed boundary values could
not be posed to the interior. That is fixed in the same commit: tokens
that are not boundary cells carry zeros in the channel, and a new contract
test covers the three paths.

**Problem.** The screened Poisson equation $\nabla^2 u - \kappa^2 u = 0$
inside a random star-shaped closed surface in three dimensions (a unit
sphere perturbed by real spherical harmonics up to order three, amplitude
about 0.1), with Dirichlet data $u$ on the boundary and the screening
parameter $\kappa \in [0, 3]$; $\kappa = 0$ is Laplace's equation, steady
conduction with pinned boundary temperatures. Exact solutions are sums of
six fundamental solutions $e^{-\kappa|x-y|}/|x-y|$ with sources outside the
body, so the interior labels are exact and every case is a new geometry, a
new trace and a new $\kappa$. Inputs: 1,024 boundary points with unit normals
and Horvitz–Thompson area weights, the trace as the one boundary scalar,
$\kappa$ as the one global scalar input, no global vector input. Output: $u$
at 256 volume-uniform interior queries through the interacting query-token
path (the query normal is the level-set gradient of the surface function).
Each case is normalized by the boundary RMS of its trace, which the linear
PDE permits.

**Arms and instruments.** (A) ISLA, `n_global_vectors=0`,
`n_global_scalars=1`, `n_boundary_scalars=1`, width 128, six layers, 64
slices, query tokens with `source_total` mass. (B) The same model with
$\kappa$ withheld (`n_global_scalars=0`). Trivial predictors: the
measure-weighted boundary mean of the trace and the nearest boundary value.
Two seeds per arm, 3,000 steps of eight fresh cases each (infinite data),
AdamW with a one-cycle schedule, bfloat16 autocast in training, float32
evaluation. Test sets of 64 held-out cases: T0 with $\kappa \in [0, 3]$; T1
with $\kappa \in [3, 4]$, parameter extrapolation, reported and not part of
the bar. Metric: per-case relative $L^2$ over the queries, mean over cases.
Hardware: the local RTX 4090 laptop GPU. Script:
`research/global_inputs_acceptance/screened_poisson_acceptance.py`; artifact
`results/global_inputs_acceptance_screened_poisson_2026-09-14.json`.

**Predictions and bars, written before the run.**

- **Acceptance.** Arm A reaches a T0 mean relative $L^2$ of **at most
  0.10** on both seeds. The boundary-mean predictor is expected near 0.5
  and the nearest-value predictor near 0.3 to 0.5; a model that does not
  beat both by at least 3x has not learned the boundary-to-interior map.
  Failing this bar falsifies the claim that the generalized inputs make
  ISLA usable, as built, on a non-aerodynamic boundary-value problem.
- **The scalar input matters.** Arm B is **at least 1.5x worse** than arm
  A on T0 (seed means). Screening at $\kappa = 3$ across a body of
  diameter about two changes the interior solution by a factor of order
  $e^{-3}$ relative to $\kappa = 0$, and the trace alone does not identify
  $\kappa$ (different source layouts and screenings give the same trace).
  If B matches A, the scalar reaches the model but is not needed here, and
  the family was too easy to discriminate conditioning; the seed-append
  conditioning would then be tested on a family where it must matter.
- **Extrapolation (reported only).** T1 will be worse than T0 for both
  arms; no bar.

**What the result cannot say.** This is an acceptance test of the input
interface on a smooth, source-generated family, not a benchmark against a
classical solver or another architecture; a boundary-element method solves
this family exactly. It says whether the zero-vector, one-scalar,
Dirichlet-data configuration trains and generalizes across geometries and
parameters at all.

## 2026-09-14 — Verdict, GLOBIN-ACCEPT at 3,000 steps: 5–7x better than the trivial predictors, the 0.10 bar missed by one seed at 0.109, the scalar input helps by 1.2x not 1.5x {#sec-nb-globin-accept-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistration of @sec-nb-globin-accept-prereg: ISLA with
no global vector input and one global scalar input ($\kappa$) predicting the
interior solution of the screened Poisson equation inside random
star-shaped bodies from the Dirichlet trace, against the same model with
$\kappa$ withheld and two trivial predictors. Two seeds per arm, 3,000
steps of eight fresh cases, float32 evaluation on 64 held-out cases per
set. Artifact:
`results/global_inputs_acceptance_screened_poisson_2026-09-14.json`
(commit bad7c142, RTX 4090 laptop GPU, 190–227 s per training run,
1.91M parameters).

**What we saw** (per-case relative $L^2$ over the interior queries, mean
over cases; T0 is $\kappa \in [0,3]$, T1 is $\kappa \in [3,4]$):

| Arm | T0 seed 0 | T0 seed 1 | T1 seed 0 | T1 seed 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, $\kappa$ as global scalar input | 0.109 | 0.099 | 0.200 | 0.181 |
| ISLA, $\kappa$ withheld | 0.119 | 0.129 | 0.235 | 0.237 |
| Nearest boundary value | 0.555 | | 1.164 | |
| Boundary mean of the trace | 0.749 | | 0.985 | |

**Against the bars.** The acceptance bar (T0 at most 0.10 on both seeds)
is **missed by one seed**, 0.109 against 0.099; the seed mean is 0.104. The
3x margin over both trivial predictors is met with room: 5.3x over the
nearest boundary value and 7.2x over the boundary mean. The
scalar-conditioning prediction (the $\kappa$-blind arm at least 1.5x
worse) is **falsified**: the blind arm is worse in all four comparisons
(both seeds, both sets), by 1.19x on T0 and 1.24x on T1, not 1.5x. The
scalar input is used and helps consistently; it is not decisive on this
family because the trace largely identifies $\kappa$: six sources at radii
1.8 to 2.8 imprint a decay pattern on the boundary from which the screening
can be read, as the preregistration's escape clause anticipated.
Extrapolation to $\kappa \in [3,4]$ costs both arms about 1.8x, and the
trivial predictors are useless there (relative error near or above one).

**Why it matters.** The zero-vector, one-scalar, Dirichlet-data
configuration trains and generalizes across geometries, traces and the
parameter on a problem that has nothing to do with aerodynamics, through
the same code path the aerodynamic recipe uses; the boundary-data channel
that this test forced open is the piece that makes a boundary-value problem
posable at all. The bar was missed by 9% on one seed with the training
loss still falling (0.30 at step 400, 0.11 at step 3,000), which says the
budget, not the architecture, set the number; the bar is not moved, the
result stands as a narrow miss, and the budget question is answered by a
separate pre-registered extension below.

**Preregistered extension (written before its run).** The same script with
9,000 steps per run (three times the budget), otherwise unchanged; artifact
`results/global_inputs_acceptance_screened_poisson_9000steps_2026-09-14.json`.
Prediction: the scalar arm reaches T0 at most 0.10 on both seeds (if it
does not, the 10% floor is a property of this model size on this family,
not of the budget), and the blind arm stays worse by a factor between 1.1
and 1.3 (if the gap closes to parity the scalar is redundant here; if it
widens past 1.5x the earlier ratio was a budget artifact).

## 2026-09-14 — Verdict, GLOBIN-ACCEPT extension at 9,000 steps: 0.043 and 0.045, the acceptance bar met on both seeds; the scalar input's advantage widened to 1.4x {#sec-nb-globin-accept-extension-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistered extension of @sec-nb-globin-accept-verdict:
the same screened-Poisson acceptance experiment (no global vector input,
$\kappa$ as the one global scalar input, the Dirichlet trace as the boundary
scalar, random star-shaped bodies, exact interior labels) at three times
the training budget, 9,000 steps of eight fresh cases per run. Artifact:
`results/global_inputs_acceptance_screened_poisson_9000steps_2026-09-14.json`
(commit 2bbdb340, RTX 4090 laptop GPU, 582–663 s per run).

**What we saw** (per-case relative $L^2$ over the interior queries, mean
over 64 held-out cases):

| Arm | T0 seed 0 | T0 seed 1 | T1 seed 0 | T1 seed 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, $\kappa$ as global scalar input | 0.043 | 0.045 | 0.086 | 0.083 |
| ISLA, $\kappa$ withheld | 0.064 | 0.059 | 0.143 | 0.125 |

**Against the bars.** The acceptance bar (T0 at most 0.10 on both seeds) is
**met with a factor of two to spare**: 0.043 and 0.045, 13x better than
the nearest-boundary-value predictor (0.555) and 17x better than the
boundary mean (0.749). The 3,000-step miss was the budget, as the falling
loss curve had suggested. The conditioning prediction (the blind arm worse
by 1.1x to 1.3x) is **missed on the high side**: the blind arm is worse by
1.41x on T0 and 1.58x under extrapolation to $\kappa \in [3, 4]$, and the
gap widened from 1.19x at 3,000 steps rather than closing. The scalar
input is used, it helps on every seed and set, and its value grows as the
model gets better at the rest of the problem; on this family the trace
still carries most of the information about $\kappa$, so the blind model
is not helpless, which is why neither the 1.5x prediction of the first
run nor the 1.1 to 1.3x band of the second was right.

**Why it matters.** This closes the acceptance item that the global-inputs
generalization opened (@sec-nb-global-inputs): the configuration with no
global direction, one PDE parameter and prescribed boundary values trains
and generalizes across geometries, traces and the parameter on a problem
outside aerodynamics, through the recipe's code path, at 4% relative
interior error with a 1.9M-parameter model and eleven minutes of laptop
GPU time per run. It is an acceptance test, not a benchmark: a
boundary-element method solves this family exactly, and no other
architecture was run.

**What's next.** Two candidates, neither started: a family in which the
scalar is *not* identifiable from the trace, so scalar conditioning is
decisive and its mechanism (seed append) can be stressed against a FiLM
alternative; and a two-vector problem (a freestream and a gravity
direction, buoyant flow) once a dataset exists.

## 2026-09-14 — Preregistration, GLOBIN-DISCRIM: a family where the scalar cannot be read from the trace, so scalar conditioning must be decisive {#sec-nb-globin-discrim-prereg}

**Setting.** On the source-generated screened-Poisson family
(@sec-nb-globin-accept-extension-verdict) the model without the scalar
input was only 1.4x worse than the model with it, because the boundary
trace carries most of the information about the screening parameter. That
result says the scalar input is used; it cannot say whether the way it
enters, appended to every token's seed features, is adequate when the
scalar is the only route to the answer. This entry preregisters the
discriminating family.

**Problem.** The same equation, $\nabla^2 u - \kappa^2 u = 0$, inside a
sphere of radius $R \in [0.8, 1.2]$, with the Dirichlet trace prescribed
directly as a random combination of real spherical harmonics up to order
three (coefficients decaying with degree, RMS normalized to one). The exact
interior solution separates: each harmonic of degree $l$ is carried inward
by the ratio $i_l(\kappa r)/i_l(\kappa R)$ of modified spherical Bessel
functions, which is $(r/R)^l$ at $\kappa = 0$ and decays sharply toward the
center as $\kappa$ grows. **The trace is independent of $\kappa$ by
construction**; the interior is not. $\kappa \in [0, 6]$ in training and
T0, $[6, 7]$ in T1. The geometry is fixed to a sphere on purpose: the
question is conditioning, and nothing else should vary. Everything else
follows the acceptance experiment: 1,024 boundary points, 256 volume-uniform
queries, query tokens, width 128, six layers, 64 slices, 6,000 steps of
eight fresh cases, two seeds, float32 evaluation on 64 held-out cases.
Script: the same file with `--family sphere_bessel`; artifact
`results/global_inputs_discrim_sphere_bessel_2026-09-14.json`.

**Predictions and bars, written before the run.**

- **The scalar arm solves it.** T0 mean relative $L^2$ at most 0.10 on
  both seeds. Failing this says the seed-append route is too weak to carry
  a decisive scalar through the slice attention, and a stronger
  conditioning (a FiLM modulation of the slice states, or the scalar in
  the routing bias) becomes the next engineering item.
- **The blind arm cannot.** The $\kappa$-withheld arm is **at least 2x
  worse** than the scalar arm on T0 (seed means). Its floor is the error of
  the $\kappa$-averaged interior against the true one; over $\kappa \in
  [0, 6]$ the degree-zero mode alone ranges from constant to $\sinh(\kappa
  r)/(\ldots)$-shaped decay, so the average is far from every member. If
  the blind arm is within 2x, the trace is not as $\kappa$-independent as
  the construction claims (a bug in the generator), or the queries do not
  reach the region where screening matters; either way the test would be
  void, not a result.
- **Extrapolation** to $\kappa \in [6, 7]$ is reported without a bar.

## 2026-09-14 — Verdict, GLOBIN-DISCRIM: with the trace blind to the parameter, the scalar input carries the answer (0.077 / 0.070) and the blind arm is 3.8x worse {#sec-nb-globin-discrim-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistration of @sec-nb-globin-discrim-prereg: the
screened Poisson equation inside a sphere with a prescribed Dirichlet trace
that is independent of the screening parameter $\kappa \in [0, 6]$ by
construction, so the interior solution can be predicted only if $\kappa$
reaches the model through its global scalar input. Two arms (the scalar
given; the scalar withheld), two seeds, 6,000 steps of eight fresh cases,
float32 evaluation on 64 held-out cases per set. Before the run the
generator was checked: the finite-difference PDE residual is $10^{-6}$ of
the source term, the $\kappa = 0$ limit reproduces the power law $(r/R)^l$,
and the same generator seed gives identical traces and interiors that
differ by 72% between $\kappa = 0$ and $\kappa = 6$. Artifact:
`results/global_inputs_discrim_sphere_bessel_2026-09-14.json` (commit
8ab498d2, RTX 4090 laptop GPU, 343–361 s per run).

**What we saw** (per-case relative $L^2$ over the interior queries, mean
over cases; T0 is $\kappa \in [0, 6]$, T1 is $\kappa \in [6, 7]$):

| Arm | T0 seed 0 | T0 seed 1 | T1 seed 0 | T1 seed 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, $\kappa$ as global scalar input | 0.077 | 0.070 | 0.119 | 0.110 |
| ISLA, $\kappa$ withheld | 0.273 | 0.286 | 0.563 | 0.572 |
| Boundary mean of the trace | 0.936 | | 1.512 | |
| Nearest boundary value | 1.024 | | 2.019 | |

**Against the bars.** Both preregistered predictions hold. The scalar arm
is under the 0.10 bar on both seeds (0.077 and 0.070), so the seed-append
route is strong enough to carry a decisive scalar through the slice
attention; no stronger conditioning is called for by this test. The blind
arm is **3.8x worse** on T0 (bar: at least 2x) and 5.0x worse under
extrapolation, where it reaches 0.57, close to predicting nothing. This is
the structural result the source family could not give: there the trace
leaked the parameter and the blind arm trailed by 1.4x; here the leak is
closed and the blind arm collapses to the parameter-averaged interior. The
trivial predictors are useless on this family (relative error near one)
because the prescribed traces have little mean and the interior decays
away from the boundary.

**Why it matters.** Together with @sec-nb-globin-accept-extension-verdict
this closes the question the global-inputs generalization opened: a
scalar PDE parameter supplied as a global scalar input is consumed, is
decisive where the boundary data cannot substitute for it, and needs no
architecture beyond what ships. The mechanism is stated and measured: the
scalar enters every token's seed, the slice states integrate it with the
geometry, and the interior decay rate follows it. Extrapolation one unit
past the training range costs about 1.5x for the scalar arm, which is the
expected price of conditioning on a value the model has not seen.

**What is not shown.** One parameter, one equation, a sphere; the
conditioning route has not been stressed with several scalars of very
different scales, where a learned normalization of the scalar inputs may
be needed, nor on a problem where the parameter changes the equation type.

## 2026-09-14 — Preregistration, KERNEL-NEUTRAL: the fused geometry kernel as the only change to the DrivAerML reference lanes {#sec-nb-kernel-neutral-prereg}

**Setting.** The kernel study (@sec-nb-kernel-study) showed that the exact
fused Triton geometry kernel brings ISLA's compiled 40,000-token step from
119 ms to 52 ms at less than half the memory, with outputs matching the
eager region to $10^{-6}$ and gradients to $10^{-5}$. It ships opt-in
(`geo_kernel="fused"`) because a numerics gate on random weights is not a
training-neutrality result: the kernel evaluates the routing bias, the
point-to-slice mix and the pooled invariants in one pass with its own
accumulation order under bfloat16 autocast, and a systematic difference
that is invisible at $10^{-6}$ per step could still move a 500-epoch run.
The rule set for the row-parallel softmax kernel applies: a kernel becomes
the default only after a training run on the reference configuration
lands within the seed noise of the eager reference.

**The lanes.** The two DrivAerML surface reference runs
(`rf_dr_mt2_meas_seed42`, `rf_dr_mt2_meas_seed43`: relative frame,
total-measure scale, width 192, twelve layers, 256 slices, no geometry
checkpointing, compile off, bfloat16, learning rate $10^{-3}$, 500 epochs,
10,000 tokens, no augmentation) re-run from the current repository head
with one change, `geo_kernel=fused`, as `kf_dr_isla_fused_seed42` and
`kf_dr_isla_fused_seed43` (launcher `kernel/fused_train_aga.sbatch`, code
snapshot `code_globin`, recipe snapshot `recipe_globin`; one GB300 node per
lane, four-hour chain links). The code head also carries the global-inputs
generalization, which is bitwise the former model at one vector, so the
kernel is the only arithmetic change. Evaluation with the float32
instrument on the sealed validation split, as for every reference number.

**Predictions and bars, written before the run.**

- **Neutral.** The fused lanes' float32 surface-pressure relative $L^2$ lies
  within **3%** of the eager reference on the seed mean (the bar the softmax
  kernel met at +1.8%), and neither seed differs from its eager twin by
  more than the two eager seeds differ from each other plus 3%. Meeting it
  makes `geo_kernel="fused"` the recommended default on CUDA, with eager
  kept as the reference implementation.
- **Not neutral.** A shift beyond 3% in either direction is a finding about
  bfloat16 accumulation in the fused region, not a speed result, and the
  kernel stays opt-in until the accumulation is made to match (float32
  accumulation of the pooled invariants is the first suspect).
- **Speed, reported.** Epoch time from the training logs against the eager
  reference's; at 10,000 tokens and compile off the study predicts a small
  gain only, the large gain being at 40,000 tokens under compile.

## 2026-09-15 — Verdict, KERNEL-NEUTRAL: not neutral by the bar (seed mean +4.9% on pressure, one seed at +8.9%); the fused kernel stays opt-in; a seed-44 pair is preregistered to separate kernel from seed {#sec-nb-kernel-neutral-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistration of @sec-nb-kernel-neutral-prereg: the two
DrivAerML surface reference lanes re-run from the current head with the
exact fused Triton geometry kernel as the only change, scored with the
float32 instrument on the sealed validation split against the eager twins'
numbers in `results/frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json`. Artifact:
`results/kernel_neutral_reduction_2026-09-15.json`; lanes
`kf_dr_isla_fused_seed42/43`, snapshots `code_globin` and `recipe_globin`
at 9f94e0df; one GB300 node per lane. Each fused-trained checkpoint was
evaluated twice, through the fused kernel and through the eager region.

**What we saw** (float32 relative $L^2$ on 48 validation cars):

| Lane | Pressure | Wall shear | Pressure ÷ eager twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eager reference, seed 42 | 0.0547 | 0.0802 | 1 |
| Eager reference, seed 43 | 0.0557 | 0.0809 | 1 |
| Fused kernel, seed 42 | 0.0552 | 0.0811 | 1.008 |
| Fused kernel, seed 43 | 0.0607 | 0.0887 | 1.089 |

Seed means: pressure 0.0579 against 0.0552
(1.049x), wall shear 1.054x. The two eager
seeds differ by 1.8%; the two fused seeds differ by
10.0%.
Evaluating one fused-trained checkpoint through the fused kernel and
through the eager region gives the same numbers to 2e-07 relative, so
the difference is a **training-time** effect, not an evaluation-time one.
Epoch time: 20 and 24 s for the fused lanes against 35 and 37 s for
the eager twins (median over 498 epochs; 1.6x), at 10,000 tokens with
compile off.

**Against the bar.** **Not neutral.** The seed mean is
+4.9% on pressure against a 3% bar, and seed 43 exceeds its
twin by 8.9%, far beyond the eager seed spread plus 3%. Seed 42 alone
would have passed (+0.8%). The kernel **stays opt-in**, as the
preregistration prescribed for this outcome, and `geo_kernel="eager"`
remains the reference implementation and the default.

**What it can and cannot say.** With two seeds the result cannot
distinguish a kernel that widens the training variance from one that
shifts the mean, nor either from one unlucky seed: the fused seed pair
spans 10% where the eager pair spans 2%, which is suggestive of variance
and is not a conclusion. The mechanism named in the preregistration, the
fused region's bfloat16 accumulation order, remains the first suspect;
the numerics gate on random weights ($10^-6$ per step) is evidently not
sufficient for a 500-epoch neutrality claim, which is the point of running
the lane.

**Preregistered follow-up (written before its run).** A seed-44 **pair**
from the same snapshot, `kf_dr_isla_fused_seed44` and
`kf_dr_isla_eager_seed44`, everything else identical (launcher indices 2
and 3 of `kernel/fused_train_aga.sbatch`). Prediction if the kernel is at
fault: the fused seed-44 lane exceeds the eager seed-44 lane by more than
3% on pressure, and the three fused seeds' spread stays above the three
eager seeds'. Prediction if seed 43 was an outlier: the pair agrees within
3% and the fused three-seed spread collapses toward the eager one; then the
neutrality question is reopened with the three-seed means and the same 3%
bar. Either way the eager seed-44 run becomes a third seed of the
reference itself. The float32 evaluation reuses `kernel/fused_eval_fp32_aga.sbatch`.

## 2026-09-15 — W2-C floor test, ISLA half: 20,000 tokens per case buy ISLA 5% at 1,260 HiLift cases (0.0384 against 0.0405, float32, rate-matched) for 2.0x the step time and 1.9x the memory; the GeoTransolver half waits on the unit-drive 20k twins {#sec-nb-floor20k-isla}

The 20,000-token floor test (W2-C, @sec-nb-w2-prereg) asked whether the
1,260-case rung's error floor is the protocol's token budget: if giving
each case twice the surface tokens helps both architectures by a similar
factor, the floor is the protocol's; if GeoTransolver gains ≥ 10 points
more than ISLA, the objection that ISLA's advantage was a token-budget
artifact stands. The two ISLA lanes (floor_hl_mt2_full_20k_seed{42,43};

the 180 validation cases at the standard 10,000 evaluation cells (jobs
749788 and 750214; bf16 twins 749787 and 750213; no loader warnings). The

GeoTransolver arms of the test (floor_hl_gt_full_20k_seed{42,43}) were the
physical-drive baseline and were stopped at epoch 153 by the rescheduling
of @sec-nb-udrv-resched; their unit-drive replacements
(udrv_hl_gt_full_20k_seed{42,43}) are training under ISLA Main's watcher and

| ISLA, 1,260 cases (180 val, float32) | pressure (42 / 43 → mean) | velocity | wall shear | step time | peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10,000 tokens (prior, mt2_hl_lr1) | 0.0393 / 0.0417 → **0.0405** | 0.0582 | 0.0923 | 1.84 s | 9.8 GB |
| 20,000 tokens (floor lanes) | 0.0380 / 0.0388 → **0.0384** | 0.0559 | 0.0880 | 3.69 s | 18.9 GB |

| Seed | Fused pressure | Eager pressure | Ratio | Wall-shear ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 43 | 0.0607 | 0.0557 | 1.089 | 1.096 |

1.025; wall shear ratio 1.030. Spread across the three seeds:

through the fused kernel or the eager region differs by at most
