token one read-back state per layer; H routings give it H.

**The change.** The research option `n_heads` on branch `isla-heads`
(commit 2f647149; cluster snapshot `code_heads`): each slice block runs H
independent routings, each with its own assignment logits, its own
equivariant anchors and relational invariants, and slice states of width
`hidden / H`, read back side by side into the same broadcast. Every
quantity is an invariant or an equivariant anchor exactly as in the single
routing, so the contracts hold (a contract test at H = 4 passes), and
`n_heads = 1` is the original routing bitwise with unchanged parameter
names (verified against the mainline). Geometry work scales with H; the
parameter count is nearly unchanged (the assignment grows H-fold, the
per-slice MLP shrinks H-fold).

**The instrument.** The OVERFIT-1 one-car floor as in CAP: one DrivAerML
car, 64 cached 10,000-cell views, 20,000 single-sample steps, bfloat16,
constant gauge (a lean-class config `isla_cg_heads` in the frozen
`recipe_ovf`: centered frame, `reference_length` 8.0), seed 42; float32
evaluation at 10,000 and 40,000 cells. Three lanes: `h1` (the same-code
single-routing control; the CAP baseline was trained on an older snapshot,
so the control removes any code-version difference), `h4` and `h8`
(`ovf_dr_isla_h{1,4,8}_seed42_v64`; launcher `overfit_heads_aga.sbatch`).

**Bars, written before the run**, on the float32 10,000-cell readout
against the `h1` control (expected near the CAP baseline 0.1064):

- **Closes the floor**: `h8` (or `h4`) at or below 0.0852, within 1.05x of
  Transolver's one-car floor; the form gap is the head count and a 435-car
  pair follows.
- **Carries**: at or below 0.90 × `h1` (a gain of at least 10%); reported
  as a partial carrier with its geometry cost.
- **Null**: at or above 0.95 × `h1`.
- **Control sanity**: `h1` within 3% of the CAP baseline 0.1064; a larger
  difference is a code-version effect and is investigated before the heads
  are read.

**Prediction.** Heads carry: `h8` lowers the one-car floor by 10 to 20%
and the training loss with it, monotone in H; if `h8` is null, the form
gap is not in the routing multiplicity and the next candidate is the
read-back (a soft read-back separate from the aggregation routing).

## 2026-09-18 — Verdict, FORM-HEADS: eight routings per block lower ISLA's one-car floor by 19%, monotone in the head count, and put it below both baselines at 40,000 evaluation cells; the form gap is the routing multiplicity {#sec-nb-formheads-verdict}

**What was run.** The three lanes of @sec-nb-formheads-prereg trained to
20,000 steps without incident (the eight-head lane across two chain links)
and were evaluated in float32 at 10,000 and 40,000 cells
(results/formheads_reduction_2026-09-18.json).

**What we saw** (float32 pressure error on the training car):

| arm | routings per block | 10,000 cells | ÷ `h1` control | 40,000 cells | tail-20 training loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `h1` (same-code control) | 1 | 0.1069 | 1.000 | 0.0814 | 0.0004 |
| `h4` | 4 | 0.1012 | 0.951 | 0.0751 | 0.0003 |
| `h8` | 8 | **0.0869** | **0.813** | **0.0729** | 0.0015 |
| CAP baseline (older snapshot) | 1 | 0.1064 | | 0.0857 | 0.0004 |
| GeoTransolver (OVERFIT-1) | | 0.0766 | | 0.0780 | |
| Transolver (OVERFIT-1) | | 0.0811 | | 0.0793 | |

**Against the bars.** The control passes its sanity bar (`h1` is 0.5% from
the CAP baseline, so the lean class on this instrument reproduces the older
snapshot). `h8` **carries** (0.813 of the control, against the 0.90 bar)
and misses *closes* by 0.0017 (0.0869 against 0.0852, that is 1.07x
Transolver's floor rather than 1.05x); `h4` is between (a 4.9% gain). The
effect is monotone in the head count, as predicted. At 40,000 evaluation
cells the ordering inverts: the eight-head ISLA (0.0729) is below
GeoTransolver (0.0780) and Transolver (0.0793) on the same car, the first
time any ISLA configuration has been below both baselines on an
in-distribution fit. The eight-head lane's tail training loss is higher
(0.0015 against 0.0004) while its evaluation is better; with 24-wide
per-head states the bfloat16 training signal is noisier and the last
twenty single-sample steps are not the fit (the evaluation is).

**Reading.** The two "form" points of @sec-nb-deficit-anatomy have a
mechanism: a token routed once per layer reads one slice state back; the
soft assignment hardens toward one slice per token
(@sec-nb-relframe-divergence-mechanism), and the read-back becomes
piecewise. Eight independent routings give every token eight anchor
neighbourhoods and eight states to compose, which is what Transolver's
eight heads do without any geometry; here they do it with every contract
intact (the contract test at four heads passes exactly). The cost is real:
the geometry region runs once per head, and the eight-head lane took 4.7
times the wall time of the control on one GPU at 10,000 cells. That cost
is the fused geometry kernel's job, not a reason to stop.

**What follows.** The one-car floor is the screening instrument; the
claim that matters is the 435-car in-distribution error of the *reference*
configuration with heads, preregistered next (@sec-nb-heads435-prereg).
`n_heads` stays a research option on branch `isla-heads` until that lands.

## 2026-09-18 — Preregistration, HEADS-435: ISLA with 4 and 8 routings per block on the full DrivAerML training set {#sec-nb-heads435-prereg}

**Setting.** FORM-HEADS moved the one-car floor by 19% at eight heads and
inverted the ordering against the baselines at 40,000 cells. CAP's width
axis transferred from the one-car instrument to 435 cars at the same
magnitude, so the instrument has predicted the full problem once; this
study asks whether it does so for the routing multiplicity, on the
flagship rather than the constant gauge.

**Arms.** `hd_dr_isla_ref_h{4,8}_seed{42,43}`: the reference configuration
(`isla_surface_reference` in `recipe_globin`: relative frame, total-measure
scale, width 192, 12 layers, 256 slices, geometry recompute on) with
`n_heads` 4 and 8, snapshot `code_heads` (branch `isla-heads`, 2f647149),
435 DrivAerML cars, 10,000 cells, learning rate 1e-3 (the protocol rate;
width is unchanged), 500 epochs, bfloat16, no augmentation; launcher
`kernel/heads435_aga.sbatch`. Float32 evaluation on the sample-frame
probe at 10,000 cells, uniform and 10:1-biased
(`kernel/heads435_eval_aga.sbatch`). Comparators on that instrument
(consistency benchmarks): reference 0.0554, constant gauge 0.0561,
Transolver 0.0520, GeoTransolver 0.0509; the reference's density factor
1.2.

**Bars, written before the run** (two-seed mean, uniform probe, pressure):

- **Closes the form gap**: eight heads at or below 0.0530, that is
  GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA at or above 0.96 at the scoreboard's budget, the
  value the anatomy assigns to a model with the form deficit removed; the
  option is promoted to the mainline with its cost stated and the scoreboard
  gains the row.
- **Carries**: at or below 0.0543 (a gain of at least 2%); promoted as a
  documented variant, the frontier restated as accuracy × cost.
- **Null**: at or above 0.0549 (less than 1%): the one-car gain does not
  transfer and the option stays on the research branch.
- **Contracts**: the density factor stays within 1.05 to 1.3 (the frame
  is untouched); a rise beyond 1.5 says the heads read the sample and the
  arm is withheld.
- **Stability**: both seeds train to 500 epochs at 1e-3; a divergence like
  RFDIV's would be read against the routing mechanism, and the width rule
  does not apply (width 192).

**Prediction.** Eight heads carry (0.0538 to 0.0543) and four heads are
between; the form points transfer at about half the one-car magnitude,
as width did. If supported, the
stratified draw becomes the recipe's inference sampler for ISLA (a
sampling-design choice that leaves the estimand and the training
convention untouched) and the scoreboard gains a labeled row; if
falsified, the count slope is a property of the trained function and the
next probe is the readout form.

## 2026-09-18 — Book overhaul: the polished chapters are rewritten as an instructive guide in the manner of a Drela user guide; the notebook and the artifacts are untouched {#sec-nb-book-overhaul}

**Setting.** The polished chapters of this book had grown by accretion over
six weeks of verdicts: the front matter opened with a three-thousand-word
verdict paragraph and a fourteen-row table of numbers, the architecture
chapter had no figure, the status chapter ran to eighteen thousand words,
and each chapter carried its own copy of the color palette. Peter asked on
2026-09-18 for a ground-up overhaul templated on a Drela-style user guide
(TASOPT, XFOIL): teach the method incrementally to an expert who has never
seen the program, illustrate concepts and results throughout, keep one
nomenclature and one color meaning, fold optional depth into expandable
notes so the throughline stays clean, and write like a teacher.

**What changed.** The book is re-arced into five parts (problem;
architecture; using ISLA; evidence; limits and status) with the appendices
unchanged. `STYLE.md` fixes the arc, the teaching pattern for every section
(message, words, picture, symbols; concrete before abstract; define at first
use; optional depth in collapsed callouts), the canonical nomenclature with
the synonyms it retires, and the color and mark semantics. `palette.py` is
the one importable house style (ISLA blue, GeoTransolver red, Transolver
amber; variants lighter with open markers; ablations hatched) and carries the
running Joukowski example, so no chapter duplicates a palette block again.
`index.qmd` now states the thesis as a priced trade in one paragraph, six
computed rows and one two-panel figure (accuracy in distribution above,
error growth under a sampling-density bias and under random poses below),
gives the key of names and colors, and states the reading order. The
architecture chapter is rewritten as `02-isla.qmd`, six ideas taught in
order on the airfoil with an executable concept figure for each (measure
weights as quadrature; position without a frame; slices and anchors; the
relational invariants; the assembled layer; the equivariant output basis),
the contracts as a test table, and the derivations, code correspondences and
"what is not a contract" in collapsed notes. A new `09-using-isla.qmd` is
the operating manual: the configuration decision, the input contract (weights
that sum to the surface area, a unit global direction, magnitudes as global
scalars), the training and inference commands, the width learning-rate rule
with its provisional status, the stratified inference sampler with its
measured effect, checkpoint loading and cost. The evidence, limits, status
and decision chapters are rewritten to the same standard in parallel, each
keeping every section, figure and table identifier that other chapters or
this notebook cite, and the status chapter is compressed to the tech tree,
its ledger and the provenance section. Chapters state current knowledge
only; every retraction and every superseded reading stays here.

**What did not change.** No artifact, no number and no verdict. Every
quantitative statement in the rewritten chapters is computed from the same
files in `results/` as before or quoted from `CLAIMS.md`; the pre-overhaul
architecture chapter is kept in the book directory as
`archive/02-meshtransformer2-pre-overhaul.qmd`, outside the build, until the
rewritten chapters have been read once against it.

**Acceptance.** The book renders with no unresolved cross-reference; every
section identifier cited from the notebook resolves; each chapter's figures
import `palette.py`; the throughline of every chapter reads completely with
all collapsed notes closed.

## 2026-09-18 — Preregistration, PREC-RES: the finite-precision residual of ISLA's covariance contracts on the GPU trained path {#sec-nb-precres-prereg}

**Setting.** ISLA's rotation and translation covariance is exact by
algebraic construction and verified in float64 unit tests on random
weights (@sec-isla-contracts). The recipe trains and evaluates under bf16
autocast, and the book has said since the audit response
(@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08) that the residual on the deployed path is a
quantity to be measured, not asserted: a CPU autocast probe on a small
random model gave a scalar rotation residual of 1.2 to 1.3% in bf16 against
6e-7 in float32. No trained checkpoint has been probed on the GPU.

**Question.** On the trained reference-configuration checkpoints, how far
from exact are the contracts in float32 and in bf16 on the GPU, and is the
bf16 residual small against the pose test's own reading (ISLA in random
poses scores 1.01x its in-pose error, @sec-pose-contract)?

**Instrument.** The two reference checkpoints trained at 435 DrivAerML
cars (seeds 42 and 43), loaded through the recipe's own loader assembly on
the 10,000-cell uniform sample-frame probe dataset, validation split, the
first twelve cars. For each car the model is evaluated on the original
inputs and on the same inputs under a random proper rotation $Q$ and a
random translation of one body diagonal (points, normals and the global
vector rotated; points shifted), in float32 and under bf16 autocast. The
readouts are the relative residuals $\lVert p(Qx+t) - p(x)\rVert /
\lVert p(x)\rVert$ for the pressure channel and $\lVert v(Qx+t) - v(x)Q^\top
\rVert / \lVert v(x)\rVert$ for the wall-shear vector, in the training
(normalized) output space, and as a reference the relative difference
between the bf16 and float32 predictions on the unrotated inputs (the
precision noise floor with no symmetry involved). Script
`kernel/precres_probe.py`, job `kernel/precres_aga.sbatch`, one GB300 per
checkpoint, minutes.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **Float32 exactness on the trained path**: scalar and vector residuals
  below $10^{-4}$ on every car. Above $10^{-3}$ on any car would mean a
  path in the trained model is not the algebra the tests verify
  (a fused or compiled kernel, a precision-dependent branch) and would be
  investigated before any other claim.
- **bf16 residual, negligible**: mean scalar residual below 0.5%, which is
  a factor of two below the pose test's 1% reading, so the pose test
  measures the model and not the arithmetic.
- **bf16 residual, material**: mean scalar residual above 2%. The
  Using-ISLA chapter then states that the contracts are exercised at
  deployment only under float32 inference, and the pose row of the
  scoreboard is annotated with the bf16 residual.
- Between 0.5 and 2%: reported as measured, with the noise-floor
  comparison deciding whether the residual is symmetry-specific (residual
  well above the unrotated bf16-versus-float32 difference) or plain
  precision noise (residual about equal to it).

**Prediction.** Float32 residuals of order $10^{-6}$; bf16 residuals of 1 to
2%, about equal to the unrotated bf16-versus-float32 difference, that is,
plain precision noise rather than a symmetry-breaking path. If so the book
states the bf16 residual as measured and recommends float32 inference where
the contract is load-bearing, which the recipe already does for reporting.

## 2026-09-18 — Verdict, PREC-RES: the contracts are exact to 3e-5 on the trained GPU path in float32; under bf16 autocast the rotation residual is 4% on pressure and 7% on wall shear, material, and mostly precision noise {#sec-nb-precres-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistration (@sec-nb-precres-prereg) asked how far
from exact ISLA's rotation and translation contracts are on the trained
GPU path, in float32 and under the bf16 autocast the recipe trains with,
using the two reference-configuration checkpoints trained on 435 DrivAerML
cars, twelve validation cars each, a random proper rotation plus a
translation of one body diagonal, on one GB300
(results/precres_2026-09-18.json).

**What we saw.** In **float32 the contracts hold on the trained path**:
the relative residual of the pressure prediction under the rigid motion is
7e-6 on average and 3e-5 at worst over the twenty-four cars, and of the
wall-shear vector 1.4e-5 on average and 4e-5 at worst, against the bar of
1e-4 on every car. Under **bf16 autocast the residual is material**: 3.3%
(seed 42) and 5.0% (seed 43) of the pressure prediction on average, 8.9% on
the worst car, and 6.1% and 7.8% of the wall-shear vector; the bar for
"material" was 2%. The noise floor with no symmetry involved, the relative
difference between the bf16 and the float32 prediction on the unrotated
inputs, is 2.3% for pressure and 4.3% for wall shear. Two independent bf16
evaluations differ by $\sqrt 2$ times that floor if the error is pure
rounding, 3.3%; seed 42's residual equals it and seed 43's is 1.5 times it,
so most of the bf16 residual is ordinary bf16 rounding of a 12-layer
network, and a smaller part is symmetry-specific (the rounding of the
relational invariants and the anchors differs between the two poses).

**Why it matters.** The book's statement "exact by algebraic construction;
the residual on the deployed path is a measured quantity" now has its
number. In float32 the algebra is what runs. In bf16 the residual is of the
same order as the pose test's reading (ISLA in random poses at 1.01x its
in-pose error, measured in float32) and about half of ISLA's whole
in-distribution error, so a bf16 deployment does not exercise the contract
at the level the book claims for it, and a bf16 prediction carries a 2.3%
rounding perturbation on its own, which is the reason the float32 reporting
instrument was adopted. The recommendation in the Using-ISLA chapter is
therefore: infer in float32 wherever the pose or consistency contract is
load-bearing, and treat bf16 inference as a 2 to 4% perturbation of the
prediction in any pose.

**What's next.** Nothing further is needed for the mainline. A float16
autocast probe (which the recipe does not use) or a bf16 probe with the
routing softmax and geometry region kept in float32 would show whether the
residual can be removed at part of bf16's cost; it is not queued, because
the deployed answer is float32 inference.

## 2026-09-18 — Preregistration, SG-REF: does the similarity-gauge variant recover part of the positional deficit against ISLA at 435 DrivAerML cars? Third seeds and the stratified instrument {#sec-nb-sgref-prereg}

**Setting.** The book prefers the reference configuration (relative frame,
no center, total-measure length unit) to the similarity-gauge variant
(measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius length unit) on principle: it
estimates nothing from the sample and presumes no single closed body. On
accuracy the two have never been separated. At 435 DrivAerML cars, two
seeds each on the independent 10,000-cell draw, the similarity-gauge
variant scores 0.0543 and the reference 0.0552, a 1.6% difference inside
the draw noise the stratified-sampler study exposed
(results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json,
@sec-nb-quadvar-verdict). The deficit anatomy assigns about two and a half
points of GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA to the positional information the relative
frame denies the model (@sec-nb-deficit-anatomy); the similarity gauge
hands each token its distance and direction from the body centroid as
extra invariant seeds, integrals of the geometry, so it is the principled
way to give part of that back. Peter asked when one would choose it; the
honest answer needs this measurement.

**Question.** With three seeds each and the stratified inference draw,
does the similarity-gauge variant recover a measurable part of the
positional deficit against the reference configuration, or are the two
within noise?

**Instrument.** One new seed (44) of each configuration at 435 cars, 10,000
cells, learning rate 1e-3, 500 epochs, bf16 training, lean class and the
same recipe copy as the reference seeds (job `kernel/sgref_aga.sbatch`);
then all six checkpoints evaluated in float32 on the 48 validation cars
under the stratified 10,000-cell draw and the independent draw, and on the
sample-frame density probe (uniform and 10:1-biased). Readout: seed-mean
surface-pressure error under the stratified draw, and the seed ranges.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **Recovers**: the similarity-gauge mean is at least 1.5% below the
  reference mean under the stratified draw and the seed ranges do not
  overlap. Reading: about one of the two and a half positional points is
  recoverable by a consistent, integral-estimated frame; the Using-ISLA
  chapter names the similarity gauge as the configuration for closed single
  bodies, the reference stays the default for its generality.
- **Within noise**: the means differ by less than 1.5% or the seed ranges
  overlap. Reading: the positional deficit is not recoverable by a
  centroid; the preference for the reference is then also unopposed on
  accuracy and the book says so.
- **Contracts**: both configurations keep their density factor within 1.05
  to 1.3 on the probe; a rise beyond 1.5 for either is reported against it.

**Prediction.** Within noise, at the edge: the similarity gauge about 1%
ahead with overlapping seed ranges. A recovery of a full point would be a
surprise worth a follow-up on the wings, where the reference's price
against the constant gauge is larger.

## 2026-09-18 — Ruling and preregistration: the constant-gauge variant leaves the main results; POSE-REF and LR-REF re-measure the two headline properties on ISLA {#sec-nb-refprops-prereg}

**Ruling (Peter, 2026-09-18).** The constant-gauge variant, a centered frame
with a fixed length unit that was the program's reference until the
relative frame replaced it, is cut from the book's main results: no row of
the standing table, no series in the scoreboard figures, no column of the
ladder. It improves in-distribution accuracy by reading a sample statistic
(the plain mean of the sampled points) that is not physical knowledge and
does not generalize to general PDE cases, the same reason the weights-off
ablation was never adopted. It may remain as a labeled diagnostic in
collapsed notes where a mechanism needs it (the plain-mean collapse under a
sampling-density bias, the single-factor ablation at 35 wing cases). Peter
raised the same objection in principle against the similarity-gauge
variant: the area-weighted centroid of a two-dimensional manifold is not a
meaningful point in three-dimensional space and "the body" is not a
well-posed notion for a PDE. That deliberation is open (SG-REF is running
and the notebook will carry the argument); the constant-gauge cut is not.

**Consequence.** Two headline properties of ISLA were measured only on the
constant-gauge variant: the pose test (every case in its own random SO(3)
pose; ISLA at 1.01x its in-pose error, 6% and 19% ahead of the augmented
baselines; research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_b_pose) and the
learning-rate grid (ISLA within 1.55x of its best across a decade of rate
where GeoTransolver degrades 9x by seed mean). Until re-measured, those
rows carry the label "measured on the legacy centered variant" in the book.
The contracts of the two configurations are identical, so the pose
*degradation* should transfer exactly; the in-pose accuracy and the
learning-rate response are properties of the trained function and need the
measurement.

**Instrument.** Six lanes of the reference configuration at 435 DrivAerML
cars, 10,000 cells, 500 epochs, bf16, lean class and the same recipe copy
as the reference seeds (`kernel/refprops_aga.sbatch`): two seeds with every
training and validation case in its own random pose (dataset
`drivaer_ml_surface_pose`, learning rate 1e-3), and two seeds each at
learning rates 3e-3 and 1e-2 in the native frame. Readout in float32 on the
48 validation cars: the posed error against the reference's in-pose error
(0.0552, two seeds) and against the augmented baselines' posed errors
(0.0602, 0.0676); the learning-rate errors against the reference at 1e-3.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **POSE-REF supports**: the posed reference is within 3% of its in-pose
  error (the contract at work; the bf16 training residual measured by
  PREC-RES is the expected source of the gap) and below both augmented
  baselines by at least 5%. The pose row of the standing table then reads on
  the reference and the label is removed.
- **POSE-REF falsifies**: the posed reference exceeds its in-pose error by
  more than 5%; then something in the recipe's posed datapipe or the
  training path is not covariant and is investigated before the row is
  restored.
- **LR-REF supports**: the reference's worst error over {1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2}
  is within 1.6x of its best (the constant-gauge value), so the
  learning-rate robustness claim transfers; the section then reads on the
  reference.
- **LR-REF falsifies**: a divergence (loss not finite, or error above 2x
  the 1e-3 value) at 3e-3 or 1e-2. Given the width-512 divergence mechanism
  (routing hardening at high effective rate), a divergence at 1e-2 would not
  surprise and would be reported as the reference's rate ceiling.

**Prediction.** POSE-REF supports (posed within 2%). LR-REF: 3e-3 within
1.2x, 1e-2 between 1.3x and divergence; the claim narrows from "a decade"
to "half a decade" for the reference.

## 2026-09-18 — Ruling and preregistration, LEN-RMS: the reference's length unit is to become the RMS pairwise distance once validated; the similarity-gauge variant is to leave the main results on principle {#sec-nb-lenrms-prereg}

**Ruling (Peter, 2026-09-18).** Two decisions, both to be validated before
they change the class default. First, the similarity-gauge variant leaves
the book's main results on the same principle as the constant-gauge
variant: a PDE has no notion of "the body", and the area-weighted centroid
of a two-dimensional surface is not a point three-dimensional physics
distinguishes, so handing every token its distance and direction from that
point is information a general PDE surrogate should not have. ISLA's slice
anchors are the legitimate version of the same object: reference points the
network derives from measure-weighted means of subsets it chooses, with
none privileged from outside. SG-REF (@sec-nb-sgref-prereg) continues to
run; its result becomes the price of not being told the body's center, not
a configuration choice. Second, the relative frame's length unit changes
from the square root of the total measure to the **measure-weighted RMS
pairwise distance** of the sample, once validated.

**Why the length unit.** Peter's worry was a boundary with structure at
every scale, a Koch snowflake. Traced through the reference configuration,
everything is well posed under refinement except one quantity: the total
measure. The routing bias is $\log w_i$ inside a softmax, invariant to a
constant factor; the anchors and separations are normalized sums; but the
length unit $\sqrt{\sum_i w_i}$ is an *unnormalized* integral, and on a
fractal boundary the total length or area diverges with refinement, so every
relational invariant, a distance in that unit, drifts to zero. The
similarity gauge's centroid and RMS radius are *normalized* moments and
converge. The center-free repair is the RMS pairwise distance, $L^2 \equiv
\sum_{ij} \tilde w_i \tilde w_j\,\lvert x_i - x_j\rvert^2$ with $\tilde w =
w/\sum w$, a normalized two-point statistic that names no center; by the
variance identity it equals $2\sum_i \tilde w_i \lvert x_i - c\rvert^2$ with
$c$ the weighted mean, so it costs one pass and the mean is an intermediate
of a scalar, never a frame. It converges wherever the normalized measure
converges, is exactly covariant under a geometric rescale, and gains an
invariance the total-measure unit lacks: a uniform rescale of the weights
alone, or of the points alone, leaves the output unchanged.

**What was built.** `scale_mode="rms_distance"` in the ISLA class as an
opt-in option (mainline commit of 2026-09-18; the default stays
`"total_measure"` until validation). Two tests: the contract test (exact
translation invariance at $10^{-12}$, rotation covariance at $10^{-10}$,
invariance to points $\times 2.5$ with and without weights $\times 2.5^2$,
invariance to weights $\times 137$, and the contrast that the total-measure
unit is not weight-rescale invariant), and a fractal-refinement test on the
Koch curve: across levels 0 to 6 the total measure grows by exactly $4/3$
per level (1.00, 1.33, 1.78, 2.37, 3.16, 4.21, 5.62) while the RMS pairwise
distance converges (0.358, 0.381, 0.3841, 0.3847, 0.38486, 0.38489), the
last two levels agreeing to $10^{-4}$. All 58 ISLA tests pass.

**Instrument for the accuracy validation.** Two seeds (42, 43) of the
reference configuration with `scale_mode=rms_distance` at 435 DrivAerML
cars, 10,000 cells, learning rate 1e-3, 500 epochs, bf16, code snapshot
`code_lenrms` (the lean class plus this option) and the same recipe copy as
the reference seeds (`kernel/lenrms_aga.sbatch`); then float32 evaluation
of both pairs under the stratified and the independent 10,000-cell draws
and the sample-frame density probe.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **Validated**: the RMS-distance unit is within 1.5% of the total-measure
  reference under the stratified draw (seed means) with overlapping seed
  ranges, trains without divergence at 1e-3, and keeps its density factor
  within 1.05 to 1.3. The class default and the recipe configs then switch
  to `rms_distance`, the book's reference configuration is restated, and the
  Koch-curve test becomes the documented reason.
- **Better**: at least 1.5% below the reference with non-overlapping seed
  ranges; adopted, and the notebook records that the normalized unit also
  helps in distribution (the total measure of a sub-sampled surface is a
  noisier estimate than its normalized second moment).
- **Worse**: more than 1.5% above the reference with non-overlapping seed
  ranges; not adopted, and the fractal argument is recorded as a known
  limitation of the total-measure unit with the option kept for boundaries
  where it matters.
- A divergence at 1e-3 would be read against the unit's interaction with
  the routing (as in the width-512 mechanism) and investigated before any
  decision.

**Prediction.** Validated, within noise: on CFD surfaces that are smooth at
the mesh scale the two units differ by a case-dependent constant factor
that the network absorbs, so the trained functions should be
indistinguishable at two seeds.

## 2026-09-18 — Interim, HEADS-435: four routings per block carry at 435 cars (0.0540 against the reference's 0.0554, 0.975x; density factor 1.23); the eight-routing pair is still training {#sec-nb-heads435-interim}

**Setting.** HEADS-435 (@sec-nb-heads435-prereg) asks whether the
routing-multiplicity gain measured on one car (@sec-nb-formheads-verdict)
transfers to the reference configuration trained on 435 DrivAerML cars.
The four-head pair (seeds 42 and 43) has finished its 500 epochs and been
scored in float32 on the 10,000-cell sample-frame probe; the eight-head pair
is at about epoch 300 and its verdict is the one the preregistration's bars
are written for.

**What we saw.** Four routings per block score **0.0540** on the uniform
draw (seeds 0.0537 and 0.0543) against the single-routing reference's
0.0554, a ratio of 0.975: the "carries" band (at or below 0.0543), short of
"closes" (at or below 0.0530). GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA moves from 0.919 to
0.943 and Transolver ÷ ISLA to 0.963. The density factor is 1.23 against
the reference's 1.24, inside the 1.05 to 1.3 contract band, so the heads
did not read the sample
(results/heads435_reduction_2026-09-18_h4_interim.json).

**Reading, provisional.** The preregistration predicted four heads
"between" and eight heads "carries"; four heads already carry, at about
half the one-car magnitude (2.5 points of ratio against the one-car study's
5 for four heads), the same transfer fraction width showed. Whether eight
heads close the form gap is the pending question; no promotion decision is
taken on the four-head pair alone. The reference configuration stays
single-routing until the full verdict.

## 2026-09-18 — Interim, LR-REF: ISLA diverges at learning rate 1e-2 (loss NaN at epochs 21 and 32 on the two seeds); the 3e-3 and posed lanes train cleanly; the 1e-2 lanes are stopped {#sec-nb-lrref-interim}

**Setting.** LR-REF (@sec-nb-refprops-prereg) re-measures the learning-rate
grid {1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2} on the reference configuration at 435 DrivAerML
cars, because the grid the book cites was measured on the legacy centered
variant. The preregistration named a divergence at 1e-2 as a possible
outcome to be reported as the reference's rate ceiling rather than a
failure of the claim.

**What we saw.** Both 1e-2 seeds trained with finite loss (0.065 and 0.063
on the last finite step) and then went to NaN within one step, seed 42 at
epoch 21 and seed 43 at epoch 32, and stayed there. The 3e-3 seeds are at
epochs 90 and 104 with finite losses and no NaN, and the two posed lanes at
epochs 90 and 91 likewise. The 1e-2 lanes were canceled and marked blocked
at 12:25 PDT so that two GPU nodes do not train NaN for 470 epochs; their
logs are kept.

**Reading, provisional.** The reference configuration's rate ceiling at
width 192 lies between 3e-3 and 1e-2. This is the same failure mode the
width-512 study found at 1e-3 (@sec-nb-relframe-divergence-mechanism): the relative frame's
routing hardens under too high an effective rate and the anchors collapse,
after which the invariants are not finite. The legacy centered variant
survived 1e-2 at 1.55x its best error; the relative frame does not survive
it at all, so the learning-rate robustness claim, once the 3e-3 lanes are
scored, will read "stable across half a decade (1e-3 to 3e-3) where
GeoTransolver degrades 9x one step above its best; diverges at 1e-2", and
the width rule remains the operating guidance for anything above the
protocol rate. The verdict on the 3e-3 pair and the posed pair follows when
they finish.

## 2026-09-18 — Preregistration, STEELMAN: the Horvitz–Thompson-centered, measure-weighted baselines through the refinement benchmark {#sec-nb-steelman-prereg}

**Setting.** The scoreboard's consistency figure shows that GeoTransolver
and Transolver become consistent under the 10:1 sampling-density bias
(density factors 1.04 and 1.03 at 10,000 cells) once their slice pooling
carries the cell measure and their datapipe centers on the
Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the surface centroid (@sec-nb-mwaw-verdict).
Peter asked the question any reader will ask of that figure: why not use
that GeoTransolver? The chapter now answers it (the fix buys consistency
with a body centroid, the construct ISLA declines, and does not make the
model covariant), but the variant has only been measured on the single-count
density probe. A steel-man of the consistency claim needs it on the
instrument the claim is made with.

**Question.** Under the refinement benchmark (uniform, area-proportional and
10:1-biased samplers at 2,500, 10,000 and 40,000 cells, float32, 48
validation cars), do the HT-centered, measure-weighted GeoTransolver and
Transolver converge toward their own uniform-sampling answer with cell count
as the measure-weighted ISLA arms do, and at what in-distribution accuracy?

**Instrument.** Evaluation only: the four existing checkpoints (two seeds
each of the two variants, trained with the HT-centered datapipe) through the
consistency-benchmark launcher on copies of the three benchmark dataset
configurations with the datapipe's area-weighted centering switched on, under
the code snapshot whose centering weights by the composed Horvitz–Thompson
measure (`bench/bench_lanes_steelman.tsv`, 36 lanes). Readouts as in
@sec-consistency-bench: each arm's area-sampler and biased-sampler error
divided by its uniform error at each count, and the uniform error itself.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **Consistent**: at 40,000 cells both samplers within 3% of the uniform
  answer for both variants (the benchmark's bar), with the deviation falling
  with count. Reading: the property is fully portable; the chapter states
  that a GeoTransolver with the measure semantics and an integral center
  matches ISLA on consistency at every count, and ISLA's remaining claim is
  covariance and center-freeness.
- **Partially consistent**: within 3% at 40,000 under the area sampler but
  not the biased one, or converging but above 3%. Reading: the centroid
  frame is consistent to first order and the residual is the raw-coordinate
  path's sensitivity to the sample; stated as measured.
- **Inconsistent**: deviations that do not fall with count. Reading: the
  single-count probe was not representative; investigated before the
  chapter's sentence stands.
- **Accuracy**: the uniform error at 10,000 within 1% of the released
  GeoTransolver's (0.0503) as on the probe; a larger gap is reported as the
  price of the HT frame.

**Prediction.** Consistent: the datapipe center is an integral and the
pooling is a quadrature, so the same mechanism that makes ISLA's arms
converge applies; the biased-sampler deviation at 40,000 will be a little
larger than ISLA's because the raw coordinates still see the sample's point
distribution through the attention.

## 2026-09-18 — Verdict, STEELMAN: GeoTransolver and Transolver with ISLA's measure-weighted pooling and an HT-centered datapipe are consistent under refinement at every count, within 1.2% of uniform at 40,000 cells, and more consistent than ISLA {#sec-nb-steelman-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistration (@sec-nb-steelman-prereg) sent the four
checkpoints of GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered
datapipe (ablation) and its Transolver counterpart through the refinement
benchmark: uniform, area-proportional and 10:1-biased samplers at 2,500,
10,000 and 40,000 cells, float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars, in the
HT-centered datapipe convention (results/steelman_reduction_2026-09-18.json).

**What we saw.** The **consistent** bar is met for both arms with room to
spare. For the GeoTransolver ablation the area-sampler error divided by the
uniform error falls 1.108 → 1.042 → 1.012 from 2,500 to 40,000 cells and
the biased-sampler ratio 1.120 → 1.015 → 1.005; for the Transolver ablation
1.097 → 1.044 → 1.010 and 1.100 → 1.013 → 1.001. Both deviations fall
monotonically with count and are within 1.2% at 40,000. In distribution the
GeoTransolver ablation scores 0.0509 on the uniform 10,000-cell draw against
GeoTransolver's 0.0503, a 1.2% price, just outside the 1% accuracy bar; the
Transolver ablation 0.0531 against 0.0517. For context, ISLA on the same
benchmark deviates 1.06 (area) and 1.03 (biased) at 40,000 cells and 1.60
and 1.23 at 10,000, so the ablations are **more consistent than ISLA at
every count**, and the prediction that their biased-sampler deviation would
exceed ISLA's was wrong.

**Why it matters.** Sampling consistency is fully portable to the
Transolver family: the two ingredients, a quadrature in the pooling and a
frame taken from an integral of the surface, make GeoTransolver consistent
at a 1.2% in-distribution price, and its consistency under refinement is
better than ISLA's, presumably because its raw coordinates in the centered
frame give every token a stable absolute position while ISLA's tokens locate
themselves through routed anchors that themselves move with the sample. The
book's consistency claim is therefore restated: what ISLA offers is
consistency **together with** exact covariance and **without** a body
centroid; the consistency alone is not an ISLA advantage over a GeoTransolver
willing to adopt ISLA's measure semantics and a centroid frame. The
scoreboard chapter's steel-man paragraph carries the numbers, and the
"not yet on the board" list drops the entry.

**What's next.** The pose test for these ablations (they are not covariant;
the interesting number is their posed error against ISLA's) is the one
remaining steel-man measurement and is queued behind the running lanes.

## 2026-09-18 — Preregistration, TOK-PROTO: what does the DrivAerML standing look like when every model trains and evaluates at 40,000 and 80,000 cells instead of 10,000? {#sec-nb-tokproto-prereg}

**Setting.** The protocol trains and scores every architecture at 10,000
sampled cells per case; the recipe's own default is 200,000, and Peter asked
why the book's baseline is so low. The choice dates from the program's
early fast loop and was kept for comparability. The deficit anatomy
(@sec-nb-deficit-anatomy) already says that 3 of ISLA's 8 points against
GeoTransolver at 10,000 cells are count noise that evaluating the same
checkpoints at 40,000 cells removes; what training at a higher count does
to the standing has been measured only at the width-512 corner
(@sec-nb-corner-wlr-verdict). The scale study
(@sec-program-status, node SCALE) trained width-192 lanes at 40,000 and
80,000 cells for GeoTransolver, Transolver and ISLA's legacy centered
variant on 435 cars, two seeds each; they finished and were never scored in
float32.

**Question.** At width 192, with training and evaluation at the same
count, how do GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA and Transolver ÷ ISLA move from 10,000
to 40,000 to 80,000 cells, and what does that say about raising the
protocol count for the final comparison?

**Instrument.** Float32 inference at the training count on the 48-car
validation split (the in-family instrument) for the twelve trained
checkpoints (`kernel/tokproto_eval_aga.sbatch`), compared with the 10,000-cell
values of the same architectures (GeoTransolver 0.0503, Transolver 0.0517,
legacy centered ISLA 0.0558). ISLA here is the legacy centered variant,
because the scale study predates the relative frame; the relative frame's
10,000-cell value is within 1% of the legacy variant's on this dataset, so
the ratios read across, and the relative frame's own higher-count lanes are
the follow-up if the ratios move.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **Count is the lever**: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA rises from 0.90 at 10,000
  cells to at least 0.95 at 40,000 and does not fall at 80,000; the anatomy's
  count-noise attribution then holds for training as well as evaluation, and
  the protocol count is raised to 40,000 (the fused kernel's parity point)
  for the final comparison of the fixed configuration.
- **Count is neutral**: the ratio moves by less than 0.02 between counts;
  the 10,000-cell protocol is then a fair instrument and only the evaluation
  draw matters, as the stratified-sampler study said.
- **Count favors the baselines**: the ratio falls with count; then ISLA's
  slice quadrature gains less from more cells than the baselines' raw
  coordinates do, and the anatomy is wrong about what the count noise is.
- Absolute errors of every model fall with count (every model benefits from
  more cells); a model whose error rises with count is a training defect and
  is investigated.

**Prediction.** Count is the lever: about 0.95 at 40,000 and 0.96 at
80,000, matching the width-512 corner (0.95 to 0.98) and the evaluation-only
anatomy. If so the final comparison, once the configuration is fixed by
HEADS-435 and LEN-RMS, is trained at 40,000 cells, and the book's protocol
section says why 10,000 was the exploration count and 40,000 is the
reporting count.

## 2026-09-18 — COST-SWEEP: training-step time and memory from 2,500 to 200,000 tokens; GeoTransolver's step is flat below 40,000 and fused ISLA tracks it at every count in half the memory; every model fits a GB300 at the recipe default {#sec-nb-cost-sweep}

**Setting.** Peter asked whether the book states per-iteration cost and
why the protocol samples 10,000 cells when the recipe defaults to 200,000.
The book had cost at two or three token counts; this sweep measures the
training step of the three architectures against token count on the
kernel-study instrument (one GB300, bf16 autocast, batch of one case, AdamW
step, compiled path, random inputs, median of ten measured steps after
warm-up; results/cost_sweep_gb300_bf16_2026-09-18.json), for ISLA on its
recipe-default path (geometry recomputed in the backward pass), ISLA with
the fused geometry kernel, GeoTransolver and Transolver.

**What we saw.** Step time [ms] and peak allocated memory [GiB]:

| tokens | ISLA default | ISLA fused | GeoTransolver | Transolver |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,500 | 41 / 0.5 | 42 / 0.5 | 44 / 0.8 | 21 / 0.6 |
| 10,000 | 46 / 1.3 | 44 / 1.3 | 45 / 2.7 | 22 / 1.8 |
| 40,000 | 115 / 4.7 | 47 / 4.5 | 48 / 10.0 | 23 / 6.6 |
| 80,000 | 215 / 9.3 | 50 / 8.8 | 51 / 19.8 | 29 / 13.1 |
| 120,000 | 322 / 13.8 | 63 / 13.1 | 64 / 29.6 | 39 / 19.6 |
| 200,000 | 529 / 22.9 | 91 / 21.6 | 106 / 49.3 | 65 / 32.5 |

GeoTransolver's and Transolver's steps are flat up to about 40,000 tokens
(the GPU is not saturated by one case at these widths) and then grow
roughly linearly; ISLA's default path grows linearly from 20,000 tokens and
is 5.0x GeoTransolver's step at 200,000, while the fused kernel tracks
GeoTransolver within 5% up to 120,000 and is 14% faster at 200,000, at
0.44x its memory. At the recipe default of 200,000 cells every model fits
one GB300 with a wide margin; GeoTransolver's 49 GiB would not fit an
80 GB card.

**Why it matters.** The token budget, not the architecture, decides the
cost comparison: below 40,000 tokens all three are within 2x of one
another and none is compute-bound; above it, ISLA needs the fused kernel to
stay at GeoTransolver's step, and with it ISLA is the cheaper model in
memory at every count. For the protocol question (@sec-nb-tokproto-prereg)
the sweep removes the cost objection to the recipe default: a 200,000-cell
DrivAerML lane costs about 2x a 10,000-cell one in step time for
GeoTransolver and, with the fused kernel, for ISLA; the training lanes are
data-loading-bound in any case. The one open cost item is a multi-head
fused kernel, needed only if HEADS-435 promotes multi-head routing, since
the fused kernel is single-routing.

## 2026-09-18 — Verdict, TOK-PROTO: count is the lever; trained and scored at 40,000 cells GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is 0.965 and at 80,000 it is 0.985, with ISLA ahead of Transolver at 80,000 (1.016) {#sec-nb-tokproto-verdict}

**Setting.** The preregistration (@sec-nb-tokproto-prereg) scored the
scale study's width-192 lanes, trained at 40,000 and 80,000 cells per case
on 435 DrivAerML cars, in float32 at their training count on the 48
validation cars: GeoTransolver, Transolver and ISLA's legacy centered
variant, two seeds each (results/tokproto_reduction_2026-09-18.json). The
10,000-cell comparators are the scoreboard's: GeoTransolver 0.0503,
Transolver 0.0517, legacy centered ISLA 0.0558.

**What we saw.** Every model improves with count, and ISLA improves most.

| cells (train and score) | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA (legacy centered) | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10,000 | 0.0503 | 0.0517 | 0.0558 | 0.901 | 0.927 |
| 40,000 | 0.0475 (0.0473 / 0.0477) | 0.0482 (0.0477 / 0.0487) | 0.0492 (0.0496 / 0.0488) | 0.965 | 0.980 |
| 80,000 | 0.0461 (0.0462 / 0.0460) | 0.0476 (0.0473 / 0.0478) | 0.0468 (0.0472 / 0.0464) | 0.985 | 1.016 |

The **count-is-the-lever** bar is met: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA rises from
0.901 to 0.965 at 40,000 and to 0.985 at 80,000, and Transolver ÷ ISLA
crosses one at 80,000. From 10,000 to 80,000 cells GeoTransolver's error
falls 8%, Transolver's 8% and ISLA's 16%.

**Why it matters.** The book's headline in-distribution deficit is mostly
an artifact of the 10,000-cell protocol: the deficit anatomy's count-noise
attribution holds for training as well as evaluation, and at 80,000 cells,
still 2.5 times below the recipe's default of 200,000, ISLA is within 1.5%
of GeoTransolver and ahead of Transolver. This is on the legacy centered
variant; ISLA's own 10,000-cell value is within 1% of the legacy variant's
on this dataset, so the ratios are expected to read across, and the
relative-frame lanes at the recipe default (@sec-nb-proto200k-prereg) are
the measurement that replaces this one in the main results. The reporting
protocol moves to 200,000 cells per case, the recipe's default, with
10,000 kept as the exploration count and stated as such.

**What's next.** PROTO-200K: ISLA and both baselines trained and scored at
200,000 cells, two seeds each, launched today; the width-192 40,000- and
80,000-cell rows above enter the book as the trend line toward it, labeled
legacy centered variant.

## 2026-09-18 — Ruling and preregistration, PROTO-200K: the reporting protocol adopts the recipe's default of 200,000 sampled cells per case; ISLA, GeoTransolver and Transolver trained there at 435 cars {#sec-nb-proto200k-prereg}

**Ruling (Peter, 2026-09-18).** The 10,000-cell protocol was the program's
exploration count; the comparison the book reports should be run as the
unified recipe ships, at 200,000 sampled cells per case, so that strong
baselines meet a strong contender. The cost sweep (@sec-nb-cost-sweep)
removes the cost objection: every model fits one GB300 at 200,000 tokens,
and the training lanes are data-loading-bound.

**Question.** At the recipe's default count, what is the in-distribution
standing of ISLA against GeoTransolver and Transolver on DrivAerML at 435
cars, and does the deficit anatomy's prediction, a remaining gap of about
two and a half points from the positional information the contracts deny
plus under a point of routing form, hold?

**Instrument.** Six lanes (`kernel/proto200k_aga.sbatch`): ISLA (relative
frame, total-measure unit, default eager geometry path, learning rate
1e-3), GeoTransolver (unit direction, 1e-3) and Transolver (unit direction,
3e-3), seeds 42 and 43, 500 epochs, bf16, 200,000 cells per case; float32
scoring at 200,000 cells on the 48 validation cars. The configuration is
the current ISLA; if HEADS-435 or LEN-RMS changes the class default, the two
ISLA lanes are rerun with the promoted configuration and these become the
single-routing, total-measure control.

**Bars, written before the run.**

- **Parity**: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA at or above 0.99 and Transolver ÷ ISLA
  at or above 1.00. The thesis's in-distribution clause is restated as parity
  at the recipe default with the contracts as the difference.
- **Anatomy holds**: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA between 0.96 and 0.99: the
  remaining gap is the positional information the contracts deny and the
  routing form, as the anatomy says, and the book states that price at the
  recipe default.
- **Gap persists**: below 0.96: count was not the whole of the noise, and
  the anatomy is revised at the new count.
- Absolute errors of every model fall from their 80,000-cell values; a
  model whose error rises is a training defect and is investigated.

**Prediction.** Anatomy holds at the upper edge: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA about
0.98 to 0.99, Transolver ÷ ISLA about 1.02.

## 2026-09-18 — Ruling and preregistration, PROTO-200K-FLEET: every evidence lane re-run at the recipe default of 200,000 cells per case {#sec-nb-proto200k-fleet-prereg}

**Ruling (Peter, 2026-09-18).** The 200,000-cell budget is the protocol
everywhere, not only for the 435-car DrivAerML row: every training lane
behind the book's evidence is re-run at the recipe default, for ISLA,
GeoTransolver and Transolver, two seeds each, with the exceptions of the
deliberate scaling studies (width and token ladders), which vary the budget
on purpose and keep their counts. Configuration decisions that are being
made at the exploration budget (multi-head routing, the RMS length unit,
the similarity gauge) are finished there first and their winners then join
the 200,000-cell fleet; they are not part of it today.

**Lanes.** DrivAerML: the 435-car surface trio (already running,
@sec-nb-proto200k-prereg), the pose test (baselines with rotation
augmentation, ISLA without), the small-data ladder (27, 54, 109, 218 cars),
and the interior task (ISLA with query tokens and GeoTransolver-volume).
HiLiftAeroML: the seven surface rungs (35, 210, 510 and 1,260 cases; 4 and
21 training geometries; the fixed angle) and the deflection split. The
manifest with every run identifier, dataset, learning rate and first job
identifier is kept on the cluster at `kernel/p200k_fleet/manifest.tsv` and
copied into `results/` once the launch is accepted. Wall-clock is
data-loading-bound: the 435-car DrivAerML lanes run at about one minute per
epoch for the baselines and under two for ISLA, so the fleet completes over
days, the 1,260-case wing rung last.

**Bars, written before the runs.** Each lane's bar is the one its 10,000-cell
predecessor had, restated at the new budget; two fleet-level bars decide what
the book says about the budget itself:

- **The budget was the gap**: on every DrivAerML row GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA
  is at or above 0.97 and on the wing rungs the ratio rises by at least 0.03
  against its 10,000-cell value; the thesis's in-distribution clause is then
  restated at the reporting protocol.
- **The wings differ**: the DrivAerML rows close while the wing rungs move by
  less than 0.03; then the wing deficit is not count noise and its
  mechanism (the mesher pattern where validation geometries recur in
  training) is the next study.
- Any lane whose 200,000-cell error exceeds its 10,000-cell error is a
  training defect and is investigated before its row is written.

**Prediction.** The budget was the gap on DrivAerML (0.98 at 435 cars); the
wing rungs rise by 0.03 to 0.05 but stay below 0.95 where validation
geometries recur in training.

## 2026-09-18 — Launch record, PROTO-200K-FLEET: eighty lanes accepted on AGA; two configuration defects found and fixed on the way {#sec-nb-proto200k-fleet-launch}

**What was launched.** Eighty chain-ahead lanes at 200,000 cells per case
(results/p200k_fleet_manifest_2026-09-18.tsv): the DrivAerML pose test (6),
the seven HiLiftAeroML surface rungs (42), the HiLift deflection split (4),
the DrivAerML small-data ladder at 27, 54, 109 and 218 cars (24) and the
DrivAerML interior task (4), each for ISLA, GeoTransolver and Transolver
(GeoTransolver and ISLA only on the deflection split and the interior) at
seeds 42 and 43, 500 epochs, bf16, with the 435-car DrivAerML trio already
running from the earlier launch. Every lane was accepted: alive, no new
traceback, first epoch logged. The wing lanes validate every 25 epochs and
the interior lanes every 10, because a 180-case validation at 200,000 cells
per epoch would dominate wall-clock; the final-epoch checkpoints are scored
in float32 separately as always.

**Defects found by the launch.** Two configurations could not run as
shipped. ISLA's surface config carries DrivAerML's one-scalar, one-vector
head; the HiLift datasets have three scalar and two vector targets, so the
sixteen ISLA wing lanes needed `model.out_scalars=3 model.out_vectors=2`,
as the earlier wing lanes had. More seriously, the volume reference dataset
configuration (`drivaer_ml_volume_reference.yaml`) never computes the unit
freestream direction that the ISLA volume config reads as its global vector
input, so `isla_volume` with its own dataset fails at the first step; the
launch inserted the `ComputeFreestreamDirection` transform after
`CenterMesh`, mirroring the support-token dataset, and the same fix is
applied to the repository copy today. The interior lanes trained by the
earlier RELINT study predate the rename of the global input and read the
physical velocity through the old keyword, which is why the defect was not
seen before.

**Wall-clock.** At the acceptance check the pose lanes were at epoch 20 and
the 27-car ladder lanes at epoch 100, the wing lanes at epochs 1 to 18 and
the GeoTransolver interior lanes at epoch 12; the 1,260-case wing rung will
finish last, in days.

**Addendum, 16:10 PDT (loader).** The 510- and 1,260-case wing lanes at
200,000 cells were data-loading-bound at launch: 0.4 s of GPU work inside a
6.6 s iteration with four loader workers per rank, which projects to about
twelve days for the 1,260-case rung. Their twelve lanes were cancelled after
two epochs and relaunched with sixteen loader workers per rank and a
prefetch factor of four (`kernel/p200k_fleet/p200k_hl_aga.sbatch`); the
other rungs, whose epochs are short, keep the recipe's four workers. The
change touches the input pipeline's throughput only, not what any model
sees.

**Addendum, 16:40 PDT (chain resume).** Two ladder lanes blocked within the
first hours with truncated checkpoints: a four-hour link killed while the
trainer was writing leaves the newest trainer-state file (and sometimes the
model file and a zero-byte normalizer-statistics file) as an unreadable zip,
and the next link fails to resume twice and is blocked by the two-strike
guard. Every launcher now runs a checkpoint pre-flight before training
(`kernel/ckpt_preflight.py`): the files of the newest three epochs are
zip-validated, an incomplete epoch's files move aside together, and the lane
resumes from the newest intact epoch, losing at most two epochs. The two
blocked lanes were repaired by hand the same way and resumed; a sweep of all
eighty lanes found no other incomplete epoch.

## 2026-09-18 — Verdict, HEADS-435: eight routings per block are null at 435 cars (0.0563 against ISLA's 0.0554) while four carry (0.0540); the one-car ordering does not transfer, and multi-head routing stays a research option {#sec-nb-heads435-verdict}

**Setting.** HEADS-435 (@sec-nb-heads435-prereg) trained ISLA with four
and eight independent routings per block on 435 DrivAerML cars at the
exploration budget of 10,000 cells, two seeds each, and scored them in
float32 on the sample-frame probe against ISLA's 0.0554
(results/heads435_reduction_2026-09-18.json). The one-car study
(@sec-nb-formheads-verdict) had found eight routings 19% better than one and
monotone in the head count, and the preregistration's bars were written for
the eight-head pair: closes at or below 0.0530, carries at or below 0.0543,
null at or above 0.0549.

**What we saw.** Four routings score **0.0540** (seeds 0.0537 and 0.0543),
0.975x ISLA, the carries band, with density factor 1.23 inside the contract
band. Eight routings score **0.0563** (seeds 0.0578 and 0.0548), 1.017x
ISLA, the **null** band, with density factor 1.20; GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA
would fall from 0.919 to 0.904 with eight heads and rise to 0.943 with
four. The seed spread of the eight-head pair (0.003) is the largest of any
ISLA arm at this rung.

**Reading.** The one-car floor overstated the routing-multiplicity effect
and inverted its ordering at full data: eight heads, the best one-car arm,
are worse than one at 435 cars, while four heads recover about half the
one-car gain. Whatever the one-car instrument measures (capacity to fit one
geometry), it is not the form deficit of the trained function across cars,
and the deficit anatomy's remaining point is therefore **unattributed**
rather than "the single-routing form". By the preregistration's rule the
option is not promoted: ISLA stays single-routing, `n_heads` stays on the
research branch `isla-heads`, and the four-head result is recorded as a
carried variant at the exploration budget. Two facts argue against pursuing
it further now: the reporting protocol has moved to 200,000 cells, where
the whole form residual is under a point (@sec-nb-tokproto-verdict), and the
fused geometry kernel that keeps ISLA at GeoTransolver's step cost at that
budget is single-routing only. If the 200,000-cell standing leaves a gap
the anatomy cannot place, a four-head lane at that budget is the test.

**Status.** HEADS-435 closed as null on its preregistered arm; the ledger
records the four-head carry.

## 2026-09-18 — Verdict, SG-REF: the similarity gauge is within noise of ISLA at 435 cars (0.0524 against 0.0533 under the stratified draw, overlapping seed ranges); the preference for the relative frame is unopposed on accuracy {#sec-nb-sgref-verdict}

**Setting.** ISLA works in a relative frame: no center is subtracted, and
the length unit is the total measure of the sampled boundary. The
similarity-gauge variant instead centers every token on the
measure-weighted centroid and divides by the root-mean-square radius, and
hands each token its distance and direction from that centroid as extra
invariant seeds. The book prefers ISLA on principle (the centroid of a
sample is not physical knowledge and presumes one closed body,
@sec-isla-variants); this study asked whether the preference costs
accuracy, since the deficit anatomy (@sec-deficit-anatomy) attributes
about two and a half points of GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA to the positional
information the relative frame denies the model. The preregistration is
@sec-nb-sgref-prereg.

**What was run.** A third seed (44) of each configuration trained at 435
DrivAerML cars on the 10,000-cell exploration budget, learning rate 1e-3,
500 epochs, bf16, from the lean class (`kernel/sgref_aga.sbatch`); then
all six checkpoints scored in float32 on the 48 validation cars on the
consistency-benchmark instrument (`bench/bench_lanes_sgref.tsv`, job
790120): the stratified 10,000-cell draw, the independent 10,000-cell
draw, the 10:1-biased 10,000-cell draw and the independent 40,000-cell
draw. Reduction: results/sgref_reduction_2026-09-18.json.

**What we saw.** Surface-pressure error, seed mean with the three seeds in
brackets:

| draw | ISLA | similarity-gauge variant | ratio (variant ÷ ISLA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| stratified, 10,000 cells (readout) | 0.0533 (0.0525 / 0.0537 / 0.0538) | 0.0524 (0.0531 / 0.0516 / 0.0524) | 0.982 |
| independent, 10,000 cells | 0.0557 (0.0549 / 0.0558 / 0.0562) | 0.0546 (0.0555 / 0.0537 / 0.0545) | 0.980 |
| independent, 40,000 cells | 0.0525 (0.0518 / 0.0527 / 0.0530) | 0.0517 (0.0526 / 0.0509 / 0.0517) | 0.984 |
| density factor (biased ÷ independent, 10,000) | 1.21 (1.19 / 1.28 / 1.17) | 1.21 (1.18 / 1.19 / 1.24) | |

**Verdict: within noise.** The similarity gauge sits 1.8% below ISLA under
the stratified draw, past the 1.5% magnitude clause, but the seed ranges
overlap (0.0516 to 0.0531 against 0.0525 to 0.0538), so the "recovers"
bar, which required both, is not met. The same 1.6 to 2.0% offset appears
on every draw, so it is a real but small tendency rather than a
recoverable point of the deficit. Both configurations keep the density
contract (factors 1.21 and 1.21, inside 1.05 to 1.3). The prediction
("within noise, at the edge, the similarity gauge about 1% ahead") was
right in kind and slightly low in size.

**Why it matters.** The price of not being told the body's center is at
most about 2% of pressure error at full data, inside seed noise. Being
told the centroid recovers essentially none of the positional deficit the
anatomy measures against GeoTransolver, which is consistent with that
deficit living in the trained function's use of *absolute* position
rather than in a single summary statistic of the geometry. Peter's ruling
of 2026-09-18 now takes effect: the similarity-gauge variant leaves the
main results (no row of the standing tables, no series of the scoreboard
figures, no column of the ladders) and remains only in collapsed notes
labeled as a diagnostic, where this measurement is quoted as the price of
the relative frame's center-freeness.

**What's next.** LEN-RMS (@sec-nb-lenrms-prereg) decides the length
unit; it inherits this instrument and these six ISLA-side numbers as its
reference arm.

## 2026-09-18 — Interim, PROTO-200K-FLEET ladder: the 27- and 54-car rows at 200,000 cells; the 27-car GeoTransolver pair scores above its 10,000-cell predecessor and a rate control is launched before the row is written {#sec-nb-proto200k-fleet-ladder-interim}

**Setting.** The DrivAerML small-data ladder trains each model on 27, 54,
109 or 218 cars and scores the shared 48-car validation split; the

results/ladder_reduction.json) ran GeoTransolver at learning rate 3e-3
against the legacy centered variant of ISLA, also at 3e-3. The fleet
re-runs the ladder at the reporting protocol of 200,000 cells per case
with ISLA, GeoTransolver at its 435-car best rate of 1e-3, and Transolver
at 3e-3 (@sec-nb-proto200k-fleet-prereg). The 27- and 54-car rungs are
the first to finish; their float32 200,000-cell evaluations are in
`p200k_fp32/` on AGA and reduced in
results/p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json.

**What we saw** (surface-pressure error, seed mean with seeds 42 / 43):

| rung | ISLA | GeoTransolver | Transolver | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27 cars | 0.1507 (0.1451 / 0.1562) | 0.1813 (0.1824 / 0.1802) | 0.1605 (0.1666 / 0.1543) | 1.20 | 1.06 |
| 54 cars | 0.0859 (0.0847 / 0.0871) | 0.0978 (0.0970 / 0.0985) | 0.0861 (0.0866 / 0.0857) | 1.14 | 1.00 |

**The flag.** The preregistration's third bar says any lane whose
200,000-cell error exceeds its 10,000-cell error is a training defect to

**The control.** Four lanes added to the ladder launcher

rate 3e-3, seeds 42 and 43. Reading, stated before the result: if

was the rate and the 27-car row is written with each model at its better
of the two rates (ISLA's control keeps the comparison symmetric); if it
stays above, the 200,000-cell budget itself hurts GeoTransolver at 27 cars
and the row is written with that finding stated. The 27-car ISLA and
Transolver rows are not flagged (ISLA has no same-configuration
10,000-cell predecessor on this ladder; Transolver has none at all).

**Standing so far.** Both rungs satisfy the "budget was the gap" clause

**Addendum, 109 cars (same evening).** ISLA 0.0614 (0.0600 / 0.0627),

GeoTransolver improved on its 10,000-cell predecessor (0.0713), so this
