## 2026-09-25 — Verdict, RANK-IO at 2,048 elasticity cases: prescribed displacement and traction as rank-1 boundary inputs with the equivariant stress head recover 63 to 72% of the log-gap to GeoTransolver-512, reproducing the 512-case result at four times the data; the boundary-value extension of the same vectors recovers 35 to 76% {#sec-nb-rankio-verdict-2048}

**Setting.** On the OLBC elasticity set (one fixed steel plate, per-sample
random prescribed displacement and traction segments) the reference ISLA
fed the prescribed vectors component by component as laboratory-frame
scalars and trailed GeoTransolver-512 by a factor of about two
(GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 0.62 on $\sigma_{11}$ at 512 cases,
0.46 at 2,048). The rank-spec interface lets the same vectors enter
as rank-1 boundary inputs (through their frame cosines and norm) and the
stress leave through the symmetric rank-2 head. At 512 cases this
recovered 43 to 65% of the log-gap (@sec-nb-rankio-verdict-elasticity); the 2,048-case
twin was the "reproduce before it counts" step. A second arm (`ext`)
extends the prescribed vectors to every query as rank-1 query inputs, the
vector form of the Poisson boundary-value extension.

**What we saw** (relative L2, two seeds each; GeoTransolver-512 ÷ arm and
the fraction of the log-gap recovered):

| arm, 2,048 cases | $\sigma_{11}$ | $\sigma_{22}$ | $\sigma_{12}$ | displacement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, components as scalars (R1) | 0.5548 | 0.5032 | 0.5341 | 0.3570 |
| ISLA, rank-1 inputs + rank-2 head (RANK-IO) | 0.3189 (GT÷ 0.81, f 0.72) | 0.3261 (0.80, 0.66) | 0.3288 (0.81, 0.70) | 0.2207 (0.75, 0.63) |
| ISLA, RANK-IO + vector extension (ext) | 0.3098 (0.83, 0.76) | 0.3309 (0.79, 0.64) | 0.3375 (0.79, 0.66) | 0.2726 (0.61, 0.35) |
| ISLA, rank-2 head with scalar inputs (TENSOR-HEAD, one seed) | 0.9809 (0.26) | 0.7810 (0.33) | 0.8918 (0.30) | 0.8078 (0.20) |
| GeoTransolver-512 | 0.2571 | 0.2611 | 0.2671 | 0.1654 |

: OLBC elasticity at 2,048 training cases, 256 test samples, float32 at every node. GT÷ = GeoTransolver-512 ÷ the arm; f = fraction of the log-gap between the scalar-input ISLA and GeoTransolver-512 recovered. Data: results/cluster_return_reductions_2026-09-25.json (group elasticity).

**Reproduced.** RANK-IO recovers 66 to 72% of the log-gap on the three
stress components and 63% on displacement at 2,048 cases, against 51 to
65% and 43% at 512: the fraction *grows* with data, and GeoTransolver's
lead shrinks from a factor of two to 1.2 to 1.3. The vector extension on
top recovers a similar share on stress (64 to 76%) and less on
displacement (35%), so it is not additive with the rank-1 inputs here.
The one-seed TENSOR-HEAD arm, which has the rank-2 head but keeps the
prescribed vectors as scalars, is *worse* than the scalar baseline (0.98
against 0.55 on $\sigma_{11}$): with laboratory-component inputs the
equivariant head has nothing equivariant to build the tensor from, and
the head's basis constraint costs rather than helps. **The input side is
what pays; the head is right only once its inputs are vectors.** That
reading also explains the Tensile2d tensor-axis result
(@sec-nb-tensor-axis-verdict-400). RANK-IO is the recommended
configuration for vector boundary data, with two datasets and two rungs
behind it (elasticity 512 and 2,048; the DeepJEB++ load vector at 1,024,
where it is neutral, @sec-nb-deepjeb-e40-verdict).

## 2026-09-26 — Preregistration, GEO-BIAS-K3: do the nonlinear routing bias and the two extra directions add, or are they one mechanism? Inlet + x + y with the MLP bias, two seeds, laptop GPU {#sec-nb-geo-bias-k3-prereg}

**Question.** GEO-BIAS (@sec-nb-geo-bias-verdict) found that a two-layer
routing bias at K = 1 recovers all of the two-axis velocity gain and a
fifth of the pressure gain. If the bias and the directions are one
mechanism for velocity, adding the bias to the K = 3 arm should leave
velocity where the K = 3 arm has it; if they are different mechanisms,
velocity should improve again. For pressure, where the bias recovered
only a fifth, an additive gain would say the two act on different
channels (routing against seed and read-back).

**Arm.** Inlet + $\hat x$ + $\hat y$ (K = 3) with `geo_bias: mlp` on the
eager region, same 160-airfoil rung, protocol and seeds (42, 43) as the
ladder; float32 relative L2 on the 40 test airfoils, two-seed means.
Comparators: the K = 3 linear arm (pressure 0.267, velocity 0.116) and
the K = 1 MLP arm (0.333, 0.116).

**Bars.** *One mechanism* (velocity): the K = 3 MLP arm within 3% of the
K = 3 linear arm on velocity. *Additive* (velocity): at least 8% better.
*Additive* (pressure): at least 6% better than the K = 3 linear arm (the
bias's own gain at K = 1). *Not additive* (pressure): within 3%.
Prediction: one mechanism on velocity (0.7), additive on pressure (0.5).

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, FRAME-3D (DrivAerML Surface, 435 cars, 200,000 cells): two body axes beside the inlet improve ISLA's pressure by 3.4% and three by 4.8%, both seeds; the 2-D step does not transfer as a step, and neither preregistered bar fires; with the body frame ISLA edges GeoTransolver-512 {#sec-nb-frame3d-verdict}

**Setting.** The nine-arm AirfRANS ladder (@sec-nb-frame-af-h-verdict,
@sec-nb-frame-af-k4-verdict) found a step: beside the inlet direction,
two more distinct in-plane directions cut ISLA's interior pressure error
by a quarter at exploration scale, one more direction did nothing, and a
fourth added nothing. The reading was an overcomplete direction set for
the ambient plane, with a sharp 3-D prediction: three directions (a
complete basis) should sit on the floor and four should show the step.
The falsifier ran at reference scale on the surface task: ISLA R1 at
200,000 cells on 435 DrivAerML cars with the inlet plus the body
$\hat y$ and $\hat z$ (K = 3) and plus all three body axes (K = 4, the
four-vector fused kernel), two seeds each, against the R1 reference pair
and GeoTransolver-512 (bars in the FRAME-3D ledger row: K = 3 within 3%
of R1 and K = 4 at least 10% better confirms the reading; K = 3 gaining
10% refutes it toward "any extra direction pays"; neither gaining bounds
the finding to 2-D or exploration scale). The body axes are written
before the centering transform, so the random rotation augmentation
carries them with the car.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 48 validation cars, seed
means with seeds in parentheses; data results/frame3d_2026-09-26.json):

| arm | pressure | wall shear | ÷ R1 (pressure / shear) | GeoTransolver-512 ÷ arm (pressure) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| ISLA R1, inlet only (reference) | 0.0419 (0.0421, 0.0418) | 0.0657 | 1 / 1 | 0.979 |
| ISLA R1, inlet + body $\hat y$, $\hat z$ (K = 3) | 0.0405 (0.0413, 0.0397) | 0.0633 | 0.966 / 0.964 | 1.013 |
| ISLA R1, inlet + body $\hat x$, $\hat y$, $\hat z$ (K = 4) | 0.0399 (0.0401, 0.0397) | 0.0626 | **0.952 / 0.953** | **1.028** |
| ISLA R2 (24 layers), inlet only | 0.0409 (0.0415, 0.0402) | 0.0641 | 0.974 / 0.976 | 1.004 |
| GeoTransolver-512 (3e-3) | 0.0410 (0.0415, 0.0405) | 0.0655 | 0.979 / 0.997 | 1 |

: FRAME-3D, campaign fa rows 2 to 5 on code_v4, against the REF pairs. Two seeds each; every K = 4 seed is below every R1 seed.

**Neither bar fires.** K = 3 is not flat (3.4% better, just outside the
3% band) and K = 4 is not a step (4.8%, half the 10% bar). The gain is
small and monotone in the number of directions, with no sign of the
2-D ladder's structure (nothing at two, everything at three). The 3-D
prediction of the overcompleteness reading is therefore not confirmed:
either the reading does not transfer from a plane to a volume, or the
step is an exploration-scale phenomenon that a 68M-parameter model at
200,000 cells no longer needs (the same directions bought 25% at 192
wide on 120 airfoils and 10% at 240 airfoils in the size ladder,
@sec-nb-frame-af-size-verdict; here, at 435 cars and twice the width,
5%). The AirfRANS reference-scale twin (fa rows 0 and 1, in the scorer)
separates the two: it is the same 2-D problem at R1 and 800 airfoils.

**What the small gain is worth.** Five percent on DrivAerML Surface at
200,000 cells is the size of the standing itself: the reference ISLA
trails GeoTransolver-512 by 2% (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 0.979), and with the
three body axes it leads by 3% (1.028), both seeds of the K = 4 arm below
both seeds of GeoTransolver-512, and it does so at a fraction of the
parameters. The body axes are legitimate inputs under the contracts
(they rotate with the car, so the model stays equivariant; they carry
the same information GeoTransolver reads from absolute coordinates) and
they cost nothing at inference. Whether they become part of the
reference configuration is a decision for after the AirfRANS twin
reports (the two-datasets rule, @sec-protocol), and it is a change of
the recommended *inputs*, not of the architecture. Depth (R2) buys a
similar 2.6%, so on this dataset the two cheapest improvements to the
reference are the body frame and 24 layers, and they are not yet tested
together.

**Limits.** One dataset at reference scale; the K = 3 arm's seeds split
(0.0413 against 0.0397) more than the K = 4 arm's (0.0401, 0.0397), so
the 3.4% at K = 3 is the least certain number in the table. The wing
body-frame lane (fa rows 6 and 7) remains staged for launch after the
AirfRANS twin.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, GEO-BIAS: a nonlinear routing bias at K = 1 recovers all of the two-axis gain on velocity (0.96 of the log-gap) and a fifth of it on pressure (0.22); linearity is the bottleneck for the vector field, not for the scalar {#sec-nb-geo-bias-verdict}

**Setting.** The direction-count ladder (@sec-nb-frame-af-h-verdict)
left one architectural suspect for why two extra global directions
help ISLA's interior fields: the per-pair routing bias is one *linear*
map of the geometric invariants, and extra directions widen what that
linear map can express. The preregistration (@sec-nb-geo-bias-prereg)
replaced the linear map by a two-layer MLP (16 units) at K = 1 on the
same 160-airfoil rung, two seeds, eager region, and asked what fraction
of the two-axis log-gain it recovers. Both seeds hit a CUDA driver fault
on the laptop near epoch 220 (simultaneously, so external) and resumed
from their checkpoints; the runs completed 300 epochs.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 40 test airfoils, two-seed
means with seeds in parentheses for pressure; data results/geo_bias_2026-09-26.json):

| arm (K = 1 unless stated) | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |
|---|---|---|---|
| inlet only, linear bias (ladder baseline) | 0.3546 (0.301, 0.408) | 0.1303 | 0.2576 |
| inlet only, **MLP bias** | 0.3330 (0.348, 0.318) | 0.1164 | 0.2290 |
| inlet + $\hat x$ + $\hat y$, linear bias (K = 3) | 0.2666 (0.248, 0.285) | 0.1158 | 0.2122 |
| MLP ÷ linear at K = 1 | 0.94 | 0.89 | 0.89 |
| fraction of the two-axis log-gain recovered | **0.22** | **0.96** | 0.61 |

: GEO-BIAS, exploration scale (192 x 12, 120 training airfoils, 20,000 queries).

**Split verdict.** On the deciding field, pressure, the "not the
bottleneck" clause fires (0.22 < 0.4): the nonlinear bias buys 6% where
two directions buy 25%. On velocity the opposite clause would fire: the
MLP bias at K = 1 matches the two-axis arm (0.1164 against 0.1158), recovering
0.96 of the gain, and on eddy viscosity 0.61. **The linearity of the
routing bias is the whole story for the vector field and a small part
of it for the scalar.** That is a useful separation. Velocity leaves
through the equivariant head basis, which at K = 1 has $2K + 3 = 5$ true
vectors and at K = 3 has 9; the head basis was a candidate for the
velocity gain, and this result rules it out: a K = 1 basis with a better
routing reaches the same velocity error, so the extra directions helped
velocity through routing, not through the head. Pressure is read from
the hidden state, and its gain from extra directions runs mostly through
something the routing bias does not touch: the seed features
$\hat n_i \cdot \hat g_k$ (a token's normal orientation in a fixed frame)
or the pooled invariants $\hat r_{is} \cdot \hat g_k$ read back into the
hidden state, which are linear in the directions and richer at K = 3.

**Consequences.** (i) The nonlinear bias is a real architectural gain at
K = 1 (11% on velocity and eddy viscosity, 6% on pressure, about 160
parameters per layer) but it runs on the eager region only, nine times
slower per step than the fused kernel here; it enters the class as an
option and the recommended path stays linear until a fused kernel with a
nonlinear bias exists (engineering candidate, recorded in the ledger).
(ii) The pressure mechanism is narrowed to the seed and read-back
channels; the cheap next control is K = 1 with the MLP bias *and* a
richer seed, which the class does not yet expose, so it is not run. (iii)
At reference scale the whole question is smaller: FRAME-3D found 5% for
three body axes on DrivAerML at 200,000 cells (@sec-nb-frame3d-verdict),
so the exploration-scale mechanism work here bounds, rather than
motivates, changes to the reference configuration. No accuracy claim at
this scale (@sec-protocol).

**Setting.** The local ladder (@sec-nb-frame-af-local-verdict,
@sec-nb-frame-af-h-verdict) found at exploration scale that two extra
distinct in-plane directions beside the inlet cut ISLA's AirfRANS
interior pressure error by a quarter, and the size ladder
(@sec-nb-frame-af-size-verdict) could not pin the step better than 10 to
25% or say what would survive at 800 airfoils. The reference-scale twin
(campaign `fa` rows 0 and 1, `code_v4`): the reference configuration
(384 wide, 12 layers, 256 slices, cosine routing, the four-vector fused
kernel, 5e-4) with the inlet plus the laboratory $\hat x$ and $\hat y$
as global directions (K = 3), 800 training airfoils, 100,000 interior
queries, internal nearest-boundary geometry, two seeds, against the
internal-geometry reference pair of INTERNAL-GEOMETRY (the same model
without the two axes). Bar: pressure at least 10% better with velocity
not more than 5% worse.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 200 test airfoils, seed
means with seeds in parentheses for pressure; data results/frame_af_ref_2026-09-26.json):

| arm | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity | GeoTransolver-volume ÷ arm (p / v / ν) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA R1, inlet only, internal geometry (reference pair) | 0.0341 (0.0322, 0.0359) | 0.0206 | 0.0355 | 0.81 / 1.85 / 0.83 |
| **ISLA R1, inlet + $\hat x$ + $\hat y$, internal geometry** | **0.0282** (0.0274, 0.0290) | **0.0161** | **0.0297** | **0.98 / 2.36 / 0.99** |
| ISLA R1, inlet only, provided geometry (scoreboard arm) | 0.0313 (0.0304, 0.0322) | 0.0153 | 0.0322 | 0.89 / 2.48 / 0.91 |
| GeoTransolver-volume, 1e-3 | 0.0277 (0.0268, 0.0286) | 0.0379 | 0.0293 | 1 |
| frame ÷ internal reference pair | **0.83** | **0.78** | **0.84** | |

: The AirfRANS interior task at reference scale, 200 test airfoils, two seeds each. The provided-geometry arm and GeoTransolver-volume are the interior scoreboard's rows (@sec-interior-airfrans); the frame arm is compared with the internal-geometry pair because it shares that geometry.

**Frame pays, at scale, on both seeds.** Against its own reference pair
the frame arm is 17% better on pressure (0.0274 and 0.0290 against 0.0322
and 0.0359), 22% on velocity and 16% on eddy viscosity, clearing the
bar on every field. By angle of attack the pressure ratio is
0.77 below zero degrees (55 airfoils), 0.89 at 0 to 5 (46), 0.96 at 5 to 10
(61) and 0.71 at 10 and above (38): the gain sits at the ends of
the angle range, where ISLA's interior pressure error was largest
(@sec-nb-hl35-percase addendum), and nearly vanishes at 5 to 10 degrees.
Two things travel with the number. The frame arm runs the internal
geometry, which INTERNAL-GEOMETRY found to cost 27% on velocity against
the stored field on this dataset; the frame recovers that velocity
(0.0161 against the provided-geometry 0.0153) and beats the
provided-geometry arm on pressure and eddy viscosity as well, so a frame
arm on the provided geometry (or on the plane projection now under test)
has room left. And the size ladder's coin flip landed on the high side:
17% at 800 airfoils against 10 to 25% at 30 to 240.

**Against GeoTransolver-volume.** The interior scoreboard's AirfRANS
row (@sec-interior-airfrans) has ISLA leading on velocity by 2.48x and
trailing on pressure and eddy viscosity (0.89 and 0.91). With the two
axes the pressure and eddy-viscosity deficits close to parity
(0.98 and 0.99) and the velocity lead holds (2.36x). By angle of attack,
GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA on pressure moves from 0.76 / 0.93 / 1.16 / 0.78
(reference arm; below zero, 0 to 5, 5 to 10, 10 and above) to 0.88 / 0.96 / 1.21 / 0.96
(frame arm): the deficit GeoTransolver held at the extreme angles is
gone, and this is the GeoTransolver-volume per-angle twin the AirfRANS
anatomy preregistered. **Two datasets now show the effect at protocol
scale**: DrivAerML Surface (three body axes, 5% on pressure, ISLA from
2% behind GeoTransolver-512 to 3% ahead, @sec-nb-frame3d-verdict) and
AirfRANS interior (two axes, 17% on pressure, from 12% behind
GeoTransolver-volume to parity). The effect is much larger in 2-D than in
3-D, in line with the ladder's reading that the third distinct direction
overcompletes a plane but only completes a volume.

**What changes.** The two laboratory axes are legitimate inputs under
the contracts (they rotate with the data), cost nothing, and pay on both
datasets. They become the recommended global inputs for fixed-frame
datasets in the recipe: the AirfRANS and DrivAerML dataset yamls gain the
constant frame fields and the ISLA model yamls the extra global
directions, as labeled *frame* variants beside the reference rows, and
the interior and surface scoreboards carry the frame rows alongside the
reference (@sec-interior-airfrans, @sec-de-result). The reference
configuration itself (the architecture's hyperparameters) is unchanged:
this is a statement about which global vectors a dataset should supply,
and the mechanism ladder says any two distinct fixed directions do. Open:
the frame arm on the provided (or projected) geometry; the wing lane
(fa rows 8 and 9); the body frame with 24 layers on DrivAerML (fa rows 6
and 7, running).

## 2026-09-26 — Interim, INTERNAL-GEOMETRY-PROJ (AirfRANS half): the tangent-plane distance recovers most of the velocity price (1.27x to 1.06x the stored field) but costs pressure (1.04x to 1.12x); the DrivAerML half is in the scorer {#sec-nb-internal-geometry-proj-interim}

**Setting.** INTERNAL-GEOMETRY (@sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict) found
that computing a query's wall distance and direction from the nearest
sampled boundary *centroid* costs 27% on AirfRANS interior velocity
against the stored signed-distance field, and preregistered the fix of
measuring to the nearest cell's tangent plane instead
(`interior_geometry: nearest_plane`, code_v5). The AirfRANS pair (sg
rows 10 and 11, two seeds, R1, 800 airfoils, 100,000 queries) is scored;
the DrivAerML Volume pair is training.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 200 test airfoils, two-seed
means; data results/batch2_reductions_2026-09-26.json, group proj_af):

| geometry | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity | ÷ provided (p / v / ν) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| provided (stored SDF and gradient) | 0.0328 | 0.0161 | 0.0323 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| internal, nearest centroid | 0.0341 | 0.0206 | 0.0355 | 1.04 / 1.27 / 1.10 |
| internal, nearest tangent plane | 0.0369 (0.0360, 0.0377) | 0.0170 | 0.0357 | **1.12 / 1.06 / 1.10** |

: AirfRANS interior task, reference configuration, three geometries for the query's distance and direction.

**Reading.** The projection does what it was built for on velocity: the
price falls from 27% to 6%, so the centroid measurement was indeed the
near-wall velocity's problem. It does not clear the 3% bar, and it moves
pressure the wrong way, from 4% to 12% worse than the stored field, with
eddy viscosity unchanged. The pressure loss is the projection's known
failure: at the trailing edge and at the leading-edge nose the nearest
cell's tangent plane understates the distance (the true nearest point is
the cell's end, not its plane), and the airfoil pressure field is set
exactly there. The centroid distance overstates near a flat wall; the
plane distance understates near a corner; the stored field does neither.
On this half the preregistered "velocity still worse by more than 3%"
clause fires, and a hybrid (plane distance clamped from below by the
nearest-vertex distance, which needs the cell extent the model does not
receive) is the only cheap route left inside the model. Verdict after the
DrivAerML half (sg rows 8 and 9), where the cells are triangles on a
closed surface and the corner case is rarer.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, OLBC-MECH combined channel at 512 Poisson cases: the domain frame on top of the boundary-value extension recovers 0.90 of the log-gap against 0.84 for the extension alone, so the two channels are redundant and the extension is the recipe on Poisson {#sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-verdict}

**Setting.** On the fixed-mesh OLBC Poisson set ISLA trails
GeoTransolver-512 by a factor of about three. The mechanism study
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict) found that a parameter-free boundary-value
extension as query scalars recovers 84% of the log-gap at 512 cases and
the domain frame as two global vectors 19%; the combined arm
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-prereg) asked whether the two add
(recovering at least $\min(1, f + e - 0.1)$) or are redundant (within 0.1
of the larger). The four combined lanes relaunched on 2026-09-25 in the
old-API form after a snapshot mismatch (@sec-nb-cluster-return-2026-09-25);
the 512-case pair is scored.

**What we saw** (relative L2 on $u$ over 256 test samples, two seeds;
data results/batch2_reductions_2026-09-26.json, group olbc_combined_512):
baseline ISLA 0.8671, GeoTransolver-512 0.2791; extension 0.3328 (fraction
0.84), frame 0.6947 (0.20), **frame + extension 0.3113 (0.90;
seeds 0.3034, 0.3193)**. The additive threshold was 0.94;
the combination sits 0.06 above the extension alone, inside the 0.1 band.
**Redundant.** The frame's small contribution at 512 cases is already
contained in the extension's; on the Poisson set the recipe is the
extension (six query scalars, no per-query cost beyond them), and the
frame is not worth its two directions here. The 2,048-case twin is in
the scorer; at that rung the frame alone recovered 67% (one seed,
@sec-nb-olbc-mech-2048-interim), so the additivity question is live
there in a way it is not at 512. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA moves from
0.32 to 0.90 with the combined channel.

The eight 24-layer lanes relaunched at 2.5e-4 after the plateau finding
(@sec-nb-cluster-return-2026-09-25) have their first scored member: the
DeepJEB++ full rung, seed 43, at 0.4874 on von Mises and
0.2453 on displacement against the R1 pair's 0.5075 and 0.2504
(0.96x and 0.98x). The depth rule holds on this dataset too: at the rate
the rule prescribes, 24 layers train and buy a few percent, the same
picture as on DrivAerML Surface. The second seed and the OLBC and lug
R2 relaunches are in flight; the DeepJEB depth row is restated when the
pair is in. Data: results/batch2_reductions_2026-09-26.json (group deepjeb_r2_rate).

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, INTERNAL-GEOMETRY-PROJ: the tangent-plane distance does not fix the internal geometry (AirfRANS velocity 1.06x but pressure 1.12x the stored field; DrivAerML Volume 1.16x on velocity, worse than the centroid's 1.14x); where a dataset carries a stored signed-distance field, `provided` is the documented default {#sec-nb-internal-geometry-proj-verdict}

**Setting.** The internal nearest-boundary geometry costs 14% (DrivAerML
Volume) and 27% (AirfRANS) on interior velocity against the stored
signed-distance field (@sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict). The
preregistered fix measured the distance to the nearest sampled cell's
tangent plane instead of to its centroid (`interior_geometry:
nearest_plane`, code_v5), exact on a flat wall. Both halves are scored:
the AirfRANS pair (@sec-nb-internal-geometry-proj-interim) and now the
DrivAerML Volume pair (sg rows 8 and 9, R1, 200,000 cells, 48 validation
cars, two seeds).

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2, two-seed means, ratio to the
provided-geometry pair; data results/batch2_reductions_2026-09-26.json,
groups proj_af and proj_drvol):

| dataset | geometry | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AirfRANS | internal, centroid | 1.04 | 1.27 | 1.10 |
| AirfRANS | internal, tangent plane | 1.12 | 1.06 | 1.10 |
| DrivAerML Volume | internal, centroid | 1.03 | 1.14 | 1.02 |
| DrivAerML Volume | internal, tangent plane | 1.05 | 1.16 | 1.03 |

: Internal geometries ÷ provided geometry (above 1 = worse than the stored field). DrivAerML plane seeds on pressure 0.0417, 0.0414 against provided 0.0397.

**Refuted as a fix.** On the airfoils the plane distance trades a
velocity gain for a pressure loss; on the cars it is worse than the
centroid on every field. The centroid overstates the distance near a
flat wall by up to half a cell, the plane understates it wherever the
nearest surface point is a cell edge or corner, and on a closed
triangulated car surface that is common enough to cancel the gain. The
stored field is the true distance to the nearest point on the surface,
which neither one-sample estimate reproduces; a correct internal
estimate needs the cell's extent (its vertices) or a second-nearest
sample, neither of which the model receives, and it is not worth
carrying through the Triton search for a velocity price the stored field
removes for free.

**Decisions.** (i) Where a dataset carries a full-mesh signed-distance
field and gradient, `interior_geometry: provided` is the documented
default and the recipe's interior configurations use it (the scoreboard
rows already do). (ii) `nearest_boundary` stays as the fallback for
datasets without a stored field, with its measured price stated in the
class docstring (14 to 27% on interior velocity, 3 to 4% on pressure).
(iii) `nearest_plane` stays in the class as a documented, measured-worse
option so the record is runnable (@sec-nb-internal-geometry-proj-interim),
not as a recommendation. (iv) The frame result on AirfRANS
(@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict) was measured on the internal centroid
geometry and still beat the provided-geometry reference on pressure; a
frame arm on the provided geometry is the natural next lane and is
preregistered in the FRAME ledger row.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, DeepJEB R2 at the depth rate: 24 layers train at 2.5e-4 and score within 2% of 12 layers (0.98x on von Mises, 1.01x on displacement, two seeds); depth does not pay on DeepJEB++ {#sec-nb-deepjeb-r2-rate-verdict}

The second seed of the relaunched 24-layer DeepJEB++ full-rung lane is
scored: R2 at 2.5e-4 gives 0.4974 on von Mises (seeds 0.5074,
0.4874) and 0.2536 on displacement against the R1 pair's
0.5075 and 0.2504. The seeds straddle R1 (one 4% better, one at
parity), so the DEEPJEB ledger's depth clause (R2 within 1.5% of R1 means
depth does not pay) fires: **depth does not pay on DeepJEB++**, as on
DrivAerML Surface where it bought 2.6%. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ R2 is
1.19 and 1.29. The plateau at 5e-4 was a rate failure and nothing
else. The OLBC and lug R2 relaunches decide the same question on the
fixed-mesh sets. Data: results/batch2_reductions_2026-09-26.json (group deepjeb_r2_rate).

## 2026-09-26 — Launched, FRAME-WING: the body frame (span and up axes) on the 35-wing rung at the reference configuration, two seeds, campaign fa rows 8-9 {#sec-nb-frame-wing-launch}

**Setting.** The body frame as extra global directions is now the
recommended input on fixed-frame datasets, on the strength of two
protocol-scale results: on AirfRANS the two laboratory axes cut interior
pressure error 17% (@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict), and on DrivAerML
Surface the three body axes cut pressure error 4.8%
(@sec-nb-frame3d-verdict). The high-lift wing rung is the third fixed-frame
dataset in the program and the one where ISLA trails GeoTransolver-512
most: 0.77 of its pressure error at 4 to 14 degrees and 0.67 from 16
degrees, where the flow separates (@sec-nb-hl35-percase). The wing lane
was preregistered there and staged on 2026-09-23; it waited on the
code_v4 snapshot (the fused kernel with up to four per-point vectors).

**What was launched.** Two lanes, fa rows 8 and 9 (seeds 42 and 43), on
the 35-wing super-scarce split at 200,000 cells,
the reference configuration and its rate 5e-4, code_v4. The dataset
variant writes two constant global vectors, span $\hat y = (0, 1, 0)$ and
up $\hat z = (0, 0, 1)$, before the centering step so that the rotation
augmentation, inserted right after centering, rotates them with the wing.
The model reads them beside the far-field direction as three global
directions (K = 3), the same channel as the DrivAerML body-frame lanes.
The five surface targets (pressure, temperature, density, velocity, wall
shear) are the ones the reference pair predicts. The staged model file
carried the DrivAerML output pair by mistake; the outputs dict was
corrected to the five HiLift targets before launch. The first launch
(jobs 882507 and 882508) failed on both seeds within a minute with
"Model YAML must declare `input_type`": the staging script had placed a
comment line above the Hydra `# @package _global_` directive, which must
be the first line, so the model block landed under the wrong
configuration key. The directive was moved back to the top and the pair
relaunched at 10:45 EDT (the two-strike blocked markers cleared).

**Prediction and bar.** On the cars, the span and up pair bought 3.4% of
pressure error. The expectation here is a gain of the same order, not the
2-D step. The preregistered bar (@sec-nb-hl35-percase) is on the deficit
to GeoTransolver-512: the frame pair's pressure error must narrow the
log-gap by at least 10% in either angle group, which is 2.6% of pressure
error at 4 to 14 degrees and 4% at 16 to 22 degrees, both seeds, against
the reference pair. A gain at high angle only would locate the frame's
value at separation, where the angle of attack matters most to the
pressure field. **One caveat is recorded in advance:** the reference
pair ran on the code_ref snapshot and this pair runs on code_v4; the two
snapshots are exact on the kernel (@sec-nb-frame-af-y-eager-verdict) and
share every configuration value, but the comparison is across snapshots.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, OLBC-MECH combined channel at 2,048 Poisson cases: frame + extension recovers 0.84 of the log-gap against 0.83 for the extension alone, so the channels are redundant at both rungs and the additive prediction is refuted {#sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-2048-verdict}

**Setting.** The OLBC Poisson set is one fixed mesh with per-sample random
Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin segments, the dataset where ISLA trails
GeoTransolver-512 by the widest margin (about four-fold at 2,048 training
cases). Two contract-preserving remedies were measured one at a time
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict, @sec-nb-olbc-mech-2048-interim): the domain's
two axes as global vectors, and a parameter-free boundary-value extension
(the measure-weighted inverse-square-distance average of the prescribed
values per condition type, plus the distance to the nearest labeled cell,
as six query scalars). The preregistration
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-prereg) predicted that at 2,048 cases the two
would add, because the frame's share there (67%) looked positional and the
extension's looked like value transport. At 512 cases they were redundant
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-verdict).

**What we saw** (relative L2 on $u$ over the 256 test cases; data
results/batch3_reductions_2026-09-26.json, group olbc_combined_2048).
Baseline ISLA 0.3949 and GeoTransolver-512 0.0981 (two seeds each);
extension 0.1250 (fraction 0.83 of the log-gap, one seed); frame 0.1555
(0.67, one seed); **frame + extension 0.1228 (0.84; seeds 0.1164,
0.1291)**. The additive threshold was $f + e - 0.1$, which exceeds one, so
the additive clause asked for the gap to close; the combination sits
0.01 above the extension alone, well inside the 0.1 redundancy band.
**Redundant at 2,048 as at 512, and the prediction of additivity is
refuted.** The frame's 67% is not a separate positional channel: whatever
it tells the model about where a query sits relative to the domain, the
extension's distance-to-labeled-cell scalar and its value averages already
tell it. On the Poisson set the recipe is the extension alone.
GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA with the extension is 0.78 at 2,048 cases (0.80
with both channels), against 0.25 for the reference. The remaining gap is
the standing that enters the chapter's mechanism passage, and it is a
one-dataset mechanism result: the extension's twin on the elasticity set
was the rank-1 input channel of RANK-IO (@sec-nb-rankio-verdict-2048).

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, FRAME-3D-R2: the three body axes and 24 layers do not add on DrivAerML Surface (0.943 of the reference's pressure error against 0.952 for the axes alone and 0.974 for depth alone); the axes carry the gain {#sec-nb-frame3d-r2-verdict}

**Setting.** On DrivAerML Surface (435 cars, 200,000 cells) the two
measured improvements to the reference configuration are the three body
axes as further global directions, worth 4.8% of pressure error
(@sec-nb-frame3d-verdict), and doubling the depth to 24 layers, worth
2.6% at twice the step time and memory (@sec-nb-ref-verdict). The
FRAME-3D-R2 ledger row asked whether they add: additive if the combined
model reaches 0.93 of the reference (the product of the two gains, 0.928,
within 1%), redundant if within 1% of the better single change (0.952).

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 48 validation cars, two seeds;
data results/batch3_reductions_2026-09-26.json, group frame3d_r2). The
24-layer model with the four global directions scores **0.0396 on
pressure (seeds 0.0397, 0.0394) and 0.0620 on wall shear**, which is
0.943 of the reference on pressure and 0.944 on wall shear. Against the
axes alone it is 0.991 on both fields, inside the 1% band; against depth
alone it is 0.968. The additive clause (0.93) is missed by 1.3 points.
**Redundant by the preregistered bar**: depth adds 1% on top of the
axes, where it added 2.6% on its own. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ this model is
1.04 on pressure and 1.06 on wall shear.

**Why it matters.** Both changes lift the same part of the error. The
reading that fits is that the extra depth was buying a better resolution
of the car's orientation-dependent pressure field, which the axes supply
directly as invariants of the seed. For the reference this settles the
DrivAerML question: the body axes are the recommended input
(@sec-using-inputs), and a 24-layer model is not worth twice the cost
with or without them. Both seeds of both arms agree; the finding is one
dataset and joins the depth-does-not-pay results on DeepJEB++
(@sec-nb-deepjeb-r2-rate-verdict) and the OLBC and lug relaunches at the
depth rate that are still training.

## 2026-09-26 — Preregistration, GEO-BIAS-PROTO: does the nonlinear routing bias carry the frame's velocity gain at protocol scale, on AirfRANS and DrivAerML Surface? Reference configuration with the MLP bias, K = 1, two seeds each, campaign gb {#sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-prereg}

**Setting.** The frame ladder on the 160-airfoil rung
(@sec-nb-frame-af-h-verdict) traced the gain from two extra global
directions to the number of distinct directions the routing bias sees,
not to the physics of a frame. The GEO-BIAS arm
(@sec-nb-geo-bias-verdict) then replaced the linear map from a
point-anchor pair's invariants to its routing bias with a two-layer MLP
(Linear(n_geo, 16), GELU, Linear(16, 1)) at K = 1 and recovered 0.96 of the
two-axis log-gain on velocity, 0.61 on eddy viscosity and 0.22 on
pressure. Both were exploration-scale results (192 wide, 120 training
airfoils, 20,000 queries), where no accuracy claim is made
(@sec-protocol). The question is whether the mechanism survives at the
reference configuration on two datasets. The fused geometry kernel
computes the linear bias only, so these lanes run the eager region; the
MLP inside the kernel is the engineering follow-up, started alongside.

**Hypothesis.** The nonlinearity of the pair-to-bias map is the capacity
that the extra directions supply for the vector field: at protocol scale
the MLP bias at K = 1 recovers most of the frame's velocity gain and
little of its pressure gain, on both datasets where the frame was
measured.

**Arms and comparators.** Four lanes, campaign gb, code_v5 and recipe_v3
(the snapshot that carries `geo_bias`): AirfRANS, the reference
configuration on the internal geometry with `geo_bias: mlp`, 800 training
airfoils, 100,000 queries, seeds 42 and 43; DrivAerML Surface, the
reference with `geo_bias: mlp`, 435 cars, 200,000 cells, seeds 42 and 43.
Comparators are the scored pairs: the AirfRANS internal-geometry
reference pair (0.0341 / 0.0206 / 0.0355 pressure / velocity / eddy
viscosity, @sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict) and its frame arm (0.83 /
0.78 / 0.84 of it, @sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict); the DrivAerML reference
pair (0.0419 pressure) and its body-axes arms (K = 3: 0.966, K = 4: 0.952,
@sec-nb-frame3d-verdict).

**Bars, in the fraction of the frame's log-gain the MLP recovers,
seed means, both seeds on the same side.** On AirfRANS: *mechanism holds*
if velocity recovers at least 0.5 of the frame's log-gain (the MLP arm at
or below 0.88 of the reference's velocity error) while pressure recovers
less than 0.5 (above 0.91 of the reference's pressure error); *general
improvement* if both fields recover at least 0.5; *null* if velocity
recovers under 0.25 (above 0.94). On DrivAerML Surface (one scalar field):
*carries over to 3-D* if pressure reaches 0.952 of the reference or
better, the K = 4 arm's mark; *3-D null* if it stays above 0.976 (under
half the K = 4 gain); between, reported. Predictions: AirfRANS mechanism
holds (0.7), DrivAerML 3-D null (0.6, since pressure was the field the
MLP did not recover in 2-D). The eager region's step time and memory are
recorded beside the reference's as the price the fused follow-up must
remove; the result enters the book only with the fused kernel exact
against this eager path, so the accuracy claim and the speed claim are
one configuration.

## 2026-09-26 — Engineering, the MLP routing bias runs inside the fused geometry kernel: exact against the eager region, 2.7x faster and 4.5x leaner than eager on the laptop GPU, 6.7x the linear kernel's region time {#sec-nb-geo-bias-kernel}

**Setting.** ISLA's per-layer geometry region evaluates, for every
point-anchor pair, a handful of relational invariants, a routing bias from
them, the point-to-slice softmax and the mix-weighted pooling of the
invariants. The fused Triton kernel (@sec-nb-kernel-study) computes that
region on register tiles and never writes the (points x slices x
invariants) intermediates. Until today it implemented only the linear
bias head, so the MLP head of the GEO-BIAS study
(@sec-nb-geo-bias-verdict) ran on the eager region, which on the laptop
GPU is nine times slower at exploration scale and materializes a (points x
slices x 16) hidden tensor per layer at protocol scale.

**What changed** (commit 9b799ac4). The kernel takes a compile-time
hidden width `H` (0 for the linear head). For `H > 0` it evaluates the
hidden units one at a time on the tile: pre-activation, exact-erf GELU,
and the unit's contribution to the bias, so no per-unit tensor is ever
larger than one tile. The backward recomputes each unit, accumulates the
gradient on the invariants across units, and writes the per-tile partial
sums of the weight gradients (W1, b1, W2) beside the linear kernel's,
reduced by torch as before (deterministic, no atomics). The Python wrapper
packs the Sequential's parameters into one flat buffer, so autograd routes
the gradient back through the concatenation without a new custom op. The
class no longer refuses `geo_bias="mlp"` under `geo_kernel="fused"` and
the automatic resolution picks the fused path for it.

**Verification.** Region level, both heads, every (K, P) in the kernel
grid, float64 and float32: outputs and every gradient agree with the eager
region to 1e-16 and 1e-7 relative. Model level, K = 2 with the MLP head in
float64: forward 1e-11, every parameter gradient 1e-10. The 51 kernel tests
and the 29 model tests that touch the region pass; the cluster snapshot
code_v6 (code_v5 plus this overlay) is under its own verification job.

**Cost** (data results/geo_bias_kernel_timing_2026-09-26.json; laptop
GPU, one region, 20,000 points x 256 slices, K = 1, bf16, forward +
backward): fused linear 5.8 ms and 0.18 GiB; fused MLP 38.7 ms and 0.18
GiB; eager linear 79 ms and 0.49 GiB; eager MLP 103 ms and 0.82 GiB. The
fused MLP is 2.7x faster and 4.5x leaner than the eager MLP, and its
memory is the linear kernel's; but it costs 6.7x the linear kernel's
region time, because the region turns from memory-bound into
arithmetic-bound (16 hidden units and 16 error functions per pair). Whether
that matters at the reference configuration is a model-level question:
the region is one part of a block whose attention and MLP GEMMs dominate
at 384 wide. The fused twin lanes of GEO-BIAS-PROTO (campaign gb rows 4-5,
code_v6, one seed per dataset) measure the step time and memory at
protocol scale against the eager pair and, incidentally, check the two
paths agree at scale. Optimization candidates if the price matters:
hoisting the per-unit weight loads, a cheaper erf, a larger tile for the
MLP branch.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, FORCEREF: on the 200,000-cell DrivAerML checkpoints the drag error against the full surface is 2.6% for both ISLA and GeoTransolver-512, of which 2.4% is the 200,000-cell sample itself; against the sampled cells the model error is 0.9% (ISLA) and 0.8% (GeoTransolver-512) {#sec-nb-forceref-verdict}

**Setting.** Every DrivAerML Surface number in this book is a field error
on 200,000 cells drawn from a vehicle surface of 14.6 to 19.8 million
cells (1.2% of the area). The quantity an engineer takes from such a
surrogate is the integrated load, and the FORCEREF ledger row asked for
lift and drag on the reference checkpoints with the force reference
stated twice: integrated over the sampled cells the model was scored on,
and over the full surface. The two references differ by the sampling
error of the Horvitz-Thompson estimate, which the recipe's force
integration already forms (each retained cell carries the inverse
inclusion probability $N/k$ as its measure weight, so the sampled sum is
an unbiased estimate of the full-surface integral). The force
coefficient vector is $\sum_c (-C_p \mathbf{n} + \mathbf{C}_f)_c A_c w_c$
with $A_\text{ref} = 1$, $C_p = (p - p_\infty)/q_\infty$,
$\mathbf{C}_f = \boldsymbol{\tau}_w/q_\infty$; drag is the component
along $\mathbf{U}_\infty$ and lift the component along $z$
orthogonalized against it. The cell normals follow the cell winding, as
in the recipe; on this dataset that makes the drag coefficient negative
(the stored winding points inward), a common sign that every relative
error and correlation below ignores.

**What was run.** Evaluation only. The four reference checkpoints (ISLA
reference seeds 42 and 43, GeoTransolver-512 seeds 42 and 43, 500 epochs
at 200,000 cells) were scored on the 48 validation cars by the same
inference command as the P200KFLEET scorer (float32, 200,000 cells,
code_ref snapshot) with the per-car predictions kept
(kernel/forceref/forceref_aga.sbatch). A separate integrator
(kernel/forceref/forceref_integrate.py, copied to
results/campaigns_2026-09-26/forceref/) then formed three coefficients per
car: the prediction on the sampled cells, the ground truth on the same
cells, and the ground truth on all cells of the full validation mesh,
read from the raw dataset in physical units. The integrator reproduces
the recipe's own per-car force numbers to $9 \times 10^{-8}$, and the
200,000 sampled cells are the same for all four checkpoints (the reader
draws them with a per-case generator; the sampled truth agrees across
runs to the last bit). Reducer results/forceref_reduce_2026-09-26.py;
artifact results/forceref_2026-09-26.json.

**What we saw** (48 cars, two seeds per architecture, relative L1 over
the population of cars). The sampled-cell truth misses the full-surface
drag by 2.4% (median per car 1.7%, worst car 11.3%, run_17, where the
sample reads 0.503 against 0.567) and the full-surface lift by 30%
(mean absolute error 0.040 on a mean lift magnitude of 0.137; median per
car 0.034, worst 0.137). The sample's represented area matches the full
area to 0.06%, so the weights are consistent; the error is the
statistical noise of a 1.2% sample of a signed integrand with heavy
cancellation, and lift, the smaller residual of the larger pressure
forces, suffers more than drag. **Against the full surface, ISLA's drag
error is 2.62% (seeds 2.56%, 2.68%) and GeoTransolver-512's is 2.65%
(2.59%, 2.72%)**; against the sampled truth the same predictions are
0.92% (0.85%, 0.99%) and 0.85% (0.84%, 0.85%) off. Lift reads the same
way: 31.3% and 31.5% against the full surface, 9.9% and 8.4% against the
sampled cells. Correlation of predicted with true drag over the 48 cars
is 0.974 (ISLA) and 0.974 (GeoTransolver-512) against the full surface
and 0.997 and 0.998 against the sampled cells; the sampled truth itself
correlates with the full-surface truth at 0.976 for drag and 0.951 for
lift. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA is 1.01 on drag and 1.01 on lift against
the full surface, 0.92 on drag and 0.85 on lift against the sampled
cells. On 37 of 48 cars the sampling error in drag exceeds ISLA's model
error at the same cells (38 of 48 for lift).

**Why it matters.** Two readings. First, at the reporting protocol the
force error an engineer would see is set by the 200,000-cell sample, not
by the model: both architectures predict the sampled-cell integral to
within 1% in drag, and the sample misses the full surface by 2.4%. A
force claim on this dataset therefore needs either the full surface at
inference (the recipe's default; the P200KFLEET protocol caps the cells
at the training count) or a stated sampling band; the book's field
errors are unaffected, since they are computed on the same cells for
every model. Second, the two architectures are indistinguishable in
integrated load against the full surface (ratios 1.01), and against the
sampled cells GeoTransolver-512 is 8% better in drag and 15% better in
lift; the drag difference is inside the seed spread and the lift
difference outside it. Both facts are one dataset (DrivAerML
Surface), so the sampling reading is interim until a second surface set
with full-mesh loads is measured; the side force is in the artifact and
not discussed, its per-car magnitudes being too small for a relative
error to mean anything.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, FRAME-PROVIDED: the laboratory frame and the stored geometry add on AirfRANS (0.80 / 0.81 / 0.91 of the provided-geometry reference on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity; 0.93 / 0.81 / 0.99 of the frame on internal geometry); ISLA leads GeoTransolver-volume on all three fields; DrivAerML Volume twin launched {#sec-nb-frame-provided-verdict}

**Setting.** Two inputs each improved ISLA's AirfRANS interior prediction
at the reference configuration: the dataset's stored signed-distance field
in place of the geometry computed inside the model from the sampled
boundary (velocity 1.27x better, @sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict), and
the two laboratory axes as global directions beside the inlet (pressure
17%, velocity 22%, eddy viscosity 16% better,
@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict). The frame result was measured on the
internal geometry, so the FRAME-PROVIDED ledger row asked whether the two
add: *additive* if the combination is at least 10% better than the
provided-geometry reference pair on pressure and at least 5% better than
the internal-geometry frame arm on velocity; *redundant* if within 3% of
the frame arm on every field.

**What was run.** Campaign fa rows 10 and 11 (code_v4, recipe_v4): the
reference configuration with `interior_geometry: provided` and the two
axes (K = 3), 800 training airfoils, 100,000 queries, seeds 42 and 43,
scored in float32 on the 200 test airfoils. Comparators: the
provided-geometry reference pair (sg rows 6-7), the frame arm on internal
geometry (fa rows 0-1), the internal-geometry reference pair (sg rows
4-5), and GeoTransolver-volume from the interior scoreboard. Data:
results/frame_provided_2026-09-26.json.

**What we saw** (seed means; pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity). The
combination scores 0.0262 / 0.0130 / 0.0295 (seeds 0.0252 and 0.0271 on
pressure, 0.0125 and 0.0135 on velocity). That is **0.80 / 0.81 / 0.91 of
the provided-geometry reference** (0.0327 / 0.0159 / 0.0311) and **0.93 /
0.81 / 0.99 of the frame on internal geometry** (0.0282 / 0.0161 /
0.0297); against the internal-geometry reference it is 0.77 / 0.63 / 0.83.
Both additive clauses fire (20% on pressure against 10% asked; 19% on
velocity against 5%). **Additive.** The frame carries the pressure gain
and the stored geometry carries the velocity gain; the eddy viscosity is
the frame's alone (the stored field adds nothing on top, 0.99). Against
GeoTransolver-volume (0.0277 / 0.0379 / 0.0293) the combined model is
ahead on every field: GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA = 1.06 on pressure,
2.92 on velocity and 1.00 on eddy viscosity, where the reference row of
the interior scoreboard reads 0.89 / 2.48 / 0.91 and the frame-on-internal
row 0.98 / 2.36 / 0.99.

**Why it matters.** The two inputs are different information. The frame
supplies orientation invariants that fix the pressure field's dependence
on the angle of attack; the stored field supplies an exact distance and
direction to the wall that the sampled boundary cannot, which is what the
velocity near the wall needs. Neither is a change to the architecture:
both are inputs a fixed-frame dataset with a stored distance field can
supply, and the recipe's AirfRANS configuration carries them as a labeled
variant. It is one dataset. The DrivAerML Volume twin launched at the
same time (fa rows 12-15, code_v4): the reference with the three body
axes on the internal geometry and on the provided geometry, two seeds
each, against the sg Volume pairs (internal 0.0655 / 0.0409 / 0.0894 and
provided 0.0576 / 0.0397 / 0.0874 on velocity / pressure / eddy viscosity,
@sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict). Prediction, from the Surface task
where the axes bought 4.8% of pressure: the frame buys under 5% of
pressure on the Volume task and adds to the stored geometry's velocity
gain (the additive clause is the same, 10% and 5%). If the Volume twin is
additive too, the recommended AirfRANS and DrivAerML Volume inputs are the
frame plus the stored field, and the scoreboard rows carry them as the
labeled variant.

*Addendum, protocol scale (2026-09-26, 14:40 EDT; data
results/geo_bias_kernel_timing_2026-09-26.json, key protocol_scale).*
Whole-epoch wall time on one GB300 node, epochs 5 to 40, seed 42 lanes of
campaign gb: with the MLP bias the fused kernel takes 57.5 s per epoch on
AirfRANS (800 airfoils, 100,000 queries) against 84.4 s for the eager
region, and 53.6 s against 78.6 s on DrivAerML Surface (435 cars, 200,000
cells), 0.68x on both. Against the fused linear kernel of the frame lanes
(34.2 s at K = 3 on AirfRANS, 24.6 s at K = 4 on DrivAerML) the MLP bias
costs 1.7x and 2.2x the epoch, so at the reference width the region's
arithmetic is a visible share of the step and the MLP bias is not free.
The optimization candidates above are the follow-up if GEO-BIAS-PROTO
finds a gain worth paying for.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, SCALE-HL: on the 510-wing rung cells are flat above 100,000 for GeoTransolver and Transolver (0.99, 0.98), GeoTransolver does not gain from width (512 ÷ 256 = 1.00), ISLA does (384 ÷ 192 = 0.84 linear, 0.96 cosine; 768 ÷ 384 = 0.97), and the deficit is width-independent under cosine routing (0.90 to 0.93) but not under linear (0.77 to 0.92); GeoTransolver-512 holds the wing memory frontier {#sec-nb-scalehl-verdict}

**Setting.** ISO-COST (@sec-nb-isocost-verdict) found on 435 DrivAerML
cars that neither ISLA nor GeoTransolver turns cells per case into
accuracy above 100,000, that a width doubling buys both about 7%, that
ISLA-768 does not improve on ISLA-384, and that ISLA-384 at 100,000 cells
sits on the iso-memory frontier against GeoTransolver-512. SCALE-HL
(@sec-nb-scalehl-prereg) is the second-dataset twin on the 510-wing
HiLiftAeroML rung: twelve lanes at 100,000 training cells (ISLA 192 / 384
/ 768 at the width rule, GeoTransolver 256 / 512 at 3e-3, Transolver 256),
scored in float32 at 200,000 cells on the 180 validation wings, two seeds,
with the fleet's 200,000-cell medium-rung lanes as the cells comparison.
The twelve were launched on 2026-09-20 with linear routing, two days
before cosine routing became the class default; the ROUTE-NORM 510-wing
lanes (cosine 192 and 384 at 1e-3, linear 384 at 1e-3, 100,000 cells) are
read beside them. Data: results/scalehl_2026-09-26.json (reducer
results/scalehl_reduce_2026-09-26.py; step time and memory from each
lane's own log, results/campaigns_2026-09-20/shl/cost_2026-09-26.tsv).

**What we saw** (seed-mean pressure relative L2; seeds in parentheses).

- *Cells.* GeoTransolver-256 at 100,000 cells scores 0.0383 (0.0377,
  0.0389) against 0.0388 at 200,000 cells at the same 3e-3 rate, a ratio of
  0.99 [superseded 2026-10-01: the seed-42 value was a 9-case partial
  scoring; the full 180-case file gives 0.0385, the arm 0.0387 and the
  ratio 1.00, @sec-nb-scalehl-cells-verdict]; Transolver-256 0.0401 against 0.0409, 0.98. **Cells are flat above
  100,000 on the wings for both baselines**, inside the 2% bar. ISLA-192
  cannot be read: its 200,000-cell fleet lane is linear-routed at 1e-3 and
  one seed sat at a validation loss 22 times the other's (0.121 against
  0.0055, the plateau signature ROUTING-SAT measured as routing collapse),
  scoring 0.5945 against 0.0556; the 100,000-cell pair is 0.0495 (0.0450,
  0.0539). The clause is decided by the cosine twin launched today
  (campaign sc, cosine 192 at 1e-3, 200,000 cells, two seeds) against the
  cosine 192 lane at 100,000 cells (0.0427; 0.0433, 0.0421).
- *Width.* **GeoTransolver-512 scores 0.0382 (0.0368, 0.0396) against
  GeoTransolver-256's 0.0383: a ratio of 1.00, no gain from doubling
  width**, where the cars gave 7%; GeoTransolver is not parameter-bound at
  510 wings. ISLA-384 at 5e-4 scores 0.0416 (0.0409, 0.0424) against
  ISLA-192's 0.0495, a ratio of 0.84 under linear routing, but the 192 pair
  is the unstable one (seeds 18% apart); under cosine routing 384 at 1e-3
  scores 0.0411 (0.0413, 0.0409) against 192's 0.0427, a ratio of 0.96.
  **Width carries for ISLA on both readings (4% under cosine), not for
  GeoTransolver.**
- *Turnover.* ISLA-768 at 2.5e-4 scores 0.0405 (0.0409, 0.0401), 0.97 of
  ISLA-384: a 3% gain, so **the DrivAerML turnover at 384 is not
  reproduced** on the wings; the third doubling still pays there.
- *Deficit under width.* GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA at the default widths is
  0.77 (256 against linear 192) and at matched parameters 0.92 (512
  against 384): a rise of 0.14, which under the preregistered instrument
  reads as width closing part of the deficit. Under cosine routing the
  same ratios are 0.90 (256 against cosine 192) and 0.93 (512 against
  cosine 384), a rise of 0.03: **width-independent**. The two readings
  differ because the linear 192 lane's deficit is training instability,
  not capacity; the cosine reading is the one that describes the
  architecture. With ISLA-768 the ratio is 0.94.
- *Iso-memory.* GeoTransolver-512 peaks at 51.8 GB per GPU at 100,000
  cells; ISLA's best lane under that budget is ISLA-768 at 40.1 GB and
  0.0405, and GeoTransolver-256 at 40.2 GB scores 0.0383. **On the wings
  GeoTransolver holds the memory frontier** (0.94 at equal memory), where
  on the cars ISLA did. Step times: ISLA 0.16 / 0.17 / 0.22 s at 192 / 384
  / 768, GeoTransolver 0.27 / 0.30 s at 256 / 512, Transolver 0.17 s.
- *Routing, beside.* The linear 384 control at 1e-3 plateaued at 0.68
  (both seeds; 16x the cosine lane's error at the same rate), the
  collapse ROUTE-NORM predicted; linear 384 at the rule rate 5e-4 trained
  cleanly (0.0416) and cosine 384 at 1e-3 is 1% better than it.

**Why it matters.** Two of the four DrivAerML statements carry to the
wings: cells stop paying at 100,000 for the baselines (ISLA's reading
pending the cosine twin), and width pays for ISLA. Two do not: on the
wings GeoTransolver has stopped gaining from width at 510 cases while
ISLA has not, and the ISLA turnover moves from 384 to at least 768. The
wing deficit narrows with ISLA's width (0.90 at 192, 0.93 at 384, 0.94 at
768 under cosine routing against GeoTransolver's best), and it narrows
with data (0.77 at 35 wings, @sec-nb-hl35-percase; 0.93 at 510): both
say ISLA is the more capacity- and data-bound model on wings, and the
learning-curve statement of @sec-nb-campaigns-2026-09-21-prereg is the place where
that is measured directly (its wing half, cosine ISLA 192 / 384 / 768 and
GeoTransolver 1,024 at 100,000 cells, is in flight). For the reference
configuration nothing changes: 384 wide at 100,000 cells remains the
frontier point on the cars, and on the wings a wider ISLA is the labeled
option for a user with the memory. The width-carries and turnover
statements in @sec-equal-budget are restated as one dataset each, with
the wing numbers beside.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, FRAME-WING: the body frame (span and up axes) cuts ISLA's 35-wing pressure error 11% on both seeds and narrows the log-gap to GeoTransolver-512 by half at 4 to 14 degrees and by a quarter at 16 to 22 degrees; every surface field improves 8 to 11%; third dataset for the frame at protocol scale {#sec-nb-frame-wing-verdict}

**Setting.** The body frame as extra global directions was measured at
protocol scale on AirfRANS (pressure 17% better,
@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict) and DrivAerML Surface (4.8%,
@sec-nb-frame3d-verdict). The 35-wing HiLiftAeroML rung is the dataset
where ISLA trails GeoTransolver-512 most, 0.71 of its pressure error
overall, 0.77 at 4 to 14 degrees and 0.67 at 16 to 22 degrees where the
flow separates (@sec-nb-hl35-percase). The lane (@sec-nb-frame-wing-launch)
gave the reference configuration the wing's span and up axes beside the
far-field direction (K = 3), placed before centering so the rotation
augmentation carries them with the wing; two seeds, 200,000 cells,
code_v4. The preregistered bar: the log-gap to GeoTransolver-512 narrows
by at least 10% in either angle group, both seeds. The prediction was a
gain of the cars' order, 3 to 5%.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 180 validation wings, seed
means; data results/frame_wing_2026-09-26.json, reducer
results/frame_wing_reduce_2026-09-26.py). **Pressure 0.1302 (seeds 0.1285,
0.1320) against the reference pair's 0.1460, a ratio of 0.89**, and every
other field moves with it: temperature 0.92, density 0.90, velocity 0.93,
wall shear 0.92 of the reference. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA on pressure
moves from 0.71 to 0.80 overall. By angle group the log-gap narrows by
0.50 and 0.46 (seeds 42, 43) at 4 to 14 degrees, where GeoTransolver ÷
ISLA goes from 0.78 to 0.88, and by 0.31 and 0.24 at 16 to 22 degrees,
from 0.67 to 0.75; **both clauses fire on both seeds, five and two times
the 10% bar.** The gain is nearly uniform across angles (frame ÷ reference
0.83 to 0.92 at every angle), largest at 12 and 16 degrees.

**Why it matters.** Three datasets now carry the frame result at the
reference configuration, and the wings are the one where it was predicted
smallest and came out at 11%. The reading from the ladder holds: the
frame's value is a richer set of distinct directions for the routing bias
and the seed, and it pays most where the pressure field depends on the
body's orientation relative to the flow, which on a high-lift wing at
angle of attack is everywhere. What it does not do is close the separated
regime: at 20 and 22 degrees GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA stays at 0.67 and 0.70,
so the deficit there is still the positional channel named in
@sec-nb-hl35-percase, not orientation. The frame becomes the labeled
variant row on the 35-wing rung as on the cars and airfoils; the caveat
from the launch entry stands, that this pair ran on code_v4 while the
reference pair ran on code_ref (the two snapshots are exact on the kernel
and share every configuration value). The 210-case twin runs when the
GeoTransolver pair on that rung scores.

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, GEO-BIAS-K3: with the two axes present, the MLP routing bias buys velocity 8% more (0.92 of the K = 3 linear arm, at the additive bar) but costs pressure 20% (1.19), an outcome outside the preregistered clauses; the bias and the frame are different mechanisms for velocity and conflicting ones for pressure {#sec-nb-geo-bias-k3-verdict}

**Setting.** On the 160-airfoil AirfRANS exploration rung (192 wide, 120
training airfoils, 20,000 queries, no accuracy claim, @sec-protocol) two
changes each improved ISLA: the two laboratory axes as global directions
beside the inlet (K = 3; pressure 0.75, velocity 0.89, eddy viscosity 0.82
of the inlet-only arm, @sec-nb-frame-af-h-verdict) and a two-layer MLP in
place of the linear map from a pair's invariants to its routing bias
(K = 1; 0.94 / 0.89 / 0.89, @sec-nb-geo-bias-verdict). GEO-BIAS-K3
(@sec-nb-geo-bias-k3-prereg) combined them: K = 3 with the MLP bias, two
seeds, eager region. Bars on the K = 3 linear arm: velocity within 3% is
one mechanism, at least 8% better is additive; pressure at least 6%
better is additive, within 3% is not. Both seeds resumed twice from
checkpoints after external CUDA faults (epochs 220 and 277); the runs
completed 300 epochs. Data: results/geo_bias_k3_2026-09-26.json (reducer
results/geo_bias_k3_reduce_2026-09-26.py; 40 test airfoils, matched by
case name).

**What we saw** (seed means; pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity). The
combined arm scores 0.3187 / 0.1067 / 0.2024 against the K = 3 linear
arm's 0.2666 / 0.1158 / 0.2122 and the K = 1 MLP arm's 0.3330 / 0.1164 /
0.2290. **Velocity: 0.92 of the K = 3 linear arm, exactly the additive
bar** (seeds 0.1071 and 0.1063 against 0.1149 and 0.1168, both better),
and 0.92 of the K = 1 MLP arm: the third gain on velocity, on top of
either single change. **Pressure: 1.19 of the K = 3 linear arm** (seeds
0.3026 and 0.3348 against 0.2483 and 0.2849, both worse), and 0.96 of the
K = 1 MLP arm: with the MLP bias in place, the axes buy 4% of pressure
instead of 25%. Eddy viscosity 0.95 and 0.88.

**Reading.** Neither preregistered pressure clause covers a loss, so the
verdict is written as measured. For velocity the two changes are
different mechanisms and add: the nonlinear bias sharpens the routing on
the pair invariants, the axes enrich the seed's orientation invariants,
and the vector field profits from both. For pressure the frame's gain
lives in the seed and read-back channels (the GEO-BIAS verdict found the
bias recovers only a fifth of it), and the nonlinear bias with eight
invariants appears to take that gain away: the most direct reading is
that the MLP bias, given the direction cosines as inputs, learns a
routing that is specific to the orientation, and at 120 training
airfoils that specificity does not generalize for the scalar field. It
is one exploration-scale result, two seeds, one dataset. Its consequence
for the program is a prediction for GEO-BIAS-PROTO
(@sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-prereg), which runs the MLP bias at K = 1 at the
reference configuration: the velocity gain should hold and the pressure
gain should be small; and a warning that the MLP bias is not to be
combined with the frame without the protocol-scale test. The class keeps
`geo_bias="mlp"` as an option; the reference stays linear.

## 2026-09-26 — Interim, FRAME-VOL (provided-geometry half): on DrivAerML Volume the three body axes on the stored signed-distance field cut pressure 4%, velocity 10% and eddy viscosity 3.5% against the provided reference pair (both seeds); GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA 1.25 / 1.95 / 1.00; the frame-on-internal pair is still training {#sec-nb-frame-vol-interim}

**Setting.** FRAME-PROVIDED (@sec-nb-frame-provided-verdict) found on

add. The DrivAerML Volume twin launched with it (fa rows 12 to 15): the

(K = 4) on the internal geometry and on the provided geometry, 435 cars,
200,000 interior queries, two seeds each, code_v4. The FRAME-VOL ledger
row's first clause is that the frame pays on the Volume task at all:
pressure at least 3% better than the same-geometry reference pair on both
seeds. The provided-geometry pair (rows 14 and 15) is scored; the
internal-geometry pair (rows 12 and 13) is at epoch 430 of 500 and decides
the additivity clause.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 on the 48 validation cars; data
results/frame_vol_2026-09-26.json). The frame on the stored field scores
**0.0381 / 0.0517 / 0.0844 on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity (seeds
0.0380 and 0.0383 on pressure) against the provided reference pair's
0.0397 / 0.0576 / 0.0874: 0.96 / 0.90 / 0.97**, both seeds under the 3%
pressure bar (0.956, 0.964). Against the internal-geometry reference it is
0.93 / 0.79 / 0.94. GeoTransolver-volume (0.0477 / 0.1008 / 0.0843) ÷ this
model is **1.25 on pressure, 1.95 on velocity and 1.00 on eddy

**Reading, interim.** The frame pays on the Volume task, 4% of pressure

underneath, ISLA leads GeoTransolver-volume by a quarter on pressure and a

AirfRANS with the frame and the stored field. Whether the frame's gain
here is additive with the stored field's (the AirfRANS reading) or
overlaps it waits for the internal-geometry pair; the additive clause is
at least 10% better than the provided pair on pressure and 5% better than
the frame-on-internal arm on velocity, and the 4% pressure gain already
says the pressure half of that clause will not fire on this dataset. The
finding that the frame is worth having on both interior tasks is now two
datasets at protocol scale (AirfRANS, DrivAerML Volume), matching the two
surface tasks (DrivAerML Surface, HiLiftAeroML 35-wing).

## 2026-09-26 — Verdict, FRAME-VOL: on DrivAerML Volume the three body axes pay on both geometries (0.95 / 0.87 / 0.96 of the internal reference, 0.96 / 0.90 / 0.97 of the provided reference; pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity, both seeds), and the stored field on top of the frame adds 9% of velocity and 2% of pressure: between the additive and redundant clauses; ISLA + frame + stored field leads GeoTransolver-volume 1.25 / 1.95 / 1.00 {#sec-nb-frame-vol-verdict}

**Setting.** The FRAME-VOL row asked two things of the DrivAerML Volume
task (435 cars, 200,000 interior queries, 48 validation cars, reference
configuration, code_v4, two seeds each): does the body frame (three axes
beside the inlet, K = 4) pay at all, with a 3% pressure bar on both seeds
against the same-geometry reference pair; and does it add to the stored
signed-distance field as it did on AirfRANS
(@sec-nb-frame-provided-verdict), with the same clauses (additive: at
least 10% better than the provided pair on pressure and 5% better than
the frame-on-internal arm on velocity; redundant: within 3% of the
frame-on-internal arm on every field). The provided half was read this
afternoon (@sec-nb-frame-vol-interim); the internal half is now scored.
Data: results/frame_vol_2026-09-26.json.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2, seed means; pressure / velocity /
eddy viscosity). The frame on the internal geometry scores 0.0388 / 0.0568
/ 0.0854 (seeds 0.0389 and 0.0387 on pressure) against the internal
reference pair's 0.0409 / 0.0655 / 0.0894: **0.95 / 0.87 / 0.96, both
seeds under the 3% bar.** The frame on the stored field scores 0.0381 /
0.0517 / 0.0844, 0.96 / 0.90 / 0.97 of the provided pair. The stored field
on top of the frame is therefore worth 0.98 / 0.91 / 0.99 of the frame on
internal geometry: 9% on velocity, 2% on pressure, 1% on eddy viscosity.
That is neither additive (the pressure clause asked 10%) nor redundant
(velocity moves 9%): **between**, and the reading is plain. On this task
the frame carries a velocity gain of its own (13%, which the Surface task
had no field to show) and the stored field's velocity gain (12% against
the internal reference on its own, @sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict)
partly overlaps it, leaving 9% on top; on pressure the frame is worth 5%
and the stored field 2% more. Against GeoTransolver-volume (0.0477 /
0.1008 / 0.0843) the frame on internal geometry stands at 1.23 / 1.78 /
0.99 and with the stored field at **1.25 / 1.95 / 1.00**.

**Why it matters.** Two datasets now say the same two things about the
interior tasks: the frame pays on either geometry, and the stored field
pays on top of it, fully on AirfRANS (both clauses) and on velocity only
on the cars. The recommended inputs on a fixed-frame interior dataset with
a stored distance field are therefore the frame and the stored field
together, and the interior scoreboard rows carry them as the labeled
variant on both datasets. The frame's velocity gain on the Volume task is
the new fact here: on the airfoils the frame's velocity gain was 22% and
on the cars it is 13%, so the frame is not a pressure-only input in the
interior. With both inputs ISLA leads GeoTransolver-volume on every
DrivAerML Volume field, as on AirfRANS. The FRAME program's protocol-scale
record is now four datasets for the frame (two surface, two interior) and
two for the frame with the stored field.

## 2026-09-26 — Interim, lug depth at the depth rate: ISLA 24 layers at 2.5e-4 on 2,400 lugs scores 0.86 of the 12-layer pair on the mean but 0.99 and 0.75 seed by seed; the 12-layer pair's 21% seed spread decides nothing, so a third seed of each runs {#sec-nb-lug-r2-rate-interim}

**Setting.** On the GINOT Bracket Lug set (600 test lugs, von Mises
relative L2) the 24-layer ISLA at the reference rate 5e-4 sat at the
mean-field plateau (0.986, both seeds) and was relaunched at the depth
rate 2.5e-4 (@sec-nb-cluster-return-2026-09-25), as on DeepJEB++ where
the relaunch trained and scored within 2% of 12 layers
(@sec-nb-deepjeb-r2-rate-verdict). The SOLIDS ledger's depth clause is
1.5%: 24 layers within 1.5% of 12 means depth does not pay. Data:
results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json (reducer
results/solids_lug_reduce_2026-09-22.py).

**What we saw.** The 24-layer pair at 2.5e-4 scores **0.00185 (seeds
0.00191, 0.00179)** against the 12-layer pair's 0.00215 (0.00192,
0.00238), GeoTransolver-512's 0.00217 (0.00183, 0.00250) and
GeoTransolver-256's 0.00202 (0.00214, 0.00190). On the means 24 layers
is 14% better than 12 and GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA moves from 1.01 to
1.17. Seed by seed the picture is different: seed 42 gives 0.00191
against 0.00192 (parity) and seed 43 gives 0.00179 against 0.00238 (25%
better). The 12-layer pair's seeds are 21% apart, the widest spread in the
lug ladder, and the 24-layer pair's are 6% apart; GeoTransolver-512's are
31% apart. **At this rung two seeds cannot say whether depth pays or the
12-layer seed 43 is an outlier.** Rather than call 14% on one seed, a
third seed (44) of the 12-layer and the 24-layer configurations runs at
2,400 lugs; the depth clause is then read on three paired ratios. This is
the one place in the program where a third seed is spent, because the
standing (ISLA ahead of the parameter match by 17% or at parity) turns on
it. The mechanism reading if depth pays here and nowhere else: the lug's
von Mises field is the smoothest target in the book and the one whose
error is closest to the seed noise, so the depth clause is the least
resolved measurement of the ladder.

*Addendum 2026-09-27 to @sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-2048-verdict (second
seeds of the single-channel arms at 2,048 cases; data
results/batch3_reductions_2026-09-26.json, rerun).* With seed 43 the
extension recovers 0.80 of the log-gap (0.1298; seeds 0.1250, 0.1346)
and the frame 0.61 (0.1689; 0.1555, 0.1822), against 0.83 and 0.67 on

seeds' mean** (paired 1.22 and 1.64). GeoTransolver-512 (0.0289) ÷ ISLA
falls from 0.35 to 0.25, and the 5e-4 pair stays at its plateau (1.000).
The R1 pair's own seeds are 40% apart on this rung, the widest spread in
the Poisson ladder, so the size of the loss is uncertain; its sign is
not.

**Reading.** Depth does not pay on the Poisson set, and at the depth rate
it costs. That makes four datasets on which 24 layers fail the 1.5%
clause (DrivAerML Surface 2.6%, DeepJEB++ within 2%, the 35-wing rung
within 4% by angle, OLBC Poisson 38% worse) against none where it
clearly pays (the lug's third seeds decide the one open case). The
Poisson result also says something about the mechanism of the OLBC
deficit: whatever ISLA lacks on a fixed mesh with random boundary data,
it is not depth, which is consistent with OLBC-MECH's reading that the
gap is value transport (@sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict). The elasticity R2
pair at the depth rate is one epoch from done and follows the same
reducer. The reference stays at 12 layers on every dataset.

## 2026-09-27 — Interim, GEO-BIAS-PROTO (DrivAerML Surface, fused twin, one seed): the MLP routing bias at K = 1 scores 1.03 of the reference on pressure and wall shear, above the 3-D null threshold; the eager pair decides {#sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-interim}

**Setting.** GEO-BIAS-PROTO (@sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-prereg) runs the
two-layer routing bias at K = 1 at the reference configuration on

the protocol-scale speed number. The DrivAerML bar: pressure at 0.952 of
the reference or better carries the frame's gain to 3-D; above 0.976 is
