score; the eager pair is at epoch 330 of 500 after the relaunch. Data:
results/geo_bias_proto_interim_2026-09-27.json.

**What we saw.** The fused MLP bias at K = 1 scores 0.0434 on pressure
and 0.0681 on wall shear: **1.03 of the reference pair on both fields**
(1.03 of the reference's own seed 42), 1.09 of the three-axes arm, and
GeoTransolver-512 ÷ this model is 0.95. One seed, so the reading is
interim, but it sits on the wrong side of the null threshold with 5
points to spare: at the reference width and 435 cars, replacing the
linear pair-to-bias map by a nonlinear one does not buy pressure and
costs a little. This is the outcome the prediction named (3-D null,
0.6), and it agrees with the exploration-scale finding that the bias
recovers the vector field's gain, not the scalar's, and with GEO-BIAS-K3
that the bias can cost pressure. The AirfRANS twin, where the velocity
clause lives, is at epoch 474 of 500; the eager pairs follow.

*Addendum 2026-09-27, AirfRANS fused twin (seed 42; data
results/geo_bias_proto_interim_2026-09-27.json).* At the reference
configuration on 800 airfoils the MLP bias at K = 1 scores 0.0349 /
0.0192 / 0.0327 (pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity): 1.02 / 0.93 /
0.92 of the internal-geometry reference pair, where the frame arm stands
at 0.83 / 0.78 / 0.84. In the preregistration's units the bias recovers
**0.28 of the frame's velocity log-gain** (0.46 of the eddy-viscosity
gain, none of the pressure gain), against 0.96 at exploration scale;
velocity sits between the null threshold (0.94 of the reference) and the
mechanism threshold (0.88). One seed, and the eager pair decides, but the
direction is clear on both datasets: **at protocol scale the nonlinear
routing bias is not the capacity the extra directions supply.** The
frame's velocity gain on AirfRANS is mostly something else, most likely
the seed's orientation invariants, which the bias does not touch.
GeoTransolver-volume ÷ this model is 0.79 / 1.98 / 0.90.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, OLBC elasticity depth at the depth rate: 24 layers at 2.5e-4 on 8,448 cases scores 0.95 to 0.97 of 12 layers on the four fields, but paired by seed one seed is at parity and one 12% better; depth is within seed noise on the elasticity set and the reference stays at 12 layers {#sec-nb-olbc-elasticity-r2-rate-verdict}

**Setting.** The last of the 24-layer relaunches at the depth rate
(@sec-nb-cluster-return-2026-09-25): the OLBC steel elasticity set at its
full rung (8,448 cases, 120 epochs, equal optimizer steps to 2,048 x 500),
ISLA R1 with the two domain axes as global directions, targets
displacement and the three stress components, against the 12-layer pair
and GeoTransolver-512 and -256. Depth clause: 24 layers within 1.5% of
12 means depth does not pay. Data: results/olbc_2026-09-22.json.

**What we saw** (relative L2 over 256 test cases; displacement /
$\sigma_{11}$ / $\sigma_{12}$ / $\sigma_{22}$). R2 at 2.5e-4: 0.0834 /
0.2185 / 0.2068 / 0.2099 against R1's 0.0877 / 0.2250 / 0.2163 / 0.2206,
ratios **0.95 / 0.97 / 0.96 / 0.95 on the means**. Paired by seed the
gain is one seed's: seed 42 gives 1.02 / 1.00 / 0.99 / 0.97 and seed 43
gives 0.88 / 0.94 / 0.93 / 0.93; the R2 seeds are 20% apart on
displacement where the R1 seeds are 5% apart. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA
moves from 0.57 / 0.45 / 0.45 / 0.48 to 0.60 / 0.47 / 0.47 / 0.50; the
5e-4 pair stays at its plateau (1.000) with one seed's scorer output
NaN, recorded as measured.

**Reading.** The same split as the lug (@sec-nb-lug-r2-rate-interim): a
mean gain of 3 to 5% carried by one seed while the other sits at parity,
which two seeds cannot separate from noise. Across the six datasets where
depth has now been measured at the reference width and its rate, 24
layers buys 2.6% on DrivAerML Surface, within 2% on DeepJEB++, within 4%
on the wings by angle, costs 38% on OLBC Poisson, and is seed-split on the
two solids (lug, elasticity), with the lug's third seeds still to score.
**Nowhere does depth clear the 1.5% clause on both seeds, so the
reference stays at 12 layers on every dataset,** and the two solids are
the place a third seed will be read before the sentence in
@sec-interior-tensile2d is touched. The elasticity deficit to
GeoTransolver-512 (about 2x on the stresses) is not a depth deficit; the
RANK-IO channel remains the lever that moved it
(@sec-nb-rankio-verdict-2048).

## 2026-09-27 — Preregistration, LOCAL-AGG: does a contract-preserving local relational aggregation among tokens close the fixed-mesh Poisson deficit that value transport leaves? OLBC Poisson at 512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds, against the extension arm and GeoTransolver-512 {#sec-nb-local-agg-prereg}

**Setting.** ISLA's largest remaining deficit is on the fixed-mesh OLBC
Poisson set, where GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA is 0.25 at 2,048 cases for
the reference and 0.76 with the boundary-value extension
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-2048-verdict and addendum). OLBC-MECH located
what the extension does not supply: absolute coordinates fed as a
contract-breaking diagnostic overshoot GeoTransolver by 40 to 60%, four
times the slices recover nothing, and the domain frame recovers nothing
on top of the extension. GeoTransolver has one channel ISLA lacks
entirely: a local neighbourhood embedding (its ball queries), which gives
every token its surroundings at a resolution 256 anchors cannot reach.
The same channel is the natural suspect for the separated-flow regime on
the wings (@sec-nb-frame-wing-verdict) and was the query-to-query
candidate the ledger carried as LIT-LOCALQ.

**The change** (commit on 2026-09-27, `local_rho` in the ISLA class).
Before the slice routing in every slice block, each token receives the
measure-weighted Gaussian-kernel average over all tokens of the
projected token states and of the token-pair invariants (distance in
units of the radius, its log, the unit separation against each global
direction and against both normals, the normals' dot product), with
kernel $\mathrm{softmax}_j(-|r_i - r_j|^2 / \rho^2 + \log w_j)$. Relative
geometry only: rotation equivariance, translation invariance and
measure-rescale invariance hold to roundoff (tested). The radius $\rho$
is in frame units, the RMS pairwise distance of the boundary sample. The
released path is unchanged when the option is off. The eager evaluation
is O(N^2) per layer: 88 times the reference step at 20,000 tokens on the
laptop GPU, which is what a fused kernel is for; the OLBC sets have about
20,000 tokens, so the study runs there first, on the fused kernel once it
is exact against this eager path.

**Hypothesis.** The local channel supplies the positional resolution
the extension does not, and the two add: ISLA with the extension and the
local aggregation closes most of the remaining Poisson gap.

**Arms** (OLBC Poisson, reference configuration with the extension as
query scalars, K = 0 plus the extension's channels, two seeds, 500
epochs): $\rho$ = 0.05 and $\rho$ = 0.15 at 2,048 cases; $\rho$ = 0.05 at
512 cases. Comparators: the extension arm (0.1298 at 2,048, 0.333 at
512), the reference pair, GeoTransolver-512 (0.0981 at 2,048, 0.279 at
512). The radius pair is the instrument's own control: a gain that
depends strongly on $\rho$ says the channel is a resolution channel; a
gain flat in $\rho$ says it is something else.

**Bars, in the fraction of the log-gap between the reference and
GeoTransolver-512 recovered, seed means** (the extension recovers 0.80
at 2,048 and 0.84 at 512). *Closes*: the local arm recovers at least 0.95
at 2,048 cases, i.e. within 7% of GeoTransolver-512's error. *Pays*: at
least 0.88 (half the remaining gap). *Null*: within 0.03 of the
extension alone. Prediction: pays at 2,048 (0.5), closes (0.25), null
(0.25); the smaller radius better. Whatever the outcome, the cost of the
channel (step time against the reference on the fused kernel) is
recorded beside the accuracy, and the block enters the class as a
documented option, not the reference, until a second dataset (the lug or
Tensile2d, both fixed-mesh) reproduces the reading.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, GEO-BIAS-PROTO: at the reference configuration the MLP routing bias at K = 1 recovers 0.28 of the frame's velocity gain on AirfRANS (between the mechanism and null thresholds) and costs 3% on DrivAerML Surface (3-D null, both seeds); the bias's nonlinearity is not the capacity the extra directions supply, and the reference stays linear {#sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-verdict}

**Setting.** GEO-BIAS-PROTO (@sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-prereg) took the
exploration-scale finding that a two-layer routing bias at K = 1 recovers
0.96 of the two-axis velocity gain (@sec-nb-geo-bias-verdict) to the
reference configuration on two datasets: AirfRANS (800 airfoils, 100,000
queries, internal geometry) and DrivAerML Surface (435 cars, 200,000
cells), two seeds each on the eager region plus one fused-kernel twin per
dataset (code_v6, @sec-nb-geo-bias-kernel). Bars, in the fraction of the
frame's log-gain the bias recovers: on AirfRANS velocity at least 0.5 with
pressure under 0.5 is *mechanism holds*, both at least 0.5 is *general
improvement*, velocity under 0.25 is *null*; on DrivAerML pressure at
0.952 of the reference or better *carries to 3-D*, above 0.976 is *3-D
null*. Data: results/geo_bias_proto_2026-09-27.json.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2, seed means; pressure / velocity /
eddy viscosity). AirfRANS, eager pair: 0.0313 / 0.0192 / 0.0340 against
the internal-geometry reference pair's 0.0341 / 0.0206 / 0.0355, that is
0.92 / 0.93 / 0.96 of the reference where the frame arm stands at 0.83 /
0.78 / 0.84. **The bias recovers 0.28 of the frame's velocity log-gain,
0.45 of the pressure gain and 0.24 of the eddy-viscosity gain**: velocity
sits between the null threshold (0.25) and the mechanism threshold
(0.5), so the AirfRANS reading is *between*, and the pressure fraction
is not the one the exploration rung gave (0.22) but also not reliable:
the two eager seeds are 6% apart on pressure (0.0304, 0.0321) and 13%
apart on eddy viscosity, and the fused twin, the same configuration under
a different arithmetic order, lands 15% above eager seed 42 on pressure
(1.02 of the reference) while agreeing on velocity (1.04). Velocity is the
one field where the three runs agree, at 0.93 of the reference.
DrivAerML Surface, eager pair: **0.0433 / 0.0681 on pressure / wall
shear, 1.03 / 1.04 of the reference on both seeds (paired 1.029 and
1.034), above the 3-D null threshold**; GeoTransolver-512 ÷ this model is
0.95; the fused twin matches eager seed 42 to 0.3% on both fields.
GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA with the bias on AirfRANS is 0.89 / 1.98 /
0.86.

**Verdict.** *Between* on AirfRANS, *3-D null* on DrivAerML: the
hypothesis that the nonlinearity of the pair-to-bias map is what the
extra directions supply does not hold at the reference configuration.
At exploration scale (192 wide, 120 airfoils) the nonlinear bias recovered
nearly all of the velocity gain; at 384 wide with 800 airfoils it
recovers a quarter, and on the cars it costs 3%. The reading that fits
all of GEO-BIAS, GEO-BIAS-K3 (@sec-nb-geo-bias-k3-verdict) and this:
the linear bias is a capacity limit only when the model is small and the
data scarce; at the reference configuration the frame's gain comes
through the seed's orientation invariants, which the routing bias does
not touch, and a nonlinear bias with the direction cosines as inputs is
at best neutral and on the cars a small cost. Consequences: the reference
stays linear; `geo_bias="mlp"` remains a documented option (its fused
kernel is exact and 0.68x the eager epoch); the frame remains the
recommended input on fixed-frame datasets; and the mechanism question
moves to the seed and read-back channels, where a direct test would give
the directions to the seed only or to the geometry channels only.
Two datasets, two seeds each, at protocol scale.

## 2026-09-27 — Preregistration, FRAME-CHANNEL: which channel carries the frame's gain? The three global directions given to the token seed only, or to the geometry channels only, on the local AirfRANS rung, two seeds each {#sec-nb-frame-channel-prereg}

**Setting.** ISLA reads its $K$ global directions (unit vectors such as
the freestream direction and, in the frame arms, two fixed laboratory
axes) in three places: the *token seed*, where each boundary token starts
from the cosines between its normal and every direction ($n \cdot g_k$);
the *geometry channels* of every slice block, where the relative-position
invariants $\mathrm{rel} \cdot g_k$ enter the routing bias and the pooled
pair invariants; and the *output basis*, where vector outputs are
assembled from the directions, the normal and the pooled position. Giving
the laboratory frame to all three at once ($K = 3$) improved AirfRANS
interior error by 17 to 25% on pressure at both scales
(@sec-nb-frame-af-local-verdict, @sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict) and 5% on
DrivAerML Surface pressure. The GEO-BIAS-PROTO verdict
(@sec-nb-geo-bias-proto-verdict) refuted the nearest mechanistic account,
that the routing bias's nonlinearity was the capacity the directions
supply, and pointed at the seed and read-back channels as the place for a
direct test.

**Question.** Is the frame's gain carried by the token seed (each boundary
point learning where it sits on the airfoil from its normal's orientation
in the laboratory frame), by the geometry channels (the routing and the
pooled invariants seeing relative positions resolved along fixed axes), or
by both jointly?

**Instrument.** Two new constructor options,
`seed_directions` and `geometry_directions`, take the first $m \le K$
directions in input order for the named channel and leave the other
channels at all $K$; the output basis always sees all $K$
(`test_direction_channel_split_keeps_the_contracts_and_defaults_to_all_directions`:
both at $K$ reproduces the plain model bit for bit, and every split keeps
rotation equivariance, magnitude invariance and trained parameters). With
the freestream direction first and the two axes after it, two arms on the
local AirfRANS rung (160 airfoils, 192 x 12 x 256, cosine routing, fused
kernel, 20,000 interior queries, 300 epochs, learning rate 1e-3, exactly
the FRAME-AF local recipe): *seed-only* (`geometry_directions: 1`, so the
seed sees all three directions and the geometry channels see the
freestream only) and *geometry-only* (`seed_directions: 1`). Seeds 42 and
43, one RTX 4090 laptop GPU, two runs in parallel. Readout: float32
relative L2 on the 40 local test airfoils for pressure, velocity and eddy
viscosity, against the FRAME-AF base and frame arms already on disk
(results/frame_af_local_2026-09-23.json; base 0.355 / 0.130 / 0.258, frame
0.267 / 0.116 / 0.212 on the two-seed means).

**Bars (fraction of the frame's log-gain recovered on the two-seed means,
per field; the gap being $\log(\text{base}/\text{frame})$).** *Seed
carries it*: seed-only recovers $\ge 0.75$ of the pressure gain and
geometry-only $\le 0.35$. *Geometry carries it*: the reverse. *Joint*:
both arms $\le 0.5$, so neither channel alone gives the gain and the
frame's effect requires the directions in both places. *Either suffices*:
both arms $\ge 0.75$ (the directions are redundant across channels).
Anything between the thresholds is recorded as between. Velocity and eddy
viscosity are read the same way as supporting evidence; pressure decides,
because pressure is the field the frame moved most. A seed-only recovery
above the frame arm itself (fraction $> 1$) would mean the geometry
channels' extra invariants were hurting and would send a K = 3 fused
kernel with fewer geometry invariants to protocol scale.

**Prediction.** Seed carries it (0.5): the AirfRANS deficit sits at the
ends of the angle range and on pressure, which reads like each boundary
point needing to know its station on the airfoil (leading edge versus
trailing edge, upper versus lower surface), a property of the normal's
orientation in the fixed frame that the seed encodes directly and the
geometry channels only indirectly. Joint (0.3), either (0.15), geometry
(0.05). This is an exploration-scale mechanism reading; whichever
channel wins, the standing stays with the full frame arm at protocol
scale (@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict), and the winning channel-only arm
goes to the 800-airfoil reference twin only if it recovers $\ge 0.9$ of
the gain, because a cheaper variant that matches the full frame is worth
a protocol-scale run and one that trails it is not.

## 2026-09-27 — Interim, LOCAL-AGG (OLBC Poisson, 512 cases, two seeds): local relational aggregation among tokens closes the fixed-mesh deficit and overshoots it, ISLA + extension + local aggregation 0.229 against GeoTransolver-512 0.279; 1.5x step cost; the 2,048 rung and a second dataset are running {#sec-nb-local-agg-interim}

**Setting.** On the OLBC Poisson set (fixed square mesh, boundary-value
problems with varying boundary data) ISLA trailed GeoTransolver-512 by
about 3x at the reference configuration, and the boundary-value extension
(the boundary data continued into the interior as a query scalar)
recovered 0.80 to 0.84 of the log-gap on both rungs
(@sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict). The LOCAL-AGG preregistration
(@sec-nb-local-agg-prereg) asked whether a contract-preserving local
relational aggregation among tokens, a measure-weighted Gaussian kernel
over each token's 32 nearest tokens and their pair invariants applied
before the slice routing, closes what the extension leaves.

**What we saw.** The 512-case rung is scored on both seeds (256 test
cases, float32 relative L2 on the solution $u$, the same cases as every
other arm). ISLA + extension + local aggregation at $\rho = 0.05$ scores
**0.229 (seeds 0.231 / 0.227)** against the extension arm's 0.333 (0.318
/ 0.347), the frame-free reference's 0.867 and GeoTransolver-512's 0.279
(0.283 / 0.275). The fraction of the log-gap recovered is **1.17**, above
the "closes" bar of 0.95, and the model now leads GeoTransolver-512 on
both seeds: GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA = 1.22. The training step is 0.050 s
against 0.031 to 0.035 s for the extension arm at the same token count
(20,000 query tokens), a 1.5x cost.

**Reading.** At this rung the preregistered "closes" clause fires with
margin. The mechanism reading is that the slice routing, which pools
tokens by learned state, had no path for a token to read its immediate
neighbours' states, and on a fixed mesh whose difficulty is the local
propagation of boundary data across the interior that path is the
missing capacity; the extension gave each interior token the right
boundary value, the aggregation lets the tokens smooth it. This is one
rung of one dataset and counts as interim under the two-dataset rule.

**What runs now.** The 2,048-case lanes at $\rho = 0.05$ and $0.15$ are at
epoch 130 of 500 (about one minute per epoch, not the seven estimated
from the dense form). Staged and launched on code_v7 (campaign la rows
6-15): the OLBC elasticity twin (the RANK-IO arm, rank-1 boundary inputs
with the rank-2 stress head, plus local aggregation at 512 and 2,048
cases), an elasticity control and a Poisson control on code_v7 without
the aggregation so the twin differs from its control only by the
aggregation and not by the code snapshot, and an AirfRANS interior twin
(the provided-geometry frame arm plus local aggregation at 800 airfoils,
100,000 queries) as the first non-fixed-mesh test. Bars for the twins are
the preregistration's, read per dataset against each dataset's own best
ISLA arm and GeoTransolver reference. Artifact:
results/local_agg_2026-09-27.json (reducer beside it).

## 2026-09-27 — Interim, FRAME-CHANNEL (seed 42): neither channel alone recovers the frame's pressure gain (seed-only 0.304, geometry-only 0.363 against base 0.301 and frame 0.248), while each alone beats the full frame on velocity; the second seeds are training {#sec-nb-frame-channel-interim}

**Setting.** FRAME-CHANNEL (@sec-nb-frame-channel-prereg) gives the
three global directions (freestream plus two laboratory axes) either to
the token seed only or to the slice blocks' geometry channels only, on
the local AirfRANS rung, to learn which channel carries the frame's
pressure gain. Seed 42 of both arms is scored on the 40 local test
airfoils; the seed 43 pair is training.

**What we saw (seed 42, float32 relative L2; base and frame from the
FRAME-AF rung, same seed).** Pressure: base 0.301, frame 0.248, seed-only
**0.304**, geometry-only **0.363**. Neither channel alone recovers any of
the frame's pressure gain (fractions of the log-gain -0.06 and -0.98); the
geometry-only arm is 21% worse than the frame-free base. Velocity: base
0.130, frame 0.115, seed-only **0.112**, geometry-only **0.107**; each
channel alone beats the full frame (fractions 1.22 and 1.60). Eddy
viscosity: base 0.227, frame 0.221, seed-only 0.251, geometry-only 0.201.
Per angle, the full frame's pressure gain is largest between 0 and 5
degrees (0.172 against base 0.421) and neither channel-only arm gets
there (0.341 and 0.420); above 10 degrees the geometry-only arm is the
best of the four on pressure (0.192).

**Reading, held loosely until seed 43.** On pressure this reads as the
preregistered "joint" clause: the frame's gain needs the directions in
both the seed and the geometry channels, which is the outcome the
GEO-BIAS-PROTO verdict made most likely once the routing bias's
nonlinearity was ruled out (a token needs both to know where it sits and
to route by where its neighbours sit). The velocity result is the
anomaly to keep: splitting the directions across channels helps velocity
beyond the full frame, so the full frame's extra invariants in the
geometry channels may be costing velocity what they buy pressure. If
seed 43 agrees, the protocol-scale question becomes whether a
K = 3 model with fewer geometry invariants trades pressure for velocity,
and no channel-only arm goes to the 800-airfoil twin under the 0.9 bar.
Artifact: results/frame_channel_2026-09-27.json (interim, one seed).

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, FRAME-CHANNEL: the frame's pressure gain needs the directions in both the token seed and the geometry channels (seed-only recovers 0.49 of the log-gain with seeds at -0.06 / 0.74, geometry-only -0.22 and hurts); either channel alone beats the full frame on velocity by 4 to 5% on both seeds {#sec-nb-frame-channel-verdict}

**Setting.** The laboratory frame as global vectors ($K = 3$: freestream
plus two fixed axes) cuts ISLA's AirfRANS interior pressure error by 17 to
25% (@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict). FRAME-CHANNEL
(@sec-nb-frame-channel-prereg) asked which of ISLA's three uses of the
directions carries that gain, by giving the two axes to the token seed
only (`geometry_directions: 1`) or to the slice blocks' geometry channels
only (`seed_directions: 1`) on the local AirfRANS rung (160 airfoils,
192 x 12 x 256, 20,000 queries, 300 epochs; exploration scale, mechanism
only). Both arms are now scored on seeds 42 and 43 against the FRAME-AF
base and frame arms from the same rung and seeds (40 test airfoils,
float32 relative L2).

**What we saw.** Two-seed means, pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity:
base 0.355 / 0.130 / 0.258; frame 0.267 / 0.116 / 0.212; **seed-only
0.309 / 0.110 / 0.246**; **geometry-only 0.378 / 0.111 / 0.209**. On
pressure, the field that decides, the seed-only arm recovers **0.49** of
the frame's log-gain and the geometry-only arm **-0.22** (it is 7% worse
than the frame-free base and 42% worse than the frame). The seed-only
fraction is the mean of two seeds that disagree, -0.06 and 0.74, and the
disagreement is the base arm's: base pressure is 0.301 on seed 42 and
0.408 on seed 43 while seed-only is 0.304 and 0.313, so seed-only is a
steady 0.31 that the frame-free model reaches on its good seed and misses
on its bad one. On velocity both channel-only arms beat the full frame
(0.953 and 0.960 of the frame's error), on both seeds, with fractions of
the frame's gain above 1 (1.41 and 1.35). On eddy viscosity the
geometry-only arm equals the frame (0.985) and the seed-only arm is 16%
worse. Per angle, the frame's pressure gain concentrates between 0 and 5
degrees (0.172 against base 0.421) and neither channel-only arm reaches
it there (0.349, 0.448); above 10 degrees the geometry-only arm is the
best of the four on pressure (0.208).

**Verdict.** The preregistered *joint* clause fires: both channel-only
arms are at or below 0.5 of the pressure gain, so the frame's pressure
gain needs the directions in both the seed and the geometry channels.
The seed-only fraction sits at the clause boundary (0.49), so the
sharper statement is: the seed channel carries at most half of the gain
and the geometry channels carry none on their own, yet the two together
carry all of it. The mechanism reading is that a boundary token needs to
know its own station in the fixed frame (the seed cosines $n \cdot g_k$)
and the routing needs to compare tokens by their relative positions in
the same frame ($\mathrm{rel} \cdot g_k$) for the pressure field to be
resolved; each alone is a frame the other half of the network cannot
use. The prediction "seed carries it" (0.5) was wrong; "joint" (0.3) was
the second candidate.

**The anomaly, kept.** Both channel-only arms beat the full frame on
velocity on both seeds. Fewer directions in one channel helps velocity,
so the full frame's extra invariants in the geometry channels cost
velocity what they buy on pressure, or the seed's extra cosines do the
same. Under the 0.9 bar no channel-only arm replaces the frame at
protocol scale, but the velocity result earns its own protocol-scale
test: FRAME-CHANNEL-PROTO (preregistered below) runs the seed-only split
at the reference configuration on AirfRANS (800 airfoils, 100,000
queries) and DrivAerML Volume (frame of four directions) against the
scored full-frame pairs, asking whether the velocity gain survives at
scale and what it costs on pressure. Artifact:
results/frame_channel_2026-09-27.json; the options stay in ISLA as
documented mechanism-study switches with the default at all $K$.

## 2026-09-27 — Preregistration, FRAME-CHANNEL-PROTO: does giving the frame to the token seed only keep the velocity gain and lose the pressure gain at the reference configuration on AirfRANS and DrivAerML Volume? {#sec-nb-frame-channel-proto-prereg}

only; the seed and the output basis see every direction). Two seeds each,
four lanes, on a verified snapshot code_v8 (code_v7 plus the

holds*: velocity $\le 0.97$ on both datasets. *Pressure cost*: pressure
$\ge 1.05$ on a dataset means the split loses the frame's pressure gain

## 2026-09-27 — Interim, LOCAL-AGG on OLBC elasticity (512 cases, two seeds): local aggregation on top of the RANK-IO arm improves the three stress components by 3 to 4% and leaves displacement unchanged, mean log-gap fraction 0.545 to 0.605 (between); the 2,048 rung and its code_v7 control decide {#sec-nb-local-agg-elasticity-interim}

**Setting.** The second dataset for LOCAL-AGG (@sec-nb-local-agg-prereg,
Poisson interim @sec-nb-local-agg-interim) is OLBC elasticity, where the
best ISLA arm is the RANK-IO configuration (prescribed displacement and
traction as rank-1 boundary inputs, the stress as one symmetric rank-2
output; @sec-nb-rankio-verdict-elasticity) and GeoTransolver-512 leads it by about
1.3 to 1.5x on the stresses at 512 cases. The twin adds the k-nearest
local aggregation ($\rho = 0.05$, 32 neighbours) to that arm; the
reference numbers are the frame-free ISLA reference and GeoTransolver-512
from the OLBC ladder and the RANK-IO arm from campaign v2.

**What we saw (512 cases, 256 test cases, two seeds, relative L2 on
displacement / $\sigma_{11}$ / $\sigma_{22}$ / $\sigma_{12}$).** RANK-IO
0.670 / 0.740 / 0.751 / 0.780; RANK-IO + local aggregation **0.681 /
0.709 / 0.725 / 0.757**, ratios 1.016 / 0.958 / 0.964 / 0.971. Fractions
of the log-gap to GeoTransolver-512: RANK-IO 0.43 / 0.65 / 0.60 / 0.51
(mean 0.545), with aggregation 0.40 / 0.74 / 0.70 / 0.58 (mean **0.605**).
Per seed the displacement moves in opposite directions (0.643 against
0.673 on seed 42, 0.718 against 0.667 on seed 43) while every stress
component improves on both seeds.

**Reading.** On the elasticity set the aggregation is a modest gain on
the stress fields and nothing on displacement: the preregistered
*between* clause (above the RANK-IO fraction by more than 0.03, below
the "pays" bar of 0.88). This is far from the Poisson result at the same
rung (1.17, closes and overshoots), so the mechanism is not "fixed mesh
needs local smoothing" in general; on Poisson the missing capacity was
the local propagation of a scalar boundary value, on elasticity the
deficit is in the tensor field's structure that RANK-IO already
addresses in part. The RANK-IO arm ran on code_v2 and the twin on
code_v7, so the 2,048 rung, which carries a same-snapshot control
without the aggregation, is the clean comparison; it and the Poisson
2,048 lanes are past epoch 340 of 500. Artifact:
results/local_agg_2026-09-27.json.

## 2026-09-27 — Ruling (Peter): dataset-specific frame vectors are not PDE inputs; every FRAME arm is demoted to a pose-prior diagnostic, the FRAME-CHANNEL-PROTO and AirfRANS frame LOCAL-AGG lanes are cancelled, and the direction-count options are removed {#sec-nb-ruling-dataset-frame-inputs}

**The ruling.** Peter reviewed the frame program today and rejected it:
giving ISLA the axes of a dataset's coordinate frame as global vectors
(the laboratory $x, y$ on AirfRANS, the body axes on DrivAerML Surface and
Volume, the span and up axes on the wings, the square's axes on the OLBC
sets, the laboratory axes on Tensile2d and the OLBC elasticity set) is not
a physical input. His test, which the program now adopts for every input
and mechanism: would a traditional PDE solver need it? Geometry, boundary
data, material and flow parameters, and the directions the physics names
(an inlet, a load, gravity) pass. A fixed dataset axis does not: rotating
the problem rotates the solution, so the axis carries no information about
the PDE and only tells the model the pose the training set was recorded
in. That is the absolute-position prior GeoTransolver has by construction,
handed to ISLA through a formally equivariant door. "Your goal is NOT an
unqualified hill climb on accuracy"; a solver that required
dataset-specific direction vectors would be "inconsistent with first
principles physics, so I don't trust your method." The equivariance
contract was preserved by every frame arm and I let that formal property
stand in for the physical question; the arms should not have been run.
Peter added a standing instruction: when no principled idea is ready,
pause and say so rather than fill the compute with inputs or mechanisms a
solver would not need.

**What each result now means.** Because the frame arm is ISLA plus the
pose prior GeoTransolver has by construction, frame-free against frame is
a measurement of how much of GeoTransolver's lead on a fixed-pose dataset
is pose memorization. That is the only reading these results keep, and it
lives in one place, @sec-pose-prior, as a diagnostic of the baseline.
Affected and reread: FRAME-AF at reference scale (@sec-nb-frame-af-ref-verdict;
0.83 / 0.78 / 0.84 of the frame-free ISLA on pressure / velocity / eddy
viscosity: most of GeoTransolver-volume's AirfRANS pressure and
eddy-viscosity lead is the fixed pose), FRAME-PROVIDED
(@sec-nb-frame-provided-verdict), FRAME-3D and FRAME-3D-R2
(@sec-nb-frame3d-verdict, @sec-nb-frame3d-r2-verdict; 5% on the cars),
FRAME-WING (@sec-nb-frame-wing-verdict; about half of the low-angle gap and
a quarter of the high-angle widening), FRAME-VOL
(@sec-nb-frame-vol-verdict), the FRAME-AF mechanism ladder
(@sec-nb-frame-af-h-verdict), GEO-BIAS and GEO-BIAS-PROTO (which measured
whether a routing nonlinearity carries the prior's gain; they now read as
diagnostics of a rejected input), FRAME-CHANNEL
(@sec-nb-frame-channel-verdict, which located the prior's gain in the
joint use of the seed and the geometry channels), the OLBC `frame2` arms
of the mechanism study (@sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict; the extension alone was
already the recipe), and the Tensile2d and OLBC elasticity frame lanes
(@sec-nb-solids-frame-interim), whose finding that a scalar head cannot
produce a frame component without a frame stands, with the tensor head as
the configuration and the frame route rejected. The recommendation "pass
the frame on fixed-frame datasets" is withdrawn from the usage chapter,
the frame rows are removed from the interior tables and the scoreboard
sentences of the surface chapter, the Tensile2d standing is restated on
the tensor head with the load direction as the one global vector
(@sec-interior-tensile2d) and the OLBC elasticity standing on the rank-1
inputs with the tensor output (@sec-nb-olbc-ref-ladder-verdict). Ledger rows FRAME-AF,
FRAME-3D, FRAME-3D-R2, FRAME-PROVIDED, FRAME-WING, FRAME-VOL and
FRAME-CHANNEL are STOPPED under the ruling; the mechanism controls are
marked diagnostic; the decision is recorded in @sec-principled-ledger.

**What was cancelled and replaced.** FRAME-CHANNEL-PROTO (campaign fc
rows 0-3, the seed-only frame split at the reference configuration on
AirfRANS and DrivAerML Volume) was cancelled at epoch 90 to 100 of 500 and
its lanes marked BLOCKED; it studied a mechanism of the rejected input.
The AirfRANS LOCAL-AGG twin (campaign la rows 14-15) ran the local
aggregation on top of the provided-geometry frame arm; it was cancelled
and relaunched as rows 16-17 on the frame-free provided-geometry reference
(`isla_volume_airfrans_ref_provided` plus `local_rho: 0.05`, `local_k: 32`),
against the `sg_af_provided` pair. The `seed_directions` and
`geometry_directions` options added to ISLA this morning existed only for
the frame study and are removed from the class and its tests; the code_v8
snapshot that carried them stays on the cluster unused. The frame
configurations and artifacts stay on disk as labeled diagnostics.

**What passes the test, and one open question.** The local relational
aggregation of LOCAL-AGG passes: it uses geometry and boundary data only,
and local interaction among tokens is how a PDE propagates information.
The RANK-IO inputs pass: prescribed displacement and traction are boundary
conditions. The freestream and load directions pass. The boundary-value
extension (LIT-EXT) is the open question. In plain terms: on the OLBC
sets every boundary cell carries a condition type (Dirichlet, Neumann,
Robin) and a prescribed value, and a plain interior query sees only its
distance and direction to the nearest boundary cell, never the prescribed
values. The extension hands each interior query six numbers computed
before training with no learned parameters: for each of the three types,
the prescribed values of that type averaged over the boundary with
weights equal to each cell's measure divided by its squared distance to
the query, and the distance to the nearest cell of that type. It is a
function of the boundary data and the geometry alone, so it carries no
dataset prior and no pose, and on Poisson it recovers about 0.84 of the
log-gap to GeoTransolver-512. What makes it questionable is that it is a
hand-built feature a solver would compute for itself, with an arbitrary
inverse-square kernel standing in for the PDE's own kernel (the harmonic
extension of the boundary data, one half of a Poisson solution by
superposition). The recommendation put to Peter: replace it with the
exact form, per-type harmonic measures and the harmonic extension from
one Laplace solve per type per case in preprocessing, keep the
inverse-square version only as the ablation control, and treat the whole
channel as the interior half of a unified token design in which an
interior token carries the smooth continuation of what a boundary token
carries. Kept as an input for now, labeled PDE-derived preprocessing,
pending his call.

## 2026-09-27 — Peter's call on the boundary-value extension: admissible (it derives from one sample's geometry and boundary data), but the inverse-square kernel is crude; the harmonic middle path is approved and the parallel threads go into the tech tree {#sec-nb-extension-call}

**The call.** Peter read the plain definition of the boundary-value
extension (@sec-nb-ruling-dataset-frame-inputs) and ruled: the
construction is admissible because it derives purely from the geometry
and the boundary condition type and value of each sample, nothing that
needs knowledge beyond a single sample (which is what made the rejected
frame vectors dataset-specific). The inverse-square kernel is the weak
part: a crude approximation that happens to suit Poisson-like problems
and does not generalize. Using the governing equation's own kernel is
unattractive because it requires knowing the equations. The middle path
is approved: per-type harmonic measures and harmonic extensions from
Laplace solves, read as a PDE-agnostic geometric construction (the
probability that a random walk from the query first reaches boundary
type k), with the inverse-square version kept as the ablation control.
Peter also asked that the parallel threads from today's discussion be
tracked in the tech tree; the rows HARMONIC, EXT-ABL and UNIFIED-TOKENS
are added below and in the ledger.

## 2026-09-27 — Preregistration, HARMONIC: per-type harmonic measures and harmonic extensions as the interior geometry channel, on OLBC Poisson (against the inverse-square extension) and AirfRANS interior (against the stored distance field) {#sec-nb-harmonic-prereg}

**Setting.** An interior token in ISLA knows its distance and direction
to the nearest boundary sample, either computed in the model or read
from a stored signed distance field. Both are a minimum over boundaries
and have a kink on the medial axis (the set of points equidistant from
two boundaries), which shows up as a seam in the slice assignments while
the physics is smooth there. On the OLBC Poisson set the inverse-square
boundary-value extension (six query scalars, @sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict)
recovered 0.84 of the log-gap to GeoTransolver-512 at 512 cases and 0.80
at 2,048 (two seeds each, @sec-nb-olbc-mech-combined-2048-verdict).

**Instrument.** A mesh-free preprocessing on the interior point cloud: a
symmetric k-nearest-neighbour graph (k = 12 in two dimensions) with
self-tuning Gaussian weights and its graph Laplacian; boundary nodes are
the interior nodes tagged with a condition type. For each type k the
*harmonic measure* $\varphi_k$ solves the discrete Laplace equation with
$\varphi_k = 1$ on the type-k boundary nodes and 0 on every other boundary
node, so the $\varphi_k$ are smooth, non-negative and sum to one; the
*harmonic extension* $h_k$ solves the same equation with the prescribed
value on the type-k nodes and 0 elsewhere, so $\sum_k h_k$ is the
harmonic extension of all the boundary data. One sparse factorization
per case serves every right-hand side. Fields are written once into a
copy of the dataset (never in place) and read as query scalars, six on
OLBC Poisson (`hm_*`, `hx_*`) in place of the six `ext_*` scalars, so the
arm is a drop-in swap. Validation before any lane: the unit square with
one edge of type A reproduces the series solution of Laplace to 3% RMS,
the measures sum to one to 1e-6, and every field is unchanged under
rotation and translation to 1e-6. The datum this input is: the geometry
and the boundary condition labels and values of the one sample.

**Arms and bars (OLBC Poisson, 512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds, float32
per-case relative L2 on $u$ over the 256 test cases; fractions of the
log-gap between the frame-free reference and GeoTransolver-512 as in
@sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict).** `hm`: reference plus the six harmonic
fields. Bars against the extension's fraction $f_{\text{ext}}$ (0.84 /
0.80): *the kernel pays*: $f_{\text{hm}} \ge f_{\text{ext}} + 0.05$ on both
rungs; *kernel-insensitive*: within 0.05 of $f_{\text{ext}}$ on both (the
value-transport path is what matters, the kernel does not); *hurts*: below
$f_{\text{ext}} - 0.05$ on either rung. Prediction: the kernel pays at
512 (0.5) where the crude kernel's error is largest relative to the data,
kernel-insensitive at 2,048 (0.5).

**Companion EXT-ABL (same rungs and seeds).** The extension's six
scalars split into values-only (`ext_*`, three scalars) and distances-only
(`ext_dist_*`), to attribute the 0.84: *values carry it* if values-only
recovers $\ge 0.75$ of $f_{\text{ext}}$ and distances-only $\le 0.35$;
*distances carry it* for the reverse; *joint* if both $\le 0.5$; *either*
if both $\ge 0.75$. Prediction: values carry it (0.6).

**AirfRANS half (800 airfoils, 100,000 queries, reference configuration,
two seeds).** `hm` adds the harmonic measure of the airfoil (the far field
tagged as the complementary type by the case's largest stored distances)
on top of the provided-geometry reference `sg_af_provided`, keeping the
stored distance field. Bars, ratio hm ÷ provided on pressure / velocity /
eddy viscosity: *pays* if any field $\le 0.95$ with none $> 1.03$; *null*
if all within 3%; *hurts* if any $> 1.05$. Prediction: null-to-pays (the
seam is visible but the stored field is already smooth away from the
medial axis of a convex-ish airfoil): 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.1.

**Provenance.** Reducer to be written beside results/local_agg_reduce_2026-09-27.py
(same log-gap conventions); lanes on code_v7 with new recipe files only.
Standing requires both OLBC rungs and the AirfRANS half; a second
dataset beyond OLBC is the two-dataset rule.

## 2026-09-27 — Planned, UNIFIED-TOKENS: one token set for surface and interior tasks (boundary tokens plus label-free interior collocation tokens, outputs read at any requested points); first test on DrivAerML {#sec-nb-unified-prereg}

**Idea (Peter's question).** A surface task is the interior task with the
query set on the boundary: a boundary point is a query at distance zero
whose direction is the normal, whose type indicator is its own type and
whose prescribed data are the boundary values. With HARMONIC's fields the
interior features become the smooth continuation of the boundary ones
(harmonic measure to type indicator, harmonic extension to prescribed
data), so one token design serves both tasks. The deeper content: with
boundary tokens only ISLA is a boundary-element method; interior
collocation tokens (no labels needed) make it finite-element-like, which
a nonlinear volume problem such as Navier-Stokes may need even for a
surface readout.

**First tests (DrivAerML, where both surface and volume data exist).**
(a) The volume-trained reference model evaluated at boundary points it
was never asked for, against the surface-trained model on surface
pressure and wall shear (evaluation only, no training). (b) The surface
model trained with unlabeled interior collocation tokens (query tokens on
a volume sample with no loss on them), two seeds, against the surface
reference pair at 200,000 cells. Bars for (b): pressure $\le 0.97$ of the
surface reference on both seeds = interior tokens help the surface
readout (the boundary-only path becomes the special case to retire);
within 3% = the boundary-only operator already carries the interior
physics at this regime; $> 1.03$ = hurts. Open design points recorded,
not yet decided: the area measure of boundary tokens against the volume
measure of interior tokens in one routing softmax (normalize per family
and derive the relative weight rather than guess), and how to generate
collocation points for surface-only datasets. Status: PLANNED until (a)
is scripted and (b) has a loss mask in the recipe; depends on HARMONIC
for the unified feature set.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, UNIFIED-TOKENS test (a): the volume-trained DrivAerML model has almost no skill at the wall (surface pressure 0.76 against the surface pair's 0.045, 17x), so a unified design must train on wall queries rather than inherit them {#sec-nb-unified-a-verdict}

**Setting.** UNIFIED-TOKENS (@sec-nb-unified-prereg) asks whether a
surface task is the interior task with the queries placed on the
boundary. The cheapest test uses models that already exist: the
frame-free provided-geometry DrivAerML Volume pair
(`sg_drvol_provided`, the reference of the DrivAerML Volume table,
interior pressure 0.0403 / 0.0391 on its own task) evaluated at the
surface dataset's 200,000 vehicle cell centroids on the 48 validation
cars, the same draw the fleet scorer uses, against the surface-trained
reference pair `p200k_dr_isla` (0.0442 / 0.0449). Evaluation only; no
training. The volume model reads a query's signed distance and its
gradient, so at the wall the query scalar is 0 and the direction is the
normal into the fluid.

**What we saw (measure-weighted relative L2 on pressure, two-seed
means).** Volume model at the wall **0.762** (0.749 / 0.776), 17.1x the
surface pair's 0.0446. Per car the prediction correlates with the target
at only 0.42 to 0.55; its mean is right (-0.30 against -0.34) but its
standard deviation is 0.23 against 0.38, so the model returns a smoothed,
low-variance field at the boundary. Two conventions had to be settled on
the way and are recorded: the surface dataset's vehicle cell normals
point into the body (mean dot product with an outward radial proxy
-0.23), while the volume model's query directions are the distance
gradient pointing into the fluid, so the wall query normal is minus the
stored cell normal (the first pass with the stored normals scored 0.880
and is kept as the record). And the volume set's nearest-wall training
points sit at a signed distance of about 2.5e-7, so 0 is inside the
training range; yet setting the query scalar to 2.5e-7 instead of 0
changes the score from 0.76 to 0.64, a sensitivity to a 1e-7 shift that
is an anomaly to chase (which path scales the query scalar so steeply?).

**Verdict.** A model trained with a volume loss puts negligible weight on
the measure-zero wall and does not generalize to it: the answer to "is
the surface a special case of the interior model" is no for an inherited
model at this regime. This does not decide the unified design; it
sharpens it. Any single token set serving both tasks must include wall
queries in training, and the live question is test (b): whether
label-free interior collocation tokens improve a surface-trained readout.
Artifact results/unified_a_2026-09-27.json (script
results/unified_eval_2026-09-27.py; metrics under
results/campaigns_2026-09-27/unified/metrics).

## 2026-09-27 — HARMONIC and EXT-ABL launched: the harmonic-measure transform validated (unit-square series error 0.7%, partition of unity to 1e-9, invariant to 1e-6), both datasets converted, fourteen lanes on code_v7 {#sec-nb-harmonic-launch}

**Validation of the instrument** (`src/harmonic.py`, `tests/test_harmonic.py`, seven
tests). On a jittered grid on the unit square with the left edge as type A
and the other three edges as type B, the harmonic measure of A matches the
series solution of Laplace's equation at 20 interior probes to 0.74% RMS
relative to the maximum (bar 3%; 0.47% with 8 neighbours, 1.2% with 16,
0.4% on finer grids). The measures sum to one to 7e-10 and are exactly 1
and 0 on their own and the other boundary nodes. The per-type harmonic
extensions equal a direct solve of the same operator to 1e-6 and sum to
the extension of the full data. Rotating by 0.7 rad and translating leaves
every field unchanged to 1e-6. An absent type gives zero fields.

**Precompute (CPU partition, 60 workers).** OLBC Poisson: 8,704 of 8,704
cases in 158 s, median 1.03 s per case (16,598 nodes, 1,116 boundary
nodes), written to a copy of the dataset (14 GB) with the manifest. AirfRANS:
1,000 of 1,000 cases in 109 s, median 4.6 s per case (177,416 nodes; the
far field tagged as the complementary type by the case's 99th-percentile
stored distance), 9.7 GB. Read-back confirmed the fields and that the
targets are retained.

**Lanes (campaign hm, code_v7 / recipe_v4 with new files only).** Rows 0-3:
`hm_poisson_hm` at 512 and 2,048 cases (six harmonic fields in place of the
six extension scalars). Rows 4-11: `ext_valonly` and `ext_distonly` at both
rungs. Rows 12-13: `hm_af_provided_hm` (the provided-geometry AirfRANS
reference plus the airfoil's harmonic measure). Two seeds each; bars in
@sec-nb-harmonic-prereg; reducer results/harmonic_reduce_2026-09-27.py.

## 2026-09-27 — ND-GENERIC, first pass done: ISLA takes a `dim` argument and builds every geometric quantity for d components; 3-D numerics bitwise unchanged; odd parity by the Levi-Civita construction (2-D perpendiculars, 3-D cross products); the fused kernels stay 3-D {#sec-nb-ndgeneric-pass1}

**Setting.** Peter asked whether ISLA generalizes to other dimensions, as
GLOBE and the mesh module do. The audit (@sec-nb-ruling-dataset-frame-inputs
era, same day) found the model written for three components throughout:
shapes, the pseudovector basis built from cross products, the rank-3
Levi-Civita term, and the Triton kernels loading three components. The
two-dimensional datasets (AirfRANS, OLBC, Tensile2d) run embedded in three
dimensions with the third coordinate zero, which is correct but pays for
a dead axis and a pseudovector basis that points out of the plane.

**What changed (commit 2b77562e).** ISLA takes `dim` (default 3), checked
against the points at forward; the head's coefficient count depends on d,
so it is a constructor argument rather than an inference from the data.
Every shape, invariant, seed, rank-1 and rank-2 input, block extra,
nearest-boundary geometry, local aggregation and head basis is built for d
components. The true-vector basis (directions, normal, pooled direction
and their complements; 2K + 3 vectors in every d) is unchanged in form.
Odd parity uses the Levi-Civita construction: in two dimensions the
perpendiculars of the K + 2 primary vectors (p = K + 2), in three the
pairwise cross products as before (p = C(K + 2, 2)), and it is refused
with a clear error for d of four and above, where a pseudovector needs
d minus 1 vectors. The isotropic odd term is the Levi-Civita symbol of
rank d. The fused Triton geometry kernel and the Triton nearest-neighbour
search stay three-dimensional and refuse other d; two-dimensional runs
take the eager region and the float64 search.

**Checks.** 201 tests before, 207 after (new: Levi-Civita and pseudovector
construction; 2-D rotation, translation, magnitude and reflection
contracts for ranks 0 to 2 of both parities; 2-D gradients, k-nearest
aggregation and interior query tokens; 2-D rank-1 and rank-2 inputs; a
4-D even-parity smoke test with odd parity refused; dimension-mismatch
refusal). A seeded 3-D fixture reproduces bitwise on all four outputs and
the parameter counts are unchanged (41,364 for a scalar plus vector
spec). On the RTX 4090 at 20,000 tokens, hidden 192, 12 layers, 256
slices: a native 2-D training step is 315 ms against 350 ms for the same
problem embedded in 3-D on the eager path, and 85 ms for the 3-D fused
kernel. So the native run is 10% cheaper than the embedded eager run and
3.7x slower than the fused kernel; a two-dimensional fused kernel is the
follow-up before any 2-D lane runs natively at protocol scale, and the
recipe's datapipe must deliver two-component point arrays and a `dim: 2`
in the model configs.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, LOCAL-AGG on OLBC Poisson (512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds each): local relational aggregation closes the fixed-mesh gap and overshoots it at both rungs, ISLA 0.229 / 0.081 against GeoTransolver-512 0.279 / 0.098; the radius is insensitive (0.05 vs 0.15); the same-snapshot control shows part of the earlier gap was the code snapshot {#sec-nb-local-agg-poisson-verdict}

**Setting.** LOCAL-AGG (@sec-nb-local-agg-prereg) adds a contract-preserving
local relational aggregation among tokens: each token pools its 32
nearest tokens with measure-weighted Gaussian kernel weights over their
states and pair invariants, before the slice routing. The question was
whether this closes what the boundary-value extension leaves on the OLBC
Poisson set, where GeoTransolver-512 led ISLA by about 3x at the reference
configuration and the extension recovered 0.80 to 0.84 of the log-gap.
The 512-case interim (@sec-nb-local-agg-interim) said closes; this entry
adds the 2,048 rung, the second radius and the same-snapshot control.

**What we saw (float32 per-case relative L2 on $u$ over the 256 test
cases; fractions of the log-gap between the frame-free reference and
GeoTransolver-512).** At 512 cases: reference 0.867, GeoTransolver-512
0.279, extension 0.333 (campaign om, code_ref), extension on code_v7
(the control) 0.299 (0.277 / 0.320; fraction 0.94), **extension + local
aggregation 0.229 (0.231 / 0.227; fraction 1.17)**. At 2,048 cases:
reference 0.395, GeoTransolver-512 0.098, extension 0.130 (0.125 /
0.135; fraction 0.80), **extension + local aggregation at radius 0.05:
0.081 (0.084 / 0.078; fraction 1.14)**, at radius 0.15: 0.082 (0.083 /
0.081; fraction 1.13). GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA = 1.22 at 512 and 1.21 at
2,048, on every seed. The step cost is 1.5x the extension arm's at 20,000
tokens.

**Verdict.** The preregistered *closes* clause (fraction $\ge 0.95$) fires
at both rungs on both seeds: ISLA with the boundary-value extension and
local aggregation leads GeoTransolver-512 by about 20% on the one dataset
where it trailed by 3x. The radius does not matter between 0.05 and 0.15,
so the gain is the existence of a direct local path among tokens, not
its scale. The control matters for the attribution: the extension alone
on code_v7 already recovers 0.94 at 512 against 0.85 on code_ref (the
snapshots differ in the routing default and the provided-geometry mode),
so against the fair control the aggregation moves the fraction from 0.94
to 1.17 at 512, a 23% lower error, and the 2,048 comparison awaits its
own control only in the sense that the extension arm there is a code_ref
run; the gain over it (0.130 to 0.081) is far larger than the snapshot
effect measured at 512 (0.333 to 0.299).

**Mechanism reading.** The slice routing pools tokens by learned state
over the whole domain; on a fixed mesh where the difficulty is the local
propagation of boundary data, a token had no path to its neighbours'
states except through the slices. The extension gives every interior
token the right boundary value, and the aggregation lets the tokens
smooth it locally, which is what a Poisson solution is. The elasticity
twin at 512 was *between* (0.545 to 0.605, @sec-nb-local-agg-elasticity-interim);
its 2,048 rung with a same-snapshot control and the frame-free AirfRANS
twin decide whether this is a Poisson-specific gain or a general one.
Under the two-dataset rule this is a standing on OLBC Poisson and an
interim for the architecture. Artifact results/local_agg_2026-09-27.json.

## 2026-09-27 — Interim, HARMONIC and EXT-ABL at 512 Poisson cases (two seeds): the harmonic fields beat the extension (0.250 against 0.299 on the same snapshot) and GeoTransolver-512 (0.279), but the per-type distances alone score 0.202, better than every arm including the value averages they were bundled with; two follow-up arms launched {#sec-nb-harmonic-interim-512}

**Setting.** HARMONIC (@sec-nb-harmonic-prereg) swaps the six inverse-square
extension scalars for six harmonic fields (three per-type harmonic
measures, three per-type harmonic extensions of the prescribed values);
EXT-ABL splits the extension into its three value averages and its three
per-type distances. All arms run on code_v7 with the provided-geometry
mode; the fair reference is the extension on the same snapshot (0.299,
fraction 0.94; @sec-nb-local-agg-poisson-verdict), not the older 0.333.

**What we saw (512 cases, 256 test cases, float32 relative L2 on $u$,
two seeds; fractions of the log-gap between the frame-free reference
0.867 and GeoTransolver-512 0.279).**

| arm | $u$ | seeds | fraction |
|---|---|---|---|
| extension, code_ref (om) | 0.333 | 0.318 / 0.347 | 0.85 |
| extension, code_v7 (control) | 0.299 | 0.277 / 0.320 | 0.94 |
| values only (three averages) | 0.307 | 0.297 / 0.316 | 0.92 |
| **distances only (three per-type distances)** | **0.202** | 0.200 / 0.205 | **1.28** |
| harmonic measures + extensions (six fields) | 0.250 | 0.242 / 0.257 | 1.10 |
| extension + local aggregation (LOCAL-AGG) | 0.229 | 0.231 / 0.227 | 1.17 |
| GeoTransolver-512 | 0.279 | 0.283 / 0.275 | 1.00 |

: HARMONIC and EXT-ABL at 512 cases beside the LOCAL-AGG and control arms. {#tbl-harmonic-512}

**Reading.** Against the preregistered bars the harmonic arm is "kernel
pays" (0.16 above the control's fraction; 11% better than GeoTransolver-512),
and EXT-ABL reads "either suffices" because both halves clear 0.75 of the
extension's fraction. But the numbers say more than the clauses. The
distances alone are the best arm on the set, 32% better than the full
extension on the same snapshot and 19% better than the harmonic fields,
and adding the value averages to them makes things worse (0.202 to
0.299). So the inverse-square value averages were not the working part
of the extension; the per-type distances were, and the averages were
noise the model had to learn around. This is Peter's per-type distance
vector (@sec-nb-extension-call) landing as the strongest single interior
channel measured so far, and it says the harmonic measures, which
compress distance into a probability in [0, 1] that saturates near the
walls, lose metric information the distances keep. Anomaly to chase: is
it the harmonic *extensions* (the value half) that drag the harmonic arm
down, as the value averages drag the extension down, and do measures plus
distances add? Both seeds agree on every ordering.

**Follow-up arms (preregistered here, launched now on campaign hm rows
14-21, 512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds each).** `hm_measures_only`: the
three harmonic measures without the value extensions. `hm_plus_dist`: the
three measures plus the three per-type distances. Bars against the
distances-only arm at the same rung: *measures redundant* if
measures-only is within 3% of distances-only and measures plus distances
within 3% of distances-only; *measures add* if measures plus distances is
$\ge 5\%$ better than distances-only on both seeds; *values hurt* if
measures-only beats the six-field harmonic arm by $\ge 5\%$ (the value
half was the drag). Prediction: values hurt (0.6), measures redundant
(0.5), measures add (0.3). The 2,048 rung of every arm is training.
Artifact results/harmonic_2026-09-27.json.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, HARMONIC on AirfRANS interior (800 airfoils, two seeds): the airfoil's harmonic measure on top of the stored distance field is 4% better on pressure, unchanged on velocity and 6% worse on eddy viscosity; with one boundary type the harmonic channel is nearly redundant with the distance field {#sec-nb-harmonic-airfrans-verdict}

**Setting.** The AirfRANS half of HARMONIC (@sec-nb-harmonic-prereg) adds
the harmonic measure of the airfoil (the far field tagged as the
complementary type) as a query scalar on top of the provided-geometry
reference, which already reads the stored signed distance field and its
gradient. Reference configuration, 800 airfoils, 100,000 queries, two
seeds, against the `sg_af_provided` pair on the same test split.

**What we saw (relative L2, two-seed means; ratio harmonic ÷
reference).** Pressure 0.0314 against 0.0328 (**0.956**; seeds 0.938 /
0.973). Velocity 0.01605 against 0.01613 (0.995). Eddy viscosity 0.0341
against 0.0323 (**1.056**; seeds 1.112 / 1.006). Under the preregistered
clauses the eddy-viscosity ratio above 1.05 fires *hurts* while pressure
clears the *pays* threshold, so the honest reading is mixed: a small
consistent gain on pressure, nothing on velocity, and a seed-dependent
loss on eddy viscosity.

**Reading.** AirfRANS has one boundary type, the airfoil, and its
harmonic measure against the far field is a smooth monotone function of
the distance the model already reads, so the channel adds little
information and the effects are at the few-percent level in both
directions. This is consistent with the OLBC result
(@sec-nb-harmonic-interim-512), where the strong gain came from the
per-type distances on a domain with three condition types: the value of
a per-type geometry channel scales with the number of boundary types the
problem has. Where the routing seam of the minimum-distance geometry sits
(the medial axis) the AirfRANS interior is far from the airfoil and the
fields are smooth, so the seam cost the reference little to begin with.
No configuration change on AirfRANS follows from this; the standing
there stays with the provided-geometry reference. Artifact
results/harmonic_2026-09-27.json.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, HARMONIC follow-ups at 512 Poisson cases (two seeds): the three harmonic measures alone score 0.207, the same as the three per-type distances (0.202); adding the value extensions (0.250) or stacking measures with distances (0.232) hurts; one geometry scalar per boundary type is the channel, and the two encodings are interchangeable here {#sec-nb-harmonic-followup-512}

**Setting.** The 512-case interim (@sec-nb-harmonic-interim-512) left two
questions: was the six-field harmonic arm dragged down by its value half,
as the extension was, and do harmonic measures add to per-type distances?
Two arms answered them: `hm_measures` (the three harmonic measures only)
and `hm_plus_dist` (measures plus the three per-type distances).

**What we saw (512 cases, two seeds; relative L2 on $u$).** Measures only
**0.207** (0.201 / 0.213), against distances only 0.202 (0.200 / 0.205),
the six-field harmonic arm 0.250 (0.242 / 0.257), and measures plus
distances **0.232** (0.213 / 0.250). GeoTransolver-512 is 0.279 and the
extension on the same snapshot 0.299.

**Verdict against the preregistered clauses.** *Values hurt* fires:
measures alone are 17% better than the six fields, so the harmonic
extensions of the prescribed values, like the inverse-square value
averages before them, cost accuracy rather than adding it. *Measures
add* does not fire; the combination is 15% worse than distances alone
and its seed spread widens (0.213 / 0.250), so redundant encodings of
the same geometry hurt at this training-set size. *Measures redundant*
does not fire on the letter of its clause only because the combination
is not within 3%; on the mean, measures alone and distances alone differ
by 2.4%, which is the seed spread.

**Reading.** The channel that closes the fixed-mesh gap is one geometry
scalar per boundary-condition type, telling each interior point how it
stands relative to every type of boundary; whether that scalar is the
minimum distance or the harmonic measure does not matter at this rung.
The prescribed values themselves should not be fed as smeared fields;
the model reads them from the boundary tokens through the routing and
does better without a preprocessed version. The harmonic measure remains
the principled choice (smooth, dimension-agnostic, a partition of unity)
and the 2,048 rung decides whether the tie holds where the seam of the
minimum distance might matter more. Both channels beat the local
aggregation arm (0.229), and the two mechanisms are different in kind (a
per-token input against a token-to-token path), so their combination is
the next arm.

**Preregistration, per-type channel plus local aggregation (campaign hm
rows 22-29, 512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds).** `hm_measures_local05`: the
three harmonic measures plus the k-nearest local aggregation
(`local_rho` 0.05, 32 neighbours); `ext_distonly_local05`: the three
per-type distances plus the same aggregation. Bars, ratio to the better
of the two single arms at the same rung: *additive* $\le 0.90$ on both
seeds; *redundant* within 5%; *hurts* $> 1.05$. Prediction: additive
(0.5), redundant (0.4). The datum the inputs are: the geometry and the
boundary condition labels of the one sample.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, REF on the 510-wing rung: 12 and 24 layers are within seed noise (0.0404 against 0.0397 on pressure, two seeds each); GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA 0.95 at the protocol cell count, the wing deficit narrowed from the 35-wing rung {#sec-nb-ref-hl510-verdict}

**Setting.** The reference-configuration board (@sec-nb-refboard-prereg)
runs ISLA at R1 (384 x 12 x 256, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4) and
R2 (384 x 24, the depth rule 2.5e-4) on every HiLift rung at 200,000
cells. The 510-wing pair finished and scored today (180 validation
wings, float32 relative L2).

**What we saw.** Pressure: R1 **0.0404** (0.0405 / 0.0403), R2 **0.0397**
(0.0399 / 0.0396); R2 ÷ R1 = 0.98. Wall shear: R1 0.0889 (0.0892 /
0.0886), R2 0.0878 (0.0876 / 0.0881); 0.99. The SCALE-LAW GeoTransolver-512
pair at 510 wings and 100,000 cells scores 0.0382 (0.0368 / 0.0396;
@sec-nb-scalelaw-wing-rung4), and SCALE-HL found GeoTransolver's cell
count flat between 100,000 and 200,000 (0.99), so the protocol-scale
standing on this rung is GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA R1 = **0.95** on
pressure, against 0.89 at 35 wings (@sec-nb-frame-wing-verdict era
numbers for the frame-free pair) and about 0.90 at 210 wings on the
interim (@sec-nb-ref-hl210-interim).

**Verdict.** Depth is null on the wings as on the cars (ROUTE-NORM found
0.0413 / 0.0407 at 12 / 24 layers on 435 cars) and on OLBC elasticity, and
costs on OLBC Poisson; the reference stays at 12 layers on every dataset
where it has been tested. The wing deficit against GeoTransolver-512
shrinks with training cases (0.89, about 0.90, 0.95 at 35, 210, 510
wings), consistent with the steeper ISLA learning curve of the SCALE-LAW
wing half (local exponents 0.50 to 0.57 against 0.45 to 0.47 between 35
and 210 wings). The 210-wing GeoTransolver-512 pair is 62 of 180 cases
into scoring and decides the 210-case anatomy twin. Metrics under
results/campaigns_2026-09-22/ref/metrics.

## 2026-09-27 — Verdict, REF on the 210-wing rung and the WING-ANATOMY twin: GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA 0.90 on pressure and 0.94 on wall shear; the deficit is 0.92 below 16 degrees and 0.87 above, a widening of 0.05 that misses the preregistered 0.08, so the 35-wing angle location does not reproduce at 210 wings {#sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict}

**Setting.** The 35-wing rung located ISLA's deficit against
GeoTransolver-512 by angle of attack: 0.77 up to 14 degrees, 0.67 from 16
degrees, where both errors double at flow separation
(@sec-nb-hl35-percase). The 210-case twin was preregistered with the bar
"a widening of at least 0.08 between the 4-14 and 16-22 degree ratios".
The GeoTransolver-512 pair at 210 wings finished scoring tonight (180
validation wings on 118 geometries, 200,000 cells, float32).

**What we saw.** Pressure: GeoTransolver-512 **0.0461** (0.0453 / 0.0468),
ISLA R1 **0.0513** (0.0550 / 0.0476; @sec-nb-ref-hl210-interim), ratio
**0.90**; R2 0.0508. Wall shear: 0.1039 against 0.1103, ratio 0.94. By
angle (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA, seed-mean per case): 0.84 / 0.87 / 0.87
/ 0.92 / 0.88 / 1.11 at 4 to 14 degrees and 0.81 / 0.89 / 0.86 / 0.92 at
16 to 22; group means **0.92 and 0.87**, a widening of 0.05. Spearman
rank correlation of the per-case errors 0.97; ISLA is the more accurate
model on 33 of 180 cases. The 24-layer variant is within 4% of the
reference in every group but one (1.11 at 16 degrees).

**Verdict.** The bar is missed: the 35-wing angle location does not
reproduce at 210 wings. The deficit shrank from 0.77 to 0.92 below 16
degrees and from 0.67 to 0.87 above, so the separated regime improved
more with data than the attached one, and what remains is a nearly
uniform 8 to 13% across angles with one angle (14 degrees) where ISLA
leads. With the 510-wing rung at 0.95 (@sec-nb-ref-hl510-verdict) the
wing deficit is a learning-rate-of-data effect that closes with cases,
not a fixed regime failure, which is the SCALE-LAW reading (steeper ISLA
exponents) and the reason the 1,260-wing rung matters. The ISLA pressure
seeds at 210 wings differ by 15% (0.0550 / 0.0476), the largest seed
spread on the wing ladder; a third seed is not warranted under the
seeds rule, but the standing is quoted with its spread. Artifact
results/hl210_percase_2026-09-27.json.

## 2026-09-28 — Verdict, lug depth at the depth rate with three seeds: 24 layers at 2.5e-4 scores 0.89 of 12 layers on the three-seed means, paired 0.995 / 0.75 / 0.95; depth pays modestly on the lug at 2,400 cases, and the 12-layer seed 43 was the outlier {#sec-nb-lug-depth-verdict}

**Setting.** The lug depth interim (@sec-nb-lug-r2-rate-interim) could not separate a depth gain from a 12-layer
outlier with two seeds (0.99 and 0.75 paired), so a third seed of both
configurations ran at 2,400 GINOT lugs, the one place in the program
where a third seed is spent. Readout: float32 relative L2 of von Mises
stress on the 600 test lugs.

**What we saw.** 12 layers (R1): 0.00192 / 0.00238 / 0.00204, mean
**0.00211**. 24 layers at 2.5e-4 (R2): 0.00191 / 0.00179 / 0.00193, mean
**0.00188**. Paired ratios 24 ÷ 12: **0.995 / 0.75 / 0.95**; mean of
means 0.89; median 0.95. The 24-layer seeds span 8%, the 12-layer seeds
24%, and the 12-layer seed 43 at 0.00238 sits 17% above its two
companions. GeoTransolver-256 0.00202 (0.00214 / 0.00190),
GeoTransolver-512 0.00217 (0.00183 / 0.00250); GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA
= 1.03 at 12 layers and 1.15 at 24.

**Verdict.** Under the SOLIDS depth clause (within 1.5% means depth does
not pay) two of three paired ratios clear it (5% and 25% better) and one
is parity, so **depth pays on the lug at 2,400 cases**, by about 5 to
10% on the robust reading and 11% on the means, with the outlier seed
supplying the larger figure. This is the one dataset where depth pays:
the cars (0.0413 / 0.0407 at 12 / 24 layers), the wings (0.0404 /
0.0397 at 510), OLBC elasticity (within seed noise) and DeepJEB (at the
depth rate) are null, and OLBC Poisson pays for depth. The reference
stays at 12 layers; the lug result is recorded as a dataset-specific
gain, and the mechanism reading offered in the interim (the lug's
stress concentration at the hole needs more sequential refinement) is
kept as the hypothesis it is. ISLA at either depth is at parity with or
ahead of both GeoTransolver widths at 2,400 lugs. Artifact
results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json (refreshed with the third seeds).

## 2026-09-28 — Preregistration, ND-GENERIC pass 2: the OLBC Poisson distances-only arm rerun natively in two dimensions (`dim: 2` on a plane-restricted datapipe), 512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds, against the embedded three-dimensional arm {#sec-nb-ndgeneric-2d-prereg}

**Setting.** Pass 1 of ND-GENERIC (@sec-nb-ndgeneric-pass1) gave ISLA a
`dim` argument so that every geometric quantity (relative vectors, the
isotropic tensors, the pseudovectors, the rank specs of vector and tensor
inputs and outputs) is built for $d$ components, with the three-dimensional
numerics bitwise unchanged. Every two-dimensional dataset in the program
(the OLBC square, Tensile2d, AirfRANS) has so far run as a
three-dimensional model on a plane at $z = 0$. The second pass closes the
loop on a real dataset: a recipe transform, `RestrictToPlane`, drops the
constant coordinate from the interior nodes, the boundary polyline and the
named vector fields (in-plane boundary normals, SDF normals) and refuses a
mesh whose dropped coordinate is not constant, so the model receives
two-component points and runs its native two-dimensional path. The
boundary-value extension computed in the plane equals the embedded one to
roundoff (recipe test `tests/test_restrict_to_plane.py`), so the arm
differs from its control in the model's dimension only.

**Question.** Does the native two-dimensional model reproduce the embedded
three-dimensional one? The embedded model carries a third component in
every relative vector and normal that is identically zero, and its
pseudovector features (cross products of in-plane vectors) point out of the
plane, so it spends parameters on components that carry no information.
The two-dimensional model has none of that. If the code path is right, the
two should agree within seed noise; a difference in either direction is
informative (a gain would say the dead components cost accuracy, a loss
would say the two-dimensional path has a defect or that the extra
components were doing work).

**Arms (campaign nd, code_v9 = code_v8 plus the ISLA overlay of commit
2b77562e, recipe_v4).** `nd_poisson_ext_distonly_2d_n{512,2048}_seed{42,43}`:
the distances-only arm (@sec-nb-harmonic-followup-512; three per-type
distances as query scalars, K = 0, eager geometry region, provided SDF
normals) with `dim: 2` on the dataset `olbc_poisson_ext_2d`. Controls: the
scored embedded arm `hm_poisson_ext_distonly_n512_seed{42,43}` (0.202
mean) and the 2,048 pair when it scores. Same rate 5e-4, 500 epochs,
20,000 interior queries, 256 test cases, float32 scoring.

**Bars (mean of two seeds, ratio native ÷ embedded on the relative L2 of
u).** Within 0.03 of one on both rungs: **dimension-generic path
validated** and the ledger acceptance criterion for ND-GENERIC is met on
the accuracy side. Below 0.97 on both rungs: the embedding costs accuracy
and the native path becomes the recommendation for planar problems. Above
1.03 on either rung: a defect or a capacity effect; the follow-up is a
seeded fixture comparing the two paths layer by layer before any further
two-dimensional lane. Also recorded: step time and peak memory of the two
arms from the training logs (the native model has fewer geometry
features, so it must not be slower). Pending after this pass: the
two-dimensional fused Triton kernel and a second native dataset
(Tensile2d or AirfRANS).

## 2026-09-28 — Verdict, HARMONIC and EXT-ABL at 2,048 Poisson cases (two seeds): the per-type distances alone score 0.0744 and the harmonic measures alone 0.0700 (6% better on both seeds), both ahead of GeoTransolver-512's 0.0981; the value channels hurt at both rungs and stacking the two encodings hurts; the geometry-per-type channel is the mechanism, and the harmonic measure is the better encoding at the larger rung {#sec-nb-harmonic-2048-verdict}

**Setting.** Two preregistered studies (@sec-nb-harmonic-prereg) share the
OLBC Poisson set, a fixed square mesh whose boundary is cut per sample into
random Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin segments with random values.
EXT-ABL splits the six-scalar boundary-value extension into its two
halves, the three per-type inverse-square value averages and the three
per-type nearest distances. HARMONIC replaces the inverse-square kernel by
Laplace solves on the interior point cloud: the harmonic measure of each
condition type (the hitting probability, 1 on that type's boundary nodes
and 0 on the others) and the harmonic extension of the prescribed values.
The 512-case verdicts (@sec-nb-harmonic-followup-512) found the distances
alone (0.202) and the measures alone (0.207) interchangeable and best,
with every arm that carried values worse. This entry closes both studies
at 2,048 cases; the reference numbers are the frame-free ISLA (0.395), the
inverse-square extension (0.130) and GeoTransolver-512 (0.0981).

**What we saw (2,048 cases, 256 test cases, relative L2 on u, seed
means with seeds in parentheses).** Distances only **0.0744** (0.0705 /
0.0783); harmonic measures only **0.0700** (0.0665 / 0.0734); the six
harmonic fields 0.0768 (0.0748 / 0.0788); measures plus distances 0.0795
(0.0774 / 0.0815); values only 0.0976 (0.0899 / 0.1053). Fractions of the
log-gap between the reference and GeoTransolver-512: 1.20 / 1.24 / 1.18 /
1.15 / 1.00. GeoTransolver-512 ÷ arm: 1.32 / 1.40 / 1.28 / 1.23 / 1.01. The
ratio of measures-only to distances-only is 0.94 on both seeds (0.943 /
0.937), against 1.02 at 512.

**Verdicts against the bars.** EXT-ABL: the values-only arm recovers 1.00
of the extension's 0.80 and the distances-only arm 1.20, so the
preregistered clause is *either suffices* on paper; the reading that
matters is that each half alone beats the two together (0.130), so the
value averages and the distances interfere when both are present, and the
distances are the better half at both rungs. HARMONIC: the six harmonic
fields recover 1.18 against the extension's 0.80, *kernel pays* by the
preregistered clause at both rungs (1.10 at 512); but the follow-up
clauses say where the gain lives: the value channels hurt at both rungs
(the six fields are 3% worse than the measures alone here, 21% at 512),
stacking the measures with the distances hurts (7% worse than the
distances at 2,048, 15% at 512), and the measures are not redundant with
the distances at 2,048 (6% better on both seeds) though they were within
2% at 512. **The mechanism is one geometry scalar per condition type that
tells a query how strongly each type of wall reaches it; the prescribed
values reach the readout better through the slice attention than through
any pre-computed average, and the harmonic measure is the better encoding
of the geometry scalar once the model has 2,048 cases to learn from.**
Both encodings are admissible inputs: they derive from one sample's
geometry and its condition labels and nothing else.

**Why it matters.** The three per-type distances are a signed-distance
field split by condition type, the harmonic measures are the same
information passed through the domain's own Laplace operator, so the
6% at 2,048 is the price of the crude encoding, not a different channel.
Against GeoTransolver-512 the frame-free ISLA trailed by 4x at this rung
(0.395 against 0.098) and now leads by 1.40x with three pre-computed
scalars per query and no learned parameters added. Artifact
results/harmonic_2026-09-27.json (poisson, 2048).

**What's next.** The combined arms (per-type channel plus local
aggregation, @sec-nb-combined-512-interim) at 2,048 are at epoch 350; the
elasticity set (three condition types, vector data) is the second dataset
for the harmonic measure and is the next lane to stage.

## 2026-09-28 — Interim, per-type channel plus local aggregation at 512 Poisson cases (two seeds): distances plus aggregation 0.164 (0.81 of the distances alone, both seeds; additive), measures plus aggregation 0.177 (0.86 of the measures alone; 0.90 / 0.81 per seed); GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA 1.70; the 2,048 rung decides {#sec-nb-combined-512-interim}

per-token input against a token-to-token path), so their combination
was preregistered with the bars: *additive* at or below 0.90 of the
better single arm on both seeds, *redundant* within 5%, *hurts* above
1.05.

**What we saw (512 cases, 256 test cases, relative L2 on u).** Distances
plus aggregation **0.164** (0.167 / 0.162), against the distances alone
0.202 and the aggregation alone 0.229: ratio to the better single arm
0.81, per seed 0.84 / 0.79, **additive**. Harmonic measures plus
aggregation **0.177** (0.182 / 0.173), against the measures alone 0.207:
ratio 0.86, per seed 0.90 / 0.81 against the distances-only arm (0.91 on
seed 42, which misses the 0.90 clause by one point) and 0.90 / 0.81
against the measures themselves; additive on one seed and at the boundary
on the other. GeoTransolver-512 (0.279) ÷ ISLA with distances and
aggregation = **1.70**, against 1.38 for the distances alone and 1.22 for
the aggregation alone.

**Reading.** The two remedies carry different information, as the
preregistration argued: the channel tells each query how each condition
type reaches it, the aggregation lets neighbouring queries share what
they resolved, and the gains compound (the log-gap fraction goes from
1.28 or 1.17 to 1.47). This is the 512-case rung only; the 2,048 lanes
(hm rows 24-25 and 28-29) are at epoch 350 and decide, together with
