results/harmonic_2026-09-27.json (poisson, 512, combined).

## 2026-09-28 — Verdict, LOCAL-AGG on OLBC elasticity at 2,048 cases (two seeds) and interim on AirfRANS (one seed): with the aggregation ISLA's three stress components reach GeoTransolver-512 (ratios 1.05 / 1.02 / 1.03) while displacement trails at 0.77; against the same-snapshot control the stresses improve 14 to 18% and displacement worsens 7%, with a 20% seed split; on AirfRANS interior the aggregation hurts every field (1.13 / 1.20 / 1.37) {#sec-nb-local-agg-elasticity-verdict}

**Setting.** LOCAL-AGG (@sec-nb-local-agg-prereg) adds a contract-preserving
local relational aggregation among tokens to ISLA. On the OLBC Poisson
set it closed the fixed-mesh gap at both rungs
(@sec-nb-local-agg-poisson-verdict). The second fixed-mesh dataset is OLBC
elasticity (a steel disc with two holes, prescribed displacement and
tractions per boundary segment, four target fields: displacement and the
three stress components), where the best ISLA arm is RANK-IO (the
prescribed vectors as rank-1 boundary inputs and the stress as one
symmetric rank-2 output). The 512-case interim
(@sec-nb-local-agg-elasticity-interim) read *between*: stresses 3 to 4%
better, displacement unchanged. The 2,048 rung carries a same-snapshot
control without the aggregation (@sec-nb-local-agg-elasticity-ctrl-2048;
0.201 / 0.297 / 0.305 / 0.301, log-gap fraction 0.787). The third
dataset is the AirfRANS interior task (800 airfoils, 100,000 interior
queries drawn per epoch from a point cloud, varying geometry), the
frame-free reference pair `sg_af_provided` against the same model with the
aggregation.

**What we saw on elasticity (2,048 cases, 256 test cases, relative L2 on
displacement / $\sigma_{11}$ / $\sigma_{22}$ / $\sigma_{12}$).** With the
aggregation **0.216 / 0.244 / 0.256 / 0.258** (seed 42: 0.198 / 0.229 /
0.239 / 0.241; seed 43: 0.233 / 0.259 / 0.272 / 0.276). GeoTransolver-512:
0.165 / 0.257 / 0.261 / 0.267, so GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA = **0.77 / 1.05
/ 1.02 / 1.03**. Fractions of the log-gap from the scalar-input reference
to GeoTransolver-512: 0.65 / 1.07 / 1.03 / 1.05, mean 0.95, the
preregistered *closes* clause on the mean, met by the three stresses and
missed by displacement. Against the same-snapshot control, aggregation ÷
control = 1.07 / 0.82 / 0.84 / 0.86 on the means; per seed, seed 42 gives
0.96 / 0.74 / 0.75 / 0.77 and seed 43 gives 1.20 / 0.91 / 0.93 / 0.95. The
two aggregation seeds are 18% apart on displacement and 13% on the
stresses where the control pair is within 7%.

**What we saw on AirfRANS (one seed, 200 test airfoils, relative L2 on
pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity).** Reference 0.0328 / 0.0161 /
0.0323; with the aggregation 0.0368 / 0.0191 / 0.0417, ratios **1.13 /
1.20 / 1.37**: the *hurts* clause (any field above 1.05) on every field.
The second seed has finished training and is being scored; the reading
would need a reversal of 20 to 37% on that seed to change.

**Verdicts.** On elasticity the aggregation is the difference between
trailing GeoTransolver-512 by 1.2x on the stresses and matching it: the
stress fields close on both seeds (worst per-seed GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA
0.97 on seed 43's $\sigma_{12}$), and displacement, the one field that
was already the closest to GeoTransolver-512 without aggregation, moves
the other way. With Poisson this is **the second fixed-mesh dataset on
which the aggregation pays**, and the reading is sharpened: the
aggregation pays on the fields whose deficit was value transport across
the fixed mesh (the stress components, which the boundary tractions
determine through the interior) and not on the field that the extension
of the prescribed displacement already served. On AirfRANS it hurts on
every field. The mechanism is not measured; the hypothesis for the
follow-up is that the neighbourhoods on a fixed mesh are the same at
every epoch and at test time, so the pooled statistics are a stable
function of position, while on the AirfRANS point cloud the 100,000
queries are redrawn every epoch and the 32 nearest neighbours of a query
change from draw to draw, so the aggregation sees a different stencil each
time and learns a noisier function. **The aggregation enters the class as
a documented option recommended for fixed-mesh interior tasks and not for
resampled point clouds; it is not part of the reference configuration.**

**What's next.** Score the second AirfRANS seed; test the stencil
hypothesis with a fixed query draw on AirfRANS (a diagnostic that isolates
the resampling from the geometry variation); a fused local kernel is
justified only if a surface task shows a gain. Artifact
results/local_agg_2026-09-27.json (elasticity 2048, airfrans).

## 2026-09-28 — Preregistration, LOCAL-AGG stencil diagnostic on AirfRANS: does the aggregation's loss on a resampled point cloud disappear when each airfoil keeps one fixed query draw? Two arms on a fixed draw, two seeds {#sec-nb-local-agg-stencil-prereg}

**Setting.** The local relational aggregation pays on both fixed-mesh OLBC
sets and hurts on the AirfRANS interior task by 13 to 37%
(@sec-nb-local-agg-elasticity-verdict). The one structural difference
between those tasks is how the queries are drawn: an OLBC case is one
fixed mesh whose 16,598 or 11,786 nodes are all present at every epoch,
while an AirfRANS case has about 177,000 nodes of which the datapipe draws
100,000 afresh every epoch, so the 32 nearest tokens of a physical point
differ from visit to visit and the aggregation learns from a stencil that
never repeats. The geometry also varies on AirfRANS and not on OLBC, so the
resampling is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis.

**Instrument.** A recipe reader, `FixedDrawDomainMeshReader`, ignores the
epoch in the subsampling seed, so each airfoil keeps the draw of epoch 0 for
the whole run (test-time draws are unchanged). Two arms on this reader,
campaign la rows 18-21 on code_v7, 800 airfoils, 100,000 queries, seeds 42
and 43: the frame-free interior reference (no aggregation) as the fixed-draw
control, and the same model with the aggregation ($\rho$ 0.05, 32
neighbours). The comparison is aggregation ÷ control on the fixed draw
against the resampled pair's 1.13 / 1.20 / 1.37 (pressure / velocity / eddy
viscosity).

**Bars (two-seed means, every field).** *Stencil hypothesis supported*:
aggregation ÷ control at or below 1.03 on every field under the fixed draw.
*Refuted*: at or above 1.10 on any field (the loss survives a fixed
stencil, so it is about the varying geometry or the point cloud itself).
*Between* otherwise. Also read: fixed-draw control ÷ resampled reference,
the price of losing the per-epoch augmentation (expected above one; it
does not enter the verdict). Prediction: supported (0.45), between (0.35),
refuted (0.2). If supported, the remedy for point clouds is a stencil that
is a function of position and not of the draw (a fixed per-case
neighbour graph, or aggregation over the boundary tokens only, which are
never resampled); if refuted, the aggregation stays a fixed-mesh option.

## 2026-09-28 — Preregistration, LOCAL-LPR: polynomial-reproduction stencil weights and finite-difference channels for the local aggregation, after the meshfree exterior calculus of Shaffer, Kinch, Hsieh and Trask (arXiv 2605.08436); AirfRANS interior (two arms) and OLBC Poisson 512 (regression check), two seeds {#sec-nb-local-lpr-prereg}

**Setting.** The local relational aggregation pays on the two fixed-mesh
OLBC sets and hurts by 13 to 22% on the AirfRANS interior, whose 100,000
queries are redrawn from a 177,000-node cloud every epoch
(@sec-nb-local-agg-airfrans-verdict). The fixed-draw diagnostic
(@sec-nb-local-agg-stencil-prereg) asks whether the redraw is the cause.
This entry preregisters the remedy that the meshfree-calculus paper Peter
pointed at suggests, and it is a test of the same hypothesis by a different
instrument. In that paper the discrete divergence on an epsilon-ball graph
is given edge weights chosen so that the stencil reproduces linear vector
polynomials at every node (one sparse quadratic program), which makes the
operator a consistent estimate of the continuum divergence for any
quasi-uniform point cloud; and the learned flux law reads invariant
edge-frame features, the midpoint state and the state difference along the
edge divided by its length. Our aggregation instead pools the 32 nearest
tokens with normalized measure-weighted Gaussian weights, a smoother whose
first moment is O(h) on an asymmetric stencil: the pooled value at a
physical point depends on which neighbours the draw supplied.

**The change (ISLA `local_weights="lpr"`, `local_gradient`; commit
56e0c74f).** With `lpr`, each token's neighbour weights are the value row
of the weighted least-squares fit of an affine field over its neighbours
(a generalized moving least squares stencil of degree one, computed from
positions only, no parameters, a (d + 1) by (d + 1) solve per token). They
sum to one and have zero first moment, so an affine field is reproduced
exactly at the token (tested to 1e-4) and the pooled value is a consistent
estimate of the same continuum quantity for any neighbour draw, which is
the property the Gaussian weights lack. With `local_gradient`, the fit's
gradient of the token states, projected on the receiving token's normal and
on each global direction (K + 1 invariant channels per hidden unit, in units
of the state per radius), is pooled alongside: the edge-frame directional
derivative of the paper's flux law, made a token feature. Both keep the
rotation, translation and reflection contracts (tests); the default path is
unchanged.

**Arms (campaign lw, code_v10 = code_v9 plus the overlay of 56e0c74f,
recipe_v4; two seeds each).** On AirfRANS interior (800 airfoils, 100,000
queries, the resampled datapipe, against the frame-free reference pair
`sg_af_provided` 0.0328 / 0.0161 / 0.0323 and the Gaussian aggregation
0.0370 / 0.0188 / 0.0393): `lw_af_provided_local05_lpr` (weights only) and
`lw_af_provided_local05_lpr_grad` (weights plus the finite-difference
channels). On OLBC Poisson at 512 cases (fixed mesh, where the Gaussian
aggregation with the per-type distances scores 0.164):
`lw_poisson_ext_distonly_local05_lpr_n512`, the regression check that
consistent weights do not undo the fixed-mesh gain.

**Bars (two-seed means).** AirfRANS, lpr arm ÷ frame-free reference, the
same bars as the stencil diagnostic: *stencil cause confirmed and remedied*
at or below 1.03 on every field (and *pays* if any field is at or below
0.97 with none above 1.03); *refuted* at or above 1.10 on any field (the
loss is not the weights' draw dependence); *between* otherwise. Gradient
arm ÷ lpr arm: *pays* at or below 0.95 on any field with none above 1.03,
*null* within 3%, *hurts* above 1.05. Poisson 512, lpr ÷ Gaussian: within
0.05 = consistent weights cost nothing on a fixed mesh; below 0.95 = they
pay there too; above 1.05 = a fixed-mesh regression that would confine them
to point clouds. Prediction: AirfRANS between (0.4), confirmed (0.35),
refuted (0.25); gradient channel null (0.5); Poisson within 0.05 (0.7).
Reading with the fixed-draw diagnostic: if the diagnostic says *supported*
and the lpr arm says *confirmed*, the resampled stencil is the mechanism
and the consistent weights are the remedy; if the diagnostic says
*supported* and the lpr arm says *refuted*, the draw dependence lives in
something the weights do not fix (the neighbour set itself); if the
diagnostic says *refuted*, the lpr arm's result stands on its own as a
discretization-invariance property. The inputs are admissible: neighbour
positions of the one sample and nothing else. Launched without waiting
for the diagnostic (no result dependency; the reading above covers every
combination).

## 2026-09-28 — Verdict, per-type channel plus local aggregation on OLBC Poisson (512 and 2,048 cases, two seeds): the two remedies compound at both rungs (distances plus aggregation 0.164 and 0.062 against 0.202 and 0.074 for the distances alone; GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA 1.70 and 1.58); the harmonic encoding under aggregation is 0.061 at 2,048 with a 15% seed split {#sec-nb-combined-verdict}

measures reach the lower mean with the wider spread.** The best ISLA on

## 2026-09-28 — Interim, LOCAL-LPR fixed-mesh check at 512 Poisson cases (two seeds): polynomial-reproduction weights cost 9% against the Gaussian weights on the fixed mesh (0.179 against 0.164; 1.03 / 1.14 per seed), a *fixed-mesh regression* by the preregistered bar; the AirfRANS arms decide whether they earn a place on point clouds {#sec-nb-local-lpr-poisson-interim}

**Setting.** LOCAL-LPR (@sec-nb-local-lpr-prereg) swaps the aggregation's
normalized Gaussian weights for degree-one polynomial-reproduction weights,
which make the pooled value a consistent estimate for any neighbour draw.
The Poisson 512 lanes are the regression check on a fixed mesh, where the
draw never changes and the consistency property buys nothing by
construction; the bar was within 0.05 of the Gaussian arm.

**What we saw (256 test cases, relative L2 on u).** Distances plus
aggregation with lpr weights **0.1785** (0.1721 / 0.1849) against the same
arm with Gaussian weights 0.1643 (0.1667 / 0.1619): ratio **1.09**, per
seed 1.03 / 1.14. Still 1.56x ahead of GeoTransolver-512 (0.279).

**Reading.** The *fixed-mesh regression* clause (above 1.05) holds on the
mean and on one seed; the other seed is within the band. A plausible
mechanism, not measured: the reproduction weights are not a convex
combination (they take both signs and their absolute sum exceeds one on
asymmetric stencils), so the pooled state carries more variance than the
Gaussian smoother's, and on a fixed mesh the smoother's O(h) bias is a
fixed function of position that the network absorbs for free. The
consistency property can therefore only pay where the stencil moves; the
AirfRANS arms (two seeds each, about a day out) decide, and if they pay
the weights become a point-cloud option gated by the datapipe, not a
replacement. Artifact results/harmonic_2026-09-27.json (poisson, 512, arm
lpr_distonly_local05).

## 2026-09-28 — Ruling (Peter) and preregistration, UNIVERSAL: per-dataset options read as p-hacking; the program wants one architecture; every option gets an always-on test on datasets its rule was not fitted on, and either becomes the default everywhere or is deleted; the local aggregation goes first (lug, Tensile2d, DrivAerML Volume, with same-snapshot references, two seeds) {#sec-nb-universal-prereg}

**The ruling.** Peter reviewed the day's ledger and objected to its shape:
"we are making lots of different variants that are dataset-specific ... I
really just want one model architecture that works well across many types
of physics and problem setups. Making tons of little tweaks that are
different for each dataset feels a little like p-hacking." The objection
is accepted on the following points. The book quotes the best ISLA arm
per dataset against a GeoTransolver-512 frozen at one configuration, and
the choice of which arm to quote is made after the test scores exist. The
local aggregation's scope (on for fixed meshes, off for resampled point
clouds) was derived from the three datasets that now confirm it. The
per-type geometry channel pays on Poisson and hurt on elasticity at 512
cases, and gating it on where it pays would be a forking path. The pushed
back part: inputs a solver also needs (condition types, geometry, and
scalars computed from them without parameters) are not tweaks, but their
inclusion must be a universal rule, tested where it was not fitted.

**The discipline adopted.** An option is a scaffold with two fates: it
becomes part of the reference configuration and is on for every dataset,
or it is deleted. No option keeps a per-dataset setting. Consequences:
(1) the headline scoreboard quotes the reference configuration only, one
recipe on every dataset, and every other number moves to a separately
labelled ablation table (a book edit, pending Peter's confirmation of the
restructure); (2) every surviving option gets an *always-on* test on the
datasets its rule was not fitted on; (3) options that already failed
their test are removed rather than documented.

**Preregistration, UNIVERSAL-AGG (campaign un rows 0-11, code_v10,
recipe_v4, two seeds each).** The local aggregation ($\rho$ 0.05, 32
neighbours) on top of the reference configuration, paired with the
reference configuration on the same snapshot, on three datasets it has
never seen, all of which draw their interior queries afresh per epoch:
the lug at 2,400 cases (scalar von Mises stress, 20,000 queries), Tensile2d
at 400 cases (tensor stress and displacement, 20,000 queries), and
DrivAerML Volume (pressure, velocity, eddy viscosity, 200,000 queries).
The aggregation rule fitted so far predicts *hurts* on all three (they are
resampled clouds like AirfRANS); the "one model" hypothesis needs
*neutral or better* on all three.

**Bars (two-seed means, aggregation ÷ same-snapshot reference, every
field).** *Default-on candidate*: at or below 1.03 on every field of every
dataset. *Not part of the model*: above 1.05 on any field of any dataset,
in which case the Poisson and elasticity results stand as findings about a
mechanism and the option is scheduled for deletion unless the AirfRANS
LOCAL-LPR arms show that consistent weights remove the loss, in which case
the lpr form is what gets the universal test. *Between* otherwise (a
single dataset within 1.03 to 1.05 triggers a third seed there before a
call). Prediction: not part of the model (0.55), between (0.3),
default-on candidate (0.15). The same test is owed to the per-type
geometry channel once the elasticity 2,048 rung reports, and to any option
proposed after today.

## 2026-09-29 — Preregistration, PROTO-COND: sample-conditioned slice prototypes (the FLARE++ routing-query idea inside ISLA's slice block), and GT-FPP: GeoTransolver with the FLARE++ backend added to the flagship baselines {#sec-nb-proto-cond-prereg}

**Setting.** Peter asked whether the FLARE and FLARE++ attention layers in
PhysicsNeMo could serve ISLA. ISLA's slice block is already a FLARE-class
two-pass mechanism (gather tokens into slices, scatter back), with two
things FLARE lacks: measure weights in the gather softmax (quadrature
consistency) and the equivariant geometric bias on the routing (the pose
robustness). Swapping the block for the shipped layer would remove both, so
it is not done. FLARE++'s one new idea, routing queries synthesized per
sample from learned seeds attending over the input, transfers cleanly:
ISLA's slice prototypes are static per layer, and a sample-conditioned
version is an architectural change with no dataset-specific input, on for
every dataset by construction.

**The change (ISLA `slice_prototypes="conditioned"`, commit 27903e6c).**
In every slice block each static prototype acts as a seed that attends over
the token states with a softmax whose logits carry the measure weights as a
log-space bias (a quadrature of the tokens, invariant to a uniform rescale
of the weights); the seed plus the attended value is the prototype the
cosine routing compares against. Token states are invariant features, so
the prototypes are invariant and rotation, translation, reflection, token
permutation and measure-rescale contracts all hold (tested to 1e-8 in
double); the cosine temperature still bounds the logits, which is the
guard against the routing collapse the reference removed. Cost: two
hidden-by-hidden maps per block, about 3.5 million parameters on the
34 million of the reference (10 percent), and one slices-by-tokens
attention per block.

**Hypothesis and instruments.** Static prototypes must cover every
sample's condition layout with one set of slots; conditioned prototypes can
reallocate slots to the segments that carry the data. The prediction is a
gain on the boundary-data problems and neutrality elsewhere. Lanes
(campaign pc, to launch when the pruning wave settles, i.e. after the
AirfRANS LOCAL-LPR and elasticity 2,048 verdicts): the reference
configuration with conditioned prototypes and no other option, against the
reference, two seeds each, on OLBC Poisson at 512 and 2,048 cases (the
frame-free reference, 0.867 / 0.395, GeoTransolver-512 0.279 / 0.098),
DrivAerML Surface at 435 cars and 200,000 cells (reference 0.0446), and
HiLift at 510 wings and 100,000 cells (reference 0.0404). Also recorded:
step time and peak memory.

**Bars (two-seed means, conditioned ÷ static reference per field).**
*Reference candidate*: at or below 0.97 on at least one dataset and at or
below 1.03 on every field of every dataset; it then goes to the full
board before becoming the reference. *Deleted*: above 1.05 on any field of
any dataset, or no dataset at or below 0.97 (a neutral change that costs
10 percent of the parameters is not kept). *Between* otherwise (a third
seed where a dataset sits in 1.03 to 1.05). Prediction: deleted (0.5),
reference candidate (0.3), between (0.2).

**GT-FPP, the baseline check (campaign gf rows 0-9, code_v11 = code_v10
plus the released GeoTransolver package with its FLARE++ backend).** Every
ratio in the book is against GeoTransolver with physics attention. The
released model now carries a FLARE++ backend (`attention_type=GALE_FPP`),
so the steel-man rule requires the stronger of the two as the baseline.
Lanes: DrivAerML Surface at 435 cars and 200,000 cells at both rates the
physics-attention reference used (3e-3 and 1e-3), HiLift 510 wings at width
512 and 100,000 cells, AirfRANS interior (GeoTransolver-volume), and OLBC
Poisson at 2,048 cases (width 512); two seeds each, otherwise the
physics-attention lanes' protocol. Reading: GeoTransolver-FLARE++ ÷
GeoTransolver-physics per dataset; where the FLARE++ backend is better by
more than 3 percent it replaces the physics-attention number as the
GeoTransolver baseline in the scoreboard (the book then quotes both), and
every ISLA ratio on that dataset is restated against it.

## 2026-09-29 — Correction and interim: the OLBC frame-free ISLA references of 2026-09-22 were plateaued runs on the code_ref snapshot (Poisson 512 validation loss flat at 0.219 from epoch 10, relative L2 0.867); the same configuration on the current snapshot scores 0.200 at 512 cases, ahead of GeoTransolver-512 (0.279) with no channel and no aggregation; every OLBC log-gap fraction is withdrawn pending the 2,048-case pair; and the first PROTO-COND reading (Poisson 512) is 2.0x worse than the static reference on both seeds {#sec-nb-olbc-reference-correction}

same-snapshot static reference on each dataset. On OLBC Poisson at 512
cases that reference, the plain frame-free configuration (condition types
and values as boundary scalars, signed distance and source as query
scalars, K = 0, no extension, no channel, no aggregation) on code_v11
scores **0.2004** (0.1996 / 0.2011, two seeds). The book's reference for
this configuration was 0.867, from the 2026-09-22 OLBC campaign on the
code_ref snapshot (@sec-nb-olbc-interim, @sec-nb-olbc-mech-verdict). The two runs are the same
recipe, dataset, split, rate, epochs and readout; they differ in the
snapshot. The old lanes' validation loss went 0.281 at epoch 1, 0.219 by
epoch 10, and 0.219 at epoch 500: a plateau from the first tenth of
training. The new lane's went 0.245, 0.029 at epoch 10, 0.019 at epoch
500. The old elasticity frame-free reference shows the same shape (0.178
from epoch 20 on, relative L2 0.90 to 1.01 on the four fields), and the
old 2,048-case Poisson reference plateaued at 0.056 (0.395). Only the
8,448-case old reference kept improving (0.011).

**What this means for the OLBC chapter.** Every "fraction of the log-gap
recovered" quoted for the extension, the per-type channels and the
aggregation on OLBC used the plateaued 0.867 / 0.395 as the base, so those
fractions measure distance from a failed run and are withdrawn. Read
against the current reference at 512 cases the arms are: the six-field
inverse-square extension on code_v7 **hurts** (0.299 against 0.200); the
three per-type distances are neutral (0.202); the three harmonic measures
are neutral (0.207); the aggregation with the distances **pays** (0.164,
0.82 of the reference) and with the harmonic measures 0.177. The reference
alone leads GeoTransolver-512 (0.279) by 1.39x at 512 cases. The 2,048
pair (pc rows 4-5, epoch 176 of 500) decides whether the 6% harmonic edge
and the 1.58x combined lead survive against a healthy reference; the
chapter is restated in one pass when it lands. What caused the code_ref
plateau on the K = 0 path is not measured; the snapshot differed in the
model API, the interior-geometry handling and the K = 0 geometry basis,
and the plateau signature (validation loss flat at a mean-field value from
epoch 10) is the one the routing-collapse study documented, so that is the

## 2026-09-29 — Verdict, LOCAL-AGG-STENCIL (AirfRANS, fixed query draw, two seeds): the aggregation hurts more, not less, when every airfoil keeps one draw (aggregation ÷ control 1.26 / 1.20 / 1.34 against 1.13 / 1.17 / 1.22 under resampling); the resampled-stencil hypothesis is refuted, and fixing the draw costs the reference itself 28% on pressure {#sec-nb-local-agg-stencil-verdict}

**Setting.** The stencil diagnostic (@sec-nb-local-agg-stencil-prereg) asked
whether the local aggregation's 13 to 22% loss on the AirfRANS interior
came from the 100,000 queries being redrawn every epoch, so that the 32
nearest neighbours of a physical point changed from visit to visit. A
recipe reader held each airfoil's draw fixed for the whole run; the
aggregation and a no-aggregation control both trained on it.

**What we saw (200 test airfoils, relative L2 on pressure / velocity /
eddy viscosity, two-seed means).** Fixed-draw control 0.0421 / 0.0174 /
0.0467; fixed-draw aggregation 0.0529 / 0.0209 / 0.0627; aggregation ÷
control **1.26 / 1.20 / 1.34** (seed 42: 1.34 / 1.29 / 1.56; seed 43: 1.18
/ 1.12 / 1.16). The same ratio under the resampled datapipe was 1.13 /
1.17 / 1.22. Fixing the draw costs the control 1.28 / 1.08 / 1.45 against
the resampled reference (0.0328 / 0.0161 / 0.0323): the per-epoch redraw is
a large augmentation on this dataset.

**Verdict.** *Refuted* (above 1.10 on every field). The aggregation's loss
on a resampled point cloud is not the moving stencil; with the stencil
frozen the loss grows. What remains as a mechanism candidate is the
geometry variation itself: on the fixed OLBC meshes the pooled
neighbourhood statistics are a stable function of position across every
sample, on AirfRANS each airfoil's neighbourhoods are different physical
configurations, and a k-nearest pool learned on one family does not
transfer to another. That reading is consistent with Tensile2d
(@sec-nb-universal-agg-t2d-interim), where geometry varies per case and
the aggregation also hurts. **Under the universalization rule the
Gaussian aggregation is deleted**; the LOCAL-LPR arms on AirfRANS, whose
premise was draw consistency, lose that premise and are read only as a
record when they land. The deletion follows the lug and DrivAerML Volume

results/local_agg_2026-09-27.json (stencil).

## 2026-09-29 — Mechanism, PROTO-COND: on the fixed Poisson mesh the sample-conditioned prototypes collapse onto one direction (pairwise cosine 0.92 / 0.93, effective rank 22 to 24 of 256, against 0.04 to 0.05 and 156 to 170 for the static seeds), so every query spreads its weight over 200 to 250 slices and the routing stops carrying the boundary data (same-node divergence across samples 0.07 bits against 0.25 to 0.34 static); on DrivAerML the collapse is confined to the early blocks and the later blocks recover, matching the neutral score {#sec-nb-proto-cond-mechanism}

**Setting.** The sample-conditioned prototypes (@sec-nb-proto-cond-prereg) replace the 256 learned routing seeds of each slice block by
seeds plus an attention-weighted average of the block's token states, one prototype matrix per sample. They score 2.0x worse than the
static reference on the OLBC Poisson set at 512 cases on both seeds (@sec-nb-olbc-reference-correction) and are neutral on DrivAerML
Surface (@sec-nb-proto-cond-dr-interim). Before the option is removed under the universalization rule, the failure is measured rather
than asserted, on the trained checkpoints (code_v11, float32, eval mode, the first 32 held-out samples, all 12 slice blocks; Poisson at
every node of the fixed mesh, 17,718 tokens; DrivAerML at 200,000 cells). Routing weights are the softmax over slices per token after
the geometric bias, the block's actual mixing weights.

**What we saw (mean over the 12 blocks; both Poisson seeds agree).**

| quantity | Poisson conditioned (seed 42 / 43) | Poisson static (42 / 43) | DrivAerML conditioned | DrivAerML static |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prototype displacement from the seeds, Frobenius, relative | 17.7 / 17.8 | 0 | 7.9 | 0 |
| mean pairwise cosine among the 256 prototypes | 0.923 / 0.931 | 0.050 / 0.042 | 0.773 | 0.082 |
| effective rank of the prototype matrix | 24 / 22 | 156 / 170 | 79 | 166 |
| per-token effective number of slices, exp of the routing entropy | 204 / 203 | 80 / 106 | 152 | 82 |
| mean top-slice weight per token | 0.045 / 0.043 | 0.134 / 0.093 | 0.110 | 0.183 |
| same node, different boundary data: Jensen-Shannon divergence of the routing [bits] | 0.078 / 0.073 | 0.337 / 0.248 | not defined (meshes differ) | |

: PROTO-COND mechanism diagnostic. The seeds the conditioned runs learned are themselves spread (pairwise cosine 0.013 to 0.017, effective rank 193 to 197); the collapse is in the synthesized prototypes. Data: results/proto_cond_diag_2026-09-29.json (runs pc_poisson_{cond,ref}_n512_seed42/43, pc_dr_{cond,ref}_seed42). {#tbl-proto-cond-mechanism}

**Reading.** The option is neither a no-op nor a fragmentation of the routing. On Poisson the attended value term dominates the seed
(the prototypes sit 14 to 19 seed-norms away from the seeds), and because that term is an attention-weighted average of the same token
cloud for every seed, all 256 prototypes point nearly the same way. Cosine routing against near-identical prototypes gives
near-identical logits for every slice, so each query spreads its weight over 200 to 250 of the 256 slices where the static model uses
80 to 105 with a top weight two to three times larger. **The slice mechanism degenerates toward one mean-field pool in most blocks, and
the routing of a given node barely responds to the boundary data (0.07 bits against 0.25 to 0.34 for the static model): the routing
carries less sample information, not more.** Per block, the collapse holds in every block (cosine 0.76 to 0.99); the routing sharpens
only in blocks 4 to 6 and 8. On DrivAerML the same collapse occurs in the early blocks (cosine 0.995, effective rank 10 in the first)
and relaxes with depth (cosine 0.56 to 0.75, effective rank 128 to 161 in the last four), and the middle blocks reach static-like
sharpness, which is consistent with the neutral score there. Why the two datasets differ is inferred, not measured: 200,000 surface
tokens with a global condition vector and varied geometry give the key and value projections enough variation for different seeds to
attend to different regions, whereas on the fixed square with weak per-token geometric variation every seed attends to essentially the
same mixture. **Consequence.** The preregistered deletion clause (worse than 1.05 on any field of any dataset) is met on Poisson with
the mechanism now measured; the option is removed when the AirfRANS and Poisson 2,048 pairs complete the record (the 510-wing pair
completes it later and cannot change the verdict).

## 2026-09-29 — Interim, PROTO-COND on the AirfRANS interior (800 airfoils, 100,000 queries, two seeds): the conditioned prototypes PAY 18% on pressure and eddy viscosity (0.82 / 0.98 / 0.82, both seeds on pressure), taking ISLA's pressure from 0.84 of GeoTransolver-volume to parity; with the 2.0x loss on the fixed Poisson mesh and the measured collapse mechanism, the option is dataset-dependent as built, and a collapse-proof form is preregistered as PROTO-COND-2 {#sec-nb-proto-cond-airfrans-interim}

**Setting.** Sample-conditioned slice prototypes (@sec-nb-proto-cond-prereg) are 2.0x worse than the static reference on OLBC Poisson
at 512 cases and neutral on DrivAerML Surface; @sec-nb-proto-cond-mechanism measured why: on the fixed mesh the attention-weighted
value term is the same for every seed and swamps it, so the 256 prototypes collapse onto one direction and the routing degenerates
toward one pool. The AirfRANS interior pair (pc_af_{ref,cond}, code_v11, same snapshot, the provided stored-field geometry, rate 5e-4,
500 epochs) is the third dataset.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 over the 200 test airfoils at 100,000 queries; ratio conditioned ÷ static on seed means, per seed
in parentheses):

| field | static reference | conditioned | ratio | GeoTransolver-volume | GeoTransolver-volume ÷ static | ÷ conditioned |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| pressure | 0.0331 (0.0330 / 0.0332) | 0.0270 (0.0269 / 0.0271) | 0.82 (0.82 / 0.82) | 0.0277 | 0.84 | 1.03 |
| velocity | 0.0161 | 0.0158 | 0.98 (0.91 / 1.05) | 0.0379 | 2.35 | 2.39 |
| eddy viscosity | 0.0347 (0.0337 / 0.0357) | 0.0285 (0.0263 / 0.0307) | 0.82 (0.78 / 0.86) | 0.0293 | 0.85 | 1.03 |

: PROTO-COND on the AirfRANS interior. Data: results/proto_cond_2026-09-29.json; GeoTransolver-volume from results/airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json. {#tbl-proto-cond-airfrans}

**Reading.** This is the first option in the program that closes the AirfRANS pressure deficit with an input that is PDE data only (the
token states themselves), where the earlier remedies either broke the input rules (dataset axes, @sec-pose-prior) or hurt
(aggregation, @sec-nb-local-agg-airfrans-verdict). The pressure gain is identical on both seeds; eddy viscosity gains on both; velocity
is neutral. So the record of the option as built reads: pays 18% on AirfRANS, neutral on DrivAerML Surface, 2.0x worse on the fixed
Poisson mesh. **Under the one-model rule that is a dataset-dependent option and it is not adopted.** But the failure has a measured
mechanism that is a defect of the construction, not of the idea: the part of the synthesized prototype that is common to all 256 seeds
carries no routing information (cosine logits compare a token against the prototypes relative to one another) and is what collapses
the routing when it dominates. A form that cannot collapse is the next rung.

### Preregistration, PROTO-COND-2: centered, scale-bounded conditioned prototypes {#sec-nb-proto-cond-2-prereg}

**Design.** In every slice block, with seeds $S \in \mathbb{R}^{256 \times H}$ and the attended value term
$\Delta_k = \sum_i \mathrm{softmax}_i(S_k \cdot k(x_i)/\sqrt{H} + \log w_i)\, v(x_i)$ as in the first form, the prototypes become

$$P_k = S_k + \frac{g\,\mathrm{rms}(S)}{\mathrm{rms}(\tilde\Delta) + g\,\mathrm{rms}(S)} \, \tilde\Delta_k, \qquad \tilde\Delta_k = \Delta_k - \frac{1}{256}\sum_{k'} \Delta_{k'},$$

with one learned scalar gate $g$ per block initialized at 0.1 and $\mathrm{rms}$ the root-mean-square entry over the matrix (over the
seeds for $S$, over the sample's $256 \times H$ entries for $\tilde\Delta$). Centering removes the seed-independent component exactly,
so a token cloud whose attention is the same for every seed changes nothing. The factor is a smooth bound, not a normalization: a
small centered term passes through unchanged (the factor tends to one) and a large one saturates at a root-mean-square of
$g\,\mathrm{rms}(S)$, so the prototypes cannot collapse by displacement and a near-uniform attention (the fixed-mesh regime) is not
amplified into a full-magnitude perturbation. (The first draft of this entry normalized rather than bounded; that form would have
turned roundoff in the identical-attention case into a perturbation of the full bound, and was replaced before any lane ran.) The construction is permutation-invariant and measure-aware as before, and its cost is the first form's.

**Predictions and falsifiers** (same-snapshot pairs on one new snapshot, two seeds each, float32; ratios PROTO-COND-2 ÷ static):
(1) OLBC Poisson 512: within 1.05 (collapse removed), with the diagnostic of @sec-nb-proto-cond-mechanism showing pairwise prototype
cosine below 0.3 and effective rank above 100 on the trained checkpoints; a ratio above 1.05 or a cosine above 0.5 refutes the
mechanism reading. (2) AirfRANS interior: pressure at or below 0.91 on both seeds (at least half the first form's gain survives the
centering); above 0.97 means the gain lived in the common component and the idea is refuted as a routing effect. (3) DrivAerML Surface
435 at 200,000 cells: within 1.03 on pressure and wall shear. (4) OLBC Poisson 2,048: within 1.05. **Adoption rule:** PROTO-COND-2
becomes part of the reference configuration only if it is neutral or better on all four (and the 510-wing pair, launched with them,
when it lands); otherwise it is removed together with the first form, and the AirfRANS gain is recorded as a lead for a future
mechanism, not as an option.

## 2026-09-29 — Verdict, LOCAL-LPR on the AirfRANS interior (two seeds): polynomial-reproducing stencil weights hurt like the Gaussian weights (1.11 / 1.19 / 1.94 of the reference on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity against 1.13 / 1.17 / 1.22), and the finite-difference gradient channels are 4.4 to 6.2x worse; refuted on both datasets, both forms are removed with the aggregation {#sec-nb-local-lpr-verdict}

**Setting.** @sec-nb-local-lpr-prereg borrowed two ideas from the meshfree exterior-calculus paper for ISLA's local relational
aggregation (32 nearest tokens, radius 0.05): weights from a weighted least-squares affine fit that reproduce constants and linear
functions exactly (generalized moving least squares, `local_weights="lpr"`), and finite-difference channels that carry the fitted
gradient of the token state projected on the boundary normal and the global directions (`local_gradient=True`). The hypothesis was that
the Gaussian aggregation's AirfRANS loss (13 to 22%) came from weights that do not reproduce even a constant field on an irregular
resampled stencil, so consistent weights would remove it. The Poisson 512 check had already read as a regression (lpr ÷ Gaussian 1.09).
Lanes lw_af_provided_local05_lpr and lw_af_provided_local05_lpr_grad (code_v10) against the provided-geometry reference pair
sg_af_provided (the K = 0 path is unchanged between those snapshots) and the Gaussian arm la_af_provided_local05.

**What we saw** (float32 relative L2 over the 200 test airfoils at 100,000 queries, seed means; ratio arm ÷ reference, per seed in
parentheses):

| arm | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| reference (no aggregation) | 0.0328 | 0.0161 | 0.0323 |
| Gaussian weights | 1.13 (1.13 / 1.13) | 1.17 (1.20 / 1.13) | 1.22 (1.37 / 1.08) |
| polynomial-reproducing weights | 1.11 (1.12 / 1.09) | 1.19 (1.18 / 1.20) | 1.94 (1.96 / 1.92) |
| polynomial-reproducing weights + gradient channels | 6.03 (5.47 / 6.58) | 4.38 (4.35 / 4.41) | 6.23 (6.73 / 5.78) |

: LOCAL-LPR on the AirfRANS interior. Data: results/local_lpr_2026-09-29.json. {#tbl-local-lpr-airfrans}

**Reading.** Consistent weights do not remove the loss: pressure and velocity are the same as with Gaussian weights within 2 to 4%, and
eddy viscosity is 1.9x worse on both seeds. The stencil-consistency hypothesis is refuted for the second time (the fixed-draw test,
@sec-nb-local-agg-stencil-verdict, had already shown the loss is not the resampling). The gradient channels are a training failure of a
mild kind: no NaN, but the training loss settles 10x above the reference's (0.0016 against 0.00018 at epoch 500) and the validation
loss 2x above, so the model with the projected finite-difference gradients in its token states fits the training airfoils far worse;
the mechanism is not separately measured. **Verdict: refuted on both datasets (Poisson 512 regression 1.09, AirfRANS 1.11 / 1.19 /
1.94 and 4.4 to 6.2x).** Under the universalization rule both forms leave the model together with the Gaussian aggregation they were
meant to repair: `local_weights`, `local_gradient`, and the aggregation itself (`local_rho`, `local_k`) are removed once the last
record lanes (lug and DrivAerML Volume universalization pairs) are scored, and the source stays in the repository history.

## 2026-09-29 — Preregistration, EXACT-SDF: the interior token's wall distance and direction from the exact point-to-triangle signed distance of the boundary mesh (physicsnemo.mesh.spatial.sdf) against the nearest-sample form the model uses today {#sec-nb-exact-sdf-prereg}

**Setting.** In interior mode every prediction point carries a wall distance and a wall direction computed inside ISLA from the
boundary sample: the distance to the nearest boundary cell centroid, signed by that cell's normal, and the unit direction from the
centroid to the point. This overestimates the true wall distance by up to a sample spacing and tilts the direction by the same order;
@sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict measured the cost of this geometry against a dataset's stored signed-distance field at 14 to 27% on
interior velocity. The library has the exact quantity: `signed_distance_field` (Warp point-to-triangle queries with pseudo-normal
signing) from the same boundary meshes the mesh-native forward now receives with their cells. Today's audit
(@sec-nb-olbc-ref-lanes is the API pass; the audit itself found the nearest-neighbour kernel and this) asked whether ISLA should use it.
Peter's ruling: a preregistered comparison, not a switch.

**Design.** A temporary constructor option `wall_geometry`, `"sampled"` (the form above, the reference) or `"exact"` (per query, the
exact signed distance to the nearest triangle of any boundary mesh and the unit direction from the closest surface point; distance
and direction enter the query embedding exactly as today). The exact form needs a triangle 2-manifold boundary in three dimensions and
is not differentiable in the boundary positions (the sampled form is). Under the option rule one form survives the verdict.

**Predictions and falsifiers** (same-snapshot pairs, two seeds, float32 scoring at the protocol query counts):
(1) DrivAerML Volume, 435 cars, 200,000 cells, 100,000 queries: exact ÷ sampled at or below 0.90 on velocity (the field the stored SDF
helped most) and at or below 0.97 on pressure; above 1.03 on any field refutes. (2) AirfRANS interior (a 2-D polyline boundary): not
applicable to the exact form; the sampled form stays there by construction, so the option cannot be universal unless a 2-D exact
distance (point-to-segment) is added; if (1) passes, the 2-D form is implemented and tested on AirfRANS before adoption (bar: pressure
at or below 0.97, nothing above 1.03). (3) Cost: the Warp query per forward must stay under 10% of the step time at 200,000 x 100,000;
above that the form is an inference-only option at most. **Adoption rule:** the exact form becomes the only form if (1) and the 2-D
follow-up pass and (3) holds; otherwise it is removed and the sampled form stays, with the stored-SDF declared inputs as the
documented way to give the model exact wall geometry where a dataset has it.

## 2026-09-29 — Verdict, GT-FPP on the OLBC ladder: the FLARE++ backend replaces physics attention only on Poisson at 2,048 cases; it ties on elasticity at 512 and 2,048 (mean stress ratio 0.99 / 0.97), loses on Poisson at 512 and 8,448 (1.07 / 1.18) and fails to train on elasticity at 8,448 (4.6x worse, both seeds); chapter 10 takes the stronger backend per rung under the 3% rule {#sec-nb-gt-fpp-olbc-verdict}

**Setting.** GT-FPP is the steel-man check of @sec-nb-gt-fpp-interim: wherever GeoTransolver with the released FLARE++ attention
backend (input-conditioned dynamic routing, `attention_type=GALE_FPP`) beats GeoTransolver with physics attention by more than 3%
on a dataset's headline field, FLARE++ becomes the baseline there and every ISLA ratio on that dataset is restated. The Poisson
2,048 rung already fired (@sec-nb-gt-fpp-poisson-verdict) and Poisson 512 did not (@sec-nb-gt-fpp-poisson-512). This entry closes
the rest of the OLBC ladder: Poisson at 8,448 training cases and elasticity at 512 / 2,048 / 8,448, campaign gf rows 10 to 19.

**Instrument.** GeoTransolver width 512 in both backends, learning rate 1e-3, the OLBC protocol of chapter 10 (500 epochs at 512
and 2,048 cases, 120 epochs at 8,448 so that the step count matches), two seeds, float32 scoring on the 256 held-out cases. The
elasticity FLARE++ lanes read the `olbc_elasticity_gt` dataset file (the same fields without the stacked-scalar transform that
GeoTransolver cannot consume); the 512 and 2,048 rungs, which also used it, tie their physics-attention twins, so the file is not
a confound. The headline for elasticity is the mean of the three stress fields; displacement is reported beside it. Reducers
`results/gt_fpp_reduce_2026-09-29.py` (artifact `gt_fpp_2026-09-29.json`) and `results/olbc_ref_reduce_2026-09-29.py`
(artifact `olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json`, read by chapter 10) now apply the same rule: physics attention is the baseline unless
FLARE++ is better by more than 3% on the headline; a difference inside 3% is a tie and physics attention stays.

**What we saw** (FLARE++ ÷ physics attention on seed means; per seed in parentheses):

| rung | headline | FLARE++ ÷ physics | per seed | displacement | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Poisson 512 | $u$ | 1.07 | 1.04 / 1.10 | | physics attention stronger |
| Poisson 2,048 | $u$ | 0.77 | 0.78 / 0.75 | | FLARE++ replaces the baseline |
| Poisson 8,448 | $u$ | 1.18 | 1.25 / 1.11 | | physics attention stronger |
| elasticity 512 | mean stress | 0.99 | 0.98 / 1.00 | 1.05 | tie |
| elasticity 2,048 | mean stress | 0.97 | 0.99 / 0.96 | 1.05 | tie (inside 3%) |
| elasticity 8,448 | mean stress | 4.57 | 4.44 / 4.72 | 6.36 | physics attention stronger |

Absolute values: Poisson $u$ at 8,448 is 0.0289 (physics) against 0.0341 (FLARE++); elasticity stresses at 8,448 are 0.098 to
0.105 (physics) against 0.458 to 0.472 (FLARE++), displacement 0.050 against 0.318.

**The 8,448-case elasticity failure is a training failure, not a scoring one.** Both FLARE++ lanes completed their 120 epochs
and were scored at epoch 120, like their twins. Their validation loss ends at 0.0370 (seed 42; the last three epochs read 0.054,
0.040, 0.037, still falling slowly) against 0.00159 for physics attention at the same epoch, a 23x gap that matches the 4.4 to
6.4x gap in relative L2. No NaN appears in either log. The same backend at the same rate trained normally on the two smaller
elasticity rungs and on Poisson at 8,448, so the failure is specific to the largest elasticity rung; the mechanism is not
measured here, and the earlier observation that FLARE++ diverges at 3e-3 on DrivAerML (@sec-nb-gt-fpp-interim) is the only
related reading. FLARE++ is a released baseline and is not tuned further (@sec-nb-gt-fpp-interim).

**Why it matters.** The stronger GeoTransolver backend changes with the rung and the set, so no single backend is "the" baseline
on OLBC. Chapter 10 therefore quotes both backends at every rung and takes the stronger one for the headline ratio under the 3%
rule: FLARE++ at Poisson 2,048 only, physics attention everywhere else. With the current-snapshot ISLA references
(@sec-nb-olbc-ref-2048), the headline GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA ratios are 1.39 (Poisson 512), 1.13 (Poisson 2,048, FLARE++)
and 0.52 (Poisson 8,448, from the same artifact; the 8,448 reference pair gets its own reading when campaign pc closes), and
0.82 to 0.89 on elasticity at 2,048 (interim, one current-snapshot seed); the elasticity 8,448 reference pair is not scored yet.

**What is next.** GT-FPP has one open pair, GeoTransolver-512 with FLARE++ on the 510 HiLift wings at 100k cells
(`gf_hl_gt512_fpp_medium_c100k`, two seeds); the ledger row closes when it is scored. Nothing else in the program depends on it.

## 2026-09-29 — Interim, PROTO-COND-2 on three of four datasets: the centered, scale-bounded conditioned prototypes pay 0.86 / 0.78 on OLBC Poisson at 512 / 2,048 cases, are neutral on DrivAerML Surface (1.00 / 1.00), and keep about a quarter of the first form's AirfRANS gain (pressure 0.95 against 0.82; velocity 1.03, one seed 1.06); the wing pair decides adoption {#sec-nb-proto-cond-2-interim}

snapshot with same-snapshot static references (campaign pc2), two seeds, on OLBC Poisson 512 / 2,048, DrivAerML Surface 435 at
200,000 cells, the AirfRANS interior and HiLift 510 medium. The first reading, Poisson 512 at 0.86, is in
@sec-nb-proto-cond-2-poisson-512 with its mechanism check (no collapse in any of the 24 block-seed cells).

`proto_cond2_2026-09-29.json`):

| dataset | field | ratio | seed 42 | seed 43 | preregistered bar | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OLBC Poisson 512 | $u$ | 0.86 | 0.96 | 0.76 | within 1.05 | pays |
| OLBC Poisson 2,048 | $u$ | 0.78 | 0.90 | 0.66 | within 1.05 | pays |
| DrivAerML Surface 435 | pressure / wall shear | 1.00 / 1.00 | 1.01 / 1.00 | 0.99 / 0.99 | within 1.03 | neutral |
| AirfRANS interior | pressure | 0.95 | 0.94 | 0.97 | at or below 0.91 on both seeds | between |
| AirfRANS interior | velocity / eddy viscosity | 1.03 / 0.95 | 0.99 / 0.94 | 1.06 / 0.96 | | |

0.0434; AirfRANS pressure 0.0331 against 0.0316, velocity 0.0162 against 0.0166.

**The references are healthy and the seed spread is real.** Every pair's validation loss is still at or within 1% of its
minimum at the last epoch (no plateaued run of the kind that spoiled the 2026-09-22 references, @sec-nb-olbc-reference-correction).
The Poisson gain is carried unevenly by the seeds: at 2,048 cases the seed-43 pair ends with validation loss 0.00092 against

## 2026-09-29 — Status, deflection at 200,000 cells: the first ISLA twin (192 wide, linear routing) fell to the mean-field plateau on both seeds (validation loss 0.0088 / 0.0101 at epoch 26, then 0.143 / 0.157 from epoch 76 to 500) and is not an arm; the reference-configuration twin is healthy at epoch 367 (0.0022 / 0.0020, level with GeoTransolver's 0.0022) and becomes the ISLA arm of the 200k sealed test {#sec-nb-p200k-deflection-plateau}

**Setting.** The deflection split trains on the 144 milder HiLift geometries and tests on 360 sealed high-deflection cases
(@sec-nb-deflection-prereg). At 10,000 cells the sealed test was falsified: ISLA 1.16x unit-direction GeoTransolver on
pressure, both degrading 1.23 to 1.25x across the geometry boundary (@sec-nb-deflection-verdict). P200K-FLEET re-runs the
split at the 200,000-cell protocol (group defl: `p200k_hl_isla_deflection`, `p200k_hl_gt_unit_deflection`, two seeds, lr 1e-3,
launched 2026-09-19 before cosine routing and the 384-wide reference configuration were adopted). REF-BOARD runs the same split
under the reference configuration (`rb_hl_isla_deflection`, rows 20-21: 384 wide, cosine routing, lr 5e-4).

**What we saw.** The four group-defl lanes trained to 500 epochs and were scored on the 180-case validation list. GeoTransolver
is healthy: validation loss 0.00222 / 0.00216 at 500, float32 pressure relative L2 0.0262 / 0.0246. The two ISLA lanes are not:
validation loss reaches 0.0088 (seed 42) and 0.0101 (seed 43) at epoch 26, rises to 0.095 / 0.148 by epoch 51 and 0.164 / 0.158
by epoch 76, and stays flat at 0.143 / 0.157 to epoch 500 with the training loss at the same value (0.1436); no NaN. Float32
pressure relative L2 on validation is 0.688 / 0.694, the mean-field level. This is the loss signature of the routing collapse
measured in ROUTING-SAT (@sec-nb-routingsat-verdict): one active slice per block, output near the field mean. It occurred under
linear routing at lr 1e-3 and 192 width, the setting ROUTE-NORM found collapse-prone and replaced with cosine routing
(@sec-nb-routenorm-p200k-verdict); it was not re-run because the reference configuration supersedes that setting.

**The reference-configuration twin is healthy.** `rb_hl_isla_deflection` seeds 42 / 43 are at epoch 367 of 500 with validation
loss 0.00224 / 0.00196 at epoch 351, still descending slowly and level with GeoTransolver's final 0.00222 / 0.00216 on the same
list (the 10k arms had ISLA 1.18x GeoTransolver on validation pressure). It becomes the ISLA arm of the 200k sealed test.

**What was done.** The sealed-test evaluator for the 200k twin (`highlift/hl_defl_test_eval_p200k_aga.sbatch`, the 10k script
with the p200k / rb lanes, their code snapshots and 200,000 cells) was submitted for the GeoTransolver pair (job 933538 tasks 2-3
running); its ISLA tasks for the plateaued lanes were cancelled. The reference-configuration pair runs once both seeds report
"Training completed" (tasks 4-5). The 200k reduction (`results/deflection_p200k_reduce_2026-09-29.py`) takes the rb lanes as the
ISLA arm, records the plateaued lanes under "superseded", and applies the 10k bars unchanged: carried at or below 0.7x
GeoTransolver on sealed pressure with $d \le 4$; falsified at or above 0.9x. The entry that reads it closes both the P200K-FLEET
deflection row and the REF-BOARD deflection twin.

whole ladder (campaign pc, @sec-nb-olbc-ref-lanes): Poisson at 512 / 2,048 / 8,448 training cases and elasticity at
512 / 2,048 / 8,448, two seeds each, with the interior-geometry arms (distances = the inverse-square extension's wall distance;
per-type harmonic measures) at 512 and 2,048 on the same snapshot. GeoTransolver-512 is read in both backends and the headline
takes the stronger under the 3% rule (@sec-nb-gt-fpp-olbc-verdict). Protocol as chapter 10: equal optimizer steps (500 epochs

`olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json`, which chapter 10 reads.

**Every reference is healthy.** Each pair's validation loss is at its minimum at the last logged epoch (Poisson 8,448:
0.00144 / 0.00074 at epoch 120; elasticity 8,448: 0.00250 / 0.00221; elasticity 2,048 within 0.2% of its minimum). None shows
the flat-from-epoch-10 trace of the withdrawn runs.

**What we saw** (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA, stronger backend; seed means; ISLA per seed in parentheses):

| set, cases | ISLA | GeoTransolver-512 (backend) | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA |
|---|---|---|---|

| Poisson 2,048 | 0.0667 (0.0674 / 0.0661) | 0.0755 (FLARE++) | 1.13 |
| Poisson 8,448 | 0.0558 (0.0730 / 0.0386) | 0.0289 (physics; GeoTransolver-256 0.0287) | 0.52 (per seed 0.37 / 0.80) |

**Poisson crosses over between 2,048 and 8,448 cases.** ISLA is the more data-efficient model on the fixed-mesh Poisson set

## 2026-09-29 — Verdict, EXACT-SDF: the exact point-to-triangle wall distance and direction change nothing on DrivAerML Volume (exact ÷ sampled 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.99 on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity, per seed within 0.97 to 1.01); the sampled nearest-boundary form stays as the only form and the exact option is removed {#sec-nb-exact-sdf-verdict}

**Setting.** @sec-nb-exact-sdf-prereg asked whether the interior token's wall distance and direction should come from the exact
signed distance of the boundary mesh (`physicsnemo.mesh.spatial.sdf`, Warp point-to-triangle queries) instead of the nearest
boundary sample, after INTERNAL-GEOMETRY had measured the sampled form 14 to 27% behind a dataset's stored signed-distance field
on interior velocity (@sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict). Bars: exact ÷ sampled at or below 0.90 on velocity and 0.97 on pressure
adopts (pending a 2-D form on AirfRANS); above 1.03 on any field refutes; otherwise the sampled form stays.

**Instrument.** DrivAerML Volume, 435 cars, 200,000 boundary cells and 100,000 interior queries, the reference configuration at
lr 5e-4, two seeds per arm, code_v13 (the mesh-native API) with recipe_v5, campaign ex; float32 scoring on the held-out cars.
All four lanes trained to 500 epochs with validation loss within 2% of its minimum at the end (no plateau). Reducer
`results/exact_sdf_reduce_2026-09-29.py`, artifact `exact_sdf_2026-09-29.json`.

**What we saw.** Pressure 0.0410 (sampled) against 0.0412 (exact), velocity 0.0655 against 0.0656, eddy viscosity 0.0887 against
0.0878: ratios 1.004 / 1.002 / 0.990, per seed 1.005 / 1.003, 0.999 / 1.006 and 0.974 / 1.007. Neither bar is met and nothing is
refuted: **the exact wall geometry is indistinguishable from the sampled one at 200,000 boundary cells.**

**Why it matters.** The 14 to 27% velocity gap to the stored field is therefore not a distance-accuracy problem at this
resolution: with 200,000 samples the nearest-sample distance and the exact distance agree to well under the model's sensitivity,
so the stored field's advantage lies elsewhere (it is a smooth volumetric field the mesh pipeline computed once with the full
surface, and it enters as a declared input rather than through the routing geometry). Under the option rule one form survives:
the sampled form, which is differentiable in the boundary positions and needs no Warp dependency. The `wall_geometry` option and
the exact path are removed from the model and its tests; the 2-D follow-up on AirfRANS is dropped with it.

## 2026-09-30 — Ruling (Peter) and program turn: fixed-mesh work is deprioritized because real CAE varies geometry and fixed meshes do not exercise ISLA's discretization independence; rejected machinery is deleted on the verdict; the PROTO-COND-2 adoption rule stands as written; one equal-epoch Poisson 8,448 pair runs as the last fixed-mesh lane; the next program is the wing deficit's mechanism {#sec-nb-ruling-fixed-mesh-2026-09-30}

**Setting.** Five decisions were open after the same-snapshot OLBC ladder closed (@sec-nb-olbc-ref-ladder-verdict): whether to
delete the refuted harmonic and distance channels, how to read the PROTO-COND-2 adoption rule, what to do about the Poisson
8,448 seed spread, which program comes next, and the two known failing tests. Peter ruled on all five.

**The rulings.**

1. **Delete the machinery of rejected experiments, always.** The per-type harmonic measures (`src/harmonic.py`,
   `src/precompute_harmonic.py`, `HarmonicBoundaryMeasures`) and the inverse-square boundary-value extension
   (`BoundaryValueExtension`, the "distances" channel) are removed from the recipe with their tests: 720 lines, 8 tests. The
   recipe suite passes (333) except the one known failure being fixed separately. The `hm_measures` and `_ext` dataset variants
   were cluster-only and stay on the cluster as provenance of the closed lanes.
2. **The PROTO-COND-2 adoption rule as written governs**: neutral or better on every dataset, wings included. The AirfRANS
   pressure clause (at or below 0.91) was a mechanism reading and does not block adoption. If the HiLift 510 pair scores within
   1.03 on pressure, `slice_prototypes="centered"` becomes the reference default and the static form is deleted.
3. **The Poisson 8,448 seed spread** (ISLA 0.073 / 0.039, both lanes still descending under the equal-step budget) gets one
   equal-epoch pair: ISLA reference and GeoTransolver-512, both at 500 epochs (campaign pc rows 44 to 47, `*_n8448_e500_*`).
   Cheap, and not a priority: it is the last fixed-mesh lane.
4. **Fixed-mesh work is deprioritized, and further fixed-mesh programs are nixed.** Very few real CAE datasets share one mesh;
   geometry variation is the point of CAE, and discretization independence is one of ISLA's strengths, so a fixed-mesh problem
   neither matters much in practice nor exercises what ISLA does right. The OLBC sets stay in the book as the closed
   boundary-data stress test (chapter 10); no new lanes are launched on them beyond ruling 3. The solids gap read against
   GeoTransolver exists only on the fixed-mesh OLBC elasticity set: on the geometry-varying solids (lug, DeepJEB++, Tensile2d
   with the tensor head) ISLA is at parity or ahead, so there is no geometry-varying elasticity gap to study. The program's open
   question is therefore **the wing deficit's mechanism**: 10% at 210 wings, 31% on the fixed-angle rung, closing with data
   (@sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict), where the per-case anatomy located nothing. The first instrument is a no-training surface
   anatomy (excess error by high-lift element and by curvature bin, preregistered in @sec-nb-wing-anatomy-surface).
5. **Fix the two known failing tests now** (the aarch64-only GLOBE subsample-measure test; the recipe's missing
   degenerate-cell warning) and then decide whether each fix rides an open upstream PR or a later one.

## 2026-09-30 — Verdict, WING-ANATOMY-SURFACE: ISLA's excess pressure error on the wings is uniform across curvature (every curvature bin within 0.10 of the whole-surface ratio, 1.21 / 1.02 at 210 wings and 1.47 / 1.42 on the fixed-angle rung, both seeds, both rungs), so H2 is refuted and the curvature axis reads H3; the five-wing element pilot puts the flap (1.37 / 1.30 at 210 wings) and the gap band (1.83 / 1.80 on the fixed-angle wing) over the bar, leaving H1 open on the flap and the coves {#sec-nb-wing-anatomy-surface}

**Setting.** On the HiLiftAeroML wings ISLA (reference configuration)
trails GeoTransolver-512 by 10% on surface pressure at 210 training wings
(0.0513 against 0.0461, @sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict) and GeoTransolver-256
by 31% on the fixed-angle rung (126 training geometries at one angle of
attack of 12 degrees, 18 validation geometries; ISLA 0.0300 against
0.0207 at GeoTransolver's better rate 3e-3, @sec-nb-fleet-single-aoa-verdict),
while on the DrivAerML Surface task the two are at parity car by car
(Spearman 0.91, @sec-nb-hl35-percase addendum). The per-case anatomy
found no location: the deficit is spread over every angle of attack
(@sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict). The next resolution is spatial: where on the
wing surface does ISLA's excess pressure error sit? Nothing is trained; the
existing checkpoints are re-scored with their per-cell predictions kept.

**Hypotheses (fixed before computing).** H1, *local resolution*: the
excess concentrates on the thin high-lift elements (slat, flap) and in the
gaps between elements, where 200,000 sampled cells leave few cells per
element and per cove. H2, *curvature*: the excess concentrates in
high-curvature regions (leading and trailing edges) regardless of element.
H3, *global*: the excess is spatially uniform, a scale or normalization
deficit rather than a local one.

**Instrument.** The float32 fleet scorer (`infer.py`, validation split,
200,000 cells per case) run once more with `+save_predictions=true` on
the four lanes of each rung, so every sampled cell carries its predicted
and true pressure, its triangle (area) and its normal. Lanes and
checkpoints: the 210-wing rung `ref_isla_r1_hl210_seed{42,43}`
(`code_ref`) against `ref_gt_w512_hl210_seed{42,43}` (`code_ref`, 512
wide, 3e-3), 180 validation wings; the fixed-angle rung
`p200k_hl_isla_single_aoa_12_seed{42,43}` (`code_lean`, 1e-3) against
`p200k_hl_gt_unit_single_aoa_12_lr3e3_seed{42,43}` (`code_lean`, 256
wide, 3e-3; no 512-wide lane exists on this rung), 18 validation wings;
all epoch-500 checkpoints, `recipe_globin`. Prediction job 938092; analysis
script `$T/highlift/wing_anatomy_surface.py`.

*Surface classes.* Curvature: the dataset's boundary meshes hold 290
million triangles per wing and the 200,000-cell sample is a disconnected
set of triangles, so curvature is measured on the sample itself as the
normal turning rate $\kappa_i \equiv \operatorname{median}_j \lVert n_i -
n_j \rVert / \lVert x_i - x_j \rVert$ over the 16 nearest sampled
neighbours (the prediction geometry is in units of $L_\text{ref}$ = 275.8
in, the mean aerodynamic chord, so $\kappa$ is in 1/$L_\text{ref}$ and is
also written in 1/in; a curvature magnitude that saturates for radii below
the mean sample spacing of 0.013 $L_\text{ref}$, 3.6 in, but still ranks
those cells at the top). Bins by area-weighted quantiles of $\kappa$ pooled over the
rung's validation samples: high curvature = the 10% of surface area with
the largest $\kappa$, medium = the next 40%, low = the remaining 50%.
Element: the dataset has no per-cell element or patch field, and only 41
of the 1,800 case directories carry an STL geometry file (4 of the 180
validation wings on the 210-wing rung, 1 of the 18 on the fixed-angle
rung). Where it exists, the STL is one connected component (slat tracks
and flap-track fairings weld the elements), so the element label comes
from a span-station segmentation (4-inch bins; the largest connected
piece per bin is the main wing and body, a smaller piece is slat if the
nearest main triangles lie behind it and flap if ahead, and a piece
farther than 0.25 $L_\text{ref}$ from the main wing, the tail and
nacelle, is excluded) and is transferred to the sampled cells by nearest
STL triangle after the CenterMesh translation is recovered by three
nearest-neighbour iterations; the gap band is every cell within 0.02
$L_\text{ref}$ ($L_\text{ref}$ = 275.8 in, the mean aerodynamic chord) of a
triangle of another element. The element readout is therefore a pilot on
five wings, stated as such, and it under-segments a slat whose cove is
sealed in the STL.

*Readout.* Per class and case, the area-weighted RMS pressure error of
the class divided by the area-weighted standard deviation of the case's
true pressure over the whole surface (one denominator per case, so
classes of a case are on one footing and the whole-surface value
reproduces the ranking of the relative L2), averaged over the validation
cases; then the ratio ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver per seed pair (42 with 42, 43
with 43). The whole-surface ratio is the reference. **Bar: a class ratio
at least 0.15 above the whole-surface ratio on both seed pairs = that
class carries the excess** (H1 if slat, flap or the gap band clear it; H2
if the high-curvature bin clears it on both rungs; H3 if no class clears
it and every class ratio is within 0.15 of the whole-surface value). Also
recorded, not part of the bar: each model's error share per class (the
fraction of its total area-weighted squared error in the class) against
the class's area share. Prediction: H2 or H3 (0.4 each); H1 is the
program's prior from the resolution argument but the fixed-angle
deficit did not move between 10,000 and 200,000 cells
(@sec-nb-fleet-single-aoa-verdict), which argues against a resolution
mechanism.

**What we saw (curvature, every validation wing; artifact
`results/wing_anatomy_surface_2026-09-30.json`, reducer and figure
`results/wing_anatomy_surface_2026-09-30.{py,png}`; prediction job 938092,
analysis job 941525, after two defective analysis passes: a float32
nearest-neighbour search that lost the neighbour distances, and an
alignment that matched $L_\text{ref}$-unit coordinates to an inch-unit
STL).** The re-scoring reproduces the standings to the fourth digit
(210 wings: ISLA 0.0550 / 0.0476, GeoTransolver-512 0.0453 / 0.0468;
fixed angle: ISLA 0.0302 / 0.0298, GeoTransolver-256 0.0206 / 0.0208),
and the whole-surface ratio of the class metric reproduces their ratio:
ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver **1.21 / 1.02** at 210 wings (seeds 42 / 43) and
**1.47 / 1.42** on the fixed-angle rung. The mean sample spacing is 3.6
in; the curvature bin edges are 0.0057 and 0.68 per inch at 210 wings
(radii 177 in and 1.5 in), 0.0060 and 0.44 per inch on the fixed-angle
rung. Class ratios, seeds 42 / 43, with the excess over the whole-surface
ratio in parentheses:

| class (share of area) | 210 wings, ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver-512 | fixed angle, ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver-256 |
|---|---|---|
| whole surface | 1.21 / 1.02 | 1.47 / 1.42 |
| high curvature (10%) | 1.22 / 1.10 (+0.01 / +0.08) | 1.44 / 1.38 (−0.02 / −0.04) |
| medium curvature (40%) | 1.20 / 1.00 (0.00 / −0.02) | 1.49 / 1.47 (+0.02 / +0.05) |
| low curvature (50%) | 1.22 / 1.07 (+0.01 / +0.06) | 1.45 / 1.33 (−0.02 / −0.09) |

The largest curvature-bin excess is +0.08 (high curvature, 210 wings, seed 43); no curvature class comes closer than 0.07 to the 0.15 bar on either rung. The
error is not on the edges for either model: at 210 wings the
high-curvature tenth of the surface carries 5 to 6% of each model's
squared error (ISLA 0.054 / 0.059, GeoTransolver 0.054 / 0.056), the
medium bin 68 to 70% on 40% of the area, and the shares of the two
architectures agree to within 0.01 in every bin; on the fixed-angle
rung the high-curvature tenth carries 17 to 18% for both.

**What we saw (elements, pilot on the five wings with an STL).** The
alignment residual is 0.56 to 0.64 in (median distance from a sampled
cell to its nearest STL triangle centroid, against a 3.6-in sample
spacing), and the element labels cover 0.7 to 3.5% of the sampled area
as slat, 3.3 to 5.6% as flap and 3.0 to 5.0% as gap band, so the
segmentation under-reads the slat (the STL slat area is 2.7% on LHC001
and 0.8% on LHC002, whose slat cove is sealed in the STL). On the four
210-wing pilot wings (LHC001 at 16 degrees, LHC002 at 6 and 18, LHC004
at 6) the flap reads **1.37 / 1.30** (+0.16 / +0.28 over the pilot's
whole-surface 1.21 / 1.02) and clears the bar; the gap band 1.27 / 1.19
(+0.06 / +0.18, one seed); the slat 1.08 / 0.82 (−0.13 / −0.20, ISLA
better on one seed); the main wing and body 1.17 / 0.98. On the one
fixed-angle pilot wing (LHC002 at 12 degrees) the gap band reads
**1.83 / 1.80** (+0.40 / +0.35) and clears the bar; the slat 1.61 / 1.41
(+0.18 / −0.03), the flap 1.48 / 1.29 (+0.05 / −0.15), the main wing and
body 1.38 / 1.43. The flap holds 8 to 11% of each model's squared error
on 5% of the area and the gap band 11 to 15% on 3 to 5%. The curvature
proxy against the STL's discrete mean curvature on these wings: Spearman
0.67 to 0.69 over the cells, but only 9 to 18% of the area the proxy
ranks in its top tenth is in the STL's top tenth, so the proxy ranks
curvature coarsely and the "high curvature" bin is the sample's rapidly
turning tenth, not a sharp leading-edge set.

**Reading.** **H2 is refuted on both rungs and both seeds**: the excess
does not sit on high-curvature regions; ISLA's ratio is the same on the
edges, on the flats and in between, to within 0.10, and both
architectures place their error on the same parts of the surface. On
the curvature axis the picture is **H3**: the excess is uniform, a
factor applied everywhere, which is the signature of a global deficit
(scale, normalization, or the whole-wing map) rather than a local
resolution failure. The element pilot leaves **H1 open on the flap and
the gaps**: the flap on four wings and the gap band on one clear the bar,
and the gap band is 0.06 to 0.40 above the whole-surface ratio on all
five wings and both seeds; the slat does not carry the excess anywhere.
Five wings with approximate labels are not a verdict, and the two
readings are consistent with one mechanism: the flap and the coves are
the regions whose pressure depends on the neighbouring element
(the slat wake over the main element, the main-element trailing edge
over the flap), a non-local dependence that a model with absolute
positions can index and a relative-frame model must route through the
slices; the flat remainder of the wing carries a uniform 2 to 47% excess
that no surface class explains. Nothing here varies an input, so it is a
location, not a mechanism.

**What is next.** (1) Element labels for every wing: the STL exists for
41 of 1,800 cases, so the label has to come from the boundary mesh
itself; a one-time preprocessing job that segments the 290-million-cell
vehicle mesh of each validation wing by span station (the same rule,
run on the full mesh, where slat and flap are separated by their coves
in nearly every station) and writes a per-cell element id into the
per-case `_cache`, which the reader then carries into the sample. With
that, the flap and gap-band bar is decided on 180 wings. (2) The
uniform component is the larger one on both rungs and is the
preregistration target for the next instrument: a per-case scale
diagnostic (the regression slope of ISLA's prediction on the truth,
area-weighted, per wing, against GeoTransolver's), which separates a
gain error from a shape error at zero training cost. (3) The
positional channel stays the candidate for the flap and cove excess:
the fixed-angle rung is where the relative frame has the least to do
(one angle, one freestream direction) and the deficit is largest, and
the gap band's 1.8 there is the largest class ratio in this study.

## 2026-09-30 — Verdict, P200K-FLEET HiLift ladder complete: at 200,000 cells GeoTransolver-256 at its better rate ÷ ISLA (earlier protocol) reads 0.73 / 0.88 / 0.69 at 35 / 210 / 510 wings and both 1,260-wing ISLA lanes fell to the mean-field plateau; the baselines' learning-curve exponents are 0.35 (GeoTransolver) and 0.32 (Transolver) over 35 to 1,260 wings against 0.49 for the reference configuration over 35 to 510, where it is at parity with Transolver (1.01) and 4% behind GeoTransolver-256 (0.96) {#sec-nb-p200k-hl-ladder-verdict}

**Setting.** The fleet that moves every evidence lane to the reporting
protocol (@sec-nb-proto200k-fleet-prereg) ran its HiLiftAeroML group
(`hl`) at 200,000 sampled cells per case, float32, two seeds, on eight
rungs: the random-split case ladder of 35, 210, 510 and 1,260 training
wings (a *rung* is one training-set size; all four validate on the same
180 held-out wings), the held-out-geometry rungs of 4 and 21 training
geometries at all their angles, the fixed-angle rung (126 geometries at
12 degrees, 18 validation wings) and the 35-wing rung trained under the
area-proportional sampling law. Three models: ISLA in the configuration
of 2026-09-19 (192 wide, linear routing, learning rate 1e-3; the *earlier
protocol* in the book's nomenclature, since superseded by the reference
configuration of 384 wide, cosine routing, 5e-4), unit-direction
GeoTransolver-256 at 1e-3 and at 3e-3 (each wing row takes its better
rate and says which), and Transolver-256 at 3e-3. The 1,260-wing rung and
the GeoTransolver 3e-3 controls on it were the last to score (today).
Earlier entries read the rungs as they landed (@sec-nb-p200k-wings-35,
@sec-nb-p200k-wings-geo4, @sec-nb-fleet-single-aoa-verdict,
@sec-nb-wing-rungs-210-verdict); this entry closes the group, states the
200,000-against-10,000-cell comparison the fleet preregistration
promised, and supplies the wing half of SCALE-LAW's case exponents
(@sec-nb-scalelaw-wing-rung4).

**Instrument.** Reducer `results/p200k_hl_ladder_2026-09-30.py`, artifact
`results/p200k_hl_ladder_2026-09-30.json`, figure
`results/p200k_hl_ladder_2026-09-30.png`; metrics under
`results/campaigns_2026-09-19/hl/metrics/<run>/<run>/metrics.jsonl`. The
readout is the area-weighted relative L2 of surface pressure on the
validation wings (the other four fields are in the artifact). Where a
scoring job was interrupted and restarted (the 35-wing files hold two
scoring blocks at epoch 500) one row per validation case is kept, the
last written. The *learning-curve exponent* is the least-squares slope of
log error on log training wings through the seed means (error
$\propto n^{-\alpha}$), with the per-seed slopes as the range; *local*
exponents are the same slope between adjacent rungs. A lane is excluded
when its train log shows the *mean-field plateau*: validation loss that
descends to about 0.01 and then jumps to 0.12 to 0.16 and stays flat with
the training loss at the same value, the routing-collapse signature of
ROUTING-SAT (@sec-nb-routingsat-verdict), confirmed by a scored pressure
error at the field-mean level (0.6 to 0.7). Every `hl` train log was
read for it today.

**Three ISLA lanes plateaued; one is excluded from SCALE-HL's record as
well.** `p200k_hl_isla_full_seed42` and `seed43` (1,260 wings) reached
validation loss 0.0225 and 0.0103 at epoch 25, jumped to 0.143 and 0.155
by epoch 50, and sat at 0.152 and 0.148 through epoch 499 with training
loss 0.154 and 0.151; their scored pressure errors are 0.691 and 0.695.
`p200k_hl_isla_medium_seed42` (510 wings) reached 0.0112 at epoch 50, rose
to 0.0245 at 75 and 0.153 at 100, and sat at 0.121 to epoch 499 (training
0.122); scored 0.594. This is the lane SCALE-HL already called "unreadable"
(ledger row SCALEHL; `results/scalehl_2026-09-26.json` carries it inside

at 1,260 wings is 1.12. Velocity and wall shear follow pressure on every

and 0.98).

**Beside the reference configuration.** Where REF-BOARD has the rung
(@sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict, @sec-nb-ref-hl510-verdict), the reference

(0.0550 / 0.0476) at 210 and 0.0404 (0.0405 / 0.0403) at 510: 3%, 7% and

better rate reads **0.75 / 0.95 / 0.96** and Transolver **0.75 / 1.03 /
1.01** at 35 / 210 / 510 wings; GeoTransolver-512, the parameter match,
reads 0.71 (0.1042) and 0.90 (0.0461) at 35 and 210 wings at 200,000
cells and 0.95 at 510 from its 100,000-cell SCALE-LAW pair (0.0382). The

area-law draw, all training in `rb`); the earlier-protocol 510-wing
value (one seed, 0.0556) is not a standing.

**200,000 against 10,000 cells.** The fleet preregistration promised

budget was the gap" if GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA rose by 0.03 or more and
"the wings differ" if it moved less. Three rungs have a unit-direction

to 0.1500 (0.98), GeoTransolver 0.1102 to 0.1098 (1.00), Transolver
0.1142 to 0.1101 (0.96); GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 0.72 to 0.73. 4
geometries: ISLA 0.2519 to 0.2659 (1.06), GeoTransolver 0.1884 at 1e-3
to 0.1798 at 3e-3 (0.95; 1.07 at the matched rate 1e-3), Transolver

the 10,000-cell baselines there were fed the physical velocity and are
not twins. The 510- and 1,260-wing rungs have no 10,000-cell twin of any
model (the lanes there predate the relative frame and the unit-direction
protocol). So the
"within 2%" that held on the 35-wing rung is that rung's property: the
budget moves every model by 20 to 25% on the fixed-angle rung and ISLA
by 14 to 23% on the two 210-case rungs, and still moves the ratio at a
matched rate by at most 0.01 on every rung that has a twin. "The wings
differ" is the group's reading on all three.

**The wing half of SCALE-LAW.** Over the four-rung case ladder
GeoTransolver-256 at its better rate has exponent **0.35** (seeds 0.34
and 0.35; local 0.46, 0.26, 0.20 over 35 to 210, 210 to 510, 510 to

(@sec-nb-scalelaw-drivaerml-verdict). ISLA at the earlier protocol has
no 1,260-wing point; over 35 to 510 wings (seed 43 at 510) its exponent
is 0.40 (seed 42 over 35 to 210: 0.58; seed 43 over 35 to 510: 0.39),
with local exponents 0.56 and then −0.01, the 510-wing stall. The
reference configuration over the same three rungs has exponent **0.49**
(0.49 and 0.50; local 0.58, 0.27), against 0.40 for GeoTransolver and
0.38 for Transolver on the matched 35-to-510 ladder. ISLA's curve is the
steeper by 0.09 to 0.11, and the whole difference is in the first step:
from 210 to 510 wings the three local exponents are 0.27, 0.26 and 0.29.
The fitted laws of GeoTransolver-256 and the reference configuration
meet at about 300 wings and those of Transolver at about 200, but the
measured 510-wing ratios (0.96 and 1.01) say the GeoTransolver curves
have not crossed, so no crossover is established; Transolver and the
reference configuration are at parity from 210 wings (1.03, 1.01). The
figure draws the four series with their fits (the plateaued lanes are
not drawn).

**Reading.** (1) The HiLift ladder at the reporting protocol is

configuration cannot supply the large rungs on this dataset, three of
