## 2026-09-30 — Preregistration, WING-ELEMENT-ANATOMY: element labels for all 198 validation wings from a span-station segmentation of each 290-million-cell boundary mesh (connected components cannot separate the elements: one welded body holds 99.3% of the area), to decide the flap and gap-band bar of H1 on both wing rungs {#sec-nb-wing-element-anatomy}

**Setting.** The surface anatomy of 2026-09-30
(@sec-nb-wing-anatomy-surface) located ISLA's excess pressure error over
GeoTransolver on the HiLiftAeroML wings by curvature on every validation
wing (uniform, H2 refuted) and by high-lift element on only five wings,
because the dataset carries no per-cell element id and only 41 of 1,800
cases ship an STL. On those five the flap (1.37 / 1.30 at 210 wings) and
the gap band (1.83 / 1.80 on the fixed-angle wing) cleared the bar, so
H1 (the excess sits on the thin elements and in the gaps between them)
stayed open. This entry preregisters the full-scale element readout: an
element label for every cell of every validation wing, derived from the
boundary mesh itself, and the same bar read on 180 wings of the 210-wing
rung and 18 wings of the fixed-angle rung.

**What is tested.** H1 against H3 on the element axis. A surface class
carries the excess when its ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver ratio (case mean of the
area-weighted RMS pressure error of the class, divided by the
area-weighted standard deviation of the case's true pressure) is at
least 0.15 above the whole-surface ratio on both seed pairs (42 / 42 and
43 / 43), the bar of the surface anatomy unchanged. Classes: slat, main
wing and body, flap, other bodies (tail, nacelle), the gap band (every
sampled slat, main or flap cell within 0.02 L_ref, 5.5 in, of a
full-mesh cell of a different element among those three), and each
element outside the gap band. Prediction if the pilot holds: the flap
and the gap band clear the bar on the 210-wing rung on both seeds and
the slat does not; the fixed-angle rung repeats the gap band. If no
class clears the bar on either rung, H1 is refuted and the wing deficit
is H3 (uniform) on both axes. Lanes and checkpoints are the surface
anatomy's: `ref_isla_r1_hl210` against `ref_gt_w512_hl210` and
`p200k_hl_isla_single_aoa_12` against
`p200k_hl_gt_unit_single_aoa_12_lr3e3` (GeoTransolver-256, the only
GeoTransolver lane on that rung), seeds 42 and 43, epoch 500, the saved
200,000-cell float32 predictions of job 938092.

**Instrument.** `highlift/wing_element_labels.py` on the cluster. The
first idea, labelling the elements as the connected components of the
full vehicle mesh, failed on the pilot wing LHC001 at 16 degrees (job
942006, vertex adjacency through `physicsnemo.mesh` and
`scipy.sparse.csgraph.connected_components` over 147 million points):
one welded component holds 99.3% of the surface area, because slat
tracks, flap-track fairings and pylons connect every element to the
main wing, and the remaining 2.5 million components are fragments below
1e-5 of the area. The label therefore comes from a span-station
segmentation of the full mesh, the rule fixed before any readout: cells
are binned by span in 1-in stations; inside a station the cells split
into connected pieces; the largest piece is `main` (wing plus body at
that station); a piece below 1% of the station's area is a fragment and
takes the label of its nearest larger piece; a piece farther than 0.25
L_ref from the main piece, or with an (x, z) bounding-box diagonal over
0.5 L_ref, is `other`; otherwise it is `slat` when the 20 nearest main
cells to its centroid lie aft of it and `flap` when they lie ahead.
Bracket stations, where a track welds the element to the main wing so
the station has no separate piece, are repaired from their neighbours:
in a station without a slat (flap) piece whose neighbours within 3
stations on both sides have one, the main cells within 1.2 in of those
neighbours' slat (flap) cells are relabelled. The saved predictions keep
the sampled cells in block order without their ids, so the sample is
mapped back onto the full mesh by recovering the reader's contiguous
block start from consecutive-centroid differences and accepting the
match when the 99th-percentile nearest-cell distance is below 0.05 in.

**Pilot (two wings, jobs 942006 and 942148).** The mapping is exact: the
99th-percentile distance from a sampled cell to its full-mesh cell is
0.0001 in on all four lanes of LHC002 at 12 degrees, against a 3.6-in
sample spacing. The labels: LHC001 at 16 degrees reads slat 5.3%, main
48.1%, flap 5.9%, other 40.6% of the surface area with 63 slat and 28
flap bracket stations repaired; LHC002 at 12 degrees reads slat 2.1%,
main 69.9%, flap 3.5%, other 24.4% (47 and 31 stations repaired). The
STL of LHC001 gives slat 2.7%, flap 4.0% and other bodies 11%, so the
full-mesh rule reads the thin elements about 1.5 to 2 times larger
than the STL (the repair adds track and cove area that the STL
segmentation, which under-read the slat, missed) and assigns 2 to 4
times the STL's area to `other`. The `other` class is reported but is
not a target of H1; the slat and flap over-read is in the direction of
diluting their ratios toward the whole-surface value, so it works
against the prediction, not for it. The gap band defined against the
full mesh holds 17% of the sampled cells on LHC002, against 3 to 5% in
the STL pilot, because it now includes the main-wing cells facing the
slat and flap coves from both sides. One case costs 7,300 to 14,100 s
for the segmentation (single process, 18 to 20 GB peak) and about 250 s
per lane for the mapping; the second pilot case was wall-killed at 4 h
after writing its labels, so the script resumes from a written label
file.

**Jobs.** Label array 944509 (20 tasks of 10 cases, CPU partition,
`cpu-normal`, 10 h wall, 300 GB per node; the cases of a task run in
parallel), chained anatomy reduction 944510
(`highlift/wing_element_anatomy.py` →
`wing_element_anatomy_2026-09-30.json`), reducer and figure
`results/wing_element_anatomy_2026-09-30.py`. Verdict follows in a
separate entry; the ledger row WING-MECH carries the state.

## 2026-10-01 — Verdict, SCALE-HL cells clause: ISLA cosine-192 at 100,000 cells scores 0.98 of its 200,000-cell twin on the 510-wing rung (0.0427 against 0.0433, two seeds; corrected the same day from 1.01 after a 77-of-180-case partial scoring was caught), inside the 2% bar, so cells are flat above 100,000 for all three architectures on both datasets; a stale 9-case GeoTransolver-256 seed corrected (ratio 0.99 → 1.00) {#sec-nb-scalehl-cells-verdict}

**Setting.** SCALE-HL (@sec-nb-scalehl-prereg, verdict
@sec-nb-scalehl-verdict) asked whether the DrivAerML scaling picture
holds on the 510-wing HiLiftAeroML rung. Its cells clause, that doubling
the training sample from 100,000 to 200,000 cells per case changes the
pressure error by less than 2%, closed on 2026-09-26 for GeoTransolver-256
and Transolver-256 but not for ISLA, whose 200,000-cell fleet lane was
linear-routed and had one seed on the mean-field plateau (0.5945 against
0.0556; the arm was voided in @sec-nb-p200k-hl-ladder-verdict). The
replacement twin, campaign `sc`: ISLA 192 wide with cosine routing at
1e-3, 200,000 training cells, seeds 42 and 43, against the ROUTE-NORM
cosine-192 lane at 100,000 cells on the same rung, both scored in float32
at 200,000 cells on the 180 validation wings.

**What we saw.** The cosine-192 lane at 100,000 cells scores **0.0427**
(0.0433 / 0.0421) and at 200,000 cells **0.0433** (0.0432 / 0.0434), a
ratio 100,000 ÷ 200,000 of **0.98**, inside the 2% bar; the 200,000-cell
seeds agree to 0.5% and the 100,000-cell pair brackets them. The
200,000-cell lane costs 0.222 s per step against 0.172 and 29.6 GB
against 15.2 GB. [Correction, same day: the first reduction read seed 42
at 200,000 cells as 0.0409 from a metrics file the evaluator was still
writing (77 of 180 cases) and reported the ratio as 1.01 with crossing
seeds; the complete file gives 0.0432. The verdict does not move. The
scored-lane waiter now requires the metrics file to be ten minutes
quiet, and the fetch refreshes a local copy whose remote has more rows.] Re-running the reducer over the current metrics files
also corrected the GeoTransolver-256 100,000-cell arm: the 2026-09-26
artifact had averaged seed 42 over a 9-case partial scoring (0.0377); the
full 180-case file gives 0.0385, so the arm is 0.0387 (not 0.0383), the
cells ratio 1.00 (not 0.99), GeoTransolver-256 ÷ linear ISLA-192 0.78
(not 0.77) and the width rise 0.14 → 0.14 (0.136 against 0.143); no
verdict moves. The artifact `results/scalehl_2026-09-26.json` is
regenerated with the new arm `isla_cos_192_c200k` and the voided linear
arm marked.

**Reading.** **Cells are flat above 100,000 per case on the wings for
all three architectures** (ISLA 0.98, GeoTransolver 1.00, Transolver
0.98), as on DrivAerML (ISO-COST, @sec-nb-isocost-verdict). The reporting
protocol's 200,000 cells buys no accuracy on either dataset over 100,000
at 1.3 times the step time and twice the memory for ISLA; the ruling
that the recipe default stays at 200,000 is Peter's (2026-09-18) and is
about the protocol, not the evidence. SCALE-HL is complete; the ledger
row moves to DONE.

## 2026-10-01 — Record, UNIVERSAL-AGG on DrivAerML Volume (two seeds): always-on aggregation ÷ same-snapshot reference 1.03 pressure, 1.08 velocity (1.09 / 1.08 per seed), 1.00 eddy viscosity; the sixth dataset confirms the removal and completes the record {#sec-nb-universal-agg-drvol-record}

**Setting.** The universalization test of the local relational
aggregation (@sec-nb-universal-prereg) switched the option on everywhere
and read it against same-snapshot references on datasets its fixed-mesh
rule was not fitted on. The verdict was reached on the lug
(@sec-nb-universal-agg-lug-verdict) and the option was removed from the
model; the DrivAerML Volume pair (`un_drvol_{ref,local05}`, 200,000
interior cells, reference configuration, seeds 42 and 43, float32 on the
test cars) was still training and was to complete the record.

**What we saw.** Reference pressure 0.0395, velocity 0.0575, eddy
viscosity 0.0851; with the aggregation 0.0409, 0.0621, 0.0849: ratios
**1.03 / 1.08 / 1.00** (seed 42 1.03 / 1.09 / 0.97, seed 43 1.04 / 1.08
/ 1.03). The *not part of the model* clause (worse than 1.05 on any
field) fires on velocity on both seeds; pressure sits between the
clauses and eddy viscosity is neutral.

**Reading.** The aggregation hurts on a sixth dataset, the interior of
a geometry-varying 3-D problem, in the same direction as on AirfRANS
(velocity worst, 1.08 here against 1.17 to 1.22 there). Nothing changes:
the option stays removed, the Poisson gain stays on record as the
measured effect of a removed option, and the record is complete. Data:
`results/universal_agg_2026-09-28.json` (regenerated; `complete: true`,
worst ratio 1.53 on the Tensile2d scalar field).

## 2026-10-01 — Verdict, ISLA-PERF-2: a real four-rank training step of the reference ISLA at 200,000 cells is GPU-bound (kernels 241 of 242 ms on DrivAerML Surface); backward is 2.2 times forward and the fused geometry kernel's backward alone is 42 ms against a 4.6 ms forward; about 1,500 small elementwise and copy kernels per step take 92 ms; the dataloader waits 7 to 9 ms; saved activations total 51 GiB, led by 18 GiB of float32 residual-stream copies and 14 GiB of pre- and post-GELU MLP hidden states {#sec-nb-isla-perf-2-verdict}

**Setting.** The 2026-09-09 profile (@sec-nb-isla-perf-verdict) found and
fixed the point-softmax kernel that was 85 to 95% of the step and left
the dense geometry region as the next cost; that region has since been
fused into one Triton kernel per layer (@sec-nb-kernel-study).
Every timing in the book since then is the synthetic cost sweep (one
GPU, random cloud, no data, no DDP, no loss): 117 ms per step and 34.9
GiB for the reference configuration at 200,000 cells. The question here
is where a *real* fleet step spends its time and memory, so that any
further optimization is aimed by measurement. Peter's question of
2026-10-01 (runtime and memory levers for ISLA) is the trigger.

**Instrument.** `results/isla_train_profile_2026-10-01.py`, run as a
fleet lane runs (torchrun, four GB300 ranks, DDP, batch 1 per rank, bf16
autocast, the recipe's reader, transforms, collate, Huber loss, metrics
and Muon optimizer; code_v15 + recipe_v7, the archive of 5511b5f1): twelve
steps of the reference ISLA (384 wide, 12 layers, 256 slices, cosine
routing, fused geometry kernel, geo_checkpoint on and moot under the
fused path) on DrivAerML Surface (`isla_surface`, 200,000 sampled cells)
and DrivAerML Volume (`isla_volume`, 200,000 interior plus 200,000
boundary tokens). A CUDA sync after every phase splits each step into the
dataloader wait, the host-to-device copy, forward plus loss, backward
(with the DDP all-reduce) and the optimizer; steps 6 to 8 run under
torch.profiler with kernel time bucketed by family, device kernels only
(the CPU-side op and annotation rows carry their children's device time
and were double-counted in a first pass); one extra step on rank 0
attributes every autograd-saved tensor to the module whose forward
created it. Artifacts: `results/isla_train_profile_drivaer_ml_{surface,volume}_2026-10-01.json`
and the surface key-averages table. Jobs 955356 (final), 953516, 953596,
953825, 954198, 954658 (superseded; see the lessons below).

**What we saw (median over nine timed steps, rank 0; the four ranks agree within 7%).**

| phase | Surface, 200k cells | Volume, 200k + 200k tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| dataloader wait | 8.7 ms | 26 ms |
| host-to-device | 0.4 ms | 0.8 ms |
| forward + loss + metrics | 69 ms | 159 ms |
| backward (incl. all-reduce) | 146 ms | 269 ms |
| optimizer (Muon) | 19 ms | 18 ms |
| whole step | 242 ms | 475 ms |
| device kernel time per step (annotations removed) | 241 ms | 426 ms |
| peak allocated memory | 44.9 GiB | 88.5 GiB |

Kernel time by family on the surface (of 241 ms): elementwise and copy
kernels 92 ms (38%; 1,211 `copy_` calls, 251 `div`, 243 `sum`, 447 `mul`,
332 `add_` per step), the fused geometry kernel 47 ms (20%; **backward
42.4 ms, forward 4.6 ms**, twelve calls each), the NCCL all-reduce 37 ms of
elapsed kernel time (overlapped with backward; six ring-LL calls of the
137 MB float32 gradient), GEMMs 30 ms (12%; `mm` 14 ms, `bmm` 9 ms),
the Muon optimizer 26 ms (11%), LayerNorm and GELU 22 ms (9%), the point
softmax 0.2 ms (the 2026-09-09 fix holds). On the volume: elementwise 174
ms, geometry 93 ms (backward 82, forward 9), GEMMs 54 ms, LayerNorm and
GELU 43 ms, optimizer 33 ms, the cuML nearest-neighbour search 24 ms (5%
of the step), NCCL 14 ms.

Saved activations (rank 0, surface): **51.3 GiB** in total for a 44.9 GiB
peak. By module: the routing logits (`blocks.*.assign`) 12.1 GiB, the
slice block's own einsums and softmaxes 9.8 GiB, the MLP's second Linear
6.9 GiB and its GELU 6.9 GiB, the broadcast Linear 4.3 GiB, the two
LayerNorms 3.5 GiB each, the MLP's first Linear 1.7 GiB. By shape:
**18.0 GiB of (200,000, 384) float32** (sixty copies, five per layer: the
residual stream and LayerNorm inputs kept in float32 under autocast),
13.7 GiB of (200,000, 1,536) bfloat16 (the MLP hidden state saved twice,
before and after GELU), 4.8 GiB of (256, 200,000) float32 (the two
point-normalized softmaxes per layer, saved as bmm operands), 4.3 GiB of
(200,000, 960) bfloat16 (the concatenated broadcast input), 4.0 GiB of
(200,000, 384) bfloat16. The volume doubles every figure (400,000 tokens).

**Reading, ranked by expected gain per unit of work.**

1. *The fused geometry kernel's backward* is the single largest kernel
   and nine times its forward (42 against 4.6 ms; 82 against 9 ms on the
   volume). The forward shows what the arithmetic costs; the backward
   re-derives the invariants, accumulates three incoming gradients and
   writes per-tile partial sums for the anchor and Linear gradients. A
   backward at two to three times the forward is the normal ratio, so 25
   to 30 ms per step (10 to 12%) is on the table in that one kernel:
   tile shape, register pressure at S = 256, the libdevice
   transcendentals, and the partial-sum layout are the things to look at.
2. *The elementwise and copy soup* around the fused region is 38% of the
   kernel time and about 1,500 launches per step: autocast casts, the
   transposes of the point softmax, the measure and bias adds, the
   normalizations and the einsum reshapes. These are exactly what
   `torch.compile` fuses; the earlier trial (@sec-nb-isla-perf-verdict,
   round 2) compiled only the geometry region and lost, but that region
   is now a custom op the compiler can treat as opaque. A compiled slice
   block with the fused kernel as a leaf, or a second Triton kernel
   covering the point softmax, the three poolings and the readback (the
   slice-attention primitive), is the lever; plausible gain 40 to 60 ms
   (15 to 25%) and, because the (256, 200,000) float32 softmaxes would no
   longer be saved, about 5 GiB.
3. *Memory, independent of time*: the 18 GiB of float32 (N, 384) copies
   are the residual stream and LayerNorm inputs; keeping the stream in
   bfloat16 between blocks (with the LayerNorm in float32 internally)
   halves them, and fusing GELU into the first MLP GEMM's epilogue drops
   the 6.9 GiB pre-activation. Together about 16 GiB of the 45 (35%),
   at no arithmetic change the loss would notice. Whole-block activation
   checkpointing remains the blunt instrument (about 1.3 times the step
   for roughly a twelve-fold activation cut).
4. *The optimizer* is 11% of the step: Muon's Newton-Schulz iterations
   over 34M parameters every step. Fewer iterations, bfloat16 iterates
   or a fused implementation are recipe-level choices; AdamW would cost
   about 3 ms here.
5. *Not levers*: the dataloader (4% surface, 6% volume), the host copy,
   the GEMMs (12%), the point softmax, the nearest-neighbour search (5%
   of the volume step), and NCCL (overlapped). The input pipeline the
   2026-10-01 discussion guessed at is not where the time goes.

**Two lessons from getting here.** (1) TF32: the first profile enabled
`torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32` (copied from the synthetic
script). The lanes never do, and with it on the dataset's GPU-side
rotation quantizes the mesh coordinates so that **43,187 of 200,000
sampled DrivAerML surface cells collapse to zero area** (three vertices
with identical x and y; `results/degenerate_diag_tf32_2026-10-01.json`);
with it off the same case has none. recipe_v6's intermediate
degenerate-cell filter had masked this as "dropping 43k cells" and
recipe_v7, where the filter is deleted, surfaced it as the loss's
positive-measure check. No lane trained under either; the deletion of
the filter stands. TF32 is off in the training path and must stay off
upstream of any geometry transform. (2) Profiling under DDP: an
`all_gather_object` of the per-rank results mis-sized its NCCL buffer
("more than 1EB"), and running the extra attribution step on rank 0
alone deadlocked its DDP backward against the other ranks' barrier until
the one-hour timeout, twice. Per-rank files plus a barrier, and every
rank runs every step.

**What is next.** Items 1 to 3 are engineering with exactness tests
already in place (`test/experimental/models/isla`); each is measured by
re-running this profiler, which is now a one-command job
(`kernel/perf/isla_train_profile.sbatch`). None changes the
architecture; Peter's decision on 2026-10-01 is which, if any, to fund.

## 2026-10-01 — Verdict, PERF-3: two of the profiled levers adopted. (1) Blackwell launch defaults for the fused geometry kernel (backward 3.76 → 2.49 ms per layer; real step 242 → 221 ms). (2) Per-block `torch.compile` (`compile_blocks`): DrivAerML Surface step 221 → 180 ms and peak memory 44.9 → 32.9 GiB, Volume 475 → 308 ms and 88.5 → 64.5 GiB, at bfloat16 roundoff; whole-model compile recompiles every case on the mesh vertex count and is not the way. Training-neutrality pairs launched (group pf) {#sec-nb-perf-3-verdict}

**Setting.** ISLA-PERF-2 (@sec-nb-isla-perf-2-verdict) measured a real
four-rank training step of the reference ISLA at 200,000 cells on GB300
at 242 ms and 44.9 GiB on DrivAerML Surface (475 ms, 88.5 GiB on the
Volume) and ranked the levers: the fused geometry kernel's backward (42 ms,
nine times its forward), the elementwise and copy glue around it (92 ms,
1,500 launches), and the saved activations (51 GiB, led by 18 GiB of
float32 residual copies and 14 GiB of MLP hidden states). Peter asked
(2026-10-01) that the levers be tried. Every number below is from the
same profiler (`results/isla_train_profile_2026-10-01.py`, four GB300
ranks, DDP, bf16 autocast, the recipe's data path; code_v15 + recipe_v7
unless stated) and every change is checked against the eager path.

**Lever 1, kernel launch configuration (adopted).** A sweep of (points
per program, warps) for both fused kernels at 200,000 points by 256
slices (`results/geo_kernel_sweep_2026-10-01.json`, candidates in
`geo_kernel_sweep_candidates_2026-10-01.json`): the defaults tuned on an
RTX 4090 (forward 8, backward 4, four warps) run 0.56 and 3.76 ms per
layer; the backward is register-bound and is fastest at **2 points per
program (2.49 ms, 1.5x)**, the forward at 4 (0.49 ms, 1.14x); 16 points
and above are 2 to 3 times slower, more warps do not help. The tile size
changes only the floating-point summation order: pointwise outputs and
per-point gradients agree with the defaults to 1e-5 relative, the
tile-summed anchor and weight gradients to 6e-6. The defaults are now
chosen by compute capability (Blackwell: 4 and 2; older devices keep the
4090 values), the ISLA suite passes (167 tests, job 957622) and the real
step falls from **242 to 221 ms** (geometry backward 42 → 25 ms).
Commit 9d03ab74. Even at its best the backward is five times its
forward, so the remaining asymmetry is the kernel's structure (it holds
all 256 slices of a tile in registers and recomputes the forward), a
rewrite rather than a tuning.

**Lever 2, torch.compile (adopted as per-block compile).** Three scopes
were tried. *Whole model* through the recipe's `compile` flag: inductor's
generated backward trips a size assertion on a reduction output, and with
the assertion disabled it is numerically right (losses track eager to
bfloat16 noise) and cuts peak memory to 32.4 GiB, but it **recompiles on
every step** (12 s per step): the dynamo log names the guard, the
vehicle mesh's vertex count, 581,092 to 584,973 points across cases for
the same 200,000 cells, so the mesh-facing forward can never be
compiled statically, and `dynamic=True` at that scope hits a dynamo
error on the custom op's float argument. *MLP stacks only*: no gain
(249 ms, same memory). ***Per slice block***: the blocks see only the
(B, 200,000, ·) tensors, which are constant across cases, so each of the
twelve compiles once; the fused geometry op is a registered custom op
and stays a leaf. Result on the surface: **step 177 to 185 ms, peak
32.9 GiB, saved activations 32 GiB** (the 18 GiB of float32 residual
copies and the 4.8 GiB float32 point-softmaxes are gone; the 13.7 GiB
MLP hidden state remains), losses matching eager at the fourth digit
(0.0564 against 0.0564 at step 11); with inductor's size assertion on,
the same; with `dynamic=True`, 168 ms, so datasets whose token count
varies per case are served by torch's default (static first, dynamic
after the second distinct shape); at 150,000 cells 151 ms and 24.8 GiB.
On the Volume: **308 ms and 64.5 GiB** from 475 and 88.5. Implemented as
the `compile_blocks` constructor option (commit 9459aa17: the compiled
object is each block's bound forward, so parameter names, the state dict
and the eager path are unchanged; an equivalence test on CPU and CUDA at
float64 1e-9) and set to true in the recipe's ISLA yamls (commit
343b284e); the class default stays false, as for any module.

**Levers not pursued.** The bfloat16 residual stream is unnecessary: the
compiled blocks already stop saving the float32 copies. The Muon
optimizer's 11% is a recipe choice. The dataloader (4 to 6%), the GEMMs
(12%), the point softmax and the nearest-neighbour search were never
levers.

**Net.** Surface step 242 → about 180 ms (1.35x) and memory 44.9 → 32.9
GiB (0.73x); Volume 475 → 308 ms (1.54x) and 88.5 → 64.5 GiB (0.73x),
with no change to the architecture or its arithmetic beyond
floating-point ordering. Against the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512
in the synthetic sweep (137 ms, 66.5 GiB at 200,000 cells, single GPU),
the real ISLA step is now near its time and at half its memory; a
matched real-step profile of GeoTransolver is the fair comparison and is
not yet run.

**Preregistration, PERF-3 training neutrality (group `pf`, eight lanes,
code_v16 + recipe_v8 at 343b284e).** Compiled against eager blocks on
the same snapshot, DrivAerML Surface (`pf_dr_cb` / `pf_dr_nocb`) and
DrivAerML Volume (`pf_vol_cb` / `pf_vol_nocb`), seeds 42 and 43, the
reference configuration, 500 epochs, float32 scoring on the held-out
cases. Bar (the KERNEL-NEUTRAL rule): the seed-mean ratio compiled ÷
eager within 3% on every field of both datasets, seeds within their own
spread. If met, `compile_blocks: true` stays the recipe default; if any
field is worse than 3% on both seeds, the default reverts and the lane
is investigated as a numerics question (bfloat16 reordering is the only
mechanism on the table). The pairs also give the first measured
500-epoch wall-clock gain of the compiled path.

**Lessons.** Profile the real step, not the synthetic one, and after
every change: the input pipeline I guessed at was 4% of the step; the
compile scope that works is the one whose inputs are shape-constant.
Three profiler bugs cost half a day and are recorded in
@sec-nb-isla-perf-2-verdict (TF32, the all-gather, the lone-rank
backward).


## 2026-10-01 — Book pass with fresh eyes: an Opus 5 review through the pi harness named the degradation mechanism (chapters stopped deleting: new lanes arrive as labels, caveats and status pointers beside old numbers); the evidence part is now six chapters, every notebook citation left the documentation chapters, program status left the front matter, 110,908 → 103,855 words {#sec-nb-book-pass-2026-10-01}

**Setting.** Peter (2026-10-01): "we go through this loop where I ask you
to overhaul the book, and it's great; then bit by bit it gets worse (more
convoluted, hard to follow) as we add more things over time", with the
suggestion to have an Opus-class model review or rewrite it with fresh
eyes. The pi harness reached Opus 5 (Opus 5.5 is gated on a newer Claude
Code client than pi presents); it read index and chapters 01 to 15 cold
against STYLE.md and Peter's rules and wrote the review at
`research/book_review_opus5_2026-10-01.md` (brief beside it). Its
verdict: not followable on one pass; the reader is lost on the thesis
table (sixteen rows mixing three ISLA configurations, three cell
budgets, undefined vocabulary, migration state), again at chapter 07's
350-word computed lede, and cumulatively (pose in four chapters,
discretization in five, the output-component clause in five, the whole
standing restated a third time in the literature appendix). Its named
mechanism: the book had stopped deleting.

**What changed (five commits, cceed55b5 to 53302f00f).** Evidence part
split into six chapters (07 DrivAerML surface; 08 data efficiency and the
wing deficit; 09 discretization and pose, now the one home for the pose
tables; 10 capacity, scaling and cost; 11 boundary to interior; 12 beyond
external aerodynamics with Tensile2d, the lug, DeepJEB++ and the OLBC
sets). Front matter: one thesis table, reference configuration only, a
four-sentence thesis, the names-and-colors key and the "what this book
does not claim" list moved to the appendices and the limits chapter. The
trained-routing pictures moved from the architecture reference to the
payoff of idea 3 in chapter 02; the pose-prior diagnostic and the OLBC
ablations moved to the design-decision appendix; the six non-aerodynamic
dataset problem figures moved beside their conversions; the literature
appendix lost its standing table, figure and ideas table and keeps the
novel-contributions argument and bibliography. Every `@sec-nb-*` citation
left the documentation chapters (55 occurrences); program status, dates,
"earlier protocol" prose, "R1", "in flight" and "interim" cells are gone
from chapters. Two number conflicts fixed from the artifacts: the ledger's
REF-BOARD row had the 210-wing GeoTransolver-256 ratio (0.89) in the
35-wing slot (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA there is 0.71,
`results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json`), and the literature appendix's
210-wing row used different lanes than chapter 07. The architecture
chapter lost a documented argument that no longer exists
(`interior_nn_chunk`) and gained the `compile_blocks` row. Render: zero
cell errors, zero unresolved cross-references outside this file; the four
notebook references to the deleted tables are repointed in this entry's
commit.

**Rule for the loop, so it does not repeat.** A result lands in the book
by replacing a number, never beside one. If a lane has not been re-run
under the reference configuration, the row shows the earlier value in the
table cell with its label and nothing in prose; an unlanded rung is not a
row. Only the status chapter and this notebook cite notebook anchors or
carry dates. Each concept has one home chapter and one centerpiece.

## 2026-10-01 — Verdict, deflection sealed test at the reporting protocol: the reference ISLA is 1.10x unit-direction GeoTransolver on sealed pressure (0.0356 against 0.0325, two seeds), at parity on velocity and wall shear (1.00), and both degrade from validation by the same factor (1.32 against 1.28); falsified, as at the exploration budget (1.16x) {#sec-nb-deflection-p200k-verdict}

**Setting.** The deflection split (@sec-nb-deflection-prereg, instrument
as amended @sec-nb-deflection-amend) trains on the 144 milder HiLiftAeroML
flap settings and scores once on the sealed 360-case high-deflection list;
the claim under test was that ISLA's geometry generalization carries across
that parameter boundary better than GeoTransolver's. At the exploration
budget (10,000 cells, 192 wide, linear routing) it was falsified
(@sec-nb-deflection-verdict: ISLA 1.157x on sealed pressure). The
200,000-cell twin's first ISLA pair fell to the mean-field plateau and was
superseded (@sec-nb-p200k-deflection-plateau); the reference configuration
pair `rb_hl_isla_deflection_seed42/43` replaced it, against the
unit-direction GeoTransolver pair at 1e-3, both scored in float32 on the
sealed test (`highlift/hl_defl_test_eval_p200k_aga.sbatch`) and on the
180-case validation list. Reducer
`results/deflection_p200k_reduce_2026-09-29.py`, artifact
`results/deflection_p200k_2026-09-29.json`; the validation scoring of the
ISLA pair had not been submitted by the evaluation pump and was nudged
through today.

**What we saw (seed means; seeds 42 / 43).** Sealed pressure: ISLA
0.0356 (0.0376 / 0.0336), GeoTransolver 0.0325 (0.0329 / 0.0320), ISLA ÷
GeoTransolver **1.10**; validation pressure 0.0269 against 0.0254 (1.06).
Velocity 0.0533 against 0.0533 (1.00), wall shear 0.0804 against 0.0805
(1.00), temperature 1.02, density 1.09. Degradation sealed ÷ validation on
pressure: ISLA **1.32**, GeoTransolver **1.28**. Against the exploration
budget the sealed pressure ratio moved from 1.157 to 1.097 and both models'
sealed errors fell (ISLA 0.89x, GeoTransolver 0.94x of their 10,000-cell
values), while the degradation factors rose slightly (1.23 → 1.32, 1.25 →
1.28).

**Reading.** Falsified under the preregistered bars (carried needed ISLA at
most 0.7x with a degradation at most 4; falsified at or above 0.9x): ISLA is
the worse model on the sealed set by the same margin it trails on the
in-distribution wings, and the two architectures lose the same fraction of
their accuracy across the boundary. There is no extrapolation advantage to
either side; the deflection split measures the in-distribution wing deficit
one more time. The limits chapter now states this as the measured
geometry-parameter extrapolation result (@sec-limits-regime). The P200K-FLEET
deflection half is complete.

## 2026-10-02 — Verdict, PERF-3 training neutrality: per-block compile is neutral on both DrivAerML tasks (compiled ÷ eager 0.995 to 1.005 on every field, two seeds, worst deviation 0.5%) and cuts 500-epoch chain wall-clock to 0.68 (Surface) and 0.70 (Volume) of eager; `compile_blocks: true` stays the recipe default {#sec-nb-perf-3-neutrality-verdict}

**Setting.** PERF-3 (@sec-nb-perf-3-verdict, whose preregistration
paragraph defined this test) adopted two profiled levers into the reference ISLA:
Blackwell launch defaults for the fused geometry kernel and a per-block
`torch.compile` of each slice block's forward (`compile_blocks`). The
compile changes only how the arithmetic is executed (operator fusion and
a different bfloat16 accumulation order), so the prereg's prediction was a
null: no scored field moves beyond seed noise. The bar was the
KERNEL-NEUTRAL rule, compiled ÷ eager within 3% on every field of both
datasets on the seed means.

**Instrument.** Eight lanes, group `pf`, code_v16 + recipe_v8 at
343b284e: the reference configuration at 200,000 cells, learning rate
5e-4, 500 epochs, seeds 42 and 43, trained with and without
`compile_blocks` on DrivAerML Surface (`pf_dr_cb`, `pf_dr_nocb`) and
DrivAerML Volume (`pf_vol_cb`, `pf_vol_nocb`). Readout: float32 per-case
relative L2 on the 48 held-out cases, averaged over cases then seeds;
reducer `results/perf3_reduce_2026-10-01.py`, artifact
`results/perf3_neutrality_2026-10-01.json`. Wall-clock is the sum of
each lane's chain-link elapsed times from `sacct`; both arms of a pair
have the same link count (Surface two, Volume three), so link startup
and the wall-killed tail of a link enter both arms alike.

**What we saw.** Every field is within 1% on the seed means and within
1.3% on every single seed:

| Task | Field | Eager | Compiled | Compiled ÷ eager | Seed 42 | Seed 43 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DrivAerML Surface | pressure | 0.0436 | 0.0438 | 1.005 | 1.000 | 1.010 |
| DrivAerML Surface | wall shear | 0.0686 | 0.0690 | 1.005 | 1.006 | 1.005 |
| DrivAerML Volume | pressure | 0.0411 | 0.0409 | 0.996 | 0.998 | 0.993 |
| DrivAerML Volume | velocity | 0.0658 | 0.0654 | 0.995 | 0.999 | 0.990 |
| DrivAerML Volume | eddy viscosity | 0.0883 | 0.0882 | 0.999 | 1.013 | 0.985 |

: PERF-3 neutrality pairs: float32 relative L2 on the 48 held-out cases, seed means and per-seed ratios (`results/perf3_neutrality_2026-10-01.json`). {#tbl-nb-perf3-neutrality}

The worst seed-mean deviation is 0.5% (Surface, both fields, compiled
slightly worse); the Volume fields lean the other way by the same
amount; the per-seed ratios straddle 1 on every field. The chain
wall-clock for 500 epochs fell from 3.39 and 3.41 hours (eager) to 2.28
and 2.36 hours (compiled) on Surface, ratio 0.68, and from 7.42 and
7.35 hours to 5.20 and 5.11 hours on Volume, ratio 0.70. These are
whole-chain numbers (data loading, validation, checkpointing and the
first-call compile included), so they are smaller gains than the

Volume) would suggest on Surface and about equal on Volume; the Surface
profile was taken before the eager arm's own kernel-default gain, so

**Verdict.** Bar met on both datasets, both seeds: **neutral**.
`compile_blocks: true` stays the recipe default; the class default
remains `False` so that a bare constructor has no compile step. PERF-3
is DONE. The ledger row carries the measured wall-clock ratio; the
using-ISLA chapter states the neutrality beside the step numbers.

**What is next.** The geometry backward is still five times its forward
(all 256 slices in registers plus forward recompute); that is a kernel
rewrite, not tuning, and is not scheduled. A matched real-step profile

is not yet run.

## 2026-10-02 — Verdict, GT-FPP closes: on the 510 HiLift wings at 100,000 cells, GeoTransolver-512 with the FLARE++ backend is 1.18x worse than physics attention on pressure (1.25 / 1.12 per seed) and 1.11x to 1.17x worse on every other field; physics attention stays the wing baseline, and the steel-man check ends with FLARE++ replacing the baseline at OLBC Poisson 2,048 only {#sec-nb-gt-fpp-hilift-verdict}

**Setting.** GT-FPP is the steel-man check on the GeoTransolver baseline:
the released FLARE++ attention backend against the released physics
attention, same width, same rate, same protocol, on every flagship
benchmark. Its rule: if FLARE++ is better by more than 3% on a dataset's
headline field, it becomes the baseline there and every ISLA ratio on
that dataset is restated. The DrivAerML, AirfRANS and OLBC readings are in
@sec-nb-gt-fpp-interim, @sec-nb-gt-fpp-poisson-verdict,
@sec-nb-gt-fpp-poisson-512 and @sec-nb-gt-fpp-olbc-verdict. This entry
closes the last open pair, the 510-wing HiLift rung.

**Instrument.** GeoTransolver width 512 with FLARE++
(`gf_hl_gt512_fpp_medium_c100k`, seeds 42 and 43, code_v11, learning rate
1e-3, 500 epochs, 100,000 cells, the SCALE-HL protocol) against the
physics-attention twins of `results/scalehl_2026-09-26.json`
(`shl_med_gt_w512_c100k`). Float32 relative L2 on the 180 held-out
wings; reducer `results/gt_fpp_reduce_2026-09-29.py`, artifact
`results/gt_fpp_2026-09-29.json`. The headline is pressure.

**What we saw** (FLARE++ ÷ physics attention on seed means; per seed in
parentheses):

| Field | Physics attention | FLARE++ | FLARE++ ÷ physics | Seed 42 | Seed 43 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pressure (headline) | 0.0382 | 0.0451 | 1.18 | 1.25 | 1.12 |
| temperature | 0.0466 | 0.0517 | 1.11 | 1.14 | 1.07 |
| density | 0.0515 | 0.0604 | 1.17 | 1.23 | 1.12 |
| velocity | 0.0573 | 0.0651 | 1.14 | 1.16 | 1.12 |
| wall shear | 0.0880 | 0.1015 | 1.15 | 1.18 | 1.13 |

: GT-FPP on the 510 HiLift wings at 100,000 cells: GeoTransolver-512 under the two backends, float32 relative L2 on the 180 held-out wings (`results/gt_fpp_2026-09-29.json`). {#tbl-nb-gt-fpp-hilift}

FLARE++ is worse on every field and on both seeds; the smallest per-seed
ratio is 1.07 (temperature, seed 43). Both lanes completed 500 epochs
without NaN; this is a plain accuracy gap, not a training failure of the
elasticity 8,448 kind.

**Verdict.** Physics attention stays the GeoTransolver baseline on the
wings; no wing ratio in chapter 08 changes. Across the whole check,
FLARE++ replaces the baseline at OLBC Poisson 2,048 only (0.77), ties
within 3% on DrivAerML Surface at the best rates and on elasticity at
512 and 2,048, and is weaker on AirfRANS (1.14 to 1.30), the wings
(1.18), Poisson 512 and 8,448 (1.07, 1.18), and elasticity 8,448 (where
it fails to train, 4.4x to 6.4x). GT-FPP is DONE. FLARE++ is a released
baseline and is not tuned further.

**Why it matters.** The steel-man question was whether the GeoTransolver
numbers the book compares against were the weaker of two released
backends. On the flagship surface and interior benchmarks they were not;
the one place the stronger backend changes is a single Poisson rung,
which chapter 12 already quotes under the 3% rule.

## 2026-10-02 — Verdict, PROTO-COND-2 adopted: the 510-wing pair reads 0.98 centered ÷ static on pressure (0.95 / 1.02) and 0.98 to 0.99 on every other field, inside the 1.03 adoption bar; the 2,048-case checkpoints keep prototype cosine 0.06 to 0.07 and effective rank 132 to 151; the centered, scale-bounded sample-conditioned prototypes are now the routing of every slice block and the static form is deleted {#sec-nb-proto-cond-2-adopted}

**Setting.** PROTO-COND-2 (@sec-nb-proto-cond-2-prereg) is the collapse-proof
form of sample-conditioned slice prototypes: in every block, learned seeds
attend over the token states with a measure-weighted softmax, the attended
term is centered across the slices and smoothly bounded to a learned
fraction $g$ of the seeds' spread, and the result is added to the seeds.
Three datasets had been read (@sec-nb-proto-cond-2-interim): Poisson 512
and 2,048 pay 0.86 and 0.78, DrivAerML Surface is neutral (1.00 / 1.00),
AirfRANS pressure 0.95 with velocity 1.03 (one seed 1.06). Peter's rule of
2026-09-30 left the decision to the 510-wing pair: within 1.03 on pressure
adopts the centered form as the default and deletes the static one under
the one-model rule; worse than 1.03 on both seeds deletes the option. The
prereg also asked for the prototype-cosine check on the 2,048 checkpoints
(bar below 0.3, effective rank above 100, as at 512) to be run with the
wing reduction.

**Instrument.** Lanes `pc2_hl_cent_medium` against `pc2_hl_ref_medium`,
seeds 42 and 43, code_v12 + recipe_v4, the reference configuration at
200,000 cells (the reporting protocol), 500 epochs, float32 relative L2 on
the 180 held-out wings; reducer `results/proto_cond2_reduce_2026-09-29.py`,
artifact `results/proto_cond2_2026-09-29.json`. The cosine check is the
PROTO-COND diagnostic (`kernel/pc/diag/proto_cond_diag.py`, job 969702) on
the four 2,048-case checkpoints, float32 eval-mode inference over the first
32 test samples at every node; artifact
`results/proto_cond2_diag_n2048_2026-10-02.json`.

**What we saw** (centered ÷ static on seed means; per seed in parentheses):

| Field | Static | Centered | Centered ÷ static | Seed 42 | Seed 43 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pressure (headline) | 0.0422 | 0.0415 | 0.98 | 0.95 | 1.02 |
| temperature | 0.0488 | 0.0483 | 0.99 | 0.97 | 1.01 |
| density | 0.0568 | 0.0558 | 0.98 | 0.95 | 1.01 |
| velocity | 0.0615 | 0.0608 | 0.99 | 0.97 | 1.01 |
| wall shear | 0.0954 | 0.0940 | 0.99 | 0.96 | 1.01 |

: PROTO-COND-2 on the 510 HiLift wings at 200,000 cells: the reference ISLA with centered and with static prototypes, float32 relative L2 on the 180 held-out wings (`results/proto_cond2_2026-09-29.json`). {#tbl-nb-proto-cond-2-wings}

Every field is inside the bar on the mean and on both seeds; seed 42 favors
the centered form by 3 to 5%, seed 43 the static form by 1 to 2%, so the
wings read as neutral with a lean toward the centered form. On the 2,048
Poisson checkpoints the centered arm's prototypes have mean pairwise cosine
0.068 and 0.060 (seeds 42 and 43; the static seeds of the reference arm
0.064 and 0.068), effective rank 132 and 151 (reference 127 and 140), a
trained gain of 0.149 and 0.145 (from 0.1), a relative prototype
displacement of 0.14, and 182 to 184 effective active slices (reference 173
to 192). No collapse at either rung.

**Verdict.** Adopted. Over the full set the form is neutral or better
everywhere: 0.86 and 0.78 on Poisson at 512 and 2,048 cases, 1.00 on
DrivAerML Surface, 0.95 on AirfRANS pressure (velocity 1.03), 0.98 on the
wings; the only reading outside 1.03 anywhere is one AirfRANS velocity seed
at 1.06. The centered, scale-bounded prototypes are now the routing of
every slice block and of the head frame; the `slice_prototypes` option and
the static form are gone from the class, the tests and the book, and the
class default is what every lane called `centered`. The change adds
$2d^2 + 1$ parameters per block and to the head frame (3.8M at the
reference width, 34.3M to 38.1M on DrivAerML Surface).

**Two corrections made while adopting.** (1) The head frame's routing
logits were computed from the token states alone, without the measures,
so under the sample-conditioned form the frame's prototypes were an
*unweighted* summary of the tokens and the vector outputs lost exact
refinement invariance (the scalar outputs were unaffected; the
refinement-invariance contract test caught it at 1.7e-3 on a doubled mesh). The frame now synthesizes its
prototypes once from all tokens with their measures and reads them for
both of its routings; the contract tests pass at 1e-10 again. The trained
pairs above carry the unweighted frame in their vector fields (wall shear
and velocity), so those two ratios come from a frame the shipped class no
longer has; the scalar headline does not depend on it. (2) When every
token state is identical (a two-cell planar probe whose only block-0
feature is the same for both cells) the centered term is exactly zero and
the root in the bound had an infinite gradient; the mean square is floored
at $10^{-30}$ before the root, which is 15 orders below any value the term
takes on real data. The goldens of the release tests (forward outputs, the
reference checkpoint and its outputs, the backbone recording) were
regenerated from the adopted architecture; the 0.1.0 checkpoint-mapper test
now rewrites the reference checkpoint to the old declarations rather than
carrying a stale fixture.

**Why it matters.** This is the first routing change since the cosine form
that pays on a fixed-mesh boundary-data problem (Poisson, 0.78 to 0.86)
without a price anywhere else, and the mechanism is measured: the gain that
survived the centering is the slice-dependent part of the token summary,
the common component that collapsed the first form is removed exactly, and
the trained prototypes stay as spread as static seeds. The architecture
chapter is the source of truth for the construction (@sec-arch-layer).

**What is next.** Every evidence lane trained before this entry carries
static prototypes; headline ratios are restated as reference-configuration
lanes are re-run under the adopted class on the new snapshot (code_v18),
starting with the DrivAerML Surface and the 510-wing rungs that the thesis
table quotes. Until then the thesis table's values are the static-prototype
ones, labeled by their artifacts.

**The code_v18 reference lanes, DrivAerML half (later the same day).** The
reference configuration trained on the adopted snapshot (lanes `v18_dr_ref`
and `v18_vol_ref`, two seeds, recipe_v8) against the last static-prototype
lanes on the same recipe and the same per-block compile (the PERF-3 pairs
`pf_dr_cb` and `pf_vol_cb`, code_v16): Surface pressure 0.0435 against
0.0438 (ratio 0.994; seeds 1.000 and 0.988), wall shear 0.0683 against
0.0690 (0.991); Volume pressure 0.0408 against 0.0409 (0.996), velocity
0.0651 against 0.0654 (0.996), eddy viscosity 0.0871 against 0.0882
(0.988), with per-seed ratios between 0.979 and 1.013. The adopted class
is neutral to one percent better on both DrivAerML tasks, inside the
adoption bar on every field, so the thesis-table values for these two rows
can be restated from the v18 lanes without a change in reading
(`results/v18_reference_reduce_2026-10-02.py`,
`results/v18_reference_2026-10-02.json`). The wing and AirfRANS halves
are scored when their lanes finish; under the characterization campaign
(@sec-nb-char-prereg) every row is in any case replaced by the
reference-configuration lanes of REF-80.

## 2026-10-02 — Verdict, WING-ELEMENT-ANATOMY: on the 210-wing rung no element class carries ISLA's excess (largest both-seed excess +0.06 / −0.01 on the slat core, bar +0.15), so the deficit is uniform over the elements as over curvature (H3); on the fixed-angle rung the slat alone clears the bar (+0.16 / +0.26; its core +0.28 / +0.38, 3% of the area, 17% of the error) while the flap and the gap band of the five-wing pilot do not {#sec-nb-wing-element-anatomy-verdict}

**Setting.** WING-MECH asks where on the wing ISLA's excess pressure error
against GeoTransolver sits: on the thin elements and in the gaps between
them (H1), on high curvature (H2, refuted by the surface anatomy of
@sec-nb-wing-anatomy-surface), or nowhere in particular (H3). The
preregistration (@sec-nb-wing-element-anatomy) set the bar from the
surface anatomy: a class carries the excess when its ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver
ratio is at least 0.15 above the whole-surface ratio on both seed pairs,
and predicted from the five-wing pilot that the flap and the gap band
clear it on the 210-wing rung and the gap band again on the fixed-angle
rung.

**Instrument.** Per-cell element labels from a span-station segmentation
of every validation wing's full boundary mesh
(`highlift/wing_element_labels.py`; 190 of the 196 wings of the two rungs
after two ten-hour resume sweeps, the six unlabelled cases listed in the
artifact and in a third sweep), read on the saved 200,000-cell float32
predictions of the surface anatomy: `ref_isla_r1_hl210` against
`ref_gt_w512_hl210` (GeoTransolver-512) on 174 of the 180 validation wings
of the 210-wing rung and `p200k_hl_isla_single_aoa_12` against
`p200k_hl_gt_unit_single_aoa_12_lr3e3` (GeoTransolver-256) on all 18 of
the fixed-angle rung, seeds 42 and 43 paired. Classes: slat, main wing and
body, flap, other bodies, the gap band (cells within 0.02 L_ref of another
of the three elements) and each element outside it. Reducer
`results/wing_element_anatomy_2026-09-30.py`, artifact
`results/wing_element_anatomy_2026-09-30.json`, figure beside it.

**What we saw** (excess of the class ratio over the whole-surface ratio,
seed 42 / seed 43; a class carries at +0.15 on both):

| Class | Area share | 210 wings (whole surface 1.21 / 1.01) | Fixed angle (whole surface 1.47 / 1.42) |
|---|---|---|---|
| slat | 0.03 | +0.02 / −0.02 | **+0.16 / +0.26** |
| slat outside the gap band | 0.01 | +0.06 / −0.01 | **+0.28 / +0.38** |
| flap | 0.04 | −0.04 / +0.08 | −0.14 / −0.15 |
| flap outside the gap band | 0.03 | −0.05 / +0.08 | −0.17 / −0.18 |
| gap band | 0.06 | +0.02 / −0.05 | +0.04 / +0.09 |
| main wing and body | 0.68 | +0.01 / −0.02 | −0.01 / −0.04 |
| main outside the gap band | 0.65 | 0.00 / 0.00 | −0.05 / −0.14 |
| other bodies | 0.25 | −0.04 / +0.05 | +0.06 / 0.00 |

: Element anatomy of ISLA's excess pressure error over GeoTransolver on the two HiLift wing rungs: per class, the ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver ratio minus the whole-surface ratio, per seed pair (`results/wing_element_anatomy_2026-09-30.json`). Bold clears the preregistered +0.15 bar on both seeds. {#tbl-nb-wing-element-anatomy}

On the 210-wing rung every class is within 0.08 of the whole surface on
both seeds and no two seeds agree on the sign of any excess: the deficit
has no element. On the fixed-angle rung the slat carries it, +0.16 and
+0.26 on the whole slat and +0.28 and +0.38 on the slat outside the gap
band; the slat is 3% of the area and about 17% of both models' error,
so removing its excess entirely would move the whole-surface ratio by a
few hundredths. The flap and the gap band, which the five-wing pilot put
at 1.37 / 1.30 and 1.83 / 1.80, read below or at the whole surface on
every seed of both rungs.

**Verdict.** H1 is refuted on the 210-wing rung and the pilot's
prediction (flap and gap band) is refuted on both: on the rung that
matters the excess is uniform over elements as it is over curvature
(H3). The slat on the fixed-angle rung is a real, two-seed location of a
small part of the excess, and the only one found; the five-wing pilot was
a sample of five. With H1 and H2 both uniform on the 210-wing rung, the
mechanism lane that WING-MECH was to pick has no local target: what
separates the models on the wings is spread over the whole surface, which
is what the pose-prior diagnostic (@sec-pose-prior in the book) and the
scaling with cases already say.

**What is next.** The six unlabelled wings are in a third resume sweep
(job 970796); the artifact is re-reduced when they land and the numbers
above are replaced, not appended. The per-cell predictions
(`highlift/anatomy_preds`, about 30 GB) are deleted after that. WING-MECH
closes with this entry; a mechanism lane is not scheduled.

## 2026-10-02 — Verdict, POISSON-8448-EQ: at equal epochs (500) on 8,448 Poisson cases GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA is 0.50 (0.38 / 0.69 per seed), so the crossover of the equal-step ladder is confirmed and is not a step-count artifact; ISLA's seed spread (0.050 / 0.030) persists at convergence {#sec-nb-poisson-8448-equal-epoch}

**Setting.** The same-snapshot OLBC ladder (@sec-nb-olbc-ref-ladder-verdict)
trains its 8,448-case rung for 120 epochs so that the optimizer-step count
matches the 512 and 2,048 rungs; there GeoTransolver-512 overtook ISLA
(0.52, per seed 0.37 / 0.80) with both models still descending and ISLA's
two seeds 1.9x apart. Ruling 3 of 2026-09-30
(@sec-nb-ruling-fixed-mesh-2026-09-30) bought one equal-epoch pair to
settle whether the crossover survives convergence: ISLA reference and
GeoTransolver-512, both at 500 epochs, two seeds, the last fixed-mesh lane.
Bar: above 1.0 on both seeds reverses the reading, below 0.9 on both
confirms it.

**Instrument.** `pc_poisson_ref_n8448_e500` and
`pc_poisson_gt512_n8448_e500`, seeds 42 and 43, code_v11 + recipe_v4,
20,000 nodes (every node of the fixed mesh), float32 relative L2 of $u$ on
the 256 held-out cases; reducer
`results/poisson8448_equal_epoch_reduce_2026-10-02.py`, artifact
`results/poisson8448_equal_epoch_2026-10-02.json`.

**What we saw.** ISLA 0.0503 / 0.0300, GeoTransolver-512 0.0192 / 0.0207;
GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA 0.50 on seed means, 0.38 and 0.69 per seed, both
below 0.9. Against the 120-epoch rung (ISLA 0.073 / 0.039,
GeoTransolver-512 0.029) both models gained from the extra epochs by about
the same factor, so the ratio did not move (0.52 to 0.50), and ISLA's
seeds stayed 1.7x apart where GeoTransolver-512's agree within 8%.

**Verdict.** Confirmed: on the largest fixed-mesh Poisson rung
GeoTransolver-512 is twice as accurate as the reference ISLA at equal
epochs as at equal steps. The seed spread is ISLA's, not the budget's:
the two reference seeds converge to errors 1.7x apart on a problem whose
geometry carries no information, which is the fixed-mesh regime Peter
deprioritized (ruling 4). Chapter 12 states the equal-epoch ratio beside
the ladder. POISSON-8448-EQ is DONE and no further fixed-mesh lane is
scheduled.

## 2026-10-02 — Preregistration, CHAR: the characterization campaign on the frozen architecture. Every benchmark re-run under the mesh-native class only, on seven geometry-varying datasets, with one 80 GB reference configuration per architecture and two realism protocols (uniform point clouds, rotated and translated validation) per dataset and model; fixed-mesh datasets leave the book {#sec-nb-char-prereg}

**Setting (Peter, 2026-10-02).** "Let's pause the architectural
modifications, since I think we're set on this front." The adopted class
(@sec-nb-proto-cond-2-adopted) is frozen. What follows is characterization:
the benchmark record is rebuilt from lanes of this class only, so that no
static-prototype, tensor-path or earlier-snapshot lane is load-bearing. No
new dataset enters except AeroZoo, when Peter says it is ready.

**Datasets and tasks.** DrivAerML (surface; volume), HighLiftAeroML
(surface on the 510-case medium set; volume), AirfRANS (interior, two
dimensions), Shift-SUV (surface), Tensile2D (interior, two dimensions,
solids), the bracket lug (interior, solids), DeepJEB++ (surface, solids).
OLBC is the one fixed-mesh set: a fixed mesh is unrealistic for almost any
engineering case and does not exercise discretization independence, so it
is not mentioned in the book; its chapters, tables and ledger rows are
removed, and the lanes stay on the cluster as provenance.

**Fairness rules.** Boundary conditions enter ISLA as boundary meshes with
per-boundary-cell fields, never as one-hot scalar fields on the interior
mesh; every dataset config is checked against this before its lane runs.
The stored signed distance and its gradient are given to both ISLA and
GeoTransolver, computed from the boundary alone (ISLA's measured best
practice is the stored field, @sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict; nothing
in it needs a volume mesh). No baseline trains with rotation or translation
augmentation: the `augmentations:` block of every dataset config is off for
every architecture. Per-case parameter vectors (the lug's and Tensile2D's
`params`, DeepJEB++'s load type) enter as named rank-0 global fields, one
per component, as the field grammar requires.

**One reference configuration per architecture (REF-80).** The most
accurate configuration that trains within 80 GB of peak device memory per
GPU at the reporting protocol (200,000 cells; 100,000 on AirfRANS), batch
one, bfloat16, the recipe's optimizer. Memory is measured, not estimated:
one profiled real training step per candidate on DrivAerML Surface
(`kernel/char/mem_probe`), the frontier is the set of candidates under 80
GB. For ISLA the candidates spend its memory lead along each axis: width
384 / 512 / 768, 12 / 24 layers, 256 / 512 slices, 200,000 / 400,000 cells.
For GeoTransolver: width 256 / 512 / 1,024 and 12 / 24 layers at 256
slices. For Transolver: width 256 / 512 / 1,024 and 8 / 16 layers. The
frontier candidates train for 500 epochs, two seeds, on DrivAerML Surface
and the 510-case HiLift medium set (two datasets); the reference configuration per
architecture is the candidate with the lowest seed-mean headline error on
both, ties within 3% resolved toward the cheaper step. The learning rate
follows the width rule of @sec-using-lr for ISLA and the recipe defaults
for the baselines. Prediction: ISLA's frontier lies at larger capacity than
the baselines' (its 384 x 12 reference uses 33 GB where GeoTransolver-512
uses about 80), and its best spend is width before depth (the capacity
ladders of @sec-capacity), with 400,000 cells neutral above 200,000 (the
cells law of @sec-nb-isocost-verdict).

**Lanes.** For every dataset and task, the three reference configurations
train for 500 epochs, two seeds each, at the reporting protocol. Scoring
in float32 on the held-out split under three protocols: (i) the native
validation mesh, as every earlier lane; (ii) the uniform point cloud,
every validation case resampled by area-weighted (surface) or
volume-weighted (interior) uniform sampling of the same cell budget, which
is what a user gets from an STL without a simulation mesh (the draw of
@sec-nb-trainarea-dr-verdict); (iii) the rotated and translated
validation set, every case under one random rotation and translation per
case (the pose test of @sec-pose-prior, now on every dataset). Ratios are
baseline ÷ ISLA per field. Prediction: ISLA is near parity on (i) and
ahead on (ii) and (iii) on every dataset; a baseline that holds its (i)
error on (iii) within 3% refutes the pose reading for that dataset.

**Book.** Results are organized by dataset, one chapter each with the
same layout: several samples (geometry, boundary conditions with their
types and values, global variables, the predicted fields), the diversity
of the set, the three-protocol table for the three architectures, the
training-cases ladder where one exists, and the cost line. The scaling
chapter stays. Chapter 3 absorbs chapter 9; chapter 5 absorbs the dataset
appendix; chapter 1 separates the boundary-to-field problem from the
surface task; chapter 4 shows each stage in code; chapter 2 extends the
routing pictures to more datasets.

**Order.** (0) the file-count quota and the mesh-native configs for
Shift-SUV, DeepJEB++, the lug, Tensile2D and HiLift volume; (1) REF-80
probes, then the frontier lanes; (2) the dataset lanes under the three
reference configurations; (3) the three scorings; (4) the book. Each step
has its own entry and ledger row.

## 2026-10-02 — Status, CHAR step 0: four datasets run through the mesh-native recipe under all three architectures (12 of 12 smoke lanes to a metric); HiLift volume has no volume targets on the cluster and leaves the campaign; the reference-frontier memory probes read eager memory only, so the frontier is measured from one-epoch real lanes; Tensile2D is geometry-varying, not fixed-mesh {#sec-nb-char-configs-2026-10-02}

**Configs (a fresh agent, brief in the session record).** DeepJEB++, the
lug, Tensile2D and Shift-SUV each trained one epoch at 20,000 cells under
ISLA, GeoTransolver and Transolver with augmentation off and produced a
validation metric (lanes `cc_smoke_*`, jobs 974975 to 975002). What it
took: a `SplitGlobalVector` recipe transform (a per-case parameter vector
standardized and split into named rank-0 global fields: the lug's four
parameters, Tensile2D's six, DeepJEB++'s load-type one-hot; the retired
standardization transform the dataset configs still referenced no longer
existed), ISLA configs `isla_lug`, `isla_tensile2d` (two-dimensional,
`RestrictToPlane` first) and `isla_surface_deepjebpp` with boundary
conditions as boundary-cell fields, Transolver configs for the three solids
sets, `SqueezeScalarFields` on the stored one-column signed distance, and
the lug's boundary pressure scaled to order one. The stored signed distance
and its gradient go to ISLA and to both baselines on the interior sets.
One deviation is structural: GeoTransolver and Transolver read Tensile2D's
boundary-condition tags on the interior nodes, because a per-boundary-cell
input is a path they do not have; ISLA reads them on the boundary mesh.
**HiLift volume is excluded**: the cluster copy carries an interior for
31 of 1,800 cases and those interiors are bare point clouds without
targets, so no architecture can be scored on it until a volume conversion
exists.

**REF-80 probes.** Twenty-five profiled training steps on DrivAerML
Surface (kernel/char/probe_*.json) gave peak memory per rank in the eager
path only: the profiler's compile switch did not engage for ISLA (step
223 ms and 44.4 GB for the reference, the eager figures of
@sec-nb-perf-3-verdict), and the recipe compiles every architecture in a
lane (`compile: true`), so the probe over-reads lane memory by an unknown
factor per architecture. Eager, the 80 GB line falls at GeoTransolver
width 256 (78 GB at 200,000 cells; width 512 is 98 GB at 200,000 and 50 GB
at 100,000 cells), Transolver widths 256 and 512 at 200,000 cells (52, 65
GB) and width 1,024 at 100,000 (47 GB), and ISLA at width 512 with 512
slices (64 GB), with width 768, 24 layers and 400,000 cells just over
(82 to 88 GB eager). The frontier is therefore read from real lanes: the
recipe's epoch summary now records the epoch's peak device memory
(maximum over ranks) and wall time, and 19 one-epoch lanes (group `rf1`,
jobs 975278 to 975307) run every candidate as the campaign would.

**Tensile2D is not a fixed-mesh set.** Checked because the dataset chapter
said the shape hardly varies: across eight cases the boundary polyline has
442 to 496 segments, the interior point arrays differ in size and content,
and the specimen waist width (normalized half-domain) runs from 0.41 to
1.37. A job over every case writes the distribution
(`results/tensile2d_geometry_2026-10-02.json`); the chapter sentence is
replaced from it. Tensile2D stays in the campaign.

## 2026-10-03 — Status, CHAR-PROTOCOLS instruments built: `_area` (uniform-on-measure Poisson draw with exact Horvitz-Thompson weights) and `_posed` (keyed rotation plus one-RMS-radius translation, in-plane for planar sets, stress components rotated as a tensor) variants for every campaign dataset, a per-lane protocol scorer, and smoke tests on finished checkpoints: ISLA's posed error equals its native error to three decimals on every centered pipeline, the baselines move 1.1x to 22x; two anomalies opened (a translation crash on AirfRANS, a 6x to 12x area-draw shift of the DrivAerML Volume model) {#sec-nb-char-protocols-instruments}

**Setting.** The characterization campaign (@sec-nb-char-prereg) scores
every lane under three protocols: the native mesh draw, a uniform-on-the-
surface point-cloud draw ("what an STL gives without a volume mesh"), and
the validation cases in a random rigid pose. The instruments existed only
for DrivAerML Surface (POSE-BENCH and TRAIN-AREA-DR). A fresh agent built
them for every campaign dataset; the brief and the full report are in the
session record.

**What was built.** In `recipe_v8/datasets/`, `<base>_area.yaml` and
`<base>_posed.yaml` beside every campaign base yaml (DrivAerML Surface and
Volume, HiLift medium, AirfRANS 2-D and 3-D, Shift-SUV, Tensile2D 2-D and
3-D, lug, DeepJEB++), identical to the base except the protocol transform.
The area variant draws from a one-million-cell pool with
`PoissonBiasedSubsampleMesh(weight_mode=area)` in place of the native
subsampling, on whatever the pipeline subsamples (the boundary surface; the
interior point clouds carry no cell measure and are untouched; where the
boundary is kept whole, as on AirfRANS, Tensile2D and the lug, the area
variant is the identity by construction). The posed variant applies
`FixedRandomPose(salt=0, translate=1.0)` as the first transform: the
POSE-BENCH keyed SO(3) rotation (its stream unchanged, verified by digest
over 503 keys) plus a translation of one RMS point radius in a keyed
direction; planar problems rotate in their plane only (`axis: 2` for the
3-D-stored Tensile2D and AirfRANS, placed before `RestrictToPlane` so the
2-D and 3-D variants of one dataset receive the identical angle), and
Tensile2D's component-stored stresses rotate as a tensor
(`symmetric_tensor_fields`). The recipe's `CenterMesh` removes the
translation on the external-aero and DeepJEB++ pipelines; AirfRANS,
Tensile2D and the lug have no centering step, so there the translation
reaches the model. The scorer `kernel/char/protocol_eval.sbatch` evaluates
a finished lane under the three protocols from the fleet manifest
(`protocol_launch.sh <run_id>`; reducer `protocol_table.py`), writing to
`evals_char/<run>/<protocol>/`. Local source change: 335 recipe tests pass
(d32aee9b4).

**Smoke results (finished or interim checkpoints; ratios against the
native protocol).** ISLA reference on DrivAerML Surface (`v18_dr_ref`):
area 0.999 / 1.019 (pressure / wall shear), posed 1.000 / 1.000. ISLA on
DrivAerML Volume (two seeds): posed 1.000; area 5.9 to 11.9 on every field.
ISLA on HiLift medium (epoch 97): area 1.003 / 1.006, posed 1.003 / 1.002.
ISLA on AirfRANS: area identity; rotation-only 1.000; the full posed run
crashes at validation sample 52 (below). The one-epoch smoke checkpoints of
Shift-SUV and DeepJEB++ read posed 1.000 for ISLA against 2.86 / 1.61
(GeoTransolver / Transolver) on Shift-SUV and 1.23 / 1.14 on DeepJEB++;
interim DrivAerML Surface baselines (epochs 79 and 125) read area 6.5 / 5.5
and posed 17 / 22. The lug and Tensile2D smoke checkpoints move under
rotation for every architecture (ISLA 1.15 and 1.45), the frame-component
territory of @sec-nb-solids-frame-interim; one-epoch checkpoints carry no accuracy
reading, so these rows wait for the campaign lanes.

**Two anomalies.** (1) ISLA's geometry path raised a CUDA
index-out-of-bounds on AirfRANS when the case is translated by one RMS
radius (rotation alone and the native frame complete all 200 cases).
Localized and fixed as a bug (a57f72227): the nearest-boundary search's
CUDA backend (cuML brute force) evaluates the squared distance in its
expanded float32 form, and for an interior query within about 1e-4 of the
wall at unit scale that form has no resolution left, the candidate is
dropped and the query keeps the library's sentinel (index -1), which the
following gather read out of bounds. Six of the 200 posed validation cases
carry 1 to 150 such queries; none of the native cases does, and the pose
only changes which near-wall values cancel (the posed interior RMS radius
is 0.85 to 1.75, so this is not a large-coordinate effect). The fix
re-searches exactly the sentinel queries by the difference form and
leaves every resolved index as returned, so inputs the backend resolves
are unchanged by construction; verified bit-identical in float32 on native
AirfRANS samples and a DrivAerML Volume sample under the same checkpoints,
with regression tests (23 of 23 on GB300 against the patched snapshot;
8 of the new tests fail against code_v18, as they should). The snapshot
with the fix is code_v19 (verify job 997426: 827 passed, 1 failed; the
failure is the fused-kernel fullgraph gradient check at 2.3e-5 against
its 1e-5 bar on one projection weight, and the same test fails
identically on an untouched code_v18 in the same job, so it is a
run-to-run tolerance of the fused kernel's atomics, not the fix). Observed on the way: the same float32 expansion returns a
wrong in-range nearest boundary cell for 0.45% of the near-wall queries on
native AirfRANS data and 0.70% on translated data, and which queries are
wrong depends on absolute position. That is the whole of ISLA's apparent
translation dependence: under code_v19 the posed AirfRANS row reads
1.001 / 1.063 / 1.040 (eddy viscosity / pressure / velocity) and the
translation-only variant 1.001 / 1.071 / 1.046, while rotation alone
reads 1.000; with the exact difference-form search in place of the
library's, native and translated agree to the fourth decimal
(0.03164 / 0.03315 / 0.01717 against 0.03164 / 0.03316 / 0.01717) and
the native error itself moves by 0.1% (`results/campaigns_2026-10-02/
char/infer_exact_nn.py`, `evals_char_smoke/_tr/`). So the trained
function is translation-invariant and the library search is not. **The
search is replaced by an exact one (0b43b42b2, snapshot code_v20)**: the
class specifies the nearest boundary cell, the library returned a wrong
one for 0.45% of near-wall queries, and no option of the installed
library reaches an unexpanded distance. The replacement is a Triton
streaming-minimum kernel (any dimension, O(1) memory, ties to the
smallest index like `argmin`; a chunked exact torch path without Triton),
measured against a float64 brute force with zero wrong indices on every
case: 0.20 ms against the library's 4.2 ms on AirfRANS (100,000 queries x
858 segments), 68.6 against 36.3 ms at 200,000 x 200,000 in 3-D (+32 ms
on the ~180 ms training step of the volume task, the price of
correctness; the chunked difference form costs 834 ms and `cdist` 46 s at
that size). On the trained checkpoints the native errors move by at most
0.01% (AirfRANS 0.033151 / 0.017170 / 0.031641; DrivAerML Volume
0.040675 / 0.064772 / 0.087934) and the translation gap on AirfRANS falls
from 7.2% / 4.6% to 0.015% / 0.006% (pressure / velocity). The a57f72227
sentinel repair is removed with the library call. Tests tightened to zero
mismatches (190 passed locally and on GB300). Lanes trained before this
entry used the library search; the campaign scores every lane with the
exact one (protocol and `cl_` scorers map to code_v20), which changes
their native numbers by the 0.01% above.
(2) The DrivAerML Volume model's error grows 6x to
12x when the boundary tokens are drawn area-proportionally with exact
Horvitz-Thompson weights, while the Surface model is unchanged under the
same construction. The control (same Poisson path, uniform inclusion,
`drivaer_ml_volume_reference_unifdraw.yaml`) reproduces the native error
to the third decimal on both tasks (Volume 0.0882 / 0.0408 / 0.0649
against native 0.0879 / 0.0407 / 0.0648 for eddy viscosity / pressure /
velocity; Surface 0.0433 / 0.0682 against 0.0433 / 0.0679), and the
structural check through the recipe's own loader shows the control draws
what the reader draws (200,296 cells, raw-area sum 0.0163, measure spread
11,849x against the native 200,000, 0.0162, 18,222x) while the area
variant changes only the inclusion law (198,620 cells, raw-area sum
0.0606, spread 6.4x). **So the instrument is clean and the shift is a
property of the trained volume model**: under the area-proportional
boundary law its interior error is 0.519 / 0.403 / 0.480 (5.9x / 9.9x /
7.4x, both seeds within 20% of each other), where the surface model reads
1.02x on wall shear and 1.00x on pressure. The interior readout therefore
depends on the boundary token law in a way the surface readout does not;
the mechanism is not measured here (candidates: the interior queries'
attention over boundary tokens weights by measure, and the area law moves
the tokens from the fine-meshed curved features to the flat panels). The
campaign records it as the volume model's uniform-draw column; the
baselines' volume numbers under the same protocol come with CHAR-LANES.
A first version of the control still carried the area law (a text
substitution that did not match) and reproduced the area numbers to four
decimals; the structural check caught it before any reading was taken.

## 2026-10-03 — Status, CHAR-LANES Tensile2D scored (first campaign task): at the reference configurations ISLA ties GeoTransolver on the stress components (σ11 0.0086 against 0.0086, σ22 0.0072 against 0.0078, σ12 0.0108 against 0.0111) and trails on displacement (0.0093 against 0.0056) and plastic strain (0.279 against 0.145); the uniform point cloud is the identity here; under the in-plane pose every architecture, ISLA included, falls to the mean-field level, an anomaly under diagnosis {#sec-nb-char-tensile2d-interim}

**Setting.** The six Tensile2D lanes of CHAR-LANES (@sec-nb-char-lanes-launched;
400 training specimens, 100 validation, 500 epochs, every node; ISLA width 768
with the symmetric-tensor stress head, GeoTransolver and Transolver width 1,024
reading the boundary-condition tags on the interior nodes, two seeds each)
finished first, in under three hours, and were scored natively and under the
three protocols (`results/char/tensile2d.json`,
`results/campaigns_2026-10-02/char/cl/metrics/cl_t2d_*`).

**What we saw (seed means over 100 validation specimens, float32).** Native:
ISLA σ11 / σ22 / σ12 / displacement / plastic strain 0.0086 / 0.0072 / 0.0108 /
0.0093 / 0.279; GeoTransolver 0.0086 / 0.0078 / 0.0111 / 0.0056 / 0.145;
Transolver 0.0106 / 0.0088 / 0.0123 / 0.0053 / 0.227. So the frozen class at
its reference width closes the stress gap this dataset used to show
(@sec-nb-solids-frame-interim recorded GeoTransolver-512 ahead on every component by
about 2x under the earlier class): ISLA now ties or leads on all three stress
components and trails by 1.7x on displacement and 1.9x on the cumulated plastic
strain. The uniform point-cloud column equals the native one for every
architecture, as it must: the boundary polyline is kept whole and the interior
is a point cloud without cell measures, so the area draw is the identity on this
dataset. **Posed (in-plane rotation plus translation): ISLA 0.81 / 0.74 / 1.14 /
0.79, GeoTransolver 1.09 / 1.23 / 1.04 / 0.98, Transolver 0.97 / 0.91 / 0.98 /
0.91.** The baselines' numbers are the expected failure of lab-frame inputs
trained without augmentation. ISLA's are not expected, and the diagnosis
found two recipe defects, neither in the model. Rotation alone reproduces the
posed numbers (0.81 / 0.74 / 1.15 / 0.79) and translation alone reproduces the
native ones, so the pose pipeline's translation and ISLA's translation
invariance are both fine. A direct model-level check (one validation
specimen rotated by 90 degrees after the native pipeline, predictions rotated
back) shows the displacement head equivariant to roundoff, so its posed error
of 0.79 is the pipeline: the recipe normalizes displacement with a nonzero
lab-frame mean (−3.4e-4, 1.05e-3; 1.3 standard deviations), and a vector
normalized about a lab-frame mean is not equivariant (the posed normalized
target is R u_n + (R m − m)/s, an offset no equivariant model can emit;
DrivAerML and DeepJEB++ vector means are zero, which is why their posed
columns match). The stress components fail for a second reason: the
campaign's ISLA Tensile2D configuration declared sig11 / sig22 / sig12 as
three rank-0 heads ("laboratory frame, as the dataset stores them"), i.e.
scalars, which are invariant under rotation and cannot follow a rotated
tensor target; the symmetric rank-2 head of @sec-nb-rankio-prereg exists for this
and was not used, and the stress normalization is per component (sig22 mean
57.7 MPa, three different standard deviations), which is not equivariant
either. **Decision (2026-10-03): every rank>=1 target in the campaign is
normalized with zero mean and one isotropic standard deviation (only
Tensile2D violated this), ISLA's Tensile2D configuration predicts the stress
as the symmetric tensor, the baselines keep their three scalar components
over the same normalized numbers, and the six Tensile2D lanes are re-run as
`cl_t2dz_*`; the first six lanes stay in the record as the mis-specified
configuration.** Applied the same evening: the isotropic stress scale over the 400
training specimens (3.74 million nodes) is 37.8 MPa (root mean of
(σ11² + σ22² + 2σ12²)/4; raw per-component means −0.1 / 57.7 / 0.0 and
standard deviations 28.5 / 32.0 / 16.9), displacement keeps its isotropic
8.22e-4 with the mean set to zero; the nine Tensile2D yamls carry the new
normalization (backups `.pre_eq`), the five 2-D ones declare the stress as
one symmetric tensor target, `isla_tensile2d.yaml` predicts
`stress: {rank: 2, symmetric: true}`, and the recipe's component selector
accepts 2x2 tensors (it hard-coded 3x3; 339 recipe tests). Three one-epoch
smoke lanes passed and the six lanes `cl_t2dz_*` run (jobs 1003874 to
1003882). The model-level check on the corrected configuration (one-epoch
checkpoint): a 90-degree rotation reproduces every field, the stress tensor
included, to roundoff. A 37-degree rotation or a one-radius translation
changes this one-epoch checkpoint's outputs by 5% to 30% (identical under
the exact and the library search, so not the nearest search); the trained
first-configuration checkpoint moved 1.4% at 37 degrees and not at all under
translation at protocol level, so the sensitivity shrinks with training.
The candidate mechanism is the nearest-boundary normal's discontinuity at
the specimen's corners (a 1e-7 coordinate perturbation can swap the nearest
segment for near-equidistant queries); it is a hypothesis for the trained
`cl_t2dz` lanes' posed column to confirm or refute.

path emits as `stress_l2` and which the baselines' component datasets now
receive as a derived metric so the three arms are compared on the same

where DrivAerML and AirfRANS read 1.000; this is the generic-angle
sensitivity of @sec-nb-char-tensile2d-interim measured at protocol level,
and the corner-normal hypothesis stands as the candidate mechanism (the
specimen's polyline has sharp corners; the nearest-boundary normal is
discontinuous there). On plastic strain ISLA (0.415) trails GeoTransolver
