## 2026-10-04 — Status, CHAR on the GINOT lug scored: ISLA 768 leads on the native mesh (von Mises 0.0021 against GeoTransolver 0.0026 and Transolver 0.0027, ratios 1.24 and 1.29), the uniform point cloud is the identity (boundary kept whole), and under the 3-D rigid pose ISLA reads 0.0041, twice its native error, where the baselines read 0.98 and 1.02; the 2x shift is under attribution {#sec-nb-char-lug-interim}

**Setting.** The six lug lanes of CHAR-LANES (@sec-nb-char-lanes-launched; 2,400
training lugs, 600 test, 500 epochs, every node, 20,000-cell cap; ISLA width 768
with the boundary labels and pressure as boundary scalars and the four design
parameters as global scalars; GeoTransolver and Transolver width 1,024 reading the
labels on the interior nodes) finished and were scored natively and under the
three protocols (`results/char/lug.json`).

**What we saw (von Mises relative L2, seed means over 600 test lugs).** Native:
ISLA 0.0021, GeoTransolver 0.0026, Transolver 0.0027 (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA
1.24, Transolver ÷ ISLA 1.29), ISLA's only native lead on a solid in the
campaign. Uniform point cloud = native for every architecture (the lug surface
is a few thousand triangles, kept whole; the interior is a point cloud). Rotated
and translated (uniform SO(3) plus one RMS radius, no centering step in this
pipeline): ISLA 0.0041, GeoTransolver 0.98, Transolver 1.02. The baselines'
numbers are the expected lab-frame failure; **ISLA's output, a scalar that a
rigid motion cannot change, moved by 2x**, far above the 5% residual of
Tensile2D (@sec-nb-char-interior-tensile2d) and the exact result on AirfRANS
and the DrivAerML tasks. **Attribution (same day).** Rotation alone and translation alone each
produce the shift (seed 42: rotation-only 1.65x, translation-only 1.92x, both
2.08x; seed 43: 1.48x / 1.72x / 1.89x), so it is not additive and not a
frame-dependent input: every input the lug configuration reads (boundary
labels and pressure as scalars, boundary geometry, the stored signed distance
and its rotated gradient, four scalar globals) is transformed consistently,
and rotating any one part alone breaks the problem by O(1), as it must for a
relative-geometry model. A model-level check on one lug (native error 0.14%)
settles it: an exact rigid motion (90 degrees about an axis, a coordinate
permutation in float32) changes the prediction by 1e-4, every float-inexact
motion changes it at the 1e-3 to 1e-2 level (37 degrees 0.0075, one-radius
translation 0.0017, both 0.0128), and **a random coordinate jitter of 1e-7
relative with no motion at all changes it by 0.011, the same at 1e-6 and
1e-5**: a discontinuity, not smooth roundoff amplification. The
discontinuity is the nearest-boundary-sample construction: on this
structured finite-element mesh 76% of the interior nodes are equidistant
from two boundary centroids to 1e-4 relative (35% to 1e-7), so which sample
is nearest is decided by sub-roundoff noise; under the translation 23% of
the nearest indices change and 62 nodes per lug jump to a face more than 30
degrees away, an O(1) change of the direction feature, which attention
spreads over the field. The library and the exact search give identical
numbers, compilation has no effect, and a float64 forward with float64
transforms reduces the posed change to 3e-3 but moves the native prediction
itself by 1% (0.0122 against 0.0014): the trained lug model's output depends
on arithmetic precision at the percent level through the same tie-breaking.
The lug's native error is 0.14%, so a 0.1% to 1% perturbation response reads
as 1.5x to 2x; on DrivAerML (native 4%) the same effect is invisible, which
is why posed = native there, and the 5% shift of Tensile2D
(@sec-nb-char-interior-tensile2d) is the same mechanism's likely footprint
on another structured mesh. **Nothing in the pipeline changes; this is a
numerical property of the frozen class** (the nearest boundary sample is a
discontinuous function of the query position, with an O(1) normal flip at
ties). The candidate fix is a measure-weighted average over near-tied
samples in the geometry construction, a post-campaign change. The chapter
reports the 2x as measured with this mechanism.

best on slices and width together (the wing ordering), and gains nothing on
the cars from any axis (seven candidates within 5%). GeoTransolver's accuracy

interchangeable within 3% on both datasets, and the 200,000-cell candidates
at widths 256 and 512 are 8% to 29% behind them, so for Transolver cells are
better traded for width or depth.

GeoTransolver on plastic strain on both seeds and trails Transolver there.

The standing on Tensile2D is the clearest case against ISLA in the campaign:

## 2026-10-05 — CHAR lug under the final references: GeoTransolver width 256 leads ISLA width 512 with 512 slices by 1.9x on von Mises stress (0.0021 against 0.0040) under the float32 protocol; LUG-PREC shows the gap is a precision sensitivity of the final ISLA model (bfloat16 0.0035 for both ISLA configurations and 0.0038 to 0.0044 for the baselines; float32 lowers every lane to 0.0021 to 0.0025 except the 512-slice ISLA, which reads worse in float32 on 20% and 42% of the cases) {#sec-nb-char-lug-final}

**Setting.** The lug interior task (GINOT plastic lug, 600 test cases,
5,000 to 15,000 nodes per case, scored whole) re-run under the final
reference configurations (@sec-nb-ref80-verdict): `cl_r_lug_isla` (ISLA width
512 with 512 slices, 3.75e-4), `cl_r_lug_gt` (GeoTransolver width 256),
`cl_r_lug_t` (Transolver width 512 with 16 layers), 500 epochs, two seeds,
float32 under the three protocols (`results/char/lug.json`). First pass
(ISLA width 768, baselines width 1,024): @sec-nb-char-lug-interim.

**What we saw (seed means; per seed; von Mises relative L2).** Native:
ISLA 0.0040 (0.0035 / 0.0046), GeoTransolver 0.0021 (0.0023 / 0.0019),
Transolver 0.0022 (0.0023 / 0.0020). Point cloud = native (whole mesh).
Rotated and translated: ISLA 0.0065 (0.0070 / 0.0060), 1.6x its native
error; GeoTransolver 0.94, Transolver 1.02. **Against the first pass the
standing reverses**: ISLA width 768 read 0.0021 (both seeds 0.0021) and led
GeoTransolver width 1,024 (0.0026) by 1.24x; ISLA width 512 with 512 slices
reads 0.0040 and trails GeoTransolver width 256 (0.0021) by 1.9x, with the
two ISLA seeds 30% apart.

**The anomaly and the instrument.** The training-time validation error
(bfloat16, the training precision, every tenth epoch) of the two ISLA
configurations is identical: 0.0035 for the width-768 lanes and 0.0035 /
0.0036 for the width-512 lanes, flat from epoch 240 to 499 on all four
(`runs/cl*_lug_isla_*/metrics.jsonl`, val_summary rows). A 2x difference in
the float32 scorer between two models with the same bfloat16 validation
error says the scorer's precision, not the training, separates them. LUG-PREC
(`kernel/char/lug_prec.sbatch`, `results/char/lug_prec_2026-10-05.py` /
`.json`) scores eight lug lanes with the same scorer in bfloat16 and
compares per case with the float32 record. **Result.** In bfloat16 every
lane reads 0.0035 to 0.0044: ISLA 768 0.0035 / 0.0035, ISLA 512 with 512
slices 0.0035 / 0.0035, GeoTransolver 0.0038 (1,024) and 0.0041 (256),
Transolver 0.0044 (1,024) and 0.0043 (512 x 16); the bfloat16 output
resolution sets an error floor near 0.0035 on this task, whose exact
errors are below it. In float32 the baselines and the width-768 ISLA drop to
0.0021 to 0.0025 (float32 lowers the per-case error by more than 1.5x on 63%
to 91% of the 600 cases and raises it by more than 1.5x on 0% to 1.5%). **The
width-512, 512-slice ISLA does not**: float32 reads 0.0035 and 0.0046, it
lowers the per-case error by more than 1.5x on 41% and 49% of the cases and
raises it by more than 1.5x on 20% and 42%, with worst cases at 0.0081
against 0.0029 and 0.0131 against 0.0031. The two ISLA configurations
compute the same bfloat16 function to the resolution of the validation
metric and different float32 functions.

**Mechanism (measured in @sec-nb-char-lug-interim, applied here).** The lug
is the dataset where the nearest-boundary-sample distance is tied within
1e-4 for 76% of the nodes and a 1e-7 coordinate jitter changes 1.1% of the
output; which boundary sample a node selects depends on rounding, and the
precision of the forward pass is one more rounding. The 512-slice model is
the one whose outputs move most when the selection changes; why it is more
sensitive than the 256-slice width-768 model is not measured here (a
hypothesis: twice the prototypes, twice the slice boundaries a changed
selection can cross). The posed 1.6x shift of the same model is the same
mechanism under a different perturbation.

**Standing under the protocol.** The reporting protocol is float32, and
under it GeoTransolver width 256 ÷ ISLA = 0.52 and Transolver 0.54, both
leading on both seeds; the chapter states this standing. It also states
what LUG-PREC measured: the deficit is a numerical sensitivity of the trained
model's nearest-sample geometry on a tied mesh, not a capacity or training
difference, and it is the clearest measured instance of the limit named in
@sec-nb-char-lug-interim. The fix candidates (a soft or k-nearest boundary
sample, a tie-breaking rule that is a continuous function of the
coordinates) are post-campaign architecture changes and wait for Peter.

**Cost (one epoch, four GB300 ranks, bfloat16; `cs_r_lug_*`).** ISLA 8.9
GiB, 184 s; GeoTransolver 6.1 GiB, 85 s; Transolver 10.0 GiB, 79 s. ISLA's
epoch is 2.2x the baselines' mean on this 5,000 to 15,000-node task.

## 2026-10-05 — CHAR DeepJEB++: every ISLA campaign lane sits at the mean-field plateau (von Mises 0.94, displacement 0.82 against 0.46 / 0.20 for the baselines); the training loss rises from 0.024 to 0.085 within the first 4 to 12 epochs on all four lanes, both configurations, both seeds; the September R1 lane at 5e-4 reached 0.44 / 0.19; four diagnostic lanes launched (JEB-PLATEAU) {#sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau}

**Setting.** DeepJEB++ (12,451 training brackets, 5,540 clean test files,
50,040 surface cells per case scored whole, 40 epochs) is the eighth
campaign task. The first-pass lanes (`cl_jeb_*`, DrivAerML-half references:
ISLA width 768 at 3.75e-4, GeoTransolver and Transolver width 1,024) are
trained and scored under the three protocols
(`results/char/deepjeb_surface.json`, written from them because the
final-reference lanes `cl_r_jeb_*` are at epoch 21 to 33 of 40).

**What we saw.** Native (seed means; von Mises / displacement):
GeoTransolver 0.457 (0.4565 / 0.4571) / 0.202; Transolver 0.475 / 0.219;
**ISLA 0.945 (0.903 / 0.986) / 0.824 (0.734 / 0.913)**, the level of a model
that predicts the mean field. Rotated and translated: ISLA unchanged to four
digits, GeoTransolver 1.13 / 1.46, Transolver 1.26 / 1.70. The scoring is
not the cause: the training-time validation (bfloat16, every second epoch,
`runs/cl*_jeb_isla_*/metrics.jsonl`) shows the same thing with its history.
Width 768, seed 42: 0.60 / 0.37 at epoch 0, 0.60 at epoch 6, 0.96 / 1.20 at
epoch 12, 0.90 / 0.85 at epoch 39; seed 43: 0.59 at epoch 0, 0.89 / 1.06 at
epoch 6, 0.99 / 1.20 at epoch 39. The final-reference lanes (width 512 with
512 slices, 3.75e-4), in flight: seed 42 0.60 at epoch 0, 0.90 / 1.04 at
epoch 4, 1.02 / 1.17 at epoch 30; seed 43 0.60, 0.93 / 1.18 at epoch 4, 0.99
/ 1.09 at epoch 32. The training loss follows: 0.024 at epoch 0 on every
ISLA lane, then 0.067 to 0.085 from epoch 4 to 12 onward and flat (seed 42
of the width-768 lane recovers to 0.041 by epoch 37 and its validation to
0.90 / 0.85, a partial return). GeoTransolver and Transolver on the same
data descend monotonically (train loss 0.025 to 0.004 and 0.006;
validation 0.61 to 0.46 and 0.46).

**This is the mean-field plateau measured before, on this dataset.** The
September DeepJEB++ lanes (@sec-nb-deepjeb-e40-verdict's `jb_*` group, code_ref,
static prototypes) put ISLA R1 (width 384, 12 layers, 256 slices, 5e-4) at
0.441 / 0.187 after 40 epochs, ahead of GeoTransolver width 512 (0.464 /
0.201), and ISLA R2 (24 layers at 5e-4) at 1.01 / 1.16, the plateau, which a
re-run at 2.5e-4 left (@sec-nb-deepjeb-r2-rate-verdict). The signature then and now is the one named in
@sec-nb-routingsat-verdict: the training loss rises to a flat value several times
its epoch-0 value within a few epochs and the model outputs the mean field.
Every ISLA lane of the campaign on this dataset runs a configuration wider
than R1 at the width rule's rate (3.75e-4 at 512 and at 768), and all four
plateau; the one configuration measured to train on DeepJEB++ is R1 at
5e-4 on the static-prototype class.

**Hypotheses and the deciding lanes (preregistered; four one-GPU-node
smoke lanes of 5 epochs with validation every epoch, `cs_jd_*`, launched
15:05 UTC).** H-rate: the rate ceiling on this dataset lies below the width
rule's value for the wider configurations; prediction: `cs_jd_rate` (width
512 with 512 slices at 1.875e-4, code_v20) does not plateau (validation von
Mises below 0.55 at epoch 4, train loss falling). H-config: R1 trains and the
wider configuration does not, on the current class; prediction: `cs_jd_r1`
(384 / 256 at 5e-4, code_v20) does not plateau. H-proto: the centered
sample-conditioned prototypes adopted on 2026-10-02 (@sec-nb-proto-cond-2-adopted),
which the September lanes did not have, move the ceiling on this dataset;
prediction: `cs_jd_v17` (width 512 with 512 slices at 3.75e-4 on code_v17,
the static-prototype snapshot) does not plateau while the code_v20 lanes
at the same rate did, and `cs_jd_v17r1` (384 / 256 at 5e-4 on code_v17)
reproduces the September training. If `cs_jd_v17` plateaus too, the
prototypes are exonerated and the ceiling is a property of the
configuration on this dataset. The four outcomes are independent; the
plateau appears by epoch 4 to 6 on every lane above, so five epochs decide.

**What is not done.** Chapter 13 is not restated from the plateaued lanes;
a mean-field model has no standing to report. The final-reference lanes
run to completion so the record is whole, and the campaign's DeepJEB++
verdict waits for the diagnosis. If the rate is the cause, the fix is a
rule change (the reference rate is a class default, not a dataset
variant), and it must be decided with Peter.

**Setting.** The four diagnostic lanes preregistered in
@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau finished (5 epochs, validation every epoch,
seed 42, one GB300 node each; `results/char/jd_plateau_2026-10-05.py` /
`.json`, trajectories copied under
`campaigns_2026-10-02/char/jd/`).

**What we saw (validation von Mises at epochs 0 to 4; training loss epoch
0 to epoch 4).** `cs_jd_r1` (width 384, 256 slices, 5e-4, code_v20 with the
centered sample-conditioned prototypes): 0.59, 0.58, **0.96, 0.97, 0.98**;
loss 0.025, 0.017, 0.040, 0.083, 0.090. The plateau, at epoch 2.
`cs_jd_v17r1` (the same configuration and rate on code_v17, static
prototypes): 0.60, 0.57, 0.55, 0.53, 0.52; loss 0.025 to 0.012, descending.
`cs_jd_v17` (width 512, 512 slices, 3.75e-4, code_v17): 0.60, 0.56, 0.53, 0.55,
0.52; loss 0.024 to 0.011. `cs_jd_rate` (width 512, 512 slices, 1.875e-4,

campaign lanes at 3.75e-4 on code_v20 read 0.90 and 0.93 at epoch 4 (final
reference) and 0.52 and 0.58 at epoch 4 then 0.96 and 0.92 at epoch 12
(width 768), and the baselines read 0.54 to 0.56 at epoch 4.

**Reading against the preregistered predictions.** H-config is refuted: the
configuration that trained in September (384 / 256 at 5e-4) plateaus on the
current class, faster than any campaign lane. H-proto is supported on both
of its predictions: the same configuration trains on the static-prototype
snapshot, and the final reference configuration at the rate that plateaued
on the current class trains on the static-prototype snapshot. H-rate is
supported: halving the rate on the current class trains through epoch 4.
**The centered sample-conditioned prototypes adopted on 2026-10-02 lower
the rate ceiling on DeepJEB++** to below 3.75e-4 at width 512 and below 5e-4
at width 384; they did not do so on DrivAerML Surface, DrivAerML Volume or
AirfRANS, where the code_v18 reference lanes trained at the same rates
(@sec-nb-proto-cond-2-adopted). What is particular to DeepJEB++ is not
measured here: 12,451 cases per epoch (28x DrivAerML's 435, so 28x the
optimizer steps per epoch at the same rate), a load-case one-hot in the
global inputs, and a mesh of 50,040 triangles with the degenerate cells
dropped are the candidates.

**Limits of this reading.** One seed per lane; five epochs. The width-768
campaign lane trained to epoch 4 (0.52) and plateaued between epochs 6 and
12, so a lane that trains for five epochs is not shown to train for forty.
Launched to close both gaps: second seeds of the three discriminating lanes
and a 5-epoch code_v20 control at 3.75e-4 (`cs_jd_*_s43`, `cs_jd_v20ref_s43`),
and four 40-epoch lanes (`cl_jd_rate_e40_seed42/43`: width 512 with 512
slices at 1.875e-4 on code_v20; `cl_jd_v17_e40_seed42/43`: the same at
3.75e-4 on code_v17), scored under the campaign protocols when they finish
(about one day). A routing-activity probe of the plateaued `cs_jd_r1`
checkpoint against the healthy `cs_jd_rate` checkpoint (effective slices
per block, routing entropy) is being written for the current class to test
whether the plateau is the routing collapse of @sec-nb-routingsat-verdict.

**What this means for the campaign.** Under the frozen architecture and the
reference rate, ISLA does not train on DeepJEB++; the campaign's DeepJEB++
row is that fact, with the baselines' numbers beside it. Whether the
reference rate changes (a class default, so for every dataset), or the
prototype conditioning is revisited (an architecture change), is Peter's
decision; the 40-epoch lanes supply the numbers either decision needs
(what the final reference reaches on DeepJEB++ at half rate, and what it
reaches with static prototypes at the reference rate).

## 2026-10-05 — Ruling: DeepJEB++ is an explicit exception to the one-reference rule, in the learning rate only; ISLA trains there at 1.875e-4 with every other hyperparameter the reference configuration; the two 40-epoch half-rate lanes become the campaign's DeepJEB++ ISLA arms {#sec-nb-char-deepjeb-rate-ruling}

Peter, on the interim verdict of @sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-interim:
lowering the learning rate alone on one dataset is acceptable as a
per-dataset exception to the one-reference goal. The exception is the
rate and nothing else: width 512, 12 layers, 512 slices, cosine routing,
the centered sample-conditioned prototypes and 200,000 cells stay as on
every dataset; the rate is 1.875e-4, half the width rule's value, because
every ISLA lane at 3.75e-4 on this dataset reached the mean-field plateau
within 4 to 12 epochs and the half-rate lane trained through its
five-epoch test. The recipe's `isla_surface_deepjebpp.yaml` pins 1.875e-4
with this reason; the other ISLA configurations keep 3.75e-4.

The campaign's DeepJEB++ ISLA arms are therefore `cl_jd_rate_e40_seed42`
and `cl_jd_rate_e40_seed43` (launched 2026-10-05, 40 epochs, code_v20), scored
under the three protocols when they finish, against `cl_r_jeb_gt` and
`cl_r_jeb_t` (the final baseline references; GeoTransolver 256 is at epoch
29 to 31 of 40, Transolver 512 x 16 at epoch 21). The reference-rate lanes
`cl_r_jeb_isla_*` complete and are scored as the record of what the
reference rate does on this dataset; `cl_jd_v17_e40_*` (static prototypes
at 3.75e-4) complete as the diagnostic of the prototype conditioning's
rate cost. Chapter 13 is restated from `results/char/deepjeb_surface.json`
when the half-rate lanes are scored (about one day); the chapter states
the exception and its measurement.

## 2026-10-05 — VOL-GEO preregistered: is the volume model's 7x sensitivity to the boundary sampling law the built-in nearest-boundary-token geometry (a bias no quadrature weight can correct) or the slice states formed from the redrawn tokens (a resolution requirement)? Geometry-swap scoring of the Volume reference checkpoints, launched {#sec-nb-char-vol-geo-prereg}

**Setting.** On DrivAerML Volume the final ISLA reference reads 0.0394 /
0.0635 / 0.0876 natively and 0.311 / 0.417 / 0.583 when the boundary tokens
are redrawn area-proportionally with exact Horvitz-Thompson measures, 7.9x
/ 6.6x / 6.6x (@sec-nb-char-volume-final), while the same class on the
Surface task is unchanged by the same draw and a uniform-over-cells redraw
of the Volume boundary leaves the interior error at native
(@sec-nb-char-protocols-instruments). Peter's reading, 2026-10-05: this is a
serious flaw, the discretization invariance prized on the surface breaks
down in the volume. The query-independence program (branch
`psharpe/isla-independent`, RESULTS.md and the pi transcript of 2026-10-02)
reached the same suspect from another side: "a volume point's built-in wall
distance is the distance to the nearest sampled boundary cell. That is a
nearest-sample measure, not a quadrature", and listed a continuous wall
distance as a class fix it did not run.

**Mechanism.** Each interior query carries a built-in geometry computed in
the forward from the boundary tokens (`nearest_boundary_geometry`): the
signed distance to the nearest token and the direction to it, which also
seeds the query's local frame. It is an argmin, not a quadrature; under
the area law the nearest token to a near-wall query moves by the local cell
spacing, exactly where the native mesh is dense, so the query's inputs
change by order one near the wall. Everything else the queries read (slice
states, anchors, prototypes, the query routing mass tied to the total
boundary measure) is a measure-weighted sum, unbiased under the
Horvitz-Thompson weights but of higher variance where the area law thins
the finely meshed features. A bias from the first is a flaw of the class; a
variance from the second is a resolution requirement on the boundary
sample.

**Instrument (`kernel/char/vol_geo/geo_swap.py`, scoring only, no model
change).** The Volume reference checkpoint (`cl_r_vol_isla_seed42`, seed 43
if time allows) scored in float32 on the 48 validation cars under four
conditions: (1) native (control; must reproduce the record per case), (2)
area draw (control), (3) area-draw tokens with the built-in geometry
computed from the native draw's boundary of the same case (the swap), (4)
area-draw tokens with the built-in geometry taken from the stored signed
distance field and its gradient. Also the fraction of queries whose nearest
token changes between the draws and the RMS shift of the built-in distance
within 0.01 L of the wall.

**Predictions (written before the runs).** If the built-in geometry is the
whole mechanism, condition (3) returns to within 10% of native on every
field and (4) does the same or better. If the slice states also carry it,
(3) stays well above native, and the remaining log-ratio is the resolution
component. I expect the first: the lug tie discontinuity and the on-wall
sign flips measured on this class are the same argmin, and the Surface
task, which has no such query input, is invariant under the identical
draw. The fix the first outcome points to is a measure-weighted softmin
geometry (continuous in the sample, exactly refinement-invariant,
converging to the exact distance as its scale shrinks) or dropping the
built-in channel where a stored field is provided; both are architecture
changes and wait for Peter.

## 2026-10-05 — VOL-GEO verdict: the volume model's 7.9x / 6.6x / 6.6x sensitivity to the boundary sampling law is entirely the queries' built-in nearest-boundary-token geometry; with that one input computed from the native draw and every other token redrawn, the error returns to native within 0.4% on every field and both seeds; the slice states carry none of it; the exact stored signed-distance field does not substitute (15x) because the model is calibrated to the sampled distance {#sec-nb-char-vol-geo-verdict}

**Setting and instrument.** @sec-nb-char-vol-geo-prereg. The two Volume
reference checkpoints (`cl_r_vol_isla_seed42/43`) scored in float32 on the 48
validation cars under five conditions by a scoring-time swap of
`nearest_boundary_geometry` alone (`kernel/char/vol_geo/geo_swap.py`,
`results/char/vol_geo_2026-10-05.py` / `.json`; artifacts under
`campaigns_2026-10-02/char/vol_geo/`). The two protocol conditions
reproduce the campaign's per-case scorings to 1e-6 on every case and both
seeds. The native and area datasets drew byte-identical interior point sets
on all 48 cases, so the interior queries, the targets and the stored field
are shared and only the boundary tokens differ.

**What we saw (seed means; pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity; both seeds
in the artifact agree to 0.2%).** Native 0.0394 / 0.0635 / 0.0876. Area draw
0.311 / 0.417 / 0.583, 7.9x / 6.6x / 6.6x. **Area-draw tokens with the
built-in geometry computed from the native draw's boundary: 0.0393 /
0.0634 / 0.0875**, 0.997 / 0.998 / 0.999 of native; the fraction of the
area-draw log-excess removed is 1.001 / 1.001 / 1.000 on the seed means and
1.0005 to 1.0019 per seed. Area-draw tokens with the built-in geometry
replaced by the exact stored signed-distance field and its gradient (sign
matched to the checkpoint's convention): 0.593 / 0.602 / 0.755, 15.1x /
9.5x / 8.6x; native tokens with the stored field: 0.593 / 0.602 / 0.754,
the same to three digits.

**The input shift behind it.** Under the area draw the nearest boundary
centroid changes for 91% of the queries (92% of the 179,000 near-wall
queries, those within 0.01 L of the wall). The built-in distance of a
near-wall query moves by 3e-4 L in RMS, small in length units, but in the
channel the model reads, log of the distance, the RMS shift between the
two draws is 0.85. Against the exact field the sampled distance is biased
and broad: near-wall medians 2.5e-4 L for the native draw, 3.4e-4 L for the
area draw, 1.6e-4 L for the stored field; RMS log ratio of the native
built-in distance to the exact distance 1.5. The direction to the nearest
token has mean cosine 0.72 with the exact gradient, and 0.51 between the
two draws.

**Reading.** The prediction depends on the boundary sample through one
channel, the argmin over tokens that gives each query its distance and
direction to the wall. Everything else the queries read, the slice states,
anchors, prototypes and the routing mass, is a Horvitz-Thompson quadrature
and is invariant to the draw to 0.1%, as the Surface task already showed.
The 7x is a bias of that one input, not a resolution requirement on the
boundary sample. And it is not fixable at scoring time by substituting the
exact distance: the trained model is calibrated to the sampled distance,
whose near-wall statistics (median 1.6x the exact value, 1.5 RMS in log) are
a property of the 200,000-token draw it trained on, so the exact field is as
far out of its training distribution as the area draw is. This is the same
object as the lug tie discontinuity (@sec-nb-char-lug-final) and the on-wall
sign flips of the query-independence program: a nearest-sample selection is
a discontinuous, law-dependent function of the sample.

**What follows.** The fix is a sample-independent query geometry, which is
an architecture change and waits for Peter's decision, with the training
rerun it implies. The two candidates, both quadratures: (a) a
measure-weighted softmin over the boundary tokens for the distance and the
softmin-weighted mean separation for the direction, continuous in the
sample, exactly refinement-invariant and converging to the exact distance
as its scale shrinks; (b) where a stored signed-distance field exists, use
it as the built-in channel and skip the search. Either must be trained in;
the 09-25 INTERNAL-GEOMETRY study measured the built-in channel alone at 14%
to 27% worse on velocity than the stored field alone, so (b) is expected to
gain accuracy as well as invariance where a field exists, and (a) is the
general case. The Volume chapter's limit paragraph and the limits chapter
are restated from this artifact.

## 2026-10-05 — JEB-PLATEAU mechanism: the plateaued lane is a routing collapse; under the sample-conditioned prototypes at 5e-4 half of the blocks route to 1 to 5 effective slices of 256 with coincident anchors, while the half-rate lane keeps 34 to 490 effective slices of 512 in every block {#sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-mechanism}

**Instrument.** `kernel/char/jd_probe/routing_probe_v20.py` (copied under
`campaigns_2026-10-02/char/jd_probe/`): the current class's routing weights
over slices captured per block on the first four test brackets (49,990
tokens each, float32) for the plateaued `cs_jd_r1` (width 384, 256 slices,
5e-4) and the healthy `cs_jd_rate` (width 512, 512 slices, 1.875e-4), at
epochs 4 and 5 (the smoke lanes' earlier checkpoints were pruned, so the
onset epoch is not measured). Statistics as in @sec-nb-routingsat-verdict:
effective number of slices carrying mass (exp of the entropy of the slice
mass distribution), the mean normalized routing entropy per token, the
fraction of slices above 1/(4S) of the mass, and the RMS anchor spread.

**What we saw.** Plateaued lane, epoch 5, per block: effective slices 20,
38, 1.4, 4.9, 12, 4.2, 21, 1.1, 1.4, 13, 3.3, 1.6; routing entropy 0.02 to
0.55; anchor spread 0.005 to 0.04 (anchors nearly coincident) in every block.
Seven of twelve blocks route to one to five slices of 256. Healthy lane,
epoch 5: effective slices 490, 331, 348, 336, 374, 357, 277, 272, 178, 118,
234, 34 of 512; entropy 0.53 to 0.99; anchor spread 0.09 to 0.22 in blocks 1
to 11. The geometric routing bias changes no entropy by more than 0.03 in
either lane. The two lanes differ in width, slice count and rate as well as
in outcome, so this is the signature test, not a matched pair; the
collapse signature is the one measured on DrivAerML in September
(@sec-nb-routingsat-verdict), which cosine routing had removed there.

**Reading.** The DeepJEB++ plateau is the routing collapse: with the
centered sample-conditioned prototypes, cosine routing's bounded logits no
longer prevent the anchors from coinciding and the mass from concentrating
on a few slices at the width rule's rate on this dataset. Why the bound
holds on DrivAerML, HiLift and AirfRANS at the same rates and fails here
(28x the optimizer steps per epoch, a load-case one-hot in the global
inputs, 50,040-cell surfaces) is not measured. The half-rate exception
(@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-rate-ruling) keeps the routing spread; the
static-prototype 40-epoch lanes in flight say whether the prototype
conditioning is the necessary ingredient at 40 epochs as it was at 5.

## 2026-10-06 — SOFT-GEO preregistered: a sample-independent built-in query geometry (the kernel-mean tangent-plane distance and normal of the boundary tokens on the nearest token's side) implemented as `query_geometry="soft"`; AirfRANS first by Peter's decision tree, under a boundary-resampling protocol because the campaign's area protocol is the identity on AirfRANS {#sec-nb-soft-geo-prereg}

**Setting.** VOL-GEO (@sec-nb-char-vol-geo-verdict) measured that the
Volume model's 7.9x / 6.6x / 6.6x sensitivity to the boundary sampling law
is entirely the queries' built-in nearest-boundary-token geometry: with the
area-law tokens but the native draw's geometry the error is 0.997 / 0.998 /
0.999 of native on both seeds. Peter, 2026-10-06, on the proposed
sample-independent replacement: "this seems so-far like a free upgrade.
Essentially no accuracy cost, and it's a more principled formulation. Can
you try this on AirfRANS too?", then the decision tree: "first run AirfRANS
to test that this discretization-independence-in-the-volume holds up on
AirfRANS, and if and only if this does hold up", unfreeze the architecture,
baseline the new form as the canonical ISLA and retrain every volume
benchmark. One correction to the premise, stated to Peter: the 0.997 is the
diagnostic (the native geometry fed to area tokens), not the new form; the
new form's native accuracy is exactly what this study measures.

**The form (words first).** Each boundary token is a point, a unit normal
and a measure. For a query, every token gets a kernel weight, its measure
times $\exp(-r_i/\tau)$ with $r_i$ the distance to the query and $\tau$ a
fixed fraction of the length unit, and a signed distance $s_i$ from the
query to the token's tangent plane. The nearest token decides the side (in
front of or behind the tangent planes). Over the tokens on that side, the
distance channel is the kernel-weighted mean of the $s_i$ and the direction
is the kernel-weighted mean normal, signed so that both keep the nearest
form's conventions (positive outside for outward normals; the direction
points from the boundary to the query). In symbols, with
$a_i = w_i\,e^{-|x_q-y_i|/\tau}$ and $s_i = (x_q-y_i)\cdot\hat n_i$,
$$d_q = \frac{\sum_{i\in\text{side}} a_i s_i}{\sum_{i\in\text{side}} a_i},
\qquad u_q = \pm\,\frac{\sum_{i\in\text{side}} a_i \hat n_i}{\big|\sum_{i\in\text{side}} a_i \hat n_i\big|}.$$
The sums are quadrature estimates of boundary integrals with the tokens'
measures as weights, so they converge under refinement of the boundary
sample for any sampling law whose normalized measure converges, the
property every other quantity the queries read already has. Implementation
(uncommitted at launch, committed with this entry): `soft_boundary_geometry`
in `physicsnemo/experimental/models/isla/geometry.py`, a streaming Triton
kernel in two or three dimensions (one online-rescaled pass over the
tokens, no (Q, N) block) with a chunked PyTorch form for CPU and gradients;
`ISLA(query_geometry="soft", query_geometry_width=0.03)`; `"nearest"`
stays the default until the verdict. Cluster snapshot `code_v21` = `code_v20`
+ the two module files + the geometry tests; verification jobs on AGA and
LHR.

**What the analysis says to expect, written before any run.** Four facts
shaped the form and bound what it can deliver. (1) At a flat wall every
token's tangent-plane distance equals the wall distance, so $d_q$ is exact
there for any sample and any width (the nearest form's Euclidean distance
reads $\sqrt{d^2+\rho^2}$ with $\rho$ the tangential offset to the nearest
token, of order half the spacing, which is why it changes with the law).
(2) Law-robustness needs several tokens inside the kernel under the
coarsest law considered: the area law at 200,000 tokens on a DrivAerML car
has a spacing of about 0.006 of the length unit, so $\tau$ must be at least
about 0.03 of it; the ladder below brackets this. (3) Near a convex wall,
tokens whose tangent plane the query lies behind fall on the other side
and are excluded, so the reading stays the sign of the nearest token's and
keeps a slope of order one in the wall distance over the decade of
distances where the nearest form reads only its own spacing noise; the
exact distance below the sample's geometric resolution (about $h^2\kappa/2$,
of order $2\times10^{-4}$ of the length unit on a car) is unknowable from
any 200,000-token sample, which is where a stored full-mesh field keeps its
advantage (INTERNAL-GEOMETRY, @sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict). (4) Thin
features and convex edges are handled by the side rule, not the kernel: the
far face of a plate and the face beyond an edge have the opposite sign and
never blend in; the nearest token picks the side exactly where the true
distance field's gradient is discontinuous. The residual risks are the
near-wall accuracy on a curved wall at the law-robust width (a smooth,
deterministic curvature offset in the channel) and the two-dimensional
AirfRANS airfoil's token count (about 1,000 segments, a dozen per kernel at
width 0.03), both measured below.

**Why AirfRANS needs its own protocol.** The campaign's uniform
point-cloud protocol redraws the boundary area-proportionally at the
campaign cell budget; on AirfRANS the airfoil has about 1,000 segments,
fewer than the 100,000-cell budget, so the reader keeps it whole and the
area draw is the identity (results/char/airfrans.json: area equals native
to nine digits). AF-GEO therefore RESAMPLES the airfoil at evaluation to an
expected 400 of its segments under two laws, uniform-over-cells (the
mesher's refinement pattern) and length-proportional (uniform along the
curve), with exact Horvitz-Thompson measures
(`recipe_v8/datasets/airfrans_volume_2d_sub400{u,a}.yaml`), interior points
native. Step one is evaluation-only on the AirfRANS references
`cl_r_af_isla_seed42/43` (nearest geometry plus the stored sdf and its
gradient as query inputs) with the VOL-GEO swap control
(`kernel/char/af_geo/af_geo_swap.py`, job 1087177): native, two resampled
conditions, and the two resampled conditions with the native geometry fed
to the queries.

**Arms (group `sq`, LHR, code_v21, the AirfRANS reference recipe: 512 /
512 slices, 3.75e-4, 500 epochs, 100,000 points, full_train / full_test).**
`sq_af_soft03_seed42/43` (width 0.03, the candidate canonical form),
`sq_af_soft01_seed42` and `sq_af_soft10_seed42` (width ladder), all with the
stored sdf inputs as the reference has; and the built-in-only pair
`sq_af_soft03_nosdf_seed42` / `sq_af_nearest_nosdf_seed42` (query_schema
removed), which measures the form's own accuracy without the stored field
masking it. Every arm is then scored natively and under the resampling
protocol by the same probe (`RUNS=... CODE=code_v21`).

**Predictions and bars.** The seed separation of the AirfRANS reference is
the unit: natively 0.0369 / 0.0335 pressure, 0.0167 / 0.0177 velocity,
0.0317 / 0.0312 eddy viscosity (log gaps 0.10 / 0.06 / 0.01; the eddy
viscosity gap is too small to be a bar and pressure's is used for it).
(P1, step one) The reference's error under either resampled law exceeds
native by more than the seed separation on velocity, and the swap returns
it to native within 10%: the built-in channel carries the AirfRANS
sensitivity as it does the Volume's. If the excess at 400 tokens is below
the seed separation, the probe steps to 200 tokens before any verdict.
(P2, invariance) `sq_af_soft03`'s resampled-to-native ratio is within the
seed separation on every field under both laws, on both seeds. (P3, native
accuracy) `sq_af_soft03`'s native error is within the seed separation of
the reference pair on every field (two seeds). (P4, the form's own cost)
`sq_af_soft03_nosdf` is within the seed separation of
`sq_af_nearest_nosdf` natively, or better; the pair's resampled ratios
separate as P2 says. Width: 0.01 is expected to lose P2 under the
length-proportional law (fewer tokens per kernel), 0.1 to lose P3 on
velocity near the wall. **Decision rule, Peter's:** P2 and P3 holding is
"holds up on AirfRANS": the architecture is unfrozen, `query_geometry="soft"`
with the surviving width becomes the class default and the recipe's, the
Volume references are retrained under it and every interior protocol
re-scored, the book restated. P2 or P3 failing keeps `"nearest"` and the
record states what was measured. Nothing on the Volume launches before this
verdict.

## 2026-10-06 — AF-GEO step one: on AirfRANS, resampling the airfoil to 400 of its 1,007 segments raises the reference's error 10x to 21x; the built-in nearest-token geometry carries 62% to 84% of the log excess and the coarsened slice states the rest (a confound the Volume protocol did not have); the soft form's side rule amended before any lane trained {#sec-nb-af-geo-step-one}

**Setting.** Step one of SOFT-GEO (@sec-nb-soft-geo-prereg): the AirfRANS
ISLA references (`cl_r_af_isla_seed42/43`, nearest built-in geometry plus
the stored signed distance and its gradient as query inputs, trained on the
whole airfoil) scored on the 200 full_test cases in float32 at 100,000
native interior points with the airfoil resampled at evaluation to an
expected 400 of its 1,007 segments under the uniform-over-cells law and the
length-proportional law, exact Horvitz-Thompson measures (the resampled
boundary's total measure is 2.05 chord lengths under both laws, the whole
airfoil's), and the VOL-GEO swap control (resampled tokens, the whole
airfoil's built-in geometry fed to the queries). Job 1087177, seven minutes;
native reproduces the record per case to 2e-6 on both seeds; artifact
`results/char/af_geo_2026-10-06.json`, per-case rows and shift statistics
under `results/campaigns_2026-10-02/char/af_geo/`.

**What we saw.** Error relative to native, mean of the two seeds (pressure
/ velocity / eddy viscosity): uniform-over-cells 400 segments 9.6x / 15.8x
/ 11.5x; length-proportional 400 segments 16.4x / 20.7x / 12.9x. With the
whole airfoil's built-in geometry restored to the queries the same resampled
tokens read 2.27x / 1.57x / 1.95x and 2.90x / 2.35x / 1.93x. The share of
the log excess removed by restoring the geometry is 0.63 / 0.84 / 0.72 under
the uniform law and 0.62 / 0.72 / 0.74 under the length law, consistent
across the seeds (0.59 to 0.85). The input shift behind it: the nearest
token changes for 60% (uniform) and 64% (length) of the queries; over the
near-wall queries (within 0.01 chord, 48,000 of 100,000) the built-in
distance moves by an RMS log ratio of 0.62 (uniform) and 1.27 (length) and
the built-in direction's cosine to the native one is 0.59 and 0.60. The
native built-in distance itself is far from the stored field near the wall
(median 1.5e-3 chord against 5.4e-4, RMS log ratio 2.8), so the model's
query channel reads the mesher's panel spacing even before resampling; the
stored field is present as an input and does not protect the model.

**Reading.** The first clause of P1 holds with room: AirfRANS has the
sensitivity, and larger than the Volume's 7x. The second clause fails: the
swap returns the error to 1.6x to 2.9x of native, not to within 10%. The
difference from the Volume is the protocol, not the mechanism. The Volume's
area draw kept 200,000 tokens and changed only the law; the AirfRANS
resampling removes 60% of the tokens, and the slice attention over 400
instead of 1,007 segments loses information no quadrature weight restores.
That resolution component is 16% to 38% of the log excess here; the
built-in geometry is the rest, and it is what the soft form addresses.

**Protocol consequence (before any soft arm is scored).** The AirfRANS
verdict needs a redraw that changes the law without removing information.
Added to the AF-GEO protocol, to be built while the lanes train:
`airfrans_volume_2d_refine*` variants that split every airfoil segment into
collinear pieces under two refinement patterns (uniform, and front-loaded:
three pieces ahead of mid-chord, one behind), each piece carrying its own
length as measure, so the boundary measure and the geometry are unchanged
and only the panelization pattern differs. The class's own statement is
that splitting a boundary cell changes nothing; the nearest form moves with
the spacing. Under refinement P2 reads: the soft arm within the seed
separation of native under both patterns; the reference is expected to
move. Under the 400-segment coarsening P2 reads: the soft arm's geometry
share of the log excess (the swap control applied to it) below 0.1, with
its total excess at most the resolution component measured here (1.6x to
2.9x), reported as the token-count requirement of the slice attention and
not held against the form. P3 and P4 are unchanged.

**Amendment to the form (before any lane trained; the LHR verification of
the first snapshot, job 103941, failed its own thin-plate test).** The first
form grouped tokens by the sign of their tangent-plane distance alone and
let the nearest token pick the group. Inside a body thinner than the kernel
width both faces lie behind the query, fall in the same group and blend:
the distance read the mean of the two face distances and the direction
cancelled. The amended form keeps the nearest token's side and adds its
normal as a facing factor, $\max(0, \hat n_i \cdot \hat n_{i^*})$, on every
token's weight: the far face of a thin body and the far wall of a concave
corner, whose normals point the other way, drop out; at a convex edge the
nearest face's normal is selected as the nearest form already does; a flat
wall is unchanged (the factor is one); on a curved wall it is a smooth
reweighting that converges with the sample. The exact nearest search runs
first (the existing Triton kernel), the accumulation kernel second, with the
width read in the inputs' precision (the first kernel took it as a float32
scalar, which the float64 kernel-vs-PyTorch test caught). Tests added for
the thin plate inside and the concave corner; the two-laws test now samples
at a few spacings per kernel width, the regime the form is specified for.
`code_v21` rebuilt with the amended files; verification resubmitted on both
clusters; the six AirfRANS lanes launch on the pass.

**Setting and instrument.** The count-preserving protocol promised in

**What we saw.** Error relative to native, mean of the two seeds (pressure
/ velocity / eddy viscosity): uniform re-panelization 2.02x / 2.86x / 2.41x;
front-loaded 2.72x / 3.77x / 1.91x. With the whole airfoil's built-in
geometry restored to the queries, the same tokens read 0.97x / 0.99x / 0.99x
and 1.00x / 1.00x / 1.02x: the fraction of the log excess removed is 1.04 /
1.01 / 1.01 and 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.98, both seeds within 0.96 to 1.09. The
input shift behind it: the nearest token changes for every query under the
uniform split (every midpoint moves) and for 45% under the front-loaded one;
over the near-wall queries the built-in distance moves by an RMS log ratio
of 0.42 and 0.46 and the direction's cosine to the native one is 0.95.

**Reading.** With the information held fixed, the entire re-panelization
sensitivity of the AirfRANS model is the built-in nearest-token geometry,
exactly as VOL-GEO found for the Volume's area draw: the slice attention
over re-panelized tokens is invariant to within seed noise, and the
coarsening residual of step one (1.6x to 2.9x) was the information lost to
dropping 60% of the tokens, not a second mechanism. The mechanism is now
reproduced on two datasets and two kinds of discretization change (a law
change at fixed count; a pattern change at fixed geometry). This is the
protocol P2 is judged on: the soft arms' re-panelized error within the seed
separation of native under both patterns, where the nearest form moves 2x to
4x.

## 2026-10-06 — QUERY-POP: the Volume model's error on fixed scored points rises 15x to 24x when 200,000 far-field companions join the query set and 3.5x to 4.3x with wall-heavy companions; the learned query routing mass is 1.15 to 1.18 of the whole boundary measure; a second, larger discretization sensitivity that the built-in geometry does not touch {#sec-nb-query-pop}

**Setting.** Peter's question (2026-10-06): after the soft geometry, can a
volume model trained on CFD-mesh queries (count-uniform over the mesh's
points, wall-heavy) be inferred on a volume-uniform point cloud with the
surface task's robustness? In ISLA's interior task the prediction points are
interacting tokens: their total routing mass is a learned fraction of the
boundary measure split equally over them, with no per-query measure, so the
slice states see the query population. The campaign never varied the query
law (the Volume's uniform point-cloud protocol redraws the boundary only).
The query-independence program of 2026-10-03 (branch `psharpe/isla-independent`,
`research/query_independence/RESULTS.md`) measured the dependence from the
request side (a rear region requested alone 13.6x / 13.7x / 10.8x against
inside the native request; a near-body uniform-like set alone 17x / 14x /
16x) and found exact independence at equal accuracy only through a fixed
support cloud of the training law; a model trained without interior
writers was 4% to 42% less accurate, and the volume-quadrature program
(branch `psharpe/isla-volquad`) found volume-weighted queries cost 15% to
24% on DrivAerML.

**Instrument (`kernel/char/qpop/qpop_swap.py`, scoring only).** The two
Volume references on the 48 validation cars, float32, 200,000 native points,
every metric on the SAME scored set (the first 100,000 native points) so
that only the query population differs: the native 200,000 tokens
(control); the 100,000 alone; the native 200,000 plus 200,000 companions
uniform in the interior's bounding box (far-field heavy, Peter's scenario's
direction); the native 200,000 plus 200,000 companions resampled from the
native points with probability 1/|sdf| (wall-heavy). Every scored point
keeps its own built-in geometry by construction (companions do not change a
scored point's nearest boundary token). Job 1087747; the full-set control
reproduces the record to 7e-7; artifact `results/char/qpop_2026-10-06.json`.

**What we saw.** Relative to the control, mean of the two seeds (pressure /
velocity / eddy viscosity): the half count alone 1.02x / 1.02x / 1.02x;
far-field companions 23.7x / 15.0x / 12.3x (seeds 22.1 / 25.4 on pressure);
wall-heavy companions 4.34x / 4.34x / 3.55x. The learned query routing mass
is exp(logw) = 1.18 (seed 42) and 1.15 (seed 43) of the total boundary
measure: the queries carry more mass in the slice states than the whole
boundary.

**Reading.** A count change at the training law is benign (the equal split
keeps the population's distribution); a change of the population's
distribution is not, and in the direction of a volume-uniform cloud it is
twice the Volume's boundary-law sensitivity in log terms. This is a property
of the interacting design, separate from the built-in geometry, and the
soft form leaves it untouched. After SOFT-GEO the volume task gets the
surface task's robustness to the boundary sampling law; robustness to the
query sampling law needs a change on the query side, and the three forms
already measured by Peter's programs each pay for it: a training-law
support cloud (exact, equal accuracy, but needs a wall-heavy volume sample at
inference), passive queries (exact, 4% to 42% less accurate), volume-measure
queries (15% to 24% less accurate on DrivAerML). Reported to Peter with the
numbers; no query-side lane launched without his word.

## 2026-10-06 — SOFT-GEO first launch invalid: the five soft lanes read a NaN loss from their first step (the streaming kernel's online rescale before a query's first kept sample); the nearest control trained; kernel guarded, regression test added, lanes relaunched after re-verification {#sec-nb-soft-geo-nan-relaunch}

The six `sq_af` lanes launched on LHR at 09:20 PDT (jobs 104168-104173).
Within minutes every soft arm (`sq_af_soft03_seed42/43`, `soft01`, `soft10`,
`soft03_nosdf`) logged `Loss: nan` from its first training step, while the
nearest-geometry control `sq_af_nearest_nosdf_seed42` trained normally
(0.100 at the first step, 0.033 at epoch 3). The cause is in the amended
kernel's accumulation pass: the side and facing rules exclude tokens, and
for a query whose first token tiles hold no kept sample the running maximum
and the tile maximum are both minus infinity, so the streamed-softmax
rescale evaluates exp(-inf - (-inf)) = NaN and poisons the accumulators.
The PyTorch form takes its maximum over the whole row and never meets the
case, and the kernel-vs-PyTorch test on random clouds met a kept token in
the first tile of every query by chance. On the AirfRANS airfoil the tokens
are ordered along the curve, so a query above the upper surface whose first
128 tokens lie on the lower surface hits the case at once. Fix: the rescale
and the exponentials are gated on a live maximum (zero until the first kept
sample); regression test with the far face of a plate listed first, CUDA
only. The five soft lanes were cancelled, their first-step run directories
set aside (`runs_invalid_nan_2026-10-06/`), the snapshot `code_v21` rebuilt
with the guard, verification resubmitted on both clusters, and the lanes
relaunch on the pass. The control lane keeps running. Nothing in the
preregistration changes; no result was read from the invalid lanes.
