## 2026-10-07 — SOFT-GEO lanes scored: the soft form is invariant to re-panelization (0.96 to 1.01) and beats the nearest reference natively, but under coarsening its built-in channel still carries half the excess and the posed error moves 1 to 6 percent; both traced to the one-sided rule and the direction's sign, fixed and relaunched {#sec-nb-soft-geo-lanes}

**Setting.** The soft built-in query geometry (@sec-nb-soft-geo-prereg)
replaces the nearest boundary token's Euclidean distance and direction by
a measure-weighted kernel average over the tokens on the nearest token's
side of their tangent planes: the kernel-mean plane distance d and the
kernel-mean normal u, width 0.03 of the length unit. Six AirfRANS lanes
trained it under the campaign protocol (code_v21, 500 epochs, 100,000
interior points, lr 3.75e-4): soft03 seeds 42 and 43, soft01 and soft10
(widths 0.01 and 0.10), soft03 without the stored signed-distance inputs,
and a nearest-form control without them. All six completed without a NaN.

**Native and posed scores** (pressure / velocity / eddy-viscosity relative
L2, 200 held-out cases, float32). soft03: 0.0292 / 0.0147 / 0.0278 (seed 42)
and 0.0311 / 0.0154 / 0.0301 (seed 43), against the nearest reference's
0.0369 / 0.0167 / 0.0317 and 0.0335 / 0.0177 / 0.0312: 10 to 21 percent
better on every field and both seeds, so bar P3 (native within the seed
separation of the reference) passes with room. soft01 0.0317 / 0.0160 /
0.0278 and soft10 0.0322 / 0.0156 / 0.0284: the width barely matters
natively. Built-in channel alone (no stored field): soft 0.0308 / 0.0185 /
0.0297 against nearest 0.0305 / 0.0196 / 0.0276, one seed each, so bar P4
(soft at least as good as nearest without the stored field) is mixed:
velocity 6 percent better, eddy viscosity 8 percent worse, pressure equal.
Under the posed protocol (an in-plane rotation and a translation of one RMS
radius per case) the nearest lanes reproduce their native numbers to five
digits; every soft lane moves: velocity +3.7 percent (seed 42), +6.2
percent (seed 43), +2.8 percent (soft01), +1.9 percent (soft10), +0.6
percent (no stored field); pressure +0.7 to +1.8 percent.

**AF-GEO** (`kernel/char/af_geo_sq/<run>/summary.json`, LHR). Under the
count-raising re-panelizations refu and reff (@sec-nb-af-geo-refine) the
soft lanes' error ratios to native are 0.955 to 1.012 on every field, both
seeds and all three widths, where the nearest control without the stored
field moves 1.43 / 2.51 / 2.79 (refu) and 1.73 / 3.39 / 2.00 (reff) and
its native geometry restores it to 0.98 to 1.01: **the soft form is
re-panelization invariant and the nearest form's sensitivity is entirely
its built-in channel.** Under the 400-segment coarsening the soft lanes
still lose 7.7 to 17.7x (uniform law) and 12.2 to 18.4x (length law), and
swapping in the native geometry returns them to 2.7 to 4.5x (the
coarsened slice states' share, as for the reference): the built-in
channel's share of the log excess is 0.46 to 0.77, the same as the nearest
form's 0.52 to 0.82, and independent of the width. **Bar P2's coarsening
clause (geometry share below 0.1) fails for the form as trained.** The
wall-node split (`af_geo_sq_wall`: native geometry restored at the wall
nodes only, or everywhere but the wall nodes) puts the whole coarsening
excess outside the wall nodes (wall-only swap 10.64 / 9.85 / 11.08 against
10.69 / 9.89 / 11.09 for soft03 seed 42; rest-only swap 2.88 / 1.84 / 1.97
against the full swap's 2.84 / 1.84 / 1.97).

**Mechanism of the posed shift** (probes `kernel/char/pose_probe/run1,
run2`: the geometry functions alone on 12 cases, four rigid motions each,
float32 and float64). In float64 both forms are invariant to 1e-12. The
AirfRANS interior sample contains the airfoil's own wall nodes (stored
distance exactly zero; 273 to 726 of 100,000 queries per case). There the
plane distance to the nearest token, s* = (x - y*) . n*, is a
roundoff-level number, so in float32 about half of the wall nodes change
side under a pose, in both forms alike (47 and 48 percent). The nearest
form's d flips sign (|d| is half a panel, median 6e-4 chord) and its
direction (x - y*)/|x - y*| never reverses; the trained nearest model does
not react. The soft form's d sits at 1e-9 chord on the outside branch and
at about kappa tau^2 (median 3e-6, up to 3e-2 at the leading edge) on the
inside branch, so its log channel changed by more than one unit at 71
percent of the wall nodes, and its direction u = sigma* nbar REVERSED at 45
percent of them; every other band of the interior changed by roundoff
only. Re-orienting u at evaluation on the trained checkpoints
(`kernel/char/f3_eval`) doubled their error (an input combination never
seen in training): the model is extremely sensitive to u at the wall nodes,
and the fix has to be trained in. A second defect found by the identity
pose: the host decided the side from s* in torch while the kernel
recomputed s with other rounding, so at |s*| ~ roundoff the nearest token
itself could drop out of an otherwise empty kept set and the kernel
returned d = 0 and a zero direction at about 3 percent of the wall nodes.

**Mechanism of the coarsening sensitivity.** The one-sided rule keeps, on
the convex side of a curved wall, only the tokens whose tangent plane the
query lies in front of: at wall distance delta those within a tangential
offset sqrt(2 delta / kappa) of the query's foot. That window is 4.5e-3
chord at delta = 1e-5 on the mid-chord of a unit airfoil: the native
sample puts about four tokens in it and the 400-segment sample one, and the
kernel-mean plane distance goes from about two thirds of delta (a window
full of tokens, whose plane distances are delta minus kappa l^2 / 2) to
delta (the nearest token alone). The truncation makes the near-wall d
depend on the token density at first order, whatever the width, which is
why the coarsening share did not move between widths 0.01 and 0.10 while
refinement, which only adds tokens to an already-resolved window, left the
form alone. The two-sided average over every facing token has no such
window: it is continuous and smooth across the wall and depends on the
sample only through the quadrature error of a kernel wider than the
spacing, at the price of a curvature bias of about kappa tau^2 on both
sides (its zero level set sits that far outside a convex wall).

**Fix** (commit f7e4377a3, snapshot code_v23, verified on LHR: 210 passed
in the first run, two test expectations corrected, re-run pending): the
direction is the kernel-mean outward normal on both sides, u = nbar/|nbar|,
the gradient of a signed distance (continuous across the wall; the side
stays in the sign of d); the nearest token is always kept (its index goes
to the kernel); and the two-sided average is a second research arm,
`query_geometry="smooth"`, beside the one-sided `"soft"`. One of the two
replaces the other after the verdict.

**Relaunch** (LHR, group sr, rows 88 to 93, jobs 112161 to 112166, code_v23,
same protocol): soft03 seeds 42 and 43 with the direction fix, smooth03
seeds 42 and 43, and the two no-stored-field pairs (soft03, smooth03, seed
42). Pre-registered: (i) both forms pose-invariant to within 0.5 percent on
every field (the direction no longer flips; for soft the remaining d jump
at the wall nodes is the residual); (ii) smooth's coarsening geometry share
below 0.1 with the coarsened ratio at the slice-state level, soft's share
unchanged near 0.5; (iii) smooth native within the seed separation of
soft (the curvature bias costs nothing the model cannot learn); (iv)
smooth without the stored field at least as good as nearest without it on
every field. If (i) to (iii) hold, smooth is the sample-independent form
and the decision tree's AirfRANS gate is passed on refinement AND
coarsening; the wall jump and the LE resolution limit (tau = 0.015 chord
is the leading-edge radius of a 12 percent airfoil) go to Peter as the
known properties of the form.

## 2026-10-07 — DeepJEB++ under the campaign protocol: the half-rate ISLA lanes reach the baselines' accuracy by epoch 18 (displacement 0.23, von Mises 0.46) and then collapse to the mean-field plateau between epochs 20 and 24 on both seeds; the scored 40-epoch checkpoints read 0.84 / 0.90 on displacement against GeoTransolver's 0.23 and Transolver's 0.19 {#sec-nb-char-deepjeb-halfrate-verdict}

**Setting.** DeepJEB++ is the campaign's one dataset on which the ISLA
reference configuration (512 wide, 512 slices, the sample-conditioned
prototypes of the current class) at the reference rate 3.75e-4 reaches the
mean-field plateau: both `cl_r_jeb_isla` lanes sit at a validation loss of
0.08 from epoch 6 to the end and score 1.18 / 0.98 on displacement and 1.02 /
1.00 on von Mises stress (@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-mechanism named the
mechanism, a routing collapse to one to five effective slices in half of the
blocks). Peter ruled a per-dataset exception (2026-10-05): the campaign arm
for DeepJEB++ trains at half the rate, 1.875e-4, every other hyperparameter
the reference's. The pair `cl_jd_rate_e40_seed42/43` (40 epochs on the
12,451 clean training brackets, AGA) finished today and was scored under the
three protocols.

**What we saw.** Both seeds descend normally for half the run: validation
loss 0.0146 at epoch 0, 0.0079 at epoch 6, 0.0065 at epoch 18, where the
trainer's validation metrics read **displacement 0.225 and von Mises 0.458
(seed 42; seed 43 within 0.01)**, level with GeoTransolver-256 (0.231 /
0.497) and Transolver 512 x 16 (0.194 / 0.436) under the campaign protocol.
Between epochs 20 and 24 the training loss jumps from 0.006 to 0.016 and then
0.06 on seed 42 (0.034 then 0.057 on seed 43) and the validation loss to
0.067 on both, the plateau value of the reference-rate lanes; the final
checkpoints, which the protocol scores, read **displacement 0.840 / 0.903 and
von Mises 0.931 / 0.931** (natively; the area protocol is the identity on this
dataset and the posed protocol reproduces the native numbers, as for every
ISLA lane). The regenerated dataset artifact (`results/char/deepjeb_surface.json`,
final-reference arms) therefore shows ISLA at 0.871 / 0.931 against
GeoTransolver-256 at 0.231 / 0.497 and Transolver at 0.194 / 0.436, with both
baselines at 1.2 to 1.5 under the posed protocol.

**Why it matters.** The half rate delays the collapse (epoch 4 at 3.75e-4,
epoch 22 at 1.875e-4) and does not prevent it, so the rate exception does not
rescue the dataset: under the frozen class the DeepJEB++ standing is a
failure by training instability, not by capacity, since the same lanes match
the baselines eighteen epochs in. This is the first campaign dataset on which
the current class does not finish its protocol, and the only one where ISLA
trails the baselines by more than a factor of two. Chapter 13 states this as
the current standing; the earlier equal-step ladder, run under the previous
class (384 wide, 12 layers, static prototypes, 5e-4), is kept as the record of
what that form achieved and is labeled as such.

**What's next.** The routing collapse on this dataset is a property of the
sample-conditioned prototypes at the reference width that the class now
carries everywhere (@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-mechanism measured 1 to 5
effective slices of 256 in the collapsed blocks). A collapse-resistant
routing is an architecture change, which the campaign freeze forbids; the
candidates (a floor on the routing temperature, a slice-usage regularizer,
or an epoch-18 early stop as a protocol rule, which would be a tuning
shortcut) go to Peter with this verdict. Nothing is launched on it.

## 2026-10-07 — SOFT-GEO verdict on the relaunched lanes: the two-sided kernel form is pose-invariant to four digits and both kernel forms are re-panelization invariant, but under 2.5x coarsening the built-in channel still carries 0.3 to 0.85 of the log excess for every form, and that residual sits at the trailing edge and wake; the one-sided form is the better built-in channel; neither arm passes the pre-registered coarsening bar {#sec-nb-soft-geo-verdict}

**Setting.** The six relaunched lanes (`sr_af_*`, snapshot code_v23, 500
epochs, 100,000 interior points, lr 3.75e-4, LHR) carry the fix of
@sec-nb-soft-geo-lanes: the direction is the kernel-mean outward normal on
both sides of the wall and the nearest token is always kept; `soft` keeps the
one-sided rule, `smooth` averages every facing token. Two seeds each with the
stored signed-distance inputs, one seed each without them. All six trained
without a NaN; they were scored natively and under the posed protocol and run
through the AirfRANS resampling probe (coarsening to 400 segments under the
uniform-over-cells and length laws, re-panelization under two patterns, each
with the native-geometry swap). Artifact:
`results/char/soft_geo_lanes_2026-10-07.json` (key `relaunch_code_v23`).

**Native and posed** (pressure / velocity / eddy-viscosity relative L2).
soft 0.0314 / 0.0168 / 0.0284 and 0.0306 / 0.0152 / 0.0288; smooth 0.0300 /
0.0160 / 0.0295 and 0.0331 / 0.0150 / 0.0307; the nearest reference 0.0369 /
0.0167 / 0.0317 and 0.0335 / 0.0177 / 0.0312. Without the stored field: soft
0.0281 / 0.0170 / 0.0280, smooth 0.0304 / 0.0278 / 0.0295, nearest 0.0305 /
0.0196 / 0.0276. **Posed over native: smooth 0.9996 to 1.0007 on every field,
both seeds and the no-stored-field lane (bar (i) passes); soft 1.010 / 1.029 /
1.007 and 1.020 / 1.054 / 1.008 (bar (i) fails):** with the direction
continuous, the one-sided form's remaining pose dependence is its distance
jump of about kappa tau^2 at the wall nodes, and the trained model reads it as
strongly as it read the reversed direction.

**Resampling.** Re-panelization (count-raising, information-preserving):
every kernel lane 0.965 to 1.021 on every field (the nearest control without
the stored field 1.43 to 3.39). Coarsening: soft 5.7 to 12.8x (uniform law)
and 8.6 to 16.7x (length law), smooth 5.6 to 7.6x and 7.7 to 10.4x, against
the nearest reference's 9.6 to 15.8x and 16.4 to 20.7x; the native-geometry
swap returns all of them to 2.7 to 4.5x, the coarsened slice states' share,
so **the built-in channel's share of the log excess is 0.33 to 0.85 for smooth
and 0.37 to 0.80 for soft, where the nearest form's is 0.52 to 0.85 (bar (ii)
fails).** The one-sided truncation I named as the mechanism of that share
(@sec-nb-soft-geo-lanes) is refuted: removing the side rule did not move it.
The geometry itself does move less than the nearest form's under coarsening
(near-wall direction cosine 0.98 against 0.59, RMS log distance ratio 0.49
for smooth against 0.62), and the model amplifies what remains.

**Where the residual lives.** Restoring the native geometry on a chordwise
band of the queries (`kernel/char/af_geo_sr_le`, 4 lanes, both coarsening
laws): ahead of x = 0.1 chord (42 percent of the queries, the whole upstream
field including the leading edge) recovers almost nothing (smooth without the
stored field, uniform law: 7.63 / 8.24 / 13.07 to 7.43 / 7.10 / 13.00); between
0.1 and 0.9 recovers nothing (7.54 / 8.06 / 13.02); **behind x = 0.9 chord (29
percent, the trailing edge and the wake) recovers most of it, 3.19 / 4.12 /
2.18 against the full swap's 2.70 / 1.37 / 1.97, and all of the eddy-viscosity
excess**; the same on every lane (soft without the stored field: 5.71 / 12.06
/ 13.02 to 2.95 / 2.68 / 2.16 with the full swap at 2.81 / 1.66 / 2.11). So the
kernel forms' coarsening sensitivity is not the leading edge, where the width
is about the leading-edge radius, but the sharp trailing edge and the wake
behind it. The mechanism consistent with every measurement is the orientation
reference: the facing factor and the one-sided rule take their reference
normal from the exact nearest token, and behind a sharp trailing edge the
nearest token is on the upper or the lower face by a hair, so when coarsening
moves the nearest token (it changes for 60 percent of all queries) the
reference flips between two normals that differ by nearly 180 degrees and the
kernel-mean normal and distance of the wake queries flip with it (the same
discontinuity the pose probe met at the medial axis, @sec-nb-soft-geo-lanes).
The nearest form has the same reference and the same flips.

**Bars (iii) and (iv).** smooth's native error is within soft's seed range on
pressure and velocity and 2 to 7 percent worse on eddy viscosity (passes).
Without the stored field smooth is 42 percent worse than nearest on velocity
(0.0278 against 0.0196; fails) while soft is better on every field (0.92 /
0.87 / 1.01): the two-sided form's curvature bias (its zero level set sits
about kappa tau^2 outside a convex wall; its sign disagrees with the stored
distance at 20 percent of the near-wall queries) makes it a poor wall-distance
estimate on its own, and the one-sided form with the continuous direction is
the best built-in channel measured.

**Verdict against the decision tree.** Peter's gate was that the
discretization independence in the volume "holds up on AirfRANS". It holds
up under the change of sampling law at preserved information (re-panelization:
both kernel forms invariant to 2 percent, the nearest form not) and under the
posed protocol for the two-sided form; it does not hold up under 2.5x
coarsening, where every form, nearest included, pays once through the slice
states (an architecture-wide information loss the baselines are being scored
for) and about as much again through the built-in channel, with the channel's
part concentrated at the trailing edge. Neither arm therefore passes the gate
as pre-registered, and the architecture stays frozen. What the data recommend,
if the gate is reopened: the one-sided form with the continuous direction as
the built-in channel (best accuracy, re-panelization invariant, pose
dependence of 1 to 5 percent from the wall-node jump), and a continuous
orientation reference at sharp edges as the next mechanism to fix, which is a
design change for Peter.

**The baselines under the same resamplings** (GeoTransolver-256 and
Transolver 512 x 16 AirfRANS references, both seeds, scored on AGA under
`airfrans_volume_{sub400u,sub400a,refu,reff}`, the three-dimensional
pipeline's variants built today): every score is bitwise identical to the
native one, 1.00 on every field under all four resamplings. That is not
robustness but blindness: the two baseline interior models drop the boundary
mesh at the reader (`drop_in_file_boundaries: true`) and read the geometry
only through the stored signed distance and its gradient, which are
precomputed from the full CFD mesh and untouched by any resampling of the
airfoil tokens. ISLA's interior model is the only one of the three that reads
the boundary sample itself, so it is the only one that can pay for a coarser
boundary, and it pays twice: once through the slice states (2.7 to 4.5x, the
information the 600 dropped segments carried) and about as much again through
the built-in channel. The comparison that would separate an
architecture-wide information loss from ISLA's own sensitivity therefore does
not exist on AirfRANS at this budget; the baselines' invariance is the
invariance of a model that never looks. It also restates what the
re-panelization result means: ISLA's kernel forms are invariant to a change
of boundary sampling that the baselines cannot even see, while remaining the
only models that would notice a geometry the stored field does not encode.

## 2026-10-08 — PATCH-SDF pre-registration: the built-in query geometry as the exact signed distance to the finite patches the tokens' measures define, with the side from the winding number behind an edge; on 12 AirfRANS cases it equals the stored field natively and flips 0.03 percent of the wake distances under coarsening where the nearest and kernel forms flip 10 percent; two AirfRANS lanes launched {#sec-nb-patch-sdf-prereg}

**Setting.** The SOFT-GEO verdict (@sec-nb-soft-geo-verdict) left the
built-in query geometry with one named residual: under the 400-segment
coarsening every form, the nearest token's distance and the kernel averages
alike, carried 0.3 to 0.85 of the log excess through its built-in channel, and
the chordwise split put that share behind x = 0.9 chord, the sharp trailing
edge and the wake. Peter asked whether a different facing factor (an even
function of the cosine, max(cos, 0) |cos| or cos^2) would remove it, and then
approved running "the form you think is most promising". This entry records
the mechanism probes that chose the form, the form itself, its measured
geometry, and the lanes that test it. Artifact:
`results/char/patch_sdf_probes_2026-10-08.json` (every probe's per-band
aggregates; per-case records in `kernel/char/pose_probe/run5..run9` on LHR).

**The symptom, measured on the geometry functions alone.** The probe
instrument of @sec-nb-soft-geo-lanes was extended to coarsening: the geometry
functions (no model) on the first 12 full_test cases, native airfoil (about
1,000 segments) against the 400-segment uniform-law coarsening with the same
100,000 queries, per band of chord position and of wall distance. Behind the
trailing edge (x > 0.9) the one-sided kernel form's distance changes by 0.25
chord RMS and the nearest form's by 0.38, and both flip the sign of 10 percent
of the wake distances above 1e-3 chord; restricted to the queries whose sign
survives, the kernel form still moves 0.032 chord where the nearest form moves
0.0006. Two mechanisms, then: **the side** (inside or outside) of a wake query
is decided by the nearest token's tangent plane, and when coarsening moves the
nearest token to the other face of the trailing edge a query above the lower
face's extended plane is declared inside, d = -L for a distance L; and **the
magnitude** of the kernel form reads the tangent planes extrapolated past the
edge, about L sin(face angle), which moves with the surviving tokens' face
angles. Neither depends on the facing factor: the squared cosine left the wake
change at 0.24 chord (run 3), so Peter's proposal, taken literally, was
refuted before anything was trained.

**What was tested for the side.** (a) A vote: the sign of the two-sided
kernel mean of the plane offsets over every facing token (even facing, so both
faces of an edge vote). It removed the wake flips (0.25 to 0.053 chord) but
read 56 percent of the near-wall fluid points as inside: with an even facing
factor the far sheet of a thin section votes with the larger plane offset, the
thickness. (b) Tie-votes among the patches nearest to the query, with the
window one patch radius, the second-neighbour spacing, or the distance between
the patches' nearest points: on a Poisson subsample the two faces' surviving
patches sit at random distances from the edge, so a window of one spacing
misses the second face a third of the time, and a window wide enough to catch
it lets the far sheet vote (12 to 15 percent flips mid-chord). (c) A relative
window (patches within a factor of the nearest distance): behind the body it
sums the plane offsets of a closed surface, which the divergence theorem makes
negative, and reads 94 percent of the far field as inside. **No local rule
separates an edge from a thin section on a sample with gaps**; the side behind
an edge is a topological question.

**The form** (`query_geometry="patch"`, `geometry.patch_boundary_geometry`,
commit c8414e583). A boundary token with measure w_i represents the flat patch
of that measure around its centroid: in two dimensions the segment of
half-length R_i = w_i / 2 in its tangent line. Under a subsample whose measures
carry the inverse inclusion probabilities (every draw of the program), the
patches tile the surface in expectation. For a query x: |d| is the exact
Euclidean distance to the set of patches (plane offset over a patch, distance
to the rim beyond it), so no tangent plane is extrapolated past its patch and a
wake query reads L. The side is the nearest patch's plane sign where the
nearest point lies inside that patch (the exact side of a closest point on a
face) or the query is within one radius of it (a gap of the subsample), and
otherwise, behind an edge, in a wake, far away, the exact winding number of
the patch set, the sum of the signed angles the oriented segments subtend over
2 pi, which is 0 outside and 1 inside a closed boundary whatever cells the
subsample kept and does not care how thin the body is. The direction is the
patch normal in the local regime (so a wall node, whose nearest patch is
decided by rounding, has a direction no rounding can turn) and the gradient of
the distance from the rim point beyond it. One constant, the reach of one
radius; two radii changed nothing measurable. Two dimensions only: a flat
disk's solid angle has no closed form, and the three-dimensional form waits
for the verdict. The cost is one chunked (Q, N) pass with an arctangent per
pair; no Triton kernel yet.

**What the probes saw** (run 9, the library form, 12 cases; the plane kernel
and the nearest form in the same probe). Natively the form reproduces the
stored signed-distance field: RMS log ratio 0.000, median ratio 1.000, sign
agreement 0.9999 (the plane kernel 0.43 / 0.91, the nearest form 0.55 /
1.00), so the stored field the baselines read is now computable inside the
model from the boundary tokens. Under coarsening, behind the trailing edge:
RMS change 5.2e-4 chord (plane 0.25, nearest 0.38), flips of distances above
1e-3 chord 0.03 percent (10 percent), direction reversals 0.5 percent (17 and
3.5 percent); in the far field no flip (4.5 percent); over the whole query set
RMS change 1.3e-3 chord against 0.14 and 0.22. Near the wall the form pays
for the gaps of the Poisson subsample: RMS change 1.8e-3 chord against the
plane kernel's 4.5e-4 and the nearest form's 3.3e-3 (over a gap the nearest
point is a rim, and the distance reads the gap), with the sign flipping only
in the convexity sliver below about 1e-5 chord and within one radius of the
trailing edge. Under a rigid motion in float32 the distance moves by 1e-5
chord RMS and the wall nodes' direction by 0.036 RMS (1 - cos) with 0.1 percent
reversals (the one-sided kernel's wall nodes turned half the time before its
fix). Pre-registered probe bars P-a (wake and far flips <= 1 percent), P-b
(wake RMS change <= 0.01 chord), P-c (native accuracy), P-d (wake reversals
<= 2 percent) and P-e (posed invariance) all pass; the vote's necessity (P-f)
was settled synthetically (the nearest patch's own plane sign fails behind
the edge for 29 percent of wake points on a closed NACA 0012 polygon) and the
reach's insensitivity (P-g) by run 7's c = 2 arm.

**Tests** (`test_isla_interior_geometry.py`, six): exactness of distance,
sign and gradient on a closed polygon; the winding-number side behind a sharp
edge against the plane-sign control; the wake side under a 40 percent Poisson
subsample with inverse-inclusion measures; covariance under rotation,
reflection, translation and scale; the three-dimensional and reach guards; the
interior model's contracts and checkpoint round trip in two dimensions.

**Lanes and bars.** `sp_af_patch_seed42` and `_seed43` (`cl_lanes.tsv` rows
94 and 95, snapshot code_v25 = code_v24 + this form, verified on LHR before
launch): AirfRANS 2-D, the campaign configuration (512 wide, 512 slices,
100,000 interior points, lr 3.75e-4, 500 epochs), with the stored
signed-distance inputs as every reference lane has. Controls: the nearest
reference lanes and the kernel lanes of @sec-nb-soft-geo-verdict. Bars, the
SOFT-GEO gate's as pre-registered: (i) posed over native within 1.005 on every
field; (ii) under the 400-segment coarsening (both laws) the built-in channel's
share of the log excess below 0.1 (the native-geometry swap of the AirfRANS
resampling probe), against 0.3 to 0.85 for every form so far; (iii) native
error within the nearest reference's seed range or better; re-panelization
(refu, reff) within 2 percent as the kernel forms are. If (ii) passes with (i)
and (iii), Peter's decision tree reopens: the form becomes the canonical
built-in channel, its three-dimensional form (disk patches with a closed-form
solid-angle approximation, a streaming kernel) is written, and the volume
benchmarks retrain. If (ii) fails while the probes say the channel is stable,
what remains of the coarsening share is the model's reading of the slice
states, and the frozen architecture stands.

## 2026-10-08 — Verdict, SCALE-LAW on HiLiftAeroML (four rungs, 35 to 1,260 wings, three widths, both architectures): the bounded-floor law is accepted for both (ISLA 2.3 percent RMS, GeoTransolver 1.7), the data exponent is 0.84 to 0.85 for both and lower than the cars' 1.3, ISLA's floor is 0.027 while GeoTransolver's fit cannot separate a floor from its flat parameter term; cases remain the better purchase across the measured range {#sec-nb-scalelaw-wing-verdict}

**Setting.** SCALE-LAW (@sec-nb-campaigns-2026-09-21-prereg) fits the
separable law $\varepsilon(n, P) = \varepsilon_\infty + a\,n^{-\alpha} +
b\,P^{-\beta}$ to the float32 surface-pressure error against training
cases $n$ and parameters $P$, for cosine ISLA at 192 / 384 / 768 wide and
GeoTransolver at 256 / 512 / 1,024, 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per case,
two seeds. The DrivAerML half (five rungs, 27 to 435 cars) accepted the
law for ISLA and not for GeoTransolver (@sec-nb-scalelaw-drivaerml-verdict).
The wing half needed a fourth training-set size for the reducer's fit gate
(@sec-nb-scalelaw-wing-rung4); the 1,260-wing lanes (campaign sl rows 80
to 91, the whole HiLiftAeroML training split) finished on 2026-10-08
after eleven days of four-hour chains, and the twelfth was scored today
(the fleet scorer had left `sl_hl_gt_w1024_full_c100k_seed42` with a
27-step partial file and no completion marker; its evaluation was rerun,
180 of 180 wings). All four rungs validate on the same 180 held-out
wings. Reducer: `results/scalelaw_reduce_2026-10-08.py`, the 2026-09-27
reducer with one repair, the fit's fixed starting floors (0.02, 0.03)
clipped to the floor bound 0.9 x best, which the wing floor near 0.032
had put out of bounds for some bootstrap draws (the DrivAerML fit is
reproduced to every digit). Lane list
`results/campaigns_2026-09-21/sl/lanes_plus_shl_2026-10-08.tsv`; artifact
`results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json` (both datasets).

**The 1,260-wing rung** (two-seed means, seeds in parentheses). ISLA
0.0362 (0.0358 / 0.0366), 0.0340 (0.0333 / 0.0348), 0.0345 (0.0346 /
0.0345) at 192 / 384 / 768; GeoTransolver 0.0342 (0.0344 / 0.0340), 0.0348
(0.0333 / 0.0363), 0.0329 (0.0333 / 0.0325) at 256 / 512 / 1,024. The
widest ISLA is not the best at this rung (384 wide leads its grid by 1.5
percent over 768), the first rung where that happens for ISLA; the widest
GeoTransolver, not the best at 35 and 210 wings, leads at 510 and 1,260.
Across the grid at 1,260 wings GeoTransolver-1024 leads ISLA-384 by 3
percent and GeoTransolver-256 leads ISLA-192 by 6 percent.

**The fits.** ISLA: $\varepsilon_\infty$ 0.0269 (bootstrap 16th to 84th
percentiles 0.000 to 0.028; upper bound 0.0306 not reached), $a$ 2.19,
$\alpha$ 0.840 (0.817 to 0.863), $b$ 2.21, $\beta$ 0.39 (0.03 to 1.27), RMS
relative residual 2.3 percent, **accepted**. GeoTransolver: $\varepsilon_\infty$
0.000 (0.000 to 0.028), $a$ 1.60, $\alpha$ 0.847 (0.811 to 0.882), $b$
0.041, $\beta$ 0.018 (0.015 to 1.43), RMS 1.7 percent, **accepted**. The
two data exponents differ by 0.006 against a bootstrap spread of 0.07
(the same). The two parameter exponents differ by 0.38 against a spread
of 1.4, which is not a statement about $\beta$: with three widths and a
sixteen-fold parameter range on each, $\beta$ is unidentified on both
fits, and GeoTransolver's fit has used that freedom to put the floor into
the parameter term ($\beta$ near zero makes $b\,P^{-\beta}$ a constant of
about 0.030 at these widths, and $\varepsilon_\infty$ then sits at its lower
bound of zero). Read as a floor, both architectures approach about 0.027
to 0.030 on the wings. The local exponents between adjacent rungs fall
for every width and both models: ISLA 0.50 / 0.57 / 0.52 (35 to 210), 0.31
/ 0.28 / 0.35 (210 to 510), 0.18 / 0.22 / 0.13 (510 to 1,260);
GeoTransolver 0.45 / 0.46 / 0.47, 0.25 / 0.23 / 0.30, 0.14 / 0.10 / 0.11,
the signature of an approach to a floor on the wings as on the cars. The
gain from the widest over the narrowest width by rung: ISLA 2 / 6 / 8 / 5
percent, GeoTransolver -3 / 2 / 6 / 4 percent.

**Against the DrivAerML half.** The data exponent is 0.84 to 0.85 on the
wings against 1.28 to 1.30 on the cars: the wing error approaches its
floor more slowly in the case count, and the two architectures share the
exponent on both datasets. ISLA's floors are 0.0356 (cars) and 0.0269
(wings); GeoTransolver's are 0.0365 on the cars (on its bound) and
unseparated on the wings. The compute-optimal crossover $n^\ast$ at the
scaling study's base width, where the fitted data and parameter terms are
equal, is 200 cars for ISLA at 192 wide and **1,819 wings**, beyond the
measured range: on the wings every unit of compute belongs to cases
throughout the range measured. GeoTransolver's wing $n^\ast$ of 106 is not
a crossover but the case count at which its data term falls below the
constant its parameter term has become.

**Bars.** Law accepted (RMS below 3 percent) on both datasets for ISLA
and on the wings for GeoTransolver (its DrivAerML fit stays at 3.3
percent); exponents the same within the bootstrap on both datasets for
$\alpha$, vacuous for $\beta$; the compute-optimal split reported per
dataset. The two-dataset rule is met for the law and the data exponent.
Chapter 15's compute-allocation section (@sec-compute-allocation) now
carries both datasets in one figure and two tables; the ISLA reference
twins at 1,260 wings (`rb_hl_isla_full_seed42/43`, at epoch 463 of 500
today) will add the 1,260-wing row to the HiLiftAeroML chapter's ladder
when they finish and score.

## 2026-10-08 — PATCH-SDF verdict: the exact finite-patch geometry is the best built-in channel natively (16 / 13 / 7 percent better than the nearest reference, better than the kernel forms on pressure and velocity) and its channel is exactly re-panelization invariant, but the trained model moves 0.6 to 0.9 percent posed and degrades 21 to 35x under the 400-segment coarsening with the channel's share at 0.55 to 0.80; the gate stays closed, and the mechanism is the gaps of a sparse boundary draw, not the edge {#sec-nb-patch-sdf-verdict}

**Setting.** The two `sp_af_patch_*` lanes of @sec-nb-patch-sdf-prereg
(query_geometry="patch", snapshot code_v25, the campaign configuration on
AirfRANS 2-D with the stored signed-distance inputs, 500 epochs, lr
3.75e-4, LHR) trained without a trace of trouble and were scored today
under the native and posed protocols (float32, 200 held-out cases) and
through the AirfRANS resampling probe with the native-geometry swap
(`kernel/char/af_geo_sp`, both coarsening laws and both re-panelizations)
and its chordwise split (`af_geo_sp_le`). The probe's form-agnostic
recorder had to learn the new geometry function first (it patched the
nearest form and asserted on zero calls, the same fault the two-sided
kernel form met on 2026-10-07). Artifact
`results/char/patch_sdf_lanes_2026-10-08.json` (generator
`patch_sdf_lanes_2026-10-08.py`; bars computed there).

**Native and posed** (pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity). Patch 0.0306
/ 0.0148 / 0.0295 (seed 42) and 0.0287 / 0.0150 / 0.0289 (seed 43), two-seed
means 0.0296 / 0.0149 / 0.0292, against the nearest reference's 0.0352 /
0.0172 / 0.0315 (seeds 0.0369 / 0.0335, 0.0167 / 0.0177, 0.0317 / 0.0312):
**both seeds beat the reference's seed range on every field**, by 16, 13
and 7 percent on the means (bar (iii) passes with room), and the form beats
the relaunched one-sided kernel lanes (0.0314 / 0.0168 / 0.0284 and 0.0306
/ 0.0152 / 0.0288) on pressure and velocity and ties them on eddy
viscosity. Against the baselines this is the smallest pressure gap an
ISLA built-in channel has shown on AirfRANS (GeoTransolver-256 0.0266,
11 percent ahead, where the nearest reference trailed by 32 percent),
velocity 2.5x ahead of GeoTransolver's 0.0378 and eddy viscosity level
with its 0.0293. **Posed over native: 1.006 / 1.003 / 0.999 and 1.009 /
1.004 / 1.000 (bar (i), within 1.005, fails on pressure for both seeds).**
The geometry probes predicted this: the distance is pose-invariant to
1e-5 chord in float32, but within one radius of a vertex two patches tie
exactly and rounding picks one patch's normal as the direction (posed RMS
(1 - cos u) 0.04 to 0.05 in the near and wake bands against the nearest
form's 0.002 to 0.01), and the trained model reads that as two thirds of a
percent on pressure. The nearest form reproduces its native numbers to
five digits; the two-sided kernel form to four.

**Coarsening and refinement.** Under the 400-segment coarsening the patch
lanes degrade **21.1 / 18.2 / 9.7x (uniform law) and 22.4 / 16.7 / 10.5x
(length law)** on seed 42 and 35.0 / 17.4 / 5.9x and 33.6 / 17.2 / 4.9x on
seed 43, more than any form before them (one-sided kernel 5.7 to 12.8x,
two-sided 5.6 to 7.6x, nearest 9.6 to 15.8x). Restoring the native
geometry returns them to 2.7 / 1.8 / 1.9x and 4.0 / 2.6 / 2.0x (seed 42),
3.1 / 1.8 / 2.1x and 4.0 / 2.6 / 1.9x (seed 43), the slice states' share
that every form pays, so **the built-in channel's share of the log excess
is 0.55 to 0.80 (bar (ii), below 0.1, fails)**, the same band as the
kernel forms' 0.33 to 0.85 and the nearest form's 0.52 to 0.85. Under the
two re-panelizations the lanes read 0.953 to 1.013 of native, with the
native-geometry swap changing nothing (0.954 / 1.003 / 0.990 against 0.953
/ 1.002 / 0.990; shares 0.00 to 0.03 where the excess is measurable):
**the channel itself is exactly invariant to re-panelization**, as the
exact distance to an unchanged polyline must be, and the 5 percent
improvement of one seed's pressure under the uniform split is the slice
states' response to twice the tokens.

**Where the coarsening sensitivity lives, and why.** The chordwise split
restores the native geometry on one band of the queries at a time. For the
kernel forms (@sec-nb-soft-geo-verdict) the band behind x = 0.9 recovered
most of the excess and the other two recovered nothing: the sign and
direction flips at the sharp trailing edge. For the patch form the order
reverses: the trailing-edge band recovers little (21.1 to 18.3x on
pressure, 18.2 to 17.3x on velocity under the uniform law, seed 42), the
mid-chord band recovers the most (21.1 to 14.1x, 18.2 to 8.6x) and the
leading-edge band recovers the length law's velocity excess almost
entirely (16.7 to 5.2x). **The trailing-edge mechanism is fixed, and a
larger one has taken its place along the whole wall.** The geometry
probes name it: a Poisson subsample of the cells leaves gaps between the
measure-stretched patches (at a 40 percent keep rate about one near-wall
query in seven sits over a gap), and over a gap the exact distance to the
patch set is the distance to the nearest rim, 10 to 300 times the wall
distance for the queries that matter most (near-wall RMS change 1.8e-3
chord against the plane kernel's 4.5e-4, which extrapolates the
neighbours' tangent planes across the gap). A model trained on the exact
distance keys its boundary-layer prediction to that distance sharply and
is unforgiving when the sample lies about it; the kernel forms trained
on a smoothed distance and the nearest form on a biased one, and both
degrade less. Exactness on the native mesh and robustness to a sparse
draw pull in opposite directions for this channel.

**Verdict.** Bars (i) and (ii) fail, (iii) passes, re-panelization passes
for the channel and nearly for the lane. The SOFT-GEO gate stays closed
and the architecture frozen. What the result adds to the program's
picture: (1) the exact signed distance to the measure-defined patches is
the most accurate built-in channel measured, and it reproduces the stored
field on the native mesh, so a dataset's stored signed-distance input can
in principle be replaced by it where the boundary is kept whole; (2) a
built-in channel for a *sampled* boundary needs the gap-bridging that the
tangent-plane kernel has, and the kernel needs the edge handling the patch
form has (rim-clamped distances, the topological side), so the next
candidate, if the gate is reopened, is a composite: the plane offset of
the nearest patch across gaps of up to one token spacing and the patch
distance beyond, with the winding-number side; (3) alternatively, the
sampler can be made hole-free: a systematic (Morton-ordered) subsample
has gaps bounded by one spacing, where a Poisson draw's are not, and the
class already has that sampler (@sec-nb-quadvar-prereg); whether the
protocol should test coarsening under it as well is Peter's call, since
the protocol's Poisson law was chosen for its exact inclusion
probabilities. The `patch` form stays in the library as a research arm
beside `soft` and `smooth` until Peter rules on the three; the three-
dimensional form is not written.

and 0.78 against GeoTransolver; at 21 geometries 0.98 and 0.97. From 510 to
1,260 wings the reference's pressure error falls from 0.0404 to 0.0350 (a
factor 1.15) and GeoTransolver-512's from 0.0382 to 0.0348 (1.10). The
scaling grid's ISLA lane of the same width at 100,000 cells scores 0.0340
(0.0333 / 0.0348) at 1,260 wings, so the 200,000-cell pair is within its
seed spread (1.03), consistent with SCALE-HL's cells-flat reading. The
training-law twin: the reference trained under the area-proportional law
scores 0.1459 (0.1483 / 0.1436) on the uniform draw against 0.1460 (0.1456
/ 0.1465) for the uniform-trained reference, a factor 1.00 (seed-paired
1.02 and 0.98), where the 192-wide lanes read 1.01 and the DrivAerML
reference twin 1.05 (@sec-nb-refboard-area-twin).

**Why it matters.** Four readings change. (1) The GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA
case ladder reads 0.71 / 0.90 / 0.95 / 0.99 at 35 / 210 / 510 / 1,260
wings: the deficit against the parameter match closes to parity at the
full pool. It does not close against GeoTransolver's best lane there,
GeoTransolver-256 at 1e-3 with a tenth of ISLA's parameters, which leads by
8 percent on the one rung where its better rate flips to 1e-3. (2) The
fixed-angle rung moves most: the reference is 22 percent better than the
192-wide lane (0.0234 against 0.0300), so GeoTransolver's lead shrinks from
0.69 to 0.89 and Transolver reaches parity (1.02 on pressure, 0.98 on
velocity and wall shear). (3) The geometry ladder barely moves (0.67 and
0.98 against 0.68 and 0.95 for the 192-wide lanes): held-out geometry is
where the reference configuration buys nothing over 192 wide, and the
4-geometry deficit stands as the largest on the dataset. (4) The
reference's training-law factor on the wings is 1.00, so the "weakly
dependent" qualification rests on the DrivAerML twin's 1.05 alone. The
preregistered bar for an ISLA advantage (baseline ÷ ISLA of at least 1.10
with ISLA lower on two thirds of the cases) is reached on no rung. Every
row of the chapter 8 wing ladder now holds the earlier ISLA reference, and
no "192 wide" row remains.

**Chapters.** Chapter 8: the case ladder gains the 1,260 row, the geometry
and fixed-angle rows read the reference twins, the lede, the reading
paragraph and both captions are restated, and the GeoTransolver-256
best-pair ratio at 1,260 wings stands beside the parameter-matched one.
Chapter 3: the training-law qualification quotes the wing twin's factor
beside the cars'. Chapter 16: the wing sentence says parity at 1,260.
Ledger: REF-BOARD DONE, P200KFLEET DONE (its 1,260-wing ISLA point is this
twin), MAINLINE's reference-configuration gate met.

**What is next.** Nothing on this node. The remaining wing question, why
the baselines gain more than ISLA from a recurring geometry at small
training sets, stays with the WING-MECH record and the open questions of
chapter 16.

## 2026-10-09 — Ruling: the soft, smooth and patch query-geometry forms are deleted from the ISLA library; the nearest form is the only built-in geometry and is no longer an option {#sec-nb-geometry-forms-deleted}

**Setting.** An interior ISLA model computes each prediction point's
built-in signed distance and direction to the boundary from the boundary
tokens. The class form is the exact nearest token's distance signed by its
normal (`nearest_boundary_geometry`). SOFT-GEO added two kernel-average
forms (`soft`, `smooth`; @sec-nb-soft-geo-verdict) and PATCH-SDF an exact
finite-patch form with the winding-number side (`patch`;
@sec-nb-patch-sdf-verdict). Both studies refuted their forms against the
pre-registered discretization gate, and both verdicts left the forms in
the library as research arms pending Peter's ruling.

**The ruling and what changed.** Peter ruled today that the unused forms
are deleted. The library now holds the nearest form only, and the
`query_geometry` and `query_geometry_width` constructor parameters are
gone rather than fixed, by the rule that settled options are hard-coded
and nothing is shimmed. Removed: `soft_boundary_geometry` with its Triton
accumulation kernel and chunked fallback, `patch_boundary_geometry` with
its chunked form, the `QueryGeometry` type, the forward branches and
validation in the model, the docstring passages, and every test of the
deleted forms (1,137 lines across `geometry.py`, `model.py` and
`test_isla_interior_geometry.py`; the nearest-form and search tests are
kept unchanged). A repository grep outside the book and the results tree
finds no remaining reference; the recipe never exposed the option. The
ISLA suite on CPU passes (143 passed, 42 CUDA-gated skips).

**Consequences.** A checkpoint saved with `query_geometry` in its
arguments no longer loads (an unexpected-keyword error at construction),
as intended; the lanes that trained those forms (`sq_af_*`, `sr_af_*`,
`sp_af_*`) stay reproducible from the cluster snapshots code_v21 to
code_v25, which carry the forms, and their evidence stays in the
artifacts (`results/char/soft_geo_lanes_2026-10-07.json`,
`results/char/patch_sdf_lanes_2026-10-08.json`,
`results/char/patch_sdf_probes_2026-10-08.json`) and in the two verdict
entries. Chapter 7's paragraph on the two tested replacements is
unchanged, since it reports what was measured. Future lanes need a new
snapshot of the library, which the AeroZoo benchmark will produce.

## 2026-10-09 — AEROZOO pre-registration: ISLA, ISLA-DTT and GeoTransolver on AeroZoo v1.2's interior task (the boundaries with their prescribed values in, the interior fields out), in distribution and with a geometry bank, an enclosure family or a Reynolds range held out; a new chapter {#sec-nb-aerozoo-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Setting.** Peter's instruction of 2026-10-09: take the ISLA architecture
as it is and the ISLA-DTT variant, test them on the AeroZoo v1.2 dataset
on the interior prediction task (given a well-posed PDE problem from the
boundaries with only their prescribed values, predict the interior
fields), optionally on the surface task (the same inputs, every solution
field on the boundaries), compare against GeoTransolver, and put the
results into a new chapter. AeroZoo (Peter's dataset, generator
`~/gh/aerozoo`, release v1.2 of 2026-10-08) is a corpus of 3,816
time-averaged transition-SST RANS solutions, each around a different body
in its own enclosure at its own scale and Reynolds number, built to stress
geometric and physical diversity: eight geometry banks (procedural blobs,
cars, streamlined bodies, airframes, two Blender banks, a CAD bank and two
mascots), four enclosure families (external boxes with five
boundary-condition profiles, two opposed-hemisphere and opposed-sphere
enclosures, internal ducts), five Reynolds decades from $10^3$ to $10^8$,
and bodies whose surface is partly no-slip and partly slip. Every sample is
a PhysicsNeMo `DomainMesh` that carries the boundary-value problem which
produced it: four boundary meshes keyed by boundary-condition type
(`inlet`, `outlet`, `no_slip`, `slip`) with the prescribed values as
per-face data, an interior point cloud of 0.6 to 24 million cell centroids
(median 5.0 million) with cell volumes and seven mean-flow fields, and
dimensional global data (density, viscosity, the inlet velocity, a
reference speed, length and dynamic pressure). The release's 22 frozen
splits place cases by a hash of the geometry, so no geometry crosses
train, validation and test. The in-distribution split `full` holds 2,713 /
386 / 716 complete cases; the held-out splits train on everything but one
family and test on it (seven geometry banks, four enclosure families, two
Reynolds splits, five box profiles, the body layout). This is the first
dataset in the program whose cases differ in enclosure, scale and Reynolds
number at once, and the first on which a whole family is held out by
construction.

**Question.** On a dataset built for diversity, how do the three
architectures rank on the interior task in distribution, and how much does
each one's error grow when a geometry bank, an enclosure family or a
Reynolds range it never saw is held out?

**Task definition (the inputs are PDE data only).** Inputs: the four
boundary meshes (positions, normals and areas computed from the
triangles), a one-hot of the boundary-condition type per face, the
prescribed values per face (the inlet velocity and its four turbulence
scalars, the outlet gauge pressure and its reverse-flow fallback values,
the wall velocity), and the global data that pose the problem (the inlet
velocity direction, the Reynolds number as $\log_{10}(U_\mathrm{ref}
L_\mathrm{ref}/\nu)$ standardized by $(\cdot - 5.5)/1.5$, and the inlet
turbulence values as globals). Not inputs: `body_id` (a label of which
wall is the body; the no-slip operator is the same on the enclosure and on
the body), the solution and derived fields, the diagnostics and identity
blocks. Targets: velocity (rank 1), gauge pressure, turbulent kinematic
viscosity, turbulent kinetic energy and specific dissipation rate (rank 0),
nondimensionalized per case by the reference speed $U_\mathrm{ref}$, the
dynamic pressure $q_\mathrm{ref}$, $U_\mathrm{ref} L_\mathrm{ref}$,
$U_\mathrm{ref}^2$ and $U_\mathrm{ref}/L_\mathrm{ref}$; the intermittency
and the momentum-thickness Reynolds number are the transition model's
internal variables and are not targets. Coordinates are divided by
$L_\mathrm{ref}$ and centered for every model. The surface task is
pre-registered as the optional second phase with the same inputs and the
boundary solution fields plus the wall shear on `no_slip` as targets; it
needs a target-extraction change in the recipe and runs only after the
interior task is scored.

**Protocol.** The reporting protocol of the book, adapted to the four
boundaries: 200,000 interior prediction points per case drawn uniformly at
random, and 50,000 boundary faces per boundary-condition type drawn
uniformly within the type (at most 200,000 boundary tokens; a type with
fewer faces is kept whole), with Horvitz-Thompson measures. The release
stores interior points in OpenFOAM cell order, which is spatially coherent
(on case `case-0000000000000000000-a48a547f8d4c` a contiguous block of
200,000 of 5.87 million rows covers 8 to 42 percent of the domain's
bounding box against 98 percent for a random draw), and the recipe's reader
draws the interior subsample as one contiguous block, so training reads a
row-permuted copy of every interior (`kernel/aerozoo/aerozoo_shuffle.py`:
one random permutation per case, seeded by the case id; boundaries, global
data and sidecars are symlinks into the release; after the permutation a
block covers 97 to 99 percent of the box). Models at the reference
configurations the characterization campaign fixed for the DrivAerML
Volume task: ISLA (512 wide, 12 layers, 512 slices, cosine routing,
learning rate 3.75e-4, per-block compile, the built-in nearest geometry and
no stored distance field), GeoTransolver's volume configuration (256 wide,
12 layers, 256 slices) with its local embedding of coordinates, the signed
distance and its gradient to the no-slip walls and the signed distance to
the slip walls, all computed from the sampled boundary, and a global vector
of the inlet direction, the standardized log Reynolds number and the four
inlet turbulence globals; ISLA-DTT in the form the Barnes-Hut fork
confirms after its parity lanes (provisionally the forest tree read at
theta 1, exactly query independent). Target statistics for the loss are
pooled over the training side of the split in use. Two seeds (42, 43).
Epochs: 250 for every model and split, chosen so that the `full` split's
2,713 training cases give 678,000 steps, within 8 percent of the 1,260-wing
rung's 630,000 at the protocol's 500 epochs; the held-out splits train on
2,100 to 3,100 cases and keep the same epoch count. Scoring: float32, the
training draw law, every field's relative L2 per case averaged over the
cases, exactly as the DrivAerML Volume task is scored; model selection on
the validation side only; the test side scored once. Both stability
populations (`mean_stable`, `mean_unstable`) stay in and are reported
separately.

**Lanes.** Phase 1: `full` for ISLA and GeoTransolver, two seeds each
(four lanes), ISLA-DTT added when its form is confirmed. Phase 2a, the
held-out families with the clearest mechanism: `family_non_box` (train on
external boxes, test on the three other enclosures), `reynolds` (train
below $10^6$, test above) and `bank_blobs` (the largest bank held out),
each trained from its own training side, three models, two seeds. Phase 2b,
the remaining held-out splits, only if Phase 2a shows the models' penalties
differing by more than seed noise. AGA, short-queue chains with
checkpoint resume; LHR with a dataset copy if AGA cannot schedule.

**Predictions and falsifiers.** (P1, in distribution, the `full` test
side) GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is at least 1.2 on velocity and at most 0.9 on
pressure, the pattern of both existing interior datasets (velocity 1.4 and
2.2, pressure 0.76 and 0.87); falsified if the velocity ratio is below 1.1
or the pressure ratio above 1.0. (P2, the enclosure held out) ISLA's
penalty, its `family_non_box` test error divided by its `full` test error
on the same fields, is at least 20 percent smaller than GeoTransolver's;
the mechanism is that ISLA reads the enclosure as boundary tokens with
their condition types where GeoTransolver sees it only through the
distance fields and the extent of the point cloud; falsified if ISLA's
penalty is not smaller than GeoTransolver's. (P3, the Reynolds range and
the held-out bank) no directional prediction; both are recorded. (P4)
ISLA-DTT's `full` test error is within 5 percent of ISLA's on every field,
the fork's parity claim carried to a new dataset; falsified beyond that.
A difference between models counts only if both seeds order the same way
and the seed-mean ratio is outside 1 ± 0.05.

**What is next.** The recipe work (dataset yaml, the boundary
harmonization and nondimensional types, the manifest and statistics
scripts), a cluster snapshot of the library and recipe after the
query-geometry deletion, the shuffled copy (AGA job 1171835), then the
Phase 1 lanes. The chapter is written when Phase 1 is scored and extended
with Phase 2.

::: {.callout-warning}

0.9 s), the eight Reynolds and blob-bank lanes waited in the normal

and the validation trajectories every ten epochs. (iii) Per-case labels
(`case_labels.py` -> `case_labels.json`, 3,816 cases): the release's

the enclosure (2,741 external boxes, 391 opposed hemispheres, 381 opposed
spheres, 303 internal ducts), the body layout (1,233 all no-slip, 2,422
with slip bands), the Reynolds decade (about 800 cases per decade from

0.0280 / 0.0141 / 0.0308 against 0.0258 / 0.0141 / 0.0307) but lost pose
invariance: under the posed protocol its error rose 1.9x, 1.25x and 3.3x,

## 2026-10-10 — AEROZOO amendment: the query-population shift becomes a scoring protocol of the benchmark for all three arms, with its predictions written before any AeroZoo score exists {#sec-nb-aerozoo-qpop-amendment}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Setting.** The AEROZOO pre-registration (@sec-nb-aerozoo-prereg)
scores every arm natively: the training draw of 200,000 interior points
per case. The DrivAerML query-population instrument (@sec-nb-query-pop)
showed that the interacting ISLA's error on a fixed set of scored points
moves 3.5x to 24x when the rest of the query population changes
(wall-heavy or far-field companions), because the prediction points are
tokens whose learned routing mass enters the slice states, while the
Barnes-Hut fork's read-only tree read does not move at all (ratios
1.0000). The fork proposes, and this entry adopts, the same instrument
on AeroZoo, where the enclosures, scales and Reynolds numbers vary from
case to case and the query cloud is the solver's cell-centroid
distribution. Peter's steer, in his reply to the fork's status report
of 2026-10-10 as that session relayed it: "I think AeroZoo is the one
that I really want to do well on, and I anticipate query-independence
paying a lot more dividends there than it does on DrivAerML (where the
variation is really quite small)." Before any AeroZoo lane is scored,
the protocol and its predictions are fixed here.

**Protocol.** Scoring only, on the native checkpoints of the `full`
split's six lanes (ISLA, GeoTransolver and ISLA-DTT, two seeds each),
on the validation side (386 cases; the test side keeps its single
scoring), float32. Every metric is computed on the SAME scored set per
case, the first 100,000 native points, so that only the query population
around them differs: the native 200,000 points (the control); the
100,000 alone (half count at the training law); the native 200,000 plus
200,000 companions drawn uniformly in the interior's bounding box
(far-field heavy); the native 200,000 plus 200,000 companions resampled
from the native points with probability inversely proportional to the
distance to the no-slip walls (wall-heavy). The GeoTransolver arm's
three stored distances are recomputed for every swapped-in point from
the same sampled boundary, so it sees each condition through its own
inputs. The readout per arm, condition and field is the relative L2 on
the scored set divided by the control's, seed means with both seeds
reported, and the mean deviation of the predictions on the scored
points from the control's predictions. The fork adapts its DrivAerML
script to the AeroZoo recipe; the script and its run line enter
`kernel/aerozoo/` when it lands.

**Predictions and bars.** (Q1) ISLA-DTT is query-independent by
construction: every ratio is 1.000 to the roundoff of float32, on every
condition and field, both seeds; a ratio outside 1 ± 0.001 on any
condition falsifies the construction on this dataset. (Q2) ISLA moves
under the far-field and wall-heavy companions on every field, with the
far-field companions the larger move, as on DrivAerML; the half count
stays within 1 ± 0.05; no magnitude is predicted, since AeroZoo's cases
differ from the cars in enclosure and scale, and the two seeds are
expected to agree in direction. (Q3) GeoTransolver moves too: it forms
its slices over the point cloud it is given, and the authors of SMART
report the same failure of Transolver and AB-UPT under query shifts on
SHIFT-SUV; the magnitude relative to ISLA's is not predicted. A move
counts when both seeds order the same way and the seed-mean ratio is
outside 1 ± 0.05. These are measurements of a contract (query
independence), reported beside the native accuracy and never in place
of it; the pre-registered P1 to P4 verdicts are unchanged.

**Why it matters.** If Q1 holds and Q2 and Q3 fire, ISLA-DTT is the
only arm whose answer at a point does not depend on which other points
were asked, which is the operational property a solver-replacement
needs (a user queries a probe line, a plane, a region, not the training
draw), and the AeroZoo chapter states it as the tree read's case. If Q1
fails, the construction has a leak on this dataset and the fork is told
first.

## 2026-10-11 — AEROZOO first scores: every ISLA lane reaches a validation loss two to three times below GeoTransolver's by epoch 30-60, then an optimization event at epoch 43-50 raises its training and validation loss three- to four-fold for the rest of the run; the final checkpoints lose P1, the best checkpoints would win its velocity clause {#sec-nb-aerozoo-instability}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**The setting.** The AeroZoo benchmark (@sec-nb-aerozoo-prereg) trains
the reference ISLA, the read-only ISLA-DTT and GeoTransolver on the
interior task of AeroZoo v1.2 (the four boundary types with their
prescribed values in, the five interior fields velocity, pressure, eddy
viscosity, turbulence kinetic energy and specific dissipation out), 250
epochs at the architectures' reference rates (ISLA 3.75e-4, a tenfold
step at epoch 100), and scores the final checkpoint in float32 on the
training draw of 200,000 points. The first lanes finished on 2026-10-11:
ISLA on the `full` split (seed 43; seed 42 hours behind) and the ISLA
pair on the held-out-box split `family_non_box`. GeoTransolver's lanes
were at epoch 205-218 when this was written, so its float32 scores do
not exist yet; its training-time validation (bf16, every ten epochs)
stands in below, labeled as such.

**What the final checkpoints score (validation side, float32, relative
L2 in training units).** ISLA `full` seed 43 reads velocity 0.450,
pressure 0.760, eddy viscosity 0.799, turbulence kinetic energy 0.787
and specific dissipation 0.775 over the 386 validation cases; the
`family_non_box` pair reads 0.428 / 0.589 / 0.864 / 0.893 / 0.848 and
0.402 / 0.595 / 0.850 / 0.825 / 0.836 over 351. GeoTransolver's
training-time validation at epoch 200 reads velocity 0.34-0.35 and
pressure 0.46-0.49 on `full`, 0.33-0.34 and 0.42-0.45 on
`family_non_box`. **Under the pre-registered rule (the final checkpoint
of each lane) GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is about 0.76 on velocity and 0.63
on pressure on `full`, and P1 is falsified as written** (its
falsification bar was a velocity ratio below 1.1 or a pressure ratio
above 1.0). The test-side scoring that the standing is defined on waits
for GeoTransolver's lanes; nothing above changes the order.

**The trajectory is the finding.** Every ISLA lane, on every split,
reaches its validation-loss minimum of 0.036-0.048 between epoch 30 and
60 (velocity 0.20-0.23, pressure 0.18-0.54 in the trainer's bf16
validation), then its loss rises more than twofold within ten to twenty
epochs and stays at 0.11-0.15 to epoch 250; GeoTransolver's validation
loss never goes below 0.09. **The training loss rises with the
validation loss, so this is an optimization event and not overfitting:**
the per-epoch mean step loss of ISLA `full` seed 43 is 0.0426 at epoch
40, 0.0757 at 45, 0.119 at 50 and 0.15 from epoch 60 on, and the
tenfold rate step at epoch 100 does not bring it back. The first epoch
whose mean step loss exceeds 1.5 times its running minimum is 44 and 45
on `full`, 43 on `family_non_box` (seed 42; seed 43's detector is
confounded by the spike cases below), 43 and 47 on `reynolds`, 50 on
`bank_blobs`, and 54 and 65 for the ISLA-DTT `full` pair: 23,000 to
30,000 optimizer steps at the constant rate. GeoTransolver has no such
event on any split: its per-epoch mean step loss falls from 0.077 at
epoch 30 to 0.047 at epoch 100 and 0.014-0.019 at the end, while its
validation loss drifts up from 0.09 to 0.11, which is ordinary
overfitting.

**It is not the DeepJEB++ signature.** On DeepJEB++ the instability was a
total routing collapse (one to five active slices per block,
@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-mechanism). The
routing probe on two checkpoints per lane (job 1199576; artifacts in
`results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/probe/routing_*.json`) finds no
block below 32 effective slices: ISLA `full` seed 43 goes from a
minimum and median of 147 and 299 effective slices across its twelve
blocks at epoch 31 to 36 and 194 at epoch 249, with the narrowing
concentrated in three blocks; the `family_non_box` lane goes from 133
and 271 to 87 and 202. Routing narrows partially after the event; it
does not collapse.

**The drift probe: the weights stall, no single tensor jumps.** The
checkpoint-drift probe (`probe/ckpt_drift.py`, job 1199719, artifacts
`probe/drift_*.json`) ranks every weight tensor by its relative change
between consecutive kept checkpoints, with a GeoTransolver lane as the
control. Across the transition no tensor jumps; what changes is the
motion of all of them. Before the event the total parameter norm of
ISLA `full` seed 43 grows by 9.1 per two epochs (336.8 at epoch 29 to
407.3 at epoch 45, mostly the block MLPs); from the transition pair on
the growth drops to 5.6, then 2.8, then 1 to 2 per two epochs, and the
relative change of the vector of per-tensor norms falls from 0.03 to
0.01. GeoTransolver's total norm grows by 20 per two epochs throughout
(402 at epoch 29 to 797 at epoch 69) with no event. The same stall
follows the transition in the other three probed ISLA lanes (seed 42
from epoch 47, `family_non_box` from epochs 57-61, ISLA-DTT from epoch
73). The one parameter that moves with the event in all four lanes is
the gain of the head-frame prototype module, the scalar that bounds how
far the output-frame prototypes may move from their seeds per sample:
0.19 to 0.26, 0.34 and 0.38 across epochs 43-49 on seed 43, 0.21 to
0.30 and 0.38 across 45-53 on seed 42, 0.21 to 0.28 across 39-43 on
`family_non_box`, 0.22 to 0.29 across 63-65 on ISLA-DTT. On seed 43 it
returns to 0.20 at epochs 57-61 while the loss stays at 0.15, so it is
a correlate and not the cause by itself. The tenfold rate step at
epoch 100 does not bring the loss back (median step loss 0.130 at
epoch 98, 0.123 at 102, 0.109 at 249), so the iterate sits in a worse
basin rather than oscillating about the old one. The degradation is
global over cases: 99 percent of the 386 validation cases are worse on
velocity at the final checkpoint than at the best (median ratio 1.9,
tenth to ninetieth percentile 1.24 to 3.18), in every bank (1.7 to
2.3) and every enclosure family (1.2 to 2.6), with the mean-unstable
cases degrading more than the stable ones (2.55 against 1.71). **The
mechanism is a loss of plasticity after 23,000 to 30,000 steps at the
constant rate, uniform over the data; what saturates is unmeasured.**

**The spike cases are a dataset finding, not the trigger.** The
per-step training loss has isolated spikes whose values are identical
across ISLA, ISLA-DTT and GeoTransolver for the same seed (the sampler's
order is seed-determined): about 5.2 on `full`, 4.3, 24 and 1,712.6 on
`family_non_box`, 2,086 on `bank_blobs`. The loss is a Huber loss on
standardized targets, so a step loss of 1,712 means the case's targets
sit about 1,700 standard deviations from the training mean on average:
a handful of training cases carry pathological fields. GeoTransolver
survives every one of them; ISLA survives the 1,712 case at epoch 24 in
the `family_non_box` seed-43 lane and transitions at epoch 44-45 on
`full` with no step loss above 1.5 in the preceding ten epochs. The
spikes therefore do not explain the event. Their identification
(subagent, `probe/outliers_*.py`, CPU job 1200497, artifacts
`probe/outliers.{json,txt}` and `probe/outliers_scan.jsonl`) reproduces
the sampler (seed plus epoch into `randperm`, drop-last truncation, the
rank-0 shard, a 1-based step counter, the logged loss being the
four-rank mean) and names one case per loss class, unanimous over every
spike, seed, arm and epoch. The 1,712 and 2,086 spikes are
`case-0000000000000001731-793b575a97a8` (cars bank, rectangular prism,
mean-unstable, Reynolds 3.1e7): one interior row carries a specific
dissipation of 5.4e11 per second, 1.2e10 standard deviations in the
`full` constants, while the case's other fields are ordinary (mean |z|
0.14 to 0.61). The 24 spike is case 2407 (blobs, mean-stable, one row
at 1.6e8 standard deviations) and the 4.3 to 5.7 spikes are case 2344
(blobs, mean-unstable, one row at 2.9e7). The loss formula checks to
the digit: the logged value is the four-rank mean of the seven-channel
mean of the unweighted Huber loss (delta 1) over the 200,000 sampled
rows, so a block that holds the worst row of case 1731 gives 6,850 / 4
= 1,712.6 in the held-out-box constants and 2,086 in the blob
constants. Case 1731 sits in the `full` validation split and the
`reynolds` test split, so the `full` lanes never trained on it; cases
2407 and 2344 are in the `full` test and training splits. **The
dataset's specific-dissipation field has a pervasive heavy tail, and
the three spike cases are its extreme:** across the 3,815 cases, 238
have a row above 1,000 standard deviations in omega, 110 above 10,000,
6 above a million; 571 of the 2,713 `full` training cases exceed either
a mean |z| of 3 or a max |z| of 100 on some field, and 24 percent of
those are labeled mean-unstable against a 26 percent base rate, so the
flags are not a stability marker. Beyond omega, 46 cases have a mean
|z| above 3 on pressure (the pressure-coefficient scale of fast cases)
and 36 on eddy viscosity (low-Reynolds cases in the opposed-hemisphere
and opposed-sphere enclosures). One consequence for the metric: the
per-case relative L2 of omega saturates at 1.0 when a single row
dominates the target norm (case 1731 scores exactly 1.00 on omega at
every checkpoint), so the omega column of every table is partly a count
of such cases rather than a measure of the field. A log transform or a
per-case clip of omega before standardization is the usual remedy;
that is a protocol change for every arm and waits for Peter with the
others.

**The best-checkpoint diagnostic (labeled, never the standing).** The
checkpoint at each lane's validation minimum (epoch 31 for `full` seed
43, 41 and 61 for the `family_non_box` pair), scored exactly like the
protocol on the validation side (`eval_bestval.sbatch`, job 1199537),
reads velocity 0.223, pressure 0.534, eddy viscosity 0.523, turbulence
kinetic energy 0.611 and specific dissipation 0.717 on `full`, and
0.203 / 0.195 / 0.515 / 0.649 / 0.744 and 0.201 / 0.184 / 0.533 /
0.674 / 0.728 on `family_non_box`: half the final checkpoint's velocity
error on every lane and a third of its pressure error on the held-out-box
split. **Against GeoTransolver's end-of-training validation, ISLA at its
best checkpoint leads velocity by 1.5x on `full` and 1.65x on
`family_non_box`, trails pressure by 0.88x on `full` (the box enclosures,
which are the hard pressure cases) and leads it by 2.2-2.4x on
`family_non_box`.** The turbulence fields stay at 0.5-0.75 for ISLA even
at its best; GeoTransolver's are not yet scored in float32.

**What is asked of Peter.** The pre-registered standing is the final
checkpoint, and the chapter reports it as such. Two remedies are on the
table and both need his word: ISLA and ISLA-DTT lanes at half the
reference rate (1.875e-4, the DeepJEB++ exception made for this dataset
too; two seeds, `full` and `family_non_box` first), and a labeled
second table scored at the validation-loss minimum of every arm,
GeoTransolver included. The recommendation is both, with one caution
written down before the result: on DeepJEB++ the half rate moved the
collapse from epoch 4 to epochs 20-24 and did not remove it
(@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-halfrate-verdict), so a half-rate lane here that
transitions at epoch 90 instead of 45 confirms a rate-bound event
without curing it, and the drift probe's answer (which tensors move)
decides whether the cure is in the rate at all. No training arm
launches before his answer; the drift probe and the spike-case
identification proceed.

## 2026-10-11 — ISLA-DTT merged into psharpe/isla as an option: the read-only interior model and its forest read enter the book {#sec-nb-dtt-merged}

::: {.callout-warning}
**AeroZoo numbers withdrawn 2026-10-19** (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn); the rest of this entry stands.
:::

**The setting.** ISLA's interior task admits the prediction points as
interacting tokens, so a prediction at a point depends on the other
points requested with it (QUERY-POP, @sec-nb-query-pop: the error on
fixed scored points rises 15x to 24x when 200,000 far-field companions
join the request). The ISLA-DTT program (branch `psharpe/isla-dtt`,
2026-10-06 to 2026-10-11) built the alternative: passive prediction
points that read every layer's slices at matched depth and never write
into them (`query_independent=True`), a global read of every boundary
cell after each slice layer (`kernel_read="mean"`,
`kernel_read_radius=None`), and that read evaluated through a Barnes-Hut
forest of `ClusterTree`s built in the boundary's own frame at opening
angle theta = 1 (`kernel_read_theta=1`). Its brief, preregistration and
dated record live in `examples/cfd/isla/research/dtt/{BRIEF,PREREG,REPORT}.md`.

**What merged.** The library changes (`model.py`, `kernel_read.py`,
`tree_read.py` and their tests; the E6 scaffolds `kernel_read_cells` and
`read_final_boundary` deleted) are on `psharpe/isla` from commit
986aec3dc. ISLA-DTT is an option of the class. The interacting form stays
the class default and the configuration of every interior standing in
the book until two measurements decide otherwise: AeroZoo's P4 (ISLA-DTT
within 5 percent of ISLA, @sec-nb-aerozoo-prereg) and the
query-population protocol on that dataset
(@sec-nb-aerozoo-qpop-amendment).

**What the chapters now carry.** The architecture chapter describes the
read-only task, the global boundary read and the forest, with the
matched-depth control and the slice-doubling table
(@sec-arch-passive-decoder, @sec-arch-global-read, @sec-arch-tree-read,
@tbl-arch-read-depth) and the new constructor arguments in its switches
table. The DrivAerML chapter carries the read-only controls on the
Volume task (ISLA-DTT at 1.12 / 1.11 / 1.12 times ISLA's error on
pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity, passive points without a read at
1.14 / 1.31 / 1.68), the ladder of how much boundary a point reads
(@sec-interior-read-only, @tbl-interior-read-only,
@tbl-interior-read-ladder) and the query-population table with the
ISLA-DTT ratios of 1.0000 beside ISLA's 24x / 15x / 12x
(@tbl-interior-query-population; the pose-free forest's own car
checkpoints, LHR job 157560: every ratio 1.000000 on both seeds under the
half, far-field and near-wall requests, largest departure 8e-6, largest
prediction change on the shared points 4.7e-5). The AirfRANS chapter
carries the airfoil controls, where ISLA-DTT is 0.74 / 0.83 / 1.03 of
ISLA and matches the dense exact read (@sec-airfrans-read-only). The
using, limits, ideas and literature chapters no longer say that the class
has no query-independent decode. One number rests on a single
instrument: the read's car-scale cost comes from one GB300 bench (job
135330) and the AeroZoo training lanes.
