every arm beside the pre-registered final-checkpoint standing. The
specific-dissipation transform discussed in
@sec-nb-aerozoo-instability is not part of the relaunch: it would
change the training signal of the relaunched lanes while GeoTransolver's
keep the old one, so the rate stays the only variable that moves. It
remains a protocol change for every arm if wanted later.

**The half-rate lanes.** Eight lanes, rows 24-31 of the campaign's lane
table: `az_full_islahr_seed42/43`, `az_nonbox_islahr_seed42/43` on the
reference ISLA (snapshot code_v26) and `az_full_dtthr_seed42/43`,
`az_nonbox_dtthr_seed42/43` on the pose-free forest read (snapshot
code_dtt16, the overrides of the reference-rate DTT lanes), every other
setting identical to rows 0-5 and 16-19: 250 epochs, 200,000 points, the
StepLR tenfold step at epoch 100, no augmentation. They run in AGA's
normal queue (jobs 1219056-1219063) because the short queue is at its
cap, so their first links wait hours and their trained state is two to
four days off.

**Predictions, written before any of them has taken a step.** The
reference-rate event is a loss of the validation minimum at 23,000 to
30,000 optimizer steps (epochs 43-50) with the training loss rising
alongside, no routing collapse and a stall of the weights. (R1) If the
event is rate-bound in the way DeepJEB++'s was, the half-rate lanes lose
their minimum later, at roughly twice the step count (the validation
loss doubles its running minimum at an epoch above 60), and their final
checkpoints still trail their best. (R2) If the half rate cures it, no
half-rate lane doubles its running minimum through epoch 250 and the
final `full` checkpoints read velocity at or below 0.25 on the
validation side, the band the reference-rate lanes reached at their
best; under this outcome the pre-registered P1 re-read on the half-rate
arms would be GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA at or above 1.4 on velocity. (R3) If
the event recurs at the same epoch (doubling at or below epoch 60), the
cause is not the step count at this rate and the rate exception does
not help this dataset. The detector is the one of
@sec-nb-aerozoo-instability (first validation epoch whose loss exceeds
twice the running minimum, validation every ten epochs). ISLA-DTT's
reference-rate pair transitioned later (epochs 54 and 65), so its
half-rate pair is read against its own pair, not ISLA's.

**The best-checkpoint table.** Protocol, fixed before the scores exist:
for every Phase 1 and held-out-box lane of both architectures, the
checkpoint is the kept one after the trainer's validation-loss minimum
(validation every ten epochs in bfloat16; checkpoints at odd epochs, so
epoch E's minimum selects checkpoint E+1), scored exactly like the
final-checkpoint protocol on the test side, float32, the training draw;
the validation side is scored as well for the lanes that lack it. The
chosen epochs are 31 and 31 for ISLA `full`, 41 and 61 for ISLA
`family_non_box`, 81 and 121 for GeoTransolver `full`, 151 and 61 for
GeoTransolver `family_non_box` (seeds 42 and 43). GeoTransolver's
minima sit at epochs 60-150 and its validation loss drifts up by 5-10
percent afterwards, so its best checkpoints will read a few percent
better than its finals; ISLA's read about half the velocity error of
its finals on the validation side (@sec-nb-aerozoo-nonbox-scored). The
table is labeled as what it is: a selection by validation, not the
pre-registered standing, and it answers one question only, what each
architecture had learned on this dataset under the reference protocol
before its training protocol failed it, if it failed. Jobs
1219118-1219121 (`eval_bestval.sbatch`, `BESTVAL_SIDE=val|test`,
`runs_bestval/<run>/checkpoints` symlinks); records land in
`scores/<run>/bestval/` and `scores/<run>/bestval_test/`.

## 2026-10-13 — AEROZOO: the test-side best-checkpoint scorer had re-scored the validation split; fixed and resubmitted; GeoTransolver held-out validation sides in {#sec-nb-aerozoo-bestval-scorer-fix}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

The best-checkpoint table of @sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-prereg is scored by
`eval_bestval.sbatch`, which takes `BESTVAL_SIDE=val|test`. The first
test-side job (1230646, lane rows 0 1 4 5) produced records identical to
the validation-side ones: the script changed only the output root, and
its inference call still read `infer_split=val`, so it scored the 386
and 351 validation cases of the `full` and held-out-box splits a second
time. The check that caught it was the case count and the first sample
id of the fetched record against the validation record (same count,
same ids, different file hash). The fix mirrors `eval_test.sbatch`:
with the test side requested, the lane override `val_split=<split>.val`
becomes `<split>.test` and the inference reads `infer_split=test`. The
four wrong outputs were deleted on the cluster and locally and never
entered the reduction; the test side is resubmitted in the short queue
(jobs 1230869 for rows 0 1 4 5 and 1230870 for rows 2 3 6 7), and the
normal-queue copy that would have run the unfixed script was cancelled.

Also in: the validation sides of GeoTransolver's Reynolds pair and
blob-bank seed 42 (job 1230629; the ISLA lanes of those splits are still
training), and validation-side best checkpoints for GeoTransolver `full`
(epochs 81 and 121: 0.343 / 0.514 / 0.517 / 0.721 / 0.748 for velocity /
pressure / eddy viscosity / turbulent kinetic energy / specific
dissipation rate), GeoTransolver `family_non_box` seed 42 (epoch 151:
0.323 / 0.405 / 0.600 / 0.874 / 0.809) and ISLA `full` seed 42 (epoch
31; the pair now reads 0.220 / 0.455 / 0.506 / 0.617 / 0.707).
GeoTransolver's selected checkpoints read worse than its finals on
pressure and eddy viscosity (0.514 against 0.473, 0.517 against 0.462):
its validation loss is flat after epoch 80 and the bfloat16 minimum does
not pick the float32 best. Against GeoTransolver's final `full`
checkpoints on the validation side (0.345 / 0.473 / 0.462 / 0.783 /
0.739), ISLA's pre-event checkpoints lead on four fields and trail on
eddy viscosity (0.506 against 0.462); the chapter's lede now computes
that clause from the reduction instead of asserting "every field", and
the test-side table decides it. The reduction carries the half-rate arms
(`islahr`, `dtthr`), the two-sided best-checkpoint block, the
instability detector per lane and the R1-R3 remedy codes; the chapter
has the labeled best-checkpoint table `tbl-aerozoo-bestckpt` and draws

## 2026-10-13 — AEROZOO best-checkpoint table on the test side: ISLA's pre-event checkpoints lead GeoTransolver's best on every field in distribution and trail on every field with the enclosure held out {#sec-nb-aerozoo-bestckpt-verdict}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**The setting.** The pre-registered standing of the AeroZoo chapter
scores the final checkpoint of every lane
(@sec-nb-aerozoo-phase1-verdict), and every ISLA final checkpoint sits
after the optimization event of @sec-nb-aerozoo-instability. The remedy
entry (@sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-prereg) fixed a second, labeled reading
before its scores existed: for every Phase 1 and held-out-box lane of
both architectures, the kept checkpoint after the trainer's
validation-loss minimum, scored exactly like the protocol on the sealed
test side (float32, 200,000 points per case, two seeds). Those scores
are in (jobs 1230869 and 1230870 with the corrected scorer,
@sec-nb-aerozoo-bestval-scorer-fix); the chapter's table is
`tbl-aerozoo-bestckpt` and the reduction's block is `bestval`.

**In distribution (`full`, 716 test cases).** ISLA's checkpoints at
epoch 31 (both seeds) read 0.226 / 0.450 / 0.519 / 0.651 / 0.712 on
velocity / pressure / eddy viscosity / turbulent kinetic energy /
specific dissipation rate, against its finals' 0.458 / 0.792 / 0.792 /
0.815 / 0.792. GeoTransolver's own best checkpoints (epochs 81 and 121)
read 0.346 / 0.494 / 0.525 / 0.722 / 0.755, within three percent of its
finals except on eddy viscosity, where the final (0.482) is better.
Best against best, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is **1.53 / 1.10 / 1.01 / 1.11
/ 1.06**, with both ISLA seeds (0.224, 0.229) below both GeoTransolver
seeds (0.351, 0.342) on velocity; against GeoTransolver's finals the
pre-event ISLA leads on four fields and trails on eddy viscosity (0.519
against 0.482). The in-distribution direction of the P1 verdict is
therefore a property of the training protocol and not of what the
architecture learned. It is also not a vindication of P1 as written:
P1 predicted GeoTransolver ahead on pressure (ratio at or below 0.9),
and best against best ISLA leads on pressure too (1.10). This reading
is the labeled diagnostic the remedy entry promised, not a re-read of
P1; the pre-registered re-read is on the half-rate arms (R2).

**With the enclosure family held out (`family_non_box`, 1,074 non-box
test cases).** ISLA's best checkpoints (epochs 41 and 61, chosen on the
in-distribution validation boxes, where they read 0.202 on velocity)
read 0.684 / 0.671 / 0.976 / 1.043 / 1.599 on the held-out enclosures;
GeoTransolver's best (epochs 151 and 61) read 0.526 / 0.640 / 0.873 /
0.836 / 0.773. GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, best against best, is **0.77 /
0.95 / 0.89 / 0.80 / 0.48**: GeoTransolver leads on every field, by
1.3x on velocity and 2x on the specific dissipation rate, where ISLA's
value above one is worse than predicting the field mean. Per seed on
velocity ISLA reads 0.703 and 0.665 against GeoTransolver's 0.476 and
0.576, both GeoTransolver seeds below both ISLA seeds. From the
in-distribution validation boxes to the held-out enclosures, at these
checkpoints, ISLA's velocity error grows 3.4x (0.202 to 0.684) and its
pressure error 3.5x (0.189 to 0.671); GeoTransolver's grow 1.5x and
1.3x (0.350 to 0.526, 0.495 to 0.640; both seeds, the seed-43
validation value from job 1231142, in after the first draft of this
entry). GeoTransolver's
final checkpoints do better still on the held-out pressure (0.359
against its best-by-validation 0.640), so for GeoTransolver the
in-distribution validation minimum does not pick the checkpoint that
generalizes best; for ISLA the selection helps (0.684 against the
finals' 0.768 on velocity) but does not close the gap.

**Verdict.** The P2 reading, ISLA's held-out-enclosure penalty larger
than GeoTransolver's, is not a checkpoint artifact: it holds at both
architectures' best checkpoints on every field. The P1 reading in
distribution is one: before the event ISLA leads GeoTransolver's best
on every field. The two together say the optimization event costs ISLA
its in-distribution lead, and that even without it ISLA generalizes
worse than GeoTransolver from box enclosures to the other enclosure
families on this dataset. The chapter's lede and table compute these
clauses from the reduction.

**Also in.** GeoTransolver's Reynolds-range and blob-bank test sides

## 2026-10-14 — AEROZOO remedy, first read: no half-rate ISLA lane loses its validation minimum through epochs 50-90, so R3 is excluded; the lanes run on the LHR site {#sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-first-read}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**The setting.** The remedy of @sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-prereg trains
ISLA and ISLA-DTT at half the reference rate, 1.875e-4, on the `full`
and held-out-box splits (eight lanes), with three outcomes written
before any step: R1, the event comes later than at the reference rate
(the validation loss doubles its running minimum above epoch 60); R2,
no lane doubles through epoch 250 and the `full` finals read velocity
at or below 0.25; R3, a doubling at or below epoch 60, which would say
the event is not bound to the step count at this rate. The detector is
the one of @sec-nb-aerozoo-instability, read on the trainer's
validation every ten epochs.

**Where the lanes run.** AGA's short queue stalled cluster-wide from
14:40 EDT on 2026-10-13 (none of our chains ran for the next 20 hours;
a scheduler dry run put the restart at 08:00 EDT 2026-10-14 and the
queue missed it), so on Peter's word the eight half-rate lanes moved to
the LHR site, which mirrors AGA's absolute paths: the AeroZoo shuffled
copy was transferred there as real files (the AGA copy symlinks its
per-case metadata, global-data and boundary directories into the
release), 794,451 files and 1.481 TB in 62 minutes, verified with zero
itemized differences; the three lanes that had started on AGA resumed
from their epoch 25-27 checkpoints and the other five started fresh at
22:45 EDT. The LHR lanes step slower than on AGA: averaged by hour over
the first 18 hours there, the half-rate ISLA lanes take 1.0-1.3 s per
step (mean 1.2 s; 0.8-0.9 s in the quietest hours) against 0.68-0.69 s
on AGA, and the half-rate ISLA-DTT lanes 1.4-1.7 s (mean 1.55 s)
against 1.25 s, so 1.75 and 1.25 times slower (an earlier one-hour
benchmark that read 2.7 times slower sampled a loaded hour and the
links' warm-up). The cause is per-sample input: the reader touches
essentially the whole case per sample (107-581 MB over about 200
files) and the LHR NFS client serves that pattern at under 1 GB/s per
node, so the pace moves with the filesystem's load; loader workers (4
against 12), pinned memory and the four-GPU collective were each
measured and ruled out. One link died at
its first step on a stale NFS file handle and the chain resumed on
another node three minutes later. Records of all of this sit in the
site's `lhr_setup/` directory and in the campaign's status file.

**What the validation trajectories show.** At the reference rate the
detector fires at epochs 50-70 on the ISLA lanes (`full` seeds 42 and
43 at 60 and 50, held-out-box seeds at 60 and 70; by epoch 50 the
`full` pair read 0.081 and 0.136 against minima of 0.043 and 0.048).
At half the rate, through 2026-10-14 14:00 EDT, no ISLA lane has
doubled: the `full` pair reads 0.0392 at epoch 60 (minimum 0.0358 at
epoch 50) and 0.0359 at epoch 70 (a new minimum), the held-out-box
seed-42 lane 0.0344 at epoch 90 (minimum 0.0338 at 80), the
held-out-box seed-43 lane 0.0363 at epoch 50 (its minimum). Every
half-rate validation minimum so far sits below the corresponding
reference-rate lane's minimum (0.0427 and 0.0477 for the `full` pair).
The ISLA-DTT half-rate lanes are at epochs 30-40 (0.045-0.053) and
cannot be read yet; their reference-rate twins fired at epoch 80 on the
`full` split and never on the held-out-box split.

**Verdict so far.** R3 is excluded for every half-rate ISLA lane that
has reached epoch 60: the event does not recur at the same step count
when the rate is halved, so it is rate-bound in the sense the remedy
assumed. R1 against R2 stays open until a doubling appears or epoch 250
is reached (about 2026-10-16 at the LHR pace); under R2 the final
checkpoints are scored on both sides by the protocol and the
pre-registered P1 re-read (GeoTransolver ÷ half-rate ISLA at or above
1.4 on velocity) is taken. The chapter's half-rate paragraph, figure
curves and remedy codes are computed from the reduction (`remedy`
block), which now carries these lanes.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).

(@sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-first-read), twelve AeroZoo lanes still sat in
AGA's short queue as chain links waiting between runs: the ISLA
Reynolds-split pair (logged epochs 132 and 100), the ISLA blob-bank
pair (98 and 98), and the six ISLA-DTT lanes on the `full` split (218
and 218), the held-out-box split (225 and 225), the Reynolds split (166
and 174) and the blob-bank split (38 and 38). AGA ran none of them for

ours at 01:30 EDT on 2026-10-15), so on Peter's instruction, "if things
are stalled on AGA, migrate them over to LHR", the lanes moved.

**What was done.** The twelve AGA chain links were cancelled, so no
AeroZoo job remains on AGA. Each lane's run directory, with every
checkpoint (saved every two epochs; the best-checkpoint table needs
them), its training log and its metrics record, streamed from AGA's
datamover hosts to LHR's as one tar stream per directory: 0.49 TB in 76
minutes, about 14 MB/s per stream, zero stream errors. Every copy was
checked against the source by file count and total byte size before
anything was submitted (twelve of twelve match). The lanes were then
submitted on LHR at 15:59 EDT as singleton chains in the normal queue
with 3 h 59 min links, because the short queue's cap of twenty
submitted jobs per user already holds the eight half-rate chains. A
dry run had placed the first link at 19:26 EDT; the queue had idle
nodes and all twelve started between 16:00 and 16:05 EDT. The lane
rows themselves are unchanged (same code snapshots, four loader
workers, same seeds), so each lane resumes from its latest complete
checkpoint and the per-epoch record continues; only the wall-clock pace
changes, by the 1.75 (ISLA) and 1.25 (ISLA-DTT) factors measured on
this site (@sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-first-read). The AGA run directories
stay in place as the pre-migration record and must not be resumed
there, or the two copies diverge.

**Acceptance.** Every lane's pre-flight found its newest checkpoint
intact and the trainer resumed one epoch above it: the ISLA Reynolds
lanes at epochs 132 and 100, the ISLA blob-bank lanes at 98 and 98,
ISLA-DTT on `full` at 218 and 218, on the held-out-box split at 226 and
226, on the Reynolds split at 166 and 174, on the blob-bank split at 38
and 38; all twelve logged training steps within six minutes of their
link start with no traceback or error line, and the fused geometry
kernel resolved on every rank.

**What follows.** At the measured LHR pace (about 17 minutes per
`full` epoch for ISLA-DTT, 11-15 minutes per epoch for the other lanes)
the ISLA-DTT held-out-box pair finishes late on 2026-10-14 and the

and the ISLA-DTT Reynolds lanes need about a day, and the ISLA-DTT
blob-bank pair about two. Every score
for these lanes (validation and test sides, the best-checkpoint rows,

since the fleet's scoring pump does not run there; the campaign's
fetcher pulls their records from LHR.

## 2026-10-14 — AEROZOO by enclosure family: ISLA's deficit sits in the spherical enclosures; Peter's rulings on the remedies; three tests pre-registered (the ISLA-DTT pressure read, one distance per boundary condition, a doubled training budget) {#sec-nb-aerozoo-family-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**The family breakdown.** A diagnostic read of the per-case test
records that already exist: the errors of the `full` and
`family_non_box` lanes grouped by the enclosure family of
`case_labels.json` (seed means of case means, float32, the training
draw). ISLA's deficit against GeoTransolver is not spread over the
dataset. At the labeled best checkpoints
(@sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-prereg), GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA in distribution
reads 1.68 on velocity and 1.30 on pressure over the 508 box cases and
1.40 and 1.21 over the 58 ducts, but 1.02 and 0.37 over the 82
hemispheres and 0.96 and 0.24 over the 68 spheres. With the enclosure
held out it reads 1.18 and 2.63 over the 303 ducts, 0.68 and 0.33 over
the 391 hemispheres and 0.35 and 0.30 over the 380 spheres. ISLA's
pressure error is 0.42 to 0.58 in every family in distribution, while
GeoTransolver's runs from 0.10 on spheres to 0.71 on ducts. The final
checkpoints show the same pattern, wider: in distribution,
GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA on pressure is 0.13 over the hemispheres and 0.08
over the spheres. Two weaknesses follow. W1 is pressure inside the
spherical enclosures, even when they are in the training set. W2 is the
transfer from boxes to the spherical families. ISLA leads on the boxes
and on the ducts, held out or not.

**Peter's rulings on the remedies.** (1) Rescaling the Reynolds number
by the ratio of the model's length unit to the dataset's reference
length is rejected: a per-sample reference length that changes the
solution is not physical, and a reference length is acceptable only
when it is not sample-specific, as in GLOBE. (2) One distance per
boundary condition, built into ISLA, is approved (WALLDIST below).
(3) The training budget is to be increased on LHR (BUDGET-2X below).
(4) Experiments beyond the proposal list are welcome.

**D1, the ISLA-DTT pressure read (no new training).** ISLA-DTT's forest
read gives every interior point a direct read of the boundary tokens
(@sec-nb-dtt-merged); on AirfRANS it lowered ISLA's pressure error by
26 percent. If W1 is a reach problem (the pressure inside a sphere is
set by the outlet dome, which ISLA's points reach only through slice
averages), the reference-rate ISLA-DTT lanes, scored the same way, read
sphere and hemisphere pressure at or below 0.6 times ISLA's (final
against final, best against best), with box pressure within 10 percent
of ISLA's. D1 is falsified if ISLA-DTT's pressure on spheres and
hemispheres is above 0.85 times ISLA's. It is read when the `full` and
`family_non_box` ISLA-DTT pairs are scored.

**WALLDIST.** An interior ISLA built with the names of its boundary
conditions gives every prediction point, besides the existing signed
distance to the nearest boundary token, the signed distance to the
nearest token of each condition, in the model's length unit, as two
channels that vanish for an absent condition: sign/(1 + |s|) and
sign log(1 + 1/|s|). Built without names, the model is unchanged. The
SST closure that produced the labels uses the distance to the nearest
wall, and GeoTransolver receives the distances to the no-slip and slip
walls (`sdf_wall`, `sdf_wall_normals`, `sdf_slip`). ISLA's one
distance is to the nearest boundary of any condition, which inside a
sphere or a hemisphere is mostly an inlet or outlet dome. Four lanes,
rows 44-47, `az_{full,nonbox}_islahrwd_seed{42,43}`, run on snapshot
code_v27, which is code_v26 plus this one change, with
`model.boundary_conditions=[inlet,no_slip,outlet,slip]` and every other
setting equal to the half-rate lanes of rows 24-27, which are the
comparison. Predictions, test side, final checkpoints, means over both
seeds against the half-rate lanes: (W-a) on `family_non_box`, eddy
viscosity, turbulent kinetic energy and specific dissipation each
improve by at least 10 percent; (W-b) on the held-out hemispheres and
spheres velocity improves by at least 10 percent, and by more than it
does on the held-out ducts; (W-c) in distribution, every field on the
box cases is within 5 percent or better. If the held-out hemispheres
and spheres improve by less than 5 percent on every field, the
role-blind distance is not the cause of W2. There is no pressure
prediction: W1 is D1's question.

**BUDGET-2X.** The 250-epoch schedule stretched twofold: 500 epochs,
with the tenfold rate step every 200 epochs instead of every 100
(`training.scheduler.step_size=200`). It runs for three arms on the
`full` and `family_non_box` splits, seeds 42 and 43: half-rate ISLA
(rows 32-35, as rows 24-27), GeoTransolver at its reference rate (rows
36-39, as rows 2, 3, 6 and 7) and half-rate ISLA-DTT (rows 40-43, as
rows 28-31). That is twelve lanes in LHR's normal queue, about five to
six days. Each arm is compared with its own 250-epoch lanes at the same
rate, test side, final checkpoints. (B1) ISLA is budget-limited: the
doubled budget lowers its velocity and pressure errors by at least 10
percent on both splits. (B2) GeoTransolver is limited by data, not by
budget (its training loss is six times below its validation loss at
epoch 200): its errors change by less than 10 percent. (B3) The
held-out GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA velocity ratio over spheres and
hemispheres is at least 1.25 times that of the 250-epoch half-rate
lanes; if it moves by less than 10 percent, the budget does not explain
W2. (B4) The half-rate ISLA lanes have passed 50,000 to 70,000 steps,
two to three times the reference-rate event's 23,000 to 30,000, without
losing their validation minimum. The stretched schedule, which holds
1.875e-4 for 200 epochs, therefore stays clean: no lane doubles its
running minimum through epoch 500.

**Two diagnostics on existing checkpoints, predictions first.**
H-BOUND concerns the reference-rate event. Each block's routing logit
is a bounded cosine term, ten times the cosine between token and
prototype, plus a learned linear map of the point-anchor invariants
(distance, log-distance and direction cosines), which has no bound
(`_geo_region` in `blocks.py`). H-BOUND holds that this geometric bias
grows until it decides the routing. The probe reads, block by block,
the spread of each term across slices, the share of points whose top
slice changes when the bias is dropped, and the routing's effective
slice counts. It uses the reference-rate checkpoints of the Reynolds
and blob-bank ISLA lanes before, during and after their event, and
the half-rate lanes at the same epochs. H-BOUND is supported if, in the
reference-rate lanes, the bias spread at least doubles between epochs
31 and 55 while the cosine spread does not, and the bias decides the
top slice of more than 20 percent of points after the event, with
neither seen at half rate. It is refuted if the bias spread stays
below the cosine spread and does not change across the event.
GAUGE concerns W1. On the validation side of the half-rate `full`
lane, it fits each case's pressure error with a constant plus a
linear function of position. If W1 is a failure to carry the
domain-scale pressure level and gradient, that affine part holds at
least half of the error energy on spheres and hemispheres and at most
a quarter on boxes.

## 2026-10-14 — AEROZOO: H-BOUND refuted; four more tests pre-registered (the 18 untested splits, velocity-and-pressure targets, a fixed head-frame gain, WALLDIST on ISLA-DTT) {#sec-nb-aerozoo-matrix-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**H-BOUND is refuted.** The probe of @sec-nb-aerozoo-family-prereg
read the four reference-rate Reynolds and blob-bank ISLA lanes and the
four half-rate lanes at epochs 11 to 153, on eight validation cases per
lane. At the reference rate the geometric bias's spread across slices
changed by a factor of 0.81 to 0.98 between epochs 31 and 55, while the
criterion asked for a doubling. It stayed below the cosine term's
spread in every block (the largest ratio is 0.62), and afterwards it
fell by 30 to 60 percent. It decides the top slice of 2 to 13 percent
of points after the event, against the criterion's 20, and of more
points at half rate (12 to 18 percent) than at the reference rate. The
bias does not decide the routing. Two correlates of the event remain,
both absent at half rate. The head frame's prototype gain grows from
about 0.2-0.3 to 1.1-1.6, its rise starting with the training-loss
departure in two lanes and after it in a third. The effective number of
slices per point falls from 150-200 to 24-48 by the latest epochs,
through the cosine term itself. The strict detector (validation every
ten epochs) fires at epochs 60 to 70 in these lanes; their training
losses depart at epochs 43 to 56. Records:
`kernel/aerozoo/probe/hbound/` on the LHR site.

**Peter's guidance, 2026-10-14.** Velocity and pressure are the
volume quantities that matter (wall shear stress and intermittency on
surfaces); predicting log(1 + ν_t/ν) and the like is a good idea but
may not be needed. Subagents and the idle LHR capacity are to be used
freely.

**AZ-SPLITS: the generalization matrix.** Half-rate ISLA and
GeoTransolver, two seeds each, on the 18 frozen splits not yet run: six
held-out geometry banks (airframes, Blender bluff and streamlined
bodies, cars, streamlined bodies, Zero-to-CAD), three held-out
enclosure families (duct, opposed hemisphere, opposed sphere), five
held-out flow profiles (confined opposed, crossflow, dual inlet, ground
effect, open opposed), the layout split, Reynolds-number interpolation,
and the two scarce-data splits (440 and 74 training cases). Every
setting equals the half-rate lanes and GeoTransolver's reference lanes;
each split has its own training-part statistics. The readout is the
test side at the final checkpoints, plus the labeled best-checkpoint
table. (M1) Built-in symmetry buys data efficiency: GeoTransolver ÷
ISLA on velocity rises from `full` to `scarce` to `super_scarce`;
falsified if `super_scarce`'s ratio is below `full`'s. (M2) ISLA leads
on velocity on at least five of the six held-out geometry banks, where
the enclosures stay as trained. (M3) As in the family breakdown, ISLA
leads on the held-out ducts and trails on pressure on the held-out
spheres and hemispheres; with the other spherical family still in
training, the sphere ratio is above the 0.35 of the `family_non_box`
split. (M4) ISLA's lowest ratios among the 18 fall on the holds that
move inlets and outlets relative to the body (opposed families and
profiles), its highest on the geometry banks and Reynolds
interpolation.

**TARGETS-VP.** The same lanes trained on velocity and pressure only,
on the `full` split for ISLA at the reference and half rates and for
GeoTransolver, and on `family_non_box` for half-rate ISLA and
GeoTransolver. The turbulence fields stay in the data and leave the
loss. (V1) If the heavy-tailed turbulence targets drive the
reference-rate event, ISLA at 3.75e-4 on velocity and pressure keeps
its validation minimum through epoch 250; if it loses it near epochs
43-70, the event is not target-driven. (V2) Half-rate ISLA's velocity
and pressure errors fall by at least 5 percent, because the
specific-dissipation tail acts as gradient noise. (V3) GeoTransolver's
change by less than 5 percent. (V4) The spherical-enclosure pressure
ratio moves by less than 10 percent: W1 is not a loss-weighting
problem.

**H-FRAME.** ISLA at the reference rate on `full`, two seeds, with
only the head frame's prototype gain fixed at its initial 0.1
(diagnostic snapshot code_v28, never merged), against the reference
lanes of rows 0 and 1. (F1) If the gain's growth causes the event, the
lanes keep their validation minimum through epoch 250. The expectation
written here is the opposite: the event recurs, because in one probed
lane the gain rose only after the loss had departed.

**WALLDIST on ISLA-DTT.** The forest-read variant with one distance
per boundary condition (snapshot code_dtt17 = code_dtt16 plus the
change), half rate, `full` and `family_non_box`, two seeds, against the
half-rate ISLA-DTT lanes; predictions W-a to W-c of
@sec-nb-aerozoo-family-prereg, read for ISLA-DTT.

## 2026-10-14 — AEROZOO: GAUGE refuted, and W1 is mostly the reference rate's early checkpoints: at half rate ISLA's sphere pressure equals GeoTransolver's {#sec-nb-aerozoo-w1-correction}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**GAUGE.** Both half-rate ISLA `full` lanes were scored at their
validation minima so far (checkpoints 51 and 71) on all 386 `full`
validation cases, with the predictions kept. The probe's relative L2
reproduces the scorer's on every case to 1.3e-7. A constant plus a
linear function of position holds this share of the pressure error
energy (medians, seed 42 / 43): 0.73 / 0.49 on spheres, 0.65 / 0.50
on hemispheres, 0.49 / 0.37 on boxes and 0.58 / 0.71 on ducts. The
criterion asked for at least half on the spherical families and at
most a quarter on boxes, so it is refuted. A smooth part, mostly the
constant, dominates the pressure error in every family, not only the
spherical ones. For velocity the affine share is at most a fifth.

**The correction.** The same records show that W1 of
@sec-nb-aerozoo-family-prereg belongs to the reference rate's early
best checkpoints, not to ISLA. Pressure relative L2, validation side,
case means, seed 42 / 43:

| Family | ISLA, reference rate, checkpoint 31 | ISLA, half rate, checkpoints 51 / 71 | GeoTransolver, best |
|---|---|---|---|
| spheres | 0.377 / 0.495 | 0.101 / 0.089 | 0.141 / 0.061 |
| hemispheres | 0.366 / 0.496 | 0.216 / 0.174 | 0.187 / 0.110 |
| boxes | 0.361 / 0.505 | 0.188 / 0.172 | 0.684 / 0.520 |
| ducts | 0.545 / 0.952 | 0.384 / 0.278 | 0.698 / 1.142 |

The medians tell the same story, so this is not a few outlying cases.
At half rate, ISLA's sphere pressure equals GeoTransolver's best. Its
box and duct pressure is about a third of GeoTransolver's. Only the
hemispheres still trail, by a factor of about 0.76, and the half-rate
lanes are still training. The reference-rate lanes' best checkpoints
come from epoch 31, before the event cut their training short
(@sec-nb-aerozoo-instability), when their pressure error was 0.36 to
0.95 in every family. In distribution, then, W1 is an effect of the
event, which is what H-EVENT says. Whether W2, the held-out transfer,
shrinks as well is read when the half-rate held-out lanes are scored on
the test side. D1 still compares ISLA-DTT with ISLA at the reference
rate, as registered, but its premise, a reach deficit specific to the
spherical enclosures, does not hold in distribution.

**The pressure metric.** The scorer computes pressure's relative L2 on
the standardized field, (Cp - 1.4261) / 4.029. Its denominator is
therefore each case's deviation from the dataset's mean pressure
coefficient, not the case's own variation. Inside the spherical
enclosures Cp is close to zero (median rms 0.067), so the same errors
measured against the case's own Cp are 1.7 to 2.0 times the signal on
spheres and 0.84 times on boxes, for the half-rate lanes. The
pre-registered metric stays as defined. Any per-family pressure
comparison states which of the two normalizations it uses.

## 2026-10-14 — AEROZOO protocol defect: every volume lane saw each large boundary as one contiguous window of faces, often without the body; today's 140 lanes cancelled, a uniform-sampling relaunch prepared {#sec-nb-aerozoo-boundary-window}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**How it was found.** Building the surface task, the implementing
lane found that the reader's cell cap takes one contiguous block. The
cause is in `physicsnemo/datapipes/readers/mesh.py`:
`_subsample_mesh_cells` reads "a cyclic contiguous block" of k cells
at a random offset per draw. Every cell's inclusion probability is
k/N and the measure is scaled by N/k, so the measure is unbiased on
average, but a draw is an exchangeable uniform sample only if the
stored rows are in random order. The AeroZoo copy permuted the
interior rows for exactly this reason (`aerozoo_shuffle.py`), but its
boundaries are links to the release and keep OpenFOAM's face order.
The dataset files cap each boundary at 50,000 faces
(`subsample_n_cells: 50000`, `boundary_subsample: cells`). Every
boundary mesh above the cap was therefore seen as one spatially
coherent window. GeoTransolver's `sdf_wall` and `sdf_slip` are
computed from the same windowed meshes, so both architectures received
the same defective boundary, and the comparisons stay fair while the
task itself was degraded.

**How large.** In 400 random cases, 66 percent of the cases with a
body have more than 50,000 no-slip faces. A draw holds on average 56
percent of the body's faces (median 46, tenth percentile 12). On
average 24 percent of draws hold no body face at all, and in 80 of the
386 cases more than half of the draws do. The inlet, outlet and slip
meshes are seen at 79, 73 and 43 percent of their faces on average.
The scorer draws once per case, so about a quarter of the scored cases
were predicted without the body in the input.

**What it touches.** Every AeroZoo volume result so far: the Phase 1
standing, the held-out splits, the best-checkpoint table, the family
breakdown, D1 and the GAUGE probe. It may also touch the reference-rate
event. A case appears in one epoch with its body and in another
without it, under the same targets. Those are contradictory training
pairs, and they would load the optimizer most at the higher rate
(H-SAMPLING, to be tested). Other datasets read their geometry the
same way (the DrivAerML car keeps 200,000 of up to 17 million surface
cells). An audit of every configuration the program trained is
running, and its result is recorded when it is in.

**Decisions.** The 140 lanes launched today (rows 32 to 171: BUDGET-2X,
WALLDIST on both variants, H-FRAME, the matrix and TARGETS-VP) were
cancelled within hours of their start. Their run directories moved to
`runs_defective_2026-10-14/` on the LHR site. The 20 lanes that were
already running continue to their end: they complete the registered
reads of the protocol as it ran (R1 to R3, D1's final half), and they
measure the defect's effect against their uniform-sampling twins. The
fix reads each boundary whole and draws 50,000 faces uniformly, with
the same Horvitz-Thompson measure, as new dataset files beside the old
ones. The relaunch is pre-registered before it starts.

## 2026-10-14 — AEROZOO uniform-boundary relaunch (AZ-UNIFORM): the fix verified, every arm relaunched, predictions {#sec-nb-aerozoo-uniform-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**The fix.** The `aerozoo_uvolume*` dataset files (branch
psharpe/isla-azuniform, commit cd4b9490b; 24 files on the LHR site's
recipe_v9 as new files) equal their `aerozoo_volume*` sources except
that the reader no longer caps the boundary cells. Instead the recipe's
`SubsampleMesh` draws 50,000 faces per boundary first in the chain:
`torch.randperm` without replacement, the measure scaled by N/k.
Over 30 cases and three epochs per case, the old block left 27 of 90
draws without a body face, and its body share ranged from 0 to 11.3
times the expected k/N. The uniform draw left none, with 0.80 to 1.03
times k/N. Its share of occupied 16³ voxels is 0.93 on the body and
0.99 on the slip walls, against 0.53 and 0.55 before. Load time per
sample is unchanged at about 5 s. The scorer's draw follows the same
rule as training, but its per-case seed depends on the sampler's order.

**Lanes.** Run names start `azu_`, and every setting except the
dataset file equals its arm's lanes above. The `full` and
`family_non_box` splits run ISLA at 3.75e-4 and at 1.875e-4,
GeoTransolver at 1e-3 and ISLA-DTT at 1.875e-4. The `reynolds`, the
`bank_blobs` and the 18 splits of @sec-nb-aerozoo-matrix-launch run
half-rate ISLA, GeoTransolver and half-rate ISLA-DTT. WALLDIST runs on
both variants, BUDGET-2X on three arms and TARGETS-VP on five arms.
All use two seeds, 166 lanes in total. H-FRAME waits for U2.

**Predictions.** (U1) The defect starved the boundary-only reader most.
Every arm's `full` test errors at the final checkpoint fall below its
twin's under the old protocol. ISLA's fall more than GeoTransolver's,
so GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA on velocity rises by at least 10 percent.
(U2, H-SAMPLING) Contradictory draws drove the reference-rate event:
ISLA at 3.75e-4 keeps its validation minimum through epoch 250. U2 is
falsified if the running minimum doubles by epoch 100. (U3) The
spherical enclosures' large domes were the most windowed boundaries,
so held-out GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA on spheres and hemispheres rises by at
least 25 percent against the old protocol's best-checkpoint values.
(U4) M1 to M5, D1's question and WALLDIST's, BUDGET-2X's and
TARGETS-VP's predictions are read on these lanes. The old protocol's
versions of the matrix were cancelled before any result existed.

## 2026-10-14 — SAMPLING-AUDIT: every configuration checked; AirfRANS's interior was also read as one contiguous window; DrivAerML, HiLift and SHIFT-SUV are shuffled and unaffected {#sec-nb-sampling-audit}

::: {.callout-warning}
**AeroZoo numbers withdrawn 2026-10-19** (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn); the rest of this entry stands.
:::

**Test.** For each stored array that a reader caps, r is the mean
distance between consecutive stored rows divided by the mean distance
between random pairs. Near 1 means the rows are in random order, so a
contiguous block is a uniform sample. Far below 1 means they run
through space in order. The probes were read-only, on the cluster
login nodes, over 400 to 3,000 cases per dataset (3 for the DrivAerML
and HiLift order tests).

| Dataset | Capped part | k / N | r | Affected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DrivAerML Surface and Volume | interior points; vehicle cells | 100k-200k / 156M-166M; 100k-600k / ~17M | 0.99-1.01 | no |
| HiLift | vehicle cells | 100k-200k / 248M-301M | 0.995-0.998 | no |
| SHIFT-SUV | vehicle cells | 200k / ~5M | 0.99-1.00 | no |
| AirfRANS | interior points | 100k / 156k-210k | 0.006-0.020 | **yes** |
| AeroZoo | the four boundaries | 50k / 22k-229k | 0.009-0.022 | **yes** |
| AeroZoo | interior points | 200k / ~6M | about 1 | no |

The small DrivAerML boundaries, AirfRANS's airfoil, DeepJEB++, the
lug and Tensile2d are unordered too, but their caps exceed their sizes,
so they are read whole. No OLBC data was found to check.

**AirfRANS.** Its converter keeps the solver's point order, so each
lane read one contiguous run of 52 to 62 percent of the stored
interior points, in training and in scoring. A draw holds the right
share of points near the airfoil, but leaves one gap of about half a
chord (at most 0.75), against 0.03 chord for a random draw of the same
size. Only 66 to 75 percent of the airfoil's length has a sampled point
within 0.01 chord (30 percent in the worst draw), against all of it for
a random draw. The models were compared on the same windows per case,
so the ratios between them probably keep their direction. Their
absolute errors, and any comparison with published full-mesh AirfRANS
numbers, do not carry over. The results that depend on these lanes
are chapter 9's tables, AF-GEO in chapter 7, and the ledger rows
AIRFRANS-INT, AIRFRANS-SCALE, INTERNAL-GEOMETRY, FRAME-AF*,
LOCAL-AGG-STENCIL, LOCAL-LPR, PROTO-COND, SOFT-GEO, PATCH-SDF and the
AirfRANS column of CHAR-PROTOCOLS. Their reference lanes are rerun
with a uniform interior draw.

**DrivAerML.** The finding that an area-proportional boundary redraw
raises interior error 6.6 to 7.9 times stands as written: training saw
uniform draws, and the redraw changes the sampling law, not the
coverage. The FORCEREF drag and lift errors are ordinary sampling error
of a uniform 1.2-percent sample.

## 2026-10-14 — AIRFRANS uniform-interior rerun (AF-UNIFORM): the fix verified, the reference lanes relaunched, predictions {#sec-nb-airfrans-uniform-prereg}

**The fix.** The six `airfrans_uvolume*` files (branch
psharpe/isla-afuniform, commit 71ecb6140; on the LHR site in
recipe_v8, as new files) drop the reader's interior cap and draw the
100,000 points first in the chain with `SubsampleMesh`
(`torch.randperm`). On 8 test cases with 10 draws each, the largest
gap near the airfoil falls from 0.50 to 0.03 chord. The share of the
airfoil's length with a drawn point within 0.01 chord rises from 66.5
to 100 percent. Load time is unchanged.

**Lanes.** The reference lanes of chapter 9's standing, with the
dataset file as the only change: ISLA (`afu_r_isla`, 512 wide, 512
slices, 3.75e-4), GeoTransolver (`afu_r_gt`, 1e-3), Transolver
(`afu_r_t`, 512 by 16, 1e-3), all on recipe_v8 and code_v20 in
bfloat16, 500 epochs, 100,000 points, seeds 42 and 43. ISLA-DTT
(`afu_dtt`, its read-only table's configuration on code_dtt16, 5e-4)
also runs. The scripts are a copy in `kernel/airfrans_u/` on the LHR
site.

**Predictions.** (AF1) The comparisons were like for like, so the
standing keeps its direction: ISLA leads GeoTransolver and Transolver
on velocity and trails them on pressure. (AF2) Every architecture's
errors fall, and pressure, the field set at the airfoil, falls by at
least 10 percent for each, because the old windows missed a third of
the airfoil's neighbourhood. (AF3) ISLA-DTT stays below ISLA's error
on velocity and pressure.

## 2026-10-15 — AIRFRANS: the old checkpoints scored on uniform draws; ISLA, trained on contiguous windows, loses 10 to 66 percent, while ISLA-DTT is unchanged {#sec-nb-airfrans-scoring-effect}

**Why.** Scoring alone moves the numbers. AF2 compares the reruns
with chapter 9, so the effect of the new draw on a fixed checkpoint has
to be measured on its own first. The final checkpoints (epoch 500) of
the six reference lanes were copied from AGA to the LHR site. They, and
ISLA-DTT's two, were scored with the reference protocol on the uniform
dataset twins (LHR jobs 202658 to 202665; 200 test cases each; branch
psharpe/isla-afscore, commit 9cdcc6bcc).

| Arm, native scoring, two-seed means | Pressure: block, uniform, ratio | Velocity: block, uniform, ratio | Eddy viscosity: block, uniform, ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA | 0.0352, 0.0442, 1.25 | 0.0172, 0.0189, 1.10 | 0.0315, 0.0522, 1.66 |
| GeoTransolver | 0.0266, 0.0246, 0.92 | 0.0378, 0.0423, 1.12 | 0.0293, 0.0359, 1.23 |
| Transolver | 0.0259, 0.0292, 1.13 | 0.0707, 0.0842, 1.19 | 0.0311, 0.0425, 1.37 |
| ISLA-DTT | 0.0259, 0.0229, 0.88 | 0.0140, 0.0141, 1.01 | 0.0324, 0.0318, 0.98 |

**Reading.** A model trained on contiguous windows of the interior
loses accuracy when the same cases are drawn uniformly. ISLA loses the
most, and ISLA-DTT nothing. This is the query-population dependence of
@sec-nb-query-pop seen from the other side. ISLA's interior points are
interacting tokens, so its predictions depend on which other points
are queried, and the training windows were the only population it knew.
ISLA-DTT's queries are exactly independent of each other, so it is
indifferent to the draw. On uniform scoring of these checkpoints,

## 2026-10-15 — AEROZOO H-LOGIT pre-registration: does an unnormalized query-key logit grow under Muon until the event? {#sec-nb-aerozoo-hlogit-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Why.** ISLA trains its weight matrices with Muon (momentum 0.95,
Nesterov, five Newton-Schulz steps, update RMS matched to AdamW's) and
its other parameters with AdamW (betas 0.9 and 0.999, eps 1e-8). Both
run at 3.75e-4 with weight decay 1e-4 and no gradient clipping. A Muon
update has a fixed size per step, so a matrix's norm grows until weight
decay balances it, and that balance point rises with the rate. A
softmax whose logit is the product of two learned maps can then
sharpen without bound. ISLA has three such sites: the seed attention
that builds each block's and the head frame's prototypes
(`seeds · k_proj(x) / sqrt(hidden)`, in `_RoutingLogits.prototypes`),
the global read's query-key term, and ISLA-DTT's mean kernel read. The
routing logits are bounded cosines, and H-BOUND refuted their unbounded
bias as the cause.

**Hypothesis.** H-LOGIT: the reference-rate event follows the growth of
the logits at one of these sites.

**Instrument.** A checkpoint probe on `azu_full_isla_seed42` (epochs 1
to 85) and on the half-rate twins `az_full_islahr_seed42` and
`azu_full_islahr_seed42`, with four fixed validation cases and fixed
draws. Per site it records the 99.9th percentile and the maximum of the
logit magnitude, the softmax's effective support (the exponential of
its entropy), the Frobenius and spectral norms of the matrices that
form the logit, and the learned gains.

**Predictions.** (L1) At one site, the 99.9th percentile of the logit
magnitude at the reference rate grows at least twofold between epochs
9 and 43. The effective support of that site's softmax falls by at
least half between epochs 39 and 55, no later than the routing's drop
in effective slices. (L2) At the half rate, the same statistic is at
most 0.7 times the reference rate's at epoch 43. It stays below the
reference rate's epoch-43 value through the latest half-rate checkpoint.
H-LOGIT is refuted if no site's logits grow twofold before epoch 43, or
if a half-rate twin passes the reference rate's epoch-43 value without
an event. The expectation written here is that L1 holds at the head
frame's seed attention, because the head frame's gain also grew in the
earlier probe. If H-LOGIT holds, the candidate remedy is to normalize
that site's queries and keys, as the routing already does. It would be
tested on two datasets before it is adopted.

## 2026-10-15 — AEROZOO H-LOGIT verdict: L1 fails as written, L2 holds; the head frame's seed attention is an argmax from epoch 29 at either rate, and the residual stream grows 190-fold from epoch 9 to 43 at the reference rate {#sec-nb-aerozoo-hlogit-verdict}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Run.** One LHR job (223072) on 48 checkpoints: `azu_full_isla_seed42`
at 28 epochs from 1 to 85, `azu_full_islahr_seed42` at 4 and
`az_full_islahr_seed42` at 16 from 1 to 185. Four fixed validation cases
with cached draws, the uniform-draw configuration for every run, and the
bfloat16 forward of training. The probe's wrappers leave the outputs
bitwise unchanged, and the float32 recomputations of the statistics
agree with bfloat16 to 0.3 percent. Code_v26 has no global read, so two
sites remain: the seed attention of the twelve blocks and of the head
frame. Files: `scratch/isla-hlogit-2026-10-15/`.

**The head frame.** The 99.9th percentile of the logit magnitude grows
749-fold from epoch 9 to 43 (3.1e3 to 2.35e6). The effective support of
its softmax falls from 6.3e4 points at epoch 1 to 1.08 at epoch 29 and
stays at 1. At the half rate the logit is 3.3e-4 of the reference value
at epoch 43 and never exceeds it (largest 1.97e4). Yet the half-rate
windowed lane's support also falls to 2 to 19 points from epoch 89 on,
with no event.

**The blocks.** Seed attention grows 2.8- to 5.4-fold from epoch 9 to 43
but stays small (0.6 to 1.3 at epoch 43), and its support does not move
(ratio 1.00 to 1.01 from epoch 39 to 55). The bounded routing logits grow
at most 1.35-fold. The routing's effective support falls from epoch 47
to 53 on (ratio 0.40 to 0.57 from epoch 39 to 55 in blocks 5, 9 and 11).

**Verdicts.** L1 fails as written: the one site that grows twofold has
an argmax softmax from epoch 29, so its support cannot halve between
epochs 39 and 55. L2 holds at that site. Neither refutation clause
fires. The head frame's saturation is not sufficient for the event,
because the half-rate lane saturates too and trains on.

**Outside the registration.** The head frame reads the raw residual
stream `h`, which no LayerNorm bounds, and its logit tracks the growth
of `h`, not of its own matrices (the spectral norm of `seeds · k_proj`
goes from 2.1 at epoch 9 to 6.1 at epoch 43). The mean token norm of
`h` is 9.1e3 at epoch 1, 3.0e5 at epoch 9, 5.7e7 at epoch 43, 2.2e8 at
epoch 51 and 5.6e11 at epoch 85. It roughly triples between epochs 49
and 51, at the event. The half-rate windowed lane's is 8.2e4 at epoch 43
and at most 6.7e5. The code gives the reason: each block's update
`h + broadcast(cat(h, back, geo_pool))` reads the raw `h` (blocks.py),
so the block multiplies the stream by `I + W_h`, where `W_h` is the
slice of the broadcast weight that reads `h`. The MLP and the routing
read LayerNorm'd states. The raw read dates from the first ISLA block
(September 2026), and no note gives a reason for it.

## 2026-10-15 — AEROZOO H-RESID pre-registration: a multiplicative residual stream collapses the routing; the broadcast reads the normalized state {#sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Hypothesis.** H-RESID: the raw read of `h` in the broadcast makes each
block's update multiplicative, and Muon's fixed-size updates at the
reference rate grow the product of the twelve blocks' gains. One
direction then dominates every token state, so the LayerNorm'd states
that the cosine routing reads become nearly collinear. The routing loses
its contrast and collapses. This would explain, with one mechanism, the
AeroZoo event at 23,000 to 30,000 steps, the DeepJEB++ plateau at about
12,000 to 37,000 steps (epochs 4 to 12 at 3,113 steps per epoch; a
routing collapse to 1 to 5 effective slices, @sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-mechanism),
and the cure by half the rate on both datasets.

**Instrument 1, a checkpoint probe** on the same checkpoints as H-LOGIT.
Per block: the mean token norm of `h`, the block's amplification (the
ratio of the norms after and before it), the spectral norm of `I + W_h`,
the share of the routing input's energy in its top principal direction
across tokens, and the mean absolute cosine between token states.
(P1) At the reference rate, the top-direction share of the routing input
rises from epoch 9 to 51 in at least one block, to at least twice its
epoch-9 value and to at least 0.5. At the half rate it stays below the
reference rate's epoch-43 value through the last checkpoint. (P2) Most
blocks amplify the stream (ratio above 1), their amplification grows
from epoch 9 to 43, and the product of the per-block ratios accounts for
at least half of the logarithm of the stream's growth.

**Instrument 2, the remedy.** One change: the broadcast reads the
block's normalized state `norm_assign(h)`, the state the routing already
reads, in place of `h`. No parameter, constant or other read changes
(the head frame's raw read stays, because the half-rate lane shows its
saturation is harmless). Two snapshots carry it: code_v26 plus the
change for AeroZoo, and code_v20 plus the change for DeepJEB++ and
AirfRANS, so that each comparison is against existing reference lanes
with one variable changed. (P3) On AeroZoo `full` at 3.75e-4, both
seeds keep their validation minimum through epoch 250, and the mean
token norm of `h` at epoch 43 is at least 100 times below the
reference rate's 5.7e7. (P4) On DeepJEB++ at 3.75e-4 (the final
reference configuration, width 512 and 512 slices, 40 epochs), neither
seed's training loss passes twice its running minimum within the first
12 epochs, and validation von Mises at epoch 12 is below 0.6. The
reference-rate lanes were at 0.90 to 1.02 from epoch 4 on, the
half-rate lanes at 0.48 to 0.50 at epoch 6. (P5) On AirfRANS with
uniform draws at the reference configuration, the remedy's pressure and
velocity test errors are within 5 percent of the reference ISLA lanes'
or better.

**What follows.** If P3 and P4 hold and P5 shows no loss, the remedy is
proposed as the reference configuration, and both rate exceptions
(DeepJEB++ and AeroZoo) are retired. The head frame's raw read is then
normalized as a separate, tested change. If P1 or P2 fails and P3 holds,
the remedy works for a reason other than H-RESID's, and the notebook
says so.

**Amendment, 2026-10-15 22:52 EDT, before any remedy lane started.**
The broadcast is not the block's only raw read of `h`. The slice states
are pooled from it (`z = einsum(a, h)`), and `back = point_mix (z +
slice_mlp(z))` keeps that raw `z`, so the broadcast's `W_b back` is
also linear in `h`. Removing only the direct `W_h h` term leaves a
multiplicative path through the averaged stream. Two arms therefore
run. Arm A, as registered above: the broadcast reads `norm_assign(h)`
(snapshot code_v29, AeroZoo rows 340 and 341). Arm A2, the candidate
remedy: the pooling and the broadcast both read `norm_assign(h)`, so the
slice sublayer reads the normalized state as a pre-LN sublayer does, and
the raw `h` enters only the residual identity and the MLP's LayerNorm.
P3 is read on both arms. P4 and P5, and the proposal in "What follows",
apply to A2. A is a diagnostic: if A2 holds P3 and A does not, the
pooled path carries the growth. Instrument 1 also records the size of
each term of the block's update, so the growth can be assigned to a
path.

## 2026-10-15 — AEROZOO H-RESID Instrument 1: P1 fails, P2 holds; every block amplifies the stream, both raw-h paths carry the growth, and the deep blocks' updates are rounded away {#sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-probe}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Run.** One LHR job (224693) on the 48 checkpoints of the H-LOGIT
probe, plus half-rate epoch 189. The hooks leave the outputs bitwise
unchanged and reproduce the H-LOGIT numbers. The residual stream is
bfloat16 from the embedding on. Files:
`scratch/isla-hresid-2026-10-15/` (`checks.md`, `summary_tables.md`).

**P1 fails.** The routing input's share of energy in its top direction
is already 0.46 to 0.76 at epoch 9 (0.56 to 0.84 at epoch 1) and rises
at most 1.29-fold by epoch 51 (1.14-fold centered). The half-rate lanes
exceed the reference rate's epoch-43 value from epoch 1. The mean
absolute cosine between routing inputs does not rise from epoch 9 to 43.
It rises at and after the event (0.52 to 0.72 at epoch 55, 0.68 to 0.87
at epoch 85) and falls at the half rate. So the routing collapse follows
the event and does not announce it, and H-RESID's proposed pathway is
wrong.

**P2 holds, but its last clause is nearly true by construction**: the
sum of the per-block log amplifications cannot fall far below the log
of the product. The informative facts are these. Every block amplifies
the stream at every checkpoint of every run (at least 1.48-fold at the
reference rate, 1.32-fold at the half rate). Every block's
amplification grows from epoch 9 to 43 (block 8 from 2.11 to 3.51,
block 11 from 2.20 to 3.85), and the product over the twelve blocks
grows from 1.4e4 to 1.6e6. The broadcast step carries the gain; the MLP
step's is 1.000 in blocks 5 to 11. The spectral norm of `I + W_h` grows
from 2.2-2.9 to 3.7-4.8 at the reference rate and from 1.8-2.2 to
2.6-3.6 at the half rate.

**Which path.** Both terms that are linear in the raw `h` carry the
growth, in similar shares. From epoch 9 to 43 the direct term `W_h h`
grows 1.8- to 2.2-fold relative to the stream, and the pooled term
`W_b point_mix z` 1.4- to 2.2-fold. The other terms shrink in the deep
blocks. At the event the jumps come from the pooled term (2.9 to 5.4
times the stream's norm at epochs 51 to 55), while the direct term rises
smoothly. Arm A removes only the direct term, so A is expected to fail
P3. A2 removes both.

**Outside the registration: the deep blocks' updates are rounded away.**
In a bfloat16 stream an update far smaller than the stream is lost in
the add. At epoch 43 of the reference rate, the share of the MLP update
lost to rounding is 0.48 in block 7, 0.79 in block 9 and 0.98 in block
11, and about 1.0 in blocks 5 to 10 by epoch 85. At the half rate it is
0.09 and 0.59 in blocks 7 and 11 at epoch 43. The geometry term is
1e-5 to 1.5e-6 of the stream in blocks 6 to 11 at epoch 43, below
bfloat16 resolution. At the reference rate the deep blocks' MLPs and
geometry therefore add nothing by the event. The rounding of the cast
at the broadcast's input is negligible (below 0.006 of the message
terms).

## 2026-10-15 — AEROZOO H-PREC pre-registration: is the event the bfloat16 rounding of the deep blocks' updates? A float32 fork from epoch 39 {#sec-nb-aerozoo-hprec-prereg}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

**Hypothesis.** H-PREC: the multiplicative stream harms training
through the rounding of the bfloat16 stream, which drops the deep
blocks' MLP and geometry updates. Float32 resolves updates about 65,000
times smaller relative to the stream, so the same growth would drop
them many epochs later.

**Instrument.** A fork of `azu_full_isla_seed42`: its epoch-39
checkpoint (model, optimizer and scheduler state) copied into a new
run, `azu_forkfp32_full_isla_seed42`, resumed with `precision=float32`
and nothing else changed, through epoch 70. The original run, which
resumed from its own checkpoints at every link, is the control: its
training loss passed twice its running minimum (0.0248 at epoch 40) at
epoch 52.

**Prediction.** (F1) In float32 the training loss does not pass twice
the running minimum before epoch 60, and the validation loss at epochs
50 and 60 stays below 0.063 (twice the control's minimum). If the fork
loses its minimum at epochs 44 to 56, as in bfloat16, the harm does not
come through the rounding, and the growth itself is the cause. Either
way A2 remains the remedy, because it removes the growth.

## 2026-10-16 — AEROZOO four reads: U2 falsified on both seeds, V1 not target-driven, H-PREC's F1 fails, H-FRAME's event comes ten epochs later {#sec-nb-aerozoo-four-reads}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

All on `full` at 3.75e-4 with uniform boundary draws; "departs" means
a completed epoch's mean training loss above twice its running minimum,
and "doubles" means the validation loss above twice its running minimum.

**U2, second seed.** `azu_full_isla_seed43` departs at epoch 38, and its
validation loss doubles by epoch 60 (0.139 against a minimum of 0.037 at
epoch 20). U2 is falsified on both seeds.

**V1.** Trained on velocity and pressure alone, ISLA loses its minimum as
before: `azu_full_islavp_seed42` departs at epoch 42 and doubles by
epoch 50 (0.099 against 0.017); seed 43 departs and doubles at epoch 30
(0.051 against 0.017). The event is not driven by the heavy-tailed
turbulence targets.

**H-PREC.** The float32 fork from epoch 39 departs at epoch 51, one epoch
before its bfloat16 control, and its validation loss at epoch 60 is
0.150 against the bar of 0.063. F1 fails: the harm does not come through
the rounding of the bfloat16 stream. The growth itself is the cause.

**H-FRAME, seed 42.** With the head frame's prototype gain fixed at 0.1,
the lane departs at epoch 62 and doubles by epoch 70 (0.082 against
0.030), ten epochs later than its reference twin (52 and 60). The event
recurs, as the registration expected, so F1 fails. Seed 43 is at epoch
26.

**Where this leaves the mechanism.** Contradictory draws, the turbulence
targets, bfloat16 rounding and the head frame's gain are each ruled out
as the cause. The multiplicative residual stream of
@sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-probe remains. Its remedy lanes (arms A and A2,
rows 340 to 343) are at epoch 27 and reach the event's window within a
day.

## 2026-10-16 — AEROZOO remedy R2, first condition holds: no half-rate lane doubles its running minimum through epoch 250 {#sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-r2-first}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Withdrawn 2026-10-19.** Every AeroZoo number in this entry was measured with label inputs that the AeroZoo input rule forbids, and its lanes and scores are deleted (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn).
:::

The four half-rate ISLA lanes of @sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-prereg (rows 24
to 27, windowed boundary protocol) finished epoch 249. With the
registered detector (validation every ten epochs), none doubles its
running minimum: the largest ratio of a validation loss to the running
minimum before it is 1.09 and 1.08 on `full` and 1.42 and 1.03 on
`family_non_box`. The final validation losses are 0.0302 and 0.0311
(`full`) and 0.0301 and 0.0315 (`family_non_box`), at or within 4
percent of each lane's best. R1 and R3 are excluded. R2's second
condition is read on the float32 scores of the final `full` checkpoints,
which the scoring pump has queued. The training-time validation velocity
at epoch 249 is 0.167 and 0.171, against the bar of 0.25. The P1 re-read
(GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA on velocity, at or above 1.4 under R2) follows
with those scores. H-RESID (@sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-probe) explains why
the half rate helps: the stream grows multiplicatively in both, more
slowly at the half rate.

## 2026-10-16 — CHAR-PROTOCOLS area-protocol audit: the uniform point cloud resampled the scored set on DrivAerML Surface, HiLift and Shift-SUV only; on DrivAerML Volume it redrew ISLA's boundary alone, and on AirfRANS, Tensile2D, the lug and DeepJEB++ it returned the native mesh {#sec-nb-char-area-audit}

**What was audited.** Whether the area-weighted (uniform-point-cloud)
column of every CHAR-PROTOCOLS artifact measures what its name says.
The audit is read-only: it reads the committed per-case records under
`results/campaigns_2026-10-02/char/protocols/` and
`results/campaigns_2026-10-14/afu/`, the dataset key of each record's
config row, the scoring yamls (md5-identical to LHR `recipe_v8`) and
the stored mesh sizes from `meta.json` on LHR; no job was run. Scripts
and outputs are in `scratch/isla-char-area-audit-2026-10-16/`. The
area twin replaces the native subsampling with
`PoissonBiasedSubsampleMesh(weight_mode=area)`, applied to every
sub-mesh of the domain (the interior and each boundary). The transform
counts cells, and returns a sub-mesh unchanged when it holds no more
cells than `n_cells_expected` (200,000 at scoring; 100,000 on the
AirfRANS lanes). It changes a sub-mesh only where more cells than the
budget reach it, and it never changes a point cloud, which has no
cells.

**Verdict per dataset.** Shifts are area ÷ native per architecture,
seed means unless stated; "identical" means bitwise-identical per-case
values.

| Dataset | Cells reaching the area step ÷ budget | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| DrivAerML Surface | 1,000,000-cell uniform pool (of 16.5M to 17.7M) ÷ 200,000 | resampled for every model | ISLA 1.005 / 1.019 (pressure / wall shear); GeoTransolver 9.6 / 6.9; Transolver 6.4 / 5.1; 0 of 48 cases identical |
| HiLiftAeroML, 510-case medium set | 1,000,000-cell pool (of about 290M) ÷ 200,000 | resampled for every model | ISLA 1.013 / 1.013; GeoTransolver 4.2 / 3.1; Transolver 9.1 / 5.5 |
| Shift-SUV | 1,000,000-cell pool (of 5.0M) ÷ 200,000 | resampled for every model | ISLA 0.999 / 1.001; GeoTransolver 3.3 / 3.0; Transolver 2.8 / 2.2 |
| DrivAerML Volume | ISLA: vehicle pool of 1,000,000 ÷ 200,000; interior 0 cells; the baselines load no boundary | ISLA's boundary only | ISLA 7.9 / 6.6 / 6.6 (pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity; seed 42 pressure 9.1); GeoTransolver and Transolver 288 of 288 per-case values identical |
| AirfRANS, block and uniform files | airfoil 843 to 1,217 segments ÷ 100,000; interior 0 cells | native mesh | baselines identical (1,200 of 1,200 block, 200 of 200 uniform); ISLA 995 of 1,000 and 200 of 200 identical, the rest within 6.4e-7; ISLA-DTT within 2e-6 |
| Tensile2D | outer polyline 496 segments ÷ 200,000; interior 0 cells | native mesh | baselines 100 of 100 identical; ISLA 46 to 48 of 100 identical, the rest within 5.8e-4 per case (aggregate within 3.2e-6) |
| lug | surface 5,448 to 8,600 triangles ÷ 200,000; interior 0 cells | native mesh | 600 of 600 identical for every model |
| DeepJEB++ | surface 50,040 triangles ÷ 200,000 (the surface is the scored set) | native mesh | baselines 5,540 of 5,540 identical; ISLA all but one (3.4e-7) |

Two probes are live draws: VOL-GEO, on the Volume twin's boundary
(@sec-nb-char-vol-geo-verdict), and AF-GEO's `sub400a` / `sub400u`,
whose budget of 400 is below the airfoil's segment count. They are the
only area-law draws measured on those datasets.

**The ISLA-only differences on the native-mesh datasets are scorer
nondeterminism.** The inputs are identical: the baselines are bitwise
identical, the early return consumes no random numbers, ISLA is
bitwise identical on the lug, and ISLA-DTT differs at 1e-6 between two
scorings of the same file. The Tensile2D per-case spread (up to 5.8e-4)
is larger than plain rounding; nearest-sample ties on the structured
mesh amplifying the order of atomic sums, the LUG-PREC mechanism, would
explain it, but that is not verified.

**DrivAerML Volume.** The area twin changes one thing for ISLA: the
vehicle tokens. Natively the reader takes a 200,000-cell uniform block
with each measure scaled N/k; under the twin it takes a 1,000,000-cell
block and the Poisson step keeps about 198,000 cells with inclusion
probability proportional to area, each measure scaled by the inverse
probability. The measure is exact (effective measure sum 1.4426 against
1.4405 on run_1 and 1.3812 against 1.3829 on run_112, built through the
scorer's own dataloaders); the spread of the token measures falls from
15,000-18,000x to 6-8x and the tokens move off the finely meshed
features onto the flat panels. The interior queries, the targets, the
stored signed distance and the global inputs are unchanged.
GeoTransolver and Transolver set `drop_in_file_boundaries: true`, so they
never load the vehicle and their whole input is unchanged. ISLA's
6.6x to 7.9x is therefore real for the trained model and not a
comparison. The unifdraw control (the same Poisson path with uniform
inclusion) reproduces native to the third decimal
(@sec-nb-char-protocols-instruments), and VOL-GEO, which keeps every
area-draw token and computes only the queries' built-in
nearest-boundary distance and direction from the native draw, returns
to native within 0.4% on both seeds: the model reads the nearest drawn
token under a sampling law it never saw in training. One caveat is
bounded by the same 0.4%: no generator is attached to the Poisson step
at inference, so if the reader's interior draw shares the global
stream, ISLA's interior sample under the twin differs from native after
the first case.

**The posed protocol.** Posed ÷ native for ISLA, seeds 42 / 43; the
baselines change on every dataset (no case identical), so the
instrument is live everywhere. ISLA is invariant to float rounding on
DrivAerML Surface (1.00002 on pressure and wall shear, per case within
1.4e-3), DrivAerML Volume (1.0001 to 1.0005, per case within 3.2e-3),
AirfRANS on both file sets (0.9999 to 1.0003), Shift-SUV (0.9998 to
1.0000) and DeepJEB++ (1.00000). Three departures: the lug, 2.01 /
1.30 (1.61 on the seed mean), the LUG-PREC tie mechanism
(@sec-nb-char-lug-final); Tensile2D within 2% on the seed means
(stress 1.016 / 1.004, displacement 1.011 / 0.980) with single cases up
to 64%, attributed to the same structured-mesh ties; HiLift 1.01
(pressure 1.009 / 1.010, wall shear 1.006) with single cases up to 9%,
cause not located. The posed instrument has no defect.

**What changes in the book.** The index lede says the point cloud is

**Next.** On AirfRANS, Tensile2D, the lug and DeepJEB++ a draw at the

## 2026-10-16 — CHAR-AREA2 verdict: at reduced boundary budgets the area law raises ISLA's AirfRANS interior errors 1.2x to 2.2x over a uniform draw of the same count, against a noise floor of 0.02 to 0.10; the lug null holds, the Tensile2D null fails on plastic strain inside its own noise floor, and on DeepJEB++ the baselines move 1.07x to 1.57x while ISLA's plateaued checkpoint does not {#sec-nb-char-area2-verdict}

**Question.** The area-protocol audit (@sec-nb-char-area-audit) found
that on AirfRANS, Tensile2D, the lug and DeepJEB++ the area-weighted
draw returned the native mesh, because every boundary has fewer cells
than the scoring budget and the scored interiors carry no cells. It
named the meaningful form: a boundary draw at a budget k below the cell
count, area law against uniform law at the same k, so that area ÷
uniform isolates the law and uniform ÷ native the count. CHAR-AREA2 ran
that form on the final checkpoints of the records the CHAR and AF-SCORE
tables use, evaluation only.

**Design.** Per unit, float32 `infer.py` on the validation split with
the original scorer's overrides and cell count, on a recipe copy whose
only change is an appended `GuardedPoissonSubsampleMesh`. The guard
fails if a cell-carrying mesh reaching the step has no more cells than
the budget, and it logs the cells before and kept, the measure sums and
an index CRC per call. Three draws per unit at one budget: `ca2a`
(inclusion probability proportional to the cell measure), `ca2u`
(uniform inclusion) and `ca2v` (uniform inclusion with an independent
boundary seed; the interior and every later random step stay in
lockstep with the other two). Measures are scaled by the inverse
inclusion probability. Ratios: r = ca2a ÷ ca2u and the noise floor
d = |ca2v ÷ ca2u − 1|, each the mean over cases of the per-case
relative L2, per field and seed; the count effect is ca2u ÷ native, with
native from the committed CHAR and AF-SCORE records. Budgets: the
AirfRANS airfoil at an expected 400 segments (of about 1,000); Tensile2D
all 201 condition-labelled segments kept plus an expected 100 of the
other 241 to 295 (about 301 kept), because 200 segments keeping the
labelled ones is infeasible; the lug surface at 2,000 triangles; the
DeepJEB++ surface, which is the scored set, at 20,000 cells. Only ISLA
was scored on AirfRANS (with ISLA-DTT), Tensile2D and the lug:
GeoTransolver and Transolver set `drop_in_file_boundaries: true` there,
so a boundary-only redraw leaves their inputs bitwise unchanged (the
audit's identical cases). DeepJEB++ is the one cross-architecture test.
Pre-registration, jobs, logs, md5s and the reducer are in
`scratch/isla-char-area2-2026-10-16/`; the reduced numbers are
committed as `results/char/area2_2026-10-16.json` (reducer
`results/char/area2_2026-10-16.py`).

**Registered predictions** (`PREREG.md`). A draft was approved with
four design changes, then amended. The amendment was written at
2026-10-16T19:05-04:00, before any scoring job was submitted, and
supersedes the draft's predictions. It added the `ca2v` control and
reads, verbatim:

> * (S) DeepJEB++ (von_mises, displacement): ISLA r within [0.95, 1.05]
>   on every field and seed; each of GeoTransolver and Transolver has, on
>   at least one field, |r - 1| larger than ISLA's and larger than its own
>   d, on both seeds.
> * (B-AF) AirfRANS afu ISLA: r > 1.05 AND r > 1 + d on pressure,
>   velocity and nut, both seeds.
> * (B-lug) null against the noise floor: ISLA |r - 1| on von_mises <=
>   max(2d, 0.05), both seeds. Reason: the laws keep nearly the same
>   cells (Jaccard 0.897) and the LUG-PREC ties make any resample move
>   the error, so the law should not move it beyond resampling noise.
> * (N-T2D) Tensile2d ISLA: r within [0.95, 1.05] on stress,
>   displacement and q, both seeds; d reported.
> * Recorded, not predicted: ISLA-DTT ratios; the count effect ca2u /
>   native (native from the committed CHAR / AF-SCORE records); d for
>   every unit.

(N-T2D) replaced the brief's prediction of a law effect on Tensile2D by
a null before any job, because the two laws are nearly the same draw
there (segment-length CV at most 0.03, case-0 kept-cell Jaccard 0.991
between the area and uniform draws). The amendment also records that
`ca2a` and `ca2u` share their inclusion uniforms and `ca2v` does not
(case-0 Jaccard area/uniform against uniform/uniform-B: Tensile2D 0.991
/ 0.603, lug 0.897 / 0.226, AirfRANS 0.429 / 0.225, DeepJEB++ 0.513 /
0.249), so d measures a full independent redraw. That makes the
(B-lug) bar easier to meet and the (B-AF) and (S) bars harder.

**Jobs.** All on LHR, short QOS: 240320 (AirfRANS, 12 units), 240574
(Tensile2D and the lug, 12 units) and 240592_[0-4] (DeepJEB++, 18
units). The AGA jobs 1287521 and 1287522 were cancelled while pending
(queue rank about 1,079, below the 500 jobs the backfill tests) and
never ran; the AGA-trained checkpoints were copied to LHR instead (50
files, md5-identical). All 42 units completed, each with 1 + N guard
lines and N inference rows (N = 200, 100, 600 and 5,540 cases), and no
guard tripped.

**Results** (seeds 42 / 43; errors are seed means).
