**Verdicts against the amendment.**

- **(S) DeepJEB++ holds, and it is weak evidence.** ISLA's r is
  1.000 on von Mises stress on both seeds and 0.973 / 0.999 on
  displacement; both baselines exceed ISLA's |r − 1| and their own d on
  both fields and both seeds. But ISLA's scored checkpoints sit at the
  mean-field plateau (@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-plateau-interim): native
  errors 0.93 on von Mises and 0.84 / 0.90 on displacement, against
  0.43 to 0.50 and 0.19 to 0.24 for the baseline seeds. A predictor near the
  field mean is unchanged by any draw almost by construction, so this is
  not evidence that ISLA's measure consistency holds on DeepJEB++.
- **(B-AF) AirfRANS holds.** r exceeds 1.05 and 1 + d on pressure,
  velocity and eddy viscosity on both seeds (r 1.21 to 2.24, d 0.02 to
  0.10). It reproduces AF-GEO's block-lane result
  (@sec-nb-af-geo-step-one) on the uniform-draw lanes: the area law
  hurts.
- **(B-lug) the null holds.** |r − 1| is 0.043 and 0.021, within
  max(2d, 0.05) = 0.05 and 0.10.
- **(N-T2D) the null fails as written, on plastic strain only.** r is
  1.069 / 1.079 on q, outside [0.95, 1.05]; stress and displacement are
  inside. q's own d is 0.35 to 0.38, so the move is well inside
  resampling noise on the heavy-tailed field. The two laws cannot be
  separated on this polyline (CV at most 0.03; the area and uniform
  draws keep 99% of the same segments on case 0).
- **Recorded.** ISLA-DTT is law-sensitive on pressure and velocity (r
  1.50 to 1.88) and not on eddy viscosity (0.92 / 0.99, within d).

**The count effect.** Thinning the boundary is itself far outside the
training distribution of every model that reads it: ISLA's interior
errors rise 7x to 29x at the reduced budgets (13x to 18x on AirfRANS,
7x to 17x on Tensile2D stress and displacement, 20x / 29x on the lug;
1.6x / 1.8x on Tensile2D plastic strain, whose native error is already
0.31 to 0.35). These checkpoints trained on the whole boundary, so the
law comparison at a reduced budget is a comparison between two degraded
states, and r is read as a property of the trained model at that
budget, not of the class. On DeepJEB++, where the reduced draw is also
the scored set and the metric is the measure-weighted estimate over it,
the count effect is 1.00 to 1.09 for every architecture.

**What it means.** On the AirfRANS interior task, as on the DrivAerML
Volume task (@sec-nb-char-vol-geo-verdict), ISLA's interior error
depends on how its boundary is sampled, in law and in count. The law
effect (1.2x to 2.2x) is far above the noise floor, and AF-GEO showed
on the block-draw lanes that the queries' built-in nearest-boundary
geometry carries 62% to 84% of the excess under the same coarsening;
CHAR-AREA2 did not repeat that swap on the uniform-draw lanes, so the
attribution on them is by that earlier measurement. This is a second
dataset for the volume model's open weakness, not a new mechanism. The
lug and Tensile2D give no law effect past the registered bars: on the
lug the law moves the error by at most 4%, inside max(2d, 0.05), with
seed 43's two uniform draws 5% apart (the LUG-PREC tie sensitivity,
@sec-nb-char-lug-final); on Tensile2D the two laws are nearly the same
draw. The one
cross-architecture surface test, DeepJEB++, shows the surface pattern
(baselines 1.07x to 1.57x under the area law, ISLA flat) on an ISLA
checkpoint that cannot show anything else, so it does not support the
thesis sentence. Confidence: high on the numbers (lockstep design;
wherever both seeds' r differ from one by more than 1% they agree in
direction, except on the lug, 1.043 / 0.979, a null whose second seed
has d = 0.051); moderate on reading the count effects.

**What changes in the book.** Chapters 9 and 11 to 13 replace the
pending area-weighted statements with these readings, each from
`results/char/area2_2026-10-16.json`: chapter 9 states the AirfRANS
law and count effects for ISLA and ISLA-DTT, chapters 11 and 12 the
Tensile2D and lug nulls and count effects for ISLA, chapter 13 the
three-architecture DeepJEB++ reading with the plateau caveat. The
index lede adds AirfRANS to the Volume sentence. The protocol tables
keep their native and posed columns; the reduced-budget draws have
their own table in each chapter. The CHAR-PROTOCOLS ledger row and
tech-tree node record the measurement.

## 2026-10-16 — GEO0: with full-mesh query geometry ISLA no longer depends on the boundary draw on DrivAerML Volume; on AirfRANS the count and pressure effects mostly vanish, a velocity law effect remains {#sec-nb-geo0}

ISLA's interior error depends on how the boundary is sampled
(@sec-nb-char-area-audit, @sec-nb-char-area2-verdict), through the
queries' distance and direction to the nearest boundary sample. A design
study (scratch/isla-geo-exact-design-2026-10-16/REPORT.md) proposes exact
point-to-face geometry against the full-resolution boundary instead.
GEO0 tests the idea without training, on existing matched pairs that
differ only in the query geometry: `sg_*_provided` (the stored full-mesh
signed distance and normals) against `sg_*_internal` (the nearest boundary
token), ISLA R1 (384 wide, 256 slices, code_v3), two seeds each, on
AirfRANS (the volume set with the windowed interior) and DrivAerML Volume.
The predictions were registered before any redraw result
(scratch/isla-geo0-2026-10-16/PREREG.md); the protocol is that of
@sec-nb-char-area2-verdict, with a second uniform draw as noise floor
(LHR jobs 241664, 241665, 241802). The rescored native errors match the
committed records exactly.

| Set | Geometry | area ÷ uniform (p, v) | uniform ÷ native | area ÷ native |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AirfRANS, 400 segments | full mesh | 1.45 / 1.38, 1.98 / 1.81 | 1.6 to 2.4 | 3.0 to 3.2 |
| AirfRANS, 400 segments | nearest token | 2.65 / 2.89, 1.74 / 1.78 | 4.0 to 7.5 | 11.4 to 13.0 |
| DrivAerML Volume | full mesh | about 1.00 | about 1.00 | 0.9975 to 1.0004 |
| DrivAerML Volume | nearest token | 8.1 to 11.2 | about 1.00 | 8.1 to 11.2 |

Noise floors are at most 0.04 (AirfRANS) and 0.003 (DrivAerML).
**On DrivAerML Volume the nearest-token geometry carries the whole
sensitivity, and full-mesh geometry removes it** (the registered bar,
within 5 percent of native, holds on every field and seed). On AirfRANS
the count bar (at most 4) holds and the law bar (area ÷ uniform at most
1.5) holds on pressure and fails on velocity (1.98 and 1.81); the
nearest-token twin is more law-sensitive on pressure but not on velocity.
The velocity effect is broad (per-case median 1.33 to 1.48, above 1 in 74
to 77 percent of cases). A reading not yet tested: the area law almost
never keeps the refined leading- and trailing-edge segments (smallest
inclusion probability about 1.3e-3), so the few it keeps carry weights
up to about 800 and the slice states' quadratures become noisy; that is
estimator variance, which no change of query geometry removes. Exact
full-mesh geometry is therefore worth building and training; a
pre-registration of the retrained test keeps velocity's law effect at 400
segments outside its bars.

## 2026-10-17 — H-RESID A2 adopted: ISLA's slice sublayer pools and broadcasts the normalized state, and the DeepJEB++ and AeroZoo rate exceptions are retired {#sec-nb-a2-adopted}

::: {.callout-warning}
**AeroZoo numbers withdrawn 2026-10-19** (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn); the rest of this entry stands.
:::

**Ruling.** Peter, 2026-10-17: "make this the ISLA default... no need
for parallel old implementations." Arm A2 of H-RESID
(@sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-prereg, amendment) becomes ISLA's slice-sublayer
reads: the slice states pool `norm_assign(h)` and the broadcast reads
`norm_assign(h)`, so the raw `h` enters a block only through the
residual identity and the token MLP's LayerNorm. The class keeps no
switch back to the raw reads. Its checkpoint version is 0.3.0; 0.1.0
and 0.2.0 checkpoints still load and warn that their slice blocks were
trained on the raw residual stream. The ruling comes before P3's final
read, on the evidence below.

**Evidence.**

- P4 holds (@sec-nb-deepjeb-hresid-p4). On DeepJEB++ at 3.75e-4,
  neither `jbn2_isla_*` lane departs. Validation von Mises at epoch 12
  is 0.447 and 0.439 (displacement 0.213 and 0.222), against the bar of
  0.6; the raw-read lanes at this rate sat at the plateau (0.90 to 1.02)
  from epoch 4.
- P5 holds (@sec-nb-airfrans-hresid-p5). On AirfRANS with uniform
  draws, A2 ÷ the reference ISLA lanes is 0.862 on pressure, 0.790 on
  velocity and 0.877 on eddy viscosity (seed means), against a bar of at
  most 5 percent loss. Both A2 seeds lie below both reference seeds on
  every field, and rotated and translated scoring gives the same ratios
  to three decimals.
- P3 interim (@sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-p3-interim). On AeroZoo `full` at
  3.75e-4 (uniform protocol), both A2 seeds keep their validation
  minimum through epoch 70: 0.0248 and 0.0236 at epoch 70, where their
  raw-read twins read 0.120 and 0.143. The mean token norm of `h` after
  the last block at epoch 43 is 1.7e3 and 1.8e3, against the bar of
  5.7e5 and the raw reads' 5.7e7, so P3's second part holds.

**What changes.** ISLA trains at the reference rate 3.75e-4 on every
dataset. The two per-dataset rate exceptions are retired: DeepJEB++ at
1.875e-4 (@sec-nb-char-deepjeb-rate-ruling) and the AeroZoo half-rate
arms (@sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-prereg, with R2 holding in
@sec-nb-aerozoo-remedy-r2). `isla_surface_deepjebpp.yaml` pins 3.75e-4
like every other ISLA config, and a recipe test checks the rate in
every ISLA model config. The AeroZoo half-rate lanes stay in their
chapter as a labeled rate control. Every standing in the results
chapters (7 to 13, 15 and 20) and in the thesis table comes from
checkpoints trained with the raw reads. Each of those chapters carries
one label that says so, and the ledger row A2-RERUN tracks the reruns
that replace them.

**Still to read.** P3 at epoch 250 on the four AeroZoo remedy lanes
(rows 340 to 343, with arm A as the diagnostic). The DeepJEB++ A2 finals
at epoch 40 (`jbn2_isla_*`), scored against GeoTransolver and
Transolver under the campaign protocol. The reference reruns with the
normalized reads on every dataset (A2-RERUN). The head frame's raw read
of `h`, which A2 leaves in place, is normalized only as a separate,
tested change (@sec-nb-aerozoo-hresid-prereg). If P3 fails at epoch
250, this notebook records it and the AeroZoo rate question reopens.

## 2026-10-17 — A2-RERUN, first two datasets: on DeepJEB++ ISLA now leads both baselines; on Tensile2d R-A2 holds on stress and displacement and fails on plastic strain as registered, a metric dominated by fields that never yield {#sec-nb-a2-rerun-jeb-t2d}

The reference reruns with the normalized reads (@sec-nb-a2-adopted;
pre-registration scratch/isla-a2-rerun-2026-10-17/PREREG.md, approved
before any lane: R-A2, A2 ÷ old reference at or below 1.05 on every
headline field, seed means, both seeds) have their first finals.

**DeepJEB++** (40 epochs at 3.75e-4, final checkpoints, the CHAR scorer;
LHR jobs 249818 and 250770; seed means with seeds 42 and 43): von Mises
0.3919 (0.3942, 0.3895) and displacement 0.1653 (0.1688, 0.1619), against
0.9311 and 0.8713 for the old reference at 1.875e-4 (on the mean-field
plateau), 0.4974 and 0.2307 for GeoTransolver and 0.4364 and 0.1944 for
Transolver. Both A2 seeds lie below every seed of every arm;
GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is 1.27 and 1.40, Transolver ÷ ISLA 1.11 and 1.18.
Rotated and translated scoring equals native. R-A2 holds.

**Tensile2d** (LHR job 251668): A2 ÷ old is 0.568 on stress and 0.519 on
displacement, and 1.265 on plastic strain q (seeds 1.125 and 1.404, both
above the old two-seed range). **R-A2 holds on stress and displacement
and fails on q as registered.** A reading after the fact
(scratch/isla-t2d-q-2026-10-17/REPORT.md) finds the q metric dominated by
fields that never yield: 69 of the 100 test cases have q identically zero,
so after the dataset's normalization their relative error measures a
constant offset (the model's absolute error divided by 0.0211), and those
cases carry 104 percent of the difference (absolute errors 6.2e-8 against
3.9e-8 in strain units). On the 31 cases with any plastic strain the
ratio is 0.978; weighted by plastic-strain energy it is 1.24 with a 95
percent case-bootstrap interval of 0.76 to 1.89, from five yielding
cases. The change is not linked to the pose deviation or to tied nearest
samples. The verdict stands as registered; pre-registrations on this
dataset do not gate on q with this metric again, since five informative
cases cannot support a 5 percent bar. Rotated and translated scoring
deviates from native by 6 to 12 percent on stress and displacement (0.98
to 1.02 before; recorded, not predicted); 2.2 percent of nodes have a tied
nearest boundary sample, mostly at the junction of two collinear
segments, where the direction feature flips sign under the pose, the class
that exact point-to-face geometry (@sec-nb-geo0) removes. Peter kept A2 on
these results (2026-10-17).

## 2026-10-18 — Baseline drive inputs: on HiLift and AirfRANS the baselines read the raw freestream vector where ISLA reads its direction; four reruns are pre-registered and launched {#sec-nb-drive-audit}

::: {.callout-warning}
**AeroZoo numbers withdrawn 2026-10-19** (@sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn); the rest of this entry stands.
:::

**Finding.** The book overhaul found, and verified on LHR, that the
REF-80 HiLift baseline lanes fed GeoTransolver
(`global_embedding: global_data.U_inf`) and Transolver
(`fx.source: global_data.U_inf`) the physical freestream vector in inches
per second, of magnitude 2,679.5 on every case read, while ISLA reads the
unit direction `U_inf_dir`. The recipe's non-dimensionalization touches
cell data only. The September unit-drive rungs measured what this scale
costs the baselines on HiLift: with the unit direction, GeoTransolver
reached 0.83 and Transolver 0.91 of ISLA's error at the 210-wing rung
(@sec-nb-udrvl-210-verdict; @sec-nb-udrv-1260-verdict). The REF-80
HiLift standing (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 1.28, Transolver ÷ ISLA 1.07) is
therefore not a fair comparison, and it is replaced when the
unit-direction pair is scored.

**Audit of every dataset** (read-only; the lanes' saved configs and 6
to 14 cases per dataset):

- **AirfRANS.** GeoTransolver and Transolver read the raw `U_inf`: speed
  31 to 94 m/s and angle −4.9 to 14.9 degrees, both varying across
  cases. ISLA reads the unit direction and the speed. The baselines'
  velocity ratios (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 3.05, Transolver ÷ ISLA 5.59 on
  the uniform protocol) are what a model that cannot read the flow angle
  would show, so they are probably inflated as HiLift's were. The speed
  carries the Reynolds number, so the fair input is the unit direction
  plus a standardized speed, not the direction alone.
- **DrivAerML Surface and Volume, SHIFT-SUV.** The baselines get a
  constant `U_inf` of 38.9 or 30 m/s: no information is missing, only
  its scale. GeoTransolver was shown insensitive to it in September
  (@sec-nb-udrv-int-verdict); Transolver at a constant drive of this size
  was never tested.
- **The lug.** The baselines get no boundary-condition labels, while
  ISLA reads clamp, hole, loaded half and pressure on each boundary
  face. The labels can be inferred from coordinates in the lug's fixed
  frame.
- **No flag.** DeepJEB++, Tensile2d and the AeroZoo global inputs are
  the same O(1) values for every model. On AeroZoo GeoTransolver has no
  inlet or outlet faces and no secondary-inlet velocity, which chapter 20
  states; it leads ISLA on most fields regardless.

**Launched**, each pre-registered before submission:

- **UDRV-HL** (JHB, 4 lanes): GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16
  on HiLift, two seeds each, the REF-80 rows with only the drive set to
  `U_inf_dir`, on the data pipeline and scorer of the HiLift A2 ISLA
  lanes (scratch/isla-udrv-hl-2026-10-18/).
- **DRIVE-FIX** (scratch/isla-drive-fix-2026-10-18/): R1, the four
  AirfRANS baseline lanes with the unit direction plus the speed
  standardized by the training-split statistics; R2, the reference
  Transolver on DrivAerML Surface with the unit direction (two seeds;
  within 3 percent of the reference Transolver on pressure and wall
  shear means no further reruns, otherwise Transolver on DrivAerML
  Volume and SHIFT-SUV and GeoTransolver on all three are considered);
  R3, GeoTransolver 256 on the lug with the four boundary-condition
  labels in its geometry input. ISLA's own AirfRANS speed input stays
  raw: it is not a fairness question.

**Rule from here on.** Every baseline lane reads the unit direction,
plus a standardized magnitude wherever the speed varies across cases,
and a lane counts only after its saved config shows the inputs
(`forward_kwargs`) it was meant to read. The recipe's baseline model
defaults still read `global_data.U_inf` and are changed separately.

**R1, AirfRANS** (uniform protocol, 200 test airfoils, native):

| Arm | Pressure | Velocity | Eddy viscosity |
|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver, fair drive | 0.0109 (0.0111, 0.0107) | 0.0400 (0.0397, 0.0402) | 0.0171 (0.0176, 0.0166) |

| Transolver, raw drive | 0.0135 | 0.0669 | 0.0212 |
| ISLA (A2) | 0.0180 | 0.0095 | 0.0223 |

The fair drive (the unit direction plus the standardized speed) lowers

## 2026-10-19 — Continuous query-geometry encoding adopted: on exact geometry, asinh distances and a sign-carrying direction lower ISLA's error on every decision field {#sec-nb-geo-cont-verdict}

**Question** (E2 of the architecture agenda, pre-registered 2026-10-18 in
scratch/isla-geo-cont-2026-10-18/PREREG.md). On exact geometry, ISLA's
query features read the scaled distance s = d / L in two channels,
`[s, sign(s) · log(|s| + 1e-12)]`, which jump across the surface and at
s = 0. Does a continuous encoding do better: `[s, asinh(s / 1e-6)]`, with
the direction channel ν = sign(d) · u (sign(0) = +1)? The arms are
CONTROL, the exact-geometry code as it stands, and CONT. Each runs two
seeds on Tensile2d, the lug and AirfRANS, from one snapshot pair.

**Rule.** Adopt if the geometric mean of CONT ÷ CONTROL over the four
low-noise fields is at most 1.01 and none reaches 1.10. The four fields
are Tensile2d displacement and AirfRANS velocity, pressure and eddy
viscosity. Noisy fields (Tensile2d stress and plastic strain, lug von
Mises) are flagged when both CONT seeds fall outside CONTROL's range.

| Field | CONTROL | CONT | CONT ÷ CONTROL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tensile2d displacement | 0.0067 (0.0072, 0.0062) | 0.0064 (0.0066, 0.0062) | 0.956 |
| AirfRANS velocity | 0.00928 (0.00989, 0.00867) | 0.00864 (0.00850, 0.00877) | 0.931 |
| AirfRANS pressure | 0.01698 (0.01671, 0.01726) | 0.01574 (0.01584, 0.01565) | 0.927 |
| AirfRANS eddy viscosity | 0.02164 (0.02271, 0.02056) | 0.02056 (0.02036, 0.02076) | 0.950 |

**Verdict: adopt.** The geometric mean is 0.941 and the largest ratio is
0.956. Of the noisy fields, Tensile2d stress (0.999) and plastic strain
(1.019) are not flagged. Lug von Mises is flagged on native: CONT 0.00174
against CONTROL 0.00155, a ratio of 1.13, with both CONT seeds above
both CONTROL seeds. With two seeds per arm, that ordering arises by
chance in one case of six. Posed it reads 1.09 and is not flagged.
Posed ÷ native is 1.0000 on Tensile2d and AirfRANS for both arms. On the
lug it is 1.08 to 1.11 for CONTROL and 1.05 to 1.06 for CONT.

**Beside the rule: exact geometry against nearest-token geometry.** CONTROL
is the exact-geometry code. On AirfRANS it scores 0.98 / 0.94 / 0.97 of the A2 reference's
nearest-token error on velocity / pressure / eddy viscosity, and CONT
scores 0.91 / 0.87 / 0.92. On the lug, CONTROL scores 0.90 of A2's
native error, and its posed ÷ native falls from 4.14 / 2.87 under
nearest-token geometry to 1.08 to 1.11. The ties between nearest tokens
caused most of the lug's pose sensitivity. What remains matches the
direction ties on the part's medial surface
(scratch/isla-geo-cont-2026-10-18/DESIGN_NOTE_medial_ties.md).

**Next.** CONT joins ISLA's new reference: exact geometry plus boundary
conditions by name (psharpe/isla-bc-names). It lands there with a new
checkpoint version, because its features change while the weight layout
stays the same.

## 2026-10-19 — AeroZoo results withdrawn: every AeroZoo lane read labels that the input rule forbids, and a corrected protocol replaces it {#sec-nb-aerozoo-withdrawn}

**Ruling.** Peter ruled on 2026-10-15, in the AeroZoo book's section on allowed inputs, what an AeroZoo model may
read: only the data of the PDE. That is the boundary meshes with their condition types, the prescribed values
(`cell_data/prescribed/*`) and the kinematic viscosity, with density only to convert pressure and shear to pascals.
Everything else in `global_data` is a label. On 2026-10-19 he added that no model may receive a reference length
that varies per sample: "If a model wants normalized coordinates, it needs to bring it to the table."

**What the AeroZoo lanes read.** Every AeroZoo lane of this program, from @sec-nb-aerozoo-prereg on, read labels
(scratch/isla-lref-audit-2026-10-19/REPORT.md; scratch/isla-az-compliant-2026-10-19/inventory/):

- ISLA, ISLA-DTT and GeoTransolver read the freestream direction from `reference.velocity`, and a log Reynolds number
  built from `reference.length`.
- The per-face prescribed ω and the inlet globals were scaled by `reference.length`.
- Every arm's eddy-viscosity and ω targets were scaled by `reference.length`.
- GeoTransolver's coordinates, signed distances and ball radii were scaled by `reference.length`.

`reference.length` is the body's largest extent before the random pose: 0.02 to 18 m, a different value in every
case, and not computable from the posed boundary.

**Action.** Peter: "If the new one is strictly better or fixes a bug, just do that and delete the old results."

- The corrected protocol replaces the label-input one under the same file names. It gives every model only physical
  PDE inputs.
  - ISLA computes its own length, velocity and Reynolds-number scales inside the model.
  - GeoTransolver reads every boundary face, with its condition type and prescribed values, through its
    geometry-features channel. Its local features are off: a supported setting, but a departure from its released
    configurations.
  - Transolver's inputs have no channel for boundary values, so it runs two floor lanes on `full`.
  - Targets are physical, with one constant scale per field, and every arm trains with a per-case relative L2 loss.
- All 391 label-era AeroZoo lanes were cancelled, and their checkpoints and scores deleted: 14.45 TB on LHR and
  1.02 TB on AGA (scratch/isla-az-retire-2026-10-19/SUMMARY.md). The entries above that report AeroZoo numbers carry a
  withdrawal note. They remain as the record of how decisions were made.

**Decisions that used AeroZoo evidence.**

- A2 (@sec-nb-a2-adopted) also rests on DeepJEB++ and AirfRANS, and it stands.
- The single-input exact-geometry design was decided by Peter on principle on 2026-10-19, after a close AeroZoo
  result, and it stands.
- ISLA against ISLA-DTT, which Peter wants AeroZoo to decide, moves to the corrected lanes, which run both.
- The AeroZoo ratios of the head-frame normalization test move to the corrected protocol.

## 2026-10-19 — Boundary-drawn anchors do not replace interacting ISLA on AirfRANS, and ISLA-DTT leads it by 26 percent on pressure {#sec-nb-anchor-verdict}

**Question** (E3b of the architecture agenda, pre-registered 2026-10-18 in
scratch/isla-anchor-2026-10-18/PREREG.md). Interacting ISLA lets the
requested points write into the slices, so its prediction at a point
depends on which other points are requested. Can a query-independent ISLA
match it when its interior writers are anchors drawn from the boundary
alone, by a cosine law along the boundary normals out to the domain
diameter? Five arms ran two seeds each on AirfRANS uniform, from one
snapshot of the A2 code (nearest-token geometry):

- A, interacting ISLA, the control;
- B, passive: query-independent, with the boundary as the only writer;
- C, ANCHOR: 50,000 boundary-drawn anchors as interior writers;
- D, ISLA-DTT: query-independent, with its boundary read;
- E, a diagnostic: 50,000 anchors at the CFD mesh nodes, which separates
  the anchors' law from their role.

**Rule.** C must first pass a validity check: far-field companion points
move its predictions by at most 1e-4 in float32 and 1e-9 in float64. C
replaces A if the geometric mean of C ÷ A over pressure and velocity is
at most 1.05 and eddy viscosity is at most 1.10. It does not replace A if
C ÷ A reaches 1.10 on pressure or velocity with both seeds agreeing.
Otherwise Peter decides.

| Arm | Pressure | Velocity | Eddy viscosity | ÷ A (p / v / eddy viscosity) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, interacting ISLA | 0.01835 (0.01808, 0.01861) | 0.00971 (0.00940, 0.01002) | 0.02257 (0.02112, 0.02402) | 1 |
| B, passive | 0.01569 (0.01685, 0.01452) | 0.01025 (0.01031, 0.01018) | 0.02417 (0.02372, 0.02461) | 0.855 / 1.055 / 1.071 |
| C, ANCHOR | 0.02601 (0.02967, 0.02234) | 0.01438 (0.01648, 0.01228) | 0.02493 (0.02873, 0.02113) | 1.417 / 1.481 / 1.104 |
| D, ISLA-DTT | 0.01361 (0.01356, 0.01367) | 0.00861 (0.00865, 0.00857) | 0.02231 (0.02137, 0.02324) | 0.742 / 0.887 / 0.988 |
| E, mesh-node anchors | 0.02068 (0.02146, 0.01990) | 0.01054 (0.01052, 0.01056) | 0.02363 (0.02388, 0.02337) | 1.127 / 1.086 / 1.047 |

Native relative L2 error, float32, 200 test cases at 100,000 points;
seed means with seeds 42 and 43 in parentheses.

**Verdict: does not replace.** C passes the validity check: far-field
companions move its float64 predictions by at most 7e-12 of the RMS
target. C ÷ A is 1.640 and 1.201 on pressure and 1.753 and 1.226 on
velocity for seeds 42 and 43, all above 1.10. The geometric mean over
pressure and velocity is 1.449. The ANCHOR line ends here and does not
go on to AeroZoo.

**Beside the rule.**

- ISLA-DTT leads interacting ISLA by 26 percent on pressure and 11
  percent on velocity, and eddy viscosity is level. Both seeds agree on
  pressure (0.750, 0.734) and on velocity (0.920, 0.856). The
  pre-registration expected the opposite, from the pre-A2 runs, in which
  ISLA-DTT trailed ISLA by 11, 26 and 21 percent. The passive arm also
  leads A on pressure (0.855). On AirfRANS, the coupling between
  requested points seems to cost interacting ISLA accuracy.
- Interior writers hurt pressure whatever their law. The mesh-node
  anchors read 1.32 of the passive arm on pressure, and the boundary-drawn
  ones 1.66.
- C is not pose-exact as built. Scored fully eager, its posed ÷ native on
  eddy viscosity is 0.971 (seed 42) and 1.011 (seed 43), while every other
  run stays within 0.23 percent. A pose changes which anchors the fixed
  evaluation stream draws. (Corrected 2026-10-21: this entry first gave
  1.185 for seed 43, a value produced by the compiled-path fault of
  @sec-nb-compiled-path-defect.)
- The query-population probe confirms that A depends on its companions:
  far-field companions raise its error 26 to 63 times. In float64, B and
  E move by at most 5e-12 of the RMS target. D first moved by 2e-6, above
  the 1e-9 line, because its cluster means ran in float32 with an
  order-dependent sum on CUDA: the same forward pass run twice moved it by
  1e-6. With the cluster means in float64, D moves by at most 3e-14, so
  ISLA-DTT is query-independent to roundoff.
- Step time at mid-run, relative to A: B 1.00, C 1.20, D 1.22, E 1.21.
  Peak memory is 38.0 GB for A, 42.0 GB for D and 55.5 GB for C
  (scratch/isla-anchor-2026-10-18/RESULTS.md).

**Next.** The corrected AeroZoo lanes decide ISLA against ISLA-DTT. This
result goes beside them as AirfRANS evidence in ISLA-DTT's favor, on the
A2 code with nearest-token geometry. The same comparison on the new
reference (exact geometry, the continuous encoding and conditions by
name) follows its adoption check.

**Verdicts.**

- R-A2 fails on pressure: A2 ÷ old reference is 1.062, and both A2 seeds

  SHIFT-SUV the same ratio is at most 5.4e-4 from one.
- P1 holds for both baselines. The unit direction lowers native pressure to

- P2: Transolver is "baseline ahead", lower than A2 ISLA on 153 of 180
  cases. GeoTransolver falls between the bands: its ratio is 0.904, but it

**Where ISLA trails** (scratch/isla-hilift090-2026-10-20/RESULTS.md).

  peaks of the main element (82 percent) and the slat (16 percent), mostly
  where Cp is below −4, which is 0.2 to 0.4 percent of the area. In this
  split, GeoTransolver and Transolver are seed 42 only.
- Against Transolver the deficit is broad: ISLA is worse on 85 percent of

- Under the area and posed protocols ISLA leads by a wide margin: baseline

**Next.** HiLift needs no decimated geometry asset for 0.9.0. HiLift is a

prediction points. Measured on a GB300, 0.9.0 takes 64.5 GiB and 0.34 s
per step, the same as A2. Its two lanes are the next HiLift row.

## 2026-10-20 — Head-frame normalization (E1): on AirfRANS and DeepJEB++ it matches or beats the raw read, and it removes the head frame's collapse to a single point on DeepJEB++ {#sec-nb-headnorm-jb}

**Question** (E1 HEAD-NORM, pre-registered 2026-10-18 in
scratch/isla-headnorm-2026-10-18/PREREG.md). Should ISLA's head frame read
the normalized state norm_out(h) rather than the raw residual stream, so that
its routing scores cannot grow with the stream? HEADNORM changes only that
read, with the same parameters. CONTROL is A2. Both arms are two seeds on
AirfRANS (scored 2026-10-19) and DeepJEB++ (5,540 test samples, epoch 40,
float32).

| Dataset | Field | CONTROL | HEADNORM | HEADNORM ÷ CONTROL (seeds) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AirfRANS | pressure | 0.01828 | 0.01808 | 0.989 (1.039, 0.942) |
| AirfRANS | velocity | 0.00950 | 0.00958 | 1.008 (1.022, 0.994) |
| AirfRANS | eddy viscosity | 0.02143 | 0.02039 | 0.952 (0.973, 0.931) |
| DeepJEB++ | von Mises | 0.40030 | 0.39652 | 0.991 (0.993, 0.988) |
| DeepJEB++ | displacement | 0.16868 | 0.16245 | 0.963 (0.951, 0.975) |

Native relative L2, seed means. Posed and area equal native to the digits
shown, since the pose is exact and DeepJEB++ is read whole. The AirfRANS
rows are compiled-path scores. Scored eager, HEADNORM ÷ CONTROL is 0.978 /
1.009 / 0.957 (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect).

**The instrument** (a read-only probe of the head frame on the first 4
validation cases, bf16 autocast forward). On DeepJEB++, CONTROL's head frame
collapses to an argmax
on both seeds from epochs 13 to 19: the smallest seed support is one point,
with a largest weight of 0.64. Its seed-logit p99.9 grows 1,335 and 1,516
times, to about 5,200. HEADNORM never collapses: its smallest support is
13,996 tokens, its largest weight 0.004, and its final p99.9 is 0.57. On
AirfRANS neither arm collapses, and HEADNORM's p99.9 is 0.54 against
CONTROL's 7.5. The stream itself still grows on DeepJEB++ in both arms, to
about 2.2e4. HEADNORM bounds what the head frame reads, not the stream.

**Verdict.** The registered rule needs 14 ratios. Two were on AeroZoo's
label-era protocol, which was retired, so the rule cannot complete as
written. On the 12 ratios that exist, the accuracy test (a') holds: the
geometric mean is 0.980, the largest ratio is 1.008, and none reaches 1.10.
The instrument tests (b1) to (b3) hold on both datasets. The two missing
ratios can block adoption only through the 1.10 clause, since each would
have to exceed 1.21 to break the 1.01 bar on the mean.

**Predictions.** P-ACC held: every ratio lies in [0.95, 1.05], and the
geometric mean lies in [0.97, 1.01]. P-JEB held, with displacement at 0.963.
HEADNORM's final p99.9 on DeepJEB++ fell in the predicted 0.3 to 15. Both
CONTROL lanes collapsed by epoch 39 as predicted. Seed 42's growth of 1,516
sits just above the predicted 200 to 1,500.

**Decision.** Adopt on principle, after one clean AeroZoo pair under the
corrected protocol. The change removes a degenerate head frame at no measured
cost. The pair is 0.9.0 with HEADNORM against the running 0.9.0 lanes on
family_non_box. It applies the 1.10 clause to velocity and pressure and the
instrument tests to AeroZoo, and it is pre-registered before submission as
E1-AZ. HEADNORM then enters the next reference version. The 0.9.0 standings
stay until that version is rerun
(scratch/isla-headnorm-2026-10-18/RESULTS_JB_2026-10-20.txt).

**Later (2026-10-22).** E1-AZ read REJECT under this rule. On the held-out AeroZoo family, HEADNORM ÷ CONTROL is 1.287 on pressure, with both seed-matched ratios at least 1.10 (1.339 / 1.178), and 1.047 on velocity. Beside the rule: on that pressure both arms do worse than predicting zero (relative L2 2.77 for CONTROL, 3.57 for HEADNORM), so the reject rests on a field where ISLA 0.9.0 has no skill; with the stream normalized, the head frame stays near-uniform. So HEADNORM does not enter the next reference, and 0.9.0 stays the reference (scratch/isla-az-decide-2026-10-21/RESULTS_E1AZ_raw.txt).

## 2026-10-21 — Correction: on AirfRANS, Tensile2d and the lug, ISLA's per-block compiled path computed a different function from the model, through a PyTorch compiler bug {#sec-nb-compiled-path-defect}

**What happened.** The recipe trains and scores ISLA with `compile_blocks`,
which compiled each slice block with Inductor's default options. In torch
2.12 and 2.13, one of them, mix-order reduction, adds the padded rows of the
last tile of tokens to the per-slice sums (pytorch/pytorch#195845, fixed on
PyTorch main on 2026-09-29). The fault needs three conditions:

- the eager geometry region (two-dimensional models, and models without a
  global direction such as the lug);
- at least 10,240 tokens;
- a token count that is not a multiple of 4.

When all three hold, every block is 3 to 8 percent wrong. The AirfRANS,
Tensile2d and lug ISLA lanes behind every standing and decision trained and
were scored in this path. The other datasets use the fused geometry kernel
and match the eager model to float32 roundoff on every case: SHIFT-SUV,
DrivAerML Surface and Volume, DeepJEB++, HiLift and AeroZoo. The capacity
audit ran eager. The query-population probe found the fault, because its
eager validity check disagreed with the scorer case by case
(scratch/isla-compile-af-2026-10-21/RESULTS.md).

**Per case.** About 153 of 200 AirfRANS cases moved by more than 1e-3 in
relative L2, by up to 53 percent. On the lug, 278 and 428 of 600 cases moved,
by up to 63 percent; on Tensile2d, 37 to 42 of 100, by up to 8 percent on
stress (see the later note). In this path ISLA-DTT was not query-independent: a fixed query's
prediction moved by up to 5e-2 when the other queries changed, against
1.2e-6 eager.

**Case means and the ratios built on them** (the same cases re-scored fully
eager; seed means):

| Quantity | Recorded (compiled path) | Eager |
|---|---|---|
| AirfRANS, ISLA 0.9.0 ÷ A2 ISLA, p / v / nut (pooled G) | 0.659 / 0.681 / 0.709 (0.683) | 0.662 / 0.675 / 0.698 (0.678) |
| AirfRANS, ISLA-DTT ÷ ISLA at 0.9.0 | 1.163 / 1.147 / 1.396 | 1.181 / 1.154 / 1.433 |
| AirfRANS, fair-drive GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 0.9.0 | 0.919 / 6.211 / 1.080 | 0.913 / 6.225 / 1.096 |
| AirfRANS, fair-drive Transolver ÷ ISLA 0.9.0 | 0.919 / 4.610 / 1.127 | 0.913 / 4.619 / 1.143 |
| AirfRANS, GLOBE ÷ ISLA 0.9.0 | 2.007 / 3.327 / 2.408 | 1.992 / 3.335 / 2.442 |
| AirfRANS (A2 era), ISLA-DTT ÷ interacting ISLA (E3b) | 0.742 / 0.887 / 0.988 | 0.754 / 0.889 / 0.995 |
| AirfRANS (A2 era), anchored ÷ interacting (E3b) | 1.417 / 1.481 / 1.104 | 1.402 / 1.485 / 1.100 |
| AirfRANS (A2 era), head-frame normalization ÷ control (E1) | 0.989 / 1.008 / 0.952 | 0.978 / 1.009 / 0.957 |
| AirfRANS (A2 era), earlier ISLA-DTT build (code_dtt16) ÷ A2 ISLA | 1.109 / 1.258 / 1.213 | 0.971 / 1.210 / 1.146 |
| GEO-CONT decision G | 0.941 | 0.943 |
| Tensile2d displacement, ISLA 0.9.0 ÷ A2 ISLA | 1.041 | 1.045 |
| Lug von Mises, ISLA 0.9.0 ÷ A2 ISLA | 1.104 | 1.099 |

No registered verdict changes. The largest single move is the earlier
ISLA-DTT build's pressure, 12 percent lower eager, which puts that build 3
percent ahead of A2 ISLA on pressure instead of 11 percent behind. One claim
was wrong and is relabelled in place: @sec-nb-anchor-verdict gave the anchored arm's posed ÷ native on eddy
viscosity as 1.185 for seed 43. Eager, it is 0.971 and 1.011 for the two
seeds.

**The fix** (merged as 6e2f247e9). The blocks compile with mix-order
reduction off. Compiled then equals eager to float32 roundoff on every case
tested: AirfRANS ISLA and ISLA-DTT, the lug and Tensile2d. ISLA-DTT is
query-independent again. The step time is unchanged: 0.387 s on AirfRANS
against 0.379 s, where fully eager takes 0.751 s. Two regression tests run
at sizes where the fusion fires, and both fail without the fix. The
existing tests ran below those sizes.

**What these numbers are.** The eager re-scores give each trained model's
own function. They do not measure training: about three quarters of every
affected lane's steps ran the perturbed forward and backward, and ISLA-DTT
trained without its query independence. So the AirfRANS, Tensile2d and lug
reference lanes are retrained under the fix, and the retrained rows become
the standings. The 22 lanes that were training under the fault were
cancelled on 2026-10-21 and relaunch under the fix: AF-EXTRAP's ISLA and
ISLA-DTT arms, ATTRIB-090's AirfRANS and lug arms, and REF-090's lug
ISLA-DTT.

**Later (2026-10-22).** An independent check of the fix (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/second-read-2026-10-22/cert.md) confirms it: with mix-order reduction off, ISLA's per-block compiled path equals the eager function on every case measured. The N % 4 rule holds exactly on AirfRANS (20 of 20), lug seed 42 (60 of 60) and Tensile2d. Lug seed 43's checkpoint amplifies float32 roundoff: its eager float32 and float64 forwards differ by a median 1.8e-3 per case, against 7e-6 on seed 42. So about 150 of seed 43's 428 moved cases are roundoff, not the fault, and roundoff moves its case means by about 0.1 to 0.2 percent. The model.py fix was certified on 20 of 200 AirfRANS cases per checkpoint, and the environment-variable path on all 200 cases of one AirfRANS ISLA-DTT checkpoint. Both certifications cover the float32 forward only. On AeroZoo the fault cannot fire at the scorer's settings: every block sees 400,000 tokens (200,000 drawn boundary tokens plus 200,000 interior points, a multiple of 4), and the geometry runs in the fused kernel. Compiled and eager agree to 4.8e-6 on ISLA and to 6.9e-4 on one ISLA-DTT case (job 333632, 20 cases each), both below the float32-against-float64 floor, which on AeroZoo reaches 1e-2 to 0.28 of the target's RMS on 4 of 20 ISLA cases (scratch/isla-az-decide-2026-10-21/cmpdiag/README.md). PROBES-090's 4.9e-4 sits inside that floor. Training under the fault changed what training found on some datasets and not on others. Models retrained on the fixed path, divided by the originals (both scored eager), read 1.024 / 0.985 / 0.998 for AirfRANS ISLA, 0.898 / 0.961 / 0.962 for AirfRANS ISLA-DTT and 0.768 for the lug's von Mises. The AirfRANS, Tensile2d and lug standings are now the eager-trained rows (@sec-nb-ref090-t2d-control).

## 2026-10-21 — ISLA's residual stream grows without bound while the learning rate is constant, and only the head frame reads its scale {#sec-nb-stream-audit}

**Question** (STREAM-AUDIT, a read-only measurement with no rule). Does
ISLA 0.9.0's residual stream grow without bound, and does the growth harm
anything? Probes on the REF-090 and AeroZoo checkpoints read the mean token
norm of the stream after the last block at every saved epoch, up to epoch
149 (AeroZoo full), 173 (AeroZoo family_non_box), 241 and 239 (lug
ISLA-DTT) and 39 and 37 (DeepJEB++).

| Dataset | Epoch 1 | Epoch 99 | Last (epoch) |
|---|---|---|---|
| AirfRANS ISLA | 127 / 109 | 1,011 / 985 | 1,025 / 981 (500) |
| AirfRANS ISLA-DTT | 141 / 134 | 1,238 / 1,208 | 1,317 / 1,243 (500) |
| DrivAerML Surface | 106 / 114 | 203 / 205 | 201 / 204 (500) |
| DrivAerML Volume | 111 / 114 | 276 / 267 | 270 / 260 (500) |
| SHIFT-SUV | 106 / 117 | 506 / 503 | 531 / 527 (500) |
| Tensile2d | 83 / 85 | 439 / 430 | 444 / 440 (500) |
| Lug ISLA | 123 / 134 | 995 / 1,139 | 1,091 / 1,213 (500) |
| DeepJEB++ | 749 / 751 | – | 20,200 / 18,870 (39 / 37) |
| AeroZoo `full` (seed 42) | 292 | 8,350 | 8,161 (149) |

Mean token norm of ISLA 0.9.0's stream after the last block (ISLA-DTT where
the row says so); seeds 42 / 43. The AirfRANS, Tensile2d and lug checkpoints
were trained under the compiled-path fault (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect).

**Findings.**

- The norm grows linearly in optimizer steps while the rate is constant
  (R² 0.92 to 1.00), except on AirfRANS, where a square-root-of-steps fit is
  better (R² 0.99 against 0.98). So its growth per epoch scales with the
  steps per epoch, times a prefactor that differs 14-fold between datasets
  (dh/dS 23 to 323). It stops at the StepLR cut: over the next 400 epochs it
  moves by −3 to +10 percent (AeroZoo, read only to epochs 149 and 173, by
  −2 and −6 percent), while the training loss falls another 2 to 45 times.
  DeepJEB++, whose schedule never cuts the rate, still grows linearly at
  epochs 39 (seed 42) and 37 (seed 43), its last ones read.
- The cause is the weights that write into the stream, which grow 1.05 to
  8.8 times (embedding 1.05 to 2.6, broadcast 1.4 to 7.3, MLP output
  projections 1.9 to 8.8). Under Muon the recipe's weight decay is
  effectively off: weights shrink by 0.04 to 1.8 percent per run in total. The lug, which has no head
  frame, still grows 9 times, so the growth needs no raw read of the stream.
- No harm was measured outside the head frame. No block update comes near
  bf16 resolution of the stream: the smallest is 3 to 30 percent of its norm
  at the end of training. Doubling the whole stream moves scalar outputs by
  at most 1.5e-4 of the target norm and vector outputs by 0.02 to 2.7
  percent. With the head frame's input divided back by 2, so that no read
  sees the doubling, vector outputs move by at most 5.8e-4 of the target
  norm.
- On the case-mean record, ISLA 0.9.0's head frame collapses on DeepJEB++
  from epoch 13 on both seeds (on the worst case alone, from epochs 9 and 7),
  as A2's did. Its largest weight passes 0.5 at epoch 31 (seed 42) and 35
  (seed 43). E1's
  head-frame normalization (@sec-nb-headnorm-jb) removes the one read that
  scales with the stream.
- The probe's hooks-on and hooks-off forwards differ by up to 1.85e-3 in
  velocity on AeroZoo family_non_box (seed 42, epoch 1), against 1.83e-3
  between two forwards without hooks. That is GPU
  nondeterminism, as E1-AZ assumed.

**What it leaves.** An implicit learning-rate decay: the stream-writing
weights grow 1.05 to 8.8 times over the full-rate phase (the MLP output
projections 1.9 to 8.8), so Muon's fixed-size step shrinks relative to them
by the same factor. This is inferred, not measured. Moonlight (arXiv
2502.16982) reports the weight growth for Muon without weight decay, not the
step shrinkage. A decoupled weight decay on the Muon matrices is predicted
to bound the stream (E5's draft gives h_last / h_e1 ≤ 3 a probability of
0.8). It is drafted (scratch/isla-stream-audit-2026-10-21/PREREG_E5.md,
about 480 GPU-h) but not run. The audit rates it worth running after E1-AZ,
at low priority, and the draft awaits the supervisor's approval. Its most
likely result is an accuracy null plus a bounded stream
(scratch/isla-stream-audit-2026-10-21/REPORT.md).

**Later.** E1-AZ (2026-10-22) rejected head-frame normalization under its registered AeroZoo rule. On the held-out AeroZoo family it raised pressure error by 29 percent (HEADNORM ÷ 0.9.0 CONTROL, seed means 1.287; seed-matched 1.339 and 1.178, both above 1.10), on a field where neither arm beats predicting zero (relative L2 2.77 and 3.57); velocity read 1.047, within seed spread. ISLA 0.9.0's head frame still reads the raw stream (scratch/isla-headnorm-2026-10-18/).

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by the reviewer on 2026-10-22 (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/SECOND_READ_2026-10-22.md).*

## 2026-10-21 — ATTRIB-090 on Tensile2d: with four seeds the CONT-to-0.9.0 step is not real, and inside 0.9.0 the BC-NAMES query embedding beats the 0.6.0 one {#sec-nb-attrib090-t2d}

**Question** (ATTRIB-090, pre-registered 2026-10-20 in scratch/isla-attrib090-2026-10-21/PREREG.md, amended before
results in its §9). REF-090 put ISLA 0.9.0's Tensile2d displacement at 1.041 of ISLA's A2 configuration (scratch/isla-ref090-2026-10-20/RESULTS_partial.md). Against E2's CONT arm
(@sec-nb-geo-cont-verdict), the last rung before 0.9.0, ISLA 0.9.0 read 1.115 of CONT on two seeds. Which piece of the bundle between them
causes it? The candidates tested were one input layer per named condition (COND), the new prediction-point embedding of BC-NAMES
(QEMB), and the removal of the stored-SDF query inputs (SDF); the gauge L and drift also changed but have no arm. Each arm is 0.9.0
with one piece put back. ALL puts back all three, which is 0.8.0 at 0.9.0 code less the gauge and drift.
Every arm runs four seeds (42-45), as do the base (0.9.0) and CONT, each of which gained two new seeds (44, 45) here.

**Rule.** For each arm, take Δ = the mean log error minus the base's. σ is pooled over the six arms (18 degrees of freedom).
An arm moves a field if |Δ| ≥ 2 SE and the effect is at least 5 %. The step itself counts as real only if CONT against the
base passes the same test (R4). Scores are fully eager float32: the per-block compiled scorer computes a slightly different
function on 37-42 of the 100 cases (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect). The scorer-path verdicts are the same. Every arm, the base and CONT trained under that defect, so the comparison is like for like and describes defect-trained models.

| arm (what it puts back) | displacement, seeds 42 / 43 / 44 / 45 | mean | ÷ 0.9.0 | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9.0 (base) | 0.00729, 0.00697, 0.00737, 0.00708 | 0.00717 | 1 | – |
| CONT (E2, 0.6.0) | 0.00662, 0.00626, 0.00711, 0.00716 | 0.00679 | 0.945 | not real (R4) |
| COND (one labelled boundary) | 0.00683, 0.00723, 0.01001, 0.00849 | 0.00814 | 1.122 | no measurable effect |
| SDF (stored SDF query input) | 0.00995, 0.00704, 0.00752, 0.00810 | 0.00815 | 1.127 | no measurable effect |
| QEMB (0.6.0 query embedding) | 0.00987, 0.00823, 0.00877, 0.00830 | 0.00879 | 1.223 | moves, away from CONT |
| ALL (all three) | 0.00720, 0.00518, 0.00724, 0.00700 | 0.00666 | 0.919 | no measurable effect |

Native relative L2, 100 validation cases, epoch 500, float32 eager. The ÷ 0.9.0 column is exp(Δ), the ratio of geometric seed
means, so it differs from the ratio of the mean column (COND 1.134, SDF 1.136, ALL 0.928). Pooled σ(log) is 0.12, so 2 SE = 0.17.
Stress and plastic strain show no measurable effect in any arm. Posed matches native within 0.1 percent on every ratio.

**Verdict: the step is not real.** With four seeds each, CONT reads 0.945 of 0.9.0 (Δ = −0.057), well inside the 2 SE bar.
The two new CONT seeds land inside 0.9.0's range (0.00697-0.00737); E2's two seeds were the low ones. Under R3, ALL shows no
measurable effect, so the registered reading is that the step is not reproduced in the reverted pieces (it lies in the gauge,
drift or noise); with R4, noise. So no cause is named, and no mirror arm runs on the lug.

**Beside the rule.**
- The one effect that passes R1 is QEMB (Δ = 2.3 SE; one arm, four seeds, so confidence in its direction is moderate). All
  four QEMB seeds lie above all four 0.9.0 seeds. Inside ISLA 0.9.0 and on these defect-trained models, the BC-NAMES
  embedding beats the 0.6.0 one on Tensile2d displacement by about 18 percent; the result does not isolate why. In the BC-NAMES embedding, the distance channels enter the prediction
  points' own seed layer, as a condition's fields enter its own layer. The 0.6.0 embedding added a type offset and a separate
  feature MLP to a shared seed embedding.
- ALL also uses the 0.6.0 embedding, with the stored-SDF features in its MLP and one labelled boundary, and it does not show
  the cost (0.919 of 0.9.0). The pieces interact, and one arm cannot say how.
- 0.9.0 is the most reproducible arm: its four seeds lie within 5.6 percent. Each other arm has one seed 10 to 33 percent
  away from the mean of its other three (CONT s43 10 percent low, QEMB s42 17 percent high, ALL s43 28 percent low, SDF s42
  32 percent high, COND s44 33 percent high). That holds for defect-trained models: eager-trained, 0.9.0's four seeds spread
  from 0.00629 to 0.01092 (σ(log) 0.232 against 0.025 here; @sec-nb-ref090-t2d-control).
- REF-090's Tensile2d flag (ISLA 0.9.0 at 1.041 of A2, 1.045 eager) is smaller than the 5.6 percent spread of the four 0.9.0
  seeds, but both A2 seeds (eager 0.00679, 0.00685) still lie below all four 0.9.0 seeds (lowest 0.00697).

**Next.** AirfRANS and the lug run their arms again under the compile fix (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect), against the retrained 0.9.0
bases. Their verdicts follow in a separate entry.

**Later.** The Tensile2d training-path control (@sec-nb-ref090-t2d-control) read (b), that the fixed compiled path trains differently from eager, on weak evidence, so the Tensile2d standing is now the eager-trained rows. These arms stay defect-trained, like their base. On AirfRANS the arms were rerun under the fix (2026-10-22, scratch/isla-attrib090-2026-10-21/RESULTS.md). NOSC, which removes ISLA's scales and also feeds the raw, unstandardized inlet speed, undoes the AirfRANS gain (φ 0.83 / 1.00 / 0.83). So the gain lies in the scales or in the input standardization, which NOSC changes together. A standardized-speed arm (NOSC-STD) is registered to separate them. Their entry follows.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by the reviewer on 2026-10-22 (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/SECOND_READ_2026-10-22.md).*

## 2026-10-21 — REF-090 R1: ISLA 0.9.0 against A2 on six datasets, pooled G 0.891, confirmed; Tensile2d displacement is the one low-noise field above 1.03 {#sec-nb-ref090-r1}

**Question** (REF-090 R1, pre-registered 2026-10-20 before submission in
scratch/isla-ref090-2026-10-20/PREREG.md, §11 amended before submission).
How does ISLA 0.9.0 compare with its A2 partner on each partner's own
protocol? 0.9.0 adds the exact full-mesh gauge, boundary conditions by name,
exact query geometry with the continuous encoding, its own scales (switched
on among these datasets only on AirfRANS), and upstream/main. Each 0.9.0
lane is its A2 partner's row with only the code and recipe replaced. Two
seeds were scored in float32 on the partner's scored set. The registered
verdict is pooled: confirmed if the geometric mean of 0.9.0 ÷ A2 over the
13 low-noise headline fields is at most 1.03, and no field reaches 1.10 on
both seeds. R1 cannot un-adopt 0.9.0, so "confirmed" says that the
standings move. It is not a test of the adoption.

| Dataset | Field | 0.9.0 ÷ A2 | Seeds (q) | G_d |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SHIFT-SUV | pressure / wall shear | 0.975 / 0.983 | 0.999, 0.952 / 0.992, 0.975 | 0.979 |
| DrivAerML Surface | pressure / wall shear | 0.924 / 0.946 | 0.925, 0.923 / 0.945, 0.946 | 0.935 |
| DrivAerML Volume | pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity | 0.939 / 0.875 / 0.961 | 0.929, 0.950 / 0.869, 0.881 / 0.954, 0.969 | 0.924 |
| DeepJEB++ | von Mises / displacement | 1.014 / 1.001 | 1.001, 1.027 / 0.958, 1.044 | 1.008 |
| Tensile2d (compiled path) | displacement | 1.041 | 1.053, 1.030 | 1.041 |
| AirfRANS (compiled path) | pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity | 0.659 / 0.681 / 0.709 | 0.695, 0.623 / 0.691, 0.670 / 0.728, 0.690 | 0.683 |
| lug (compiled path; noisy, no verdict) | von Mises | 1.104 | 1.053, 1.155 | – |

Native relative L2, seed means of seeds 42 and 43; q is one new seed ÷ the
A2 seed mean. "Compiled path" marks the datasets where ISLA's per-block
compile hit pytorch#195845 in training and scoring, on both sides
(@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect). Tables: scratch/isla-ref090-2026-10-20/r090_final_tables.md.

**Verdict: confirmed.** The pooled G over the 13 fields is 0.891. No
low-noise field reaches 1.10 on both seeds: the largest q is 1.053, on
Tensile2d displacement. No dataset has G_d above 1.05, so none is listed for
Peter. The largest is Tensile2d at 1.041, whose registered false-alarm rate
at G_d > 1.03 is 0.045.

**The fields that move up.** Two fields read above 1.03 with both 0.9.0
seeds above both A2 seeds: Tensile2d displacement (1.041) and Tensile2d
stress (1.135, noisy, outside the verdict). The lug's von Mises reads 1.104,
but its seeds overlap A2's: 0.9.0's 0.001816 sits below A2's 0.001850.
Both seed-matched ratios are above one (1.134, 1.077).
HiLift's wall shear (R-HL090, @sec-nb-hilift-090-scored) is the reverse case:
1.022, under 1.03, with both seeds above both A2 seeds. Its gap is about
10 times A2's 0.2 percent seed gap.

**R3, posed ÷ native** (seeds 42, 43, every headline field):

- SHIFT-SUV, DrivAerML Surface and DeepJEB++: 1.0000 to 1.0001.
- Tensile2d: 1.0000 on stress, displacement and plastic strain. A2 read

- AirfRANS: 1.0015 to 1.0028 on pressure and velocity, 1.0000 on eddy
  viscosity.
- DrivAerML Volume: 1.0027 to 1.0040 on pressure and velocity, 0.9998 to

- lug: 1.141 / 1.107, from the medial ties. A2 read 4.14 / 2.87.

The area protocol is degenerate on DrivAerML Volume at 0.9.0. ISLA draws its
vehicle tokens by area inside the model, so area equals native by
construction. Its comparison with A2's area figures measures no robustness.

**Predictions.**

- P1 to P4 held: R1 per dataset on SHIFT-SUV, DrivAerML Surface and Volume

- P5 failed: Tensile2d displacement reads 1.041, against r ≤ 1.03 (r ≤

- P6 to P8 held: AirfRANS G is 0.683, the lug's 1.104 is inside

- P9 and P10 held: the surface tasks are within 1 ± 0.002, and AirfRANS and
  Tensile2d are within 1 ± 0.005.
- P11 held at 1 ± 0.01 and failed at 1 ± 0.002 (Volume velocity, 1.0040).
- P12 held: 1.141 / 1.107 on the lug.
- P13: the AirfRANS part failed. ISLA-DTT ÷ ISLA on the r090 rows reads

- P14 failed for the REF-090 lanes: the two lug ISLA-DTT lanes were

**Beside the rules.**

- With eager re-scores of both sides on the three affected datasets

  to 0.678, and the lug to 1.099. No verdict, flag or band changes.
- Comparability: the scored points and targets are identical, per case, for

- Against the baselines (baseline ÷ ISLA 0.9.0): DeepJEB++ GeoTransolver

- The lug ISLA-DTT arm is incomplete as registered. It was cancelled

**Standings (R2).** Final now: SHIFT-SUV, DrivAerML Surface and Volume, and
DeepJEB++ take their 0.9.0 rows. HiLift took its 0.9.0 rows under R-HL090.
Pending the training-path control: AirfRANS, Tensile2d and the lug. There,

under (b), and the supervisor's choice under (c). For Tensile2d, §13 is a

That is what the control tests.
