## 2026-10-21 — Capacity audit, phases 1 and 1b: trained on one case with fresh point draws, ISLA fits the field to within 1.2-1.7 times the best baseline on DrivAerML Surface and HiLift 18°, and on AirfRANS velocity and eddy viscosity, but is 2.6-2.7 times GeoTransolver on AirfRANS pressure, whose excess sits 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the wall {#sec-nb-cap-audit-p1}

**Question.** Peter asked whether ISLA can overfit a single sample. If it can, the architecture can represent that
sample's variation. If it cannot, the residuals show where capacity is missing. Each arm trains on one case, over and
over, until its error stops falling. ISLA 0.9.0 (width 512, 12 layers, 512 slices) runs against GeoTransolver 256 and
Transolver 512 x 16 at their standing configurations (on AeroZoo the Transolver arm runs its own config's width, 9.0 M
parameters), on the same case, points and budget. An ISLA floor far above the
best baseline's, and not limited by the training budget, is a deficit of ISLA's architecture (PREREG section 7). A floor shared by all three is a limit of the optimizer or the
precision. Pre-registration: scratch/isla-cap-audit-2026-10-20/PREREG.md (phase 1 approved 2026-10-20 10:30 EDT;
phase 1b, section 13, before any of its numbers; the section 14 amendment before the readout, with a disclosure).

**Instruments.** The cases are fixed by a rule set before any run: per dataset, the case at the lower median of
ISLA's per-case error, plus the named post-stall HiLift case and its low-angle control.

| Key | Case | ISLA's cross-case error on it |
|---|---|---|
| drs / drv | DrivAerML run_171, surface / volume | 0.040 / 0.040 |
| hl18 / hl6 | HiLift LHC002 at 18° / 6° | 0.137 (0.9.0) / 0.024 |
| af | AirfRANS case 76.343_0.584_… | 0.015 |
| lug | lug_1581 | 0.0015 |
| t2d | Tensile2d sample_000071 (yields) | 0.0080 |
| az | AeroZoo case …3751 (random) | - |

The case's own measures normalize the loss: each field's squared error over the case's sum of squared standardized
targets, with the fields weighted equally. Training is float32 with TF32 off, the recipe's Muon + AdamW at each arm's
reference rate, cosine decay to 0 over 20,000 steps, and no regularization. Every ISLA run is eager: compile_blocks false
throughout, so the compiled-path defect (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect) does not reach these numbers. Checks: a
40,000-step run on the lug, Tensile2d and AirfRANS, and bf16 on drs. A floor F is the median of the last five logged
relative L2 values, steps 19,600-20,000.
- **Phase 1** trains on one fixed draw of the case: the scorer's 200,000 cells (AirfRANS 100,000 points; the whole
  lug and Tensile2d mesh). ISLA's boundary tokens stay fixed (eval mode). The held-out set is the dataset's next draw
  of the same case; on the lug and Tensile2d, a seeded fifth of the nodes is held out of the loss.
- **Phase 1b** trains drs, hl18 and af on a fresh datapipe draw at every step. ISLA runs in train mode, so its tokens
  are redrawn too. ISLA-DTT is added on AirfRANS. The scores are on phase 1's two fixed draws, so a model succeeds only
  by representing the field.

LHR jobs: 302616 and 302617 (60 runs, planned at about 333 GPU-h; about 314 GPU-h of training steps) and 303992 (20 runs,
planned at about 126 GPU-h; about 124).

**What we saw: phase 1, fixed point-set fitting.** Every arm except the AeroZoo baselines fits its fixed draw closely:
relative L2 from 3e-5 to 0.013 (GeoTransolver and Transolver on AeroZoo: 0.085 to 4.3).
ISLA's floors are:

| Case and field | ISLA floor |
|---|---|
| drs pressure | 0.0019 / 0.0020 |
| hl18 pressure | 0.0022 / 0.0020 |
| hl6 pressure | 0.0016 / 0.0017 |
| af pressure | 0.0009 / 0.0008 |
| drv pressure | 0.0007 / 0.0007 |
| lug von Mises | 2.0e-4 / 1.8e-4 |
| t2d stress | 0.0013 / 0.0012 |

Against the better baseline, usually Transolver, ISLA is 2.2-24 times higher on 15 of 18 headline fields: drs, hl18 and
hl6 2.2-11; af 2.4-4.9; the lug 6; t2d stress and q 4.6-6.4; drv 11-24. That is a deficit by the registered rule (section 7),
but the same rule labels the AirfRANS (all three fields), lug and Tensile2d q deficits budget-limited, since ISLA's
40,000-step floor is at most F / 1.5, so they are not called architecture floors. The DrivAerML Volume pressure and
eddy-viscosity deficits are flagged possibly budget-limited (S2 above 15,000). ISLA is level on Tensile2d displacement. It
leads on AeroZoo by 17-330 times: the baselines, which get no per-case scale, do not learn this slow case's magnitude in the
budget, so the registered label is a scale-handling advantage (PREREG section 10), not capacity.

These floors measure how well a model fits a fixed point set, not how well it represents the field. On
DrivAerML, HiLift and AirfRANS, every arm's held-out error is 9 to 15,000 times its training floor (median 40, 81 pairs;
ISLA's DrivAerML Volume values excluded). On AeroZoo, also a separate-draw case, ISLA's is 3.3 to 38 times and the
baselines', which fit nothing, about 1. On drs pressure, for
example, ISLA's held-out error is 0.39, GeoTransolver's 0.14 and Transolver's 0.13. Doubling the budget lowers every
arm's floor on AirfRANS, the lug and Tensile2d (ISLA's AirfRANS pressure by 3.2 times), but ISLA's ratios stay at 2.7
or more. bf16 raises every arm's drs pressure floor more than 2 times: ISLA's by 2.8, the baselines' by 4.4-5.5.

**What we saw: phase 1b, with fresh draws.** Held-out floors, seeds 42 / 43:

| Case and field | ISLA | ISLA-DTT | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA ÷ best baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| drs pressure | 0.0166 / 0.0174 | - | 0.0149 / 0.0150 | 0.0119 / 0.0118 | 1.40 / 1.48 |
| drs wall shear | 0.0353 / 0.0366 | - | 0.0293 / 0.0293 | 0.0229 / 0.0228 | 1.54 / 1.61 |
| hl18 pressure | 0.0082 / 0.0076 | - | 0.0055 / 0.0055 | 0.0049 / 0.0048 | 1.69 / 1.60 |
| hl18 wall shear | 0.0409 / 0.0408 | - | 0.0345 / 0.0349 | 0.0332 / 0.0323 | 1.23 / 1.26 |
| af pressure | 0.00165 / 0.00168 | 0.00148 / 0.00219 | 0.00061 / 0.00064 | 0.00097 / 0.00077 | **2.70 / 2.61** |
| af velocity | 0.00112 / 0.00119 | 0.00125 / 0.00137 | 0.00072 / 0.00086 | 0.00088 / 0.00087 | 1.55 / 1.39 |
| af eddy viscosity | 0.00165 / 0.00157 | 0.00123 / 0.00121 | 0.00104 / 0.00121 | 0.00129 / 0.00115 | 1.57 / 1.36 |

- With a fresh draw every step, the held-out error (F_ho) and the training-draw error (F_tr) nearly agree: G = F_ho ÷ F_tr
  is 0.91-2.19, and at most 1.5 on 42 of 48 pairs, against a phase-1 median of 36 on the same runs and fields.
  Every arm's held-out error falls 3-90 times below its phase-1 value.
- Only AirfRANS pressure is representation-limited, meaning at least 2 times the best arm on both seeds: ISLA 2.70 /
  2.61 and ISLA-DTT 2.43 / 3.40 against GeoTransolver. Every other arm, case and field is under 2 times.
- **The single-case field floors sit far below ISLA's cross-case test errors on the same cases:** drs pressure 0.017
  against 0.040, hl18 pressure 0.008 against 0.137, af pressure 0.0017 against 0.015. (The cross-case errors are seed means: drs from ISLA 0.9.0, hl18 from ISLA 0.9.0 with
  seeds 0.081 and 0.193, af from ISLA A2, because no 0.9.0 per-case score of this case is in the record.) Fitting one case is not what
  limits ISLA's generalization on these datasets.

**Where the AirfRANS excess sits.** By wall distance in chords, on the phase-1b held-out points:
- **The band from 1e-3 to 0.1 chords** holds 39 percent of the points and **71 percent of ISLA's excess** squared error
  over GeoTransolver's. There ISLA's local error is 3.0-3.7 times GeoTransolver's.
- Below 1e-4 chords the ratio is 2.0, from 1e-4 to 1e-3 chords 2.3, from 0.1 to 1 chord 1.7, and beyond 1 chord 2.3.
- Velocity's excess sits in the same band, and inside 1e-4 chords ISLA's velocity error is the lowest of the four arms.
- ISLA's error is more concentrated than either baseline's: half of its squared error lies on 2.6 percent of the points,
  against 9.5 percent for GeoTransolver and 6.9 percent for Transolver (ISLA-DTT's is more concentrated still, 1.6 percent).
- The fixed-draw maps show the same band (81 percent of the excess between 1e-4 and 1e-2 chords).

On HiLift the excess is not regional. ISLA's error is a near-uniform multiple of Transolver's on the slat, main element,
flap and the rest (1.4-1.8 times, fresh draws). HiLift's suction peaks hold 12 percent (fixed draw) and 26-27 percent (fresh
draws) of ISLA's area-weighted pressure error on 2 percent of the area: 6-14 times concentrated, but under the
registered 40 percent bar.

**Predictions.**

- Phase 1 (section 8):
  - H1 (drs pressure floor at most 1e-3, 0.15) failed.
  - H1b (at most 1e-2, 0.65) held.
  - H2 (40 percent of the error at the suction peaks, 0.6) failed.
  - H3 (no deficit, 0.45) failed.
  - H4 (a deficit falls on AirfRANS or Tensile2d, 0.6) held as worded, but the deficits are not specific to those two.
  - H5 (in-case interpolation, 0.6) failed: 7 of 93 pairs.
  - H6 (2x budget lowers some arm's floor on each check case, 0.7), H7 (bf16 doubles ISLA's floor, 0.4), H8 (hl18
    within 1.5 times hl6, 0.6) and H9 (all finite, 0.85) held.
- Phase 1b (section 13):
  - P1 (the gap shrinks, 0.6), P3 (DTT's gap is smaller, 0.6), P4 (the training-draw floor rises, 0.85), P5 (G at
    most 1.5 on 80 percent of pairs, 0.7) and P6 (drs pressure Q < 1, 0.8; Q = fresh-draw held-out floor ÷ the same
    arm's phase-1 held-out floor) held.
  - P2 (ISLA within 2 times everywhere, 0.6) failed, on AirfRANS pressure.
  - P7 (Transolver moves little, 0.5) failed: fresh draws also remove most of Transolver's held-out error (Q 0.09-0.34).

**Beside the rules.**

- **An instrument defect, found in phase 2's DrivAerML Volume control (PREREG 15.8).** On volume tasks the held-out set
  joined the next draw's points to the training draw's boundary. On DrivAerML Volume the datapipe centers each draw
  on its own mean (CenterMesh), so those held-out points sat 1.16 mm off the wall they were scored against, 1.4 times
  the median wall distance. ISLA, which computes its wall geometry from the boundary, read shifted geometry there.
  - ISLA's phase-1 held-out values on DrivAerML Volume are invalid, and are left out of the gap statistics above.
  - Its AeroZoo held-out values are valid. AeroZoo runs no CenterMesh, and its two draws read identical boundaries
    in raw coordinates. There ISLA's held-out error is 3.3-4.1 times its training floor on velocity and 33-38 times on
    pressure.
  - The registered floors, which are training-point floors, are unaffected.
  - AirfRANS (no centering), the surface tasks (whole next draw) and the lug and Tensile2d (held-out nodes of the
    same forward pass) are unaffected.
- An interim note had explained Transolver's better interpolation by its not reading point-set context. That
  explanation is withdrawn: its physics-attention slices pool all N points too.
- The observation itself holds only in part:
  - Transolver has the lowest held-out error on drs and drv.
  - It splits with GeoTransolver on hl18 and AirfRANS.
  - ISLA has the lowest on the lug and on Tensile2d q.

**What it means.** The plain answer to Peter's question:
- With fresh draws, ISLA fits one case to within 1.2-1.7 times the best baseline on the three fresh-draw cases
  (DrivAerML Surface, HiLift 18° and AirfRANS), except AirfRANS pressure. There it is 2.6-2.7 times GeoTransolver, and
  the excess sits 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the airfoil.
- Its single-case floors are 2 to 17 times below its cross-case errors. So on the DrivAerML Surface car and the
  post-stall HiLift case, the error budget lies in generalization across cases, not in representing one case.
- On a fixed point set, ISLA memorizes less tightly than the better baseline on 15 of 18 headline fields (2-24 times). It
  is level on Tensile2d displacement and 17-330 times tighter on AeroZoo, where the baselines fit nothing. Every arm's
  fixed-set floor is memorization, not field fitting.

**Next.** Phase 2 (PREREG section 15) asks whether width (256 / 512 / 1024), depth (6 / 12 / 24) or slices
(128 / 512 / 2048) close the AirfRANS pressure gap, with fresh seeds, two seeds on each top rung and a 40,000-step
check on each. It also runs the DrivAerML Volume fresh-draw control with the corrected held-out set. The runs paused
for the LHR maintenance of 2026-10-21. The ladder resumed at 20:50 EDT that day and the DrivAerML Volume control at 21:02
EDT, after the 15.8 check passed.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by the reviewer on 2026-10-22 (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/SECOND_READ_2026-10-22.md).*

**Later (2026-10-23).** The DrivAerML Volume datapipe divides every coordinate by the case's reference length, 5 m, so the lengths CAP-AUDIT derived from it are in units of 5 m: the 15.8 offset given above as 1.16 mm is 5.8 mm, and its ratio to the median wall distance, 1.4, is unchanged (scratch/isla-cap-audit-2026-10-20/RESULTS.md, erratum).

## 2026-10-23 — Capacity audit, phase 2: neither width, depth or slices nor twice the steps bring ISLA's single-case AirfRANS pressure to the baselines' (1.6-2.5 times GeoTransolver at equal budget, the excess fixed 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the wall); on DrivAerML Volume, fresh draws leave ISLA 2.2 times behind on velocity and eddy viscosity, the latter in the far field {#sec-nb-cap-audit-p2}

**Question.** Phase 1b (@sec-nb-cap-audit-p1) found one field where ISLA cannot fit a single case as well as the
baselines when the points are redrawn every step: AirfRANS pressure, at 2.70 / 2.61 times GeoTransolver. Phase 2
asks whether more parameters close that gap, and whether DrivAerML Volume, phase 1's largest fixed-draw deficit, has a
field-fitting deficit at all. Pre-registration: scratch/isla-cap-audit-2026-10-20/PREREG.md.
- Section 15, approved 2026-10-21 with the conditions of 15.7.
- Amendments, each before the numbers it reads: 15.8 (a held-out instrument fix), 15.9 (a 40k control), 15.10 (a drv
  down-rung ladder) and 15.11 (a path and seed check).
- The case was selected by the rule the supervisor set after a reviewer's audit (section 14), with a disclosure of the
  values seen before it.

**Instruments.** Phase 1b's harness throughout: a fresh datapipe draw every step, ISLA in train mode, float32 with
TF32 off, Muon + AdamW, cosine decay to 0 over 20,000 steps, and scoring on phase 1's two fixed draws.
- **The ladder** varies ISLA 0.9.0 on the AirfRANS case one axis at a time from the reference (width 512, 12 layers,
  512 slices):
  - width 256 / 1024, with the program's rate rule lr = 1e-3 x 192 / width;
  - depth 6 / 24;
  - slices 128 / 2048.
  - Seeds are fresh (44, and 45 on the reference and the top rungs). Each top rung also gets a 40,000-step check.
  - The ladder trains through the per-block compiled path with the fix (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect). On every
    final model, compiled and eager predictions agree to 0.6-2.5e-6 on held-out pressure.
- **The DrivAerML Volume control (Part B)** is phase 1b on run_171 for all three arms, eager, seeds 42 and 43.
- **Rules:**
  - for each axis, b = the slope of log F against log(axis value);
  - "helps": b <= -0.3, the top rung at least 1.2 times better than the reference, and the seeds separated;
  - "plateau": under 1.07 times per doubling;
  - "weak gain": any other improvement;
  - "budget-limited": the 40k floor at most the 20k floor ÷ 1.5.

**What we saw: the ladder** (AirfRANS pressure, held-out floor; seeds 44 / 45 as a geometric mean on the reference
and the top rungs):

| Axis | Low | Reference | Top | b | Label | Top at 40k (÷ 20k) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width 256 / 512 / 1024 | 0.00209 | 0.00198 | 0.00193 | -0.06 | plateau | 0.00080 (0.48) |
| Depth 6 / 12 / 24 | 0.00209 | 0.00198 | 0.00180 | -0.11 | weak gain | 0.00064 (0.33) |
| Slices 128 / 512 / 2048 | 0.00140 | 0.00198 | 0.00201 | +0.13 | plateau | 0.00071 (0.38) |

- No axis helps at 20k. Depth's weak gain rules out the registered "missing component" reading, so the registered
  reading is mixed. Velocity plateaus on every axis.
- Every top rung is budget-limited. The 40k control (15.9) put the reference itself at 40k: 0.00096 and 0.00062 on its
  two seeds, a fall to 0.49 and 0.31 of its 20k floor. Read against the seed mean, budget explains most of the top
  rungs' fall. Only d24 falls clearly more than the reference (1.20 times the seed-mean factor).
- **At equal budget the gap stays.** At 40k GeoTransolver reaches 0.00039 and Transolver 0.00042 (one seed each).
  Every ISLA arm is 1.59-2.47 times GeoTransolver. Against GeoTransolver's same seed at 20k (0.00061), the same ISLA
  arms are 2.8-3.3 times, so twice the steps narrows the gap, since ISLA gains more from steps than GeoTransolver
  (0.31-0.49 against 0.64), but it does not close it.
- **The excess does not move.** On every rung, ISLA's local pressure error in the band 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the
  wall is 0.0024-0.0031, against GeoTransolver's 0.0005-0.0007. The exception is s128, at 0.0017-0.0018. That band
  holds 39 percent of the points and about 70 percent of ISLA's excess.
- **Run-to-run spread is wide on this case.** The path and seed check (15.11) trained the reference eager and compiled
  at the same seeds.
  - At seeds 44 and 45 the two paths agree to 2 percent (P = -0.018). Training through the compiled path costs
    nothing.
  - At seed 42 they sit 15 percent apart (0.00139 compiled, 0.00165 eager).
  - Over seven 20k runs the reference ranges from 0.00139 to 0.00199, 1.43 times, and its two 40k seeds are 1.56 times
    apart. One-seed rungs cannot resolve differences that small: s128's two seeds (gm 0.00157, 1.27 times better than
    the reference) fall inside the spread.

**What we saw: DrivAerML Volume with fresh draws** (Part B; held-out floors, seeds 42 / 43):

| Field | ISLA | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA ÷ best |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pressure | 0.0101 / 0.0115 | 0.0065 / 0.0065 | 0.0059 / 0.0058 | 1.72 / 1.99 |
| Velocity | 0.0192 / 0.0200 | 0.0101 / 0.0097 | 0.0088 / 0.0086 | 2.18 / 2.32 |
| Eddy viscosity | 0.0239 / 0.0219 | 0.0109 / 0.0106 | 0.0098 / 0.0100 | 2.44 / 2.20 |

- With fresh draws GeoTransolver's and Transolver's held-out errors fall 18-83 times below phase 1's (ISLA's phase-1 drv held-out values are invalid, 15.8). So phase 1's drv gap of 11-24 times
  was point-set memorization.
- What remains is a field-fitting deficit of about 2.2 times on velocity and eddy viscosity (both seeds), and none on
  pressure. The fixed epoch-0 draw gives the same verdicts.
- **Velocity's deficit is uniform:** ISLA's local error is 1.9-2.8 times Transolver's in every wall-distance decade.
- **Eddy viscosity's is regional** (lengths in metres; the datapipe's are in units of the case's reference length,
  5 m, so its band [1, inf) is beyond 5 m; RESULTS.md, erratum): the 0.7 percent of points more than 5 m from the
  car hold 49-66 percent of ISLA's
  error and 61-72 percent of its excess. There ISLA's local error is 0.035-0.044, against Transolver's 0.010. On
  DrivAerML ISLA reads only the vehicle surface and the freestream direction, no inlet, outlet or domain walls.
- **Depth is the capacity axis on drv (15.10, seed 44).** Shrinking the model one axis at a time:
  - halving depth to 6 layers raises velocity, eddy-viscosity and pressure floors by 1.59, 1.36 and 1.61 times;
  - halving width raises them by 1.03-1.12 times (velocity just at the bar);
  - quartering the slices changes nothing.
  - The reference's three seeds span 1.04-1.15 times. A 24-layer rung, the direction that might help, does not fit on
    one GB300 without block-level activation checkpointing.
  - No rung moves the far-field eddy viscosity (local error 0.029-0.042 beyond 5 m).
- **Three probes of the far-field miss** (descriptive, no training):
  - **Height explains it, the inlet does not.** On run_171 and ten validation cases, height above the floor explains
    31-46 percent of the far-field eddy-viscosity variance (cross-validated R^2). The streamwise distance from the
    inlet explains 6-10 percent, and the distance to the car 3-6 percent. The files carry the floor strip, the slip
    walls, the inlet and the outlet as meshes; ISLA reads only the vehicle.
  - **The distance channels do not saturate.** ISLA's query embedding changes 2.8-3.3 per unit log wall distance
    within 5 m (2.8-3.0 within 0.5 m) and 5-10 beyond it.
  - **Far points have slice mass.** From block 4 on, far points hold most of the mass of 3-31 slices per block, and their mean
    mass per slice is 1.5-9 times their share of the queries, except in seed 43's last block (1 slice, 0.5 times; probe_bc_cap_drv_isla_rd_s43.json,
    a block the record's ranges leave out).
  - So the miss points to an input ISLA lacks, the ground and the domain walls, rather than to saturated features or
    starved slices.

**Beside the rules.**

- **An instrument defect, found and fixed before any registered floor (15.8).** The held-out set joined the next
  draw's points to the training draw's boundary. On DrivAerML Volume the datapipe centers each draw on its own mean, so
  the held-out points sat 5.8 mm off the wall, 1.4 times their median wall distance. ISLA, which computes its wall
  geometry from the boundary, then scored 0.39 on pressure; on a correct set it scores 0.022.
  - Part B uses the corrected set from its resume.
  - ISLA's phase-1 drv held-out values are invalid.
  - AeroZoo, which runs no centering, was checked and is unaffected.
- ISLA on DrivAerML does not resume bit-for-bit: its losses depart from the first segment within 100 steps of a
  checkpoint, with or without the fix. ISLA on AeroZoo and HiLift and phase 1b's runs resume exactly.

**What it means.** The plain answer to Peter's question:
- ISLA has the capacity to fit one sample. On a fixed point set its training-point floors are 1.8e-4 to 0.013 on every
  case (phase 1).
- With fresh draws it fits every field tested to within 1.2-1.7 times the best baseline on DrivAerML Surface, HiLift
  and two of AirfRANS's three fields.
- Where it trails, on AirfRANS pressure more parameters do not close the gap at 20k, and twice the steps narrows it without closing it; on DrivAerML Volume only smaller models were trained.
  - On AirfRANS pressure, the excess sits in and just outside the boundary layer on every rung. That points to changing
    the component that represents near-wall variation (the slice routing and its resolution there are the first
    suspects, given s128's lead), not to adding width, depth or slices.
  - On DrivAerML Volume, velocity trails uniformly by about 2 times, and depth is the axis it is sensitive to (halving it
    costs 1.4-1.6 times). Eddy viscosity trails in the far field. Its level there follows the height above the floor,
    a boundary ISLA is not given. The evidence points to a new input, the floor and walls as boundary meshes by name,
    not to more parameters.

**Next.** The supervisor's decisions of 2026-10-23:
- **SLICES-AF:** a full-data AirfRANS test of 128 slices against the standing's 512, about 180 GPU-h, read about
  2026-10-25. It replaces the single-case slice test: the single-case floor is 9 times below ISLA's error across the AirfRANS
  test cases (0.0017 against 0.015, @sec-nb-cap-audit-p1) and its run-to-run spread is 1.43 times, while full-data scores resolve a 20 percent effect on two seeds
  (HANDOFF.md, decision 1).
- **FLOOR-DRV:** a single-case DrivAerML Volume probe with all four domain meshes the case files store, the floor
  strip, the slip walls, the inlet and the outlet, as named boundary meshes: the domain's whole boundary, as on
  AeroZoo. Its smoke measured ISLA 0.9.0's step 1.58 times longer with them (5.27 against 3.33 s), so the run costs
  about 120 GPU-h, four single-case runs on one 4-GPU node for about 30 h. Submitted 2026-10-23, read about 2026-10-24
  evening (scratch/isla-floor-drv-2026-10-23/PREREG.md, section 8). It is a diagnostic: adopting that input would
  change the task's input contract and needs Peter's word.
- The deeper drv rung (24 layers, with block-level activation checkpointing) is deferred until FLOOR-DRV reads.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-23 (scratch/isla-book-cap-2026-10-23/SECOND_READ_CAP_P2.md).*

## 2026-10-21 — Training path on Tensile2d: the registered reading is that the fixed compiled path trains differently from eager, but on weak evidence, and the eager-trained rows become the standing {#sec-nb-ref090-t2d-control}

**Question** (PREREG §13, written 2026-10-21 after the fix-trained Tensile2d result was seen; a deviation for
Tensile2d, fixed before any eager-trained result existed). ISLA's per-block compile hit pytorch#195845
(@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect). Its fix turns Inductor's mix-order reduction off. Models trained on the
fixed path differ from those trained under the bug, by field. On four seeds each, ISLA 0.9.0's displacement is
1.099× and its stress 1.075× the bug-trained value (bug-trained seeds 44/45 are ATTRIB-090's att_t2dz_base rows),
while its plastic strain is 0.778×. ISLA A2's displacement is 1.216× and its plastic strain 0.525×. Two readings were possible: (a) the bug's
perturbation changed training, and the fixed path trains the model's eager function; or (b) the fixed
path itself trains differently from eager. The control trains with eager blocks: 0.9.0 on seeds 42-45
and A2 on seeds 42/43. Every row was scored fully eager in float32 on Tensile2d's 100 validation cases.

| Model | Field | Eager-trained | Eager ÷ fix-trained (\|d\| / 2SE) | Eager ÷ bug-trained (\|d\| / 2SE) | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A2 | displacement | 0.00707 (0.00760, 0.00655) | 0.853 (1.06) | 1.037 (0.24) | (b) |
| A2 | stress | 0.00815 | 0.874 (1.53) | 1.044 (0.21) | (b) |
| A2 | plastic strain | 0.309 | 1.446 (0.42) | 0.760 (0.32) | (c) |
| 0.9.0 | displacement | 0.00849 (0.00783, 0.00629, 0.00891, 0.01092) | 1.077 (0.26) | 1.183 (0.72) | (c) |
| 0.9.0 | stress | 0.01113 | 1.130 (0.34) | 1.215 (0.59) | (c) |
| 0.9.0 | plastic strain | 0.273 | 1.362 (0.92) | 1.060 (0.15) | (c) |

Native relative L2, seed means; SE from each set's σ(log) over its seeds. "Matches" means
|d| ≤ 2 SE. Tables: scratch/isla-ref090-2026-10-20/t2d_control.md.

**Verdict: (b), as registered, on weak evidence.** The overall reading follows displacement, and the
pre-registered weighing lets A2 decide when the two models disagree. They do: A2 reads (b) on
displacement and stress. ISLA 0.9.0 reads (c) on every field. Its displacement and stress point estimates lean toward (a)
(eager ÷ fix-trained 1.077 and 1.130, against eager ÷ bug-trained 1.183 and 1.215), and its plastic strain leans toward
(b) (1.362 against 1.060).
A2's (b) rests on two seeds. Its eager seeds lie below both fix-trained seeds, at a margin of only
1.06 × 2 SE. Under the registered consequence, the Tensile2d standing becomes the eager-trained rows,
and AirfRANS and the lug are retrained eager (PREREG §14).

**The mechanism check finds nothing behind (b).** The registered lockstep check (job 317142) was inconclusive: eager
training is bitwise deterministic, so its eager-repeat floor is zero, and both the fixed path and the bug path leave eager
by bf16 roundoff (300-step parameter distance 0.94 and 1.13 of eager's displacement). It was then repeated against eager
float32 gradients (jobs 317294 and 323041). One-step training gradients were compared against
eager float32 gradients, on 8 batches at three checkpoints and one fix-trained checkpoint:

- In float32, the fixed path's gradient equals eager's: medians 4e-6 to 3e-5 for both models, and
  2.7e-4 on the A2 fix-trained checkpoint. The bug's gradient is off by 7 to 106 percent.
- In bfloat16, as the lanes train, eager's own gradient sits 0.12 (epoch 51) to 1.0-1.4 (epochs 251-500)
  from the float32 one. The fixed path (0.14-1.44) and the bug path (0.13-1.58) sit at about the same distance.
- Late in training, the per-step bf16 gradient is dominated by roundoff for every path. The bug's
  per-step error is inside that noise, so any effect it had on training came from its bias summed over
  many steps.
- A2's fix used Inductor's environment switch. It reaches only the compiled blocks, since every lane
  builds its optimizer uncompiled (`compile=false`).

This analysis sits beside the verdict and does not change it.

**Beside the rules.**

- 0.9.0 trains far less reproducibly on Tensile2d without the bug: σ(log) of displacement is 0.23
  eager, 0.16 fix-trained and 0.025 bug-trained. The eager seed 45 spiked at epoch 200 (in-training
  validation displacement 0.0188, from its best of 0.01012 at epoch 180) and never recovered, ending at 0.01196 after 240
  epochs on a plateau near 0.012. The bug's case-dependent extra term in the routing softmax, the
  padded rows of the last token tile, which reach about 40 percent of cases, may have acted like a
  stabilizing sink. That is a hypothesis. On the lug the opposite held: the fix-trained seeds lie 1.2 percent apart
  (0.001463, 0.001445), the bug-trained seeds 12 percent apart (0.001780, 0.002006). An explicit null term in the routing softmax would test it, as
  a later design experiment.
- R1 on Tensile2d under one function (eager-trained both sides, eager-scored): 0.9.0 ÷ A2 displacement is
  1.200 on all four 0.9.0 seeds and 0.998 on seeds 42/43; stress 1.366 and 1.079; plastic strain 0.885
  and 1.069. The registered R1 (0.891 pooled, @sec-nb-ref090-r1) stands; it read the original rows.
- The Tensile2d standing moves against ISLA on displacement and stress, and toward it on plastic strain: GeoTransolver
  256 ÷ ISLA 0.9.0 (eager-trained) displacement 0.473 (was 0.584 against A2), stress 0.478 (0.682), plastic strain 1.684
  (1.111); Transolver 512 × 16 0.649 (0.800), 0.619 (0.883), 0.843 (0.556). Posed ÷ native displacement is 0.9997 to
  1.0023 for the four ISLA 0.9.0 eager-trained rows (1.069 and 1.166 for the two ISLA A2 eager-trained rows).

**Next.** The eager-trained AirfRANS ISLA, AirfRANS ISLA-DTT and lug ISLA lanes run from 2026-10-21 22:44
EDT. On AirfRANS the A2 pair's two-seed gaps are 5 to 9 percent; on Tensile2d, ISLA 0.9.0's displacement σ(log) is
0.16 (fix-trained) to 0.23 (eager-trained). The AirfRANS training-path reading is pre-registered with the same rule
(PREREG §14), and it was then expected to be the cleaner test (but see Later).

**Later.** On 2026-10-22, AirfRANS ISLA 0.9.0 retrained on the fixed path matched its bug-trained original (fix-trained ÷ bug-trained pressure 1.024, velocity 0.985, eddy viscosity 0.998, seed means, both scored eager), so the AirfRANS read cannot tell (a) from (b). For the lug ISLA 0.9.0 the fixed path trained a better model (0.768 of the bug-trained von Mises, both seeds below both bug-trained seeds). The eager-trained lug read is therefore registered as the decisive test of the fixed path (PREREG §15, written before any eager-trained lug result).

## 2026-10-21 — QUERY-POP-090 and REMESH-090: at 0.9.0, interacting ISLA's prediction at a point depends strongly on the other queried points (4 chunks raise AirfRANS error 33-40 percent, a single point 85-118 times; ISLA-DTT stays at float32 roundoff), while re-meshing the same boundary leaves it unchanged (AirfRANS re-panelization d 3e-5, DrivAerML Volume 4x subdivision within 0.6 percent) {#sec-nb-probes090}

**Setting.** ISLA claims two invariances: its prediction at a point should not depend on which other points are
queried, and it should not depend on how the boundary is meshed. Neither had been measured at 0.9.0. Query
independence was last probed on A2-era AirfRANS (E3b, @sec-nb-anchor-verdict) and pre-A2 DrivAerML Volume (@sec-nb-query-pop). The area
protocol that stood for boundary robustness is degenerate at 0.9.0, because the model draws its own tokens. The
pre-registration (scratch/isla-probes090-2026-10-21/PREREG.md, approved 2026-10-20 23:59 EDT) set readouts, labels and
predictions before any number. Both probes are inference only, on the final checkpoints, fully eager in float32. While
the query probe was being ported it found the compiled-path defect (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect). So every AirfRANS row
below is labelled defect-trained: the eager function of weights trained under that defect. The registered re-read on the
fix-trained weights (the training-path measurement) repeats every label (Reading, below). The re-read on the eager-trained
weights behind the AirfRANS standing is pending (read in @sec-nb-probes090-eag).

**Instruments.** QUERY-POP-090 keeps a fixed scored set per case, a seeded random half of the native points. It changes
only the rest of the query population: the scored half alone; 4 chunks; 1,000 scored points queried in groups of 1,000,
100 or 10, and the first 100 of them one at a time (AeroZoo: 250 points in groups of 10 and 25 singly), each ratio read on
the points that were queried; 50 percent more points at the native law; as many far-field points (uniform in the bounding box, outside
the body); or as many wall-heavy points (resampled with probability proportional to 1/|sdf|). Readouts: the error ratio
r against the native population on the same points, and the prediction move d = RMS(Δpred) / RMS(target).
REMESH-090 scores the native points while it changes the boundary the model is given:
- AirfRANS: exact re-panelization (every segment split in 2 or 4, or front-loaded 3/1); in-model token budgets of 800
  to 200, with a redraw of the same budget as the noise floor; a decimated polyline (new geometry);
- DrivAerML Volume: token budgets of 100k and 400k; one level of subdivision (4x cells, exact geometry); two redraws at
  200k as the floor; the watertight STL in place of the CFD wall (new geometry).
Validity, read first: eager float32 against float64-eager references on AirfRANS (≤ 2.3e-4) and against the scorer on
DrivAerML Volume (≤ 1.9e-5). Every mode and variant changed the input on every case. LHR jobs 310635, 310636 and 310637
(about 17 GPU-h); AeroZoo 322430; the fix-trained re-read 325715, 326381, 330576 and 330583; post hoc 310919,
311989-311991, 312063 and 312116 (about 36 GPU-h for all of these).

**What we saw: query population** (error ratio, seed means, pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity; both seeds agree on
every label):

| Arm | half | 4 chunks | 1,000 points | 1 point | +50% same law | far-field | wall-heavy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AirfRANS ISLA 0.9.0 (defect-trained) | 1.11 / 1.12 / 1.14 | 1.33 / 1.36 / 1.40 | 4.7 / 5.0 / 5.7 | 85 / 91 / 118 | 0.95 / 0.95 / 0.95 | 136 / 62 / 133 | 20 / 30 / 22 |
| AirfRANS ISLA-DTT 0.9.0 (defect-trained) | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| AirfRANS GEO1 ISLA (defect-trained) | 1.14 / 1.09 / 1.15 | 1.44 / 1.30 / 1.40 | 5.6 / 4.6 / 5.4 | 237 / 74 / 87 | 0.93 / 0.96 / 0.95 | 30 / 30 / 50 | 52 / 21 / 59 |
| DrivAerML Volume ISLA 0.9.0 | 1.01 / 1.01 / 1.02 | 1.03 / 1.03 / 1.15 | 4.5 / 4.0 / 5.5 | 21 / 13 / 18 | 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 | 20 / 16 / 14 | 6.2 / 4.5 / 4.5 |
| AeroZoo `full` ISLA 0.9.0 (179 of 716 test cases) | 1.00 / 1.01 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 1.01 / 1.00 | 1.09 / 1.05 / 1.04 | 4.0 / 2.9 / 2.3 | 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 | 1.04 / 1.05 / 1.03 | 1.44 / 1.24 / 1.30 |

ISLA-DTT's largest |r − 1| over the ten modes is 4.3e-6, and its median d is below 1e-6. Labels as registered: on
AirfRANS, half and 4 chunks are "material" (above 1.10 on both seeds); far-field, wall-heavy and every small subset are
"severe" (above 2 on both seeds) on AirfRANS and DrivAerML Volume. On AeroZoo `full` only the single point is severe
(pressure 4.0); far-field is not (1.04), wall-heavy reaches 1.44, and 1,000 to 10 points stay below 2; on DrivAerML Volume, half, 4 chunks and the same-law addition are not material on
pressure or velocity. The A2 rung is incomplete as registered. Its validity gate failed because A2's signed distance has
an ill-posed sign at on-wall points, which float32 and float64 resolve differently.

**What we saw: re-meshing** (error ratio, seed means, pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity):

| Arm and variant | ratio | d (median) | label |
|---|---|---|---|
| AirfRANS ISLA, split x2 / x4 / front-loaded | 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 | 3e-5 | invariant |
| AirfRANS ISLA-DTT, split x2 / x4 / front-loaded (pressure) | 1.011 / 1.036 / 1.060 | 2-3e-3 | invariant / small / small |
| AirfRANS ISLA, 800 / 600 / 400 / 200 tokens (pressure) | 1.02 / 1.37 / 2.39 / 5.21 | 400: 0.018 | small / sensitive ×3 (400: within draw noise) |
| DrivAerML Volume, 100k / 400k tokens | 1.001 / 1.000 | 1-3e-3 | invariant (d 1.3-1.4x the redraw floor at 100k; 400k within draw noise in d, 0.87x) |
| DrivAerML Volume, 4x subdivision | 1.002 / 1.005 / 1.000 | 2-9e-3 | invariant (d 1.2-3.4x the redraw floor) |
| DrivAerML Volume, watertight STL | 2.95 / 1.84 / 1.48 | 0.06-0.12 | sensitive |

Beside the registered reading, labelled post hoc:
- **The STL rise is all near the wall.** Beyond 0.01 L the STL changes the error by at most 1.1 percent. Within 1e-3 L it
  raises it 2.4 to 5.2 times, and on the 1.6 percent of points inside the STL 11 to 119 times. The two surfaces coincide at
  0.01 L: no point of either is 0.01 L from the other (the largest separation is 7.8e-3 L, from the STL to the CFD wall;
  2.2e-3 L the other way). But they differ everywhere by a median 1.3e-5 L, the chord error of the
  coarser STL, which is ten times the softening of ISLA's log-distance channel. That offset moves the 5.5 percent of
  interior nodes that sit on the CFD wall off it (in a uniform sample of nodes). This fits the near-wall rise, but the link
  was not tested.
- **ISLA-DTT's refinement sensitivity is its tree read.** Rerun at a smaller opening angle, the pressure ratios of the
  three refinements fall from 1.011 / 1.036 / 1.060 (θ = 1, as trained) to 1.0006 / 1.003 / 1.0008 (θ = 0, the exact
  read). The weights were trained at θ = 1, so at θ = 0 the native error is 2.2 times its θ = 1 value on pressure (1.6
  times on velocity and 4.2 times on eddy viscosity; seed 42); pricing a small θ needs a model trained at it.

Against the registered predictions (PREREG §6, RESULTS.md §5): Q2, Q4, Q5 and R2 held; Q3 held for chunks and half, and
failed for the same-law addition (0.95); Q6 failed (AeroZoo far-field 1.04, no material mode); R1 failed (ISLA-DTT moves
under the x4 and front-loaded splits); R3 held for invariance and failed for draw noise (d 2.9-3.4 times the floor); R4
held for 400k and failed for 100k (invariant, not sensitive); R5 held for sensitive and failed for \|r − 1\| ≤ 0.05; Q1
held on AirfRANS, with AeroZoo pending; Q7 is incomplete. The §8 prediction (every label repeats on the fix-trained
weights) held.

**Reading.** At 0.9.0 the two invariances come apart. Re-meshing invariance holds for interacting ISLA under exact
re-meshing of the boundary: AirfRANS re-panelization (d 3e-5), and DrivAerML Volume 4x subdivision and 100k to 400k
tokens. In-model token budgets far below the boundary's own cell count are not invariant, though they keep the geometry
exact: 600 to 200 tokens raise AirfRANS pressure error 1.37 to 5.21 times. The slice reads are measure-weighted and the
gauge is exact (scratch/isla-probes090-2026-10-21/remesh/FACTS_CHECKED.md #1), and the invariance is now measured, not
assumed. Query independence does not hold for interacting ISLA. Beside the registration (Q7's comparison with A2 is
incomplete, because A2 failed validity), the dependence did not shrink under far-field companions. They raise AirfRANS
pressure error 136 times (seeds 91 and 181; 98 on the fix-trained weights), against 30 times for GEO1 ISLA and 26 to 63
times for A2-era interacting ISLA in E3b (@sec-nb-anchor-verdict; E3b read the compiled path). Under wall-heavy
companions and single points it shrank from GEO1 ISLA (pressure 52 to 20 and 237 to 85). The forms that matter to a user
are measured too. On AirfRANS, chunking a query raises the error by a third, and querying 1,000 points or fewer raises the
error 4.7 to 118 times (from 1,000 points to a single point). On DrivAerML Volume, chunking and halving are benign on
pressure and velocity (at most 3.4 percent; 4 chunks raise the eddy-viscosity error 15 percent, above 1.10 on both seeds
but outside the registered fields), but small queries are not. ISLA-DTT is query-independent to float32 roundoff, and
under exact refinement its pressure error moves 1 to 6 percent because of its θ = 1 tree read. Its error ratios fall to
within 0.3 percent at θ = 0, though not monotonically (at θ = 0.5 the x2 split reads 1.014, against 1.011 at θ = 1).
The prediction move d falls only from 2-4e-3 to 1-3e-3, and θ = 0 raises the native error (above). On AeroZoo `full` the interacting form's error is nearly indifferent to chunking, halving and far-field
companions (at most 6 percent). Its predictions still move (median d 0.10 on pressure with far-field companions), and
single points raise the error 1.4 to 4.4 times over its five fields (2.3 to 4.0 on pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity); its native errors there are large (pressure 0.30), which compresses the ratios.
On the fix-trained AirfRANS weights (the training-path measurement, PREREG §8) every label of both forms repeats:
interacting ISLA half 1.11, 4 chunks 1.33, far-field 98, exact re-panelization invariant (d 3e-5); ISLA-DTT at roundoff
in every mode and 1.0-7.0 percent under refinement. So the training-path defect did not create or hide these
properties. The eager-trained rows behind the AirfRANS standing are read when they finish training, about 2026-10-23 (read in @sec-nb-probes090-eag).
These numbers enter the cross-dataset table of PREREG_v2
§13(b) (scratch/isla-az-compliant-2026-10-19/PREREG_v2.md) beside the AeroZoo verdict
(scratch/isla-az-decide-2026-10-21/QUERYPOP090_FOR_12F.md); the AeroZoo ISLA-DTT probe follows when its checkpoints finish.

## 2026-10-22 — SUV-XFAM, zero-shot estate to fastback on SHIFT-SUV: registered summary mixed / no difference. On pressure the three architectures' penalties (fastback-test error ÷ estate-test error) are indistinguishable across ISLA 0.9.0, GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16: 2.557, 2.561 and 2.557 (registered: no difference; GeoTransolver's own seeds give 2.39 and 2.74), while ISLA 0.9.0's wall-shear penalty is smaller (1.78 against GeoTransolver 256's 1.93 and Transolver 512 × 16's 1.97), so its wall-shear error goes from 1.044 times Transolver's on estates to 0.941 times on fastbacks {#sec-nb-suv-xfam}

**Question.** Does a model trained on one SHIFT-SUV rear-end family predict the other? Every SHIFT-SUV checkpoint in
the book trains on the estate family only, and the fastback family had never been scored by a current one, so the
cross-family question was open (@sec-shift-suv-limits, @sec-limits-transfer). It is a generalization test on a surface task beside AeroZoo's volume test,
with a near shift: both families are parametric morphs of one SUV (same footprint, varying height) at the same 30 m/s
far field and the same single no-slip boundary, and only the class of the rear end changes. It tests neither a new
boundary role nor Reynolds extrapolation.

**Setting.** The six standing estate checkpoints, as trained (794 estates, 500 epochs, bf16): ISLA 0.9.0 (width 512,
512 slices; `r090_suv_isla_seed42/43`, code_r090 / recipe_r090), and the fair-drive GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver
512 × 16 (`clud_suv_{gt,t}_seed42/43`, code_v20 / recipe_v8). Each is scored with its own snapshot and its own saved
normalization; no fastback statistic reaches any arm. Native protocol, float32, 200k scored cells for every arm
(Transolver 512 × 16 trained at 100k cells and is scored at 200k, as in the standing estate scorer), final checkpoint, on
three splits: fastback test (99 cases, never used before; the lead), fastback val (99; the replicate), and estate test
(100; the in-family reference). The fastback data file is the reference `shift_suv_surface.yaml` with only its data root
changed. The scored cells and targets are identical per case across the three loaders (loader hashes, and reference
force coefficients agreeing to 4.2e-5 relative across all six checkpoints). Pre-registered
(scratch/isla-suv-xfam-2026-10-22/PREREG.md, approved 2026-10-22 10:20 EDT with floors of 3 percent on R2 and 5 percent
on the part-B trigger) before any fastback or estate-test score (the estate-val scores and the old 10k-cell
near-transfer numbers were already known). LHR jobs 333701 (loader check), 333702 and 333789 (scoring); 1.5 GPU-h.

**What we saw** (relative L2, seed means, pressure / wall shear; seeds 42 · 43 in RESULTS.md):

| arm | estate test | fastback test | penalty P = fastback ÷ estate, geometric mean of the two seeds' ratios | fastback val |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA 0.9.0 | 0.0437 / 0.0657 | 0.1118 / **0.1168** | 2.56 / **1.78** | 0.1109 / 0.1174 |
| GeoTransolver 256 | 0.0450 / 0.0656 | 0.1155 / 0.1267 | 2.56 / 1.93 | 0.1150 / 0.1276 |
| Transolver 512 × 16 | **0.0416** / **0.0629** | **0.1063** / 0.1241 | 2.56 / 1.97 | 0.1061 / 0.1247 |

| cell | R1: fastback test, baseline ÷ ISLA | R2: P_baseline ÷ P_ISLA (D / SE) | part-B cell |
|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver 256 pressure | 1.034, level | 1.002 (0.0), no difference | no |
| GeoTransolver 256 wall shear | 1.085, ISLA leads | 1.087 (3.0), ISLA transfers better (registered label) | yes |
| Transolver 512 × 16 pressure | 0.952, Transolver leads | 1.000 (0.0), no difference | no |
| Transolver 512 × 16 wall shear | 1.063, ISLA leads | 1.110 (11), ISLA transfers better (registered label) | yes |

**Verdict, as registered.** R1, on unseen fastbacks: ISLA leads both baselines on wall shear; Transolver leads ISLA on
pressure by 5 percent, as it does on estates; GeoTransolver is level with ISLA on pressure. R2: the pressure penalties
are the same for all three; ISLA's wall-shear penalty is smaller than both baselines'. Both wall-shear cells clear the
registered screen (D = 3.0 and 11.4 SE(D), and above ln 1.03), but each SE rests on one degree of freedom per arm, so
the 2-SE band is a rough screen and not a 95 percent test; the GeoTransolver cell sits at 3.0 SE. The registered summary
is "mixed / no difference", because it needs three of four cells to agree and only the two wall-shear cells do. The
part-B trigger fires on both wall-shear cells. Every cell repeats on fastback val. Of ten predictions seven held; the
three that failed had expected no difference in the R2 wall-shear cells (P3 against GeoTransolver, P4 against
Transolver) and a level R1 GeoTransolver wall-shear cell (P8). The caveat stands: P mixes the transfer gap with how hard
fastbacks are in themselves, and only the reverse direction (train on fastbacks, score on estates) separates them.

**Beside the rules** (post hoc, no verdict):
- The wall-shear advantage is on nearly every case: ISLA's seed-mean error is lower than GeoTransolver's on all 99
  fastback-test cases and lower than Transolver's on 96. The case-bootstrap 95 percent interval of the penalty ratio is
  1.070-1.105 against GeoTransolver and 1.093-1.126 against Transolver. These intervals hold the seeds fixed, so they
  show consistency from case to case, not seed noise. The advantage holds on every component, most on the y component,
  along the dataset's axes (penalty ISLA 1.64, GeoTransolver 1.83, Transolver 1.86).
- The wall-shear advantage is not an artifact of different in-family floors. ISLA 0.9.0's extra fastback error is
  smaller additively (fastback − estate: 0.051 against 0.061 / 0.061, 16-17 percent smaller) and in quadrature
  (√(E_f² − E_e²): 0.097 against 0.108 / 0.107, 10-11 percent smaller). On pressure ISLA's excess lies between the two
  baselines' under both measures (additive 0.068 against 0.071 / 0.065; quadrature 0.103 against 0.106 / 0.098).
- The registered pressure penalties agree to 0.2 percent across the three architectures (2.557, 2.561, 2.557). One
  hypothesis, untested because predictions were not saved: the extra pressure error sits where the rear ends differ
  (the sloped rear window), which an estate-trained model has not seen.
- Transfer amplifies GeoTransolver's seed spread: its two seeds differ by 0.1 percent on estate-test pressure and by
  15 percent on fastback-test pressure (seed 42 ÷ seed 43 = 0.1234 ÷ 0.1076 = 1.146). ISLA's seed gap is 3.6 percent on
  estate test and 3.2 percent on fastback test, with the order flipped (seed 42 higher on estates, seed 43 on
  fastbacks), and Transolver's under 1 percent.
- At old versions (10k cells, @sec-nb-window-readout-1 and @sec-nb-mega-synthesis) GeoTransolver's estate-to-fastback
  penalty was about 2.4, the exact-kernel predecessor's about 2.0-2.4 (0.21-0.23 on fastbacks against its own
  0.097-0.104 in family), and ISLA-v3c reached parity with GeoTransolver on absolute fastback error (0.117-0.131
  against 0.11-0.12; fastback val split, old metric). At the current configurations and 200k cells, all three arms sit
  at 2.56 on pressure.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by the reviewer on 2026-10-22 (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/second-read-2026-10-22/suvx.md).*

## 2026-10-23 — SUV-XFAM-B, stage 1: against models trained on fastbacks, ISLA 0.9.0's smaller wall-shear penalty is mostly a transfer advantage over Transolver (estate-trained error 1.78 times the in-family fastback error, against 1.93; Transolver ÷ ISLA 1.085 at 5.8 SE), fastbacks are not harder in themselves (H 0.97-1.02), and the reverse direction shows no difference at two seeds {#sec-nb-suv-xfam-b1}

**Question.** Part A (@sec-nb-suv-xfam) found that, trained on estates, ISLA loses less than the baselines on fastback
wall shear (penalty 1.78 against 1.93 and 1.97) and the same on pressure (2.56 for all three). The penalty divides the
fastback error by the *estate* error, so it mixes two things: how far an estate-trained model is from what a model can
do on fastbacks (the transfer gap) and how hard fastbacks are in themselves. Models trained on fastbacks measure the
second part and separate them.

**Setting.** ISLA 0.9.0 and the fair-drive Transolver (512 × 16, `fx.source = U_inf_dir`), seeds 42 and 43, trained on
the fastback train split (796 cases; validation on fastback val), 500 epochs. Each lane is its estate reference lane
(`r090_suv_isla_seed4x`, `clud_suv_t_seed4x`) with only the dataset file changed: the saved configs differ only in
`dataset` and `run_id`. A loader check showed that training read exactly the fastback manifest's train and val cases.
The recipe fits no normalization statistic on SHIFT-SUV (wall shear is divided by a declared constant, pressure is Cp
from each case's own far field), so no statistic of either family reaches any model. Every fastback-trained checkpoint is
scored on fastback test, estate test, fastback val and estate val: native, float32, 200,000 cells, final epoch, part A's
scorer. With E(x→y) the error of a model trained on family x and scored on family y (geometric seed means):
- the forward gap G = E(est→fb) ÷ E(fb→fb), on fastback test;
- the reverse gap R = E(fb→est) ÷ E(est→est), on estate test;
- the hardness H = E(fb→fb) ÷ E(est→est).

Part A's penalty is P = G × H. Each comparison is D = ln(X_Transolver ÷ X_ISLA), with an SE from the seed spreads of the
four runs it involves. A cell reads *better* or *worse* only past 2 SE and 3 percent. Pre-registered before any
fastback-trained run existed (scratch/isla-suv-xfam-2026-10-22/PREREG_B.md, approved by the supervisor 2026-10-22
15:00 UTC). LHR jobs
334400 (loader checks), 334401 (smoke), 334466-334469 and their chain links (training), 345738 and 347052 (scoring);
147.5 GPU-h.

**What we saw** (relative L2, pressure / wall shear, geometric seed means; seeds in RESULTS_B.md):

| | ISLA 0.9.0 | Transolver | Transolver ÷ ISLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| E(fb→fb), fastback test | 0.0425 / 0.0656 | **0.0405** / 0.0643 | 0.953 (Transolver leads) / 0.980 (level) |
| E(est→fb), fastback test (part A) | 0.1117 / **0.1168** | 0.1063 / 0.1241 | |
| E(fb→est), estate test | 0.1374 / 0.1298 | 0.1427 / 0.1285 | |
| E(est→est), estate test (part A) | 0.0437 / 0.0657 | 0.0416 / 0.0629 | |
| forward gap G | 2.63 / **1.78** | 2.63 / 1.93 | 0.999 (no difference) / **1.085, 5.8 SE (ISLA transfers better)** |
| reverse gap R | 3.14 / 1.98 | 3.43 / 2.04 | 1.091, 1.6 SE (no difference) / 1.034, 0.6 SE (no difference) |
| hardness H | 0.97 / 1.00 | 0.97 / 1.02 | 1.001 (no difference) / 1.023, 3.8 SE (no difference: under 3 percent) |

**Verdict, as registered.** On wall shear, ISLA **transfers better** than Transolver from estates to fastbacks. Its
estate-trained model is closer to what a fastback-trained ISLA reaches than Transolver's is to a fastback-trained
Transolver: 1.78 against 1.93 times, a ratio of 1.085 at 5.8 SE, and 1.098 at 8.7 SE on the fastback-val replicate. The
registered reading is "transfer advantage, estate → fastback only", because the reverse gap reads *no difference*.
Of part A's 11 percent wall-shear ratio, 78 percent is this transfer gap and 22 percent is hardness. On its own the
hardness part is 2.3 percent, at 3.8 SE but under the 3-percent floor. On pressure every comparison reads *no
difference*, and part A's pressure penalties were level, so the two models lose alike on fastback pressure. The
stage-2 trigger (GeoTransolver trained on fastbacks) fires; the supervisor approved stage 2 (PREREG_B section 9), and
it is running. Ten of eleven predictions held. The one that failed (Q4,
p = 0.45) had expected the reverse wall-shear gap to favor ISLA as well.

Validity: all scorings passed their checks, and the scored points and targets are identical across loaders (one
digest per split). The registered force-coefficient identity check failed on estate val, at 1.28e-4 against a 1e-4
bound. The failure sits on one near-zero roll moment (case 00888, CMR = -4.4e-6) and is the same for the standing
estate-trained Transolver. It passes on all four splits under amendment 2 (PREREG_B section 8), approved by the supervisor before results, which
scales the
denominator by the component's median (largest value 6.1e-7).

**Beside the rules** (no verdict):
- Fastbacks are not harder than estates in themselves: a model trained and tested on fastbacks does as well as one
  trained and tested on estates (H between 0.97 and 1.02 for both models and both fields). Part A's penalties are
  therefore almost all transfer gap.
- The reverse transfer costs more than the forward one, for both models and both fields: R exceeds G in every cell
  (pressure 3.1-3.4 against 2.6).
- The reverse direction is not resolved because of seed spread, not because the gaps agree. ISLA's reverse pressure
  gap is 9 percent smaller than Transolver's, but each model's two fastback-trained seeds differ by 7-9 percent on
  estates, against under 1 percent on fastbacks. Part A saw the same with GeoTransolver: out of family, the seed spread
  grows by an order of magnitude.
- In family, the fastback ordering repeats the estate one: Transolver leads on pressure by 5 percent, and on wall shear
  it is 2 percent ahead (level) on fastback test and 3 percent ahead on fastback val.

| forward gap G | 2.63 / **1.78** | 2.63 / 1.92 | 2.63 / 1.93 |

**Verdict, as registered.** On wall shear, ISLA **transfers better** than GeoTransolver from estates to fastbacks:

## 2026-10-23 — Peter's rulings on canonical ISLA: a close call on AeroZoo makes ISLA-DTT the default interior form; the geometry robustness bundle goes into ISLA once the tie experiment shows no accuracy cost, with its cost documented and a fused fast path built beside it; ISLA reads every stored piece of the PDE domain's boundary on every dataset {#sec-nb-canonical-rulings}

**Questions.** The supervisor asked Peter three questions in one form at about 17:00 EDT; Peter answered at 17:08 EDT.

1. *ISLA against ISLA-DTT.* "If AeroZoo reads a close call between interacting ISLA and ISLA-DTT, which should be
   ISLA's default interior form?" Peter chose "ISLA-DTT, on principle".
2. *The geometry robustness bundle.* "If the tie experiment shows no accuracy cost, does the geometry robustness bundle go
   into canonical ISLA at its measured cost?" Peter: "Adopt it, and then document the cost. Then, start a parallel thread
   where we try to make it faster with a fused kernel. Correctness is most important; correct + fast is even better. If
   the speedup experiment works, then add an optional fast path (like our other kernels, where we default iff triton is
   installed), and then remove the documented limitation / change it."
3. *The whole boundary.* "May ISLA read the domain's full boundary on DrivAerML Volume (the floor, slip walls, inlet and
   outlet the case files store), adopted if FLOOR-DRV shows it fixes the far-field miss?" Peter: "Yes! And in fact, not
   only CAN it read the whole boundary - it SHOULD read the whole boundary! As you say, this is a matter of PDE
   well-posedness and correctness. Seeing where the floor is through raw coordinates is a bug, not a feature. Even if
   there were an accuracy *cost* to reading the whole boundary (not that I expect it), I would recommend this. I don't
   care that they make each step 1.58x as long. Think about something like AeroZoo - there, reading the whole boundary
   is not a "choice", it's actually mandatory. WE should be doing that on all PDEs. The boundary conditions matter."

**What follows for the program** (the supervisor's application of the three answers):

- *The interior form.* AeroZoo's registered bands stand as written (scratch/isla-az-compliant-2026-10-19/PREREG_v2.md,
  section 12(f) with section 13; md5 ebd75524). With R = ISLA-DTT ÷ ISLA on seed means, on velocity and pressure over
  the six held-out splits: "ISLA-DTT clearly" is R ≤ 1.05 on both fields on every held-out split, "ISLA clearly" is an
  arithmetic mean of R of at least 1.10 on velocity or on pressure, and everything else is a close call. A close call
  makes ISLA-DTT the default interior form (Peter's answer), and so does "ISLA-DTT clearly" (the supervisor's reading).
  "ISLA clearly" keeps interacting ISLA by the registered rule; the cross-dataset table of section 13(b) still goes to
  Peter (the supervisor's application). Section 13(b) had kept interacting ISLA as the default
  in the first two bands until Peter answered an explicit question; his answer settles it for a close call, and the
  supervisor's reading for "ISLA-DTT clearly".
  Removing the interacting form stays a separate proposal to Peter (section 12(f) edit i, section 13(d)). The AeroZoo
  ISLA-DTT lanes that the rule reads are still training.
- *The geometry robustness bundle.* Branch psharpe/isla-geo-bundle (f13eb5ce0) is merged into canonical ISLA once the
  tie experiment (TIE-EXP) reads "adopt" by its registered decision rule: its flip test F passes (the flip residual at
  float32 roundoff) and its native-accuracy reading N is not "cost" on either dataset. N is Peter's condition; the
  supervisor keeps F, because without it the registered rule reads nothing else as a property of the tie rules. It has
  no result yet. The ledger and this notebook state the bundle's measured cost until it merges; the chapters
  state the adoption rule. On
  GB300 (scratch/isla-medial-tie-2026-10-22/DESIGN.md section q.4, LHR job 346068; REF-090 settings, bfloat16, eager,
  one GPU per version, medians after 5 warm-up steps), the training step is +7 / +29 / +17 / +49 percent on AirfRANS /
  the lug / AeroZoo / DrivAerML Volume. That is the mean of the head's three per-run medians over the mean of the base's
  two per-pass medians (1.067, 1.291, 1.174, 1.493). Over every head run against every base pass it is 1.03 to 1.12,
  1.22 to 1.40, 1.14 to 1.20 and 1.47 to 1.50 times (@sec-nb-geo-bundle). Until the merge, the cost stands in the

  psharpe/isla-geo-fast, scratch/isla-geo-fast-2026-10-23/) builds an optional fused fast path, chosen automatically
  when CUDA and Triton are present, with the exact path kept as the reference. If it succeeds, the documented cost
  changes.
- *The whole boundary.* Canonical ISLA reads every stored piece of the PDE domain's boundary, by name with its
  condition type, on every dataset. No accuracy or cost result reverses this. The recipe's ISLA configurations
  (`conf/model/isla_*.yaml`, `forward_kwargs.boundary_meshes`) read the body alone on DrivAerML Volume (`vehicle`),

  domain meshes (5.27 against 3.33 s; scratch/isla-floor-drv-2026-10-23/PREREG.md section 8), the factor Peter's
  answer names.

**For the book.** Chapter 20 gains a limit, *the whole boundary of the domain* (@sec-limits-whole-boundary), and an open

**Where the pieces come from** (SETUP-RESEARCH, scratch/isla-setup-research-2026-10-23/SETUP.md, every claim sourced).
- *DrivAerML.* The four domain meshes are not CFD output: physicsnemo-curator synthesized them (PR #58, commit 60ed919,

  and a translating floor (belt layout not stated). The side walls', roof's and outlet's conditions and the domain's extent

  version built with the curator's generators (recommended by the lane; SHIFT-SUV about 1 day plus 1-2 CPU-h, HiLiftAeroML
  1-2 days plus 60-150 CPU-h, under 1 MB per case); or SHIFT-SUV's raw volume meshes (about 6.5 TB, 3-5 days).
- The supervisor's readings (20:53 EDT, which Peter may veto): pieces synthesized from the documented domain count as the
  dataset's (DrivAerML's precedent); where the stored data and a paper disagree, the stored data win (HiLiftAeroML's far
  field from the interiors, about 89 MAC); SHIFT-SUV's speed is the stored 30 m/s; SHIFT-SUV's undocumented pieces would be
  named by what they are, with no claimed condition type. A new dataset version and the supply plan are Peter's decisions.

## 2026-10-23 — The surface task, decided: a surface task reads every named boundary and predicts at the cells of the boundaries it names (option A, built and timed on its own branch), by Peter's ruling of 23:26 EDT; ISLA-DTT's form of the surface task is revisited once ISLA-DTT's speed and memory work lands {#sec-nb-surface-bc}

**Question.** An ISLA surface task predicts at every cell it is given, so it cannot take the DrivAerML tunnel box by
configuration (@sec-nb-boundary-audit). At 20:34 EDT the supervisor asked Peter how a surface task should read the domain's
boundary: (A, the supervisor's recommendation) the task declares the boundary that carries its outputs and reads the others
as conditions only; (B) a surface task becomes an interior task whose prediction points are the vehicle's cell centres.
Lane SURFACE-BC (20:53-22:45 EDT) built (A) on its own branch while the question was open.

**What was built** (scratch/isla-surface-bc-2026-10-23/REPORT.md, DESIGN.md). psharpe/isla-surface-bc (head e636f29bd,
pushed, not merged): a keyword-only `forward(..., prediction_boundaries=[...])`, required for a surface task and refused for
an interior one. It owns no parameters, so the constructor, the state dict and every 0.9.0 checkpoint are unchanged (no
version bump), and a call that names every given boundary computes what 0.9.0 computed. Every given boundary's cells are
tokens; the outputs come back at the named boundaries' cells. In the recipe the DrivAerML Surface reader loads the four domain
meshes whole beside the subsampled vehicle and runs `PlaceGroundUnderBody` on the whole vehicle before its subsample;
`isla_surface.yaml` reads all five and predicts at the vehicle; the HiLiftAeroML and DeepJEB++ configurations name their
prediction boundaries. Seven new model tests (outputs only at the named cells; a condition-only boundary changes the vehicle's
output; pose covariance with every boundary moved alike; gradients reach every condition). The ISLA test directory: 280
passed, 47 skipped; recipe tests 534 passed, 2 failed in `test_campaign_c_hooks` with the same message on the base. A second
shape, the same declaration as a constructor argument, was not built.

**Cost** (cost_table.md; GB300, bfloat16, eager with compiled blocks, one case, 0.71 GPU-h). The training step is 223 ms with
the vehicle alone and 273 ms with the whole boundary (1.22x), the eval forward 64 and 73 ms, peak training memory 69.1 and
70.7 GB, and $L$ grows from 2.17 to 59.50 m. The 1.22x is the token count's alignment, not the tunnel: 200,000 + 5,054 =
205,054 tokens is not a multiple of 8, and any such count costs about 45 ms (20 percent) per step, the vehicle alone at
199,994 or 205,054 cells included (the bf16 GEMMs fall to slower kernels). At 205,048 tokens the whole boundary takes 229.5
ms against 228.0 ms for the vehicle alone at the same count, 1.03 times the 200,000-token step. (B) would take the Volume
task's step on the same five pieces: 2,897 ms and 140.6 GB at 0.9.0.

**Peter's answers.** At 22:31 EDT: "Yeah I mean spiritually I want to say B as that is 'more correct' in some sense. But if
A has practical benefits (and it might - it avoids the whole DTT read, as I understand), then we can do that. What do you
think? Let's discuss pros and cons more, based on the evidence you have". The supervisor answered at 23:15 EDT with
SURFACE-BC's evidence and a proposed rule: (A) as the canonical surface task if SURF-QPOP showed a surface prediction's
dependence on the request shrinking with the request size and splitting a request in four changing the error by under 5
percent; otherwise a (B) lane in the ISLA-DTT form, since (B)'s interacting form keeps a request dependence through the
prediction points' routing mass. He asked Peter to agree to that rule. Peter ruled at 23:26 EDT: "I agree that interacting B is the
least-attractive option here. It's gotta be either A or ISLA-DTT. You can do A for now, but then revisit ISLA-DTT after the
kernel speedups / memory savings land. If we can make ISLA-DTT practical in the long term, that would be awesome. TBD how
fast we can go there. Please don't hesitate to use parallel subagents - a huge number of them - to accelerate research on
this."

**What follows** (the supervisor's application). (A) is ISLA's surface task for now, in the forward-keyword shape on
psharpe/isla-surface-bc; the constructor shape stays an alternative Peter may prefer. Interacting (B) is dropped. The
surface task in ISLA-DTT form is revisited once ISLA-DTT's speed and memory work lands, and making ISLA-DTT fast and lean is a
program priority: two coordinator lanes launched at 23:33 EDT, DTT-FAST (exact performance work on ISLA-DTT's read) and

decides; it characterizes (A)'s request dependence (@sec-nb-surf-qpop). Lane ALIGN8 checks the unaligned-count cost in the

## 2026-10-23 — SURF-QPOP: on DrivAerML Surface, ISLA's prediction at a cell depends on the other requested cells through a quadrature error that falls close to 1/sqrt(N); four chunks cost what a four-times-smaller request costs, 6 to 8 percent; half a car alone costs 10 to 18 times; registered labels: wall shear "request-coupled beyond quadrature", pressure neither {#sec-nb-surf-qpop}

**Why.** Under option (A) the requested cells of the body are also the model's view of the body: every requested cell is a
boundary token, and the slice states are measure-weighted means over the requested cells with Horvitz–Thompson measures. A
cell's prediction then depends on which other cells are requested with it. SURF-QPOP measured that dependence on the
DrivAerML Surface standing (r090_dr_isla, both seeds, all 48 validation cars, float32, eager), pre-registered at 23:11 EDT
before any job (scratch/isla-surf-probe-2026-10-23/PREREG.md, md5 aadf3179, no amendment). After Peter's ruling it
characterizes (A) rather than deciding it. Inference only: LHR job 362779, 1.47 GPU-h with the smokes.

**Instrument.** A request is built as the reader builds the scored sample: rows of the full stored vehicle (about 17 million
cells), the Horvitz–Thompson factor, then the dataset's transform chain. Rebuilt this way the scored sample is identical
tensor for tensor on all 96 car-seed pairs; eager equals the scorer's compiled record to 3.9e-6; a repeated forward is
bit-identical, so every spread below is request dependence.

**Results** (scratch/isla-surf-probe-2026-10-23/RESULTS.md, md5 0f3d21e8; data results/out/reduced.json; means over the
48 cars; s is the relative L2, on the shared cells, of the difference between two independent requests' predictions, and
one request's noise is s / sqrt(2)):

| | pressure (seeds 42, 43) | wall shear (seeds 42, 43) |
|---|---|---|
| s, 50,000 → 800,000 cells | 0.0248 → 0.0061, 0.0244 → 0.0060 | 0.0360 → 0.0093, 0.0355 → 0.0091 |
| slope of log s on log N [95 % car bootstrap] | -0.509 [-0.517, -0.501], -0.507 [-0.514, -0.501] | -0.488 [-0.500, -0.475], -0.485 [-0.495, -0.474] |
| s(800k) ÷ s(200k) (the pure law: 0.500) | 0.492, 0.492 | 0.518, 0.508 |
| one request's noise at 200k ÷ its error | 0.211, 0.207 | 0.191, 0.190 |
| error at 50k, 400k, 800k ÷ error at 200k | 1.075, 0.986, 0.981; 1.074, 0.989, 0.983 | 1.066, 0.989, 0.985; 1.064, 0.990, 0.986 |
| 4 disjoint 50k chunks ÷ one 200k request | 1.075, 1.073 | 1.063, 1.063 |
| half the car alone (low x, high x) ÷ the same cells in a covering request | 18.4, 17.2; 17.4, 15.3 | 10.4, 11.1; 10.4, 10.4 |
| repeated forward | 0 | 0 |

Splitting a request in four costs what a four-times-smaller request costs, to within 0.003. The excess squared error from 50k
to 800k tracks the request noise squared (factor 1.15-1.22), and the extrapolated error of an infinite request puts the
scored 200k request's share of request noise at 2.0-2.6 percent of its error. The error comes within 1 percent of its 800k
value only at 400k. Given half a car, the model has no skill on it (errors 0.64-0.87). For comparison, interacting ISLA's
AirfRANS interior error rises 1.31 / 1.36 / 1.40 times under four chunks (@sec-nb-probes090-eag), a dependence with no knob
that converges.

**Registered reading, as written.** P1, P2, P4-P8 and V2 held; P3's third part (a plateau at 200k or below) failed, at 400k.
By PREREG section 3, "sound quadrature" needs the slope's interval to contain -0.5 and P2 to hold; "request-coupled beyond
quadrature" needs the interval to exclude -0.5 and lie above -0.4, or s(800k) not below half of s(200k). Wall shear reads
**"request-coupled beyond quadrature"** on both seeds, through the second clause (0.518, 0.508; seed 42 satisfies both
labels). Pressure takes **neither label**: its intervals miss -0.5 on the steep side, by 0.0006 and 0.0005, a case the
rule did not foresee. The supervisor's proposed rule of 23:15 EDT (@sec-nb-surface-bc), which Peter's ruling replaced before any result, also
asked that four chunks change the error by under 5 percent; at 6.3 to 7.5 percent that condition would not have held.

**Post hoc, beside the registered labels.** The clause that fires tests the pure law at its own value: an exact 1/sqrt(N)
law gives s(800k) / s(200k) = 0.500, so a sound quadrature fires it on about half of all draws. Every measured exponent lies
within 0.015 of -0.5, and s × sqrt(N) is constant to within 4 percent over the 16-fold range of N on both fields and seeds;
the lane reads the dependence as a Monte Carlo quadrature error falling as 1/sqrt(N). The shallow wall-shear exponent comes
mostly from 800k on seed 42, which this probe does not resolve. Also beside the rule: the scored 200k draw reads 0.4-0.8
percent below fresh 200k draws of the same cars (shared by both seeds, so not independent), either chance or a mild selection
on the program's fixed validation draw; unresolved, and below the two-seed gaps rulings use.

**For use.** A surface request covers the body: a user who wants one region asks for a covering sample and reads the region
from it. A larger sample, or the mean of several independent samples, lowers the error, at a linear forward cost (0.48 s at
200k and 1.98 s at 800k, 7.4 and 28.7 GB peak). An ISLA-DTT-style surface readout, with prediction cells apart from the
boundary tokens, would remove the covering condition; it is the point to measure when ISLA-DTT's surface form is revisited.
No standing number changes.

pressure, and lower 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the wall, both inside that case's run-to-run spread of 1.43 times
(@sec-nb-cap-audit-p2). Does the lead hold on the full dataset?

configuration with `n_slices=128` the only change, trained eagerly as the AirfRANS standing (full_train, 500 epochs,
3.75e-4, seeds 42 and 43), against that standing's two runs (r090eag_af_isla, 512 slices). Scored as the standing: the 200
test cases, float32, native deciding, posed beside, area degenerate. Per field: *helps* if D = ln(S ÷ B) < ln 0.90 and |D| >
2 SE, *harms* if D > ln 1.10 and |D| > 2 SE; on pressure 2 SE was 0.123, so helping needed S ÷ B below 0.88. A second
dataset was registered only on a pressure gain.

**Result: no change on every field** (RESULTS.md, md5 53b1cdc2; reading.md). 128-slice ÷ 512-slice ISLA, seed means of the
case-mean relative L2: pressure 0.998 (0.012450 against 0.012479), velocity 0.997, eddy viscosity 0.969; seed-matched on
pressure 0.920 and 1.085. Posed reads the same (0.998 / 0.996 / 0.970); area equals native exactly (degenerate). Per case,
the 128-slice model has the lower pressure error on 47 percent of the 200 airfoils. The near-wall band does not move: the
case-mean pressure error 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the wall is 1.01 times the reference's; its pooled value is 0.90 times, but
only through the reference's worse seed 42 (on seed 43 the 128-slice model is higher). The single-case lead was seed spread.

allocated memory 0.777 (33.4 against 43.0 GiB); over the whole run 0.41 (0.312 against 0.755 s), and 37.0 / 37.1 against
88.9 / 89.4 GPU-h per lane. AirfRANS runs ISLA's unfused geometry region, where the per-token, per-slice tensors dominate
the step; on a dataset that runs the fused geometry kernel the saving may be smaller. The lane used about 76 GPU-h of its
cap of 200.

**Predictions.** No change on pressure (0.70), velocity (0.85) and eddy viscosity (0.83) held; the step ratio in 0.60-0.85
(0.65) failed, cheaper than predicted; the near-wall band lower on both seeds (0.40) failed; memory below 0.80 (0.60) held.

**Consequence.** By the registered rule there is no accuracy stage 2, and the reference stays at 512 slices. A smaller slice
count is a speed option that costs nothing measurable on AirfRANS; before it can enter the scope freeze it needs a no-harm

  unchanged); the lug 1.28 at f13eb5ce0 and 1.25 with the fast path; AeroZoo 1.16 and 1.15; DrivAerML Volume with the vehicle
  1.49 and 1.36; with the whole boundary 1.11 at f13eb5ce0 and 0.29 with the fast path, 0.31 on the head's reference path.
- Peak memory of the training process is the same for every version. The geometry call's own peak on DrivAerML Volume is
  18.3 GiB at f13eb5ce0, 16.8 on the head's reference path and 17.7 on the fast path.
- On the DrivAerML vehicle case the fast path reached 296 ms against the design's estimate of about 210 ms, because the
  exact phase was not written in Triton (35 to 45 ms at that size); the optional 2-D kernel was not built either.

**What it means** (FINAL_REPORT.md). The fast path cuts the bundle's added step on the vehicle-only DrivAerML Volume case by
about a quarter, from +49 to +36 percent, and by less elsewhere. The larger change on the whole boundary comes from the
reference: every ISLA version paid about 2 s per call there, and fb263fa29 removes it. The lane's confidence in the
correctness rests on every check being exact; its timings agree within 3 percent with an earlier run (job 362819).

**A defect of the reference, found by GEO-FAST** (RESULTS.md, reported to the supervisor 01:08 EDT 2026-10-24). On a cell
with two coincident vertices the reference raises an IndexError, or on CUDA a device-side assert, or silently returns a
farther cell: the ball search's lower bound mishandles such a cell (torch's cross product of two equal vectors is 6e-18, not
0), and so does `_closest_weights` in the vertex order (b, b, a). On degenerate soups 5 of 40 float32 sets raise and 260 of
35,000 float32 queries are silently wrong; in float64 33 of 40 raise and 80 of 7,000 are wrong. In the real cases dumped
there are 0 such cells in 36,136,773 (26 cases). The fast path reproduces the reference's behaviour on them exactly. The
supervisor's decision (the supervisor's, not Peter's), as GEO-DEGEN's design quotes it: fix it, do not refuse such meshes;
a zero-area cell is the set its vertices span, never supplies a normal or an on-wall direction, and adds nothing to the
winding number (scratch/isla-geo-degen-2026-10-24/DESIGN.md). Lane GEO-DEGEN builds the fix on psharpe/isla-geo-fast and
checks it on GB300; the fast path merges after it.

Cost: 7.76 GPU-h of a 30 GPU-h cap, in 16 jobs (359447 to 363922). fb263fa29 alone went into ISLA with the bundle
(@sec-nb-geo-adopted).
