## 2026-10-24 — ALIGN8: a token count that is not a multiple of 8 costs 20 to 40 percent per step in bfloat16 on GB300, and a multiple of 8 that is not one of 32 about 8 percent, from the slice attention's token-axis matrix products and LayerNorm's backward pass; the standings are mostly aligned, so the stake is 1 to 3 percent of the rerun; a padding fix equal to roundoff is built, not merged {#sec-nb-align8}

**Question.** SURFACE-BC measured about 45 ms, 20 percent, per eager bfloat16 step on GB300 at a token count that is not a
multiple of 8 (@sec-nb-surface-bc). Does that hold in the standings' configuration, what causes it, and does padding remove
it? Records: scratch/isla-align8-2026-10-23/FINAL_REPORT.md (01:55 EDT 2026-10-24), results/repro_table.md and
exposure/exposure_gpuh.md there.

**Reproduction** (GB300, bfloat16, step in ms; base 32fa15389, fix e60be94d4 at j = 1 to 7 tokens added).

| case, path | N0 | base N0 | base odd N | base even N, not mod 8 | fix | odd / fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DrivAerML Surface, eager | 200,000 | 349 | 470 | 422 | 351 | 1.34 |
| DrivAerML Surface, compile_blocks | 200,000 | 219 | 313 | 268 | 223 | 1.40 |
| AeroZoo, eager | 400,000 | 723 | 966 | 872 | 731 | 1.32 |
| AirfRANS ISLA, eager (standing) | 100,992 | 662 | 727 | 701 | 668 | 1.09 |
| AirfRANS ISLA-DTT, eager (standing) | 100,992 | 820 | 891 | 863 | 833 | 1.07 |

: ALIGN8's reproduction (FINAL_REPORT.md; full table results/repro_table.md). {#tbl-nb-align8}

- Odd counts cost +32 to +40 percent, even counts not a multiple of 8 about +20 percent, eager and with the blocks compiled
  alike; the forward pass alone loses 6 to 27 percent. The small cases (the lug, Tensile2d, DeepJEB++) are launch-bound and
  their wall times too noisy to resolve it; profiled GPU time gives +5 percent on the lug at N + 1 and +8.6 percent on
  Tensile2d, and under 1 percent on DeepJEB++.
- **Cause** (results/gemm_362691.jsonl and the profiles): the slice attention's matrix products along the token axis (the
  slice pooling, the prototype attention and its value sum), for which cuBLAS leaves its sm103 kernels for slower ones when
  the token stride is not 16 bytes; and LayerNorm's backward pass, whose weight-gradient reduction takes its aligned path
  above 65,536 rows only when N is a multiple of 32 (1.49 to 2.54 ms per call), which is why an 8-aligned count (200,008)
  still cost 377 against 350 ms.
- **Exposure.** N is fixed per case. AeroZoo (all seven splits), DrivAerML Volume (vehicle or whole boundary), DrivAerML
  Surface (vehicle) and SHIFT-SUV are multiples of 32 on every case. AirfRANS (87 percent of cases misaligned), AirfRANS
  with its far field (74 percent), the lug (64), Tensile2d (89), DeepJEB++ (75) and DrivAerML Surface with the whole
  boundary (100 percent, 205,054 tokens) are not; with four ranks waiting on the slowest, 98 to 100 percent of their steps
  are exposed. The GPU-h at stake: about 28 measured and at most about 70 per two-seed set, 1 to 3 percent of a 2,500 to
  4,000 GPU-h rerun. A count one off on AeroZoo would cost +32 percent per step, about 1,100 to 2,200 GPU-h on REF-090's
  AeroZoo lanes.
- **Fix** (psharpe/isla-align8, pushed, not merged; 0fef70a42 pads to a multiple of 8, e60be94d4 to `TOKEN_ALIGNMENT = 32`):
  `_forward_tokens` appends −N mod 32 padding tokens, every field zero and log-weight −inf, as passive tokens are; they hold
  no mass in any softmax over points, and the tree read and the head read only the real tokens. No parameter, no flag, the
  state dict unchanged. Padded against unpadded on CPU: at most 1.2e-6 on outputs and 3.4e-5 on gradients in float32, 2.3e-15
  and 7.1e-14 in float64. The ISLA test directory gives 276 passed and 47 skipped (363324 to 363326). With the fix every j
  runs at the aligned time (DrivAerML Surface eager 470 to 351 ms, AeroZoo 966 to 731 ms), and at j = 0 it costs at most +1
  percent.

The lane recommends merging e60be94d4 before the final rerun, as cheap insurance on AeroZoo and DrivAerML; the merge is the
supervisor's. Chapter 06 states the cost (@sec-using-cost). Cost: 5.86 GPU-h of a 6 GPU-h cap (362691, 362753, 363327 and
363671, the last cancelled at 55 minutes; cpu-short 362791 to 362793, 363324 to 363326, 362817 and 362818).

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-24 (scratch/isla-book-tie-2026-10-24/SECOND_READ_TIE.md).*

## 2026-10-24 — DTT-KNOBS stage 1, inference only: on its trained checkpoints ISLA-DTT's opening angle acts as a trained constant (the exact read scores 1.8 to 4.7 times worse than θ = 1), a cheaper read saves time only at car scale (400,000 DrivAerML Volume points fit one GB300 at θ ≥ 1.5 and not at θ = 1, where the memory fit puts the limit at 349,000), the read's inference-time slack is in its kernel basis, and the gap to interacting ISLA is one of fit that no inference-time setting of the read explains {#sec-nb-dtt-knobs-stage1}

**Question.** Peter's ruling of 23:26 EDT 2026-10-23: "If we can make ISLA-DTT practical in the long term, that would be
awesome" (@sec-nb-surface-bc).
Which of its boundary read's settings trade accuracy for cost, and where does its accuracy gap to interacting ISLA come
from? Stage 1 trains nothing: it reads the trained checkpoints at other settings and prices the read. Nothing is adopted.

**Design** (scratch/isla-dtt-knobs-2026-10-23/, STAGE1.md and six child reports). The checkpoints are the AirfRANS pair
r090eag_af_dtt (eager-trained, the standing's ISLA-DTT arm) and the lug pair r090fix_lug_dtt, seeds 42 and 43, each trained
at θ = 1 with leaves of 4 cells, read against r090eag_af_isla and r090fix_lug_isla. Every read ran on the code its run
trained with, in float32, on the standing's sets in the scorer's order (AirfRANS `full_test`, 200 cases; lug `test`, 600),
native and posed; a setting changed only on a copy of the model in the probe's process. Gate: each harness reproduced the
standing's per-run scores before any other number was read, and every scoring part passed (AirfRANS within 1.8e-6
relative; lug 0.00221933 / 0.00183431 against the standing's 0.002219 / 0.001834). The cost model, which scores nothing,
ran random weights and bfloat16 training steps on psharpe/isla-geo-bundle code with the whole boundary. There was no
acceptance bar beyond the gate.
21.76 GPU-h of the 30-GPU-h cap on LHR; production jobs 363160 and 364211 (sensitivity), 363435 and 364009 (cost), 363020
and 363328 (capacity), 363336, 363640 and 363641 (read order), 363147, 363156 and 363365 (gap), 364468 (forest precision).

**Result 1: θ acts as a trained constant.** Read natively, both datasets score best at θ = 1 on every field and both
seeds, the error rises on both sides of θ = 1, and the exact read is the worst native setting (sens/sens_table.md):

| θ | AirfRANS pressure | AirfRANS velocity (in-plane) | AirfRANS eddy viscosity | lug von Mises |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (exact) | 2.71 / 2.36 | 1.79 / 2.04 | 3.54 / 4.68 | 4.62 / 3.47 |
| 0.25 | 2.07 / 1.86 | 1.58 / 1.73 | 3.17 / 3.98 | 2.90 / 2.53 |
| 0.5 | 1.41 / 1.40 | 1.18 / 1.23 | 1.27 / 1.44 | 1.97 / 2.00 |
| 0.75 | 1.07 / 1.03 | 1.03 / 1.05 | 1.04 / 1.08 | 1.24 / 1.29 |
| 1.25 | 1.18 / 1.20 | 1.04 / 1.07 | 1.07 / 1.07 | 1.39 / 1.41 |
| 1.5 | 1.35 / 1.35 | 1.10 / 1.14 | 1.16 / 1.17 | 2.12 / 1.94 |
| 2 | 1.86 / 1.91 | 1.30 / 1.33 | 1.38 / 1.44 | 3.20 / 2.79 |

Each entry is the native error at θ ÷ the same checkpoint's error at θ = 1, seeds 42 / 43, float32, eager. This is E2
seen from the other side: checkpoints trained with the dense read moved 2 to 20 times when read through the tree, and these
tree-trained ones move 1.8 to 4.7 times when read exactly. So the knob rule's test, whether the error converges as θ
tightens, needs models trained at each θ. The leaf size is not shown to be trained in: leaves of 2 or 8 cells change
AirfRANS by at most 0.1 %; on the lug, leaf 8 changes it by at most 0.8 % and leaf 2 by +2 % (seed 42) and +33 % (seed
43). Pairs per point at θ = 1 / 2 / 0.5 / 0 are 21.6 / 15.0 / 34.7 / 1,007 on AirfRANS and 118 / 54 / 300 /
6,525 on the lug, yet the eager forward time is flat for every θ > 0 (AirfRANS 475 to 498 ms, lug 195 to 252 ms; the exact
read 751 and 353 ms).

**Result 2: a cheaper read pays only at car scale** (cost/cost_table.md). Pairs per point follow A θ^-p leaf^-r (log2 N −
c) for cluster nodes plus a near-cell term; on DrivAerML p = 0.91, and on the volume datasets nodes are 93 to 99 % of
pairs at leaf 4. The step costs 5.16 ms and 0.265 GiB per million pairs per block on DrivAerML (held-out memory error at
most 0.4 %). At 400,000 prediction points on the DrivAerML Volume task with the whole boundary, a GB300 (274 GiB usable)
ran θ = 3 (1,837 ms / 248 GiB), θ = 2 (2,070 / 260) and θ = 1.5 (2,734 / 273, at the limit); θ = 1 ran out of memory, and
the memory fit puts θ = 1.25 at 285 GiB. By that fit, the largest counts that fit are 349,000 at θ = 1, 380,000 at 1.25,
431,000 at 2 and 462,000 at 3 (projections, not runs). The settings that fit take 2.3 to 3.4 times interacting ISLA's
796 ms at 400,000 (measured with the car alone). The normal-coherence test is vacuous
at θ ≥ 0.919 in 3D and 0.765 in 2D, because inside one sign octant |mean n| ≥ 1/√d; no node is refused at θ ≥ 1
on any dataset; below that bound θ tightens two tests at once.

**Result 3: at inference, the read's slack is in the kernel basis** (cap/cap_table.md; inference ablations of models
trained with every read and head, not retrains). The 16-function basis has effective rank 4 on AirfRANS and 1.5 on the
lug. Projected onto 8 directions it costs 1.11 / 1.28 times on AirfRANS and 1.9 / 3.6 times on the lug. Keeping the 4
strongest heads costs 6 to 9 times, although they carry 55 to 100 % of each block's update energy. Every read carries
part of the trained model, except the lug's first two (blocks 0 and 1), which are unused in both seeds. Reading after
every second block costs 15.5 / 11.5 times on AirfRANS and 21 / 31 times on the lug, the best of the forms with at most 6
reads. The 12 per-block reads alone are 9 % of the AirfRANS step and 26 % of the lug's (eager, with the shared forest, walk
and basis still running, so lower bounds).

**Result 4: at θ = 1 the read is far from the exact read** (order/order_table.md, AirfRANS, 50 cases per seed). Each
block's read update differs from the exact read on the same states by 3.9 to 27 % (median over points), mostly through the
clusters' mean values. The difference falls slowly where the model reads, as θ^0.33 to θ^0.69 from θ = 2 to 0.5,
and the median reaches 1 % only at θ 0.08 to 0.26 (pooled over seeds). A second-order cluster correction (H1) has a worse
median than the monopole's at every θ ≥ 1 in every block (1.01 to 3.81 times at θ = 1) and a worse p95 at every θ ≥ 0.5;
end to end at θ = 1 it scores 5.6 to 24 times worse. No H1 kernel is worth building unless a model retrained with it beats
the monopole at θ ≥ 1.

**Result 5: the gap to interacting ISLA is one of fit** (gap/gap_table.md, treeprec/treeprec_table.md). ISLA-DTT ÷ ISLA on
the first 200 / 600 training cases is 0.987 / 1.083 / 1.413 on AirfRANS (pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity) and 1.434 on
the lug, against 0.994 / 1.129 / 1.342 and 1.394 on test; the AirfRANS training subset covers Re 2 to 3e6 only, and the
test's low-Re quartile reads alike. On AirfRANS the gap is a smooth bias, not per-point tree noise, except eddy viscosity
beyond 0.1 chord, where its gap sits (roughness 0.076 / 0.112): in-plane velocity is 1.95 / 1.99 times ISLA's error in
the wake (seeds 42 / 43), and eddy viscosity 1.48 / 2.47 times beyond one chord, where ISLA-DTT's own two seeds differ by
1.72 times. The eddy-viscosity gap's share in the wake rests on seed 43 (wake ratios 1.02 / 1.35). Near the wall eddy
viscosity is 1.20 times but carries at most 5 % of the gap. On the lug the float32 gap covers 96 % of cases and sits 90 %
on surface nodes. Scored in bfloat16 the lug's two forms read level (1.043 [1.096, 0.989]), mostly because bfloat16
read-out noise (about 0.0033, twice the float32 errors) compresses the gap toward 1; ISLA-DTT is still worse in 73 % of
cases and on the surface (1.11). This says nothing on whether bfloat16 training causes the gap.
Ruled out as causes: every inference-time θ (beyond one chord the gap is smallest at θ = 1, 1.41 / 1.72 / 2.05, against
1.64 / 1.91 / 2.22 at 0.5); the bfloat16 training forest, whose reading widens the gap slightly (lug 1.394 to 1.399,
AirfRANS eddy viscosity 1.342 to 1.351); and the stored signed distance and the old query embedding (ATTRIB-090 §3c).
C_f = 0.131 / 0.121 (pressure / eddy viscosity) of ISLA-DTT's bundle cost stays unattributed; DK-GAP's reading that the
gap is mostly not a bundle effect is a reading, since C_f on eddy viscosity could be about 40 % of log(1.342) = 0.294.
Whether a retrained finer read closes the gap is untested.

**Two code facts found on the way** (CODE_FACTS.md; handed to DTT-POSE, no fix proposed). Under bfloat16 training the
forest is built from bfloat16-rounded coordinates: `points @ frame` in `BoundaryForest.build` and `point_pairs` runs under
the caller's autocast, so the trees' coordinates, boxes and node measures are bfloat16, while the box diameters and the
walk's box table stay float32. Every float32 score therefore reads a different forest: 82 % of AirfRANS points and 99 % of
lug points get a different list, and native error moves by 0.2 to 0.7 % (pressure level). The bfloat16 forest is not
pose-invariant: on the lug's posed set it doubles the error (1.90 [1.95, 1.85]); which of two candidate mechanisms
dominates is untested. Second, the lug's posed float32 score differs from native at every θ > 0 (1.53 / 1.98 at θ = 1,
1.0000 at θ = 0, with 1.29 times the pairs posed). 84 % of the lug's cells have a normal component below 1e-5 in the
canonical frame (measured under bfloat16 autocast in job 364211; the float32 share was not measured), so their sign
octant rests on rounding residues. That the pose flips those signs and so builds a different forest is inferred, not
tested: posed octant labels were not compared, no tie-break was tried, and the frame's own near-ties (skews about 1.2e-6
against the 1e-9 threshold) are not excluded.

**Consequence.** An inference probe cannot price a retrain: θ is trained in, and the capacity ablations rank models
trained with every read and head. Stage 2 is pre-registered and was not yet run when stage 1 was read: retrained AirfRANS arms at θ = 2 and θ = 0.5,
reads after every second block, a kernel basis of 8, the exact read, and ISLA-DTT without scales on a standardized inlet
speed, each against the standing's pair (scratch/isla-dtt-knobs-2026-10-23/PREREG.md, md5 84a25280: about 1,010 GPU-h
without the exact read, which adds about 330 to 390 GPU-h and is submitted only if its smoke prices it at 300 or less;
the supervisor's amendment moved that gate to 400, @sec-nb-dtt-knobs-prereg).
The θ = 2, 1, 0.5, 0 arms form the knob rule's ladder: if the error falls toward the exact-trained model's as θ
tightens, the tree read earns its credit as a convergent approximation; if the exact-trained model is no better, θ is a
pure cost knob on AirfRANS. The second dataset waits for the AirfRANS reads.

**For the book.** No standing changes. The DTT ledger row gains the trained-constant reading and the two code facts; 05
states what θ and the forest's precision do on a trained model; 04 and 20 read the exact read's error ratio on the
standing's own pair; 19 adds the DrivAerML Volume memory ladder; 12 and 16 say where the gap sits; 20 gains the open
question of a retrained read (@sec-oq-dtt-theta), and 05 states the two code facts as limits of the code as it is, each
with an In-flight callout for DTT-POSE (records copied to results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_knobs/).

## 2026-10-24 — GEO-DEGEN: a cell of zero area is read as the segment or point its vertices span, bitwise unchanged on every input without one and correct on 291,100 degenerate queries, where the base raised on 38 sets; thin cells of nonzero area and overlapping coplanar cells remain limits {#sec-nb-geo-degen}

**Question.** GEO-FAST found that the reference geometry raises, or silently returns a farther cell, on cells with two
coincident vertices (@sec-nb-geo-fast). The supervisor's decision (the supervisor's, not Peter's): fix it, do not refuse
such meshes; a zero-area cell is the set its vertices span, never supplies a normal or an on-wall direction, and adds
nothing to the winding number. Can the reference and the fast path both do that without changing any output on a mesh
that has no such cell? Lane GEO-DEGEN, branch psharpe/isla-geo-fast. Records: scratch/isla-geo-degen-2026-10-24/DESIGN.md
(md5 18c7bec9), RESULTS.md (md5 f151d5ea), FINAL_REPORT.md (md5 c7d099c3); copies in
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_degen/.

**What was built** (a9592e9a3, the fix; 1086cf42e, covered cells left out; no new custom op, ISLA's version unchanged).

- The flag (`_zero_area`) tests the cross product for exact zero: a float64 filter with Shewchuk's error bound clears most
  cells, and the cells it leaves get exact products summed as a nonoverlapping expansion. There is no tolerance constant.
  It is exact for all float32 coordinates and for float64 magnitudes in [2^-485, 2^510].
- A flagged cell gets NaN planes and corners, so no lower bound of the ball search drops it, and its closest point is the
  nearer of the two edges between consecutive canonical vertices. (GEO-FAST's "longest edge" rule was right in distance,
  but at a T-junction it made a feature no mesh cell shares, which changed the direction at 91 of 2,964 queries.)
- In the exact phase and at ties a flagged cell contributes its distinct vertices and edges, has no normal and parity 0 in
  the winding number. An on-wall query held only by zero-area cells takes d = 0 and u = 0, the least-norm element of the
  generalized gradient.
- A zero-area cell lying along the edges or at a vertex of other cells is dropped by an index test, so the outputs are
  bitwise those of the mesh without it.
- The fast path runs the same code on the same values, with the flag permuted into the tree order.

**Checks** (RESULTS.md; every comparison bitwise unless a bound is named).

| check | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| a, unchanged on inputs without a zero-area cell, against 0570fc6c8 under a renamed op (op outputs, w, d, u, gradients) | CPU, 50 cases; GB300 365177, 102 cases (DrivAerML vehicle and whole boundary, AeroZoo, 20 lug cases, AirfRANS, Tensile2d) | 0 of 427,884 and 0 of 2,265,906 queries differ, under each kernel |
| b, correct on degenerate input, against an independent float64 brute force | CPU and GB300, 152 set-and-precision runs, 1,919 zero-area cells | 291,100 queries: 0 raises, 0 non-finite, 0 distances beyond 8 u(\|x\| + R), 0 wrong cells, 0 wrong signs of 239,824, 0 bad of 3,024 queries held only by zero-area cells; the base on the same sets: 38 sets raise, 4,629 distances beyond the bound, 3,999 wrong cells, 14 wrong signs |
| b, covered cells added to closed meshes | CPU and GB300 | 0 of 110,948 queries change |
| c, fast against reference | GB300, 86 runs and the degenerate sets | 0 of 1,958,096 and 0 of 291,100 queries differ; 0 of 520,761 in the forced-fast GPU tests |
| d, tests | LHR cpu-short 365178; GB300 365177 | ISLA test directory 358 passed, 100 skipped, 0 failed; the new test_isla_geometry_degenerate.py (18 CPU and 16 CUDA tests, 13 of the CPU tests fail at 0570fc6c8); GPU geometry, tree-read, geometry-fast and degenerate files 208 passed, 1 skipped, forced and under `auto` |

: GEO-DEGEN's checks of the zero-area fix. {#tbl-nb-geo-degen}

**Cost.** On the DrivAerML Volume task's whole boundary (16.65 million cells, 200,000 queries, GB300) the flag takes
2.4 ms; the geometry call goes from 406 to 412 ms under the reference kernel and from 340.5 to 341.1 ms under the fast
kernel. Real dumps hold no zero-area cell (0 of 16,652,301 on DrivAerML), and GEO-FAST found no cell with two coincident
vertices in 36,136,773, so no trained result changes.

**Two limits that stay as they were at the base** (RESULTS.md, "Out of scope"; reported to the supervisor at 02:10 EDT).

- Thin cells of nonzero area: on float64 soups of 8 slivers whose middle vertex sits a relative 1e-13 off the line, 8 of
  10 soups raise IndexError (1e-16: 10 of 10); float32 slivers and float64 at 1e-10 and above give 0 of 14,000 wrong. With
  the plane bound turned off none raise, but 3 of 14,000 queries get a farther point. A fix changes outputs on inputs
  without zero-area cells, so it is a lane of its own; the lane proposes a per-cell certified plane bound and the closest
  point taken as the least of the face projection and the three edge points. The float32 cast of TIE-FIX's midpoint is such
  a thin cell (5 of 1,646 queries, as at the base).
- Overlapping coplanar cells change the direction at ties: zero-area cells inside a face but off its edges, kept as
  segments, change 905 of 9,768 float32 queries, and the control, triangles of nonzero area in the same place, changes 891
  at the head and at 0570fc6c8 alike.

The supervisor launched GEO-THIN at 04:18 EDT for both, with a census of every dataset's meshes.

Cost: 0.66 GPU-h of the 4 GPU-h cap (364908, 365177; CPU jobs 364909, 365178).

## 2026-10-24 — DTT-KNOBS stage 2 registered and approved: ISLA-DTT retrained on AirfRANS with a cheaper or a finer read (θ = 2, θ = 0.5, a read after every second block, a basis of 8, the exact read) and without scales on a standardized inlet speed, each against the standing's pair by rules R1 to R5; caps 1,050 GPU-h and 400 for the exact read {#sec-nb-dtt-knobs-prereg}

**Question.** Stage 1 found that every inference-time change of ISLA-DTT's read is worse on checkpoints trained at
θ = 1 (@sec-nb-dtt-knobs-stage1), so only retraining can say what a setting costs. Q1: does ISLA-DTT trained with a cheaper
read predict as well as the standing? Q2, Peter's knob rule: retrained at θ = 2, 1, 0.5 and 0, does the error converge as
θ tightens, or is θ a pure cost knob? Q3: does a finer read narrow the gap to interacting ISLA in the wake and beyond one
chord? Q4: does ISLA-DTT without ISLA's scales but with the inlet speed standardized read like the reference ISLA-DTT
(ATTRIB-090's B)? Record: scratch/isla-dtt-knobs-2026-10-23/PREREG.md (approved as md5 84a25280; md5 e601d4af with the
amendment appended), second-read in PREREG_REVIEW.md; copies in results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_knobs/.

**What was seen before registering** (PREREG section 2). All of stage 1, including every inference-time number on the
control's checkpoints (θ = 2 costs 1.30 to 1.91 times at inference, θ = 0.5 1.18 to 1.44, the exact read 1.79 to 4.68;
every second read, mean-replaced, 15.5 / 11.5 times; the basis projected onto 8 directions 1.11 / 1.28); the control's
and interacting ISLA's scores in full; ATTRIB-090's results; DK-GAP's regional table; the control lanes' step times and
link history. No stage-2 arm existed.

**Arms** (AirfRANS, the standing's eager protocol, two seeds each; each snapshot is the control's code with one change).

| priority | arm | the one change | trained | control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | K-THETA2 | `TREE_READ_THETA = 2.0` | eager | r090eag_af_dtt 42 / 43 |
| 2 | K-THETA05 | `TREE_READ_THETA = 0.5`, the coherence test kept | eager | r090eag_af_dtt |
| 3 | K-B1 | the tree read only after 1-based blocks 2, 4, ..., 12 | eager | r090eag_af_dtt |

| 5 | K-EXACT | `TREE_READ_THETA = 0.0`, the exact read | eager | r090eag_af_dtt |
| 6 | DTT-NOSC-STD | ATTRIB-090's NOSC-STD configuration with read-only prediction points | fix-trained | r090fix_af_dtt (ATTRIB-090's B) |

: DTT-KNOBS stage 2's arms (PREREG section 3). {#tbl-nb-dtt-knobs-arms}

The arms keep stage 1's two code facts, as the control does, so each comparison is within one code. Scoring is the
control's: float32, the 200 `full_test` cases, the final checkpoint, eager, native and posed (area is degenerate on
AirfRANS and not scored), with checks of epoch, case count, snapshot and dataset before any row is read.

**Rules** (PREREG section 5; CM is the case-mean relative L2, native, per field: pressure, in-plane velocity, eddy
viscosity).

- R1, each of arms 1 to 5 against the control: D = ln(seed-mean CM of the arm ÷ that of the control), SE from both pairs'
  two-seed spreads; helps if D < ln 0.90 and |D| > 2 SE, harms if D > ln 1.10 and |D| > 2 SE, otherwise no change; a
  sub-bar flag at ratios beyond 1.03 or 0.97 with both seeds on one side.
- R2, the ladder of Peter's knob rule, from the R1 labels at θ = 2, 0.5 and 0: converges, pure cost knob (sub-label free
  to θ = 2), exact read worse, or mixed, per field and overall by two of three fields.
- R3, decision use for the cheaper arms: no harm on any field and no up flag makes an arm a candidate for the scope freeze
  as a free cost cut; K-B1 changes where the model reads, so its adoption also needs Peter's word.
- R4, the far-field gap: in-plane velocity in the wake and eddy viscosity beyond one chord, narrows or widens by R1's shape
  on the regional errors.
- R5, DTT-NOSC-STD against B and against DTT-NOSC, by ATTRIB-090's test (|Δ| ≥ 2 SE and an effect of at least 5%), read as
  whether standardization removes DTT-NOSC's loss.

Twelve predictions with probabilities are in PREREG section 6 (for example, K-THETA2 no harm on all three fields, p 0.45).

## 2026-10-24 — DTT-FAST, piece COMPILE: ISLA-DTT's compiled blocks are certified against eager block by block (float32 within 1.5e-5, float64 at roundoff), and Inductor leaves out the bfloat16 casts inside them, so compiled bfloat16 blocks round fewer intermediates than eager, with block outputs no farther from float64 than eager's; one policy for every compiled region, the supervisor's {#sec-nb-compiled-casts}

**Question.** Peter's ruling of 23:26 EDT 2026-10-23 makes ISLA-DTT's speed a priority ("If we can make ISLA-DTT practical
in the long term, that would be awesome", @sec-nb-surface-bc). What does `compile_blocks` compile in an ISLA-DTT step, does
it compute eager's function, and can more of the read be compiled? Lane DTT-FAST, piece COMPILE, reference f13eb5ce0.
Records: scratch/isla-dtt-fast-2026-10-23/compile/RESULTS.md (md5 884f4b23) and REPORT.md; copies in
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_fast_compile/.

**The map.** `compile_blocks` compiles only the 12 slice blocks (the fused geometry kernel is a custom-op leaf inside them;
the eager geometry region of two-dimensional cases is traced into them). The whole read runs eager: the forest, walk and
plan, the pair invariants and basis MLP, `node_means`, the read's LayerNorms and projections, the kernel term and the
segment softmax; so do the geometry call and the head.

**The certification** (RESULTS.md section 2; AeroZoo `azc_full_dtt` and AirfRANS `r090eag_af_dtt`, seeds 42 and 43, each
block on the eager float32 run's own inputs at full size, beside float64 eager; gradients at 20,000 tokens and points).

- Float32: the compiled blocks agree with eager to 1.5e-5 relative or better, the largest on AeroZoo, where the first
  block's eager float32 output is itself 8.5e-4 from float64.
- Float64: every output and parameter gradient at roundoff, 2.3e-13 relative or better.
- Bfloat16: the compiled blocks' outputs are no farther from float64 than eager's (AeroZoo seed 42, 8.2e-2 against
  1.4e-1), and their output fields and parameter gradients are 1.0 to 1.4 times eager's distance to float64 in every
  group. One scalar sits higher: on the DrivAerML whole boundary at random initialization the bfloat16 loss reads 1.70,
  with every tensor group at 1.13 or below.
- Float32 gradients: on AirfRANS seed 42 the compiled path's are 2.0 to 2.3 times eager's distance to float64 (3.4 on the
  loss), because eager sits unusually close to float64 there and 2 to 3 float32 ulps double the distance; elsewhere 1.0 to
  1.6.
- Pair lists are equal in every case and precision.

**The cast finding** (RESULTS.md section 4). Inductor by default leaves out the round trip to bfloat16 between the operations
it fuses (`emulate_precision_casts=False`), so the compiled blocks do not round where eager does: their bfloat16 outputs
differ from eager's by up to 5.8e-2 relative (AeroZoo block 0), against 5.0e-3 with the casts kept. Every result trained
with compiled blocks used them as they are. The lane's `block_precision_casts.patch` restores eager's rounding points; it is free on
three-dimensional cases but adds 11 to 14% to the AirfRANS step and 5% to the lug's, and changes the function every
checkpoint trained under. The lane recommends against it. Its read patch (`compile_read.patch`: the read's projections,
`node_means` and the basis compiled, 3 to 7% of the model step and 1 to 8 GiB of peak) compiles with the casts kept.

**The policy** (the supervisor's, 2026-10-24, LANE_RULES "Compiled regions"): one policy for every compiled ISLA region, old
and new: Inductor's default casts (no `emulate_precision_casts`), certified block by block against eager at a maximum
deviation of 1e-5 in float32 and at roundoff in float64, plus a bfloat16 check that the region's error against float64
stays within 1.5 times eager's. The current blocks are kept, although their largest float32 deviation, on AeroZoo, is 1.5e-5 and the bfloat16 loss of
the randomly initialized DrivAerML whole-boundary model reads 1.70 times eager's distance; the read patch is not merged,
and under this policy it would compile without the emulated casts.

Cost: 4.79 of 6 GPU-h (eight GB300 jobs, 363857 to 365445; cpu-short 365063).

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-24 (scratch/isla-book-geofast-2026-10-24/SECOND_READ_GEOFAST.md).*

**Later (2026-10-24).** The supervisor restated the policy at 06:51 EDT (LANE_RULES "Compiled regions"). It certifies each compiled region per tensor group (the block outputs and each group of parameter gradients) against float64 eager on the same inputs: in each precision the compiled region's distance to float64 may exceed eager's by at most eager's own change under a one-ulp perturbation of the region's inputs, measured; in float64 the two agree at roundoff; a scalar loss is reported beside and never gated, since its eager error can sit near zero by chance. It replaces the 1e-5 bound and the bare 1.5 ratio: the first fails an ill-conditioned block however accurate its compiled path (AeroZoo block 0, whose eager float32 output is itself 8.5e-4 from float64), and the second fails where eager sits within an ulp of float64 (AirfRANS seed 42). Whether the current compiled blocks pass the restated policy has not been measured; 05 states the policy as the supervisor's, with an In-flight callout (@sec-arch-cost).

**The merge.** Lane MERGE-PREP, launched by the supervisor at 04:18 EDT 2026-10-24, took ALIGN8's fix (psharpe/isla-align8

**What the class does.** `_pad_tokens` completes the token set to a multiple of `TOKEN_ALIGNMENT` = 32 with tokens whose
fields are zero and whose log-weight is $-\infty$: like read-only prediction points they hold no measure in any softmax
over points, so no other token reads them, and no output is read from them. e60be94d4 ran the padding even at an aligned
count (`F.pad` with zero padding is a clone), and its surface gradients were not bitwise. With 1062d6086 an aligned count
runs no padding in eager mode: outputs, every gradient and the aten compute ops are bitwise the base's on 20 cases (surface
in three and two dimensions, interior, ISLA-DTT, interior in two dimensions; float32 and float64; train and eval), before
and after the merge with 7213c70c5. Under the whole-model compile the pad always runs, since a test for an empty pad would
guard the dynamic token count.

mode; case 0 of each training split at its natural token count and at the largest multiple of 32 below it; medians over

## 2026-10-24 — DTT-POSE: what makes ISLA-DTT's forest depend on pose and precision is measured (rounded octant labels and exact box-test ties on the lug, bfloat16 coordinates under autocast); the supervisor approves a forest that depends on the boundary alone, which makes ISLA 0.12.0, and its retrain check is registered as DTT-POSE-EXP {#sec-nb-dtt-pose-design}

**Question.** DTT-KNOBS stage 1 found two code facts (@sec-nb-dtt-knobs-stage1): under bfloat16 autocast the forest is
built from rounded coordinates, which is not pose-invariant and differs from the float32 forest a score builds; and on the
lug ISLA-DTT's posed error at $\theta = 1$ is 1.53 / 1.98 times native, attributed, without a test, to octant labels that
rounding decides. Lane DTT-POSE, launched by the supervisor on 2026-10-24, measured why and designed a forest that is a
function of the boundary alone. Records: scratch/isla-dtt-pose-2026-10-24/MECHANISMS.md (md5 2e89f066) and DESIGN.md
(md5 8420670e); copies in results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_pose/.

**The mechanisms** (phase A; GB300 probes of a copy of the 0.11.0 forest checked bitwise against the real one on all 106
forests; the lug's 24 test cases posed by the scorer's dataset, 24 AirfRANS cases, two DrivAerML Volume cases with the
whole boundary; $\theta = 1$, leaves of 4).

- **Octants, in float32 too.** The lug's faces are parallel to its principal axes, so most normal components are exactly
  zero in the canonical frame and the stored ones are rounding residues: 86% of the lug's cells (78 to 90%) have a smallest component below the bound on its rounding from the cell's float32 vertices, and 84% one below
  $10^{-5}$, the share DTT-KNOBS measured below $10^{-5}$ in bfloat16. Posed against native 11% of the cells (4 to 20%) flip octant and every point's list changes. Built with
  the native octant labels, the posed forest gives 94% of the points their native list back.
- **Box-test ties.** The lug's prediction points are its hexahedral mesh's nodes, commensurate with its boundary cells, so
  at $\theta = 1$ the admission test is an exact equality for many pairs: a change of $\theta$ by $1 \pm 10^{-6}$ changes
  6.7% of the lug's lists, against 0.001% on AirfRANS and 0.07% on DrivAerML. With the labels forced and the box test
  given its error band, the median lug case differs at one point.
- **The frame is not the cause.** Posed and native canonical coordinates differ by at most $2.6 \times 10^{-7}$ of the
  extent and no axis changes sign in 32 cases; the two nearly symmetric axes' third moments, $1.1$ and
  $1.3 \times 10^{-6}$, move under pose by at most $1.1 \times 10^{-7}$, so `CANONICAL_SKEW_TIE` decides nothing.
- **bfloat16.** Under autocast `points @ frame` casts both factors to bfloat16 and rounds the product. With the labels and
  the box band held, the uncentred product rounded to bfloat16 changes nearly every posed lug list (the median 100%, at least 98%) and 87%
  of AirfRANS's (the median), and the
  cast of the factors does the same, so both candidate mechanisms break pose on their own; a centred product rounded to
  bfloat16 changes one lug list and four AirfRANS lists (medians) but is still not the float32 forest. The boxes and the
  node measures are bfloat16, which scales every node's mean keys and values by up to $2^{-9}$ and shifts its log measure
  by as much.
- **Why AirfRANS was spared.** Its normals have no component below $10^{-5}$, only 0 to 8 cells flip octant, and its
  points are not on a lattice commensurate with its cells.
- Renumbering the cells changed no list in any case.

**The design** (DESIGN.md; approved by the supervisor at 06:07 EDT 2026-10-24). D1: build and walk with autocast
disabled, in the inputs' precision. D2: centred canonical coordinates in float64, about the measure-weighted centroid,
rounded once. D3: the cube face of each normal (the axis of its largest component, with its sign; $2d$ classes) in place
of the $2^d$ octants, with a tie band of twice the bound on the components' rounding and the frame's rotation, ties to the
lowest axis. D4: the box test with its error band, so an exact tie opens the node in every pose. D5: each token's normal
error bound carried into the forest. A face holds normals with $\lvert n_k \rvert \geq 1/\sqrt d$, as an octant does, so
the coherence test still admits every node at $\theta = 1$, and a normal and its negative still land in different trees.
It changes ISLA-DTT's function on every case, so it is ISLA 0.12.0 and merges only after a registered retrain check;
interacting ISLA computes the same function.

**Measured on the prototype** (GB300 366658, 366705; a random-weight ISLA-DTT, hidden 64, two layers; posed against
native in float32, and a bfloat16-autocast forward against the float32 one).

| | lug, 12 test cases | AirfRANS, 12 cases | DrivAerML Volume, 2 cases |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| forward, posed against native, RMS difference ÷ RMS: 0.11.0 / prototype | 2.1e-6 / 1.6e-7 | 7.1e-5 / 7.1e-5 (pressure; not the forest) | 3.3e-5 / 3.3e-5 (not the forest) |
| forest pairs unmatched, posed against native: 0.11.0 / prototype | 52% / 0.0002% | 9.5% / 0.001% | 5.0% / 0.52% |
| bfloat16 forest bitwise the float32 one: 0.11.0 / prototype | 0 / 12 of 12 | 0 / 12 of 12 | 0 / 2 of 2 |
| pairs per point: 0.11.0 / prototype | 117 / 112 | 21.6 / 21.1 | 706 / 586 |
| `tree_read_pairs`, eager [ms]: 0.11.0 / prototype | 115 / 95 | 65 / 59 | 230 / 192 |

: DTT-POSE's prototype against the 0.11.0 forest (DESIGN.md section 3). {#tbl-nb-dtt-pose}

Interacting ISLA, which builds no forest, is bitwise unchanged. What no construction removes is a generic residual:
posing in float32 moves every input by its rounding, so a few cells per case sit within rounding of a face's edge or a
Morton grid line (DrivAerML's 0.52% of pairs). Phase C is DONE (07:01 EDT): ISLA 0.12.0 on psharpe/isla-dtt-pose (0673bff1d, 40b411df5, 4242962e0, refusing every
earlier state dict; merged with 1b25eb899 as 0f06e4065; not merged into psharpe/isla), the ISLA test directory 375 passed
(367224). Its registered bound, the random-weight lug forward posed against native at most 1e-6 on every one of 24
cases, is not met as stated: 23 of 24 meet it (median 1.5e-7), and on case 1884 (1.74e-5) the forest is identical posed
and native and the excess is the same at $\theta = 0$, with no forest, on 0.11.0 and 0.12.0 (366947, 367092), so it
comes from the query geometry. Trained 0.9.0 checkpoints read through the new forest score posed ÷ native 1.0000 to
1.0003, with native errors 1.9 to 7.0 times their own, since they were trained on the octant forest; only the retrain
check prices the change (scratch/isla-dtt-pose-2026-10-24/FINAL_REPORT.md).

**The retrain check, registered** (lane DTT-POSE-EXP, launched by the supervisor at 06:51 EDT; PREREG md5 2f46a10c,
approved at 07:10 EDT with the supervisor's amendments before submission A1.1 to A1.5; cap 650 GPU-h). Arms: ISLA-DTT
trained with the new forest, ported to 0.9.0, on the lug and the AirfRANS interior task, two seeds each, every other byte
the controls' (the standings' ISLA-DTT pairs). Rules: native accuracy N per field, cost if
$D = \ln(\text{arm} \div \text{control}) > \ln 1.10$ and $\lvert D \rvert > 2\,\mathrm{SE}$; on the lug also a paired
reading, cost if both seeds' ratios exceed 1.10 (amendment A1.3); the pose check P, posed ÷ native within 1.02 on each lug
seed; the precision check Q, the bfloat16 forest bitwise the float32 one on every scored case. The supervisor's adoption
rule: the forest goes into canonical ISLA if no field reads cost and P and Q pass; a cost goes to Peter. Predictions (the
lane's): any cost 0.10, adoption 0.75.

**For the book.** 05 states the lug's mechanisms as measured and the design with the prototype's numbers; 03, 04, 09, 16, 20
and 21 drop "inferred, not tested"; In-flight callouts in 05, 16 and 20 point at the retrain check; 20 adds the frame's
sign rule as an open question (@sec-oq-frame-sign), since `canonical_frame` is shared by the token draw and the forest.

## 2026-10-24 — GEO-THIN phase A: no stored dataset is exposed to thin cells (0 wrong of 310,545 recipe queries against an exact rational brute force, in both precisions and under both kernels), adversarial float64 queries on the thinnest stored AeroZoo faces raise, and the tie direction at near-duplicate normals moves at most 3.9e-5 under one-ulp vertex moves; the supervisor approves a certified design {#sec-nb-geo-thin-census}

**Question.** GEO-DEGEN left two limits of the exact geometry (@sec-nb-geo-degen): thin cells of nonzero area and
overlapping coplanar cells. Lane GEO-THIN, launched by the supervisor at 04:18 EDT 2026-10-24, counted them in every
stored boundary mesh, checked the geometry on the recipe's draws and on adversarial ones, and took over the
tie-conditioning probe. Records: scratch/isla-geo-thin-2026-10-24/RESULTS.md (md5 6daa2865, phase A) and DESIGN.md
(md5 f7f8ed68); copies in results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_thin/. Code under test: the geometry of 7213c70c5.

**The census** (A1; per mesh, after the weld; $\rho$ is twice a triangle's area over its longest edge squared).

- No stored mesh has a cell whose float64 normal is uncertain beyond 4 float32 ulps, so the float32 lower bound's failure
  does not occur on stored data.
- DrivAerML (both tasks, whole boundary and vehicle), SHIFT-SUV, the lug: $\rho \geq 0.037$, no cell near the failure
  index. AeroZoo: $\rho$ down to $6.5 \times 10^{-7}$ in the recipe's dump, 2 cells past the float32 index and 156 past the
  float64 one; DeepJEB++ 1,169 to 1,779 per case past the float64 index; HiLiftAeroML's wing, read by no exact geometry,
  $\rho$ down to $2.5 \times 10^{-11}$.
- No coplanar fold and no overlap in an axis plane anywhere; AeroZoo's dump has 4 near folds $3 \times 10^{-4}$ rad from
  flat. DrivAerML's whole boundary has 110 exact T-junction vertices on 74 edges of the tunnel floor.

**Against an exact rational brute force** (A2; jobs 366241, 366627). Every query of each recipe dump through the op; 310,545
of them checked: 0 raises, 0 wrong distances, cells or signs, 0 on-wall decisions wrong, in float32 and float64, under the
reference and the fast kernel. AeroZoo's recipe queries near its 4 near folds get bitwise the same distance and direction
without the thinner cell. T-junctions (366938): no query of a 200,000-point draw has its closest point at one, and with
every cell over such an edge split at its T vertices the distance, the direction and the sign are bitwise unchanged at all
of them, in both seeds.

**Adversarial queries** (A2b, A3). On the 50 thinnest cells of each stored mesh, 5,000 queries on and off the face: in
float32 none is wrong; in float64 the recipe's AeroZoo dump and stored case 0 raise a device-side assert under both
kernels (no candidate survives). On a cube with a thin cap or needle in one face, rotated and shifted, queries fail from
$\rho \approx 10^{-5}$ in float32 (a needle; a cap from $10^{-6}$) and $\rho \approx 10^{-3}$ in float64, and GEO-DEGEN's float64 sliver soups at
$10^{-13}$ raise in 8 of 10. The causes: the float32 lower bound reads each edge plane's side by a rounded sign test; the
float64 ball test drops a cell whose computed distance exceeds the radius; and Ericson's closest-point weights, ratios of
determinants of size $\rho^2$, move the point along the face by about the unit roundoff over $\rho^2$. With exact weights
and both prunings off, every thin-cell set is correct; the winding number gave no wrong sign on any clearly off-wall query.

**The tie direction** (A4). On the lug and Tensile2d, a random one-ulp move of every float32 vertex changes the direction
at tied queries by at most $3.9 \times 10^{-5}$ and $6.4 \times 10^{-6}$, at most 2.6 times the normals' own change, and
the least-norm point's active set changed at no persisting tie. Which queries tie is itself decided by rounding (the
lug's 1,639 tied queries become 5,777 to 5,823), with the direction continuous through it. On synthetic near-duplicate
normals the point is Hölder-continuous of order 1/2. This settles the tie-conditioning question.

**The design** (DESIGN.md; approved by the supervisor at 06:27 EDT 2026-10-24 with conditions 1 to 7). F1: edge planes
oriented by the cell's vertex order, with the cell's normal certified, and a cell whose normal is not certified never
rejected by them. F2: the float64 ball test keeps a cell unless its distance less a certified bound on Ericson's error
exceeds the radius. F3: where that bound exceeds the arithmetic's, an accurate closest point in the frame of the cell's
longest edge, taken only where the two answers differ beyond the bound. Every certificate is a derived bound on IEEE
float64 rounding, and every cell without the defect keeps its arithmetic bitwise. Overlapping coplanar cells and
T-junctions stay limits. Phase C is RUNNING (a lane-writer from 06:35 EDT); the expected effect on stored data is no
change, checked bitwise as GEO-DEGEN's check a.

**For the book.** 05 states the three kinds of input as limits with their counts and the certified fix in an In-flight
callout; 20's `sec-oq-ties` states the tie direction as measured and leaves thin cells as its open part, with a callout.

Cost: GB300 short and cpu-short jobs within GEO-THIN's cap of 8 GPU-h; its JOBS.md lists them and gives no total

## 2026-10-24 — NEARWALL: under the whole boundary ISLA's distance channel is linear for 19.5 percent of AirfRANS's drawn points, and the standings' input layers code log d; the supervisor approves keeping the channel, with its documentation corrected, and holds a viscous softening ready {#sec-nb-nearwall-design}

**Question.** With the whole boundary, ISLA's length unit $L$ is the size of the domain, so the softening of its distance
channel $\operatorname{asinh}(s / 10^{-6})$, $s = d / L$, moves out with the far field. Lane NEARWALL, launched by the
supervisor at about 07:40 EDT 2026-10-24, measured what that does, with probes only. Records:
scratch/isla-nearwall-2026-10-24/RESULTS.md (md5 43888a10), DESIGN.md (1ff494b6) and its review REVIEW_DESIGN.md
(08b55280, "sound with fixes", each applied); copies in results/campaigns_2026-10-23/nearwall/.

- **Exposure** (the recipe's drawn points at 2b15490b2). Off-wall points in the linear part, body alone against whole
  boundary: AirfRANS 0 against 19.5% (first nodes at $5.2 \times 10^{-9} L$), DrivAerML Volume 0 against 0.57%, AeroZoo
  0.01% as it stands, the lug and Tensile2d none. On AirfRANS the knee sits at $U d / \nu = 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{Re}_L$ = 610
  to 1,830, $y^+$ about 25 to 90 with an estimated friction velocity: the sublayer, the buffer layer and the start of the
  log layer.
- **Response** (the standings' trained checkpoints at fixed weights). The input layers code $\log d$: their change per
  decade of $d$ is flat over five decades (about 15 on AirfRANS, 17 on DrivAerML). Read with the whole boundary's $L$, a
  tenfold change at AirfRANS's first nodes moves the input layer 38 times less and the embedding's sensitivity per unit
  $\ln d$ 200 times less. Only a retrain prices it (AF-WHOLE).
- **Precision.** $10^{-6}$ is about 17 times float32's unit roundoff: rounding moves the channel by at most 0.12 wherever
  the body sits in its domain. A softening that gives AirfRANS's first nodes a logarithmic code moves by up to 3 to 4 when
  the body sits 30 chords from the origin, mostly through the kernel's closest point formed in absolute coordinates
  (GEOMETRY_NOTE.md).

**The design** (DESIGN.md section 4). Of eight candidates, the lane recommends keeping the channel: it is the one defined
identically on every dataset, with no fallback, no new declaration and no recipe constant, and robust to rounding
anywhere in the domain; the viscous softening $\operatorname{asinh}(d U / \nu)$ is undefined on three of five datasets
and changes every AeroZoo case. Its documentation claimed that $10^{-6} L$ lies below the reference datasets' finest wall
spacing, which is false under the whole boundary. **The supervisor approved the design at 08:43 EDT**: canonical ISLA keeps
its channel, the docstring is corrected on psharpe/isla-nearwall, and the viscous softening is held ready, to be tested
only if AF-WHOLE reads a near-wall harm, with its adoption Peter's. Lane predictions: a harm on velocity or eddy viscosity
in AF-WHOLE 0.40; given one, mainly near the wall 0.45.

**For the book.** 05 states the softening as a precision margin with its consequence; 03 no longer says the boundary
layer is resolved over many decades; 20 adds the near-wall question with the held alternative and an In-flight callout
(@sec-oq-nearwall).

Cost: 1.0 of 6 GPU-h (six GB300 short jobs, 367460 to 367749).

edge points), taken when the two distances differ by more than one unit of $u_{64}(\lvert x \rvert + R_k)$. The
reference and the fast path stay bitwise equal.

## 2026-10-24 — DTT-FAST BF16-DIAG: the chunked step's bfloat16 excess on AirfRANS comes from an unpadded boundary side under PyTorch's default reduced-precision bfloat16 reduction, and padding it as the merged forward pads removes it; bfloat16 equivalence is judged against a one-ulp family of at least seven {#sec-nb-dtt-fast-bf16}

**Question.** DTT-FAST's pass-2 table (14, the DTT-FAST row) left open why ISLA-DTT's query-chunked training step, in
bfloat16, sat farther from float64 than the unchunked step on AirfRANS. Piece BF16-DIAG of DTT-FAST measured it on LHR.
Records: scratch/isla-dtt-fast-2026-10-23/bf16diag/REPORT.md (md5 0cba3be8) and RESULTS.md (8a8ad8b4); copies in
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/dtt_fast_bf16diag/.

**The cause.** The chunked step runs the boundary side on the boundary tokens alone: 1,017 on AirfRANS, an odd count.
At that count, under PyTorch's default `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = True`,
cuBLASLt computes the slice anchors ($z_s$ and $m_s$ of every block, and the frame's anchors) with split-K partial sums
rounded to bfloat16: 25 such kernels per step (2 per block for 12 blocks, plus the frame's), against none in the
unchunked step at 3,017 tokens (profiler, 367990). Running the chunked step on the unchunked token tensor reproduces the
reference's loss bitwise, and dropping the leaves changes nothing, so the chunking itself is exact.

**How it shows.** Over 14 one-ulp parameter samples at 2,000 points, 6 chunked runs land at 2.1 to 6.8 times the
reference's bfloat16 block error, and no reference run above 1.00 times; at all 180,593 points, 1 of 5 lands at 6.1.
The tail sits in the geometry and routing weights of blocks 0 to 3. On DrivAerML's whole boundary, whose 200,000
boundary tokens are already a multiple of 32, every chunked sample lies inside the reference's own one-ulp spread, which
reaches 6.6 times on the loss (mse) and 3.35 times on the blocks.

**The remedy.** Padding `_QueryChunks`' boundary side to a multiple of 32 as psharpe/isla 1b25eb899's `forward` pads
(`_pad_tokens`), prototyped as a patch: on AirfRANS the blocks sit at 0.74 to 1.01 times the reference over 14 samples at
2,000 points and 0.73 to 0.98 over 5 at all points; DrivAerML and the lug are unchanged; peak memory rises 3 MB and the
step time does not change; the ISLA test directory passes (398 passed, 0 failed; 368050). DTT-FAST's integration pass 3
applies it. Turning `allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction` off also removes the tail (0.92 to 1.00 times). The lane's
open risk: padding only steers cuBLAS's choice of kernel by shape, so another token count could meet a reduction with
bfloat16 partial sums again; only the setting rules that out everywhere.

**The yardstick.** The supervisor's rule, now in LANE_RULES ("bf16 equivalence"): a change's bfloat16 numerics are
judged against a family of at least 7 one-ulp perturbations of the reference (inputs or parameters), and per tensor group
the changed path's distance to float64 must lie inside that family's range. One reference run is not a yardstick: on
DrivAerML Volume the reference's own one-ulp spread reached 6.6 times on the loss and 3.35 times on the blocks.

**The setting.** Whether to turn PyTorch's reduced-precision bfloat16 reduction off for the final rerun is the
supervisor's question for the scope freeze. The setting is program-wide and changes the reference's bfloat16 numerics at
some shapes, so a timed benchmark measures it first.

**For the book.** No chapter changes: the chunked step is on an unmerged branch, and every chapter cost stays the merged
code's. 14's DTT-FAST row carries the progress.

Cost: 2.22 of 4 GPU-h (GB300 short jobs 367557, 367780, 367888, 367990 and 368049) and seven cpu-short jobs.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-24 (scratch/isla-book-geothin-2026-10-24/SECOND_READ_GEOTHIN.md).*

## 2026-10-24 — Verdict, LRE-AZ: on AeroZoo's Reynolds split the fixed Reynolds scale z = log10(Re / 1e6) costs ISLA 13 % on velocity, growing to 1.28× 1.5 to 2 decades above the band, so it does not carry over from AirfRANS, and ISLA keeps its fitted constants {#sec-nb-az-lre-verdict}

**Setting.** On AirfRANS's `reynolds` split, training ISLA 0.9.0 with its Reynolds input on a fixed physical scale,
z = log10(Re_ISLA / 1e6), instead of the per-split fitted z = (log10 Re_ISLA − m) / s, cut its below-band pressure error to
0.53-0.58× (@sec-nb-af-lre-verdict). There the fitted spread was 0.062 decades. The program counts a result once it holds on
two datasets, and adopting the scale would change a reference default. So LRE-AZ ran the same control on AeroZoo's `reynolds`
split, whose fitted constants are m = 5.062, s = 0.8985. The test was registered as a harm check, because there the fixed
scale only rescales z by 0.90 and shifts it by −0.94 (scratch/isla-lre-az-2026-10-23/PREREG.md, approved 2026-10-23 01:37
EDT; @sec-nb-lre-az-prereg).

The split trains on label Re 10^3-10^6 (2,119 cases) and tests on 10^6-10^8 (1,385 cases, 0.002-2.0 decades above the band).
By ISLA's own Re, which uses its length unit, 414 test cases lie inside the training band and 971 above it. Arms: A is the
standing `azc_reynolds_isla_seed4x` (fitted z, reused). B is the same snapshot and resolved config with only the dataset file
`aerozoo_uvolume_reynolds_lre.yaml` (`isla_constants.reynolds {6, 1}`), trained from scratch: two seeds, 250 epochs, bf16,
scored float32 on the native protocol by AZ-DECIDE's scorer. Every score row's dataset file and checkpoint were checked to
carry {6, 1} for B and {5.062, 0.8985} for A. No event-guard hit.

**What we saw.**

| field | A, fitted scale (s42, s43) | B, fixed scale (s42, s43) | B ÷ A | 2 SE | registered verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pressure | 0.506, 0.512 | 0.516, 0.570 | 1.067 | 0.100 | no change |
| velocity | 0.161, 0.168 | 0.183, 0.187 | 1.126 | 0.046 | **harms** |
| ν_t (beside) | 0.819, 0.887 | 0.677, 0.744 | 0.833 | 0.123 | helps |
| k, ω (beside) | | | 1.004, 1.001 | | no change |

: AeroZoo `reynolds` test set (1,385 cases), case-mean relative L2, float32. B ÷ A is the ratio of seed means. {#tbl-nb-az-lre}

- B ÷ A by distance above the band, for 0-0.5, 0.5-1, 1-1.5 and 1.5-2 decades: velocity 1.01, 1.05, 1.19, 1.28; pressure
  1.01, 1.04, 1.11, 1.10; ν_t 1.01, 0.95, 0.84, 0.74. The rise holds on both seeds.
- Inside ISLA's own training band the two scales agree (pressure 1.015, velocity 1.007). Above it, the ratios are 1.081 and
  1.169.
- The medians move less (velocity 1.068, pressure 1.080, ν_t 1.03, all "no change"), so the cost sits in the far-out,
  higher-error cases.

**Reading.** The registered consequence of "harms" on velocity is that the fixed scale is not adopted without Peter; it
is not adopted, and ISLA keeps its per-split fitted constants. The AirfRANS gain does not carry over. With a wide fitted spread the fixed scale changes
nothing inside the band, but it makes ISLA extrapolate worse on velocity, and somewhat on pressure, one to two decades
beyond it. How far z overshoots its training range does not explain this: the fixed z overshoots by up to 2.09 units, the
fitted one by 2.33. The mechanism is untested. Two seeds per arm, one training configuration. Not tested, each needing a
new registration: a fixed scale whose spread suits every dataset, or the fixed scale with an inference clamp of z. Records:
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/lre_az/ (lreaz.json, tables.md, posthoc.md, RESULTS.md, PREREG.md); reduction reduce_lreaz.py.
Cost about 193 GPU-h (registered about 188, budget 300).

## 2026-10-24 — KERNEL-TESTS: the five CUDA tests that failed after the token padding failed on the tests' premise, not on a code defect; the fix gives the compiled blocks their unaligned token counts again and checks the count they receive; every CUDA test passes on a GB300 (526 passed, 1 skipped), merged as eba038f08 {#sec-nb-kernel-tests}

**What failed.** The token padding (1b25eb899; @sec-nb-align8-merged) merged with 5 failing CUDA tests in
`test_isla_kernels.py`, because no lane ran that file on a GPU. Each failed on its forced-on positive control,
`assert err > 5e-6`: `test_compile_blocks_float32_matches_eager_at_every_token_count` at n = 12001, 12002 and 12003
(err 2.68e-7, 2.72e-7, 2.67e-7) and `test_compile_blocks_query_independent_float32_at_every_token_count` at nq = 6001
and 6002 (1.82e-7, 1.86e-7).

**The cause, in the tests' premise.** GB300 job 368568 ran the whole ISLA test directory with every CUDA test on four
code versions, one per GPU and one version per process. The same 5 fail at the head 921472488 and at 1b25eb899 with the
same message, and all 469 pass at 7213c70c5, before the padding; the test file is identical at 7213c70c5 and 1b25eb899
(md5 fd8e36ff). The padding hides the unaligned count the tests rely on: the compiled blocks see 12032 tokens, a multiple
of the 4-row tile, so forcing mix-order reduction on does no harm there, and the positive control finds no error to
detect. The fixed-path assertions (the compiled blocks match eager and build no mix-order kernel) passed throughout.

**The fix** (396459aec, the test file only, +54 −3; no test deleted).
- Both guards set `TOKEN_ALIGNMENT` to 1 by monkeypatch, as `test_isla_token_padding.py` already does for its unpadded
  reference, so the forward's padding does nothing and the compiled blocks receive the unaligned count. A recorder around
  `_block_callables()` asserts the count they receive.
- Both original assertions stay, with unchanged tolerances.
- A new test, `test_compile_blocks_see_an_aligned_token_count` (surface and ISLA-DTT, CPU and CUDA), checks that in a padded
  forward 301 cells, and 301 cells plus 7 queries, reach the compiled blocks as 320 tokens.

**Tests.** GB300, every CUDA test: 526 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (the head had 522 tests; the skip is the opt-in
`ISLA_AF_POSED_SAMPLE` data test, the same in all four versions). CPU (LHR cpu-short 368574): 397 passed, 122 skipped,
0 failed. 2.02 GPU-h against a cap of 3. Merged into psharpe/isla as eba038f08.

**The rule that follows** (the supervisor's, 2026-10-24): on CPU the CUDA tests skip, so before a branch that changes
`physicsnemo/` or `test/` is called ready to merge, the whole ISLA test directory also runs on a GB300 with every CUDA
test, not a chosen set of files, in one short-QoS job with the five bad nodes excluded and a guard of about 60 minutes.
Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/kernel_tests/ (FINAL_REPORT.md, RESULTS.md).

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-24 (scratch/isla-book-az-2026-10-24/SECOND_READ_AZ.md).*

## 2026-10-24 — SLICES-DRV: on DrivAerML Volume, ISLA 0.9.0 with 128 slices reads "no change" against the 512-slice standing on every field (1.002 / 0.995 / 0.999), at 0.63 of the step and 0.83 of the memory; 128 slices now reads no harm on two datasets {#sec-nb-slices-drv}

**Question.** SLICES-AF found 128 slices no different from 512 on full AirfRANS at 0.42 of the step (@sec-nb-slices-af):
a cost result on one dataset, which needs a no-harm check on a second before the scope freeze. DrivAerML Volume is where
fewer slices would most likely harm: far points own slices from block 4 on, and ISLA's eddy-viscosity excess sits in the
far field (@sec-single-case-floor). Does 128 slices harm ISLA there?

**Design (pre-registered, PREREG md5 88e36cd7, with the supervisor's amendment before submission).** ISLA 0.9.0 at the
DrivAerML Volume standing's configuration (body only, code and compile path of the standing) with `n_slices=128` the
only change, two seeds, against the standing's two runs. Scored as the standing: the 48 validation cars, float32, native
(decides), posed beside, area degenerate. Rule per field (SLICES-AF's): harms if D = ln(S ÷ B) > ln 1.10 and |D| > 2 SE.
On this dataset 2 SE is 0.013-0.022, so the ln 1.10 bar binds; the amendment added that a seed-separated shift above 1.03
(both 128-slice seeds above both 512-slice seeds) also keeps 512. Guards: the geometry kernel resolved to the fused path
on every rank; a block-wise compiled-against-eager check of the 128-slice graph passed at 5e-7 (bar 1e-5) before any
lane; an eager re-score agreed with the compiled scores to 6e-6.

**Result: no change on every field, no flag.** 128-slice ÷ 512-slice ISLA, seed means of case-mean relative L2: pressure
1.002 (0.038466 against 0.038377; seed-matched 1.013 and 0.992), velocity 0.995 (1.001, 0.988), eddy viscosity 0.999
(0.999, 0.999). Posed reads the same. The 128-slice seeds lie inside the 512-slice seed range on pressure and below its
mean on velocity. By wall distance, nothing moves: beyond 5 m from the car the eddy-viscosity error is 1.003 / 1.001
times the standing's, seed-matched, and velocity stays within 0.97-1.04 in every decade from below 0.5 mm to beyond 5 m.

**Cost.** On the same GB300 node the 128-slice step is 0.625 of the standing's (0.403 against 0.645 s) and its peak
allocated memory 0.832 (107.1 against 128.6 GiB); over the whole run 0.67 of the step and 28.7 against 40.4-40.9 GPU-h per
lane. DrivAerML Volume runs the fused geometry kernel, which never builds the per-token, per-slice tensors, so it saves
less than AirfRANS on the unfused path (0.42 / 0.78).

**Consequence.** By the registered decision use, 128 slices is a candidate for the scope freeze on two datasets
(AirfRANS and DrivAerML Volume): no field harmed, no seed-separated shift. Whether the reference changes is the
supervisor's decision at the freeze. ISLA-DTT, the surface task and solid mechanics were not run at 128 slices; SLICES-ALL
checks ISLA-DTT on AirfRANS and the lug and the interacting surface form on DrivAerML Surface, and decides at the freeze
whether 128 slices holds for every form. Beside: on full data at 512 slices the 0.7 % of points beyond 5 m hold 46-47 % of
ISLA's eddy-viscosity squared error (about 27 % of the squared target), as CAP-AUDIT found on one case; the slice count
does not move it.

Predictions: no change on pressure (0.90), velocity (0.90) and eddy viscosity (0.87) held, no harm on all three (0.82)
held; the sub-bar flag (0.30) did not fire; the step ratio in 0.55-0.80 (0.60) and memory in 0.80-0.95 (0.55) held.
Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/slices_drv/ (RESULTS.md, reading.md, PREREG.md, farfield/farfield_table.md). Cost
about 60 GPU-h.

## 2026-10-24 — BC-SUPPLY: canonical ISLA reads SHIFT-SUV's CFD box and HiLiftAeroML's inlet and outlet, both built by recipe transforms at load, beside the vehicle and the deduplicated wing; the built far field equals the stored one bit for bit; the baselines' inputs are bitwise unchanged; HiLiftAeroML's symmetry plane stays out; merged with this batch {#sec-nb-bc-supply}

**What was asked.** Peter, asked whether SHIFT-SUV's CFD box and HiLiftAeroML's far field without its symmetry plane may
be added in the recipe, answered at 10:21 EDT: "Yes, of course you can do that" (@sec-nb-supply-approved). Lane BC-SUPPLY
built both into canonical ISLA, on psharpe/isla-bc-supply (head 0a706b148, which contains eba038f08). It changes only the
unified recipe; it touches neither `physicsnemo/` nor `test/`.

**HiLiftAeroML's far field, a load-time transform (the supervisor's decision at 10:42 EDT).** The brief asked for
per-case sidecar files. The lane found that curator's generator builds the inlet and the outlet from four inputs alone,
the radius, `n_theta`, `n_phi` and the freestream `U_inf`, and that the 1,800 cases store 10 distinct `U_inf` vectors, bit
for bit, one per angle of attack, so 690 sidecars would have held 10 distinct far fields. On the lane's question the
supervisor approved a recipe transform instead, with eight conditions, all met.
- `AddHemisphereBoundaries` (`src/domain_transforms.py`) copies curator's `build_hemisphere` and `split_by_freestream` with
  their arithmetic and tie rule unchanged, and names the source file and commit; curator is not imported. It is the first
  transform of `highlift_surface.yaml`, in raw inches: radius 24,533.41796875 in (88.95 mean aerodynamic chords), `n_theta`
  64, `n_phi` 32, split by each case's stored `U_inf`. It needs no file, fingerprint or manifest.
- BC-SIDECAR's scaffolds (its reader option, its `_whole` dataset and model files, their path entry and tests) are removed.
- `isla_surface_highlift` reads the deduplicated wing (HL-DUP's reader; @sec-nb-hl-dup), `inlet` and `outlet`, predicts at
  the wing, and reverses the wing's winding for ISLA alone, since the wing is wound into the body on 6 of 6 deduplicated
  cases checked. The symmetry plane is absent: the stored roots are open on every geometry but LHC001, and a rebuild of the
  root outline from the stored vertices is being prototyped.

**SHIFT-SUV's box.** `AddBoxBoundaries`, the first transform of the five SHIFT-SUV dataset files, builds the inlet, the
outlet, the floor, the side walls and the roof from constants on each case before any pose or centering (@sec-nb-bc-sidecar).
`isla_surface_shift_suv` reads them beside the vehicle, named by role with no claimed condition type, since the dataset
documents none, and predicts at the vehicle. The stored vehicle is wound into the fluid, as the box is, so nothing is
flipped.

**Checks.**
- The built far field against the stored one (job 368914): on LHC001_AoA_10 and _12, in the full dataset and the -medium
  copy (8 meshes), the built inlet and outlet equal the stored ones bit for bit, 1,024 points and 1,952 cells each, as
  sorted points and as oriented cells; only the order differs, since the stored order is curator's permutation.
- Against curator's own code, run on the same node: for each of the 10 `U_inf` vectors, bit for bit and in order (20 of
  20). The census puts every one of the 1,800 full-dataset and 690 -medium cases on one of those 10 vectors.
- The radius: on the 13 stored interiors that hold points, the extent along ±x and ±z equals 24,533.41796875 to the bit;
  between those axes the CFD far field's own nodes reach 1.0188 times it (90.6 chords).
- The pieces move with the body (job 369235, 0 failures): fitting one similarity from the raw to the output box maps it to
  within 2.9e-6, and the raw vehicle to within 3.0e-7, where the box spans about 16, on all 5 SHIFT-SUV files with augment
  off and on and rotations up to 170°; the far field to within 1.4e-5 and the wing to within 3.9e-6 on HiLiftAeroML.
- The baselines (job 368882): GeoTransolver's and Transolver's collated inputs and targets are bitwise unchanged on 60 of
  60 items with the box (5 files × 3 cases × both models, augment off and on) and on 24 of 24 with the far field.
- Tests on the merged head 0a706b148: the whole ISLA test directory on CPU, 397 passed, 122 skipped, 0 failed; on a GB300
  with every CUDA test, 526 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed; the recipe tests, 579 passed, 12 skipped (all CUDA), 2 failed,
  `test_campaign_c_hooks`' `initialize_slurm` errors, which occur only inside a Slurm job and fail with the base's message.
  The three real-data far-field tests ran and passed.

**Cost.** The box takes 1.9-2.1 ms per load and adds 4,332 cells (722 each for the inlet, outlet, floor and roof, 1,444
for the side walls); the far field takes 3.5 ms per load and adds 3,904 (1,952 each). In a 20-step GB300 smoke, ISLA's
SHIFT-SUV step was 217 ms reading the box against 169 ms on the vehicle alone, but the smoke ran beside other jobs' data
loaders, so the ratio may include loading. The HiLiftAeroML smoke step times measure data loading, not the model.

**What it changes.** Canonical ISLA reads the whole stored or built boundary on all nine tasks, HiLiftAeroML's symmetry
plane aside. SHIFT-SUV's and HiLiftAeroML's standings were trained reading the body alone, and the final reference rerun
retrains them with these pieces. Merged into this book batch as eb5a9c92f. Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/bc_supply/
(REPORT.md, FINAL_REPORT.md, book/BOOK_CHANGES.md, out/hl_val_368914.jsonl, out/move_369235.jsonl, gb/smoke_summary.txt).

## 2026-10-24 — GEO-BAND: the exact geometry's tie and on-wall bands rest on derived worst cases (C = 91 in 3-D and 17 in 2-D, K = 168, the 1-unit switch certified), its storage term stays in the frame the inputs were given in, its arithmetic runs in the boundary's centered frame, a tie needs certified-distinct directions; no sign or on-wall decision changes, posed lug tie flips fall from 90,221 to 25, no retrain; merged with this batch as ISLA 0.12.0 {#sec-nb-geo-band}

**What it did.** GEO-BAND made the exact query geometry's tie and on-wall decisions rest on derived worst cases and freed
its arithmetic from the boundary's position. The change is psharpe/isla-geo-band 9e0d52e27, merged with psharpe/isla
eba038f08 as 2e9cd7fda; BAND-MERGE added the version commit 3f3fef69f (ISLA 0.12.0, @sec-nb-version-0120). It merges into
psharpe/isla with this book batch.

**The rule (the supervisor's approval at 11:24 EDT, the lane's variant VF), one rule with no flag.**
- The band is E_k = u (|x| + R_k) + C u64 (|x'| + R'_k). The first term is the inputs' storage rounding, measured in the
  frame they were given in: a case placed far from the origin is rounded more coarsely, so a storage term measured about
  the centroid is not a bound. GEO-THIN had seen it fail on lug case 1909, and the lane confirmed why: with the vertex term
  measured about the centroid, exactly medial nodes see a re-rounding gap the band no longer covers, and 170 lug nodes
  over the 20 dump cases take |du| = 1 posed.
- The second term is the float64 arithmetic's, measured in the frame centered on c, the measure-weighted centroid of the
  distinct cells, computed from exact int64 fixed-point sums, so a function of the set of cells, not of their order, and
  rounded to the queries' precision, so float32 inputs center exactly.
- C = 91 in 3-D and 17 in 2-D, a worst case (the first-order 13 and 10 before). The greatest path is a guarded pair that
  keeps Ericson's point, within the 1-unit switch of the accurate point, whose worst case is 87 units at a face that
  rounding rejects (GEO-THIN's first-order count was 77; the lane's first draft 88): 88, plus 1 for the centering and 2 for
  the second-order terms and the band's own evaluation. K = 168 holds as a worst case (second-order terms 3e-15
  relative). The switch needs no bound of its own: any threshold tau is certified once C >= tau + 88.
- Each bound is derived (DERIVATION.md, version 2) and was re-derived independently by a reviewer child
  (REVIEW_DERIVATION.md), whose corrections are applied to the derivation and the code's comments. One disagreement is
  recorded: the 2-D brute-force prefilter's margin for float64 queries, 33.5 units by the reviewer's count against the 32
  the code allows; the lane counts its err_max as already covering it. Either way it changes only candidates, never an
  output, since a wider prefilter adds only candidates beyond the band.
- A tie needs two certified-distinct directions: farther apart than the sum of their bounds tau = sqrt(2) s (2 where s
  >= 1), s a bound on the sine of each computed direction's error.
- The offset x - p is formed in float64 and rounded once to the queries' precision.
- The reference and the fast search stay bitwise equal: the branch matches variant VF bitwise in 106 of 106 runs, on every
  op output, d, u and both gradients (job 369316), and the fast path differs from the reference at 0 of 588,689 queries.

**What it changes** (float32 unless named; the recipe's draws of the DrivAerML Volume task's whole boundary, AirfRANS with
its far field, AeroZoo, the 20 lug cases and Tensile2d).
- Natively: no winding sign and no on-wall decision changes on any dataset. Distances move at rounding level, at most 0.7
  percent at AirfRANS's first nodes, where the old float32 cancellation was that large. Directions move at ties: up to
  6.5e-3 at 7,932 of 400,000 DrivAerML points, 1.6e-5 on the lug, not at all on Tensile2d.
- Rotated and translated by one RMS radius of the boundary: tie-membership flips fall from 90,221 to 25 on the lug and
  from 231 to 0 on Tensile2d. DrivAerML's band-edge flips (3,706 points of 400,000 move u by more than 1e-3, against
  3,000 at 921472488) each lie within their certified direction uncertainty (the supervisor at 11:24: state this
  wherever the numbers appear).
- NEARWALL's compute rounding far from the origin falls to 1.9e-7 at the 99.9th percentile (DrivAerML whole boundary
  translated by L, softening 1e-9 L; 0.0156 at 921472488). Its input part stays: on AirfRANS at 30 chords, queries within
  the float32 storage rounding of the wall are on it.
- Lug case 1884's node 6997 remains a band-edge node, answered correctly for its own inputs in each pose (excess
  1.74e-5).
- The irreducible limit: a case's float32 storage rounding grows with its distance from the origin, so band-edge nodes
  can still flip under translation. The extreme is AirfRANS with its far field translated by one boundary RMS radius:
  16,077 of the 400,000 drawn points, all near the wall, become on-wall, whatever the frame of the arithmetic.
- Trained models (the pre-registered, gated check, INFER_CHECK.md, job 369317): TIE-EXP's four checkpoints (ISLA with the
  class's tie rule on the lug and Tensile2d, two seeds each) read through the new geometry reproduce 36 of 36 registered
  summaries on the old one, and move by at most 2.96e-5 in log(N / O) and 4.4e-5 in posed ÷ native, against limits of
  0.01. Criterion met: no retrain. Beside it, not gated: AF-WHOLE's seed 42 (epoch 197) and FLOOR-DRV's fdF seed 42
  (step 2000), both trained with 0.9.0's geometry, read N / O within 0.99990 to 1.00014.
- Cost on the DrivAerML whole-boundary geometry call (GB300, median of five after three warm-up, two draws): +13 ms (2.8
  percent) under the reference search, +14 ms (3.5 percent) under the fast one.

**Tests.** GEO-BAND, on 2e9cd7fda: the ISLA test directory on a GB300 with every CUDA test, 548 passed, 1 skipped, 0
failed (369573); on CPU, 409 passed (369574). BAND-MERGE, on 3f3fef69f: GB300 550 passed, 1 skipped (369879), CPU 411
passed (369880), the recipe tests 551 passed and 2 failed (`test_campaign_c_hooks`, the base's E line; 369988). The golden
checkpoint regenerates bitwise in its 59 tensors; of the six changed test lines none weakens a test (REVIEW_TESTS.md).

**Open, not explained.** On the lug with float64 queries posed in float64, 12 to 49 nodes per 20 cases change u by 1 under
every variant (float32: 0). It is not the recipe's precision and was not chased. The fused kernel for the thin-cell path
(the lane's phase D) did not fit its cap; GEO-THINFAST builds it.

**For the book.** 05 states the band, its two frames, the derived constants with the one recorded disagreement, the
certified tie test, the float64 offset, what they change, and the remaining band-edge limit in place of the medial one; 06
gives the refused versions through 0.11.0 and the bands' cost beside its cost table, not re-timed; 20 loses the derived-bands
question (`sec-oq-ties`) and its In-flight callout, states the band-edge limit in its tie section, and gives the near-wall
alternative's rounding without the arithmetic's share; 21 states the certified decisions. Three references of older entries
to `sec-oq-ties` point at 05's geometry section instead, their text unchanged. Records:
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_band_final/ (FINAL_REPORT.md, RESULTS.md, DERIVATION.md, INFER_CHECK.md,
REVIEW_DERIVATION.md, DESIGN.md) and results/campaigns_2026-10-23/band_merge/ (FINAL_REPORT.md, REVIEW_TESTS.md).

## 2026-10-24 — DEFAULT-DTT: ISLA-DTT is the class's and the recipe's default interior form; `query_independent=None` resolves to the task, every interior configuration trains ISLA-DTT compiled per block, and ISLA-DTT's outputs at shared points stay at roundoff when other points join a request; integrated with ISLA 0.12.0 and merged with this batch {#sec-nb-default-dtt}

**What it did.** AZ-DECIDE read AeroZoo's registered test of the two interior forms as a close call, and Peter's
ruling of 2026-10-23 for that case is "ISLA-DTT, on principle" (@sec-nb-az-decide). DEFAULT-DTT put the ruling into the
code on psharpe/isla-default-dtt: 9d27ae47b (the model's default and docstrings), b0fd82da8 (the recipe's interior
configurations and README) and e1a6d7853 (the tests and two fixtures), merged with psharpe/isla 0d46b2f9b as e10681b33.
DTT-DEFAULT-INT then merged GEO-BAND into the branch (616992605) and reworked one test for ISLA 0.12.0 (f9b0014c8). The
branch merges into psharpe/isla with this book batch.

**The supervisor's design decisions.**
- `query_independent` defaults to `None`, which resolves to the task: ISLA-DTT on the interior task, interacting ISLA on
  the surface task. An explicit `True` on the surface task is still refused.
- An explicit `query_independent=False` builds interacting ISLA on an interior task.
- The class writes the resolved value into its stored arguments, so a checkpoint carries its form and never depends on
  the default.
- The switch itself changes no version.
- Every interior recipe configuration (`isla_volume`, `isla_volume_aerozoo`, `isla_volume_airfrans`, `isla_lug`,
  `isla_tensile2d`) states `query_independent: true` and trains with per-block compile (`compile: false`,
  `compile_blocks: true`), because ISLA-DTT's boundary read breaks the whole-model graph. The surface configurations keep
  the whole-model compile.

**Tests.** Interacting ISLA's tests now pass `query_independent=False` explicitly. New tests: a state dict of one interior
form is refused by a model of the other, in both directions and on every loading path; new interior checkpoints store
their form; every interior recipe configuration runs ISLA-DTT compiled per block. The assertion audit removed no message
or match string and weakened no tolerance; no golden was regenerated. On e10681b33: the ISLA test directory, 401 passed
and 122 skipped on CPU (job 369930), 531 passed and 1 skipped on a GB300 with every CUDA test (369933); the recipe tests,
585 passed, 15 skipped and 2 failed (370095), the two `test_campaign_c_hooks` tests that fail at the base with the same
message inside a Slurm job.

**The integration with ISLA 0.12.0 (DTT-DEFAULT-INT).** DEFAULT-DTT's first head carried a fixture of an interior
checkpoint written before the switch, on 0.11.0, and a test that it loaded as interacting ISLA. 0.12.0 refuses every

compatible with current version 0.12.0"), which two existing refusal tests already cover. DTT-DEFAULT-INT deleted the
