## 2026-10-24 — GEO-THINFAST: the thin-cell guard and the accurate closest point fused into the fast search's Triton kernels, bitwise equal to the reference over 16.5 million queries; the lug's fast geometry call falls from 74.1 to 37.6 ms, and the fast search beats the reference by 22 to 55 percent on every three-dimensional case; the 2-D prefilter margin widened to 40 units; merged with this batch {#sec-nb-geo-thinfast}

**Why.** GEO-THIN's bounds for thin cells made the exact geometry correct on thin cells, but their guard and accurate
closest point ran as about a hundred small torch launches, twice per call. On the lug, where a third of the candidate
pairs are guarded, the fast search had become no faster than the reference (@sec-nb-geo-band). Peter's ruling on the
geometry's cost (2026-10-23): "Correctness is most important; correct + fast is even better. If the speedup experiment
works, then add an optional fast path (like our other kernels, where we default iff triton is installed), and then remove
the documented limitation / change it."

**What was built** (psharpe/isla-geo-thinfast at b959a6735, which contains psharpe/isla b66013630 and GEO-BAND's
3f3fef69f). The fast search computes the whole closest-weights step of triangles (Ericson's weights, the edge
recomputation, the thin-cell guard and the zero-area segments) in one Triton kernel over the pairs, and the accurate
point with its switch in a second kernel over the guarded pairs alone, listed by the first without a host
synchronization. Each float64 operation is written in the form and order that torch's CUDA kernels use, measured on the
GB300 first (jobs 369877, 369899, 369906): a sum of three over the last axis is ((x0 + x2) + x1) + 0, a norm the root of
((x0^2 + x2^2) + x1^2) with no fma, a cross product's component an fma, and a scalar divided by a tensor the tensor's
reciprocal times the scalar. The kernels are launched without contraction, and a negation is written as a product with
-1, since Triton's unary minus is 0 - x and loses the sign of zero. The reference stays the torch code, unchanged. The
kernels run only in the fast search, on CUDA with Triton and contiguous inputs, a choice made from the inputs' metadata
before the launch. The same branch widened the two-dimensional brute force's prefilter margin for float64 points from
32 to 40 units, which covers both counts of GEO-BAND's derivations (32 and the reviewer's 33.5), and pinned the band
units to {2: 17, 3: 91} in a test.

**Review.** A lane reviewer, at d42fc83d5, blocked the merge on one P0: a column-major query tensor gave wrong weights
or an IndexError on the fused path. It also found int32 row offsets that overflow beyond about 238 million pairs. Both
are fixed and tested in 1730022cb: the fused path runs only on contiguous inputs, and the offsets are int64. A
pre-existing quirk stays: the reference's own outputs differ at roundoff between contiguous and column-major queries, so
"bitwise for every input" holds per layout.

**Result: bitwise equal to the reference.** In integer views, on every op output, the distance, the direction and both
gradients, in float32 and float64, forced fast and under auto (job 370582): 0 differences over 1,240 runs and 16,527,248
queries (every GEO-THIN and GEO-BAND dump, native, posed and with column-major queries, the adversarial AeroZoo sets and
GEO-THIN's 88 adversarial thin-cell sets), 0 of 46,538,000 candidate pairs' weights, 0 of 673,850 queries in the forced
plug-in check over the ISLA test directory, and 0 over 298 runs of the margin change against psharpe/isla's geometry,
each version in its own process.

**Timing** (job 370584, GEO-BAND's phase-0 protocol: GB300, bfloat16, eager, the median after five warm-up calls or
steps, the arms interleaved and the GPUs rotated; the mean of the passes, three for each fast arm and two for the
reference). The fast geometry call, before and after the fusion, with the reference beside it: lug 74.1 to 37.6 ms
(reference 83.5), AeroZoo 113.7 to 92.8 (135.9), DrivAerML vehicle 384.4 to 345.2 (450.4), DrivAerML whole boundary
436.1 to 403.3 (514.3); AirfRANS, in two dimensions, does not use the kernels (31.7 to 31.6, reference 33.2). The lug's
step falls from 204 to 166 ms. The lug's fast call is back at its value before the bounds for thin cells, 36.7 ms; on
DrivAerML the fusion takes 33 to 39 ms off the call, and what remains of the bounds' cost there is their test in the ball
search. Peak memory is unchanged.

**Tests.** The ISLA test directory on a GB300 with every CUDA test (370582): 620 passed, 1 skipped (environment-gated), 0
failed. Under the forced plug-in, 605 passed and 1 failed, a recompile guard on the plug-in's own counter, which passes
under auto in the same job. On CPU (370585): 413 passed, 200 skipped, 0 failed. GPU use 4.26 of the 6 GPU-h cap.

**The supervisor's decision.** No version change: the branch changes no output, gradient or state dict.

**For the book.** 06's geometry cost table takes the class's columns from this timing, with the derived bands included,
and keeps the standings' 0.9.0 column from GEO-BAND's phase 0, another job on another node. Its paragraphs say that the
fast search cuts the geometry call by 22 to 55 percent on every three-dimensional case and that the fused kernels take
the thin-cell cost back on the lug. 06's In-flight callout on the fused kernel is gone. As Peter's ruling asks, the
documented limitation, a fast search no faster than the reference on the lug, is gone from the chapters, and the cost on
DrivAerML is given at the new numbers. 05 states the prefilter margin of 40 units, which covers both counts. 20's
whole-boundary geometry call reads the same table. Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_thinfast/ (FINAL_REPORT.md,
RESULTS.md, REVIEW.md, lhr/timing_table.md).

## 2026-10-24 — DTT-FAST, done: ISLA-DTT's read made exact and fast on the GPU (a Warp forest build and walk, a searchsorted pair plan, a fused Triton read and basis with faster backward passes, and query-chunked training under a size rule); on GB300 its training step is 1.6 to 1.8 times faster than the reference read's on DrivAerML and AeroZoo at 0.7 to 0.8 times its peak memory, and it trains 400,000 points and up to 12.8 million on DrivAerML; the same function, the same version (0.12.0) and the same state dict; merged with this batch {#sec-nb-dtt-fast-final}

**Why.** Peter's ruling on the surface task (2026-10-23, 23:26 EDT): "You can do A for now, but then revisit ISLA-DTT
after the kernel speedups / memory savings land. If we can make ISLA-DTT practical in the long term, that would be
awesome." With ISLA-DTT the default interior form (@sec-nb-default-dtt), its read set the cost of every interior lane
of the final rerun. DTT-FAST, launched by the supervisor at 23:33 EDT 2026-10-23 with a cap of 80 GPU-h and a rule that
each piece be equivalent to the exact read before its speed counts, ended at 18:35 EDT 2026-10-24 with about 81 of 88
GPU-h used (the cap raised during the run).

**The pieces** (psharpe/isla-dtt-fast at 4d281a702, which contains psharpe/isla b4b10d5a9; each piece verified or
reviewed by a separate child, then integrated in five passes):
- *A Warp forest build* (`tree_build.py`): the frame and classes by the reference's own code, the topology, boxes and
  node sums on the GPU; every forest field bitwise the reference's; 107 to 11-18 ms per build, and 187 host
  synchronizations down to 5.
- *A Warp walk* (`tree_walk.py`): a count pass and a fill pass over every point and tree; the lists equal the
  reference's in its order; 122 to 12 ms, and 183 synchronizations down to 1.
- *A fused Triton read* (`fused_read.py`) that computes the kernel term inside the read and recomputes it in the
  backward pass, as flash attention recomputes its logits, keeping nothing per pair but the basis; its backward is
  deterministic and 1.41 times faster. *A fused basis* (`fused_basis.py`) computes the pair invariants with the basis
  network; its backward is 1.66 times faster.
- *The pair plan* (`PairPlan.build`) by `torch.searchsorted` over the sorted indices.
- *Query-chunked training* (`ISLA.query_chunks` and the recipe's `chunked_forward_backward`): the boundary side runs
  once, the prediction points in chunks, the boundary side's backward once after them, with gradients equal to the
  unchunked step's up to summation order. It is the recipe's training path for ISLA-DTT, with no switch. The size rule
  (`_chunk_spans`) takes the fewest chunks of one size whose predicted peak, a linear fit in a chunk's pairs and points
  refitted on the final code (bfloat16 0.136 GiB per million pairs and 23.25 GiB per 100,000 points, with a margin of
  7.6 GiB), fits the device; under data parallelism an all-reduce takes the smallest fitting size over the ranks, which
  bounds every rank's chunks and decides one pass or two the same way on every rank (a rank may then add chunks for its
  own pair counts), before any point's forward pass, as the supervisor's rule on execution choices requires; the step
  logs the choice when it changes.
- *One execution attribute*, `tree_read_kernel` (`"auto"` or `"reference"`). Under `"auto"` the build runs fast on
  CUDA with Warp in two or three dimensions, the walk on CUDA where the forest's depth fits its stack, and the read and
  its node means fused on CUDA with Triton outside float64. The reference path is unchanged; it is the CPU fallback,
  and the read's float64 fallback (the build and the walk keep their Warp kernels in float64 on CUDA). Checkpoints do not store the attribute.
- *Dropped*, with their reasons recorded: checkpointing of the read (chunking makes it redundant), the compiled read
  projections (part P, which missed certification by 1 of 1,440 groups), and per-chunk padding (no gain).

**Equivalence** of the head against psharpe/isla b4b10d5a9, each version in its own process, on five first-batch inputs
(DrivAerML vehicle and whole boundary, AeroZoo, AirfRANS, the lug) at 2,000 points: pair lists raw-equal on all five;
float64 at most 3.1e-13 relative; the float32 distance-to-float64 ratio at most 1.14 (bound 2). In bfloat16, on
DrivAerML vehicle and AirfRANS, against families of seven one-ulp samples over two cold processes per version, every
group lies inside the reference family's range but for single-run maxima (AirfRANS blocks 3.94 in one run of seven
against 1.46; DrivAerML vehicle kernel_basis 1.14 against 1.12) and one group: AirfRANS "other" (the remaining
parameter gradients) sits at 0.99 / 1.03 / 1.07 against the reference's 0.97 / 0.99 / 1.01, a 4% shift of a group whose
reference range is 4% wide. The whole ISLA test directory on a GB300 with every CUDA test: 709 passed, 0 failed (job
371487); on CPU 461 passed, 241 skipped (371488). Version 0.12.0 and its state dict are unchanged; a 0.12.0 ISLA-DTT
checkpoint loads strictly with bitwise outputs.

**Step time** (final2/TABLE.md: one GB300, the recipe's own bfloat16 step with per-block compile, median of 15 steps,
interacting ISLA, the reference ISLA-DTT at b4b10d5a9 and the head in one job per case). DrivAerML Volume with the whole
boundary at 200,000 points: 4,112 ms at f13eb5ce0 (before the exact geometry's fast search), 2,105 ms at 7213c70c5 and
2,126 to 2,152 ms at b4b10d5a9 (both before DTT-FAST), and 1,209 to 1,231 ms at the head in the fixed-count state
training runs in (1,212 to 1,219 ms with varying counts). At 400,000 points the reference runs out of memory; the head
takes 1,586 ms with the vehicle and 1,790 to 1,792 ms with the whole boundary. AeroZoo at 200,000: 1,250 ms at 7213c70c5
(1,239 to 1,264 at b4b10d5a9) to 699 to 718 ms. Against the reference at b4b10d5a9 the head is 1.62 to 1.81 times
faster on DrivAerML and AeroZoo, 1.40 on the lug and 1.00 to 1.37 on AirfRANS, at 0.69 to 0.82 times its peak. Against
interacting ISLA at b4b10d5a9 (per-block compile) it costs 1.27 to 1.48 times the step on DrivAerML (2.5 times at
DTT-FAST's start, by its final report), 1.15 on AeroZoo, 1.10 to 1.33 on AirfRANS and 1.69 on the lug, with 1.08 to 1.13 times its peak on
DrivAerML, 0.95 to 1.00 on AeroZoo and 0.77 to 0.79 on AirfRANS. The chunked step trained up to 12.8 million vehicle
points on DrivAerML in the plan piece.

**Peak memory.** The head's peaks are 1.3 to 1.9 times the pass-2 table's (143 GiB against 107 GiB at DrivAerML 200,000
with the whole boundary), because the size rule now runs every point in one chunk where pass 2 cut chunks of 100,000, so
it fills the card; its steps are 5 to 20% faster than pass 2's for it. AirfRANS with every point and the airfoil alone is
the one setting where the head is slower than pass 2 (782 against 693 ms), level with the reference; the final rerun
trains neither that boundary nor that count. The AirfRANS varied-count state moves 17 to 20% between processes of the
same code, so its fixed-count numbers are the ones to read.

**The spike** (spike/RESULTS.md). In 557 distinct bfloat16 one-ulp samples (234 compiled, 323 eager), one compiled
AirfRANS step of ISLA-DTT's unchunked reference blew up the gradient (block 9's `assign.weight` to 6.7e5, against a true
maximum of 6e-4, repeated in a second cold process with the same kernels); no eager sample did. The cause, by the
spike child's quantitative reading, is the slice block's normalization of a slice's mean normal,
`m_s / |m_s|.clamp_min(1e-12)`: a slice spread over a closed boundary has a mean normal near zero (the blown-up row is
block 9's slice 446, |m| = 9.9e-4, the block's smallest), bfloat16 rounding with split-K partial sums can make it exactly
zero, and the clamp then amplifies the gradient by |m| / 1e-12, up to 1e9 (observed 1.5e9). FLAG's earlier reading,
1/dist in the relational invariants, is refuted on this input. No such spike shows in 267 training runs: 0 skipped
steps and 0 non-finite losses in their logs, and no spike of that size in the optimizer states of 12 of them; Muon bounds
the update, and finite routing spikes leave at most a one-epoch loss blip of about 15%. The certification of the
compiled path would catch it only by chance (95% needs about 60 sample-processes at its setting's rate). A deterministic
test is possible: a closed boundary with uniform routing has m_s = 0 exactly.

**The surface form, revisited.** ISLA-DTT's form of the surface task on DrivAerML with the whole boundary at 200,000
cells went from 3,996 ms at f13eb5ce0 (1,492 at pass 2) to 1,188 ms at the head, still 4.3 times option A's 276 ms (3.6
times at 400,000); on HiLift it still runs out of memory inside the exact geometry. On Peter's ruling of 23:26 EDT the
supervisor reads the revisit as keeping option A for the surface task.

## 2026-10-24 — HL-SYMPLANE: HiLiftAeroML's symmetry plane built at load from the closed root cap of the dataset's own source STL, after a per-case check; all 690 canonical cases pass, the worst vertex 0.061 in from the cap's outline against a derived tolerance of 0.1345 in; the built plane matches the curation pipeline's to 4.6e-9 in area; the baselines' inputs bitwise unchanged; merged with this batch {#sec-nb-hl-symplane}

**Question.** The supervisor asked Peter: "may HiLift's symmetry plane take its root outline from the closed root cap in the
dataset's own source STL files, applied to every case after a check that the case's own root points lie on it?" Peter
answered, at about 19:10 EDT: "Yes, that works". Can the plane be built so, at load, for every canonical case, and does it
match the plane the curation pipeline stored on its two files?

**Method.** `AddSymmetryPlane` (`src/symmetry.py`, psharpe/isla-hl-symplane bc4081e75) runs in HiLift's reader on the whole
stored wing, in raw inches. It reads the cap from the first source STL in sorted order (geo_LHC001_AoA_10, 966 cells, its key
accepted; the outline is one simple loop of 968 vertices) and builds the far field's $y = 0$ disk with that outline as its hole,
triangulated by constrained Delaunay with every normal into the fluid, on the same hemisphere as `AddHemisphereBoundaries`.
A case gets the plane only if every stored on-plane vertex and open root edge lies on the outline within a tolerance tau
derived from the cap alone:

- storage: eps = sqrt(2) × the float32 spacing at 2,583 in = 3.45e-4 in, which bounds the change of a point-to-segment
  distance under storage rounding;
- the chord sagitta: between two cap vertices the section is a convex arc inside the tangent triangle of its end turnings,
  widened by their float32 uncertainty, of height L / (cot b1 + cot b2); the largest, 0.1341 in, is on a 1-in chord near the
  flap whose ends turn 11.8° and 20.5°;
- tau = 0.1341 + 0.0003 = 0.1345 in.

The exact check costs 13 to 23 s and a 6.4 GB scan per wing, so it cannot run at every load. The supervisor decided at
19:28 EDT to keep the verdicts in one fingerprinted dataset-level record on LHR, which holds no geometry; the reader checks each
case's fingerprints against it at every load. A case that fails gets no plane, logged.

**Checks.**

- Census (LHR 374043 to 374045, 6.2 core-h; record md5 bc2ed653): 690 of 690 canonical cases (train 510, val 180) pass. The
  worst on-plane vertex is 0.061264 in (0.46 tau), the same vertex on every case. The worst open-edge midpoint is 0.060 in on
  689 cases and 0.1266 in (0.94 tau) on geo_LHC024_AoA_8, where two root edges of about 20 in have their ends within 0.004 in
  of the outline, so the distance is those edges' own sagitta.
- Against the stored plane of LHC001_AoA_10 and _12 (LHR 374370): the equator is bitwise equal; the area differs by +4.6e-9
  of the whole; the hole holds 0.99999 of the stored hole's area; the hole Hausdorff distance is 0.0613 in from the stored hole
  to the built one and 0.00085 in back; the built hole is one simple loop where the stored one, the pipeline's walk of the CFD
  root, has 11 vertices of degree 4. Inlet, outlet and plane together leave open exactly the 968 hole edges.
- One similarity moves every piece with the wing (8 samples, posed rotations 121° and 165°; residuals at most 1.5e-5 of the
  extent).
- GeoTransolver's and Transolver's collated inputs and targets: 24 of 24 items bitwise equal.
- Recipe tests: 605 passed, 12 skipped; the 2 test_campaign_c_hooks failures carry the base's messages. GB300 smoke with the
  plane: 32.51 GB and 98,300 tokens (the plane adds 1,032), against 32.23 GB and 97,268 without it, step time unchanged.
- The condition type is the dataset paper's (arXiv:2605.19565v2, section 2.3 and appendix A.2.1): "The symmetry plane is
  treated with a no-stress boundary condition". The README documents none.

**Reading.** Canonical ISLA's configuration on HiLift now reads the whole boundary of its PDE domain: the deduplicated wing,
the inlet, the outlet and the symmetry plane, the last three built at load, the dataset unchanged. HiLift's standing is still
of checkpoints trained with the wing alone; the final reference rerun retrains ISLA with the plane.

**Left open.** The full 1,800-case root has no record yet (about 15 core-h to build); the open-edge check includes a long edge's
own sagitta, so a future case with a longer root edge could fail although its root is correct; and a case that failed would
leave `isla_surface_highlift` without the boundary it names.

**For the book.** 05's, 06's and 20's generated tables gain `symmetry`; 06, 07, 10, 20 and 21 say the plane is built and read,
with the check, its tolerance, the census and the comparison; the symmetry-plane In-flight callouts in 10 and 20 are gone.
Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/hl_symplane/ (FINAL_REPORT.md, RESULTS.md, BOOK_CHANGES.md).

*Applied for the supervisor by the book lane BOOK-SYM and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-24, its findings applied
(scratch/isla-book-sym-2026-10-24/SECOND_READ_SYM.md, SECOND_READ_DISPOSITION.md).*

## 2026-10-24 — HL-AREA: on the uniform point cloud ISLA's error on the deduplicated HiLift wing is unchanged (0.989 to 0.999 of native) while the baselines' pressure error rises 3.6 to 5.5 times; the deduplicated lanes price within 6% of the stored-wing lanes {#sec-nb-hl-area}

**Question.** HL-DUP stage 2 scored its six deduplicated-wing checkpoints (ISLA 0.9.0, GeoTransolver and Transolver
with the unit drive, seeds 42 and 43) on the native mesh and rotated and translated only, and the book priced HiLift from
the lanes trained on the wing as stored. What do the same checkpoints score on the uniform point cloud, and what did their
own training cost?

**Method.** The scorer was HL-DUP stage 2's, with only these changes: the protocol, the run directory, the time limit, the
bad nodes excluded, and the Transolver rows run beside two others on the same node to stay within a 3 GPU-h cap. It used
the same inference command: float32, the 180 validation cases, the final checkpoint. The point cloud is CHAR-PROTOCOLS'
twin applied to the deduplicated dataset file. The reader draws a 1,000,000-cell block and drops the extra copies (about
934,000 cells kept). The area-proportional draw with exact Horvitz–Thompson weights then takes about 200,000 cells. The
cost is the book's rule (cost_090), from the six lanes' own training logs: the median step without compile steps, the
peak memory, and GPU-h from the scheduler.

**Checks.** Every row was at epoch 500 and scored the same 180 cases as native. The protocol is not degenerate: the
per-case pressure differs from native on 180 of 180 cases for every run. HL-DUP's RESULTS_STAGE2 ("Not done here") calls the
area protocol "degenerate for ISLA, as before"; on HiLift it is not, since the point cloud redraws the scored cells for every
arm, as CHAR-PROTOCOLS' audit of 2026-10-16 found. The cost extractor, rerun on the stored-wing lanes, reproduces
cost_090.json's per-seed values exactly.

**Result.** Seed means, seeds 42 / 43 in parentheses:

| arm | pressure, point cloud | wall shear, point cloud | point cloud ÷ native, pressure |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA 0.9.0 | 0.0543 (0.0525, 0.0561) | 0.0961 (0.0942, 0.0981) | 0.989, 0.999 |
| GeoTransolver 256 | 0.261 (0.239, 0.283) | 0.353 (0.331, 0.375) | 4.72, 5.48 |
| Transolver 512 × 16 | 0.189 (0.195, 0.184) | 0.295 (0.310, 0.280) | 3.60, 3.58 |

Baseline ÷ ISLA on the point cloud is 4.81 (pressure) and 3.67 (wall shear) for GeoTransolver, and 3.49 and 3.07 for
Transolver. The per-seed ratios run from 2.86 to 5.05. On the native mesh the same ratios are 0.936 / 0.957 and
0.966 / 0.954. ISLA's point-cloud error is 0.1 to 1.1% below its native error on every field and seed.

Cost, seed means, deduplicated (stored wing):

| | step [s] | peak [GiB per GPU] | GPU-h per lane |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA | 0.323 (0.341) | 64.6 (65.6) | 32.8 (32.5) |
| GeoTransolver | 0.431 (0.457) | 77.9 (77.9) | 38.3 (39.2) |
| Transolver | 0.323 (0.342) | 62.3 (62.3) | 32.3 (31.9) |

Each step is 5 to 6% shorter on every architecture because each draw keeps about 7% fewer cells. Loading and validation
fill the rest of each epoch, so GPU-h per lane moves only 0.98 to 1.01 times.

**Reading.** HiLiftAeroML has a point-cloud standing again, and it reads as DrivAerML Surface and SHIFT-SUV do. ISLA's
prediction does not depend on how the surface was sampled. Both baselines read the mesher's cell density, and their
errors rise 2.8 to 5.5 times across the five fields. Firm: the two seeds agree within 15% on every baseline ratio. The cost
table's cross-architecture ratios do not change.

**For the book.** The point-cloud scores are records (`hl_dup_stage2_area`); `hilift_surface_090_dedup_2026-10-24.py` now
reads them and writes `results/char/hilift_surface_090_dedup_v2.json`, and `cost_090_2026-10-22.py` prices HiLift from the
deduplicated lanes into `results/char/cost_090_v2.json`; the earlier files stay as they were, and every other entry equals

cost/); LHR job 375068, 1.09 GPU-h.

- One version, ISLA 0.13.0, covers (a), (b) and (e).
- For the book (this batch): the standings stay interacting ISLA 0.9.0's until the final reference rerun, with their
  callouts; interacting ISLA's parameter count is no longer computed from the class, so 05 names its one routing-mass
  scalar and 09 counts the boundary read from ISLA-DTT; the rank-2 refusal is a limit in 20.

**Why the Reynolds feature is kept, and moved exactly.** REYNOLDS-OUT surveyed the class: its application-specific
pieces were the `reynolds` argument, the viscosity role, the fluid names of the scales' vocabulary and z $\equiv (\log_{10}(U L / \nu) - m) / s$, which
`_case_scales` appended to the global scalars; only the AirfRANS and AeroZoo configurations used them. On AirfRANS
ISLA-DTT without its scales is 1.208 / 1.203 / 1.177 times worse on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity (DTT-KNOBS R5),
so the scales stay, and with them z is ISLA's only channel for the Reynolds number; removing it would need a no-harm
check the lane priced at about 950 to 1,300 GPU-hours. The relocation computes the same z in the recipe from the same
$L$ and $U$. REYNOLDS-OUT measured it on GB300 (LHR 376561 and 376855, 0.41 GPU-h), with three 0.9.0 checkpoints
(AirfRANS ISLA, AirfRANS ISLA-DTT, AeroZoo ISLA on `reynolds`):
- z: bitwise on 160 of 160 cases (64, 64 and 32), in float64 and in float32, and the network's z input bitwise in
  every forward;
- outputs: bitwise wherever the GPU forward repeats itself (AirfRANS ISLA, 6 of 6 cases over both jobs; AeroZoo
  case 1; every run on CPU). On AirfRANS ISLA-DTT the old and new forms differ by 1.76e-6 to 2.59e-6, the size of
  either form's own run-to-run spread (1.89e-6 to 2.37e-6 over repeats of the old form and of the new), which starts at
  the first tree read. On AeroZoo case 0 one
  new-form forward of three matched the old model at all 24 block tensors, and the other two differed from it and from
  each other by up to 8.8e-6, from a variation that enters before block 0, not from z.

So no retrain check is needed. ISLA-API's GB300 job 377645 checked the datapipe end to end: `re_z` from the recipe is
bitwise the base's in-model z on 8 of 8 cases (AeroZoo 4, AirfRANS 4), over two dumps against four runs of the old side.

**What changed in the code** (psharpe/isla-api-013, fc6ed19d0..7c88b2e1f, 58 files):
- the `query_independent` argument, attribute and stored argument; `_QueryTokens`'s routing mass `qt.logw`; the
  interacting branch of `_query_tokens`; and `_log_count` are deleted. `query_chunks` refuses a surface model.
- An interior model with a rank-2 boundary field is refused at construction, since ISLA-DTT's boundary read has no pair
  contraction for a tensor; no recipe configuration declares one.
- `reynolds`, the viscosity role and z are deleted; the AirfRANS and AeroZoo configurations append the two transforms
  and declare `re_z: {rank: 0}`.
- The renames, in the class, its attribute and the recipe's keys; `velocity_moments` becomes `rms_moments`.
- The version commit 25bea52cb: `_version` 13, every state dict of 0.7.0 to 0.12.0 refused, the .mdlus golden
  regenerated with its 59 tensors bitwise the 0.12.0 file's; only its file version, state-dict version and stored
  arguments differ. The surface and ISLA-DTT forward goldens are unchanged. One test-only commit follows (7c88b2e1f).
- The tests of the interacting interior form are deleted, each with its reason (DELETED_TESTS.md, DELETED_TESTS_RE.md);
  the tests that used it only as a vehicle for another contract run on ISLA-DTT, with a live boundary read. The
  assertion audit found no tolerance loosened; two refinement checks run with the exact read ($\theta = 0$), and one
  padding check is weaker, with its reason recorded.

**Tests.** The ISLA test directory: 453 passed, 240 skipped and 2 xfailed on CPU (377644), and 698 passed, 1 skipped and
2 xfailed with every CUDA test on a GB300 (377645). The recipe tests: 613 passed and 2 failed (378081), the two
`test_campaign_c_hooks` tests that fail identically on the base under Slurm. Six training smokes OK, the five interior

**For the book.** 30 cells in 05, 06, 09 and 19 broke on the new API (17 root causes, 13 cascades); each now reads its
names from the code (the signature, `scales.DEFINES`) and runs. The prose of 03 to 07, 09, 12, 13, 15, 16 and 20 to 22

## 2026-10-25 — GEO-TIEORDER: the on-wall direction follows the cells' order and the queries' precision at near-equal normals; a rule that breaks exact distance ties by position and takes the holding normals' least-norm point on the wall removes it; a candidate for ISLA 0.14.0, not merged {#sec-nb-geo-tieorder}

Lane GEO-TIEORDER, launched by the supervisor on MAIN-MERGE's defect (@sec-nb-main-merge); records
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/geo_tieorder/ (FINAL_REPORT.md md5 e10e95eb, RESULTS.md md5 e73972e8, NOTEBOOK_DRAFT.md md5
b2372ba7). GB300 377610, 377673, 377915, 377708, 378186, 378187, 378687; cpu-short 378185, 378676, 378382; 6.51 GPU-h of the
cap the supervisor raised from 6 to 7.5.

- **Two causes, both in `_closest_candidates_impl`.** Cells that share the closest point compute it bitwise, so they tie
  exactly in float64, and the closest cell was the least cell index, the input order; that index reaches the untied on-wall
  direction, the on-wall label and the off-wall rebuild. And on the wall the certified-distinct test chose between one normal
  and the normals' least-norm point with a bound that scales with the queries' precision. The same causes act at a fine
  polyline's vertices in 2-D and off the wall at edge and vertex closest points, at float64 rounding.
- **Rule** (the supervisor's approval, 00:50 EDT, DESIGN.md v2): T1, exact distance ties broken by the cells' canonical
  vertex positions, then parity; T2, on the wall, the least-norm point of the hull of the holding cells' normals wherever they
  differ, certified or not, which lies within their certified uncertainty and is the certified case's own value; off the wall
  the certified rule stands. No new constant. Reference and fast stay bitwise equal.
- **float32 change** (378186): DrivAerML on-wall direction at 3.1k and 3.2k of 200k points (median 2.8e-4, largest 4.5e-3);
  AirfRANS 70 to 93 airfoil nodes per draw (largest 1.6e-4); the lug at rounding; Tensile2d and AeroZoo none. The distance,
  the sign and the on-wall label do not change. Renumbering moves (2.6k and 2.7k per DrivAerML draw) and float32/float64
  mismatches (3.1k and 3.2k) fall to 0 on every dump.
- **HiLift** (its surface task never calls the geometry): the full-resolution wing runs out of memory on a GB300 in the base
  too; on a 2.4M-cell slab the base's direction moved under renumbering at 29 to 33 percent of queries and the head's at none.
- **Pose:** DrivAerML's on-wall direction steadier (largest posed change 1.4e-2 to 3.1e-3; tie flips 630 to 0); on the lug's
  planar faces the tie flag flips at about 2,000 points per case, which reaches only the direction's vertex gradient. The
  lane recommends accepting these flips; the decision is open.
- **Inference** (377708, GEO-BAND's checkpoints): no metric moves by more than 2.7e-4 in log (DrivAerML), 6.5e-5 (AirfRANS),

## 2026-10-25 — DRAW-EXACT: today's GPU evaluation draw is not repeatable at AeroZoo's half-integer shares and there keeps duplicate cells and drops cells it must keep; an exact int64 line removes it; a candidate for ISLA 0.14.0 the supervisor intends to adopt, not merged {#sec-nb-draw-exact}

Lane DRAW-EXACT (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/draw_exact/, FINAL_REPORT.md md5 a0700900, DESIGN.md md5 67dace2c);
psharpe/isla-draw-exact 5b5e72c2f, pushed, not merged; LHR 377433, 377520, 378082, 378518, 378892 and cpu-short 378083,
378832, 378893; 3.20 of 4 GPU-h.

- **Mechanism.** In evaluation the systematic draw starts at 0.5, and AeroZoo's water filling often gives half-integer
  shares (one case: 31,250, 58,315.5, 52,119 and 58,315.5), so hits land exactly on condition boundaries and on every cell
  boundary of a condition kept whole that starts at a half-integer offset. The rounding of CUDA's float64 scan, which
  varies from run to run, decides which side they fall on: over six runs one case's kept cells changed by up to 4 and
  another's by up to 9, with 0 to 4 and 1 to 13 duplicate cells per run and as many cells of probability one dropped. This
  is the mechanism behind REYNOLDS-OUT's unrepeatable AeroZoo case 0. Separately, with equal measures and share equal to
  the cell count, the keep probability comes out one minus a few ulps on 26 of 244 cases.
- **Options** (18 real cases, budget 200,000): an exact int64 line (A), a host cumsum (B, +26 ms and a sync), a
  fixed-order Triton scan (C), ATen's deterministic scan under a global flag (D). Built: A for the line, with the tail sums
  in a fixed-order float scan and π = 1 exactly where the share reaches the cell count.
- **After** (378892): six runs bitwise on all six real boundaries checked, no duplicates, every cell of probability one
  kept, CPU equal to GPU bitwise, compiled equal to eager. Against today's CPU draw: one kept cell of 200,000 in 5 of 18
  evaluation draws, 27 over 544 random draws, the size of today's own CPU-to-GPU gap. The draw costs 1 to 3 ms more.
- **Effect on scores.** One changed token moved AeroZoo case 0's outputs by 2.8e-6 to 8.8e-6, so the AeroZoo GPU scores
  are not materially affected. 20 states the defect as a limit (@sec-limits-draw-ties), and 03, 05, 06 and 21 scope
  "deterministic" and "exact on a condition kept whole" to it.
- **Suites:** CPU 466 passed, 245 skipped, 2 xfailed; GB300 716 passed, 1 skipped, 2 xfailed; the new determinism tests
  fail on the base.
- **The supervisor's decision:** adopt it at the 0.14.0 assembly; Peter may veto.

## 2026-10-25 — AF-WHOLE read: with the AirfRANS far field, ISLA reads a harm on every field (1.35 / 1.20 / 1.28), ISLA-DTT a harm and a broken pose through an octant tie; the velocity and eddy-viscosity harm sits at the wall, where the length unit of the whole boundary stretches the distance channel's softening over the boundary layer {#sec-nb-af-whole-read}

AF-WHOLE trained ISLA 0.9.0 and ISLA-DTT on full AirfRANS with the far field read as the named condition `freestream`. The
far field comes from the raw release's `_freestream.vtp`, geometry only, through `VtkBoundaryDomainMeshReader`
(psharpe/isla-whole-boundary 8e93f2307). The arms are two seeds each, eager-trained like the standings, and the read is
against r090eag_af_isla / r090eag_af_dtt (@sec-nb-af-whole-prereg). All checks and the supervisor's far-field guard
passed. The input is Peter's ruling (2026-10-23); this measures its effect.

**Result.**

| pair | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity | pose (posed / native) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, far field / standing | harms, 1.35 | harms, 1.20 | harms, 1.28 | holds, 1.0001-1.0014 |
| ISLA-DTT, far field / standing | harms, 1.94 | harms, 1.53 | harms, 1.89 | **broken**, 1.53-2.52 |

  chords), falling to 1.01 and 1.00 at 0.1 to 1 chord. It is larger below the softening's knee, 1e-6 L = 3.05e-4 chords,

  median of 2 airfoil cells.

## 2026-10-25 — KERNEL-BUGS: four of the pinned defects fixed with every float32 and bfloat16 forward bitwise; the Triton read differentiates the log measure, and the fused tree read refuses measure weights that require a gradient instead of dropping it {#sec-nb-kernel-bugs}

Lane KERNEL-BUGS (results/campaigns_2026-10-23/kernel_bugs/FINAL_REPORT.md, md5 c4672341); psharpe/isla-kernel-bugs
0d0ce638b on b841486a5, 10 files, +142/-87, merged into psharpe/isla by the supervisor as e44015436. One writer, a reviewer
("approve with nits", nits fixed); 1.83 of 3 GPU-h.

- **The log measure's gradient (W3-B2).** The Triton backward returns it, a sum over heads computed in float32, only
  when it is asked for. On a GB300 its relative distance to float64 is 2.95e-7 against eager float32's 1.12e-6; asked
  for, the backward on the DrivAerML body plan at 200k points takes 30.3 against 29.6 ms and 1.0 GiB more; not asked
  for, it is bitwise the base's. The fused tree read does not differentiate the log measure: with measure weights that
  require a gradient, an unsampled interior forward on CUDA now raises a `ValueError` naming
  `tree_read_kernel="reference"`, where it dropped that gradient silently. The lane notes the alternative, one contract
  on every path by detaching `log_frac` in `tree_read_walk`, as the maintainer's call.
- **The eager read's bf16 gradients (W1-B1).** It casts before its gather; against float64, bf16 grad.v goes from 2.9e-1
  to 1.8e-3, grad.q from 2.6e-2 to 2.0e-3, grad.k from 1.6e-2 to 3.2e-3.
- **float16 autocast (W2-1, W2-2).** On CUDA `resolve_geo_kernel` picks the fused region only when autocast is off or
  bf16, from the autocast state before the forward, the same on every rank; on CPU the routing logits normalize float16
  rows in float32. Both strict xfails now pass.
- **Bitwise.** The CPU A/B harness: 110 of 110 tensors bitwise for three fixes, and for W1-B1 exactly the six bf16
  gradient entries it must change; the CUDA goldens 155 of 155; the whole model's float32 and bf16 outputs and every
  parameter gradient bitwise on a GB300. Under CUDA float16 the gradients change by up to about 1e-3 of their largest
  entry, toward float64. `goldens_v1.pt` regenerated for those six entries with the documented `--regenerate`.
- **Suites.** The full CPU tier 708 passed, 472 skipped, 5 xfailed (383618); the GB300 tier 1,196 passed, 5 xfailed
  (383532). The five strict xfails left: W3-B1 twice, GEO-TIEORDER's quad diagonals twice, and the core `Module.load` gap.

**For the book** (TEST-BUILD and KERNEL-BUGS). 06 gains a section on the class's tests (@sec-using-tests: the tiers and their
counts, what they hold the code to, the determinism they state, float16), and its kernel bullets state the float16 choice
and the fused tree read's refusal; 20 gains the five strict expected failures as a limit (@sec-limits-xfail).

## 2026-10-25 — AF-FIX: on AirfRANS with its far field the face forest moves no far-field cell under pose; the far field takes 99.75 percent of ISLA-DTT's slice mass and most of its tree read even next to the wall; four principled fixes proposed, none adopted {#sec-nb-af-fix}

Lane AF-FIX, launched by the supervisor on AF-WHOLE's read (@sec-nb-af-whole-read). Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/af_fix/
(FINAL_REPORT.md md5 7ba2a114, DESIGN.md, PRESSURE_PROBE.md, PREREG_DRAFT.md 553e4714). LHR 381565, 381714 and 381746,
cpu-short 381569, 381862 and 13 jobs of its child TIE; 3.10 of 6 GPU-h; no commits. A lane-reviewer confirmed the numbers.

- **The tie** (200 full_test cases, posed as the scorer poses them). DTT-POSE's cube-face forest moves 0 far-field cells
  between trees in every case; the octants move 15.4 / 28.9 / 45.1 percent (min / median / max). On the airfoil the faces
  move 1 cell in 3 cases. The faces still leave 4.1 / 15.8 / 26.5 percent of posed pairs with no native match, mostly in
  the airfoil's trees, which sit 27.8 chords from the forest's origin. Rule 1, one set of face trees per declared
  condition about that condition's own centroid, leaves a median 0.026 percent as a counterfactual and equals DTT-POSE
  bitwise on one condition.
- **The near-wall length.** 0.13.0 forms x - p in float64, so every candidate passes NEARWALL's precision gate (p99.9
  below 2e-7). The viscous length (ii), `distance_softening: {nu: 1, U: -1}` in the `units` grammar, opt-in, with no fluid
  name in model.py, puts AirfRANS's first node at t = 8.3 against 0.0069 today, with a pose change of 0.018 at p99.9; a
  floor in the stored frame fails pose (8.4), one about the centroid stays linear (t 0.077), per-condition gauges flip
  sign on open pieces.
- **The pressure harm** (the eight AF-WHOLE runs, 16 test cases each). Measured: in W-DTT the slices' mass is 99.75
  percent far field and their anchors lie about 60 chords from a mid-field point; the tree read gives the airfoil 12
  percent of the attention 1e-6 to 1e-5 chord off the wall and 10 percent at 0.01 to 0.1 chord, against 100 percent in
  B-DTT; in W-ISLA the airfoil holds 0.09 percent of the slices' mass. Inferred, not tested: that this causes the pressure
  harm at 0.01 to 0.1 chord; the across-case test has no power (the airfoil's share is 0.141 to 0.146 percent on every
  case) and reweighting at inference is off the trained distribution (pressure errors rise 2.3 to 18 times in W-ISLA and
  23 to 55 times in W-DTT).
- **Proposed.** Rule 1; ii; C, per-condition quadratures with learned shares (log w = log a - log A_k + beta_k, beta
  starting at 0), which changes every dataset that declares more than one condition; and Omega, a solid-angle prior on
  ISLA-DTT's read alone. What C does not fix: L still grows with the truncation radius.
- **Decisions named.** For the supervisor: the campaign and its cap, rule 1 as a change to DTT-POSE's frozen forest,
  NEARWALL's contingency, a fourth arm. For Peter: adopting ii, and whether AeroZoo declares it; adopting C; whether
  rule 1 groups by declared conditions or by connected components.

## 2026-10-25 — PERF-SURVEY: where ISLA 0.13.0's training step goes on a GB300, and fifteen opportunities ranked by what Peter is likely to approve; a correctness fault past 2^31 elements in the fused geometry kernel {#sec-nb-perf-survey}

**Why.** Peter asked, in a forked session, verbatim: "Please look at the current ISLA model architecture, and look for
performance optimization opportunities that I am likely to approve of." Lane PERF-SURVEY, launched 08:00 EDT 2026-10-25,
eight children; records results/campaigns_2026-10-23/perf_survey/ (FINAL_REPORT.md md5 a8d88b85, OPPORTUNITIES.md
f85d83b7, infer/RESULTS.md e476ea41). 39 GB300 jobs, 9.24 of 12 GPU-h.

**The profile** (382020; bf16, the recipe's configurations, one GB300, median of 10 steps): DrivAerML Volume with the
whole boundary at 200k, 1,190 ms and 143 GiB (geometry 31 percent, blocks and point reads 26, fused read 18, basis 8; 92
of its 101 host syncs in the geometry); AeroZoo 716 ms (blocks and point reads 46 percent); AirfRANS with its far field
530 ms compiled and 895 eager (point reads 59 to 63 percent, since 2-D models run the eager geometry region); the lug 234
ms compiled, host-bound (GPU busy 42 percent); the DrivAerML Surface task 246 ms (slice blocks 75 percent, memory-bound).
Every case peaks in the chunk's backward. The optimizer launches 750 to 850 kernels a step and starves the GPU 25 to 70
ms on the small cases.

**Five for Peter's decision** (each measured; exactness B bitwise, C certified within rounding, N a numerics change):
1. FUSED-PAD: 2-D models and models without a global direction take the fused geometry region with exact zero padding.
   AirfRANS step 0.59x compiled and 0.42x eager; lug eager 0.78 to 0.82x, lug compiled neutral; C for eager blocks; the
   compiled-regions certification on real AirfRANS, lug and Tensile2d checkpoints is left.
2. 64-bit offsets in `geo_kernel`: a correctness bug, since ISLA's forward faults once tokens x slices reaches 2^31, at
   2^31/512 + 64 tokens with 512 slices, as a full AeroZoo case (5.87M points and 200k boundary tokens) does at inference. B below the limit;
   kernel time 0.995 to 1.012x. Whether the read kernels share it is not checked.

## 2026-10-26 — FLOOR-DRV: given the domain's whole boundary, ISLA's far-field eddy-viscosity error on one DrivAerML Volume car falls 2.4 times, to within 1.12-1.34 times Transolver's (registered "closes"); its velocity floor falls 20-28 percent ("helps") but stays 1.72-1.74 times Transolver's {#sec-nb-floor-drv}

**Why.** The whole boundary is adopted by Peter's ruling of 2026-10-23; FLOOR-DRV measures its effect. Peter (17:08 EDT
2026-10-23, @sec-nb-canonical-rulings): "Seeing where the floor is through raw coordinates is a bug, not a feature. Even
if there were an accuracy *cost* to reading the whole boundary (not that I expect it), I would recommend this." The
registered readings, written while adoption was open, stand as written. Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/floor_drv_read/
(RESULTS.md, tables/reduce_fd.md md5 eea5db7c, tables/resid_fd.md 560eba98); PREREG.md md5 d04462aa (amendments A1, A2).

- **Design.** CAP-AUDIT's Part B protocol on run_171 (a fresh draw of 200,000 points every step, 20,000 steps, eager,
  float32, the corrected held-out set), two seeds per arm in one job on one node. Arm F reads the vehicle and the four
  domain meshes the case files store (`no_slip`, the ground under and behind the car; `slip`, the sides, the roof and the
  upstream ground; `inlet`; `outlet`), each by its name with no fields, since the files store none on them. C is Part B's
  ISLA rerun beside it. Transolver and GeoTransolver are Part B's runs; they read each point's coordinates, so they see the
  ground's height through z.
- **Checks.** On all 484 files the four meshes exist and every face points into the fluid. In every draw they move with
  the car by one scale and translation (within 0.004 mm). With them ISLA's length unit is 59.5 m instead of 2.04 m, and 18
  percent of the points are nearer a domain wall than the car. All four runs completed 20,000 steps.
- **Readings** (registered, PREREG section 4; seeds 42 / 43):
  - far-field eddy viscosity (more than 5 m from the car), held-out e_R: F 0.0130 / 0.0119, C 0.0310 / 0.0281,
    Transolver 0.0097 / 0.0107 (GeoTransolver 0.0115 / 0.0114); F / Transolver 1.34 / 1.12, F / C 0.42 / 0.42; label
    **closes** (bar: at most 1.5 times Transolver on both seeds);
  - velocity, held-out floor: F 0.0153 / 0.0149, C 0.0191 / 0.0207, Transolver 0.0088 / 0.0086; F / C 0.80 / 0.72, both F
    seeds below all five ISLA reference runs (0.0191-0.0207); label **helps** (bar: at most C / 1.2 on both seeds and below
    every reference). On seed 42 the margin is thin (0.80 against the bar 0.83).
- **Beside them** (descriptive): pressure floor F / C 0.95 / 0.68, eddy viscosity 0.69 / 0.65; the share of the
  eddy-viscosity squared error beyond 5 m (0.7 percent of the points) falls from 41 percent (C) to 16 percent (F); F's error
  is below C's in every wall-distance band, on all three fields and both seeds (36 of 36), so the 29 times smaller
  s = d / L costs nothing near the wall; C reproduces Part B's ISLA (velocity 0.995 / 1.033 of it).
- **What it means.** On this car the missing boundary was a cause of ISLA's far-field eddy-viscosity miss. It explains a
  part of the uniform velocity factor, not most of it: F's velocity floor is still 1.72-1.74 times Transolver's, and 1.4-1.9
  times in every band (CAP-AUDIT 15.10 points to depth). One car and two seeds per arm; the eddy-viscosity effect (2.4
  times) is far above the 1.46 times spread of the five ISLA reference runs.
- **Cost.** The registered cost finding is the smoke's: with the four meshes ISLA 0.9.0's step took 1.58-1.61 times as
  long (5.27-5.29 s against 3.29-3.33 s). Over the full runs it was 1.74-1.76 times (5.25 s against 3.01 s; C's step
  settled at 3.00 s after its first 1,000 steps, F's did not). Memory unchanged (234.4 GiB). Almost all of the added time

  resumed six times from its checkpoints, C three times, not bit-for-bit); 148.2 GPU-h in all, under the 150 GPU-h cap the
  supervisor set.
- **Predictions** (PREREG section 5): W1 nu_t "closes" (p 0.15) true; W6 velocity "helps" (p 0.12) true; W9, W10, W11
  true; W2-W5, W7, W8 false.

## 2026-10-25 — GLOBE on DrivAerML Surface: at its published configuration it trails A2 ISLA about twofold, so the AeroZoo stage does not run {#sec-nb-globe-dr-scored}

**Question** (GLOBE-SCORE, pre-registered 2026-10-19 in scratch/isla-globe-2026-10-19/PREREG.md, at Peter's request).
Where does GLOBE stand on DrivAerML Surface? It runs at the settings of its own DrivAerML example: 256 × 3 Padé kernels,
8 latent scalars and 4 latent vectors, 4 Legendre terms, θ = 1.5, 1.0M parameters, 80,000 faces per step at a rate of
1e-2. Everything else follows the recipe protocol: Muon and AdamW, StepLR, Huber loss, bf16 and 500 epochs. The reference
lengths are constant (L_ref = 1, δ_turb = 0.015), per Peter's reference-length ruling. Scores are in float32 on the 48
validation cars at ISLA's 200,000 cells. Records: results/campaigns_2026-10-23/globe_dr/ (RESULTS_DR.md md5 869c6670,
NOTEBOOK_DRAFT_DR.md 86248b7c, scores_dr/globe_dr_scores.json).

| Arm | Pressure | Wall shear | GLOBE ÷ arm |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLOBE | 0.09782 (0.09701, 0.09863) | 0.12145 (0.12037, 0.12254) | 1 |
| A2 ISLA | 0.04452 | 0.07004 | 2.197 / 1.734 |
| ISLA 0.9.0 (the standing's) | 0.04113 | 0.06622 | 2.378 / 1.834 |
| GeoTransolver, fair drive | 0.04552 | 0.06962 | 2.149 / 1.744 |
| Transolver, fair drive | 0.04234 | 0.06782 | 2.310 / 1.791 |

Native relative L2, seed means; GLOBE's seeds 42 and 43 in parentheses. Every per-seed ratio lies on the same side of one
as its mean.

**Verdicts.** There is no adoption rule: the result adds a GLOBE column to the DrivAerML Surface standing. The fallback did
not trigger; the worst validation was 1.016 times its running minimum. The AeroZoo stage requires GLOBE within 1.10 of A2
ISLA on some headline field of either dataset. The closest fields are AirfRANS pressure at 1.32 and DrivAerML wall shear
at 1.73, so the trigger does not fire and the stage does not run. GLOBE-SCORE is done.

**Beside the rules.**

- GLOBE is worse than ISLA 0.9.0 on all 48 cars on both fields; per car, the ratio runs from 1.50 to 3.19 on pressure and
  from 1.24 to 2.29 on wall shear.
- GLOBE underfits: its final training loss, 0.00175, is close to its validation loss and 6.7 times ISLA 0.9.0's under the
  same loss. Its 1.0M parameters are its authors' choice; ISLA 0.9.0 has 69M.
- Posed ÷ native is 1.03 to 1.08, against float32 equality on AirfRANS. The DrivAerML model sums with a Barnes-Hut tree of
  axis-aligned boxes (θ = 1.5), where the AirfRANS model sums exactly (θ = 0). This is the likely cause; it was not
  isolated. GLOBE's posed score, 0.104 / 0.127, is still about ten times better than the baselines' posed scores.
- Area ÷ native is 1.010 / 1.021. Scored at Transolver's 100,000 cells, GLOBE is 6 percent worse than at 200,000, because
  its boundary input is the scored subsample.
- Registered predictions: GLOBE below A2 ISLA (0.3 and 0.25) failed, posed within 1e-3 of native (0.9) failed, 100k within
  3 percent of 200k (0.8) failed; area within 5 percent (0.75) and no fallback (0.7) held.
- As on AirfRANS, the recipe protocol departs from the example's (RAdam, plateau schedule, gradient clipping, its own loss
  and targets, ground planes). This tests GLOBE under the shared protocol, not the example's own numbers.

**Next.** None for GLOBE-SCORE. Testing GLOBE under its own training protocol, or at a larger width, would be a new piece
of work.

**For the book.** 09 gains @sec-drivaerml-globe, GLOBE against the standing's three reference configurations, with ISLA
0.9.0 as the standing's ISLA.

*Applied for the supervisor by the book lane BOOK-MORNING on 2026-10-26, from NOTEBOOK_DRAFT_DR.md.*

**Why.** PERF-SURVEY's item 1 (@sec-nb-perf-survey); Peter answered "yes to all" to building it with five other items
before the final rerun. Lane FUSED-PAD (records results/campaigns_2026-10-23/fused_pad/, FINAL_REPORT.md, RESULTS.md),

as 9f279664c at 14:12 EDT 2026-10-25, after INT64-OFFSETS. 4.57 of 5 GPU-h.

- **Speed** (GB300, per iteration, synchronized ABAB windows, job 384802): AirfRANS with its far field 575 to 284 ms
  compiled (0.49x) and 928 to 368 ms eager (0.40x); the lug 242 to 253 ms compiled (1.04x, host-bound) and 377 to 308 ms
  eager (0.82x); Tensile2d 218 to 220 ms compiled and 346 to 294 ms eager (0.85x).
- **3-D models with a global direction run bitwise as before**: after 8 compiled recipe steps every parameter matches on
  DrivAerML Volume (431 tensors) and AeroZoo (432); AeroZoo's 12-worker loader is not bitwise run to run, so the check
  used one worker.
- **Eager certification passes**: float64 at roundoff (5.6e-14 AirfRANS, 7.2e-14 the lug, 3.8e-13 Tensile2d); float32 no
  group above eager plus eager's one-ulp change; on real checkpoints 0 aggregated failures, and 1-4 of 1,152 per-tensor
  groups up to 1.9x, inside the fused path's own one-ulp family.
- **Compiled certification** (cert_fp.py, real checkpoints of AirfRANS, the lug and Tensile2d, bf16 families of 16 from two
  cold processes): per tensor, the base itself fails the rule on every dataset (AirfRANS 19-21 fp32 and 10-11 bf16 groups
  per process), in the same routing-gradient groups as the branch; on aggregated groups AirfRANS and the lug pass every
  group for both codes, and Tensile2d fails 1 of 5 on the branch and 3 of 6 on the base. The base's compiled path is more
  accurate than eager in and after the geometry region because Inductor elides eager's bf16 casts there; the fused kernel
  keeps eager's roundings by design.
- **Suites**: GB300 every CUDA test 1,232 passed, 5 xfailed; CPU full tier 708 passed; recipe 615 passed.

**The supervisor's certification reading** (14:13 EDT 2026-10-25, before CERT runs; scratch/isla-main-2026-10-14/LANE_RULES.md):
the gate is the aggregated reading, as in DTT-FAST: tensor groups pooled by role (each block's outputs, each block's
parameter gradients, the routing gradients, the heads), each pooled group's distance to float64 inside the eager reference
family's range (bf16: at least 14 samples from at least two cold processes). The per-tensor counts are reported beside and
do not gate. A compiled path that calls a Triton kernel, whose roundings follow eager by design, is judged against the
eager family, with the base compiled family beside. On this reading AirfRANS and the lug certify with FUSED-PAD (the lug
can train compiled: 253 ms against 377 ms eager), and Tensile2d does not, so Tensile2d trains eager unless CERT certifies
it on the final code.

**For the book.** 05's certification paragraph states the pooled reading with the per-tensor counts beside, and its
In-flight callout names CERT on the final code; 05's and 06's kernel rules say that planar and direction-free models run
the fused kernel; 20's engineering row gives the measured steps.

*Applied for the supervisor by the book lane BOOK-MORNING on 2026-10-26.*

## 2026-10-25 — INT64-OFFSETS: 64-bit offsets where ISLA's kernels passed 2^31 at full resolution, merged; every golden output below the limits bitwise {#sec-nb-int64-offsets}

**Why.** PERF-SURVEY's correctness finding (@sec-nb-perf-survey): the fused geometry kernel faulted once tokens x slices
reached 2^31, as an unchunked full AeroZoo case does. Approved by Peter ("yes to all"). Lane INT64-OFFSETS (records
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/int64_offsets/, FINAL_REPORT.md, AUDIT.md), branch psharpe/isla-int64-offsets 21707ae5f,
merged into psharpe/isla as 59cf602c4 at 12:53 EDT 2026-10-25. 1.43 of 4 GPU-h.

- **Fixes.** df266e504, the prototype's 80a58e1e8 cherry-picked: the fused geometry kernel forward and backward in 64-bit
  offsets (tokens x slices reach 3.1e9 in the unchunked AeroZoo forward, the backward's partials 9.3e9). 330497096: the read
  kernels take int64 pair offsets whatever the plan's dtype (latent: the model's own plans keep int64). 389b5092c: the ball
  search runs in blocks of rows under Warp's limit of 2^31 entries per array, so the DrivAerML Volume full case (about
  1.5e8 points) gets past it. 21707ae5f: the fused geometry backward reads r and n_hat with their own strides, a non-width
  bug found in the audit.
- **Audit** (AUDIT.md): one row per kernel and expression with its maximum at production scale; the rest safe or guarded.
- **Tests.** Each new test faults or raises on the base and passes on the head (slow GPU tests past 2^27, 2^28 and 2^31,
  the strides test on CUDA, the blocked ball search on CPU). CPU full tier 710 passed, 478 skipped, 5 xfailed; GB300 tier
  no failure. Goldens: CPU 110 of 110 and CUDA 154 of 155 bitwise; the flagged output, a declared atomics family, varies by
  the same one ulp within base and within head at 20 repeats, so no output below the limits changed.
- **Left.** The ball search holds about 1.6-1.8 kB per query, about 240 GiB at the DrivAerML Volume full case; chunking
  `exact_boundary_geometry` over queries is the next step, not done. Torch's CUDA sort refuses more than INT_MAX elements
  (the reviewer's reading, not run), which caps a pair plan at 2^31 pairs per chunk and fails loudly.

**For the book.** 20's `sec-limits-int32` and its In-flight callout go: the fault is fixed. 06's kernel bullet states the
64-bit offsets.

*Applied for the supervisor by the book lane BOOK-MORNING on 2026-10-26.*

  of 38 cases over 5 datasets has a zero-measure cell.

  DeepJEB++ with their posed and area twins, the HiLift dedup files, DrivAerML area and SHIFT-SUV fastback). Each reads its

## 2026-10-22 — MECH-090: on Tensile2d the fixed compiled path's float32 gradients sit at a one-ulp eager floor, and pytorch/pytorch#195845 added a unit-dependent sink to ISLA's slice-state softmax (registered emulations not confirmed; a post-smoke emulation matches) {#sec-nb-mech090}

**Question.** REF-090's Tensile2d control (@sec-nb-ref090-t2d-control) read (b) by its registered weighing, in which A2
decides: A2's eager-trained rows matched the bug-trained ones (eager ÷ bug 1.037, overlapping) and not the fix-trained
ones (eager ÷ fix 0.853, below); ISLA 0.9.0 read (c). Does the fixed compiled path train something other than the eager
model, and what exactly did pytorch/pytorch#195845 do to ISLA?

**Setting.** Rules: PREREG.md §§1-5 (registered md5 58d8096d, copy PREREG.md.registered); its §6 addendum (10:31 EDT,
written after the smoke) carries no rule weight. Records: scratch/isla-mech090-2026-10-22/RESULTS.md. LHR jobs 333750
(smoke) and 333837 (main), about 0.85 GPU-h.

**On Tensile2d the fixed path computes the eager model's gradients, to float32 roundoff.** To give the one-step
gradient comparison a real floor, we moved every block input of the eager model by one float32 ulp. On eight Tensile2d
checkpoints from ISLA 0.9.0 and ISLA A2, the fixed path's gradients sit at that floor (0.55 to 1.19 times it); the bug
path's sit at 1,574 to 32,531 times the floor. Over 300 float32 training steps from one epoch-251 checkpoint per family
(seed 42), the fixed path's distance from eager's trajectory stays within 0.85 to 2.2 times the one-ulp copy's at each
of the six reported steps (1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300), with no growing ratio. (This lockstep is descriptive, with no
registered rule.) One ulp of roundoff alone takes the trajectories apart, to 0.42-0.56 of eager's own displacement by
step 100, and 0.89-0.91 by step 300. So, as far as one-step gradients and 300 steps show, a fix-trained seed differs
from its eager-trained twin the way two eager runs with different roundoff do; full-length (50,000-step) runs were not
compared. A seed-paired re-read of the existing scores, descriptive because its inputs had been seen, does not separate
the paths when pooled ((c), n = 5 after the P1 pairing check dropped ISLA 0.9.0 seed 43: ē = +0.043, SE 0.069,
sign-flip p = 0.22). ISLA 0.9.0 alone reads (a)-side on displacement (ē = +0.127, 2.09 SE, 3 of 3 seeds); A2 alone
leans the other way (fix ÷ eager error about 1.18 on average).

**What the bug was.** We read the generated Triton kernel. Inductor fused the geometry region's softmax over slices
with the column sum of the slice-state softmax over points, and the column sum skipped the row mask. On an input whose
token count N (≥ 10,240) is not a multiple of 4, each slice's denominator gained k = (−N) mod 4 phantom tokens. Each
phantom token has value 0 and, as far as the emulation shows, measure 1 in the data's raw units, and its logit equals
the block's geometry-logit bias: an attention sink. The masked log_w load has no `other`, so its value on padded rows is
undefined, and the emulation's match is the evidence that it reads 0. None of the three registered emulations (EMU-A, EMU-S,
EMU-AS) matched
(M0 as registered: not confirmed; the closest, EMU-S, sits at 4e-3 to 1.2e-2). A kernel-derived emulation (EMU-Sb,
phantom logit b_geo), added after the smoke in the PREREG §6 addendum, which carries no rule weight, matches the bug
path's block outputs to 2.9e-7-3.4e-7, at or below the k = 0 float32 floor of 3.5e-7-5.2e-7. That holds on three
affected Tensile2d training cases per family (epoch 500), forward only, while eager sits at 1.7e-2-4.2e-2. We measure
the sink's strength as ρ′ = k·e^{b_geo} ÷ Σ_i w_i e^{x_is}, phantom mass over real mass, where x_is is the slice-state
logit including b_geo. It is computed the same way on every dataset and reported as the median over affected (case,
block, slice) entries. ρ′ is the kernel-derived measure from the §6 addendum. The registered ρ (phantom logit 0) gives
state-softmax medians of 0.075, 0.077, 0.29 and 20. Since a phantom token's measure is 1 in raw units, the strength
depends on the units of the measure (epoch-500 checkpoints; AirfRANS and the lug from one ISLA 0.9.0 checkpoint, seed
42):
- Tensile2d (median total measure 18.5-18.6; ISLA 0.9.0 and A2, 151 of 400 training cases affected): phantom ÷ real
  mass 8-9 % (median 0.082 and 0.091).
- AirfRANS (median total measure 4.0; ISLA 0.9.0 only, 155 of the first 200 cases affected): about 31 % (median 0.308).
- Lug (median total measure 0.039; ISLA 0.9.0 only): phantom ÷ real mass about 37 (median). On 89 of the first 200
  training cases (45 %), the median affected slice state was shrunk 38-fold (by 1 ÷ (1 + ρ′)).

**Against the registration** (PREREG §§1-5). The fixed path reads "at the floor's order" on all eight checkpoints
(R_fix at most 1.19, against the registered cut of 10), and the bug path's R_bug is at least 1,574; F1, F2 and F3
held. M0 is not confirmed, so M1 failed. The registered ρ is non-negligible on Tensile2d (38 % of training cases
affected; medians 0.075 to 0.098 over the anchor and state softmaxes, at least 2^-8 as registered), so S1 held, and
AirfRANS's sink is stronger than Tensile2d's, so S2 held. The supervisor declined both proposed arms on 2026-10-22: EMU
is not run, and SINK is deferred to the architecture agenda. SINK will be revisited, with a fresh pre-registration, if
the eager-trained AirfRANS and lug standings show seed spreads large enough to matter.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by the reviewer on 2026-10-22 (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/second-read-2026-10-22/mech.md).*

## 2026-10-22 — E1-AZ reads REJECT as registered: on AeroZoo's held-out non-box family, HEADNORM (ISLA 0.10.0) ÷ CONTROL (ISLA 0.9.0) is 1.287 on pressure with both seed-matched ratios at least 1.10 (1.339 / 1.178), so HEADNORM is not adopted; post hoc, both arms are worse than predicting zero on that pressure, and the normalized head frame stays near-uniform {#sec-nb-e1az}

**E1-AZ: HEADNORM rejected on AeroZoo pressure.** E1 makes ISLA's head frame read the normalized stream `norm_out(h)`
instead of the raw stream (ISLA 0.10.0); the stream itself is unchanged. Its AeroZoo pair was registered to complete
E1's rule (@sec-nb-headnorm-jb; PREREG_AZ, md5 5f18f7e0): two seeds on `family_non_box` against the ISLA 0.9.0 lanes
`azc_nonbox_isla_seed42/43`, scored on the test side at epoch 250 in float32. The pair was registered (2026-10-20) by
supervisor decision after E1's other 12 ratios were known. No amendment was written before those results, so its
registration is later than E1's original rule (PREREG.md). The REJECT follows the text of PREREG_AZ as written.

- **Ratios (HEADNORM ÷ CONTROL error; above 1 means HEADNORM is worse).** Velocity 1.047 (seed-matched 42 / 43:
  1.022 / 1.081), within seed spread. Pressure 1.287 (1.339 / 1.178). Its unpaired seed ranges overlap, so the
  registered reporting marks it within seed spread, but both paired ratios are ≥ 1.10. Recorded, outside the rule: nut
  1.030 and tke 1.042, both within seed spread.
- **The rule.** Pressure meets the registered reject clause: the seed-mean ratio and both seed-matched ratios are each
  at least 1.10. G14, the 14-field geometric mean of HEADNORM ÷ CONTROL, is 1.004, below the 1.05 reject bar. That bar
  cannot bind on AeroZoo in practice. The 12 known ratios give G12 = 0.9797, so G14 reaches 1.05 only if
  r_vel × r_p ≥ 2.534. Those 12 were also measured on A2 code (ISLA 0.4.0 CONTROL against 0.5.0 HEADNORM), not on
  ISLA 0.9.0, and they hold about 5 independent numbers.
- **The registered instrument, (b1)-(b3), holds on AeroZoo.** There is no HEADNORM collapse (minimum support 3.44e5 of
  4.0e5 tokens). HEADNORM's final seed-logit p99.9 is 0.595 (0.550 / 0.640), against CONTROL's 25.0 (15.76 / 34.26);
  HEADNORM ÷ CONTROL is 0.024. CONTROL's p99.9 grows 33× and 104× over its epoch-1 value.
- **Verdict: REJECT.** ISLA 0.9.0 stays the reference.

Beside the rule (post hoc):

- Both arms do worse than predicting zero on nonbox pressure: physical relative L2 2.77 (CONTROL, ISLA 0.9.0) and 3.57
  (HEADNORM, ISLA 0.10.0), where predicting zero scores 1. CONTROL's failure is broad across cases: per-case median
  1.51, p90 6.3, and the 5 worst cases carry 4 % of the mean. HEADNORM's per-case distribution was not reduced.
  GeoTransolver 256 reads 1.17 there (median 1.00), i.e. it predicts about zero pressure. Seed 42 is the worse seed in
  both arms, so pairing keeps both ratios above 1.10.
- (Post hoc.) On these lanes HEADNORM bounds the head frame's logit scale: final p99.9 0.55 / 0.64, against CONTROL's
  15.8 / 34.3. Under (b3)'s definition it still grows 7.1× and 12.0× from a smaller epoch-1 value, and the stream grows
  as in CONTROL. Nonbox pressure gets worse, not better. So the frame's logit growth alone does not explain the failure.
  The same change also left the frame near-uniform, so this one intervention has two effects.
- With the frame reading `norm_out(h)`, the head frame stays near-uniform: a support fraction of 0.93 / 0.90 at epoch
  250, the same as at epoch 1 (0.92); minimum seed support 3.44e5 / 3.46e5 of 4.0e5 tokens. Its input norm fell from
  22.48 at epoch 1 to 5.36-5.90 from epoch 99 on (final 5.63 / 5.90). Over the same span the RMS of norm_out's gain went
  from 0.99 at epoch 1 to 0.94-0.95, which alone would give 21.3-21.6. The likely cause is a few outlier channels that
  dominate the grown stream and carry a small gain. That is an inference; the activations were not inspected. The
  registered instrument checks only the collapse side, (b1), not this uniform side, so this is a finding, not a rule
  outcome.
- Registered predictions: V gave REJECT 0.04. A2, A3, A5 and I1 (as written) failed. A1, A4 and I2-I5 held.
- Record: `scratch/isla-headnorm-2026-10-18/RESULTS_AZ_2026-10-22.md`.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by the reviewer on 2026-10-22 (scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/second-read-2026-10-22/e1az.md).*

## 2026-10-22 — AeroZoo diagnostics: no compiled-path exposure; GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16 end as about a zero predictor on pressure; ISLA 0.9.0's pressure error is above 1 on two held-out families, on profile_crossflow as an amplitude error from about a 2× velocity overshoot (a post hoc reading) and on family_non_box as a shape error by family, with part scale extrapolation on ducts {#sec-nb-azdiag}

**Four diagnostics on compliant AeroZoo before the ISLA-DTT read.** The 16 baseline lanes and the 14 ISLA lanes are
scored: test side, epoch 250, float32. All checks pass (`tables_partial.md`; it and every folder below are in
scratch/isla-az-decide-2026-10-21/). Four diagnostics then asked whether those numbers mean what they seem to mean.
Each pair below gives the seed mean, then [the median over cases of the per-case seed mean]; 'a / b' is seed 42 / seed
43. A relative L2 of 1.0 is the zero predictor.

- **Compiled-path exposure: none** (job 333632, `cmpdiag/`).
  - Setup: ISLA 0.9.0 (azc_full_isla_seed42, epoch 250) and ISLA-DTT (azc_full_dtt_seed42, epoch 155, its latest
    checkpoint; that lane is still training), on 20 `full` test cases each.
  - The compiled and eager paths agree to a median d = RMS(compiled − eager) / RMS(target) of 1.8e-6 (ISLA 0.9.0) and
    3.4e-6 (ISLA-DTT). The maxima are 4.8e-6 (ISLA 0.9.0) and 6.9e-4 (ISLA-DTT case 00078: 0.20 of that case's float64
    floor, per-field ratio ≤ 0.22; its query-independence probe reads 1.2e-3 compiled against 1.8e-4 eager).
  - On the 20 `full` test cases measured, for both ISLA 0.9.0 (epoch 250) and ISLA-DTT (epoch 155), every block sees
    N = 400,000 tokens (N % 4 = 0) and the geometry runs in the fused kernel. Either fact alone keeps the
    pytorch/pytorch#195845 fusion from firing at the scorer's inputs. N is 400,000 only when a case has more than
    200,000 boundary faces (these 20 have 0.29-1.39 M). Face counts were not recorded for the other splits (non-box
    ducts included) or for the training draw, so on those cases the protection rests on the fused kernel.
  - The geometry kernel is chosen by the model's configuration and device, not by the case. At its first forward pass
    ISLA picks the fused kernel when the inputs are on CUDA, Triton is importable and the configuration's constraints
    hold (one to four per-point vectors counting the global directions, at most 1,024 slices, no rank-2 inputs), and
    caches the choice per device (physicsnemo/experimental/models/isla/model.py: the 'Kernels' paragraph of the ISLA
    docstring, lines 242-258, and `ISLA.resolve_geo_kernel`). The fused kernel excludes the faulty fusion, whose first
    condition is the eager geometry region (COMPILE-AF, @sec-nb-compiled-path-defect), so the protection holds on every
    AeroZoo case and training draw. So no AeroZoo lane is retrained (supervisor's decision, 2026-10-22).
  - PROBES-090's 4.9e-4 (azc_full_isla at epoch 155, eager against the infer.py scorer, two processes, 40 cases) is not
    reproduced by the compiled path here (epoch 250, same process: metric difference ≤ 6e-6). It is of the size of this
    family's float32 floor and of the run-to-run float32 nondeterminism (4.7e-4 on one bank_zero_to_cad case). Its
    source was not checked: that would mean reading the test-side score file. It stays unexplained.
- **Side finding: a percent-level float32 floor** on some AeroZoo cases.
  - Float32 eager differs from float64 eager by more than 1e-2 of RMS(target) on 4 of 20 ISLA 0.9.0 cases (up to 0.28
    on k; case metric up to 8 %) and on 6 of 20 ISLA-DTT cases (up to 0.044). AirfRANS shows at most 2.3e-4. The
    float64 pass may draw different boundary tokens inside the model, so this floor may include a draw difference and
    is not pure roundoff (`f32floor/PREREG.md`, amendment).
  - The cause is open: float32 geometry on raw-metre coordinates, or a network that is ill-conditioned there.
- **GeoTransolver 256 is about a zero predictor on pressure, and Transolver 512 × 16 about a zero predictor on every
  field** (`basecheck/`).
  - No pipeline bug was found: every field reaches the loss; no head is frozen: the pressure row of the output layer
    receives a non-zero gradient (median |grad| 0.54, 14, 0.0014 and 0.4 on the four runs checked); the normalization
    matches.
  - At epoch 250 the output weight rows for p, ν_t, k and ω are about 0 (weights and outputs measured on 4 of the 16
    baseline lanes: GeoTransolver 256 full s42, full s43, nonbox s42 and Transolver 512 × 16 full s42, on 30 cases
    each; the loss curves of all 16 lanes, both Transolver seeds included, sit at the zero-predictor plateau).
    Transolver 512 × 16 predicts a constant 0.010 Pa of pressure and about 0.02 m/s of velocity in every case: its
    documented floor (PREREG_v2 Q2), since it cannot see the inlet.
  - GeoTransolver 256 sees the inlet values and learns part of the velocity (cosine about 0.9). Pressure, though, has a
    median over cases of 1.00 on every split; its means are 1.00-1.25, which is no better than predicting zero.
  - Likely mechanism: under one dataset-wide scale, the training cases' RMS pressure spans 8 decades (2.6e-4 Pa to
    2.8e4 Pa). The case-relative loss scales each case's gradient by 1/RMS. On that argument the 100 cases with the
    smallest pressure RMS would carry 51 % of the gradient near the zero predictor (computed from the per-case RMS, not
    from measured gradients). The 3,332 cases are the union of the nonbox and crossflow training sets, not each lane's
    own training set. The step median of the pressure loss ends at 1.00-1.02 on all 16 lanes.
  - GeoTransolver 256's velocity is under-converged. It is still falling at epoch 250 (`full`: 0.88 → 0.59 over the
    last 50 epochs), and its seeds differ by about 2× (reynolds 0.48 against 0.94).
- **ISLA above 1 on pressure: an amplitude overshoot on crossflow, a shape error on non-box** (ISLA 0.9.0; `pdiag/`:
  30 random test cases per split, seed 42, plus seed 43 on nonbox and crossflow; `preddiag/`: 20 worst and 10 random
  crossflow cases).
  - *profile_crossflow* (pressure 2.66 [2.49]). ISLA 0.9.0 keeps the inlet direction but does not turn the flow toward
    the adjacent outlet (its mean is 24-31° off the true mean direction), and it drives the flow about 2× too fast: RMS
    speed ratio (predicted to true, RMS |u_pred| / RMS |u_true|) 2.07 / 1.86 on pdiag's 30 random cases; on
    preddiag's sample (20 worst + 10 random) ISLA reads 2.26 / 2.04 against 0.99 for GeoTransolver 256. The 1.42
    velocity L2 near √2 is a coincidence.
  - Read post hoc, its pressure follows from that overshoot: the affine fit p ≈ α p̂ + β of the prediction p̂ to the
    truth p gives β ≈ 0 and α·(speed ratio)² = 1.06 / 1.34 (about 1 when p̂ is too large by the square of the speed
    ratio). Dividing each case's p̂ by its own (speed ratio)² takes the median L2 over the 30 cases from 3.34 / 2.00 to
    0.33 / 0.36 (seed 42 / 43). By the pre-registered table (M2_methods (c),
    scratch/isla-review-2026-10-21/second-read-2026-10-22/M2_methods.md) this pattern matches no row: the offset share
    is 0.85 / 0.90, not small, and the mean-removed L2 is 1.21 / 0.59, not about 0.3. The amplitude reading rests on a
    post hoc test, dividing p̂ by (speed ratio)², and on pdiag's argument that the large offset share comes from
    scaling a pressure that is mostly a level (post hoc).
  - ISLA also does not hold p ≈ 0 at the adjacent outlet: near it, it predicts 1.2-1.8 RMS p, where the truth is
    0.017. Crossflow is the one layout whose outlet is adjacent to the inlet rather than opposite it.
  - *family_non_box* (pressure 2.77 [1.51]; velocity 0.53 [0.48]). This is a shape error, by family: affine residual
    0.79 / 0.75, corr 0.48 / 0.49. Opposed spheres and hemispheres overpredict by 1.3-7.5×, ducts mostly under-predict
    the pressure (RMS ratio 0.01-0.75), and bends (2 cases per seed) overshoot 6-9×. The 3.76 / 1.79 seed split is
    broad, not one case. Seed 42 is worse on 72 % of the 1,074 cases (per-case medians 1.68 against 1.10). The 10
    largest per-case gaps carry 0.25 of the 1.97 difference in the means; case 9c74 (52.7 / 7.7 across seeds) carries
    0.04 of it. In-model scales (`scales/`; z = log10 Re): most of the 20 worst nonbox cases have U, L and z inside the
    training ranges. 2 lie outside in L and 2 in z (9c74 among them: z above the training maximum). 9 of the 10
    velocity-worst ducts have a head velocity RMS below every training case, as do 40 % of all duct test cases.
  - On full, reynolds, blobs and bank_zero_to_cad the fit is clean: α = 0.97-0.98, offset share ≤ 4 %, speed ratio
    0.99-1.00.
  - Per-case pressure medians, ISLA 0.9.0: full 0.29, reynolds 0.54, blobs 0.42, bank_zero_to_cad 0.37, and
    profile_dual_inlet 0.79, the mirror of crossflow: speed ratio 0.49 (predicted to true RMS speed), pressure RMS
    ratio 0.37, offset share 0.70, an amplitude undershoot that stays below 1.
  - Reynolds split (`reynolds/`): ISLA 0.9.0's error grows with the distance above the training band. Velocity grows
    ×1.23 per decade (0.14 → 0.20) and pressure ×1.67 per decade (0.38 → 0.72). GeoTransolver 256 stays flat (velocity
    ×0.97 per decade at about 0.7, pressure ×1.01 per decade at about 1.0, the zero predictor). That flatness is not
    better extrapolation: GeoTransolver sits at the zero-predictor level on pressure and is under-converged on
    velocity, so it has no in-band skill to lose.

**Pending.** Two follow-ups are running and are not yet results: the cause of the float32 floor (float64 geometry with
float32 blocks, and the reverse; `f32floor/PREREG.md`, amended 11:29 EDT before its GPU job), and a head-only AdamW
scout of GeoTransolver 256's pressure collapse, which asks whether the Muon optimizer's fixed step limits it (`gtopt/`).
