## 2026-10-22 — AF-EXTRAP, AirfRANS's extrapolation splits at 0.9.0: registered summaries angle of attack "mixed / no difference" and Reynolds "ISLA extrapolates worse". Outside the angle-of-attack band ISLA 0.9.0's error grows less than GeoTransolver 256's and Transolver 512 × 16's on pressure and eddy viscosity (ρ = g_baseline ÷ g_ISLA 1.5-4.2); outside the Reynolds band it grows more on pressure, and in a post hoc inference-only test, holding its Reynolds input at the edge of the training range halves its below-band pressure error, which suggests that its learned dependence on log Re extrapolates poorly {#sec-nb-af-extrap-090}

**Setting.** AirfRANS ships two extrapolation splits: `reynolds` (504 training airfoils at Re 3e6-5e6; 496 test airfoils at
2e6-3e6 and 5e6-6e6) and `aoa` (804 training airfoils at −2.5 to 12.5 degrees; 196 outside). The only earlier run
(@sec-nb-airfrans-extrap-verdict) used an old ISLA and the windowed interior draw. Here four architectures ran at their current
AirfRANS reference configurations, changing only the split: ISLA 0.9.0, ISLA-DTT 0.9.0, GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16,
two seeds each, 500 epochs, 100,000 interior points, scored in float32 on the test side. Every fitted constant was refit on each
split's training side, for every arm: ISLA's Reynolds standardization and ν_t scale, the ν_t target statistics, and the
baselines' standardized freestream speed. The ISLA-family lanes trained on the fixed compiled path (code_cmpaf_fix;
@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect), after the first launch was cancelled for the compiled-path defect; their in-distribution reference is
the fix-trained full_test standing r090fix_af_*. The rules were registered before any score
(scratch/isla-af-extrap-2026-10-21/PREREG.md, md5 35d3349d through §13): §6 on 2026-10-20; S-RE (§11) before submission; §12,
before any score, replaced the ISLA family's in-distribution reference with the fix-trained r090fix_af_* standings; the clamp test
(§13) was written after the scores were read and before it ran. R1 compares the test errors (band max(3 %, 2σ), seed ranges
separate), R2 the penalty ρ = g_baseline ÷ g_ISLA with g = test error ÷ in-distribution error (band max(1.10, e^{2√2σ}), both seed
pairs agreeing; a task summary needs 4 of 6 cells and none against).

**What we saw.**

| arm | in distribution p / v / ν_t | Reynolds test | penalty g | AoA test | penalty g |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA 0.9.0 | 0.0122 / 0.0063 / 0.0156 | 0.0389 / 0.0195 / 0.0457 | 3.18 / 3.08 / 2.94 | 0.0485 / 0.0163 / 0.0538 | 3.97 / 2.57 / 3.46 |
| ISLA-DTT 0.9.0 | 0.0127 / 0.0071 / 0.0215 | 0.0335 / 0.0175 / 0.0590 | 2.65 / 2.46 / 2.75 | 0.0528 / 0.0168 / 0.0745 | 4.17 / 2.36 / 3.47 |
| GeoTransolver 256 | 0.0109 / 0.0400 / 0.0171 | 0.0246 / 0.0466 / 0.0467 | 2.26 / 1.17 / 2.74 | 0.1809 / 0.0880 / 0.2313 | 16.6 / 2.20 / 13.5 |
| Transolver 512 × 16 | 0.0109 / 0.0297 / 0.0178 | 0.0274 / 0.0381 / 0.0466 | 2.51 / 1.28 / 2.62 | 0.0856 / 0.0493 / 0.0938 | 7.85 / 1.66 / 5.27 |

: AirfRANS extrapolation splits, relative L2 error, seed means over two seeds, float32 (scratch/isla-af-extrap-2026-10-21/RESULTS.md, section 1). {#tbl-nb-af-extrap-090}

- *AoA.* ISLA 0.9.0 leads GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16 on every field of the test set (baseline ÷ ISLA 1.7-5.4).
  Its error grows far less on pressure (ρ 4.19 against GeoTransolver, 1.98 against Transolver) and eddy viscosity (3.92, 1.52).
  Velocity reads "no difference" against GeoTransolver and "worse" against Transolver (0.646), so the registered summary is
  "mixed / no difference". That one cell is floor-driven. Post hoc: ISLA's velocity excess is smaller than Transolver 512 × 16's
  under both measures (ISLA ÷ Transolver: additive 0.51, quadrature 0.38). The registered ρ penalizes ISLA's 4.7× lower
  in-distribution floor (Transolver 512 × 16's own g is 1.66). Post hoc: the baselines' per-case errors rise steadily with the
  angle outside the band (Spearman 0.68-0.97; GeoTransolver 256's slope below the band 0.24 / 0.063 / 0.21 per degree), ISLA
  0.9.0's much less (Spearman 0.19-0.66; slope 0.067 / 0.016 / 0.031).
- *Reynolds.* ISLA 0.9.0 trails GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16 on pressure (baseline ÷ ISLA 0.63, 0.70), leads on
  velocity (2.39, 1.96) and is level on eddy viscosity. R2 reads ISLA extrapolates worse on pressure (ρ 0.709, 0.789) and
  velocity (0.379, 0.417), so the registered summary is "ISLA extrapolates worse". Post hoc, the pressure result holds under
  every measure we tried (ISLA ÷ baseline, above 1 means ISLA's excess is larger: additive 1.95 / 1.62, quadrature 1.68 / 1.47;
  matched-case ρ = g_baseline ÷ g_ISLA on the 103 full_test cases outside the band, below 1 means ISLA's error grows more:
  0.69 / 0.70). The matched-case g still compares a 504-case model with an 800-case model. Post hoc: the velocity cells depend
  on the measure. Under the additive excess ISLA's is still larger (1.98 / 1.56); under the quadrature excess it is smaller
  (0.77 / 0.77). Both baselines' in-distribution velocity error is 4.7-6.3× ISLA's, which caps their penalty. The registered
  data-size control, S-RE, trains the same architectures in distribution on a fixed 504-case subset of full_train. S-RE
  (registered beside the verdict; it controls case count only, not the 2.2× lower density of cases per decade of Re, and ρ_504
  is still a ratio of ratios) leaves the Transolver 512 × 16 pressure cell inside the band (ρ_504 = g_baseline ÷ g_ISLA 0.898,
  no difference), which is consistent with training-set size. The GeoTransolver 256 cell stays worse (ρ_504 0.716). Post hoc:
  the gap is mostly below the band (per-side ρ = g_baseline ÷ g_ISLA on pressure, below 0.62 / 0.78, above 0.92 / 0.81). Below
  the band ISLA's pressure error grows 0.62 per decade of Re, against 0.16 and 0.32.
- *ISLA-DTT 0.9.0* reads "no difference" against ISLA 0.9.0 on all six penalty cells of both tasks; its Reynolds penalty is
  smaller in point estimate (R3 ρ = g_DTT ÷ g_ISLA 0.832 / 0.799 / 0.936), inside the band.
- *Input reach (post hoc, registered before running).* ISLA 0.9.0 reads z = (log10 Re − m) / s with the split's constants:
  training −2.05 to 1.80, test down to −4.85. GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16 read the standardized speed: training
  −1.80 to 1.75, test down to −3.57. Clamping each model's input to its training range at inference halves ISLA's below-band
  pressure error (post hoc, clamped ÷ native over the 241 below-band cases whose z the clamp changes, both seeds, beyond 2σ:
  0.47×; ISLA-DTT 0.58×; over all 254 below-band cases 0.477 and 0.590). ISLA's z uses its own length unit L, so 45 test
  cases (13 of them below the band) lie inside its z range and are unchanged. Post hoc: clamped, the four architectures' below-band
  pressure errors meet. On the same 254 below-band cases they are ISLA 0.9.0 0.0260, ISLA-DTT 0.0262, GeoTransolver 256 0.0261
  and Transolver 512 × 16 0.0248 (0.025-0.026), with the baselines' standardized speed clamped to their training range
  [−1.80, 1.75]. On ν_t the clamp costs the baselines 2.2-3.3× and ISLA 0.9.0 1.10-1.35× (clamped ÷ native; within noise below
  the band), since ISLA's ν_t is in units of U L. ISLA-DTT's ν_t below the band improves (0.87×, within noise) and worsens above
  it (1.50×).

**Reading.** At 0.9.0, AirfRANS's angle-of-attack extrapolation again favors ISLA 0.9.0, consistent with the 2026-09-22 reading
at the old version. One post hoc reading: ISLA 0.9.0 is rotation-equivariant, so an out-of-band angle of attack is, for it, only
a new relative angle between body and flow. GeoTransolver 256 and Transolver 512 × 16 read the freestream direction as an input
whose values also lie outside their training range. The baselines' steady per-case growth with angle (Spearman up to 0.97) fits
that reading. It is not tested here. Reynolds extrapolation does not favor ISLA 0.9.0: its pressure error grows more than the
baselines' below the training band. The clamp points at how ISLA reads its own Reynolds input far outside its training range.
That is a hypothesis: the clamp also lowers Transolver 512 × 16's below-band pressure error (0.65×, beyond 2σ), and it does not
test the flow features. The hypothesis is about reach: a log scale puts the lowest-Re test case 2.8 training standard deviations
(z units) beyond the edge of its training range, where the baselines' linear speed puts it 1.8 (in training ranges: 0.73 against
0.50). A linear first layer absorbs any fixed affine scale. So a fixed rescaling, such as the z = log10(Re/1e6) control, cannot
change how far the test cases sit outside the training range in units of the training spread. That control (about 57 GPU-h) is
still a log coordinate, so it cannot test this reach hypothesis; it tests only whether a different scale changes what training
learns, which is plausible but untested. The direct test is an ISLA 0.9.0 arm whose Reynolds input is linear in Re, standardized
on the training side like the baselines' speed. On this split ν is constant, so that input is the baselines' own coordinate up to
ISLA's per-case length unit. As registered, it places the lowest-Re case 0.45 training ranges out instead of 0.73. If ISLA's
below-band pressure growth then falls to the baselines' level, the log coordinate's reach is the cause. Both training controls
are running and have no result yet: ISLA 0.9.0 with the dataset-independent scale z = log10(Re/1e6), which tests the
training-dynamics part, and ISLA 0.9.0 with a linear, training-side-standardized Re, which tests the log coordinate's reach
below the band, each registered before it ran (PREREG.md §14 and §14b). Two seeds per arm, so each σ pair has one degree of
freedom (the band pools 8 pairs). The Reynolds and AoA pressure and ν_t results are large against those bands; the velocity
cells depend on the measure. With AeroZoo's `reynolds` split (AZ-DECIDE), this is the second dataset for the Reynolds question.

## 2026-10-23 — REF-090 standings on the fixed path: eager-trained ISLA 0.9.0 on AirfRANS, Tensile2d and the lug; the lug's training-path read is (c) {#sec-nb-ref090-standings}

**Question** (REF-090 R2 and PREREG §§12-15). On AirfRANS, Tensile2d and the lug, ISLA's per-block compile
trained under pytorch#195845 (@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect). Which rows become the ISLA 0.9.0 standings
there, and does the fixed compiled path train the model's own (eager) function? The Tensile2d control read
(b) on weak evidence (@sec-nb-ref090-t2d-control). Under the registered consequence, the standings on all
three datasets are eager-trained rows: two seeds each on AirfRANS and the lug, four on Tensile2d. Every
row below is scored fully eager, in float32, at epoch 500.

Native relative L2, arithmetic seed means. Every ratio is a ratio of arithmetic seed means; the last two columns are

44/45 are ATTRIB-090's att_t2dz_base rows. The baselines are the book's standing arms.

**The lug read: (c), as registered** (PREREG §15). Fix-trained and bug-trained separate cleanly on the lug: fix ÷ bug is
0.768, at 2.2 × 2 SE, with both fix-trained seeds below both bug-trained ones. So the lug read was registered as the
decisive test of the fixed path. The eager-trained pair, though, lies 25 percent apart (0.001376, 0.001771). As ratios
of arithmetic seed means, eager ÷ fix-trained is 1.083 (0.31 × 2 SE; 1.074 as a ratio of geometric seed means, the form
ATTRIB-090 quotes) and eager ÷ bug-trained is 0.831 (0.66 × 2 SE), so the eager rows match both. Both eager seeds lie
below both bug-trained seeds, by a hair (0.001771 against 0.001780), and the point estimate leans toward (a). Posed ÷
native: 1.246 / 1.619 eager-trained, 1.346 / 1.383 fix-trained, 1.194 / 1.105 bug-trained.

**The AirfRANS read: (c) for ISLA 0.9.0 and for ISLA-DTT** (PREREG §14). On AirfRANS, fix-trained and
bug-trained ISLA 0.9.0 agree within 2.4 percent: 1.024 on pressure, 0.985 on velocity, 0.998 on eddy viscosity. So this
read could not tell (a) from (b), as expected. Eager-trained ÷ fix-trained is 1.021 / 1.005 / 0.986 (|d| / 2SE 0.12,
0.11, 0.25), and eager-trained ÷ bug-trained is 1.045 / 0.989 / 0.985 (0.27, 0.25, 0.21). All three training paths lie
within 5 percent, and every seed range overlaps. Eager-trained, posed ÷ native is 1.0022 to 1.0025 on pressure, 1.0016
on velocity and 1.0000 on eddy viscosity. For ISLA-DTT the paths separate on pressure: eager-trained 0.01241 lies below
both fix-trained 0.01265 (eager ÷ fix-trained 0.981, 1.37 × 2 SE) and bug-trained 0.01410 (eager ÷ bug-trained 0.880,
2.97 × 2 SE), so pressure reads (c); velocity reads (c) (1.007 and 0.968) and eddy viscosity (a) (0.958 at 0.28 × 2 SE,
0.922 at 1.26 × 2 SE). One field of three reads (a), so ISLA-DTT reads (c). Every ratio is of arithmetic seed means
(eag_af_dtt.md, scorers 350103 and 350296). Eager-trained ISLA-DTT, posed ÷ native is 1.0017 to 1.0022 on pressure,
1.0010 to 1.0012 on velocity and 1.0001 on eddy viscosity.

**Beside the rules.**

- MECH-090 (scratch/isla-mech090-2026-10-22/RESULTS.md) puts the fixed path's float32 gradients at a one-ulp eager floor

**Standings.** AirfRANS takes r090eag_af_isla, Tensile2d r090eag_t2dz 42-45 and the lug r090eag_lug_isla. On the lug
ISLA 0.9.0 leads both baselines, and on Tensile2d it trails both on displacement and stress. On AirfRANS ISLA 0.9.0
trails both on pressure (0.874) and leads both on velocity (6.29, 4.67) and eddy viscosity (1.11, 1.16); against the
compiled-path rows (baseline ÷ ISLA 0.919 / 0.919 on pressure, 1.080 / 1.127 on eddy viscosity), baseline ÷ ISLA fell 5
percent on pressure and rose 3 percent on eddy viscosity. The other datasets' standings are unchanged
(@sec-nb-ref090-r1).

## 2026-10-23 — ATTRIB-090, stage 2: on AirfRANS ISLA's gain over its earlier form comes from standardizing the global input, not from its scales; on the lug the fix-trained 0.9.0 leads the fix-trained CONT (directional) {#sec-nb-attrib090-stage2}

**Question** (ATTRIB-090, scratch/isla-attrib090-2026-10-21/PREREG.md §§5, 9-11). @sec-nb-attrib090-t2d settled Tensile2d. On
AirfRANS, one arm carried the whole step from E2's CONT code to ISLA 0.9.0: NOSC, which removes ISLA's declared scales. NOSC
also feeds the raw inlet speed (m/s), unstandardized, where 0.9.0 feeds the standardized log Reynolds number, so it was
confounded (@sec-airfrans-attribution). Stage 2 splits the confound. It adds ISLA-DTT's own reading of the scales and the lug's
reads against a CONT retrained under the compile fix. Every arm and base is trained on the fixed compiled path
(@sec-nb-compiled-path-defect), except where a row says otherwise. AirfRANS: 200 test cases at 100,000 points; the lug: 600
cases at 200,000 cells; float32, epoch 500, seeds 42 and 43, native.

**Rule.** Δ is an arm's mean log error minus that of B, the base. B is ISLA 0.9.0 (r090fix_af_isla; r090fix_af_dtt for
ISLA-DTT; r090fix_lug_isla). σ is pooled over the arms. An arm moves a field if |Δ| ≥ 2 SE and the effect is at least 5
%. φ is Δ divided by the step from CONT to B. For NOSC-STD (§10): φ ≤ 0.3 means input standardization carries the
field's step, φ ≥ 0.7 means the scales carry it, and values between mean both share it. If NOSC-STD does not move a
field by R1, that field reads "input standardization carries the step" whatever φ.

| AirfRANS arm (ISLA) | what it changes from 0.9.0 | ÷ 0.9.0 (p / v / nut) | φ | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONT (E2, retrained) | the earlier code | 1.286 / 1.353 / 1.411 | 1 | the step |
| NOSC | no scales, raw speed | 1.232 / 1.354 / 1.331 | 0.83 / 1.00 / 0.83 | carries it (confounded) |
| RAWU | scales kept, raw speed in place of the log Reynolds number | 1.292 / 1.351 / 1.333 | 1.02 / 0.99 / 0.83 | carries it (confounded) |
| NUT0 | scales kept, eddy viscosity without the units U L | 0.982 / 1.009 / 0.990 | ≈ 0 | no measurable effect |
| **NOSC-STD** | no scales, standardized speed | **1.003 / 1.029 / 1.043** | **0.01 / 0.10 / 0.12** | **no measurable effect** |
| **STDU** (read later, below) | scales kept, standardized speed in place of the log Reynolds number | **1.008 / 1.015 / 0.995** | **0.03 / 0.05 / −0.02** | **no measurable effect** |

The ÷ 0.9.0 column is exp(Δ), a ratio of geometric seed means.

**Verdict: input standardization carries the AirfRANS step on all three fields; the scales do not.** If the inlet speed
is standardized as the baselines read it, a 0.9.0 model without ISLA's scales is as accurate as 0.9.0. That model has no
Reynolds number, eddy viscosity in the dataset's units and a bf16 head. The step from CONT to 0.9.0 (0.9.0 ÷ CONT 0.778
/ 0.739 / 0.709, a ratio of geometric seed means) came from replacing an unstandardized dimensional input, the raw speed
of 31 to 94 m/s that every token's seed read, by an O(1) input. RAWU and NUT0 agree. On AirfRANS ν is constant and L
nearly so, so the log Reynolds number is a monotone reparametrization of the speed. The gain is real and has a sound
reason, but it is a side effect of the scales change, not of its physics.

**ISLA-DTT** (B = r090fix_af_dtt):
- DTT-CONT ÷ B = 1.109 / 1.169 / 1.026, against arm D of @sec-nb-anchor-verdict (bug-trained, scored eager) 1.103 / 1.218 / 1.047.
  Exact geometry and CONT did not move ISLA-DTT.
- R5 reads ρ_CONT = 0.895 on pressure. So the reversal of the ISLA / ISLA-DTT order happened in the 0.9.0 bundle. At
  CONT, ISLA-DTT led by about 10 percent. At 0.9.0, fix-trained, ISLA-DTT ÷ ISLA is 1.035 / 1.126 / 1.381 (a ratio of
  arithmetic seed means, REF-090's definition).
- DTT-NOSC ÷ B = 1.264 / 1.225 / 1.158. It carries the same raw-speed confound, so it is most likely the standardization as well.
  No ISLA-DTT standardization arm was run.
- DTT-NOSC is 14 percent worse than DTT-CONT on pressure, with the raw speed in both. So for ISLA-DTT the rest of the bundle costs
  about 12 percent, which interacting ISLA does not pay. Two mirrors, DTT-SDF and DTT-QEMB, are in flight to find which part.
- Beside the rules: the compile defect had cost ISLA-DTT about 10 percent at 0.9.0 (fix ÷ bug-trained 0.898 on pressure). It
  cost interacting ISLA about nothing.

**The lug** (directional; labelled "fix-trained"; the lug training-path read gave (c), with no reading, @sec-nb-ref090-standings):
- With CONT retrained, CONT ÷ B is **1.151**. Fix-trained 0.9.0 leads fix-trained CONT by 13 percent, both its seeds
  below both of CONT's. Bug-trained, REF-090 had read 0.9.0 ÷ CONT at 1.092.
- The retrained CONT carries a label (deviation 4): "trained under code_gcont + TORCHINDUCTOR_MIX_ORDER_REDUCTION=0; its compiled
  block 2 deviates from eager on 5 of 100 lug cases, up to 4.5e-4 of the block's update". The per-block option gives the same
  deviation, so this is a second, unidentified fusion difference in that code's lug graph. 0.9.0's per-block path reads at most
  4.4e-7 on the lug.
- L-FLIP (E2's winding) reads 1.088 and does not move (2 SE = 0.087). A zero-training test reproduces B's predictions to
  a median 1.5e-4 of the target per case (at most 4.7e-4) and its case-mean metric to 0.3 percent: negate the
  orientation-carrying weight columns and run on the flipped lug. Training is equivariant under that negation (Muon's
  Newton-Schulz and AdamW are both sign-equivariant). So the flip is a reparametrization up to the tie residual below,
  and 1.088 reads as seed noise.
- The residual sits at 8,428 interior closest-feature ties (2.2 percent), which the float32 BVH resolves by search order
  (@tbl-lug-ties). The tie rule MEDIAL-TIE is on the agenda.
- L-ENC (CONT's encoding replaced by the sign·log one, trained eager) reads 1.141 against B: it moves (directional,
  registered base). Against the eager-trained base r090eag_lug_isla it reads 1.062 (exp(Δ)), within that base's own seed
  gap: its larger seed is 1.29 times its smaller (REF-090 gives the same pair as 25 percent apart, relative to their
  mean). The lug's training path moves its error by as much as the effect. Eager ÷ fix-trained 0.9.0 is 1.083 as a ratio
  of arithmetic seed means (REF-090's definition), or 1.074 geometric.

**Next.** STDU (scales kept, with the standardized speed in place of the log Reynolds number) is the last check of the AirfRANS
reading. DTT-SDF and DTT-QEMB locate ISLA-DTT's bundle cost. All three are in flight. Proposed model change, not made: ISLA
refuses, or standardizes by fitted constants, any rank-0 global without units, so that no configuration can feed a raw
dimensional scalar again.

**For the book.** On AirfRANS, ISLA 0.9.0's accuracy over its earlier form comes from feeding its one global scalar in
standardized form, not from its declared physical scales. Where the Reynolds number varies through the inlet speed
alone, the scales are one principled way to get that standardization, not a source of accuracy. Whether they add
accuracy where the Reynolds number varies widely, as on AeroZoo, is untested: ATTRIB-090 has no AeroZoo arm. On the lug,
once the compile fault is fixed, 0.9.0 leads its predecessor, and the winding flip is a reparametrization.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-23 (scratch/isla-book-1023/SECOND_READ_ATTRIB_STAGE2.md).*

**Later (2026-10-23).** STDU read under the same rule, with B and the step as above (scratch/isla-attrib090-2026-10-21/RESULTS.md
§2d). σ, now pooled over nine degrees of freedom (0.076 / 0.048 / 0.056), leaves every reading above unchanged. STDU keeps
ISLA's scales (the inlet velocity as the velocity source, eddy viscosity in units of U L, the fp32 head) and reads the
standardized inlet speed, (U_inf_mag − 62.116) / 17.914, in place of the standardized log Reynolds number. STDU ÷ 0.9.0 is
1.008 / 1.015 / 0.995 (exp(Δ), a ratio of geometric seed means), φ 0.03 / 0.05 / −0.02: no measurable effect on any field
(posed 1.008 / 1.015, the same). With the scales on, a standardized speed serves as well as the standardized log Reynolds
number, while RAWU, the same with the raw speed, carries the whole step. So on AirfRANS the form of the global scalar (log
Re or speed) does not matter; its standardization does. This closes the AirfRANS attribution: the gain from CONT to 0.9.0
is the standardization of the one global scalar. NOSC-STD and STDU sit at 0.9.0's level; NOSC and RAWU, the raw speed without
and with the scales, sit at CONT's. Label: fix-trained.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-23 (scratch/isla-book-noon-2026-10-23/SECOND_READ_STDU.md).*

**Later (2026-10-24).** The two ISLA-DTT mirrors read under PREREG §11 as amended by §12 (md5 dcd52514), the supervisor's
amendment, written at 20:17 EDT 2026-10-23 before any mirror score existed (the mirrors were read at 23:37 EDT), which replaced §11's label, since that label had
the sign of a gain (scratch/isla-attrib090-2026-10-21/RESULTS.md §3c, md5 e01a94de). B is fix-trained 0.9.0 ISLA-DTT; the
cost to locate is C_f = log(DTT-NOSC ÷ DTT-CONT), +0.131 on pressure and +0.121 on nut (1.140 and 1.129 as ratios;
velocity's 1.048 is below the 5 percent floor, so no cost is located on velocity), and ψ = −Δ ÷ C_f. DTT-SDF (the stored
signed distance and its normals put back, also in ISLA-DTT's tree read) reads ÷ 0.9.0 1.040 / 1.043 / 1.009 and ÷ DTT-CONT
0.938 / 0.892 / 0.984; DTT-QEMB (the reduced form's prediction-point embedding) reads ÷ 0.9.0 0.983 / 0.994 / 0.949 and ÷
DTT-CONT 0.887 / 0.850 / 0.925 (p / v / nut; exp(Δ), ratios of geometric seed means). With the mirrors pooled in, σ is
0.042 / 0.029 / 0.064 (6 dof), so neither mirror moves any field: "no measurable effect" (φ against ISLA-DTT's own step
+0.38 / +0.27 / +0.36 and −0.16 / −0.04 / −2.07). By §12, neither carries ISLA-DTT's bundle cost on pressure or nut (ψ −0.30
and +0.13 on pressure, −0.07 and +0.44 on nut; SE ÷ C_f 0.32 and 0.53). Posed reads the same. So the cost on pressure, C_f = +0.131 (DTT-NOSC 14 percent worse than DTT-CONT), is not in either piece alone, as far as two seeds can show. Beside the rule: at this σ only ψ ≥ 0.64 on
pressure would register; the 2 SE upper ends rule out the stored signed distance as carrying even half the pressure cost

## 2026-10-23 — AF-EXTRAP LRE and LIN, the Reynolds-input training controls: the registered Reynolds summary "ISLA extrapolates worse" stands; beside it, ISLA 0.9.0 trained with its Reynolds input on the fixed scale z = log10(Re_ISLA / 1e6) has 0.53-0.58× the fitted-scale model's below-band pressure error (registered reading "the fixed scale helps"), and with a linear, training-standardized Reynolds input 0.62-0.63× ("helps") {#sec-nb-af-lre-verdict}

**Setting.** On AirfRANS's `reynolds` split, ISLA 0.9.0's pressure error grew more than GeoTransolver 256's and
Transolver 512 × 16's outside the training band (@sec-nb-af-extrap-090). The registered summary was "ISLA extrapolates
worse" (pressure ρ = g_baseline ÷ g_ISLA 0.709 against GeoTransolver 256, 0.789 against Transolver 512 × 16), and it
stands. Post hoc, the growth was concentrated below the band (pressure error 0.62 per decade of Re, against 0.16 and
0.32), and an inference-only clamp of ISLA's Reynolds input z to its training range (PREREG §13, registered before it
ran) cut ISLA's below-band pressure error to 0.477× (clamped ÷ native, ratio of two-seed arithmetic means over the 254
below-band cases). ISLA read z = (log10 Re − m) / s, with m and s fitted on the 504 training airfoils (s = 0.062, so z
spans about ±2 in training and reaches −4.85 on the test side). Two training controls were registered before any of
their runs (scratch/isla-af-extrap-2026-10-21/PREREG.md §14, §14b; md5 5b38aa09 after §14b). Each is afxf ISLA's lane
(fix-trained, two seeds, 500 epochs) with only z changed. LRE uses z = log10(Re_ISLA / 1e6), a dataset-independent fixed
scale set as `isla_constants.reynolds: {mean: 6.0, std: 1.0}` in
examples/cfd/external_aerodynamics/unified_external_aero_recipe/datasets/airfrans_uvolume_2d_reynolds_lre.yaml (on
psharpe/isla since commit bb991f73e; md5 af151886), with no code change; z spans 0.096 to 0.335 in training. LIN is a
diagnostic, not a candidate (a one-line change of ISLA's model code that removes the log10, committed to no branch): z =
(Re_ISLA − m) / s, linear in Re and standardized on the training side, which puts the lowest-Re test case 1.73 training
standard deviations beyond the training edge, against 2.81 for the fitted log scale and 1.78 for the baselines'
standardized speed. Re_ISLA = U L / ν uses ISLA's own length.

**What we saw.**

| arm | Reynolds test p / v / ν_t | below-band pressure ÷ afxf ISLA (s42, s43) | in-band fit ÷ afxf ISLA (training cases) | below-band pressure slope [relative L2 per decade of Re] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA 0.9.0, fitted log scale (afxf) | 0.0389 / 0.0195 / 0.0457 | 1 | 1 | 0.62 |
| LRE, fixed log scale | 0.0246 / 0.0111 / 0.0364 | 0.530, 0.576: **helps** | 0.91 / 0.94 / 0.94: passes | 0.16 |
| LIN, linear standardized Re | 0.0311 / 0.0161 / 0.0419 | 0.620, 0.632: **helps** | 1.02 / 1.00 / 0.99: passes | 0.23 |
| GeoTransolver 256 | 0.0246 / 0.0466 / 0.0467 | | | 0.16 |
| Transolver 512 × 16 | 0.0274 / 0.0381 / 0.0466 | | | 0.32 |

: AirfRANS `reynolds` split, relative L2, float32, 100,000 interior points, final checkpoints (epoch 500). Test errors: the 496 test airfoils, arithmetic means of seeds 42 and 43. Below-band ratio: per seed, the case-mean pressure error over the 254 test airfoils below Re 3e6, arm ÷ afxf ISLA (registered reading (a); bar ≤ 0.8 on both seeds). In-band fit: ratio of two-seed means on the 504 training airfoils, scored eager (registered guard (b); bar ≤ 1.05 on every field; fit inside the band, not generalization). Slope: least squares of the two-seed-mean per-case error against decades below Re 3e6. Data: scratch/isla-af-extrap-2026-10-21/lre.json, afx_results.json, posthoc.json (RESULTS.md §6). {#tbl-nb-af-lre}

- Both controls pass the registered bar (≤ 0.8 on both seeds), so the registered joint reading is **"both help"**: the
  log coordinate's reach and the training dynamics of a narrow fitted spread both contribute. Post hoc: the fixed log
  scale helps more (per seed 0.530 / 0.576, against LIN's 0.620 / 0.632).
- Beside the rules (PREREG §14 reading (c), post hoc): the R2 rule with LRE in ISLA's place reads "no difference" on
  pressure against GeoTransolver 256 (ρ = g_baseline ÷ g_LRE 1.12; band ×1.195) and "LRE extrapolates better" against
  Transolver 512 × 16 (ρ 1.25; seed pairs 1.26, 1.23). LRE has no full-split run, so g_LRE divides LRE's test error by
  ISLA's fix-trained in-distribution error (r090fix_af_isla). On the training airfoils LRE's pressure error is 0.91×
  afxf ISLA's, so the borrowed reference may favor LRE. LRE's test-set pressure error is level with GeoTransolver 256's
  (GeoTransolver 256 ÷ LRE 0.998) and with Transolver 512 × 16's (1.11), and LRE leads both on velocity (baseline ÷ LRE
  4.20 and 3.43, against 2.39 and 1.96 for afxf ISLA). The velocity cells still read "LRE extrapolates worse" (ρ 0.664,
  0.731); post hoc, as for afxf ISLA, the baselines' in-distribution velocity error (0.030-0.040) is already close to
  their test error, which caps their penalty (RESULTS.md §3b).
- Beside the rules (PREREG §14 reading (d), a post hoc diagnostic): clamping LRE's z to its training range lowers its
  below-band pressure error only to 0.876× (s42 0.859, s43 0.894; ratio of two-seed means over the 254 below-band
  cases), inside §13's noise band (|ln 0.876| = 0.13 against 2σ = 0.14), against 0.477× for afxf ISLA on the same cases,
  and raises velocity 1.63× and ν_t 2.13×. By §14 (d)'s criterion, LRE no longer extrapolates harmfully in z.
- Post hoc: one LRE seed-42 test case just above the band, airFoil2D_SST_78.545_-2.454_3.406_6.14_0.0_5.302 (Re 5.03e6;
  inside LRE's training z range, so the clamp leaves it unchanged), has relative L2 p 0.85, v 0.35, ν_t 10.7 (seed 43:
  0.24 / 0.057 / 0.14; afxf ISLA seed 42: 0.16 / 0.040 / 0.055). The table's ν_t mean includes it: without it LRE seed
  42's test-set ν_t is 0.0251 instead of 0.0466, against seed 43's 0.0262, so this one case makes LRE's seed gap on ν_t.
  It lies outside reading (a)'s population (below the band).

**Reading.** Post hoc reading (AirfRANS only, two seeds, fix-trained ISLA): how ISLA encodes its Reynolds input sets
most of its Reynolds pressure penalty here. The registered joint reading, "both", splits it between the log coordinate's
reach (LIN helps) and the training dynamics of a narrow fitted spread (LRE helps more). A fixed affine rescaling cannot
change how far a test case sits outside the training range. Post hoc, untested as a mechanism: it can change what
training learns. On the fitted scale z spans about ±2, on the fixed one about ±0.12 around 0.22, and LRE's below-band
pressure slope is 0.16 per decade against the fitted scale's 0.62. The fixed scale is also the dataset-independent input
contract the program wants for cross-dataset training. A linear Reynolds number helps less, and it could not span
AeroZoo's five decades. Two seeds per arm, AirfRANS only, ISLA family fix-trained.

**For the book.** On the AirfRANS Reynolds split (two seeds, fix-trained ISLA), the registered summary "ISLA
extrapolates worse" stands. Beside it, two training controls registered before they ran show that the scale of ISLA's
Reynolds input sets most of its pressure penalty. With the Reynolds number in ISLA's own length unit read on a fixed
scale, log10(Re_ISLA / 10^6) with no fitted mean or spread, ISLA's pressure error below the training band is 0.53-0.58×
its value with the fitted scale (per seed), its test-set pressure error is level with GeoTransolver's (GeoTransolver ÷
ISLA 0.998), and it leads both baselines on velocity (baseline ÷ ISLA 3.4-4.2). A linear, training-standardized Reynolds
number helps less (0.62-0.63×). Recommendation, not a result: adopt the fixed scale as ISLA's Reynolds input after a
confirming run on AeroZoo's Reynolds split.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-23 (scratch/isla-book-1023/SECOND_READ_AFX_LRE.md).*

## 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-23 — The geometry robustness bundle, a candidate for ISLA's geometry, not adopted: closest-feature ties take the least-norm direction, the wall distance is signed by the generalized winding number, the token draw is computed in float64 in the boundary's canonical frame, and a point is on the wall when its distance is within its own rounding bound; the review's blocker is fixed; the f32floor rerun reads "the fold sign removes ISLA's float32 floor on AeroZoo" as registered; on GB300 the training step costs 1.03 to 1.50 times the base's {#sec-nb-geo-bundle}

**Question.** Four steps of ISLA 0.9.0's geometry are decided by rounding, by the search order or by the dataset's axes
(@sec-medial-ties): the direction at a closest-feature tie, the sign of the wall distance at a fold, the cells the token draw
keeps, and the fixed cutoff `EPS = 1e-12` below which a point is on the wall. Can each become a function of the input mesh
alone, at a cost training can carry? Ten lanes worked on it: GEO-ROBUST (the GPU tie search and the on-wall rule),
TIE-REVIEW, TIE-FIX, TIE-FIX2, FOLD-SIGN, TOKEN-DRAW (with TOKEN-COST), ONWALL, GEO-BUNDLE, DV-COST and DV-COST2. Records:
scratch/isla-medial-tie-2026-10-22/DESIGN.md (sections a-h the tie rule's design and CPU prototype, i-j GEO-ROBUST phase 1,
k-q one per lane), scratch/isla-tie-review-2026-10-22/REVIEW.md, scratch/isla-fold-sign-2026-10-22/ (PREREG.md,
f32floor_tables.md, JOBS.md) and scratch/isla-token-draw-2026-10-22/DESIGN.md. The bundle is branch psharpe/isla-geo-bundle
at f13eb5ce0 (pushed, not merged into psharpe/isla).

**The rules.**

- *Ties* (DESIGN a, b, j; ea49d23ea, f56068328). A cell is in a query's tie set when its float64 distance interval
  `[D_k - E_k, D_k + E_k]` reaches the least upper end, with `E_k = (u_p + (3d + 4) u_64)(|x| + max_v |v|)` and `u_p` the
  unit roundoff of the queries' precision, and when its closest point is a local minimum on the surface (a valence count,
  with no tolerance). At a tie the direction is the minimum-norm element of the convex hull of the tied directions, the
  least-norm element of the Clarke generalized gradient: the midpoint of two, 0 where they cancel, kept unnormalized. Each
  cell's vertices are put in lexicographic order, the permutation's parity carrying the orientation, so the result does not
  depend on the numbering or the search order; a winding flip leaves the tie set and the direction bitwise unchanged and
  negates `d` and `sign(d) u` bitwise. The search is a Warp ball traversal of a BVH over the cells in 3-D and a brute force
  in 2-D.
- *On the wall* (f56068328; ONWALL 1e2c431cd). The direction is the least-norm point of the hull of the normals of the cells
  within the bound, computed odd in them. A query is on the wall when `D_min - E_min <= 0`, in place of `d_min <= 1e-12`.
- *The fold sign* (FOLD-SIGN 476521aac). Every off-wall `d` is `sign(sigma/2 - w(x))` times its magnitude, with `w` the
  generalized winding number (Jacobson, Kavan and Sorkine-Hornung 2013; Barill et al. 2018's far field at
  `WINDING_NUMBER_BETA = 2`, exact float64 solid angles at the near leaves; an exact float64 sum in 2-D) and `sigma` the sign
  of the enclosed signed volume. The pseudo-normals and the tie votes are deleted. The BVH is built in the boundary's
  canonical frame, so `w` is the same in every pose, and identical oriented cells count once.
- *The token draw* (TOKEN-DRAW 2042c50cf and c2db0445e; TOKEN-COST 3d9acfa63). The draw reads float64 centroids, the means of
  the input vertices, and float64 measures, the stored measure cast or else the areas of the float64 vertices; the Morton
  codes are taken in the boundary's canonical frame (`tree_read.canonical_frame` over every cell, in float64, its projections
  taken as column products). *(Note, 2026-10-26: the frame now comes from the library,
  `physicsnemo.mesh.spatial._frame.canonical_frame`, bitwise the same; @sec-nb-lib-sampling.)*
- *Normals in float64* (GEO-BUNDLE 96f1ad583). The on-wall and tie normals come from the float64 copy of the input vertices.

**The review's blocker and the fixes.** TIE-REVIEW blocked d3d9da49d. With float32 inputs, the on-wall directions were
float32 unit normals cast to float64, off unit length by about 1e-8 to 1e-7. The least-norm routine assumes exactly unit
inputs, so it decided that 0 lay in the hull and returned `u = 0`: at 210 of 642 vertices of a posed icosphere and 398 of 400
vertices of a 2-D ellipse, and, by the review's reading, at the lug's on-wall nodes (about 15 percent of its queries) and
Tensile2d's boundary nodes, which ones depending on rounding and so on pose. Its other findings: a zero-area cell holding an
on-wall node forced `u = 0` (major); a float32 distance that rounds to 0 at a tie lost its sign (minor); the group key could
overflow int64 (minor). TIE-FIX (19fb0a754) renormalizes the on-wall directions in float64, drops cells with a zero or
non-finite normal from the on-wall set, signs a tie's `d` on its float64 distance, and groups by a stacked unique. It also
found a defect the review had not listed: where directions nearly coincide, the routine took the least-norm candidate over
all faces and returned 0 when that one failed the optimality certificate, in float64 as well (a posed oriented torus: 10
on-wall points with `|u| < 0.5` in float64 and 342 in float32 before, 0 and 0 after). It now takes the least-norm candidate
among those that pass. TIE-FIX2 (34654e01d) adds the rule for a row where no candidate passes: the separating candidate with
the least duality gap, else 0. With unit inputs it fired on no row of the test meshes and of 84,000 random sets (DESIGN m.2).

## 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-25 — The outlet pressure gauge: ISLA holds AeroZoo's prescribed outlet pressure by construction on every test case; trained, it reads "no change" on `profile_crossflow` and `full` by the registered rule, though both crossflow seeds improved (pressure 0.46 and 0.27 of ISLA 0.9.0's); it costs 1.5 times ISLA's step as implemented, and it is not adopted {#sec-nb-outlet-gauge}

**Question.** On `profile_crossflow`, ISLA 0.9.0 predicts 1.2 to 1.8 times the case's RMS pressure next to the outlet, where
the truth is 0.017 (@sec-nb-azdiag). Incompressible flow fixes the pressure only up to a constant unless a boundary prescribes
it, and AeroZoo's outlet does: a gauge pressure of 0 Pa (`bc_pressure`) on every case. Can ISLA satisfy it by construction,
so that the free constant is never predicted? Lanes OUTLET-GAUGE (design and CPU prototype), OUTLET-REVIEW and OUTLET-EXP.
Records: scratch/isla-outlet-gauge-2026-10-22/DESIGN.md and estimate.md, scratch/isla-outlet-review-2026-10-22/REVIEW.md,
scratch/isla-outlet-exp-2026-10-22/PREREG.md, JOBS.md and prof/PROFILE.md. Branch psharpe/isla-outlet-gauge, 9250072af
(pushed).

**The design** (DESIGN sections 1, 3-5). One declaration, `dirichlet: pressure` on the outlet's `bc_pressure`, makes the model
return the head's pressure plus the one constant `C* = sum_j a_j (p_bc,j - p_hat_j) / sum_j a_j` over the outlet's drawn
tokens, with their Horvitz-Thompson measures `a_j`. Of all constants, `C*` minimizes the measure-weighted squared residual
on the outlet, so the output's residual there has zero weighted mean, and any constant the head adds cancels exactly. The
outlet tokens are read as passive queries (log-weight minus infinity, ISLA-DTT's mechanism), so in interacting ISLA they
change no other prediction beyond float32 roundoff (the review, below), and ISLA-DTT stays query-independent. The shift is
applied to the returned, standardized output, with the prescribed value standardized the same way, so the identity holds in
pascals. It is a rank-0 invariant, so the rigid-motion, similarity and query-permutation contracts hold as before, and
splitting outlet cells into equal-measure copies leaves the shift unchanged (tested: a reflection with a translation, a
query permutation and an outlet remeshing). It adds no parameter and leaves the state dict unchanged; without the
declaration, or on a case with no outlet token, the model is bitwise unchanged. Options rejected: interacting probes (they
break query independence), every full-resolution outlet face (up to 890k extra tokens), the nearest queries' mean (it
depends on the request), a soft penalty (a tuned weight), and a post hoc shift (below). A hard pointwise condition,
`p = p_bc + phi N` with `phi` the distance to the outlet, is a later step if the pointwise outlet residual matters. Tests:
the whole ISLA test directory passes at 9250072af on CPU, serial (282 passed, 47 skipped, 0 failed; the supervisor's run,
scratch/isla-main-2026-10-14/outlet-suite-2026-10-23/suite_9250072af.log, and DESIGN section 7); the 9 new tests fail on
the base.

**A post hoc estimate** (DESIGN section 2; estimate.md; not a test of the construction). PDIAG's rows (LHR 333637; ISLA
0.9.0, epoch 250, float32, 30 random test cases per split) give the exact effect of shifting each case's scored prediction
by the constant that makes its area-weighted mean over 4,096 outlet face centroids 0 Pa, the face mean taken from PDIAG's
second pass, which appended the centroids as interacting queries:

| split | seed | scored | outlet-face shift | best constant shift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | 42 | 0.302 | 0.314 | 0.257 |
| reynolds | 42 | 0.554 | 0.580 | 0.507 |
| blobs | 42 | 0.369 | 0.409 | 0.365 |
| bank_zero_to_cad | 42 | 0.498 | 0.504 | 0.410 |
| profile_dual_inlet | 42 | 0.649 | 0.705 | 0.363 |
| nonbox | 42 / 43 | 2.224 / 1.096 | 3.333 / 1.492 | 1.984 / 0.881 |
| profile_crossflow | 42 / 43 | 3.341 / 1.997 | 2.581 / 0.817 | 1.215 / 0.591 |

: Median pressure relative L2 over 30 cases, ISLA 0.9.0, post hoc (scratch/isla-outlet-gauge-2026-10-22/estimate.md). {#tbl-nb-outlet-estimate}

Post hoc reading: the shift recovers 23 and 59 percent of crossflow's error (26 and 28 of 30 cases improve) and worsens every
other split, by 1 to 11 percent and by 36 to 50 percent on nonbox. The unconstrained model never trained on the outlet, and
its prediction there is off by more than its interior offset (full: -0.03 RMS p at the faces against -0.004 inside), so
subtracting it adds error. So no inference-only fix: a model trained with the construction learns pressure relative to its
own outlet value, which this estimate cannot show. The best constant still leaves crossflow at 1.215 and 0.591; PDIAG read
crossflow's error as mostly amplitude, from about a 2× velocity overshoot (a post hoc reading, @sec-nb-azdiag), which no
gauge fix touches.

**The review** (OUTLET-REVIEW, read-only, CPU; 44 tests passed; verdict "OK with notes", no code defect).

- Major, procedural: the scorer silently drops the construction unless the override is repeated. `infer.py` builds the model
  from the command-line config and restores only the weights, the state dict is identical with and without the
  declaration, and with the declaration the head's pressure bias gets almost no gradient (3e-7 against 3.9 for the other
  columns, on the review's toy case), so a B checkpoint scored without the override is an unconstrained model with an
  arbitrary pressure constant.
- Minor: in float32 the other outputs of interacting ISLA equal the undeclared model's only to roundoff (velocity up to
  3.6e-7, k 1.4e-6; 1e-12 in float64), since the probes lengthen the reductions. And `compile_blocks` recompiles once on the
  probe count.
- Cleared: the construction and its units, the passive probes (no all-minus-infinity softmax, no NaN in float32 or bf16), the
  probe set, the no-op, and the B configuration.

**The registered test** (OUTLET-EXP; PREREG.md md5 6c055a88, written 16:15 EDT 2026-10-22 before any B job, approved at 16:24;
amendment section 8, md5 5a478506, at 16:29, before any B job).

- Arms. A reuses the standing ISLA 0.9.0 lanes `azc_profile_crossflow_isla_seed{42,43}` and `azc_full_isla_seed{42,43}` and
  their scores. B is A's snapshot and resolved config with the prototype's model.py and scales.py ported onto it
  (`$T/code_outlet`; the port has offsets only) and the declaration in the lane's override, which the scorer passes on.
  Primary splits only: `profile_crossflow` and `full`.
- Amendment, from the review: a B score row counts only if the scorer's saved Hydra config and B's training config show the
  declaration, every B mechanism unit asserts the declaration before it reads a case, every A unit asserts its absence, and a
  failed check makes the read incomplete as registered.
- M1, the event guard: on every scored case of every B run (2,588), the measure-weighted mean of B's shifted pressure over the
  probes equals the prescribed mean to at most 1e-5 times max(1, max |value|) in standardized units, the shift is one
  constant over all outputs to the same tolerance, and the probe set is not empty; one failure, or a scored case with no
  mechanism row, makes B invalid and nothing is read. M2, descriptive: the mean predicted gauge pressure on the 1 percent of
  points nearest the outlet, A and B.
- R1, per split: `D = ln(mean_seeds median p_L2(B) / mean_seeds median p_L2(A))`, `SE = sqrt((s_A^2 + s_B^2) / 2)` with `s` an
  arm's two-seed standard deviation of the log median. Helps: `D < ln 0.85` and `|D| > 2 SE`. Harms: `D > ln 1.15` and
  `|D| > 2 SE` on pressure, or the same on velocity. Otherwise no change. A's own seeds already bound it: on crossflow
  (medians 3.025 / 1.888) "helps" needs `exp(D) < 0.624` even with `s_B = 0`; on full the `ln 0.85` bar binds unless
  `s_B` exceeds about 0.09 (PREREG section 4 says 0.20, a slip in its note beside the rule; the rule is unchanged).
- Adoption: adopt B if it helps on crossflow and harms on no split tested. "Helps nowhere and harms nowhere" means adoption
  on principle after a cost check (step time within 25 percent), which goes to the supervisor as a decision; any reading
  the two clauses do not cover is reported as "not adopted by the rule" and goes to the supervisor too. A validation loss
  above twice its running minimum stops the read.
- Predictions: M1 passes 0.95; M2, B's crossflow band median of the absolute predicted mean at most 0.3 RMS p on both
  seeds, 0.7; crossflow helps 0.30, no change 0.60, harms 0.10; full no change 0.85, harms 0.08, helps 0.07; B's step
  within 25 percent of A's 0.85; adopted by the first clause 0.25, on principle to the supervisor 0.50, neither 0.25.

**The smoke** (LHR 338532, 34 minutes, 2.3 GPU-h; no smoke number is a result). One epoch of A and B on crossflow seed 42
through the lane launcher, scored on 8 test cases. Every check of the amendment passes: the declaration is in B's training
and scorer configs and absent from A's; M1 holds on 8 of 8 cases (`|residual|` / scale 4.6e-13 to 1.3e-8); the probes are
31k to 62k of 31k to 93k outlet faces, never the whole outlet, with measure over area 0.99995 to 1.00001; the mechanism
driver's per-case pressure equals the scorer's. The median step after 50 steps on one node is 0.646 s for A and 0.804 s for
B (1.24 times); against A's lanes' own median of 0.541 s, B's is 1.49 times. Peak memory 129.8 and 161.0 GiB. B recompiles
once more, at step 2, on the probe count.

**Cost.** The registered projection, A's GPU-h per lane times the smoke's ratio, gave about 625 GPU-h, and A's lane logs
about 723, both above the 600 cap. The supervisor set a cap of 750 GPU-h for the lane at 19:05 EDT: the step cost depends on
how the construction is implemented and does not change what the lanes measure. A descriptive profile (LHR 340909, one GPU
per variant, 100 steps after 50 warm-up steps, the same crossflow cases) reads B / A 1.40 on the mean step (0.686 against
0.490 s). Of B's extra 0.197 s, the probe tokens through the blocks take 87 percent (21 forward, 66 backward), the probes'
geometry 7 percent, dynamic-shape kernels 2 percent, and the selection and shift 0.5 percent. The median probe count,
50,000, is 12.5 percent more tokens than A's 400,000, and raises the blocks' forward time by about 34 percent and the
whole backward pass by about 40 percent. The registered cost check reads B's lanes' own logs (median step within 25 percent
of A's); if it fails, it is reported as "fails on cost as the code stands".

**Result** (OUTLET-EXP RESULTS.md md5 457eba6e, tables.md md5 1bdbde00; PREREG md5 69283aa5 with the 10-23 erratum, read as
registered; results/campaigns_2026-10-23/outlet_exp/).

- **The mechanism holds on every case.** On all 2,588 scored test cases of the four B runs, the measure-weighted mean of B's

  tolerance 1e-5), so B is valid. The declaration is in every B training and scorer config and in no A config. No lane
  approached the event guard (largest validation-loss ratio 1.37).
- **R1 reads no change on both splits.**

| split | ISLA 0.9.0 (A) p / v, s42 / s43 | with the outlet level (B) p / v, s42 / s43 | seed-mean p ratio exp(D), 2 SE | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profile_crossflow` | 3.02 / 1.51; 1.89 / 1.41 | 1.39 / 1.18; 0.52 / 1.01 | 0.389, 2 SE 1.09 vs \|D\| 0.95 | no change |
| `full` | 0.300 / 0.109; 0.271 / 0.103 | 0.288 / 0.109; 0.274 / 0.108 | 0.983, 2 SE 0.115 | no change |

: Median relative L2 over the test cases per seed (pressure / velocity, seed 42; seed 43), float32, 200,000 interior points (OUTLET-EXP RESULTS.md, R1). {#tbl-nb-outlet-result}

  On crossflow both seeds' pressure ratios (0.46, 0.27) and velocity ratios (0.78, 0.72) are below 0.85, but B's two seeds

## 2026-10-22 — TIE-EXP registered: ISLA with the tie rules trained eager on the lug and Tensile2d against REF-090's eager-trained base, scored on flip symmetry, native accuracy and the lug's pose excess; gated before launch, with one supervisor-approved deviation (A7); read about 2026-10-24 {#sec-nb-tie-exp-prereg}

**Question** (scratch/isla-tie-2026-10-22/PREREG.md; DESIGN f of scratch/isla-medial-tie-2026-10-22). Do the tie rules of
@sec-nb-geo-bundle, the least-norm direction at closest-feature ties and on the wall, restore exact flip symmetry on the
lug and Tensile2d at no native cost, and how much of the lug's posed excess do they remove? Registered 15:11-15:40 EDT
2026-10-22 (md5 fecaeedd), before any TIE checkpoint, smoke or pre-step output existed; budget about 200 GPU-h for the four
arms, eager, with a cap of 220 GPU-h for everything (supervisor, 15:00 EDT).

**Arms.** B is reused: r090eag_lug_isla and r090eag_t2dz_isla, seeds 42 and 43, on code_cmpaf_fix. TIE is B's lane rows byte
for byte, apart from the run id and the code: `$T/code_tie2`, code_cmpaf_fix with geometry.py and tree_read.py of TIE-FIX
19fb0a754 (A2, A5; the first snapshot, code_tie at d3d9da49d, carried TIE-REVIEW's blocker (with float32 inputs the on-wall
rule returned u = 0 at most on-wall nodes); its pre-steps and one-epoch smoke are superseded, and no arm ran on it). Both
train eager in bfloat16 at 3.75e-4 for 500 epochs and are scored as B was: final checkpoint, float32, fully eager, native,
area and posed, 200,000 cells, the lug's 600 test cases and Tensile2d's 100 val_100 cases. A verdict attributes to the tie
rules jointly, never to one of them.

**Rules** (PREREG section 4; registered verdicts stand as written).

- **F (symmetry).** On the TIE checkpoints (flip_probe_tie2.py of A1; the lug's first 60 test cases, Tensile2d's 100 val
  cases), the median over cases of the compensated flip residual `d_F` is at most 1e-6 for every target field, both seeds,
  both datasets: "exact flip symmetry restored". Otherwise "a residual source remains", to be located before anything else
  is read as a property of the tie rules.
- **N (native).** `r` = TIE ÷ B on seed means; `sigma = max(sigma_reg, s_pool)`, with `sigma_reg` 0.036 on the lug and
  0.232 / 0.330 / 0.303 on Tensile2d's displacement / stress / plastic strain. `|log r| <= 2 sigma` "no cost",
  `log r > 2 sigma` "costs native accuracy", `log r < -2 sigma` "gain" (r above 1 means TIE's error is larger);
  Tensile2d's verdict is displacement's.
- **P (pose, the lug).** The excess `e` = posed ÷ native - 1 of each arm: `e_TIE <= 0.5 e_B` "the medial ties carry most of
  the lug's pose sensitivity", `e_TIE >= 0.8 e_B` "they do not; look elsewhere", between "partial"; read only if
  `log(1 + e_B) > 2 sigma_lug`, otherwise "not readable: B shows no pose excess". Tensile2d is the control, not a verdict:
  predicted `|log((1 + e_TIE) / (1 + e_B))| <= 2 sigma_T2D` (displacement), p 0.95.
- **Decision.** Adopt (with section d's kernel or a per-mesh cache) if F passes and N is not "cost" on either dataset; P
  decides whether the 2026-10-18 note's other options are still needed. A rule that cannot complete is reported incomplete
  as registered.
- Predictions: F restored on both 0.65; N on the lug no cost / gain / cost 0.70 / 0.10 / 0.20, on Tensile2d no cost 0.90; P
  most / partial / do not 0.40 / 0.30 / 0.30.

**Amendments before any arm result.**

- A1: the flip probe also negates the head rows of coefficients odd under the flip, since ISLA assembles outputs of rank 1
  or more, such as Tensile2d's displacement and stress, from the head's coefficients and the basis vectors n and
  pc(rhat, n), which are odd under the flip (thresholds unchanged).
- A2: the code under test becomes code_tie2 after TIE-REVIEW's blocker (float32 on-wall directions were not unit, so u = 0
  at most on-wall nodes); every pre-step and smoke on code_tie is superseded; new gate item (a) checks the float32 features
  against float64, and new item (b) runs the two geometry test files on GB300.
- A3 and A8: the stated assumption that TIE stands for the whole geometry bundle on these two datasets rests on the cell
  count (every boundary cell kept), FOLD-SIGN's count of 0 sign changes on the lug and Tensile2d, and the count of
  0 queries in the band where ONWALL's rule could move them. A3 measured the count against d3d9da49d, before TIE-FIX, and
  states the assumption for code_tie2 only once a repeat against the fix commit is recorded in the PREREG. FOLD-SIGN
  repeated it against 19fb0a754 with the same counts (LHR 341328 and 341486; DESIGN k.4 of
  scratch/isla-medial-tie-2026-10-22), but no amendment through A8 records the repeat.
- A4 to A6: gate (a) against an exact least-norm reference, then items (4) to (6) on the CPU and GPU paths (every row of
  the routine against the exact point, the gray-zone count, degenerate cells); code_tie2 fixed at 19fb0a754; a transfer
  argument to TIE-FIX2 (34654e01d) through item (4)'s count of zero outputs; the supervisor's diagnosis rule for a failure
  of (a)(1) and (a)(2).
- **A7, the deviation** (21:10 EDT). Every gate item passed except (a)(1) and the float32 half of (a)(2), on the lug only,
  and the instrument's self-check (5.2e-9 against 1e-12, on 3 float64 rows with 5 near-duplicate directions). At 190 of
  about 3.8M lug on-wall nodes, `|u32 - u64|` reaches 2.07e-5, above the 1e-5 bar. The routine returns the exact least-norm
  point of the normals it receives at both precisions; the point itself is ill-conditioned at the lug's split hex faces,
  whose normals form clusters 0.0005 to 0.003 degrees wide and 9 to 12.9 degrees apart. The supervisor's rule of 20:16 EDT
  launched only if the change propagated at most two to one (`r <= 2`); measured `r` exceeds 2 at all 190 nodes (max 2,261,
  median about 300), so that premise was wrong, and the supervisor overrode its do-not-launch branch at 21:10 EDT after
  seeing the diagnosis. Item (4)'s count of zero outputs was not 0 (189,092 and 172,836 lug rows, all with exact point 0),
  so A6's transfer was measured directly: 0 uncertified rows and 0 differing rows in 5,143,196 (342299). Stated before any
  result, as why F, N and P are unaffected: F compares a flip within one precision, where the rule negates `u` bitwise; for
  N and P the network reads these features under bf16 autocast, about 200 times coarser than 2e-5, and only 0.005 % of
  on-wall nodes are affected.

**Launch.** The four arms were submitted at 21:10 EDT on code_tie2 (342513 to 342516) with the rules unchanged. No TIE score
is read before the registered read, about 2026-10-24; the registry expects the arms to end by 2026-10-25.

**Later (2026-10-24).** Read as registered at 01:43 EDT: F "exact flip symmetry restored", N "no cost" on the lug and
Tensile2d, P "the medial ties carry most of the lug's pose sensitivity"; the decision rule reads adopt, and A3's condition is
not met as registered (@sec-nb-tie-exp-read).

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-23 (scratch/isla-geo-nb-2026-10-23/SECOND_READ_TIE.md).*

## 2026-10-23 — LRE-AZ registered: ISLA 0.9.0 with the fixed Reynolds scale z = log10(Re_ISLA / 1e6) on AeroZoo's `reynolds` split, a check for harm before that scale is proposed as ISLA's Reynolds input; read about 2026-10-24 midday {#sec-nb-lre-az-prereg}

**Question** (scratch/isla-lre-az-2026-10-23/PREREG.md, md5 f9964333, written 01:33 EDT 2026-10-23 before any B job;
approved by the supervisor at 01:37 EDT). On AirfRANS the fixed scale cut ISLA's below-band pressure error to 0.53-0.58
times the fitted scale's (@sec-nb-af-lre-verdict), where the fitted spread was 0.062 decades. On AeroZoo the fitted spread
is 0.8985 decades, so the fixed scale only rescales and shifts z (z_fixed = 0.8985 z_fitted - 0.938). z enters ISLA 0.9.0
as one more global scalar into linear layers, which can absorb a fixed affine map; only what training finds can change. So
the test is registered as a check for harm on a dataset whose Reynolds number spans several decades, not as a test for a
gain.

**The split** (labels and ISLA's own log10 Re = log10(U L / nu), with its length unit L):

| quantity | train (2,119 cases) | test (1,385 cases) |
|---|---|---|
| label log10 Re | 3.003 to 5.999 | 6.001 to 8.000 |
| ISLA's log10 Re | 3.247 to 7.040 | 6.233 to 9.133; 414 inside ISLA's training band, 971 above it |
| fitted z (A) | -2.020 to 2.202 | 1.304 to 4.531 |
| fixed z (B) | -2.753 to 1.040 | 0.233 to 3.133 |

: AeroZoo `reynolds` split (scratch/isla-lre-az-2026-10-23/PREREG.md section 2, tables_A.md). {#tbl-nb-lreaz-split}

**Arms.** A reuses `azc_reynolds_isla_seed42` and `_seed43` and their scores (code_r090, recipe_r090; checkpoint args
`reynolds: {mean: 5.062, std: 0.8985}`). B is A's snapshot and resolved config with one change,
`dataset=aerozoo_uvolume_reynolds_lre`: a copy of A's dataset file `aerozoo_uvolume_reynolds.yaml` (md5 f7cc0d6d) with
`isla_constants.reynolds {mean: 6.0, std: 1.0}` and a header (md5 eb37789f; branch psharpe/isla-lre-az 4781af873, pushed),
in the recipe snapshot `$T/recipe_lreaz`. Scoring exactly as A: float32, 200,000 interior points, the 1,385 test cases,
native, final checkpoint. `reynolds` is a plain attribute, not a buffer, so a score of B built with A's dataset file would
silently use A's z. A four-part check on each score row (the score row's dataset, the scorer's saved config and recipe, the
dataset file's md5, and the checkpoint's args) must therefore show that B read {6, 1} and A did not; a failed check makes
that row invalid and the read incomplete as registered.

**Rules** (PREREG section 5).

- R1, per field on the test set, pressure and velocity ruled: `D = ln(mean_seeds CM(B) / mean_seeds CM(A))` with CM a run's
  case-mean relative L2, `SE = sqrt((s_A^2 + s_B^2) / 2)`, with s an arm's two-seed sample standard deviation (n - 1) of
  ln CM. Helps: `D < ln 0.90` and `|D| > 2 SE`. Harms: `D > ln 1.10` and `|D| > 2 SE`. Otherwise no change. Eddy viscosity,
  k and omega are computed the same way and reported beside it. A's seeds give `s_A` 0.0083 on pressure and 0.0293 on
  velocity, so the 10 percent bars bind unless `s_B` exceeds about 0.06 to 0.07 (PREREG section 5 says 0.13, a slip in its
  note beside the rule; the rule is unchanged).
- R2, descriptive: per bin of distance above the training maximum, B ÷ A and the slopes per decade.
- Consequence: "harms" on pressure or velocity means the fixed scale is not adopted without Peter. Otherwise the supervisor
  proposes z = log10(Re / 1e6) as ISLA's Reynolds input at the scope freeze, about 2026-10-27, on principle: it is
  dataset-independent, it helped below the band on AirfRANS (registered reading "helps", @sec-nb-af-lre-verdict), and it
  would cost nothing here.
- Event guard: if a B lane's validation loss passes twice its running minimum, the read stops and goes to the supervisor.
- Predictions: pressure no change / helps / harms 0.80 / 0.08 / 0.12; velocity 0.80 / 0.07 / 0.13; no harm on either 0.75.

**Smoke and launch.** The smoke (LHR 345967, 0.79 GPU-h) passed every registered item: every rank read
`reynolds={'mean': 6.0, 'std': 1.0}`, z over one epoch's training batches spans -2.7533 to 1.0402, the training split's own
extremes, and the resolved config equals A's but for the dataset, the run id and the output and checkpoint paths. Its
epoch-0 median step, 0.655 s, matches A's 0.651 and 0.644 s. The two lanes were submitted at 01:53 EDT 2026-10-23 (346117,
346118), and both have trained since. Cost about 188 GPU-h against the brief's 300. The read is expected about
2026-10-24 midday.

*Read by the supervisor and second-read by a lane reviewer on 2026-10-23 (scratch/isla-geo-nb-2026-10-23/SECOND_READ_LREAZ.md).*

## 2026-10-23 — PROBES-090 on the AirfRANS standing's eager-trained checkpoints: the registered prediction that every label repeats (p 0.7) fails narrowly; every query-population label repeats and interacting ISLA stays invariant to exact re-meshing, and ISLA-DTT under a two-fold re-panelization moves from invariant to small move {#sec-nb-probes090-eag}

**Question** (PROBES-090, scratch/isla-probes090-2026-10-21/PREREG.md §9, an amendment before results). The AirfRANS
standing comes from eager-trained checkpoints (r090eag_af_{isla,dtt}; @sec-nb-ref090-standings). The book's AirfRANS rows
of the query-population and re-meshing probes read the fix-trained pair (@sec-nb-probes090). Do the registered labels hold
on the standing's own checkpoints? Registered prediction: every AirfRANS label repeats (p 0.7). Jobs (LHR): QUERY-POP
350362 (ISLA) and 350363 (ISLA-DTT), REMESH 350364, all COMPLETED 0:0; read by REF-090-CLOSE2 (RESULTS.md §7b).

**Validity, read first: pass.** Each probe's native request reproduces the official eager scorer record on all 200 test
cases at epoch 500: bitwise for ISLA (0.0 on both seeds, both probes), within 2.5e-6 for ISLA-DTT (registered gate 1e-3).
Every mode and variant changes the input on every case; no row is degenerate.

| request or boundary | ISLA 0.9.0, eager-trained (p / v / nut) | fix-trained | label |
|---|---|---|---|
| half the points | 1.10 / 1.12 / 1.15 | 1.11 / 1.13 / 1.14 | material |
| four chunks | 1.31 / 1.36 / 1.40 | 1.33 / 1.37 / 1.41 | material |
| at most 1,000 points (all fields) | 4.5 to 126 | 4.6 to 159 | severe |
| far-field companions | 120 / 75 / 105 | 98 / 54 / 131 | severe |
| wall-heavy companions | 19 / 30 / 22 | 19 / 29 / 24 | severe |
| ISLA-DTT, every mode | largest abs(r − 1) 4.1e-6 | 4.5e-6 | roundoff |
| exact re-panelization (ISLA) | within 0.012 %, d 3e-5 | within 0.011 % | invariant |
| 800 / 600 / 400 / 200 tokens (ISLA, p) | 1.02 / 1.32 / 2.30 / 5.22 | 1.02 / 1.32 / 2.41 / 5.32 | small / sensitive |
| exact re-panelization (ISLA-DTT, p) | 1.017 / 1.057 / 1.059 | 1.010 / 1.039 / 1.070 | small move (refine2 was invariant) |

Seed means of seeds 42 and 43 (the mean of the two seeds' ratios), 200 test airfoils, float32, eager, final checkpoints.
Every ratio is the error under the probe ÷ the same checkpoint's error on its native request or boundary.

**Registered reading: the prediction is false, narrowly.** Every label repeats but one. ISLA-DTT under a two-fold split of
the panels (refine2) reads 1.017 on pressure, seed 43 at 1.0235, just past the registered 0.02 for "invariant" (seed 42
reads 1.0111; the prediction moves by a median 1.6e-3 and 2.7e-3, inside 0.01), so its label is "small move". The size sits
in the 1 to 7 percent band that the opening-angle sweep traced to ISLA-DTT's θ = 1 tree read (@sec-nb-probes090), so it is
the same mechanism at a two-seed boundary, not a new one. No conclusion in the book changes.

**Beside the rule.** Interacting ISLA's query-population dependence and its invariance to exact re-meshing are the same on
the defect-trained, fix-trained and eager-trained weights, so they are properties of the architecture, not of how it
trained. The far-field ratio moves within its seed spread (pressure 91 to 181 defect-trained, 93 to 103 fix-trained, 106 to
135 eager-trained). Two 400-token draws still lie farther from each other than either from native (median pressure distance
0.032 and 0.033 against 0.017 and 0.018), so the 400-token loss is draw variance. Under the registered text (r and d both
within the redraw's), interacting ISLA's 400-token row misses "within draw noise" by 0.4 percent on eddy viscosity (1.388
against the redraw's 1.382); ISLA-DTT's qualifies.

**For the book.** The AirfRANS probe rows in 03, 04, 05, 09, 12 and 20 read the eager-trained checkpoints (records copied to
results/campaigns_2026-10-23/probes090/; chapter 20's numbers from book_E/limits_090_2026-10-23.py there), and the three
In-flight callouts on them go (04 sec-query-population, 20 sec-limits-boundary-law, 20 sec-limits-query-independence). The
ranges shift a little: four chunks 1.31 to 1.40; small requests 4.5 to 126 times; ISLA-DTT's refinement 1.7 to 5.9 percent.
